Title: MSM-Mamba: A multi-scale multimodal Mamba framework for non-stationary time series forecasting
Abstract: In real-world scenarios, time series data often exhibit complex patterns, such as long-term dependencies, trend changes, and local high-frequency disturbances. These patterns make it difficult for existing forecasting models to accurately describe non-stationary dynamics, which limits further gains in forecasting performance. To address this problem, we propose MSM-Mamba, a multi-scale multimodal Mamba framework for non-stationary time series forecasting. MSM-Mamba uses a trend decomposition module to split the original sequence into trend and dynamic residual components. It applies a stationary wavelet transform to decompose the residual sequence at multiple scales, while learnable frequency-band weights adaptively fuse the high-frequency detail sub-bands. The fused residual sequence is encoded by S-Mamba to capture non-stationary dynamics and long-range dependencies. At the same time, the multi-scale wavelet detail sub-bands are converted into two-dimensional time-frequency images. A convolutional visual encoder extracts local texture features and cross-scale structural information from these images, while a dynamic gating mechanism adaptively integrates the predictions from the visual and numerical branches. During training, multi-directional perturbation constraints are introduced to improve the stability and discriminative power of the learned representations. Experimental results on the ETT series, Electricity, and Exchange datasets show that MSM-Mamba achieves better forecasting performance on most prediction tasks, indicating the effectiveness and generalization ability of the proposed method.

Title: Physics-data fusion as an intelligent prognostic instrument for Sim2Real-based power prediction in Sucker Rod Pumping Systems
Abstract: The Sucker Rod Pump System (SRPS) is a primary energy consumer in oilfields, making accurate electric load forecasting critical for grid stability and intelligent regulation. However, current forecasting methods are often hindered by scarce fault samples and heavy reliance on labeled data. This study proposes a physics-data fusion framework that integrates mechanistic simulation with data-driven residual learning, facilitated by a Simulation-to-Real transfer strategy to bridge the simulation-reality gap and enable high-fidelity prediction. A full-process dynamic simulation model is established, and a Multi-Head Self-Attention (MHSA) mechanism is adopted to learn the nonlinear residuals with respect to the measured electrical power, thereby constructing a high-fidelity virtual ground-truth dataset under various operating conditions. Leveraging this enhanced dataset, a Convolutional Neural Network–Long Short-Term Memory (CNN-LSTM) architecture, optimized via Ant Colony Optimization (ACO), is developed for intelligent power prediction across multi-time scales (24–96 h). Experimental results demonstrate that the framework achieves a Mean Absolute Relative Error (MARE) of 4.74% and a Normalized Root Mean Square Error (NRMSE) of 4.99% between the predicted power curves and field measurements. Application of this predictive model to coordinated peak shaving of well clusters shows superior practical performance. Future work will focus on the unmodeled downhole components and further improve its adaptability to extreme fault conditions under small sample scenarios.

Title: Efficient acoustic detection of dental food impaction: An interpretable fusion framework
Abstract: Problem: Interproximal food impaction is an important contributor to oral diseases, including gingivitis and periodontitis. Conventional diagnostic methods are subjective and poorly repeatable because they rely heavily on clinician experience. Although artificial intelligence-based acoustic analysis offers a potential objective approach, its utility for dental-floss-induced food-impaction assessment requires task-specific datasets and systematic evaluation Approach: We constructed a dedicated dental-floss acoustic dataset and developed an interpretable artificial intelligence framework, termed the Interpretable Time-Frequency Dual-Stream Joint Learning Fusion Network, for site-level food-impaction detection. Main contribution: The study systematically evaluates a time–frequency fusion scheme that combines temporal and spectral modeling components. The two branches characterize transient waveform responses and localized Mel-spectral energy patterns, while a cosine-similarity threshold determines whether temporal features are introduced into the frequency-domain representation. The evaluation includes component comparisons, noise-robustness testing, operator-external validation, and human–machine assessment. Key results: In the subject-level five-fold comparison on the dental food-impaction acoustic dataset, the framework achieved an accuracy of 97.05% and consistently high sensitivity, specificity, F1-score, and precision, with higher performance than the evaluated spectrogram-image classification, audio recognition, and medical sound recognition baselines. These findings support the utility of the evaluated time–frequency fusion framework for site-level food-impaction assessment under the studied acquisition conditions.

Title: Hierarchical flower-like Au/trimetallic oxide heterostructures for LDI-MS metabolic fingerprinting toward livestock health surveillance and food chain safety
Abstract: Rapid analytical methods capable of discriminating livestock diseases are highly desirable for early animal health surveillance and food-chain risk control. Herein, a gold nanoparticle-modified ternary metal oxide hierarchical flower-like heterostructures (Au/TOHFHs) was developed as a high-performance matrix for laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry (LDI-MS)-based metabolic fingerprinting. The hierarchical architecture and plasmon-enhanced interface synergistically improved metabolite enrichment, energy utilization, and ion efficiency. Using standard metabolite solutions, the Au/TOHFHs matrix exhibited good analytical reproducibility, with coefficients of variation of 5.24−14.95% for intra-spot replicate measurements and 6.71−14.90% for inter-spot spatial sampling. Using 178 bovine serum samples, including 96 samples from cattle with bovine tuberculosis, 31 from cattle with brucellosis, and 51 healthy controls, the platform accurately distinguished bovine tuberculosis and brucellosis from healthy cattle, achieving receiver operating characteristic curve areas under the curve of 0.983 and 0.899, respectively, in independent validation. Furthermore, simplified nine-metabolite and seven-metabolite biomarker panels for bovine tuberculosis and brucellosis, respectively, retained robust predictive performance, with independent-validation areas under the curve of 0.983 and 0.958, respectively, while reducing model complexity. This strategy enables rapid, label-free, and high-throughput livestock screening from minimal serum volumes, providing a practical tool for large-scale herd surveillance and strengthening food safety management through source-level risk control.

Title: Generalized multi-source assimilation: A framework for cross-modal integration and source optimization
Abstract: This work establishes the theoretical foundations for optimal weight learning in multi-source scientific machine learning. By moving away from empirical, ad-hoc weighting, our framework explores the automated and mathematically sound fusion of diverse numerical methods, neural architectures, and noisy measurements. We analyze a comprehensive spectrum of coupling mechanisms, ranging from unconstrained Softmax parameterization to explicitly constrained formulations like ADMM, as well as single-timescale, two-timescale, and adaptive- ρ Augmented Lagrangian methods. For the Lagrangian frameworks, we derive separate convergence rates for model parameters (O(1/k)) and source weights (O (1/ k)), proving that time-scale separation ensures robustness against varying source reliability. We further establish specific regularity conditions for ADMM, including rank and strong convexity requirements for variable splitting. For single-timescale Augmented Lagrangian coupling, by contrast, we establish sufficient conditions under which it achieves sublinear convergence governed by an effective condition number that quantifies the curvature imbalance between primal and dual variables. We validate these theoretical insights across a diverse architectural scope, ranging from Fourier Neural Operators (FNO) and DeepONets to Finite Difference schemes, applied to tasks including multi-scale modeling and large-scale data assimilation. Our results provide insight into a fundamental trade-off: Lagrangian and ADMM approaches provide strict constraint satisfaction and stability for physical laws, while Softmax parameterization offers superior computational efficiency for high-dimensional, entropic ensembles.

Title: SAR image ship detection network based on quasi-gaussian convolution and pooling-gated mechanism
Abstract: Ship detection from Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) images is critical for maritime surveillance and defense. Existing deep learning methods emphasize network architectures but often neglect the pixel-distribution characteristics of ship targets and lack specialized operators. We propose QGPG-Net, a novel SAR ship detection network integrating Quasi-Gaussian Convolution (QGConv) and a Pooling-Gated Mechanism (PGM). QGConv models the quasi-gaussian pixel distribution of ships to enhance feature extraction and expand the receptive field. PGM employs pooling operations and a gating unit to retain key contextual information while reducing computational cost, improving robustness against complex backgrounds. Additionally, we introduce a Scale-aware Detail-Enhanced (SDE) detection head with weight-shared, cascaded convolutions that capture coarse structure and fine-grained texture simultaneously. For bounding-box regression, we adopt Distance-IoU (DIoU) loss to improve localization precision. Evaluated on the CSSD dataset, QGPG-Net attains an AP<inf>50</inf> of 86.5%, (Formula presented) of 56.6%, and F1-score of 82.7%, achieving relative gains of 2.8%, 2.8%, and 2.2% over the YOLO11 baseline, respectively, while reducing parameters and FLOPs. Furthermore, QGPG-Net demonstrates robust performance in cluttered shorelines, varied sea states, and targets of diverse scales. This design enables a favorable balance between detection accuracy and computational efficiency, making QGPG-Net well-suited for real-world maritime applications.

Title: CCSC: Cross-domain multimodal deception detection with chebyshev spectral filtering and consistency-aware fusion
Abstract: Multimodal deception detection has emerged as a pivotal component in security, judicial systems, and interactions between humans and AI. Current techniques depend heavily on spatial appearance features or handcrafted descriptors specific to a single domain. Such models often overfit to source-domain noise like lighting changes or background sounds. This tight connection to the training data prevents effective performance in new environments. Simple fusion tools also fail to fix timing gaps between different data types. These flaws often lead to positional biases or shifts in data spreads. This work presents CCSC, a framework for Cross-domain multimodal deception detection that leverages Chebyshev Spectral filtering and Consistency-aware fusion in the frequency domain. It enhances representations of single modalities and performs fusion with alignment sensitive to data distributions. Specifically, a Temporal Synchronization Module (TSM) provides unified preprocessing and synchronization for audio and video. This eliminates the need for specialized features or invasive signals. We then propose a Learnable Chebyshev Spectrum Filter (LCSF) that operates on power spectra to emphasize task-relevant bands and suppress noise by embedding a learnable Chebyshev basis into the spectral transformation. The pipeline culminates in a mechanism for Consistency-Aware Fusion, which quantifies the similarity of posteriors across modalities via Jensen Shannon divergence to adaptively recalibrate the fused representation. This strategy mitigates sensitivity to positional mismatches and enhances stability under distribution shifts. On standard benchmarks, including Real Life Trial, DOLOS, and Box of Lies, CCSC robustly outperforms strong unimodal, fusion, and transfer baselines. It achieves superior F1, ACC, and AUC in settings both within and across domains.

Title: Artificial intelligence integration in franchise-based digital businesses: how to foster value co-creation
Abstract: Purpose – This study examines how artificial intelligence (AI) is integrated into franchise-based businesses in the digitalized entertainment sector. The aim is to offer a nuanced decision lens to guide managers in fostering value co-creation. Design/methodology/approach – We adopted a qualitative multi-case study research, supported by sectoral analysis and conducted by gathering primary and secondary data. The study focused on four sub-sectors (film and television, music, sports and gaming) to strengthen solidity. Through NVivo [15], we employed an inductive approach to trace AI integration across dynamic capabilities. Findings – The study reveals AI integration shifts franchises along a continuum from full value co-creation to full value co-destruction, with intermediate leaning states. Such effects impact dynamic capabilities, leading to augmentative or substitutive outcomes. This happens through two different processes: optimization achieved with non-intrusive AI integration; disruption determined by intrusive AI. Results identify common mechanisms adopted by multiple companies within the entertainment industry, leading to either outcome. Originality/value – This research introduces a franchise-applicable “AI Integration–Dynamic Capability Alignment Framework” that enhances managerial decision-making. The study advances existing literature by classifying AI integration through contingency mechanisms. It enables managers to design and scale AI according to the superior outcome. Future research should apply the framework to other sectors and quantify performance effects.

Title: From Assistance to Autonomy: AI Integration in Structured Research-Based Learning for Higher Education
Abstract: Despite the growing interest in artificial intelligence (AI) for science education, little is known about its role within structured research-based learning (RBL) frameworks that balance technological assistance with developing independent research competencies. Existing studies often focus on AI as an isolated tool or a single-stage intervention, leaving a gap in understanding how AI can be systematically embedded across the research process without diminishing students’ cognitive engagement. This study addresses that gap by implementing the newly developed IFTAR model, which organizes RBL into five sequential phases—Identification, Find Literature, Determine Methodology, Accommodate/Analyze/Interpret Data, and Report & Present—with AI selectively integrated into the literature search and data analysis stages. A quasi-experimental, non-equivalent control group PreTest–PostTest design was conducted with ninety undergraduate physics education students assigned to one control and two experimental groups. Cognitive outcomes were measured using a validated instrument and analyzed through classical ANCOVA, rank-based ANCOVA, and robust ANCOVA to account for assumption violations. Across all analytical approaches, both experimental groups significantly outperformed the control group, with no significant difference between the experimental conditions. These findings demonstrate that phase-specific AI integration within a transparent and scaffolded RBL framework can enhance cognitive performance while preserving methodological autonomy, offering a replicable model for purposeful AI use in STEM higher education.

Title: A novel deep learning framework integrating temporal convolution and bidirectional LSTM for multi-city AQI forecasting
Abstract: Accurate forecasting of the AQI is critical for public health protection and urban environmental management. This study presents a hybrid deep learning method for multi-city short-term AQI prediction by integrating TCN, PSOGSA, BiLSTM, and an attention mechanism. The model integrates TCN for multi-scale local feature extraction, BiLSTM networks for capturing long-term bidirectional dependencies, and a temporal attention mechanism for adaptive weighting of salient temporal patterns. In addition, PSOGSA is employed to optimize model hyperparameters, improving the stability of the training process. Experimental evaluations on datasets from four Chinese cities—Haikou, Guiyang, Nanjing, and Shanghai—show that the proposed method achieves consistently strong performance compared with competitive baseline and state-of-the-art models across MAE, RMSE, MAPE, and R<sup>2</sup> metrics. A comprehensive ablation study verifies the effectiveness of each component, while non-parametric statistical significance tests, including the Friedman test and the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, further confirm the reliability of performance improvements across multiple independent runs. Furthermore, a computational complexity analysis is conducted to evaluate the computational efficiency and scalability of the proposed method. The proposed method provides a robust and well-validated solution for multi-city AQI forecasting, with potential extensions toward uncertainty-aware and probabilistic forecasting.

Title: Deep learning of SHERLOC Raman spectra for facilitating Mars Astromaterial identification
Abstract: Raman spectroscopy has been explored for planetary exploration, particularly through the SHERLOC instrument for Mars habitability and astromaterial search tasks. The SHERLOC and other Raman-based astromaterial search tasks mostly rely on comparative Raman peak analysis and expert interpretation with respect to known spectral peaks. It is desirable to employ machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) methods for high-performance automated astromaterial identification from Raman spectra. In this work, for the first time, we benchmarked three ML and two DL models for the identification of six mineral classes from SHERLOC Raman spectra. Using the expert-labeled spectra of two campaigns (Crater Floor and Upper Fan), the best-performing DL model yielded identification accuracies of 89.3%, while maintaining competitive class-wise performance under class-imbalanced conditions. The best-performing DL model was further applied to non-diagnostic and unlabeled SHERLOC Raman spectra, and the resulting predictions were broadly consistent with material characteristics reported in the literature. These results suggest that DL methods may provide supportive information for automated Raman-based astromaterial identification and spectral interpretation in planetary exploration.

Title: Infrared spectroscopy and machine learning for post-consumer plastics recycling
Abstract: The pollution of plastic materials represents one of the most important environmental challenges, due to the rapid and uncontrolled increase in their production, consumption, and use. Therefore, the recycling and valorization of post-consumer plastics are strategic solutions to mitigate this phenomenon. These processes are subject to rigorous international regulations that require recycled polymers to exhibit physical properties and quality consistent with those of their virgin counterparts. To achieve this goal, a thorough and accurate classification of plastic materials before and after recycling is essential. Infrared (IR) spectroscopy has emerged as a fundamental technique for this purpose, enabling non-destructive identification of polymers through their characteristic vibrational features. However, the high spectral similarity between different plastics often leads to misclassification. To overcome this limitation, in this paper, we integrate IR spectroscopy with advanced Machine Learning (ML) algorithms. We develop and validate a rapid, automated ML-based classifier for the identification of four prevalent plastic types: HDPE-B, HDPE-P, LDPE, and PP. The classification models were trained on a dedicated IR spectral database generated from original experimental measurements. Using the open-source Quasar platform, we performed a comparative analysis between traditional ML algorithms and standard Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture. The study shows that both CNN and classical algorithms, in particular Random Forest (RF), achieve optimal performance in the classification task, with accuracies of 1.000 and 0.998, respectively. Our results demonstrate that the integration of deep learning architectures with IR data significantly enhances the accuracy and reliability of plastic recognition, providing a robust tool to support the industrial transition toward high-quality recycled polymers.

Title: An early detection model of wheat stripe rust utilizing two-dimensional correlation spectroscopy for eliminate growth-related interference
Abstract: Wheat stripe rust, caused by Puccinia striiformis f. sp. Tritici (Pst), represents a significant threat to global wheat production. Early detection, particularly during the asymptomatic phase, is critical for effective disease management. Hyperspectral sensing can detect subtle physiological alterations associated with initial infection; However, its effectiveness is frequently limited by substantial background interference from normal plant growth. In this study, the reliability of hyperspectral data obtained from early asymptomatic leaves was first validated using quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qPCR). To mitigate background the interference, generalized two-dimensional correlation spectroscopy (2D-COS) was employed, utilizing infection time as the perturbation variable. This approach surpasses conventional dimensionality reduction techniques such as principal component analysis (PCA) and the chemometric feature selection algorithm known as competitive adaptive reweighted sampling (CARS). Through this methodology, six feature bands exhibiting distinct absorption changes were identified. Analysis of synchronous and asynchronous 2D-COS correlation features from 1 to 6 days post-inoculation (dpi), enabled effective discrimination between spectral variations attributable to growth and those specific to disease responses. The biological significance of these spectral dynamics was empirically validated using steady-state chlorophyll fluorescence imaging and destructive biomass measurements. This combined evidence confirmed that Pst -induced chloroplast functional impairment strictly precedes macroscopic tissue structural collapse. This process effectively suppressed background noise while preserving critical infection-related signals. Subsequently, three classifiers—support vector machine (SVM), random forest (RF), and eXtreme gradient boosting (XGBoost)—were evaluated using the extracted 2D-COS features. Asynchronous features generally produced superior classification performance, with XGBoost achieving the highest accuracy (86.79%) and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) (94.12%). Compared to conventional methods like PCA and CARS, 2D-COS more effectively attenuated growth-related interference and accentuated early disease signatures. These results demonstrate that the integrated framework of “multiplicative scatter correction (MSC) + Asynchronous Correlation Features + XGBoost” offers substantial potential for accurate, non-destructive, and early diagnosis of wheat stripe rust.

Title: Trade-Offs in Statistical and Machine-Learning-Based Imputation for Algal Time-Series: A Multi-Criteria Evaluation on Optical Density Data Without Ground Truth
Abstract: Missing values are pervasive in algal cultivation monitoring, where instrument failure and transmission loss remove whole runs of consecutive observations, and the repair method chosen silently shapes every downstream analysis. This study asks which repair method should be used, and on what evidence, when no complete reference series exists. Twelve methods are compared on optical density and ten covariates recorded across 30 open-pond production cycles at five geographically distinct sites: four interpolation schemes, a propagation scheme, two nearest-neighbor schemes, three chained-equation variants, a random-forest ensemble and a mechanistic growth-curve fit. The principal contribution is a validation framework organized in two clearly separate tiers. The first tier needs no ground truth and applies to the naturally missing values, comparing central tendency, dispersion, distributional shape, autocorrelation structure and coverage between observed and repaired series. The second tier withholds values that were in fact recorded and rebuilds them, so reconstruction error can be measured directly; it is replicated over ten random seeds, three masking proportions and four contiguous outage lengths, giving 25,200 paired evaluations in which every method sees an identical pattern of withhold cells. Key findings found that no method dominates. Ensemble and chained-equation learners rebuild individual values most accurately, with a normalized error of 0.1927 against 0.2645 for linear interpolation, but they compress dispersion and distort distributional shape, whereas shape-preserving interpolation and propagation protect those properties and rebuild less accurately. Gap structure matters: interpolation loses accuracy when gaps are contiguous rather than scattered, while multivariate learners gain. Regularizing the chained equations removes a convergence failure that left one pond unrepaired. An aggregated decision analysis turns these trade-offs into a weight-dependent selection rule, giving practitioners an auditable basis for matching method to analytical objective instead of a single universal default.

Title: A novel automated method for UML modeling integrating instruction, reasoning LLMs and vision language model evaluation
Abstract: Automated generation and validation of UML diagrams from natural language requirements remain a significant challenge in software engineering, hindered by semantic ambiguity and the lack of robust evaluation methods. This paper introduces a novel, end-to-end pipeline that automates UML modeling by synergistically integrating three specialized AI model types. Our pipeline first employs an instruction-tuned model (LLaMA−3.2-1B) to generate user-centric feature descriptions. These are then processed by a reasoning-centric LLM (DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B) to synthesize PlantUML code through structured reasoning. Finally, an ensemble of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) performs a weighted, multimodal evaluation to ensure the semantic and structural correctness of the generated diagrams. Experiments on a large-scale dataset of 15,000 diagrams across nine types show our pipeline achieves a high Mean Weighted Score of 4.23 on a 1–6 VLM evaluation scale. A human evaluation with 155 participants confirms a strong correlation between our automated scores and expert judgment. Our work establishes a new benchmark for generalized UML automation and demonstrates the effectiveness of a multi-stage pipeline that combines instruction tuning, reasoning-based code synthesis, and multimodal validation.

Title: Temporal Evolution of Hit Song Predictors from Spotify Audio Features: A Machine Learning and Explainable AI Study
Abstract: Understanding the factors that distinguish commercially successful songs remains an important problem in music analytics, with implications for applied data science. While previous studies have demonstrated that machine learning models can predict hit songs from audio features, they generally treat the prediction task as static and pay limited attention to how the determinants of success evolve over time. This study investigates the temporal evolution of hit-song predictors using Spotify audio features extracted from 41,103 Billboard-labelled tracks released between 1960 and 2019. The dataset is divided into three industry eras (Analog, CD/Digital, and Streaming) to examine changes in predictive performance and feature importance across distinct periods of music production and distribution. Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and K-Nearest Neighbours are optimized using grid-search cross-validation and evaluated with accuracy, F1-score, and ROC-AUC. Model interpretability is achieved through SHAP analysis. Cross-era differences in feature importance are statistically evaluated using bootstrap confidence intervals, while robustness is further assessed through repeated random seeds, permutation importance, alternative era definitions, and data de-duplication. Among the evaluated models, Random Forest consistently achieves the highest predictive performance, with ROC-AUC ranging from 0.848 to 0.917 across the three eras, indicating that chart success has become increasingly predictable from audio characteristics over time. Explainable AI analysis reveals a systematic evolution in the importance of musical attributes: instrumentalness remains the strongest predictor throughout, loudness becomes substantially more influential in the Streaming era, whereas speechiness and acousticness progressively decline in importance. These patterns are supported by bootstrap statistical testing and remain stable across multiple robustness analyses, suggesting that the observed temporal changes are not artifacts of sampling variability, model specification, or data partitioning. Overall, this study demonstrates that explainable machine learning can characterize the temporal evolution of feature importance, providing a robust analytical framework for investigating long-term changes in cultural data.

Title: Analysis of barriers to self-monitoring of blood glucose among community-dwelling elderly patients with diabetes mellitus: a cross-sectional study integrating artificial intelligence-based risk prediction
Abstract: Background: Self-monitoring of blood glucose (SMBG) is essential for diabetes management, yet elderly patients face multiple barriers that compromise adherence and glycaemic control. This study aimed to assess barriers to SMBG among community-dwelling elderly patients with diabetes mellitus, identify associated factors, and develop an artificial intelligence (AI)-based predictive model for high-risk individuals. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted at Chun’an First People’s Hospital from March to August 2025. Two hundred elderly patients (≥ 60 years) with diabetes were enrolled using convenience sampling. Data were collected using validated instruments: a sociodemographic questionnaire, SMBG Barriers Scale, Flourishing Scale (FS), and Digital Health Literacy Scale (DHLS). Statistical analyses included descriptive statistics, Pearson correlations, and multiple linear regression. For predictive modelling, the dataset was split into training (80%) and testing (20%) sets. Random Forest, XGBoost, and Support Vector Machine algorithms were developed and evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC-ROC. Model interpretability was assessed with SHAP values. Results: The mean SMBG Barriers score was 47.6 ± 9.8. Significant negative correlations were found between SMBG barriers and FS (r = − 0.42) and DHLS (r = − 0.51) scores. Multiple regression showed DHLS (β = −0.38), Flourishing score (β = −0.25), education, and diabetes education as protective factors, while complications and living alone were risk factors (R² = 0.462). The Random Forest model achieved the best performance (accuracy 88.5%, AUC 0.921). SHAP analysis identified digital health literacy, psychological well-being, and AI acceptance as the strongest predictors. Conclusion: This study highlights the importance of psychosocial and digital factors in SMBG barriers and demonstrates the effectiveness of explainable AI for risk prediction in elderly diabetic patients. Targeted interventions addressing modifiable factors could improve self-management. Clinical trial registration: This study is a cross-sectional observational study and was not registered as a clinical trial.

Title: Forecasting residential aged care expenditure with learning algorithm and demographic simulation
Abstract: In Australia, residential aged care accounts for a significant share of government expenditure, with financial sustainability and changing population profiles emerging as critical concerns. This study utilizes a longitudinal dataset and develops a statistical simulation model to project the profiles of individuals entering residential aged care, the number of admissions, and the associated government spending. Our approach integrates ensemble learning methods, including eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), with the Hamilton–Perry demographic projection method to provide precise predictions of residents’ length of stay. This integration enables more reliable forecasts of the future residential aged care landscape. The analysis was conducted at the state level to capture regional differences. We examined both demographic features, such as age, marital status, and gender, and medical features, including dementia status and care needs as measured by the Aged Care Funding Instrument (ACFI). We find that XGBoost outperforms previously used survival models for predicting residents’ length of stay. Our simulation model projects that both the number of residents and aggregate government expenditure in residential aged care will continue increasing until 2041. The model also provides groundwork for future research by offering micro-level insights into usage patterns and financial sustainability challenges.

Title: Exploring the nonlinear impacts of the intra-urban built environment on carbon emissions using an interpretable ensemble machine learning framework
Abstract: The urban built environment (UBE) substantially shapes carbon emissions trajectories, yet existing studies largely rely on fragmented dimension analyses, coarse administrative units, and homogeneous linear assumptions, leaving the comprehensively multidimensional, spatiotemporally heterogeneous, and nonlinear interplay between UBE and carbon emissions largely understudied, particularly from an intra-urban perspective reflecting real-world anthropogenic activities. Taking 286 Chinese prefecture-level cities from 2010 to 2024 as testbeds, this study architected an intra-urban UBE framework encompassing 5D (e.g. , density, diversity, design, destination accessibility, and distance to transit ) and developed an interpretable ensemble learning model to decouple the intricate association between intra-urban UBE and carbon emissions. The result reveals that intra-urban UBE collectively accounts for 61.51% of the impacts, surpassing the socioeconomic factors. Moreover, the results identify non-linear thresholds and interactive effects: density and diversity exhibit inverted U-shaped relationships, whereas urban compactness and urban green and blue spaces show consistent negative associations. Critically, active transport networks reduce emissions only when combined with public transit proximity; road density expansion cuts emissions only in compact cities; and polycentricity with compactness achieves emission reduction only within a moderate window. Temporally, the relative importance of greenness, active transport, diversity, and polycentricity has increased, while that of density has declined. Spatially, the effects of intra-urban UBE vary markedly across regions and cities. Polycentricity works best in emerging agglomerations, and transit proximity has reached diminishing returns in core megacities. The findings underscore that low-carbon urban policy must be spatiotemporally tailored with context-sensitive thresholds, positioning intra-urban UBE as a foundational climate mitigation instrument.

Title: Machine learning-based snow depth estimation in forested mountain environments using LiDAR and UAV RGB image-derived photogrammetric products
Abstract: Accurate snow depth (SD) estimation in forested mountain environments remains challenging owing to terrain complexity and vegetation effects. Although UAV-LiDAR provides high-resolution three-dimensional measurements, LiDAR-derived SD estimation may be insufficient to account for SD spatial variability associated with forest structure and local terrain conditions. This study developed an integrated framework combining UAV-LiDAR data, structure-from-motion photogrammetry, and machine learning (ML) algorithms to improve high-resolution SD estimation. UAV-LiDAR surveys were conducted during snow-covered and snow-free periods in 2024, and the datasets were processed using DJI Terra and Pix4Dmapper, to generate digital canopy height models (DCHMs) and digital elevation models (DEMs). Initial SD estimates were obtained by subtracting the snow-free DEM from the snow-covered DEM. Subsequently, remotely sensed variables, including initial SD estimates, DEMs, DCHMs, and distance to trees, were integrated with ML models and evaluated the predictive performance with validation of field data (n = 167). A linear mixed-effects model was used to compare the predictive accuracies of the different integrated approaches. The results demonstrated that the predictive accuracy differed significantly among the integrated approaches. Among all combinations, the estimated SD range (0.419–0.925 m) generated using the DJI Terra-derived SD map, DCHM, and distance to trees with Random Forest model achieved the highest predictive performance (R<sup>2</sup> = 0.811, RMSE = 0.049, MBE = 0.008, and MAE = 0.037). The findings demonstrate that integrating DJI Terra-derived SD with forest structural and tree proximity information through ML can improve high-resolution SD estimation, thereby supporting operational snow monitoring in forested mountain environments.

Title: Leakage-controlled and uncertainty-adjusted screening hypotheses for cryogenic alloys using an interpretable lightweight pipeline
Abstract: A generalised leakage-controlled and uncertainty-adjusted screening pipeline is presented for cryogenic alloy down-selection from literature-mined datasets. Literature-mined records often contain strong within-source correlations owing to the compositions, processing routes, specimen preparation, and testing protocols that are frequently shared within the same publication. Conventional random splits can therefore inflate apparent performance through source-level leakage. The workflow enforces DOI-level grouped partitioning and evaluates models under repeated DOI-grouped partitions and a repeated ten-DOI hold-out benchmark while complementing regression metrics with screening-oriented ranking measures, including Spearman correlation and top-decile hit rate. The feature design combines elemental composition with thermodynamic descriptors, and CPU-friendly tree ensemble models without deep learning are employed for prediction. Feature representations are compared on matched source splits, and evaluation includes the missing-metadata conditions encountered during candidate screening. Prediction uncertainty is quantified using publication-level split conformal calibration with candidate-dependent residual scales for all three properties. The resulting lower bounds are normalised using training-derived scales before weighting, and both uncertainty effects and weight sensitivity are evaluated explicitly. Applied to the AlloyData-2024LT cryogenic dataset, the pipeline produces temperature-specific candidate shortlists and multi-objective Pareto sets at 4, 20, 77, and 120 K. The resulting candidates are therefore presented as experimentally actionable hypotheses for subsequent validation by experiment, CALPHAD assessment, or high-fidelity simulation. The lightweight nature of the approach enhances deployability and accessibility through a browser-based Hugging-Face-Space interface that allows users to screen candidates by temperature and property thresholds. This study ultimately provides a reproducible template for trustworthy, interpretable, and resource-efficient computational screening of literature-mined materials data.

Title: MAWC-DETR: lightweight small-object detection in UAV imagery via multi-stage adaptive weighted calibration
Abstract: Small objects in UAV imagery usually produce weak detection responses. Existing methods lack a small-object weight calibration mechanism across multiple detection stages, making it difficult to preserve effective small-object responses and fully optimize subtle localization errors. To address these issues, we propose MAWC-DETR, a UAV small-object detection framework based on multi-stage adaptive weighted calibration. In the feature extraction stage, cross-scale weighted convolution (CSWC) is proposed to address the equal-weight modeling limitation across spatial positions. It adaptively enhances local responses of small objects while enabling lightweight and discriminative feature extraction. In the feature fusion stage, a recalibration attention network (RCAN) recalibrates small-object feature weights through detail recovery and semantic modeling, compensating for feature loss caused by sampling and fusion. In the regression supervision stage, WMFIoU is constructed to break the equal-penalty pattern for samples and errors. It adaptively focuses on difficult small objects and subtle localization deviations, improving bounding-box regression accuracy. By jointly optimizing feature extraction, fusion, and regression supervision, MAWC-DETR enhances effective small-object representation under lightweight constraints. Experiments on VisDrone2019-DET show that MAWC-DETR achieves 52.0% mAP50 and 32.3% mAP50:95, outperforming RT-DETR by 4.6 and 3.2 percentage points, respectively, while reducing parameters from 19.9M to 10.9M and GFLOPs from 57 to 48. With an inference speed of 41.6 FPS, MAWC-DETR achieves a favorable balance among accuracy, lightweight design, and real-time efficiency for UAV small-object detection. It should be noted that the DGX Spark platform differs from actual UAV onboard embedded computing devices, and the real-time performance in practical onboard deployment remains to be further verified. Results on AI-TOD, DIOR, and HIT-UAV further demonstrate its generalization capability.

Title: Strategies for improving piano teaching effectiveness using deep learning with big data models
Abstract: Piano instruction has traditionally depended on one-on-one human interaction, limiting its scalability and adaptability for diverse learners. The integration of artificial intelligence into music education introduces opportunities for more effective, data-driven teaching strategies. Deep learning methods are capable of modeling musical features, including accuracy, timing, and expressive dynamics. This study proposes a Deep Learning-based big data model to Enhance Piano Teaching (DLEPT), a system designed to improve piano instruction through real-time, multimodal assessment and intelligent feedback generation. DLEPT uniquely combines MIDI and audio inputs to provide expressive, context-aware performance analysis and generates pedagogically-informed corrective feedback. DLEPT is developed using the MAESTRO dataset, which contains over 200 h of professionally performed and aligned MIDI and audio recordings. A Transformer-based architecture is employed to compare student performances against expert references, detecting deviations in rhythm, dynamics, and phrasing. The model is optimized using the AdamW optimizer, combined with learning rate warm-up and cosine decay scheduling, with additional regularization such as dropout and label smoothing, to ensure stable convergence and generalization during training. Corrective feedback is then generated to guide learners in improving technical accuracy and musical expression. The trained system achieved an accuracy of over 92% in detecting common performance issues and produced feedback validated against expert-level evaluations. The combined use of MIDI and audio inputs enabled expressive and context-aware performance analysis. In conclusion, DLEPT provides a scalable and intelligent solution for enhancing piano instruction through modern deep learning and optimization techniques, representing a novel multimodal approach in intelligent music pedagogy.

Title: A hybrid scale attention network for uncertainty aware brain tumor MRI classification
Abstract: Accurate and reliable classification of brain tumors from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is critical for timely clinical decision-making. Existing deep learning methods suffer from three key limitations: overconfident predictions without principled uncertainty estimates, lack of external validation across acquisition protocols, and parameter-heavy architectures unsuitable for resource-constrained deployment. To address these gaps, we propose Hybrid Scale-Attention Network, a lightweight framework comprising an EfficientNet-B3 backbone, a depthwise-separable Adaptive Multi-Scale Module (AMSM), and an Evidential Deep Learning (EDL) classification head. AMSM fuses three parallel dilated convolutional branches at rates {1, 2, 4} and an identity branch via learned softmax gating, forming a convex combination of multi-scale representations at an approximately 6.6× lower parameter cost than equivalent standard convolutions. The EDL head enables single-pass evidential uncertainty estimation based on Dirichlet strength. Through systematic four-variant ablation, we find that stacking a Dual Attention Module after AMSM degrades cross-dataset generalization despite modest in-domain gains, motivating its exclusion. On BRISC 2025, the proposed model achieves 99.20% accuracy and 99.30% macro-F1 with only 10.97 M parameters. Development-stage external validation on the PMRAM-BD cohort yields 97.41% accuracy without fine-tuning, indicating strong cross-dataset performance. Misclassified samples carry higher mean evidential uncertainty than correctly classified ones, with a misclassification detection AUROC of 0.9461 at single-pass inference cost (16.8 ms), offering an efficient alternative to MC-Dropout. Grad-CAM and UA-GradCAM visualizations alongside MSAD provide radiologist-interpretable localization and per-class scale-branch analysis. These results demonstrate that the proposed model offers a favorable trade-off among accuracy, parameter efficiency, and principled uncertainty quantification, supporting potential retrospective clinical investigation.

Title: Repurposing a commercial artificial intelligence vision platform for automated surgical instrument identification: a proof-of-concept study
Abstract: Background: Retained surgical items are classified as never events but continue to occur, and the count meant to prevent them is often recorded as correct even when an item is retained. Computer vision could provide an independent check on what is on the instrument table, but purpose-built surgical systems are scarce. Industrial vision platforms offer a faster route, although their surgical performance is unknown. Methods: In a prospective experimental study, a commercial artificial intelligence vision platform developed for industrial inspection was applied to 19 surgical instruments and 3 suture items, each presented once in 100 runs (2,200 experiments). No software redesign was required, but the classifier had been trained on this item set, making this a supervised rather than a zero-shot setting. Two outcomes were recorded: whether the platform assigned the exact item identity, and whether it registered an item as present at the packing step irrespective of type, termed count-presence detection. Because experiments are clustered within items and runs, the primary estimate is the mean per-item accuracy with cluster-adjusted intervals. Results: The correct instruments were identified in 2,036 of 2,200 experiments (92.5%). The mean per-item accuracy was 92.5% (95% confidence interval 88.4 to 96.7; cluster-adjusted 87.7 to 95.6). Count-presence detection was 99.1% (98.7 to 99.4). Performance was reproducible across runs (intraclass correlation 0.02), whereas variance clustered by item (0.12). Accuracy ranged from 64% (suture needle 6-0) to 100% (six items). Errors were directional and almost always within visually near-identical sub-types. Conclusions: An industrial vision platform detected item presence with high reliability and identified item type with high accuracy, however, with a residual error rate of 7.5%. The errors were predictable and confined to visually similar classes, pointing to correctable mitigations rather than a fundamental limit. These figures represent an upper bound under highly controlled conditions rather than expected intraoperative performance. Such a system is intended to support rather than replace the perioperative team. This study establishes feasibility rather than clinical benefit; a prospective intraoperative study is the necessary next step.

Title: Adaptive streaming data-driven anomaly detection for enhancing service stability and user experience in music streaming platforms
Abstract: With the rapid expansion of digital entertainment services, music streaming platforms face massive user interactions, high-frequency playback requests, and rapidly changing traffic. This paper proposes ASDADet, an adaptive streaming data-driven anomaly detection model that combines real-time stream processing, prediction-reconstruction joint learning, dynamic task weighting, and adaptive thresholding. ASDADet continuously analyzes playback records, user-behavior traces, access traffic, and system logs, and updates its detection strategy as the stream distribution changes. The early-warning targets include abnormal playback bursts, automated or abusive account activity, traffic surges, service interruption signals, abnormal content access, and unusual interaction patterns that may increase buffering, playback interruption, or response latency. Experiments use a de-identified music-streaming dataset containing 10 million access records and 5 million playback logs, together with three public streaming benchmarks for complementary anomaly-pattern evaluation. ASDADet achieves 92% accuracy, 88% recall, and a 90% F1 score, exceeding the benchmark method by 7 percentage points in accuracy and reducing end-to-end detection latency by about 30%. Stable performance under high-traffic conditions further demonstrates its suitability for real-time service monitoring.

Title: Design of robot-assisted intelligent piano teaching platform
Abstract: Robot-assisted intelligent piano teaching platform (RA-IPT) with the help of AI would transform the process of teaching piano into a more interactive, adjustable, and flexible training. Artificial intelligence-assisted and traditional instruction are combined in the book. The dependence on human teachers, the absence of real-time feedback as well as the impossibility to adapt to the speed of learners makes the teaching of piano slow, uninspiring, and inefficient. The guidance, correction of mistakes, and adaptive difficulty adjustment of robotic gesture imitation, audiovisual recognition, and machine-learning-based performance assessment can be automated using the RA-IPT platform. When the robots give students fast feedback in areas such as hand placement, rhythm, and accuracy of notes, students self-correct and become focused. It is suggested to have interactive and data-driven classes that enhance non-teacher-assisted learning. Experiments show that this smart, scalable music teaching system is faster and more accurate than traditional skill-development techniques. Regular usage of the proposed approach enhances learning accuracy by 98%, reaction speed by 150 ms, gesture recognition by 95%, mistake detection by 35%, and abilities by 90%.

Title: Digital inheritance and innovative development of music based on deep learning and the Internet of Things
Abstract: The preservation and innovative development of traditional music are essential for sustaining cultural heritage, artistic identity, and creative expression. Rapid digitalization and a lack of systematic preservation threaten the inheritance of invaluable musical resources. This research proposes a framework for digital inheritance and innovative music development by integrating deep learning (DL) with the Internet of Things (IoT). IoT-enabled sensors were used to capture real-time performances of vocal, instrumental, and dramatic music, recording acoustic, temporal, and environmental parameters. The collected signals underwent preprocessing, including noise reduction, normalization, and Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT), to ensure accurate feature representation of musical patterns. For pattern recognition and creative innovation, an Intelligent Water Drop-driven Versatile Deep Neural Network (IWD-VDNN) was employed. The VDNN is the core DL model designed to analyze, preserve, and generate traditional music patterns. The IWD algorithm optimized the learning process, improving convergence and model efficiency, enabling the system to generate new musical sequences inspired by traditional styles. The proposed method implemented in Python significantly enhanced digital music inheritance and innovation. It achieved 94% accuracy, 92.2% recall, a Style Match Accuracy of 95%, and a Musical Quality Score of 4.91, demonstrating superior performance in preserving traditional music while enabling interactive, creative, and high-quality music generation, effectively bridging cultural heritage with innovative composition and adaptive digital learning. Integration of IoT and DL provides a scalable, accurate, and interactive platform for safeguarding traditional music while promoting its creative evolution for future generations.

Title: How does AI-generated assessment compare to expert assessment in simulation-based experiences: Analyzing AI-human interrater reliability
Abstract: Background: In the health professions, artificial intelligence simulation-based experiences (AI-SBEs) are increasingly used to evaluate learner performance and provide feedback. Benefits of AI-SBEs include providing instantaneous feedback, allowing more practice opportunities than feasible using traditional methods, and reducing educator burden. However, methods for calibrating AI feedback are underdeveloped. Methods: This study evaluated the feedback provided by a generative AI-based software program (SimConverse) when assessing simulated patient interactions using the Weight Sensitivity Instrument (WSI), a checklist used to assess learners’ weight bias-related clinical behaviors. A two-phase interrater reliability (IRR) approach was used. First, iterative prompt engineering was guided by AI-human IRR results. Four authors and four volunteers generated 31 interactions in SimConverse. Interaction transcripts were downloaded, and another author with expertise in the WSI manually reviewed and scored the transcripts. Percent agreement and Gwet’s AC1 were calculated to compare AI and expert assessments, and the research team reviewed feedback statements and agreement statistics to identify rubric instructions in need of revision. After revising the rubric in SimConverse, four authors produced 10 additional SBE interactions. Expert and AI assessments were explored. In phase two, the AI-SBE was piloted with 60 medical students in a larger intervention study. A random sample of 30 student transcripts were assessed for AI-human IRR, and students’ comments about the AI-SBE were reviewed. Results: Of the 11 WSI items, expert and AI agreement was consistently good or very good for 7 items across all rounds (Gwet’s AC1=0.71 and higher). One item initially showed poor agreement (Gwet’s AC1=0.56), but agreement improved after prompt engineering (final Gwet’s AC1=0.89). The improved item assessed whether students made specific statements (asked if weight loss was a priority). Three other items had persistent poor agreement (final Gwet’s AC1=0.42, 0.66, 0.64). These items required broader contextual assessment of the transcripts. Most open-ended student reactions to the AI-SBE were positive. Conclusions: Findings suggest that AI scoring and feedback within AI-SBEs requires iterative prompt engineering and educator/researcher guidance. Tuning was more successful for content-specific items than context-dependent items. Future work could explore best practices for prompt refinement, particularly for more complex and context-dependent rubric items.

Title: A hybrid multi-task transformer with multi-scale attention mechanism for multimodal energy forecasting in regional power grid integrated energy systems: MK-Former
Abstract: The digital transformation of power grid regulation has driven large-scale deployment of hyperscale dispatch centers and distributed edge nodes, forming complex integrated energy systems (IES) characterized by GPU-intensive computing and coupled electricity-heat-cooling loads. Accurate multi-energy load forecasting with multi-modal data is thus critical for efficient energy scheduling and reliable grid operation. However, existing approaches face three critical challenges: single-energy forecasting ignores inherent electricity-heat-cooling couplings; they cannot simultaneously capture multi-scale temporal patterns; and mainstream deep learning models are computationally prohibitive for real-time edge deployment, with poor robustness under non-ideal conditions. To address these issues, we propose MK-Former, a light-weight hybrid multi-task Transformer tailored for multi-modal energy forecasting in power grid regulation. The framework integrates three complementary design elements: a multi-scale spatiotemporal attention mechanism that fuses features extracted by different convolution kernels, together with hybrid hard-soft parameter sharing to balance cross-task knowledge transfer and task specificity; KAN-based efficient nonlinear modeling paired with Dynamic tanh (DyT) activation for normalization-free training; and matrix multiplication-free (MatMul-free) dense layers to reduce reliance on conventional dense matrix multiplications. Extensive experiments on an integrated energy dataset demonstrate that MK-Former achieves strong performance among the compared models (RMSE = 4.6921, MAE = 2.7589, MAPE = 0.0526, R² = 0.9246), with the lowest RMSE, MAE, and MAPE among the compared models. With only 34.826 K parameters, it combines favorable theoretical complexity with noise-robust predictive performance, retaining strong performance even under severe Gaussian noise ( σ = 0.2). This work provides a high-performance, scalable solution for real-time intelligent energy management in modern power grid infrastructures, and offers new insights for light-weight multi-modal time series forecasting model design.

Title: Psychosomatic Susceptibility Profile (PSSP): a machine-learning-derived eight-item instrument integrating personality and coping for psychosomatic risk stratification
Abstract: Psychological, behavioral, and physical factors jointly contribute to heterogeneity in health-related outcomes, yet existing instruments often assess these domains separately or require lengthy questionnaires. In this study, we aimed to identify multidimensional psychosomatic profiles and develop a brief machine learning–based tool for their classification. Data from 3,207 employees (aged 18–65 years) were analyzed using responses from the NEO Five-Factor Inventory (NEO-FFI), coping questionnaires, the 12-item General Health Questionnaire (GHQ-12), body mass index (BMI), and physical activity measures. To enable integrated analysis, questionnaire responses were transformed into text-based representations and encoded using DistilBERT embeddings, followed by dimensionality reduction using principal component analysis. Spectral clustering identified latent psychosomatic profiles, resulting in three distinct subgroups characterized by different psychological, behavioral, and physical patterns. A supervised machine learning model was then trained to classify profile membership, and SHAP-based feature selection identified a minimal subset of informative items. This process yielded an eight-item instrument, the Psychosomatic Susceptibility Profile (PSSP), consisting of selected personality and coping items. An XGBoost classifier with five-fold cross-validation demonstrated good internal performance (F1 = 0.80; recall = 0.81). Overall, this study presents a data-driven framework for identifying multidimensional psychosomatic profiles and deriving a brief, interpretable classification tool for efficient profile assignment in research and applied settings.

Title: Integrating ChatGPT into 5E inquiry-based learning to scaffold EFL academic research writing
Abstract: Large language models such as ChatGPT are increasingly used in education, yet evidence on how to integrate them systematically into EFL academic writing pedagogy remains limited. This study examined a 16-week undergraduate EFL composition course at a national university in Taiwan that embedded ChatGPT within the 5E inquiry-based learning (IBL) cycle (Engage, Explore, Explain, Elaborate, Evaluate). Students completed sequenced research-writing tasks (outline, questionnaire design, initial findings, abstract/introduction, and a full research report) with ChatGPT used as a dialogic scaffold. Using an exploratory classroom-based mixed-methods design, the study collected pretest and posttest writing scores, peer-discussion transcripts, writing artifacts, ChatGPT interaction logs, and reflective journals. Descriptive statistics and paired-samples t-tests examined score change, while qualitative content and thematic analyses triangulated engagement patterns across phases. Results showed a modest, non-significant increase in timed argumentative writing performance, while qualitative findings suggested process-oriented development in inquiry-based academic research writing practices. Students used ChatGPT throughout the 5E cycle for higher-order inquiry work, including topic framing, instrument refinement, and data interpretation as well as for drafting and language polishing. Across the semester, they developed phase-sensitive prompt literacy and critical filtering by selectively adopting, revising, or rejecting AI suggestions to maintain authorial control. An illustrative case further demonstrated how this phase-sensitive ChatGPT engagement unfolded across the five inquiry phases. Overall, the 5E IBL structure appeared to channel AI use toward purposeful inquiry and responsible academic writing development.

Title: Development and external validation of an explainable machine-learning model for early complications following robot-assisted radical prostatectomy: a multicenter study
Abstract: Complications occurring early after robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP) can hinder postoperative recovery. Existing risk instruments, however, generally incorporate few predictors and assume linear associations. We aimed to derive and externally validate an interpretable machine-learning model that combines clinical, laboratory, and intraoperative information and to translate the model into an online risk calculator. Records were reviewed for 1,254 patients with prostate cancer (PCa) who received RARP at the First, Third, or Fifth Medical Center of the Chinese PLA General Hospital. Among them, 1,001 patients from the First and Fifth centers were randomly allocated 7:3 to training (n = 701) and internal testing (n = 300), while 253 patients from the Third center provided an independent external cohort. Sixty-four candidate variables underwent univariate screening and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression. The tested algorithms were gradient boosting decision trees (GBDT), random forest, logistic regression, support vector machine, AdaBoost, Gaussian naive Bayes, and multilayer perceptron. We examined discrimination with the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), agreement between predicted and observed risk with calibration plots, and clinical usefulness with decision curve analysis (DCA). SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used to interpret predictions. The leading model was also benchmarked against the Comorbidity Score for Robotic Surgery (CRS). Feature selection yielded eight predictors for model training. For the multilayer perceptron (MLP), the AUC was 0.880 on internal testing and 0.843 in the independent external cohort. Across both evaluations, this algorithm offered the most balanced combination of performance measures, good calibration, and favorable clinical net benefit. SHAP ranked crystalloid infusion as the leading predictor; operative time and thrombin time (TT) ranked next. In an exploratory comparison in the external cohort, MLP showed greater potential than CRS in discrimination, calibration, and net benefit. We visualized the final model and deployed it as a web-based calculator. The interpretable MLP model accurately estimated the likelihood of early postoperative complications among patients with PCa undergoing RARP. Its accompanying online calculator may assist clinicians in recognizing high-risk patients as soon as surgery is completed and may inform individualized risk classification, postoperative monitoring, and clinical care.

Title: Computing intelligent models for cross-border E-commerce supply chain optimization using artificial intelligence
Abstract: Background: Cross-border e-commerce (CBEC) is among the fastest-growing areas of global trade, yet predicting on-time delivery remains difficult owing to fragmented logistics networks, customs variability, and demand uncertainty. Most existing methods rely on single-model architectures that do not jointly capture the spatial, temporal, and relational dependencies of supply-chain data. Methods: We propose ADAPT-FUSE (Adaptive Deep Attention Prediction Transformer with Fuzzy Unified Stacking Ensemble), a five-layer hybrid framework that integrates Temporal Convolutional Networks, Bidirectional LSTM encoders, Multi-Head Self-Attention Transformers, Graph Neural Networks, and Fuzzy Inference Systems. These extractors are combined through an adaptive gated fusion mechanism, tuned by dual-objective Bayesian and Genetic Algorithm optimization, and aggregated by a calibrated stacking ensemble. Dataset: Evaluation uses a fully synthetic benchmark of 5000 CBEC transactions across eight major Chinese provinces (2021–2024), with marginal distributions calibrated to publicly available aggregate trade and logistics statistics; no proprietary records or human-participant data were used. The dataset, generator, model code, seeds, and raw result logs are released for full reproducibility. Results: ADAPT-FUSE attains the best accuracy (0.8940), macro recall (0.8504), and macro F1-Score (0.8543) among eight evaluated models, with macro precision (0.8585) and AUC (0.9441) level with the strongest baseline; five-fold stratified cross-validation gives accuracy 0.8752 ± 0.0095. The margin over the strongest baseline is not statistically significant (McNemar p = 0.5044), and ablation shows the fuzzy-inference and recurrent branches carry the most weight while the attention and graph branches contribute little at this data scale. Conclusion: ADAPT-FUSE offers a competitive, fully reproducible architecture for delivery-risk prediction that shifts the operating point toward better minority-class recall. Because the benchmark is synthetic and the observed margin is not statistically significant, we frame the contribution as an architecture rather than a performance breakthrough; validation on real operational data is required before deployment. Future work will extend the framework to multi-modal data such as satellite imagery and real-time weather feeds.

Title: Cultural guidance optimized patch mix contrastive learning enabled ensemble model for asthma detection and classification from respiratory audio
Abstract: One of the chronic respiratory conditions is asthma, which causes airway inflammation and affects millions of individuals worldwide. Early and accurate asthma detection is essential for timely clinical intervention; however, existing respiratory-audio-based detection mechanisms suffer from high training complexity, limited generalization capability, inadequate feature representation, and inconsistent classification performance. To address these challenges, this research develops a Cultural Guidance Optimized Patch-Mix Contrastive Learning enabled Convolutional Neural Network Light Gradient Boosting Machine (CGO-PC2BM) framework for automatic asthma detection and classification. The novelty of the proposed framework lies in the synergistic integration of Spectrogram Statistical Audio Features (S2AF), Patch-Mix Contrastive Learning, CNN-LightGBM ensemble classification, and Cultural Guidance Optimization Algorithm (CGOA)-based adaptive hyperparameter optimization within a unified respiratory-audio analysis framework. The proposed S2AF mechanism combines VGGish embeddings, hybrid CQT-STFT spectrogram representations, and statistical audio descriptors to capture complementary semantic, spectral, temporal, and statistical characteristics of respiratory sounds. Furthermore, Patch-Mix Contrastive Learning enhances discriminative representation learning and improves generalization toward unseen respiratory audio samples, while LightGBM accelerates model training and improves classification accuracy. In addition, CGOA optimizes model hyperparameters and improves convergence towards the optimal solution. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves specificity, accuracy, F1-score, precision, and sensitivity values of 96.08%, 96.61%, 96.39%, 95.76%, and 97.03%, respectively, on the Asthma Detection Dataset Version 2, demonstrating its effectiveness for respiratory-audio-based asthma detection and classification.

Title: Spatial information explained by prediction models under block cross-validation
Abstract: Spatial information in geographic data arising from the dependence between variable values and their locations fundamentally shapes the performance and evaluation of spatial prediction models. Model evaluation primarily relies on global accuracy metrics such as root mean squared error (RMSE), which quantify prediction error but do not assess spatial structure a model explains in observed data. However, there are still challenges in the spatial information as a measurable quantity in prediction modelling and the assessment of spatial learning performance under spatial block cross-validation. This study develops the spatial information explained (SIE) metric to assess the extent to which spatial prediction models explain spatial information during modelling, through quantifying the relative reduction in spatial information from a response variable to its prediction residuals. SIE integrates block cross-validation residual computation that enforces spatial separation between training and evaluation sets, and mutual information-based quantification of spatial information contents, and softmax-weighted multi-scale aggregation. A spatial simulation study validates that SIE is effective in measuring spatial learning performance. The developed SIE metric is implemented in predicting C4 natural grass area percentage across Australia with multi-source environmental data of photosynthetic advantage, temperature, and precipitation variables, and ten machine learning models evaluated under block and random cross-validation. Results show that SIE effectively distinguishes machine learning models in spatial learning performance, and reveals that model rankings under SIE differ from those under RMSE, and prediction accuracy and SIE represent distinct evaluation dimensions. Specifically, KNN, the neural network, and XGBoost achieve the highest multi-scale SIE of approximately 0.50 together with high prediction accuracy, SIE rankings correlate weakly with accuracy rankings across the ten models, and random cross-validation overstates SIE relative to block cross-validation for all ten models, by 2.1% to 17.0% with a mean of 9.9%. The validation power of SIE arises from the information-theoretic property that mutual information captures all forms of spatially statistical dependence between residuals and spatial location, including nonlinear spatial associations that domain-average accuracy metrics cannot detect. SIE measures spatial learning performance that complements conventional accuracy metrics, with broad applicability to spatial prediction tasks in Earth and social sciences, and advanced geospatial artificial intelligence and foundation modelling, where capturing geographic structure is analytically required.

Title: A multiway approach to overcome the peak resolution challenges in gas-chromatography coupled to ion mobility spectrometry
Abstract: Background: Gas-chromatography coupled to ion mobility spectrometry (GC-IMS) is a powerful platform for untargeted analysis of volatile compounds, combining high sensitivity and short analysis times. However, its practical implementation still presents several analytical and computational challenges. From the instrumental perspective, the high sensitivity of isothermal GC–IMS makes it prone to signal saturation and memory effects, which can compromise the reproducibility of measurements. On the data-analysis side, the nature of GC–IMS outputs produce large and collinear datasets, in which baseline drift, shift in ion mobility and retention time modes, and peak overlap hinder the reliable extraction of relevant chemical information. Results: This work proposes a comprehensive workflow from the analytical strategy to the data analysis using as benchmark a data set of honey samples of different origin. Analysing the GC-IMS data, obtained with an instrument operating in isothermal condition, a prominent and marked memory effect was observed; it could be contained only through the systematic use of frequent blanks. Notably, most papers in the literature do not adopt blanks at such frequency. Attention was then devoted to the preprocessing, to improve data quality prior to modelling while limiting the number of preprocessing steps. A multiway approach, i.e. Parallel Factor Analysis 2 (PARAFAC2) applied interval wise, was adopted, for the first time, to resolve overlapping peaks and extract chemically meaningful components from the GC-IMS landscape. The results obtained were also compared with Multivariate Curve Resolution–Alternating Least Squares (MCR–ALS) and recent improved PARAFAC2 algorithms. Significance: A complete pipeline for the GC-IMS analysis was carefully developed and validated. PARAFAC2, was successfully applied for the deconvolution of GC-IMS data. This approach provided comparable results with previous methods and indicated that the same grade of automation reached in the analysis of GC-MS data with the same approach is feasible.

Title: Development of a personalized gamified mobile learning app using an AI-based virtual assistant for financial literacy
Abstract: This study presents the implementation of a mobile application that integrates gamification and artificial intelligence to strengthen financial literacy in college students. The solution combines a user-centered approach, educational and structured content, and interactive challenges, integrating a virtual assistant powered by Gemini AI. The application is composed of three stages: an initial diagnostic assessment, gamified challenges, and a final assessment. The system offers personalized feedback, financial topics with levels of difficulty, and a system of achievements and rewards, which seeks to enhance engagement and learning outcomes. The development stage was carried out under the Scrum framework over eight sprints, using Unity and FastAPI for frontend and backend development, respectively. On the other hand, the evaluation included usability and user experience analysis using two instruments: the System Usability Scale (SUS) and the User Experience Questionnaire (UEQ), as well as an analysis of the educational impact by comparing pre-test and post-test results. The results obtained from testing with 50 university students show high usability (SUS = 91.9) and a positive experience in all dimensions evaluated by the UEQ. Likewise, a shift toward higher levels of performance in financial knowledge is observed after using the application. These findings suggest that the integration of gamification and AI in mobile environments can contribute to strengthening financial learning in university contexts.

Title: A systematically designed open-access dataset for cross-microscope machine learning benchmarking in complex steel microstructure classification
Abstract: The establishment of robust machine learning workflows for microstructure analysis requires datasets that systematically capture the variance introduced by the imaging pipeline. While existing studies in this field predominantly rely on well-curated, homogeneous datasets optimized for high classification performance, these conditions rarely reflect the variance encountered in real-world settings. This work presents a publicly available, FAIR-compliant dataset of 5327 annotated micrograph patches, showing bainitic and martensitic microstructural constituents in quenched and quenched-and-tempered low-carbon steels, acquired on three different optical microscopes across two magnification levels (20x and 50x) and under deliberately varied acquisition conditions. Identical regions of interest were imaged on all platforms and aligned by image registration, enabling optimal comparability by pixel-wise alignment across instruments and magnifications. This correlative structure makes the dataset uniquely suited for systematic investigations of cross-instrument and cross-magnification domain generalization. Using this dataset, the influence of microscopy modality-induced domain shifts on the classification performance of deep convolutional neural networks was analyzed. A general model trained on the full dataset achieved near-perfect classification (F1 score of 99.91%), demonstrating that modern deep learning is capable of handling the full range of imaging-induced variance when sufficient data coverage is provided. Cross-domain experiments revealed that generalization is governed primarily by the physical fidelity of the input representation and the coverage of imaging-induced variance in the training data, rather than by model architecture or nominal magnification alone. The direction in which resolution gaps are bridged between training and validation domains proved more decisive than information density per se. Among single-instrument configurations, broad variation of acquisition conditions, such as aperture, exposure, and color temperature, contributed more effectively to cross-domain robustness than optical diversity between objective lenses alone. These results suggest that targeted variation of acquisition conditions, rather than purely morphological diversity, is a particularly effective strategy for improving model generalization. The dataset is released to the community as a benchmark resource for domain shift analysis, generative modeling, and domain-aware learning in microstructure-based machine learning.
