Title: A multi-scale state-space expert hybrid network algorithm for acoustic-based glacier calving event detection
Abstract: Glacier calving generates broadband underwater acoustic emissions that encode valuable information about ice-shelf dynamics and ice–ocean interaction. Compared with satellite remote sensing, passive acoustic monitoring enables continuous, high-temporal-resolution observation of short-duration calving events, but automated detection remains challenging because calving signals are highly diverse, non-stationary, weakly labeled, and often embedded in complex polar background noise. To address these challenges, we propose an adaptive state-space expert hybrid network for unsupervised glacier calving event detection. The proposed model adopts a hierarchical encoder–decoder architecture composed of stacked adaptive state-space expert (ASSE) modules. Each module combines: 1) multi-scale feature extraction to represent acoustic components associated with different physical processes, 2) a dynamic routing mechanism to adaptively weight scale-dependent experts, and 3) a state-space-model (SSM) expert pool to capture both long-range temporal dependencies and short transient structures with linear complexity. The model is trained only on normal background acoustic data and detects anomalous calving events through reconstruction error, thereby avoiding the need for large labeled datasets. Experiments were conducted on passive acoustic recordings collected by the NOAA NRS01 station during 2014–2015 at a sampling frequency of 5000 Hz. After 5 s segmentation, the dataset contained 97,869 background-noise samples and 2900 calving-event samples. Using 2900 background-noise samples and 2900 calving samples for testing, the proposed method achieved Precision = 0.9742, Recall = 0.8933, F1-score = 0.9319, and AUC = 0.9830, outperforming classical unsupervised detectors and strong deep-learning baselines, including Autoformer (AUC = 0.9121). Ablation studies further verify that both the multi-scale feature extraction and dynamic routing mechanism contribute substantially to detection performance. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides an effective and computationally efficient solution for long-term, real-time, autonomous monitoring of glacier calving activity in polar underwater environments.

Title: Machine learning integrated MIL-88B@ZIF-67 built-in electric field heterojunction nanozyme for enhanced colorimetric detection of ascorbic acid and alkaline phosphatase
Abstract: A MIL-88 B@ZIF-67 heterojunction nanozyme was rationally designed by adopting a MOF-on-MOF assembly strategy to boost catalytic performance through interfacial electronic structure modulation. Owing to the Fermi level difference between ZIF-67 and MIL-88 B, spontaneous electron transfer from ZIF-67 to MIL-88 B occurs upon interfacial contact, leading to the establishment of a built-in electric field that promotes charge separation and accelerates electron migration. As a result, MIL-88 B@ZIF-67 exhibits significantly enhanced peroxidase-like activity toward the oxidation of 3,3′,5,5′-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) in the presence of H<inf>2</inf>O<inf>2</inf>. Based on this feature, the developed colorimetric sensing platform enabled sensitive detection of ascorbic acid (AA) within a limit of detection (LOD) of 0.65 μM and a linearity of 1-82 μM. Furthermore, a cascade sensing system for alkaline phosphatase (ALP) was developed by exploiting its hydrolysis of ascorbic acid phosphate (AAP) into AA, affording a linear range from 0.5 U·L<sup>−1</sup> to 68 U L<sup>−1</sup> and a LOD of 0.23 U L<sup>−1</sup>. Machine learning analysis shows that the Random Forest-Support Vector Machine (RF–SVM) stacking model exhibits the best predictive performance and enables the reliable determination of AA and ALP in real samples.

Title: RIST-Net: A risk-aware spatiotemporal interaction and risk-guided multi-scale trend decoding network for vessel trajectory prediction
Abstract: Vessel trajectory prediction is a critical task for maritime traffic situational awareness, collision risk warning, and intelligent navigation decision-making. Existing AIS-based trajectory prediction methods have made considerable progress in temporal dependency modeling and spatial interaction learning. However, in complex multi-vessel traffic scenarios, the future motion of a target vessel is affected not only by its own historical states but also by the interaction risks posed by neighboring vessels and the temporal evolution of such risks. Most existing methods characterize inter-vessel relationships mainly based on geometric proximity or implicit attention mechanisms, making it difficult to explicitly distinguish the risk-driven effects of different neighboring vessels on the future motion of the target vessel. Meanwhile, short-term motion continuity, medium-term interaction responses, and long-term trend stability in long-horizon prediction have not yet been sufficiently modeled within a unified framework. To address these issues, this paper proposes a risk-aware spatiotemporal interaction and risk-guided multi-scale trend decoding network for vessel trajectory prediction, named RIST-Net. The proposed model jointly captures historical multi-vessel motion states, pairwise inter-vessel relation features, and historical interaction risk sequences within an end-to-end framework. In the interaction encoding stage, RIST-Net first employs a node temporal encoder to extract historical motion representations for each vessel, and then uses a risk-injected edge temporal encoder to integrate inter-vessel relation features with risk evolution information. Subsequently, an explicit risk bias is introduced into the risk-aware graph interaction layer, enabling high-risk neighboring vessels to receive greater attention during message aggregation. In the future prediction stage, a risk-guided multi-scale trend decoding module is designed to divide the prediction horizon into three consecutive stages, namely short-term, medium-term, and long-term stages. Scale weights are adaptively generated according to the historical interaction risk statistics of the target vessel, thereby improving trajectory trend consistency and final-position prediction accuracy over long horizons. Experimental results obtained from five repeated runs on three real-world AIS datasets show that RIST-Net achieves the best performance in terms of MAE, RMSE, ADE, FDE, and FD. Compared with the strongest competing result for each metric on each dataset, RIST-Net achieves average reductions of 4.73%, 7.44%, 4.15%, 5.01%, and 4.82% in these five metrics, respectively. Further scenario analyses across the three waterways demonstrate that RIST-Net generally maintains favorable prediction performance under typical encounter relationships and different interaction-risk levels, with more pronounced average advantages under Extreme-risk conditions, supporting its adaptability to complex multi-vessel traffic scenarios.

Title: A generalizable time-gated Raman spectroscopy–machine learning workflow for accurate identification of challenging plastics in electronic waste
Abstract: Electronic waste (E-waste), the fastest-growing solid waste stream, is projected to reach 82 million metric tons globally by 2030. E-waste plastics are difficult to sort due to diverse polymer compositions and the widespread use of pigments and other additives, which introduce complexity and/or strong fluorescence interference for spectroscopic based methods, especially for Raman spectroscopy. Raman spectroscopy coupled with machine learning (ML) has been explored for plastic identification, but its performance and applicability remain limited by the strong fluorescent backgrounds and reliance on small, instrument-specific datasets. In this study, we developed a generalizable analytical framework for accurate identification of the seven most common e-waste plastics (i.e., ABS, PS, PE, PP, PET, PC, PMMA) by integrating time-gated Raman spectroscopy, ML, and community-derived spectral libraries. Briefly, plastic spectra from open-source and our in-house libraries were standardized and combined to train ML models, which were subsequently validated on external data collected for real e-waste plastics obtained from a recycling facility. This ML-based workflow achieved higher identification accuracy compared with conventional correlation-based methods (i.e., 95% vs 66%), including for the dark plastics (i.e., 84% vs 52%), which have been challenging in previous studies. Beyond the improvement in identification performance, this study established a generalizable framework that enables integration and standardization of heterogeneous community-derived spectra for training robust ML models, providing a scalable, transferable and FAIR data principle-aligned solution for real-world e-waste plastic sorting.

Title: Noise-robust personalized keyword spotting via multi-task gradient compensation
Abstract: Personalized Keyword Spotting (PKWS) is a speech processing task that aims to detect predefined keywords spoken by enrolled speakers in audio streams. It inherently integrates two subtasks: Keyword Spotting (KWS) and Speaker Verification (SV). Although recent deep learning-based PKWS systems have demonstrated promising performance in relatively clean environments, achieving accurate PKWS in strong noisy environments remains a significant challenge. To address this issue, we propose a noise-robust personalized keyword spotting system, which consists of a Speech Enhancement (SE) module followed by two parallel branches for KWS and SV. This architecture enables simultaneous keyword detection and speaker verification in noisy environments. However, jointly optimizing multiple subtasks within a unified framework is challenging due to potential conflicts among their competing learning objectives. To mitigate this problem, we develop a novel Pareto-based multi-task gradient compensation algorithm that dynamically balances gradient updates across tasks, thereby reducing mutual interference and improving convergence efficiency. Extensive experiments on the Google Speech Commands dataset validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, achieving a speaker verification accuracy of 97.95% and a keyword detection accuracy of 92.23%. Furthermore, our model outperforms state-of-the-art multi-task gradient optimization methods across various Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) conditions, exhibiting strong robustness and superior generalization ability for real-world applications in complex acoustic environments.

Title: FastNano Liquid: An Automated Platform for Small-Angle X-ray Scattering-Based Materials Discovery
Abstract: Despite recent progress in machine learning for materials research, a persistent bottleneck is the generation of large, high-quality datasets to train models. Here, we present a laboratory-based small- and wide-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS/WAXS) platform designed for combined synthesis and characterization of (nano)materials. The platform is constructed around an automated SAXS/WAXS instrument coupled with several reactor systems in three different workflows: batch, screening, and continuous flow. The batch workflow allows mL- to L-scale syntheses to be monitored online and in situ under controlled temperature, pH, and reactant injection. The screening workflow uses a liquid-handling robot to perform syntheses in standard reservoirs and microwell plates, which are passed to the SAXS instrument for high-throughput at-line ex situ analysis. The continuous flow workflow enables reactions to be monitored inline and in situ within microfluidic or millifluidic systems by SAXS/WAXS, UV–vis, and/or Raman spectroscopy. Additionally, a spray deposition and laser annealing workflow is presented to enable the preparation and at-line ex situ characterization of functional thin films from nanomaterial suspensions. We characterize the general performance of the platform and then present a case study for each workflow, illustrating its potential for accelerating materials discovery with future autonomous and machine learning-based methods.

Title: From Divergent Guidelines to Delphi-Ready Items: Tutorial for Large Language Model-Assisted Guideline Harmonization Using Penile Cancer as a Worked Example
Abstract: Background: Clinical practice guidelines are central instruments of evidence-based care; yet, in many domains, particularly rare or complex diseases, multiple guidelines coexist and frequently offer conflicting advice. Existing strategies for resolving such divergences are often labor-intensive, opaque, and insufficiently reproducible. Objective: This tutorial aimed to develop and demonstrate a reproducible workflow for transforming divergent clinical guideline recommendations and literature-derived white areas into human-reviewed Delphi-ready candidate items. Methods: Following a step-by-step tutorial structure, we demonstrate the workflow using penile cancer as a worked example. The process comprises manual selection of clinical guidelines, a systematic PubMed search for literature-derived candidate issues potentially unaddressed by the selected guidelines, selection of 3 complementary large language models (LLMs), and execution of predefined prompts, multimodal recommendation extraction, semantic harmonization, and item-level guideline stance classification. The evaluative process combines a 3-LLM ensemble consistency check with an independent pre-Delphi appraisal by 4 penile cancer experts using a predefined 5-point suitability scale and acceptance threshold. Results: In the worked example in the field of penile cancer as a high-stakes use case, the workflow extracted 157 clinical recommendations from 5 guidelines and consolidated them into 68 harmonized guideline-derived items. Stance classification identified 15 uniformly supported items and 53 divergent, ambiguous, or incompletely addressed items. In parallel, literature processing generated 95 harmonized white-area items, of which 9 were classified as true white-area items not addressed by the included guidelines. The final methodological output was a set of 62 human-reviewed Delphi-ready candidate items for subsequent clinical consensus voting. Conclusions: This methodology provides a scalable, transparent, and transferable approach for identifying and structuring interguideline inconsistencies and evidence gaps. By combining LLM-assisted analysis with independent external expert appraisal, it supports the reproducible transformation of heterogeneous guideline content into Delphi-ready candidate items.

Title: Synthetic training enables markerless 3D instrument tracking for intraoperative optical coherence tomography
Abstract: This work experimentally demonstrates automatic optical 3D tracking of target areas of interest within wide-field digital stereoscope imagery to guide high-resolution intraoperative optical coherence tomography (iOCT) acquisition in real time. Eye surgeries such as cataract surgery are among the most commonly performed surgeries in the world and require precise visualization, especially in the axial dimension. By enabling unparalleled axial sensitivity, iOCT has emerged as a leading modality to enhance surgical visualization of the eye. However, current iOCT visualization of ophthalmic surgeries is limited by the small field of view (FOV) of OCT relative to that of the surgical microscope, requiring extensive manual realignment by a trained operator. We have developed an iOCT computer vision system that utilizes the built-in stereo microscope video feed to automatically align the OCT volume with the surgeon's tool tip in 3D, tracking over a wide FOV and without modifications to surgical tools. Furthermore, our system used a deep-learning detection model trained on a novel synthetic microscope image generation pipeline and annotated real images to create what is believed to be a new 3D tracking system that is both fast and accurate. We integrated this tracking system into a high-speed iOCT stereo microscope to acquire 3D tool-tip-aligned OCT volumes in real time. We demonstrated successful tracking performance by consistently positioning the iOCT volume ( x = 5mm, y = 5mm, and z = 7mm ) at the tool tip ( x = 0.72 ± 0.44mm, y = 0.78 ± 0.47mm, and z = 2.07 ± 1.43mm error) in testing with a motorized three-axis stage and by simulating ex vivo porcine eye cataract maneuvers with real surgical instruments. Our synthetic eye dataset pipeline and iOCT tracking system pave the way for more effective and usable visualization in eye surgery.

Title: Evaluating space-based methane detection through a one-year blind test
Abstract: Space-based remote sensing allows detection and monitoring of large, concentrated methane sources worldwide<sup>1</sup>. However, independent evaluation of instruments and algorithms is limited, and new satellites and artificial intelligence techniques have not been tested under controlled, single-blind conditions<sup>2</sup>. Here we conduct a year-long, single-blind test involving 746 events: 481 methane releases of 9.5–1,183.7 kg h<sup>−1</sup> and 265 blank controls. We released metered methane quantities in Arizona, USA, coinciding with overpasses from 12 government, commercial and non-profit satellites. Fifteen analysis teams from nine countries generated more than 2,250 estimates, making this, to our knowledge, the largest controlled test so far and one of the first evaluations of the instruments EMIT, Tanager-1 (Carbon Mapper) and GHOSt. Performance is heterogeneous: ‘built-for-purpose’ instruments designed to target methane demonstrate excellent detection performance (92–100% true positive rate, 0–11% false positive rate) and quantification accuracy (slope 0.83–1.00, 44% mean absolute percentage error). Instruments repurposed for methane sensing perform more variably (detection rates 62–88%, 46% mean absolute percentage error); still, many demonstrate significant skill. Broad land scanners detect poorly at tested rates but have consistent global coverage and historical archives, motivating additional work. Artificial intelligence-based methods show promise, but caution is warranted; 79% of false positives emerge from these methods. Ground-measured cloud cover >20% degraded performance across systems, raising concerns for use in some locations. Our findings show that satellite-based measurements can achieve accurate detection and quantification of methane point sources when the source location is approximately known.

Title: Augmented Transformer framework for quantification of PM2.5 chemical composition via one-step laser desorption/ionization single particle aerosol mass spectrometry (LDI-SPAMS)
Abstract: Fine particulate matter (PM<inf>2.5</inf>) significantly affects the environment and public health. Single particle aerosol mass spectrometry (SPAMS) provides real-time, size-resolved, and particle-resolved chemical characterization of atmospheric particles, while quantitative analysis of PM<inf>2.5</inf> species from SPAMS signals remains a major challenge due to matrix effects, shot-to-shot variability and nonlinear instrument responses from the inherent limitations of one-step laser desorption/ionization (LDI) process. Here we propose an Augmented Transformer framework to quantify hourly PM<inf>2.5</inf> species relative mass fractions from temporally aggregated single-particle mass spectra and concurrent meteorological covariates. The model was trained and evaluated on a long-term dataset collected in Guangzhou, China, comprising 595,339 valid single-particle mass spectra co-located with bulk measurements and atmospheric monitoring. Our model achieved an overall test-set R<sup>2</sup> of 0.62 across all 15 species, with R<sup>2</sup> > 0.70 for chloride, nitrate, Na<sup>+</sup> and K<sup>+</sup>, and substantially outperformed evaluated baselines including tree-based ensemble models and some neural networks. Ablation experiments confirmed the complementary contributions of particle-resolved spectral inputs and meteorological conditioning. Integrated gradients (IG) identified temperature, relative humidity, NO<inf>2</inf>, and O<inf>3</inf> as dominant atmospheric drivers, with attribution patterns consistent with established aerosol chemistry. Prototype-level analysis revealed spectral signatures matching known SPAMS marker ions for major species. Temporal reconstruction across heterogeneous atmospheric regimes demonstrated consistent composition tracking within the long-term measurement campaign. This study advances SPAMS from a predominantly qualitative tool toward an interpretable and quantitative framework for PM<inf>2.5</inf> composition analysis.

Title: Interpretable machine learning for one-year mortality prediction in acute aortic dissection: a multimodal model integrating CT imaging features and electrocardiographic parameters
Abstract: Background: To address the high mortality rate of aortic dissection (AD) and the limitations of existing prognostic tools, this study aimed to develop an interpretable machine learning (ML) model combining CT imaging features and electrocardiographic (ECG) parameters to predict 1-year mortality. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 834 of 907 screened AD patients from January 2019 to August 2023 after excluding 73 patients with incomplete CT or ECG data. Sixty-three features were extracted, including demographics, vital signs, laboratory tests, CT imaging, and ECG parameters. Patients were randomly divided into training (n = 583) and validation (n = 251) cohorts. Key predictors were selected using LASSO regression. Six ML models, including Logistic Regression, Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM), and XGBoost, were trained and optimized. Model performance was evaluated using Brier score, AUC, AUC-PR, and SHAP analysis. A web calculator was developed for clinical use. Results: The 1-year mortality rate was 18.94%. The GBM model showed superior overall performance (AUC: 0.892, Brier score: 0.101, AUC-PR: 0.710). SHAP analysis identified top predictors such as CT-ascending aortic involvement, CT-intramural hematoma, age, serum creatinine, and diastolic blood pressure. Patients were stratified into high- and low-risk groups, with observed 1-year mortality rates of 49.40% and 4.17%, respectively. Conclusions: The multimodal GBM model showed robust discrimination and clinically meaningful risk separation for 1-year mortality in acute AD. CT-ascending aortic involvement, CT-intramural hematoma, age, serum creatinine, and diastolic blood pressure emerged as key contributors, supporting individualized risk stratification through the web calculator.

Title: Morphological saliency prior-guided band-aware multi-modal disease diagnostic fusion network for vibrational spectroscopy
Abstract: Multimodal vibrational spectroscopy provides a powerful biochemical probe for non-invasive clinical diagnosis. However, when mapping high-dimensional spectral features, existing deep neural networks are highly susceptible to overfitting high-variance noise, including baseline drift and amorphous broadband signals. Because underlying physicochemical constraints are rarely incorporated into representation learning, such diagnostically driven paradigms often lack prior-based interpretability, thereby limiting their reliability in complex medical decision-making. Here, we propose a Morphological Saliency Prior-guided Band-aware multimodal fusion network, termed MSPBA. In contrast to previous studies on spectral disease diagnosis that primarily emphasize multimodal fusion architectures or improvements in classification performance, our work focuses on constructing a Morphological Saliency Prior jointly defined by peak prominence, full width at half maximum and local residual fluctuations. This prior is embedded into both the model input and the early feature-extraction stage, enabling the network to preferentially attend to physically reliable spectral bands during the learning of high-dimensional serum spectral representations. By transforming spectral regions with both high response intensity and narrow peak width into prior masks, the proposed framework guides the neural network towards highly ordered core bands at the early stage of feature extraction, thereby reducing interference from complex broadband noise from a physicochemically informed perspective. In addition, we designed a lightweight band-aware synergy module to adaptively capture complementary feature associations across modalities. Validation on two clinical serum cohorts comprising more than 570 cases, collected from different hospital sources, instrument platforms and spectral dimensionalities, demonstrated that MSPBA achieved strong diagnostic performance and cross-cohort stability in both three-class thyroid tumour classification and binary thyroid dysfunction classification. Specifically, the model achieved an accuracy of 97.97% and an AUC of 0.9961 in the thyroid tumour cohort, and an accuracy of 97.62% and an AUC of 0.9938 in the thyroid dysfunction cohort. Furthermore, MSPBA enabled physically prior-matched band identification for interpretability analysis. By incorporating spectroscopic prior knowledge into the representation-learning process, this study improves the classification performance of multimodal spectral diagnostic models in complex classification tasks, while enhancing discriminative stability and feature interpretability across distinct clinical diagnostic settings.

Title: Disentangled variational information bottleneck with hyper-cluster for few-shot class-incremental audio classification
Abstract: Few-shot class-incremental audio classification (FCAC) presents a significant challenge of adapting models to sequentially arriving novel classes using scarce data while preserving base knowledge. Existing approaches often struggle with the stability-plasticity trade-off due to two primary limitations: feature entanglement and prototype bias. To address these issues, a robust framework, disentangled variational information bottleneck with hyper-cluster (VIB-D-HC), is proposed. First, to enhance stability, a disentangled variational information bottleneck (VIB-D) backbone is developed. By establishing an adversarial minimax game via a gradient reversal layer (GRL), VIB-D explicitly filters out nuisance style factors while retaining compact, class-discriminative semantics in the latent space. Second, to improve plasticity under data sparsity, a hyper-cluster (HC) strategy is designed to construct dense feature manifolds via Mixup-based convex hull interpolation. Finally, a nonparametric local metric inference mechanism is employed to perform robust matching against these augmented manifolds. Extensive experiments on the LS-100 (Speech) and NSynth-100 (Music) benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves state-of-the-art performance. Notably, it reaches a peak average accuracy (AA) of 96.53% on the texture-rich NSynth-100 dataset, while restricting the performance drop rate (PD) to merely 5.29% on LS-100. Complexity analysis further confirms that the framework achieves zero incremental parameter updates, making it highly viable for real-time intelligent edge audio applications. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/keyonghu/VIB-D-HC.

Title: Multimodal emotion recognition using hybrid deep learning architecture
Abstract: Multimodal emotion recognition plays a crucial role in advancing human-computer interaction through understanding of emotions. By combining Electroencephalogram (EEG) signals and audio data, Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies process cognitive information. The fusion of EEG and audio signals bridges the divide between machine performance and the complexity of human emotions, enabling the development of responsive artificial systems. The central challenge for researchers is building models that can effectively decode emotions from both signals. In this paper, a novel Multimodal Emotion Recognition system using a Spatial Pyramid Pooling-based LeNet (MER-SPP-LNet) model is proposed. The proposed MER-SPP-LNet system processes the augmentation of both the EEG signals and audio for emotion classification. First, the preprocessing step removes noise, in which EEG signals use Modified Amplitude-assisted Complete Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition with Adaptive Noise (MA-CEEMDAN), while audio signals are normalized. In feature extraction process, EEG features are derived using S-transform and Common Spatial Patterns (CSP), while audio features use Enhanced Magnitude Square updated Power Normalized Cepstral Coefficients (EMS-PNCC). After the feature extraction process, the extracted features are subjected to feature selection step to reduce dimensionality of the feature set using the Principal Component Analysis (PCA) technique. Finally, the emotion recognition step classifies the emotions, which involves two classifiers, such as GhostNet and Spatial Pyramid Pooling-based LeNet (SPP-LNet). Finally, the system outputs classified emotions using a soft voting mechanism that improves the recognition accuracy through multimodal integration. The MER-SPP-LNet achieved superior performance compared to traditional approaches with peak accuracy (0.958), specificity (0.975) and NPV (0.976).

Title: Preliminary Study on the Application of the Lights-out Laboratories in Water Quality Monitoring
Abstract: The sample analysis work of traditional environmental monitoring laboratories mainly re-⁃ lies on manual operation. This mode has such prominent problems as long analysis cycle， low effi-⁃ ciency，significant influence by the operators，and high susceptibility to accidental errors，making it difficult to meet the demand for high-throughput and high-precision analysis in modern environmen-⁃ tal monitoring. Existing assembly-line lights-out laboratories have achieved automation，yet are constrained by fixed workflows，resulting in shortcomings such as insufficient system flexibility，low resource utilization，and limited functional scalability. Lights-out laboratories based on a flexible architecture are highly compatible with standard classical monitoring methods. By imitating manual experimental procedures，the hardware system is decomposed into standardized functional units，forming a software and hardware system featuring unified management，flexible interconnection， and multisystem coordination. Through dynamic adjustment of functional units and scheduling of machine time，such laboratories effectively break through the dual constraints of testing indicators and physical space，with the technical advantages of strong system flexibility，high resource utilization， and excellent scalability. A water-⁃quality lights-out laboratory was constructed using the flexible architecture，and verification was performed on seven typical inorganic water-⁃quality indicators selected according to experimental procedures. The results show that the laboratory achieves closed-⁃loop automation of the entire testing process，with all performance indicators complying with current standards. The large-scale application of flexible-architecture lights-out laboratories is still restricted by factors including insufficient digitalization of pretreatment equipment and closed measurement and control software of testing instruments. The development of intelligent agents for instrument operation and the establishment of crossdomain resource sharing models will become the key breakthroughs and development directions for this technology.

Title: A low-cost room-temperature electronic nose prototype for gas sensor characterization and simulated breath analysis
Abstract: This work addresses the need for cost-effective and scalable platforms for chemiresistive gas-sensor characterization and exhaled breath (EB) analysis, as conventional laboratory instruments are often expensive and complex. A low-cost, room-temperature electronic nose (E-nose) prototype, termed the E-nose tester, was developed as a versatile platform for multichannel signal acquisition, sensor characterization, and data analysis. The system enables stable signal acquisition and reliable evaluation of key sensing parameters, including response, repeatability, and detection limit. To validate the platform, three PANI-based gas sensors (PANI, PANI/Au, and PANI/Ag) fabricated via a vapor phase polymerization method were systematically tested. The developed platform demonstrates stable sensing performance, low detection limits, and good repeatability while maintaining substantially lower hardware cost than conventional laboratory instruments. To further demonstrate its applicability, the E-nose tester was extended to simulated EB analysis experiments using ammonia, a volatile compound frequently reported as chronic kidney disease related breath biomarker. Simulated breath samples with different ammonia levels were analyzed using feature extraction and machine learning methods. The results demonstrated the feasibility of integrating the proposed platform with pattern-recognition workflows for simulated EB analysis scenarios. Overall, the proposed system provides a low-cost and scalable solution for chemiresistive gas-sensing research, E-nose development, and future EB analysis studies.

Title: Photometric Redshift Estimation via a Spectra-guided Gaussian Mixture Density Framework
Abstract: Accurate and computationally efficient photometric redshift estimation is essential for cosmological analyses and studies of the large-scale structure of the Universe. However, applying existing template-fitting and machine learning methods to rapidly growing survey data sets can involve trade-offs between predictive performance and computational throughput. Moreover, feature extractors developed for natural images may not be well suited to the sparse, source-centered, and multiband characteristics of galaxy images. We present PRISM (Photometric Redshift Estimation via a Spectra-guided Gaussian Mixture Density Framework), a multimodal framework that jointly exploits multiband image cutouts and catalog-level photometric measurements. PRISM incorporates feature-extraction modules tailored to source-centered astronomical images and a dedicated fusion module that captures complementary information from the imaging and tabular modalities. During training, a frozen spectral encoder provides an auxiliary representation-alignment objective, encouraging selected photometric features to retain information associated with galaxy spectra without requiring spectroscopic data at inference time. A Gaussian-mixture density head models the conditional redshift distribution, enabling PRISM to produce a full predictive probability density function in addition to a point estimate. We evaluated PRISM through five-fold cross-validation on 1.98 million galaxies constructed from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument Data Release 1 and the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys. Within this benchmark, PRISM reduces the mean absolute error and catastrophic-outlier fraction by 17.1% and 20.0%, respectively, relative to the best baseline value for each metric. Our PRISM ablations showed that combining multiband images with catalog flux measurements improved predictive performance relative to either input alone. Spectra-guided supervision provided a smaller additional gain in the full multimodal configuration. The code and data catalog are publicly available at https://github.com/qintianjian-lab/PRISM.

Title: A multi-atlas ensemble learning framework for autism spectrum disorder diagnosis
Abstract: Objective. Clinical autism spectrum disorder (ASD) relies on subjective scales and neuroimaging, with traditional approaches suffering from high subjectivity and insufficient feature extraction, increasing misdiagnoses risk. Approach. To improve the diagnostic accuracy, we propose a multimodal ASD prediction network (APN) that integrates resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging with non-imaging data. Algorithmically, we first introduce a novel cumulative distribution divergence score (CDDS) feature selection method based on the multi-atlas functional connectivity (FC), which quantifies statistical distributional differences between positive and negative samples, effectively addressing the limitations of the traditional F-score in overlapping or weakly discriminative features. Building upon this, we adapt existing deep learning (DL) paradigms to construct a deep neural architecture (variational autoencoder-denoising autoencoder (VAEA)), combining a variational autoencoder (VAE), a denoising autoencoder, and a multilayer perceptron. The combination of these modules is non-trivial: the novel CDDS first purifies the high-dimensional feature space, enabling the VAEA to learn robust latent probabilistic representations via unsupervised pre-training without suffering from the curse of dimensionality. This is followed by the supervised fine-tuning to optimize parameters. We further incorporate demographic factors including age, full-scale intelligence quotient, and gender via a late-fusion strategy to prevent them from being overshadowed by imaging features, thereby enhancing the discriminability. FC features from three atlases including AAL, CC400, and Dosenbach160 are weighted and integrated to achieve the effective multi-source fusion. Main results. We conduct 10-fold cross-validations on the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE) dataset, and the proposed APN achieves 81.63% accuracy, 81.89% sensitivity and 81.46% specificity, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art methods. Interpretability analysis identifies hippocampus, amygdala, and cingulate gyrus as strongly ASD-associated regions, offering neural mechanistic insights. Significance. This study provides an efficient, objective, and interpretable multimodal DL framework for ASD assisted diagnosis, with substantial clinical application and neuroscience value.

Title: Effective scale-adaptive deep residual learning method for multi-object velocity measurement in normal intersection surveillance
Abstract: With advances in measurement instruments, multi-object velocity measurement using traffic cameras constitutes a crucial component of traffic analysis in normal intersection surveillance scenes. However, certain small-scale traffic objects pose challenges in terms of detection and tracking, potentially undermining the accuracy of multi-object velocity measurement. In this paper, we present an effective scale-adaptive deep residual learning method for assisting multi-object velocity measurement in normal intersection surveillance scenes. The method builds upon residual structures to enhance feature extraction, presents a dual-stage attention mechanism to refine feature representations, and constructs a multi-level feature fusion structure to enrich semantic context. Experiments are conducted to evaluate the performance of the presented method. In velocity measurement, the presented method can achieve root mean square deviation (RMSD) values of 0.93 meters per second for estimating instantaneous speeds and 0.91 meters per second for estimating average crossing speeds, with the efficiency of 37.7 frames per second. Additionally, the RMSD values are 0.92 meters per second and 0.91 meters per second for cars, 0.99 meters per second and 0.94 meters per second for persons, as well as 0.97 meters per second and 0.92 meters per second for bicycles, with each pair pertaining to instantaneous speed and average crossing speed, respectively. Experimental results demonstrate that the presented method enables velocity measurement of small-scale traffic objects and supports multi-object velocity measurement in normal intersection surveillance scenes.

Title: Fear-EEG-AI: A Conceptual and Operational Framework for Designing EEG-AI Systems for the Inference of Fear-Compatible Neurophysiological States
Abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) and artificial intelligence (AI) are central tools in affective computing, yet fear-related inference remains constrained by a gap between experimental performance and deployable evidence: high accuracy on controlled datasets guarantees neither neurobiological specificity, nor robustness across users, nor traceable inference. Title: Explainability-Guided Multimodal Optimization for Arabic Music Genre Classification
Abstract: Classifying Arabic music genres is a challenging task because Arabic music encompasses a wide range of rhythms, melodies, and musical structures. Multimodal learning combines complementary information from multiple representations to improve classification; however, it can produce new feature spaces with potentially weak or redundant dimensions that can adversely affect classification performance. Explainable AI methods such as SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) are usually used after model training for interpretation, yet they are not often used to improve the training process itself. In this work, we propose an explainability-guided evolutionary optimization method for audio–symbolic Arabic music genre classification. First, Genetic Algorithm (GA), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), and Evolution Strategy (ES) are applied directly to the original fused representations to establish optimization-only baselines. Next, the framework uses global SHAP importance values and transforms them into bounded continuous feature weights, assigning higher weights to the most informative dimensions. A validation-guided pruning step is then performed to remove low-importance dimensions only when their removal improves validation performance. The resulting representation is used for evolutionary classifier hyperparameter optimization. Experiments are conducted on 1800 aligned audio–symbolic pairs from six Arabic music genres. Under the matched per-seed optimization protocol, the validation-selected SHAP-refined CNN14+BERT system achieved 95.30% mean accuracy, compared with 94.40% for the corresponding optimization-only control. Title: Forecasting futures settlement returns with LSTM for options trading strategies
Abstract: Algorithmic trading has traditionally centered on investment portfolios and asset pricing research, largely overlooking the potential of options in trading strategies. However, options present unique advantages as financial instruments, offering risk management and strategic opportunities based on market trends. This paper introduces a novel approach for options trading by integrating long short-term memory (LSTM) and Monte Carlo Simulation (MCS) with the options spread strategy to estimate the expected value and achieve positive long-term returns. Title: Examining Artificial Intelligence Literacy among Music Students in Higher Education: A Causal-Comparative Approach
Abstract: This study analyzes the artificial intelligence (AI) literacy levels of music education students and explores how future music educators perceive and integrate AI tools within creative and instructional contexts. The research group consisted of 143 students enrolled in music education programs from different faculties, such as Education, Fine Arts, and Conservatory. Participants were selected through a purposeful sampling technique, ensuring inclusion of individuals likely to encounter AI in educational and performance settings. The study employed a causal-comparative (ex post facto) design, which enables examination of naturally existing groups differing in characteristics such as prior exposure to or familiarity with AI technologies. Quantitative data were analyzed to compare students’ AI literacy levels across demographic variables, including gender, type of high school graduated from, academic achievement level, and prior knowledge of AI. However, it was determined that the artificial intelligence literacy level of music teacher candidates who have knowledge about artificial intelligence programmes and use artificial intelligence programmes in music education is significant. Results indicated that students’ AI literacy levels were at a medium level. No significant differences were found in AI literacy by gender, type of high school graduated from, academic achievement, or frequency of internet use. However, significant differences were observed among students from different faculties, as well as among those who had prior knowledge of AI programs, used AI applications in music and music education, and used them more frequently. These findings suggest that direct engagement with AI tools contributes to higher literacy levels.

Title: Artificial Intelligence–Based Computer Vision Feedback to Improve Clinical Performance in Surgical Technology Education
Abstract: Introduction: Advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) and computer vision offer new opportunities to improve clinical skills training. This study developed a real-time, AI-based computer vision system for detecting surgical instruments and evaluated its association with clinical performance among surgical technology students. Methods: A quasi-experimental pre-test/post-test study with a control group was conducted among 48 eligible surgical technology students at Iran University of Medical Sciences during the 2025–2026 academic year. Participants who met the predefined inclusion criteria were enrolled using census sampling. Following ethics approval (IR.IUMS. REC.1403.928), the participants were allocated to an intervention group (n=31), which received immediate AI-generated visual feedback after each instrument arrangement task, and a control group (n=17), which received routine instructor-led training without AI feedback. A YOLOv8-based deep learning model was trained using transfer learning on annotated images of surgical table setups. Clinical performance was assessed using a validated observational checklist (CVI=0.90; Cronbach’s α=0.87). Data were analyzed using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, Spearman’s correlation, and the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) in SPSS version 27. All 48 participants completed the study (attrition rate=0%). Results: The AI model achieved excellent object detection performance (precision=0.974, recall=0.979, mAP@0.5=0.981, mAP@0.5:0.95=0.808), with an average inference time of 1.6 seconds per image. Clinical performance was significantly higher following AI-assisted feedback (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, Z=−4.879, p<0.001, r=0.88). After adjustment for baseline performance using ANCOVA, AI-assisted feedback was associated with higher post-intervention performance scores than conventional training (F (1,45)=19.51, p<0.001, partial η²=0.302). Excellent agreement was observed between AI-generated assessments and expert human ratings (ICC=0.984). Conclusions: Real-time, AI-based computer vision feedback was associated with improved surgical instrument arrangement performance among surgical technology students while providing an objective and reliable assessment of practical skills. The proposed system represents a promising proof-of-concept educational tool for simulation-based training and competency assessment and may complement conventional instructional approaches in surgical technology education.

Title: Decoding the Anxiety Burden in Asia and Developing an XGBoost-Based Online Screening Tool Using Korean Data
Abstract: Anxiety disorders impose a substantial burden across Asia, yet comprehensive regional surveillance remains limited. In addition, the utility of the Health-Related Quality of Life Instrument with 8 Items (HINT-8) for anxiety screening in the Korean population has not been fully clarified. This study integrated data from Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 and Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (KNHANES) to comprehensively assess the prevalence, incidence, and disability-adjusted life year (DALY) rates of Anxiety disorders across 48 Asian countries and territories from 1990 to 2021. Joinpoint regression, age-period-cohort modelling, decomposition analysis, and health inequality indices were employed to analyse trends and driving factors. In the Korean dataset, eight machine learning algorithms were compared. SHAP analysis was used to interpret the results, and the best-performing model was ultimately developed into an online prediction model. In 2021, Asia accounted for over half of global anxiety cases, and age-standardized rates increased by 14.6%–17.1% since 1990. After 2019, incidence (APC = 9.532%) and DALY rates (APC = 9.157%) rose sharply. Burden patterns varied by sex and age, and population growth was a major driver. In the Korean dataset, XGBoost showed the best performance (AUC = 0.894). An 8-feature parsimonious model performed comparably to the 17-feature model while improving interpretability and practical feasibility. Asia's growing anxiety burden demands prioritised care for women, adolescents, and middle-aged populations and better crisis mental health services. A Korean machine-learning tool shows potential but requires broader Asian validation.

Title: Machine-learning-guided inverse design of Anderson localization in one-dimensional chains with multi-scale correlated disorder
Abstract: Abstract: We study localization control in a one-dimensional tight-binding chain with diagonal disorder whose spatial correlations are governed by one or two exponential length scales. The main objective is not only to characterize localization, but to develop an interpretable machine-learning framework for inverse design: given a desired transport or localization behavior, the method identifies disorder profiles that realize it. We compare three disorder ensembles: uncorrelated disorder, single-scale exponentially correlated disorder, and a two-scale correlated ensemble with correlation function C(r)=a1e-r/ξ1+a2e-r/ξ2, where a1+a2=1. Exact diagonalization is used to compute central-window eigenstate observables, including the participation ratio normalized by system size, PR/N, and the localization length normalized by system size, ℓloc/N. Even with a second, independently tunable correlation scale, we find no signature of a genuine localization-delocalization transition: dedicated finite-size scaling up to N=1024 shows no size-independent crossing point, so the correlation-length and weight dependence remains a smooth, monotonic crossover throughout the exponential-correlation family rather than a critical phenomenon. A central outcome of the work is a machine-learning surrogate and inverse-design workflow. An ensemble ExtraTrees regressor learns the mapping from disorder parameters and system size to the normalized logarithmic observables, achieving R2≈0.98 on held-out data for the two targets (R2≈0.980 for the normalized participation ratio and R2≈0.979 for the normalized localization length; Sect. 3). The surrogate provides smooth interpolation of the high-dimensional parameter space, uncertainty estimates, SHAP-based feature attribution, and a fast inverse-design search for disorder profiles that maximize localization (the framework is equally applicable to a delocalization objective, though only the localization-maximizing search is reported here). The analysis shows that the scaled correlation lengths and the disorder-weight asymmetry are the dominant controls on transport, and that the strongest localization is realized by short-range-dominated disorder at the edge of the sampled correlation-length range, consistent with the general expectation that weakly correlated disorder localizes most strongly. This combination of exact diagonalization, interpretable machine learning, and inverse design establishes a practical framework for designing and controlling localization in low-dimensional quantum systems. Title: SAMURAI: Runtime Attack Detection in AI Accelerators Using AI Performance Counters
Abstract: AI accelerators, which improve performance for diverse AI tasks are becoming increasingly vulnerable to different adversarial attacks. These attacks, particularly Evasion attacks, introduce small, imperceptible perturbations to input data, leading to incorrect model predictions. Detecting such attacks is challenging because of their subtle nature. To address this, we propose SAMURAI, a framework designed for run-time attack detection in AI accelerators. SAMURAI features an array of AI Performance Counters (APCs) to monitor the dynamic behavior of AI models, in the same way as Hardware Performance Counters (HPCs) count hardware-related activities in modern microprocessors. It also integrates a lightweight on-chip Machine Learning (ML) engine, called TANTO (Trained Anomaly Inspection through Trace Observation). The APCs track low-level hardware events during AI processing, while TANTO concurrently analyzes these data to detect security threats and ensure secure AI usage. This approach enables run-time identification of potential threats without relying on traditional software-based methods. The study applies various adversarial attacks to both image and audio signals to assess the robustness of AI models. For audio data, both raw audio data and their 2D Mel-spectrogram representations are examined. Experimental results on image and audio datasets demonstrate that the proposed system excels in both accuracy and resilience against adversarial attacks. SAMURAI achieves a detection accuracy of 98% with minimal overhead, consumes less than 3% of the total energy, incurs less than 4% area overhead, and has a latency of 10% over the original inference time. The source code for SAMURAI is publicly available on GitHub.<sup>1</sup><sup>1</sup>https://github.com/habiburiit/SAMURAI-Defense.

Title: Edge seismic phase picking: Model distillation for multimodal early-warning systems
Abstract: Seismic monitoring is entering a high data volume, multimodal sensing regime driven by dense sensor deployments, including micro-electro-mechanical systems arrays, large-N (100s–1000s) Nodal arrays, distributed acoustic sensing, and other geophysical instruments. Machine learning models, with appropriate tuning and calibration, are capable of achieving close to expert-level performance in seismic detection and phase picking. The emerging operational challenge is how to scale that machine intelligence across future multimodal sensing networks. Effective incorporation of these capabilities remains constrained by telemetry bandwidth, centralized computation architectures, and communication latency. Here, we present XiaoNet, a proof-of-concept edge machine learning architecture for seismicity monitoring based on a simple system principle: perform first-pass inference near the sensor and transmit concise metadata rather than continuous streams. Using knowledge distillation, we compress a state-of-the-art PhaseNet model by over 93% into XiaoNet, a 240 KB model designed for edge deployment, while preserving strong phase-picking performance across datasets. Deployment on a Raspberry Pi 5 shows sub-millisecond inference latency for 30-s 3-channel waveform windows. By shifting inference to the edge and transmitting concise event metadata payloads, the framework demonstrated the potential for edge inference to reduce communication latency. Substituting an event metadata message payload for continuous raw waveform stream largely mitigates the dominant source of variable telemetry delay under moderate to heavy load. This result supports a feasible architecture in which edge inference devices complements centralized observatories, potentially improving resilience and response speed for seismic monitoring and may extend to future multimodal subsurface and infrastructure sensing systems.

Title: Tool wear classification using compact language models with multi-scale filter bank extractor and low-rank adaptation
Abstract: Tool wear monitoring is essential for predictive maintenance and machining efficiency, yet existing deep learning approaches often rely on large, computationally intensive models that limit deployment in real-world industrial settings. This paper presents a novel architecture utilizing compact pre-trained large language models (LLMs) for tool wear classification from acceleration and cutting force signals. The proposed framework integrates a Multi-Scale Filter Bank Extractor with squeeze-and-excitation attention mechanisms to capture implicit temporal representations, while explicitly encoding statistical signal descriptors through prompt engineering enabling joint multimodal reasoning within the LLM embedding space. The experiments use the dataset, which was collected under varying cutting parameters using CK45 and RVS 304 stainless steel without cooling fluids. The objective is to classify tool conditions into two labels, safe and unsafe, based on a predefined wear threshold. The data are stratified into training and test sets at an 80:20 ratio while preserving the wear-state distribution and operating conditions. A systematic evaluation of five compact LLM backbones (0.5B–1.7B parameters) demonstrates consistently strong performance, with the best result reaching 94.96% mean accuracy and a 94.89% mean weighted F1-score. To enable efficient fine-tuning, Low-Rank Adaptation is employed, reducing trainable parameters while preserving full fine-tuning quality. Ablation and embedding-space analyses show that the Multi-Scale Filter Bank Extractor and LLM contribute complementarily: the former provides robust feature extraction, while the latter improves class separability and prediction calibration. Within the evaluated setting, these results suggest that compact language models with parameter-efficient adaptation may be useful for tool wear monitoring.

Title: Machine learning algorithms for transplanting accelerometer observations in future satellite gravimetry missions
Abstract: Accurate and continuous monitoring of Earth’s gravity field is essential for tracking mass redistribution processes linked to climate variability, hydrological cycles, and geodynamic phenomena. While the GRACE and GRACE Follow-On (GRACE-FO) missions have set the benchmark for satellite gravimetry using low–low satellite-to-satellite tracking (LL-SST), the precision of gravity field recovery still strongly depends on the quality of accelerometer (ACC) performance. Traditional electrostatic accelerometers (EA) face limitations that can hinder mission outcomes, prompting exploration of advanced sensor technologies and data recovery techniques. This study presents a systematic evaluation of accelerometer data transplantation (i.e., the reconstruction and transfer of non-gravitational acceleration measurements between satellites) using novel accelerometer configurations, including Cold Atom Interferometry (CAI) accelerometers and hybrid EA-CAI setups, and applying both analytical and machine learning-based methods. Using comprehensive closed-loop LL-SST simulations, we compare four scenarios ranging from the conventional EA-only setup to ideal dual hybrid configurations, with a particular focus on the performance of transplant-based approaches using different neural network approaches. Our results show that the dual hybrid configuration provides the most accurate gravity field retrieval. However, the transplant-based hybrid setup, particularly when supported by machine learning (ML), emerges as a robust and cost-effective alternative, achieving comparable performance while significantly reducing the need for high-precision accelerometers across the constellation, thereby lowering mission costs and system complexity. These findings highlight the promise of combining quantum sensor technology and data-driven transplantation for future satellite gravimetry missions, paving the way for improved global monitoring of Earth’s dynamic gravity field.

Title: Exploring the added value of assimilating satellite altimeter measurements in a North Sea wave model using the Deterministic Ensemble Kalman Filter
Abstract: This study reports on the impact of assimilating satellite altimeter measurements with the Deterministic Ensemble Kalman Filter (DEnKF) using a regional SWAN wave model for the North Sea. We assimilated satellite altimeter measurements over a 3-month period (December 2021 - March 2022) from the following satellites: nadir CFOSAT, Haiyang-2B, Cryosat-2, Jason-3, Sentinel-3, Saral and Altika. The wind forcing is used as control variable to represent system uncertainty and a coarse resolution wave model was used for computational efficiency. Validation against independent wave and wind observations shows a significant performance increase. The assimilation improves predictions of significant wave height with a mean RMSE reduction of 20 %. Unlike most wave data assimilation approaches, the full wave spectrum is used as the state, resulting in automatic adjustment of the full wave spectra and other integral wave parameters. Hence, we also found improvements in mean wave period (10 %) and peak period (5%). Modest improvements in wind speed and direction are found for part of the stations. The DEnKF updates the wave spectrum indirectly through ensemble-based covariances, significant wave height observations and wind forcing. This is most effective in unimodal sea states, which we attribute to the assimilation of significant wave height only. The mean time difference between pass-overs is approximately 3 hours, ranging from within one hour to approximately 14 hours and 46 minutes. Our results indicate that the accuracy decreases when time gaps between satellite pass-overs increase. Effective spectrum-wide corrections, while assimilating significant wave height only, can potentially be achieved with an improved wave model, refining the wind noise model, assimilating other integral wave parameters and potentially extending the wind model beyond wind forcing. The results highlight the added benefit of assimilating satellite altimeter measurements in a regional wave model with a DEnKF using the wave spectrum as the state. To make this a viable approach for operational forecasting, a reduction of the memory and compute requirements are needed. Other potential applications are reanalyses of past wave states for studies of risk and climate change, and more recently training Machine Learning models.

Title: Ensemble Deep Architecture Trained on Selective Feature Set from Normalized Data for Stock Market Prediction
Abstract: Stock market prediction refers to forecasting the future price of a company’s shares or other financial instruments traded on an exchange. Accurately predicting these prices offers the potential for significant profits. However, developing a deep learning (DL) model for stock market forecasting is a challenging task. This is primarily due to the inherent volatility and non-linear patterns in market behavior, along with the limitations of historical data, which often fail to capture all the influencing factors. Additionally, the task becomes more complex because external events and investor sentiment can significantly affect market dynamics, further complicating the modeling process. Hence, this research introduces a novel Stock Market Price Prediction (SMP) model that enhances forecasting accuracy through a multi-phase approach comprising preprocessing, feature extraction, feature selection, and prediction stages. Initially, an adaptive Z-score normalization technique is employed for pre-processing the input data, which effectively standardizes the data, mitigating the impact of different data scales and improving the model’s overall performance. Subsequently, a set of technical indicators-based features, including Average True Range (ATR), Rate of Change (RoC), Relative Strength Index (RSI), Average Directional Movement Index (ADM), William’s %R (WILLR), Money Flow Index (MFI), and Triple Exponential Average (TRIX), are extracted from the preprocessed data to capture a comprehensive view of the market’s behavior. Then, the improved wrapper-filter model in the feature selection phase helps address the challenge of high-dimensionality by identifying and retaining only the most relevant features, thus reducing overfitting and enhancing model efficiency. Finally, the prediction phase leverages an ensemble deep learning model composed of an improved Attention-based SqueezeNet (IA-SQN), Deep Convolutional Neural Networks (DCNN), and GhostNet classifiers for producing the final predicted outcomes. The integration of these models allows the method to harness the strengths of each, improving prediction robustness and accuracy. Furthermore, the suggested model is evaluated against the traditional methods. From the analysis, the proposed EC (IA-SQN(Formula presented)GSNet(Formula presented)DCNN) attained less Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.466376, and Mean Squared Logarithmic Error (MSLE) of 0.004, which is exceptionally better than the traditional approaches. Therefore, the proposed method not only improves forecasting accuracy but also enhances decision-making and efficiency in trading operations.

Title: Direct Position Determination Based on a Two-Stage Deep Learning Model under Nonuniform Noise and Array Errors
Abstract: To address the performance degradation of direct position determination (DPD) algorithms caused by the strong coupling of nonuniform noise and array errors in a moving single-station scenario, this article proposes a two-stage deep learning (DL)-based direct localization method. The joint failure mechanism of these nonideal factors in the DPD method based on the multiple signal classification (MUSIC) algorithm, referred to as DPD-MUSIC, is first theoretically analyzed, demonstrating that the systematic position bias induced by subspace perturbation is difficult to effectively eliminate through analytical approaches. Building upon this analysis, the first stage designs a U-Net denoising network integrated with a convolutional block attention module (CBAM), which employs a real-imaginary decoupling strategy and a triple physics-informed loss function to suppress nonuniform noise and correct array errors. The second stage constructs a multiarchitecture fusion localization network that takes the denoised signal and the spatial position spectrum as dual-path inputs, and achieves subgrid multitarget localization through fractional label encoding and an improved binary cross-entropy (BCE) loss. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves significantly higher localization accuracy than multiple representative algorithms under both known and unknown target number scenarios, while exhibiting strong robustness against array errors and nonuniform noise.

Title: Performance evaluation of dual-mode vapor chamber for PEM fuel cell and machine learning assisted parameter optimization
Abstract: Thermal management System (TMS) plays a vital role in operational stability, enhancing performance and extending the life of proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFC). Vapor chambers (VC) are tremendously efficient passive heat spreaders that can handle high heat loads with low thermal resistance (R<inf>th</inf>). This experimental study presents thermal analysis and optimization of the VC for PEMFC TMS. The work has two primary focuses: (i) performance evaluation and optimization of the VC, and (ii) developing a novel dual-mode approach using a cooling block (CB) for maintaining optimal temperature in PEMFCs. Thermal performance of the VC is investigated under diverse operating conditions. The temperature uniformity index (TUI) of the proposed design demonstrated extremely uniform temperature ranging from 0.38 °C to 1.28 °C. The predictive models are developed through Response Surface Methodology (RSM) and Multi-layer Artificial Neural Network (ANN) to establish the optimum relationship in performance & parameters. The integrated ANN-Genetic Algorithm (ANN-GA) predicted the operating design parameters as the VC inclination angle 69.26°, coolant flow rate 2.00 LPM, and a load of 30.83 W corresponding to an R<inf>th</inf> of 0.04129 K/W. The dual-mode approach is integrated using CB to demonstrate simultaneous heating and cooling of PEMFC. Mainly two heating configurations are investigated: the top heating (TH) and bottom heating (BH), with the CB placed at the top and bottom of the VC, respectively. Among these configurations, the BH mode showed low R<inf>th</inf> with uniform temperature distribution, demonstrating its potential for simultaneous heating and cooling in fuel cell thermal management systems.

Title: Estimation of fine resolution LAI for forest ecosystems using Landsat reflectance and machine learning algorithms
Abstract: Leaf Area Index (LAI) is a crucial parameter for monitoring the vegetation dynamics. The spatial resolution of current remotely sensed LAI products limits their application in ecohydrological studies. The present study attempts to estimate fine resolution 30 m LAI based on Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) LAI and Landsat 7/Landsat 8 surface reflectance, vegetation indices and topographic data over a forested region. Three machine learning (ML) algorithms: Random Forest Regression (RFR), Artificial Neural Network (ANN), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) were adopted to estimate 30 m LAI in forested regions. A nested cross-validation strategy was used to optimize the model hyperparameters of the three ML algorithms. In the absence of ground truth data, global datasets comprising of LAI data from 9 BigFoot, 6 Validation of Land European Remote Sensing Instruments (VALERI), and 4 independent locations were used for validation. All models yielded comparable performance at 500 m resolution (RMSE: 0.62 m²/m², R²: 0.6). An inter-site comparison revealed that ML estimated 30 m LAI performed superior to MODIS LAI, with lowest RRMSE values ranging from 27 to 77% across different sites. The spatial variability analysis indicated that fine resolution LAI has an overall higher agreement and sub-pixel heterogeneity with the ground measurements as compared to MODIS LAI. The variations in Landsat image acquisition timing, associated cloud cover and vegetation type affected the accuracy of LAI estimation. The proposed data-driven framework can be useful in generating long term fine resolution LAI.

Title: A Machine Learning-Based Model of Three-Dimensional Ion Fluxes in the High-Altitude Earth's Northern Cusp
Abstract: Magnetic reconnection at the dayside magnetopause is the primary pathway for transferring mass, momentum, and energy from the solar wind into the terrestrial magnetosphere. Despite the abundance of in situ cusp observations from multiple space-based instruments, intermittent sampling spacecraft moving quickly along their trajectories precludes characterization of the cusp's global response to dynamic upstream drivers. This model is based on a residual neural network trained on solar wind parameters from NASA's OMNIWeb database, and ion flux measurements from the CIS/HIA instrument aboard ESA's Cluster mission. The model reproduces longitudinal and latitudinal displacements of the cusp under (Formula presented.) - and (Formula presented.) -dominated interplanetary magnetic field regimes, in close agreement with reconnection theory. To quantify uncertainty and evaluate performance, we use an ensemble of 100 identical networks with randomized training and validation splits, reserving a fixed test set shared by all models. The statistics indicate consistent predictions within the central cusp region. Also, we used Shapley Additive exPlanations to visualize input feature contributions to the model's outputs. Title: Quality of life and perceived care in Lynch syndrome: Associated factors and interpretable machine-learning classification
Abstract: Purpose To examine associations between pathogenic variant carrier status, cancer status, health-related quality of life (QoL), and perceived quality of care in Lynch syndrome, and to inform oncology nursing supportive care. Methods This cross-sectional study included 288 adults with Lynch syndrome carrying a pathogenic germline variant, with or without a history of cancer, and non-carrier relatives. Clinical and demographic data were extracted from medical records. QoL and perceived quality of care were assessed using validated instruments. Analyses included descriptive and inferential statistics, logistic regression, and supervised machine learning models (Decision Tree, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and Logistic Regression). Results Overall, 61.8% of participants were pathogenic variant carriers and 27.4% had a history of cancer, predominantly colorectal cancer. Carriers reported poorer QoL, with lower physical and cognitive functioning and greater symptom burden, particularly fatigue, insomnia, and pain. Participants with a history of cancer also showed poorer physical functioning than those without cancer (22.4 vs. 63.2; p < 0.001). Satisfaction with clinical care was high, whereas satisfaction with administrative services was lower. Logistic Regression showed the highest predictive performance (AUC = 0.826; accuracy = 80.4%). Physical functioning and family history of cancer were the strongest predictors of pathogenic variant carrier status. Conclusions Personalised supportive care is needed for individuals with Lynch syndrome. Oncology nurses play a key role in symptom assessment, patient education, psychosocial support, and care coordination. Supervised machine learning may complement conventional statistical analyses by identifying patients with greater supportive care needs, although external validation is required before clinical implementation.

Title: Citrate-capped gold nanoparticle aggregation-based colorimetric sensor for creatinine quantification via deep learning regression on digital image features
Abstract: This work presents a colorimetric chemical sensing platform based on citrate-capped gold nanoparticles (C-AuNPs) combined with deep learning regression on digital image features for creatinine quantification. C-AuNPs were synthesized via the Turkevich method, yielding monodisperse particles (13 ± 1.05 nm), and evaluated using creatinine standard solutions (20–500 μM) and urine mimic samples (20 μM–30 mM). Upon creatinine addition, C-AuNP aggregation drives a progressive red-to-blue chromatic transition captured by digital imaging. Six color parameters extracted from Red-Green-Blue (RGB) and hue–saturation–value (HSV) spaces served as inputs to the deep learning regression model for instrument-free creatinine quantification. Analytical results revealed a robust linear correlation between the A<inf>670</inf>/A<inf>520</inf> ratio and creatinine concentration (R<sup>2</sup> = 0.99), with a limit of detection (LOD) of 27.28 μM and outstanding selectivity against common urinary interferents. The deep-learning regression model delivered consistent predictive performance, yielding R<sup>2</sup> of 0.942 for aqueous standards (20–500 μM) and 0.971 for the urine mimic matrix; in the latter, reliable quantification was obtained over the millimolar range (effective quantitative range ≈ 14–30 mM, spike recoveries 86–112%), which covers the upper portion of the physiological urinary creatinine window (2.47–19.18 mM), while lower concentrations in this matrix produce a qualitative response owing to matrix-suppressed aggregation. The platform requires only sample addition and digital imaging within a total analysis time of ∼25 min, suggesting a practical approach for rapid and AI-assisted creatinine quantification in point-of-care diagnostic applications.

Title: Feature Adaptive Learning DETR for small object detection in aerial images
Abstract: Aerial images often contain a large number of small targets. Due to their small proportion in the image and weak feature expression, these small targets are vulnerable to interference from complex backgrounds and other targets. At the same time, blurred imaging and dense targets will further weaken their feature representation. In this article, we propose Feature Adaptive Learning DETR (FAL-DETR), which effectively solves the problem of feature extraction and representation of small targets. Aiming at the problems of high computational complexity and insufficient discriminability of the existing attention mechanisms, this paper proposes the Dual Attention Gated Network (DAGNet). This network adopts the spatial-channel parallel attention branch to enhance the high-frequency information, such as the target edge. It combines the dynamic gating unit to adaptively enhance the features in the two dimensions of the channel and space. Secondly, the proposed Enhanced Adaptive Complementary Fusion (EACF) module adaptively adjusts the weights of features according to the different scales and contents of the feature map. It biaxially fuses high-resolution and low-resolution features to capture the features of small targets more efficiently. To address the unsolved problem of insufficient small-target detailed feature capture after multi-scale fusion in existing methods, we finally propose the Dynamic Adaptive Re-parameterized Aggregation (DARA) module. By integrating multiple layers of convolution and optimizing the reasoning mechanism, the performance of the overall model was further improved. Extensive experiments on three datasets (Visdrone2019-DET, AI-TOD, HIT-UAV) demonstrate our method’s superior performance. Specifically, on VisDrone, it outperforms the baseline by 7.3 percentage points in mAP50 to 52.1 and by 6.2 percentage points in APs to 24.6. On AI-TOD, our model achieves a mAP50 of 55.7, an APvt of 17.5 and an APt of 28.9, surpassing other comparative methods. On HIT-UAV, its mAP50 reaches 81.3 and mAP reaches 53.3, which are 2.2 and 3 percentage points higher than the baseline.

Title: Statistical learning and rhythmic ability in Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder: Individual differences outweigh group effects
Abstract: Speech segmentation is fundamental to language acquisition and supported by statistical learning (SL). Research on SL is inconclusive as to whether it can occur outside the scope of attention and whether SL is impaired in individuals with Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD). Furthermore, individual differences in SL are hypothesized to be influenced by other cognitive abilities such as musical rhythmic ability (RA) and phonological working memory (WM), which previous literature indicated may be impaired in ADHD.The current study investigated SL in participants diagnosed with ADHD (N = 41) and neurotypical (N = 118) peers, exposing them to an artificial language and assessing SL both during exposure using EEG-measures of neural entrainment, as well as behaviorally after exposure. Furthermore, we explored whether multiple tasks assessing RA and WM were related to SL ability, and how SL related to vocabulary size.Bayesian statistical evidence indicated absence of group differences on SL, RA, WM, and vocabulary. Instead, individual variability outweighed group effects. Combining the groups yielded anecdotal evidence for a positive correlation between SL and vocabulary size, but not between SL and RA or WM. These results suggest that SL operates comparably in our samples of neurotypical individuals and individuals with ADHD, and was not found to be related to tasks assessing RA or WM. Notably, our sample consisted of mostly female participants in both groups. Future studies may want to further examine gender differences in ADHD symptoms and take a dimensional approach to ADHD symptomatology in relation to individual differences in SL ability.
