Title: Performance Optimization of Digital Music Multi-Instrument Recognition Based on an Improved DCNN Model and Bi-LSTM
Abstract: To solve the problems of low accuracy and insufficient robustness in instrument recognition in multi-instrument scenarios of digital music, a parallel structure combining a standard Convolution Neural Network and a multi-scale Dilated Convolution Neural Network (CNN-DCNN) is designed to extract multi-scale spatial acoustic features from Mel spectrograms. The feature sequence extracted by CNN-DCNN is fed into a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) network for bidirectional context modeling, and a self-attention mechanism is introduced to dynamically weight temporal features, capturing the inherent long-range temporal dependencies of music signals. The findings demonstrate that the proposed fusion-improved model achieves optimal performance across multiple key metrics, with mean accuracy, macro-average F1 score, and mean precision reaching 88.92%, 87.11% and 88.34%, respectively, and significantly outperforming other comparative models. Ablation experiments further confirm the effectiveness of the parallel convolutional structure, temporal modeling, and attention mechanism. The proposed model, by deeply fusing multi-scale spatial features with bidirectional temporal contextual information, provides a high-performance solution for multi-instrument recognition in complex acoustic scenarios and offers valuable references for intelligent music analysis and retrieval.

Title: Gear-CIoU: Geometry-Aware Reweighted Complete-IoU Loss for Tiny Ship Detection
Abstract: Tiny ship detection in satellite remote sensing imagery remains a challenging task due to weak spatial features, complex sea surface background information, and severe gradient imbalance during bounding-box regression. To address this issue, this study proposes Gear-CIoU, a geometry-aware reweighted Complete-Intersection over Union (CIoU) loss that incorporates the instance size as a scale factor to balance the centre-distance and aspect-ratio weighting coefficients. This design alleviates the degradation of tiny-ship learning performance in conventional IoU-based losses. In addition, the baseline detector is enhanced with an MCA-C3k2 feature aggregation module and a PPADetect head, improving multi-scale feature representation and aggregation efficiency. Experiments on the LEVIR-Ship dataset demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an average precision at IoU=0.5 (AP<inf>50</inf>) of 85.0% with 2.97 M parameters and 8.8 GFLOPs, outperforming the baseline by 10.1% and achieving the state-of-the-art (SOTA) method. Across LEVIR-Ship, AI-TODv2-Ship, and SODA-A (HBB), Gear-CIoU improves AP50 over CIoU by 1.4%–7.7%across all object scales. Sensitivity analysis further shows that AP<inf>50</inf> varies by approximately 2.5% under different scale-weight coefficients, confirming the importance of explicit geometry-aware modeling.

Title: EEG-Based Imagined Speech Classification Using Statistical Features and Machine Learning Models
Abstract: Silent articulation of speech in the mind termed as Imagined speech. it refers to the internal articulation of speech in the absence of overt vocalization or physical movement of the speech apparatus. Decoding imagined speech from brain signals has significant potential for brain-computer interface (BCI) applications, particularly for individuals with severe speech or motor impairments. Electroencephalography (EEG), a non-invasive technique for recording neural activity through scalp electrodes, provides a practical approach for studying imagined speech patterns. In this study, EEG signals corresponding to two imagined words, "good"and "bad,"were recorded from three participants in a controlled experimental environment. A total of 81 statistical features were extracted from the EEG signals to capture temporal and nonlinear characteristics of neural activity. Classification performance was evaluated using three machine learning models: Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), and Decision Tree (DT). Model robustness and generalization were assessed using five-fold cross-validation and leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) validation. Experimental results show that the Decision Tree classifier achieved the highest validation accuracy of 85.31 ± 7.99% under five-fold cross-validation, while SVM demonstrated the most consistent performance across folds and achieved the best generalization accuracy of 84.54 ± 2.53% under LOSO evaluation, indicating its effectiveness in handling inter-subject variability in imagined speech EEG signals.

Title: Machine learning-assisted FTIR-ATR mid-infrared spectroscopy for predicting soil total carbon in tropical Brazilian soils
Abstract: Accurate quantification of total carbon in soil (TC) is essential for sustainable agricultural management and environmental monitoring programs, but conventional laboratory methods are expensive, time‑consuming, and generate toxic waste. Mid‑infrared (MIR) spectroscopy combined with machine learning (ML) algorithms emerges as a rapid, low‑cost, non‑destructive alternative. This study aimed to develop and compare ML models for predicting TC content from MIR spectra obtained by FTIR‑ATR on 330 tropical soils from different regions, under different management systems. Spectra were pre‑processed using Standard Normal Variate (SNV) and subjected to principal component analysis (PCA) for dimensionality reduction. Five algorithms were calibrated and validated (repeated 10 × 3 cross‑validation): Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), Kernel Ridge Regression (KRR), Gradient Boosting Regression (GBR), Partial Least Squares Regression (PLSR), and Support Vector Regression (SVR). GPR with 10 principal components achieved superior performance under internal cross-validation (R<sup>2</sup> = 0.971; RMSE = 0.083% C), largely outperforming the other algorithms (R<sup>2</sup> ranging from −0.047 to 0.544). These results support the hypothesis that MIR+ML integration can predict TC with high accuracy under internal cross-validation. Cost, analytical speed, and environmental performance relative to conventional methods were not quantified in this study, so such operational advantages remain to be demonstrated under deployment conditions. The MIR- and GPR-based approach is a potentially efficient and accurate complement to conventional methods for determining TC, with prospective application in soil monitoring programs; however, because predictive uncertainty was not evaluated, use of the model for carbon accounting or certification is not yet supported. The main limitation of this study is that validation relied exclusively on internal repeated cross-validation of the calibration dataset; independent external validation across regions, soil classes, instruments, and management systems is still required before operational use.

Title: Neural Networks as Diagnostic Instruments: A Strong-Inference Methodology for Engineering Validation
Abstract: Most applied machine-learning studies are built to confirm that a proposed model beats a metric. When the model loses, the result is often discarded as a failed experiment. We argue, using an eleven-experiment radar-error investigation as a worked example within a single engineering domain, that a neural network can be useful as a diagnostic instrument when it is embedded in a strong-inference design where wins and losses both eliminate hypotheses. We identify five roles observed in the study: (1) a hypothesis tester, where leave-one-folder-out (LOFO) cross-scenario R<sup>2</sup> adjudicates between structural hypotheses; (2) a stress test, where Durbin-Watson (DW) residual diagnostics help distinguish underfitting from the absence of first-order temporal autocorrelation under the chosen ordering; (3) a diagnostic signal, where a physically implausible cross-validation R<sup>22</sup> of 244,811 prompted an investigation that localized a 22π azimuth-wrapping data error contaminating 9 of 13 datasets, a misdiagnosis (attributing the collapse to circular topology) was refuted when a principled sin/cos encoding barely moved the reading (-244,811 to -60,047), redirecting the investigation to the data; (4) a collapse diagnostician, where a catastrophic LOFO fold was traced to feature extrapolation 2.8× beyond the training envelope (R<sup>22</sup> = -1277 at seed 42; -769 under the strongest stabilization); and (5) an attribution probe, where leave-one-column ablation converted a performance number into model-specific, physically interpretable attribution. These roles come from one radar-engineering case study, so we present them as a descriptive taxonomy rather than a validated general framework. The resulting 6-step protocol is a prospective proposal for studies with a meaningful null, grouped validation, interpretable features, and auditable failure modes; its transfer to other domains remains to be demonstrated.

Title: Galaxy survey data reduction with deep learning
Abstract: PAUS is a 40 narrow-band imaging survey using the PAUCam instrument installed at the William Herschel Telescope (WHT). Since the survey started in 2015, this instrument has acquired a unique dataset, performing a relatively deep and wide survey, but with a simultaneous excelled redshift accuracy. The survey is a compromise in performance between deep spectroscopic survey and wide field imaging, showing an order of magnitude better redshift resolution than typical broad band surveys. The survey data reduction was designed based on classical data reduction techniques. For example the redshift template fitting needed a different algorithm to properly handle the PAUS data. While the data reduction and redshift estimation worked, it had room for improvements. In this talk, we detail the different efforts of replacing steps in the PAUS data reduction with deep learning algorithms. First, deep learning techniques obtain a 50% reduction in the photo-z scatter for the fainted galaxies. This is achieved through various techniques, including using transfer learning from simulations to handle a small data set. Furthermore, we have constructed multiple algorithms to improve the data reduction stage. Noise estimation from background estimation from a nonuniform background was handled in BKGNet, the galaxy photometry (light measure) was introduced with Lumus. Recent work includes the effort of directly estimating the galaxy distance from images.

Title: Synthetic Content Validation of Pediatric Trust Instruments Using Persona-Driven Large Language Models: Development and Evaluation Study
Abstract: Background: Large language models (LLMs) could assist in streamlining health care instrument validation. This is particularly relevant as traditional instrument development is time-intensive and resource-intensive. Currently, there is a significant gap in specifically developed and validated trust instruments for pediatric emergency and surgical contexts. Such tools are key because trust is foundational to the patient family–physician relationship and is associated with improved care-seeking and treatment adherence. Objective: This study aimed (1) to develop new trust instruments and conduct their preliminary content validation confirming item relevance through a Synthetic Instrument Validation approach integrating human and LLM capabilities and (2) to evaluate appropriate use cases for LLMs in psychometric assessment. Methods: Two trust instruments were developed (patient family and physician versions). In phase 1, instruments underwent a 2-stage content validation process using parallel synthetic and human expert panels (5 patient family members, 3 physician synthetic experts, and 7 unique human experts). Synthetic panels consisted of 3 persona-prompted LLMs (Claude Sonnet 4, GPT-5, and Grok 4), with human panels serving as comparators. The scale–content validity index (S-CVI) threshold was set at ≥0.80, percent agreement on item relevancy was used to compare panels. In phase 2, LLM performance in quantitative research tasks was evaluated. The patient family instrument underwent Flesch-Kincaid assessment; both instruments underwent cosine similarity analyses using algorithmic and LLM-based methods. Results: In phase 1, percent agreement between panels for the patient family and physician instruments was 90.9% and 88.9% for dimensional validation and 90.9% and 100% for contextual validation. Fleiss κ for within-panel agreement ranged from poor to almost perfect; 0.20 (95% CI -0.23 to 0.63) to 1.00 (95% CI 1.00-1.00). All instrument subsections met or exceeded S-CVI thresholds across both rounds and panels. Phase 2 Flesch-Kincaid metrics converged across all 3 methods to target benchmark (mean Grade Level 8.1, SD 1.1; mean Reading Ease 60.1, SD 5.6), while reference readability was near target, showing convergence across implementations of the same formula. In contrast, cosine similarity analyses revealed significant LLM performance limitations; cosine similarity analyses were, therefore, abandoned in favor of the algorithmic method alone, which achieved a maximum cosine similarity of 0.83, indicating acceptable item distinctiveness overall. Conclusions: Persona-prompted LLMs effectively assisted preliminary content validation and may help reduce timelines from months to weeks, but showed limitations in quantitative computations. This suggests that, in this study, persona-prompted LLMs performed better in subjective rating tasks than in deterministic cosine similarity computations. These findings help illustrate task-dependent boundaries for LLM integration in psychometric research, necessitating selective human-LLM collaboration. While these instruments achieved preliminary content validity, they require full psychometric testing before they can be considered validated for clinical use. Synthetic Instrument Validation offers a feasible approach to preliminary health care instrument development while preserving key elements of content validation.

Title: Deep Learning for Non-Invasive Obstructive Sleep Apnea Screening in Children: A Systematic Comparison of Seven Architectures
Abstract: Overnight polysomnography remains the diagnostic gold standard for pediatric obstructive sleep apnea, yet is widely inaccessible due to cost and infrastructure constraints. This study benchmarks seven deep learning architectures on the Cleveland Children's Sleep and Health Study cohort of 517 children, using 59 non-invasive features spanning craniofacial proxies, anthropometric measurements, and symptom-based questionnaire responses. While attention-based models led cross-validation performance, ResNet achieved the highest test AUC of 0.7375, underscoring the generalization advantage of architecturally parsimonious models in low-sample clinical settings. A weighted ensemble further yielded a three-tier risk stratification with OSA prevalence rising from 6.0% to 50.2% across strata, offering a practical triage instrument for primary care. These findings establish a reproducible non-invasive screening benchmark and advocate for generalization-aware model selection in pediatric clinical machine learning.

Title: Are AI Multimodal Learning Assistants Up to the Task? Evaluating NotebookLM Through the Task-Technology Fit Model
Abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) tools become increasingly integrated into educational settings, understanding how they align with learners’ needs and support meaningful engagement has become a research priority. Among emerging AI tools, Google’s NotebookLM offers a novel, multimodal learning experience that allows students to interact with personalized content through summaries, podcasts, mind maps, and simulated dialogues. However, empirical evidence on its effectiveness from the learner’s perspective remains limited. This quantitative study examines the effectiveness of NotebookLM in enhancing student engagement and perceived academic performance, utilizing the Task-Technology Fit (TTF) model as a theoretical framework. The study involved a convenience sample of 61 third-year undergraduate students from a university in Saudi Arabia who used NotebookLM to study project management course materials. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire with measurement items adapted from previously validated instruments, complemented by a post-session quiz designed to assess students’ understanding of the instructional material. Our findings highlight that content quality played a key role in shaping students’ perceptions of how well the technology supported their learning, alongside technology features. Importantly, a higher perceived fit between tasks and technology was positively associated with higher student engagement and perceived academic performance (i.e., students’ self-reported perceptions of productivity, effectiveness, and task completion rather than objective grades), while a quiz was administered as an additional learning check. This study discusses practical implications for educators and instructional designers and offers directions for future research on the broader adoption and long-term impact of AI multimodal learning assistants in higher education.

Title: Adaptive Audio Enhancement Using Recursive Dynamic Noise Tracking for Low-Latency Edge Devices
Abstract: Environmental noise can substantially affect speech quality and intelligibility in real-time audio systems, particularly when speech enhancement is implemented on computationally limited edge platforms. Conventional frequency-domain techniques, including spectral subtraction and Wiener filtering, provide computationally efficient solutions, but their effectiveness can decrease when the acoustic noise varies with time. Deep learning-based enhancement methods can achieve stronger noise suppression, although their computational, memory, and latency requirements may restrict deployment on lightweight embedded hardware. This work presents a Recursive Dynamic Noise Tracking (RDNT) framework with adaptive spectral gain estimation to provide low-latency speech enhancement under varying noise conditions. The proposed framework processes speech in the Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) domain and recursively updates the noise spectrum using successive noisy-speech observations. The resulting noise estimate is used to determine frequency-dependent suppression gains, while the original phase is retained during speech reconstruction. Evaluation was conducted using clean speech from the VoiceBank dataset combined with Gaussian, traffic, and crowd noise, with environmental recordings obtained from the DEMAND dataset. RDNT was compared with spectral subtraction and Wiener filtering using SNR, PESQ, STOI, SDR, SI-SDR, processing latency, and subjective Mean Opinion Score (MOS). Across the evaluated conditions, the proposed method improved the measured speech-enhancement performance while preserving intelligibility and maintaining a maximum processing latency of 0.082 s. These results demonstrate that recursive noise tracking can provide a practical compromise among noise suppression, speech preservation, and computational efficiency for real-time speech enhancement on edge platforms.

Title: DAE-Aided MUSIC for Direction-of-Arrival Estimation Under Spatially Correlated Noise
Abstract: The basis for Direction-of-Arrival (DOA) estimation using the Multiple Signal Classification (MUSIC) algorithm is founded on an assumption of spatial white noise that rarely holds in real-world applications. This paper examines what happens when a covariance denoising autoencoder (DAE), trained entirely on white noise data is tested in environments where the noise is spatially correlated, modeled here as a first order autoregressive (AR(1)) Toeplitz covariance. The paper evaluates the proposed solution using Monte Carlo simulations with a ten element uniform linear array and show that the structural learning that is provided by training the model in a white noise regime allows it to be robust across many different test cases that lie outside of this regime. The method outperforms Sample MUSIC, the Tyler M-estimator and Spatial Smoothing MUSIC across a wide range of correlation coefficients. At high correlation (ρ =0.95), the white noise trained DAE still reduces root-mean-square error (RMSE) by 31% relative to Sample MUSIC. A lightweight fine-tuning step,using only 5% correlated noise samples recovers full performance, achieving a 68% RMSE reduction over Sample MUSIC at ρ =0.95. Overall, the results point to strong generalization capacity in learned covariance priors and offer a practical low overhead path for adapting such models to unseen noise environments.

Title: SWARANOTE: An ML-Based Carnatic Notations Prediction System
Abstract: Behind the richness of Carnatic music hides complex microtonal variations (Swarasthanas) and oscillations (Gamakas). Unlike the western music system, identifying the notes of the Carnatic system demands years of training and practice. To comprehend different notes and complex patterns of Carnatic ragas, we have developed an application that is designed to learn from audio data and predict the possible notes from the given song or tune. To achieve this, we have used a specialized Deep Learning Architecture called Bi-directional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM), which is highly efficient for working on audio input. Bi-LSTM learns patterns from complex audio data, in both forward and backward directions, just like a human listening to sounds. The Model was trained on a 33-minute custom made dataset using Carnatic violin recordings of two fundamental ragas Shankarabharanam and Mayamalavagowla. Through Data Augmentation, we achieved a large collection of over 26,000 Swara samples. The accuracy of the system stands at 90.69%, proving its reliability in identification of notes. The system was designed not only to identify the notes but also the raga to which the given input audio belongs, based on the pattern of the notes. On integrating this smart prediction system with an easy-to-use flask web application, this paper provides a helpful tool for beginner music students and researchers to convert the audio input into written notations corresponding to the nomenclature of the raga.

Title: Hybrid Leveraging AI Models and Deep Learning Framework Using MRI for Brain Tumor Detection
Abstract: Tumours of the brain are among the most severe neurological diseases, and fast and accurate diagnosis is essential for increasing treatment effectiveness and patient survival. Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) can provide detailed visualisation of cerebral anomalies, but manual interpretation is often labour intensive and prone to diagnostic inconsistency. The effectiveness of current machine learning and deep learning methods are promising, but still facing challenges such as tumour heterogeneity, feature representation, multi-scale localisation and computational efficiency as major obstacles. We propose a Hybrid Leveraging Artificial Intelligence and Deep Learning Framework for improving MRI based brain tumour detection and classification in this paper. The proposed system includes a modified architecture of YOLOv8 with GhostConv blocks, a Vision Transformer Encoder (VTE), an improved Spatial Pyramid Pooling Fast Plus (SPPF+) module, multi-scale feature fusion strategies, and RT-DETR detection heads. Transfer learning with pre-trained COCO weights is used to improve feature generalisation and reduce dependence on large annotated medical data sets. The MRI images are preprocessed and divided into training and testing sets. The model is trained to accurately localise and classify brain tumours of different severity levels.The proposed approach is evaluated experimentally on the Kaggle Brain Tumour MRI dataset and the results show its effectiveness. The model achieved an accuracy of 99.6%, precision of 99.5%, recall of 99.6% and F1-score of 99.5% outperforming several traditional and state-of-the-art methods such as DenseNet, CNN Ensemble, SVM and Xception-based models. Further support for the framework's robustness is provided by the analysis of the confusion matrix, showing few false-positive and false-negative predictions.The results show that the hybrid architecture proposed provides excellent accuracy, reliability and computing efficiency in the detection and localisation of brain tumour from MRI data. The combination of sophisticated deep learning, transformer-based attention mechanisms and multi-scale feature fusion makes the system a promising computer-aided diagnostic instrument, which can assist radiologists in early diagnosis, clinical decision making and treatment planning.

Title: Forecasting Tourism Demand Based on Multiple Sources of Data: A SARIMAX Approach with YouTube Indicators
Abstract: This study investigates the use of YouTube data to predict tourism demand with AI-based time series models. Multiple datasets are used, represented by Oman's monthly inbound tourism and YouTube data. Two models are suggested: the SARIMA model, built to capture time-dependent patterns as a baseline, and SARIMAX models tested with different external variables, including engagement index, attention index, and log-transformed views. In addition, lagged versions of these variables are used. The results indicate that, despite YouTube-based variables bringing some changes in model performance, their impact on forecasting accuracy is not very significant. Specifically, enngagement-based measures can capture extreme variations in tourist demand, while attention-based variables also improve model fit. However, these variables do not substantially improve overall prediction accuracy relative to the baseline model for either type of variable. In addition, it has been experimentally shown through MLR that the lagged Attention Index is significantly associated with tourism demand, suggesting that YouTube data can be used to identify influencing factors, even if the predictive power appears to be limited. These results indicate that the seasonal components of tourism demand are domestic, and the YouTube indicators attain limited results. The research demonstrates the need to combine different types of data to improve predictive models for tourism.

Title: Particleboard surface defect recognition using shared-weight feature learning
Abstract: Rare defect categories in particleboard manufacturing often have limited labeled samples, reducing the effectiveness of conventional image recognition methods. To address this issue, this study proposed shared-weight supervised contrastive learning for particleboard surface defect recognition (SSCL-PSDR), a particleboard surface defect recognition framework combining a shared-weight representation learning with supervised contrastive optimization. The framework focuses on five defect categories–Glue Spot, Scratch, Sand Leakage, Pollution, and Damage–and is evaluated on a single-source industrial dataset containing 393 defect patches. DINOv2 Transformer is adopted as the feature extraction backbone to capture global representations, while a lightweight multi-scale fusion and downsampling module enhances defect recognition at different spatial scales. An improved coordinate attention strategy further strengthens directional feature perception and highlights discriminative defect information. Supervised contrastive loss reduces intra-class variation and improves inter-class separability. Experimental results show that SSCL-PSDR achieves 88.8% accuracy, 88.9% precision, 88.7% recall, and 88.8% F1-score under fixed single-split evaluation, while maintaining robust average accuracy of 88.4 ± 0.8% across three independent data partitions and moderate computational complexity with 23.0M parameters and 25.2G FLOPs. Compared with a conventional pairwise Siamese baseline, SSCL-PSDR achieves improved recognition performance and remains competitive with other advanced deep learning models, demonstrating effectiveness for small-sample particleboard defect recognition under investigated industrial conditions.

Title: Interference Reduction in Music Source Separation Through Recurrent Inference with Deep Neural Network Models
Abstract: The issue of music source separation is discussed, focusing on its use in many audio processing tasks like remixing, target sound extraction, and audio quality improvement. This work addresses the problem through a recurrent inference framework that uses a pretrained deep neural network model, specifically within m a sk-based t i mefrequency d o main models. An iterative refinement me thod is introduced, where the output of the pretrained spectrogram separator network is fed back into the model repeatedly to extract the target source. Experiments with the Open-Unmix model show that, although the method achieves significant S i gnal-to-Interference Ratio (S IR) improve-ments comparable to top-performing discriminative models, the naive recurrent setup without mixture consistency correction can cause distortions, leading to lower Signal-to-Artifact Ratio (SAR) and Signal-toDistortion Ratio (SDR) scores. Different consistency correction techniques are then tested, demonstrating that optimizing via gradient descent in the ratio mask domain helps maintain stable performance.

Title: Forecasting Minimum Support Price-anchored Mandi Prices for Wheat and Maize in India: AComparative Machine-learning and Time-series Framework
Abstract: Background: India’s minimum support price (MSP) regime creates an administered floor for wholesale (mandi) prices, making accurate price forecasting the analytical foundation for farmer revenue-risk assessment, government procurement planning and the design of price-or revenue-based crop insurance instruments. Wheat and maize present a sharp institutional contrast: wheat is procurement-binding through the Food Corporation of India, while maize receives little procurement support and its price is left largely to private trade. This study benchmarks machine-learning and classical time-series forecasters for the monthly modal mandi price of both crops across a structurally distinct, post-pandemic hold-out period and defines, in measurable terms, what it means for such a series to be MSP-anchored. Methods: This analysis was carried out at Sri Sathya Sai Institute of Higher Learning (SSSIHL), Prasanthi Nilayam, Andhra Pradesh, India, during 2026. Daily AGMARKNET records for wheat and maize (April 2008-March 2025) were aggregated into 204 monthly All-India modal-price observations per crop-the mean of daily modal prices-with the corresponding MSP reported for reference. Eight algorithms-ridge regression, support vector regression, random forest, extremely randomised trees, gradient boosting, XGBoost, ARIMA and SARIMA-together with a naïve persistence benchmark, were trained on 177 months (April 2008-December 2022) and evaluated out-of-sample on 27 held-out months (January 2023-March 2025) using the mean absolute error, root mean squared error and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE). Result: Ridge regression on lagged prices and a month indicator dominated every fitted ensemble and, with ARIMA and SARIMA evaluated as static multi-step forecasts, every time-series competitor for both crops, achieving a MAPE of 2.75 per cent for wheat (mean absolute error ₹ 68.97/quintal) and 2.59 per cent for maize (₹ 55.97/quintal). Tree-based learners and support vector regression deteriorated sharply on the trending test window; SARIMA was competitive only for maize. Against naïve persistence, however, ridge’s edge was modest for wheat and mixed for maize-persistence matched ridge on MAE and MAPE and narrowly beat it on RMSE-indicating ridge’s advantage lies chiefly over the more flexible learners. This is attributed to the near-unit autocorrelation of MSP-anchored series and the inability of tree ensembles to extrapolate beyond their training range, consistent with, though not proving, the institutional asymmetry between procurement-stabilised wheat and procurement-absent maize. These forecasts form the price engine for companion volume-forecasting and procurement-liability studies within the broader actuarial data-science revenue-protection framework.

Title: Machine Learning Prediction of Torrefied Biomass Properties From Diverse Agricultural Residues
Abstract: Torrefaction has emerged as a promising thermochemical pretreatment to enhance the fuel properties of agricultural biomass, yet predicting product characteristics remains challenging due to feedstock variability. This study developed and compared four machine learning (ML) models, support vector regression (SVR), artificial neural network (ANN), gradient boosting machine (GBM), and random forest (RF), to predict the higher heating value (HHV), mass yield (MY), and energy yield (EY) of torrefied biomass. A comprehensive dataset comprising 117 experimental samples from 11 biomass types torrefied at 200–280°C for 20–60 min was utilized. Input variables included the contents of proximate composition (ash, fixed carbon, and volatile matter), ultimate composition (C, H, N, O, S), and process conditions (temperature and residence time). SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis revealed that torrefaction temperature was the most influential parameter, followed by volatile matter and ash content. Results demonstrated that GBM consistently outperformed the other models, achieving an acceptably high coefficient of determination, with minimal prediction errors across different input configurations. Notably, simple proximate-analysis data provided performance comparable to that of more detailed and instrument-intensive ultimate analysis (UL), highlighting the practical value of GBM for operators handling diverse biomass feedstocks with limited access to specialized analytical instruments.

Title: From digital technologies to business sustainability: the central role of innovation in Thai SMEs
Abstract: This study examines how AI-chatbot usage, social media usage, and customer value anticipation are associated with business sustainability in Thai small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) through an innovation-centered capability pathway. Drawing on a dynamic capabilities perspective, the model positions innovation as the central mechanism through which digital and customer-sensing inputs are linked to network learning, business performance, and business sustainability. The measurement instrument was initially validated through a Fuzzy-Rough Set e-Delphi procedure involving 23 experts, followed by covariance-based structural equation modeling using 703 valid SME responses. A pooled seven-construct confirmatory factor analysis demonstrated satisfactory measurement-model fit, reliability, convergent validity, and discriminant validity. All 10 hypothesized structural relationships were statistically significant. AI-chatbot usage, customer value anticipation, and social media usage were positively associated with innovation, while innovation was associated with network learning and business sustainability. Network learning, customer value anticipation, and social media usage were associated with business performance, which in turn was associated with business sustainability. The model explained modest-to-moderate variance in the endogenous constructs. The study contributes by extending prior SME capability research with AI-chatbot and social media inputs and by showing how innovation provides a central pathway connecting digital engagement and customer sensing with learning, performance, and longer-term business sustainability.

Title: Beyond Global and Local: A Stacked Ensemble Approach to Symbolic Music Emotion Recognition
Abstract: Symbolic Music Emotion Recognition (MER) has often been approached through global and local scopes of musical structure independently. However, evidence on when these paradigms are complementary remains limited. This paper presents a framework for fusing SVM, CNN+BiLSTM, and Transformer models that each capture different scopes of musical structure for binary valence and arousal classification in symbolic MER through meta-learner stacking, achieving notable performance improvements, especially on large-scale datasets. We further explore model complementarity and feature-level behavior across emotion dimensions to explain when and how these models provide complementary information.

Title: LFA-Net: A Lightweight Frequency-Adaptive Semantic Segmentation Network for Efficient Wireless Signal Identification
Abstract: Wireless signal semantic segmentation based on deep learning often suffers from over-parameterization, high computational cost, and insufficient exploitation of radio frequency physical characteristics. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a Lightweight Frequency-Adaptive Segmentation Network (LFA-Net) with an encoder-decoder architecture. The encoder extracts rich semantics via multi-scale features and performs lightweight fusion via a dual-weighted scheme based on signal and noise first- and second-order statistics. The decoder integrates progressive feature refinement for boundary reconstruction and channel recalibration to further mitigate semantic edge blurring. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that LFA-Net achieves a mean accuracy of 97.31% with only 0.287M parameters and 6.75 ms inference time, while exhibiting robust semantic recognition performance across a wide signal-to-noise ratio range from -10dB to 60dB. The source code is available at https://github.com/husaiyu985/spectrogram-segmentation.

Title: Data-Driven Landslide Susceptibility Mapping: A Multimodal Deep Learning Framework for Integrating Multi-Source Geospatial and Environmental Data
Abstract: Landslides are among the most data-intensive geohazards to characterize: their occurrence, timing, and severity depend on the interaction of terrain, hydrological, geological, and anthropogenic variables that must be sensed, curated, labelled, and modelled before any hazard statement can be made. This paper presents a data-centred machine learning framework for landslide susceptibility mapping (LSM) that treats data explicitly as the input fuel, the test material, the validation instrument, and the final output of the analysis. We review the principal open data streams that underpin contemporary susceptibility modelling such as global and regional landslide inventories (e.g., the NASA Cooperative Open Online Landslide Repository), digital elevation models, precipitation records, land-cover products, and soil information and we examine the well-documented data-quality problems (reporting bias, positional uncertainty, class imbalance, spatial autocorrelation) that condition what a model trained on them can honestly claim. To make the pipeline concrete and reproducible, we construct a literature-informed synthetic multi-source conditioning-factor dataset spanning a 21,600-cell mountainous terrain and use it to train and evaluate five commonly used classifiers such as logistic regression, random forest, gradient boosting, support vector machines, and a multilayer perceptron which are under two validation regimes: conventional random k-fold splitting and spatial block cross-validation. Consistent with prior findings in the susceptibility-mapping literature, random forest and neural-network models achieved the strongest discrimination (AUC 0.76–0.77 under random validation), while all models showed a measurable performance decline under spatially independent validation, confirming that spatial autocorrelation inflates apparent accuracy when training and test pixels are geographically adjacent. We report standard classification metrics (AUC, accuracy, precision, recall, F1, Cohen’s kappa, Brier score), a feature-importance ranking dominated by slope, rainfall, distance to roads, lithology and land cover, and a susceptibility surface in which the top two hazard classes (16.3% of the study area) capture 59.8% of landslide-labelled cells. We conclude with a discussion of data provenance, uncertainty propagation, and reproducibility considerations relevant to the Data Science Journal community, and we argue that susceptibility mapping is best understood as a data curation and validation problem as much as a modelling problem.

Title: Electroencephalography Changes in Emotional Recognition: A Signal Processing Approach Using Wavelet Features
Abstract: Background: motion recognition using electroencephalography (EEG) has gained significant attention in the fields of affective computing and human–computer interaction due to its ability to capture real-time neural responses. EEG signal variations associated with emotional states can be analysed using wavelet-based signal processing within the arousal–valence framework. Purpose: This study aims to analyse EEG signal variations associated with emotional states using a wavelet-based signal processing approach within the arousal–valence framework. Methods: A prospective observational study was conducted on 48 healthy participants. Emotional states were induced using image, video and music stimuli categorised under the arousal–valence model. EEG signals were recorded using the standard 10–20 electrode placement system. The acquired signals were pre-processed and analysed using discrete wavelet transform (DWT) to extract time–frequency features, including energy and entropy. Statistical analysis was performed to evaluate hemispheric differences and gender-based variations. Results: Differences in EEG activity were observed between the left and right hemispheres across multiple emotional states (p < .05). Video and music stimuli produced stronger and more distinguishable EEG responses compared to image-based stimuli. Negative emotions demonstrated higher discriminative patterns than positive emotions. Gender-based variations were also observed in EEG responses. Conclusion: Wavelet-based EEG feature analysis provides meaningful and discriminative information for emotion recognition and may provide a robust feature set for future machine learning-based emotion recognition systems. Further studies incorporating classification algorithms and larger data sets are required to validate their predictive performance.

Title: Physics-Guided Multi-Channel Restoration for Efficient and Accurate Atomic Force Microscopy Imaging
Abstract: Scientific imaging instruments often acquire multiple physically complementary signals within a single measurement. In atomic force microscopy (AFM), high-throughput imaging requires higher scan speeds, however, image quality is fundamentally limited by multiple distortions. These artifacts are further amplified for sharp nano/microstructures, making accurate image restoration inherently challenging. Most deep learning-based approaches rely on a single primary channel and improve performance by increasing model complexity or training data. Here, we introduce a physics-guided multi-channel input approach for AFM that utilizes co-acquired auxiliary signals to improve image restoration efficiency and accuracy. We construct a four co-acquired channel input, each containing complementary physical information. By integrating these channels into a lightweight convolutional neural network, the proposed approach significantly improves restoration quality with minimal additional parameters. At a scan rate of 7.0 Hz, the four-channel DnCNN achieved higher reconstruction accuracy than a single-channel Restormer with approximately 47 times as many parameters, while providing approximately 24 times faster inference. Across the evaluated EFM and PFM conditions, four-channel inputs reduced the training-patch requirement by approximately two to three times at matched PSNR.

Title: Expressive music performance generation from symbolic scores via conditional variational autoencoders and performance context embeddings
Abstract: This research proposes a conditional generative framework that transforms symbolic music scores into expressive performances using deep learning. The proposed adaptive deer hunting optimised conditional variational auto-encoder (ADHO-CVAE) model incorporates performance context embeddings – such as global tempo profiles, expressive style categories, and performer-specific tendencies – to produce nuanced variations in timing, dynamics, and articulation not captured in standard notation. Trained on the Maestro-Piano-Midi dataset (N = 1,276) with aligned score-performance pairs, the model learns conditional distributions of expressive features including timing deviation, velocity variation, and articulation ratio. Experimental results show the model outperforms existing approaches, achieving higher fluency (4.6), emotional expression (4.7), and harmony (4.5). The framework effectively bridges symbolic notation and human-like musical interpretation for intelligent music systems.

Title: Non-destructive Prediction of Remaining Useful Life for Nickel-Titanium Rotary Files Using Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy and Artificial Intelligence
Abstract: Introduction Nickel-titanium (NiTi) rotary files are widely used in modern root canal therapy. Although instrument separation is relatively uncommon, sudden fatigue fracture may lead to serious clinical consequences. Current methods are limited to detecting macroscopic defects and cannot quantitatively assess early-stage microscopic fatigue damage. To address this issue, we combined electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) with artificial intelligence to develop a framework for the non-destructive prediction of the remaining useful life of NiTi rotary files. Methods We conducted EIS monitoring on 94 NiTi rotary files from their pristine state until fatigue fracture, and built a dataset containing 864 valid measurements. We designed a frequency point and sliding window joint optimization strategy to select key features and eliminate feature dimensionality redundancy. Using five-fold cross-validation, we evaluated 18 models: nine traditional machine-learning models, eight conventionally trained deep-learning architectures, and the pretrained tabular foundation model TabPFN; we established a three-level clinical risk-warning system. Results Among the evaluated models, CatBoost, a gradient-boosting decision-tree algorithm, achieved the lowest cross-validated mean absolute error (0.133 ± 0.015) and a mean three-level risk-classification accuracy of 71.1% ± 2.9%. Furthermore, the joint optimization strategy reduced feature dimensionality by 83.0% without significantly compromising the performance. The best-performing traditional machine-learning models outperformed conventionally trained deep-learning architectures and TabPFN on this small tabular dataset. Conclusions This study confirms that an EIS- and AI-based non-destructive assessment method enables the quantitative evaluation of the fatigue state of NiTi rotary files prior to fracture, providing a clinically meaningful basis for personalized instrument replacement decisions.

Title: Algorithm–Architecture Co-Design for Vertically Integrated AI and HPC Systems: Challenges, Advantages, and Future Outlook
Abstract: Next-generation scientific instruments in high-energy physics, X-ray imaging, fusion diagnostics, and other data-intensive applications generate data rates that increasingly exceed practical communication bandwidth and power budgets, making the traditional approach of transferring raw data to remote computing systems unsustainable. This paper presents the Vertically Integrated AI for Sensing and High-Performance Computing (VIAS) project, which treats three-dimensional heterogeneous integration not merely as an advanced packaging technology but as a computational design paradigm that jointly shapes algorithms, hardware architectures, and memory organization. Rather than focusing on a single accelerator, VIAS explores a diverse set of AI and HPC workloads, including compact neural networks, spiking neural networks, hyperdimensional computing, vision transformers, machine-learning-based compression, and modular chiplet accelerators, to demonstrate how vertically integrated architectures reduce data movement through algorithm–architecture–technology co-design. Across these case studies, we identify recurring design principles that exploit dense vertical interconnects, memory locality, and specialized heterogeneous compute engines to enable real-time processing directly at the detector edge. We further discuss the common system-level challenges, including thermal management, memory hierarchy, communication, and 3D-aware design automation, that must be addressed to realize future intelligent scientific instruments. Together, these efforts establish a reusable co-design methodology for next-generation edge-AI and HPC systems built around vertically integrated heterogeneous architectures.

Title: Anchor-driven Multi-modal Multi-scale Expert Selection for Survival Prediction
Abstract: The integrative analysis of histopathological Whole-Slide Images (WSIs) and transcriptomic profiles holds significant promise for cancer survival prediction. However, existing methods typically project multi-modal features directly into a shared latent space without explicit alignment, leading to the entanglement of mismatched morphological cues and molecular signals. Furthermore, current fusion strategies often treat the extreme spatial heterogeneity of WSIs uniformly, lacking mechanisms to adaptively prioritize clinically relevant tissue scales for individual patients. To address these limitations, we propose an Anchor-driven Multi-modal Multi-scale Expert Selection (AM<sup>2</sup>ES) framework for survival prediction. Specifically, we present an Anchor-driven Multi-modal Fusion (AMF) module, which introduces learnable semantic anchors as cross-modal mediators to bridge the semantic gap by enforcing a structurally regularized alignment between transcriptomic features and multi-scale pathology representations. Built upon this aligned semantic space, we further design a Hierarchical Mixture-of-Experts (H-MoE) selection module to decouple the hierarchical prognostic selection process. Mimicking the pathologist's diagnostic workflow, H-MoE performs (i) Intra-scale Expert Filtering to discriminatively identify salient tumor regions within each magnification, and (ii) Inter-scale Hierarchy Routing to dynamically weight and select the most informative resolution levels. Extensive experiments on multiple TCGA cancer cohorts demonstrate that our AM<sup>2</sup>ES achieves state-of-the-art performance while offering fine-grained interpretability by visualizing how specific molecular pathways drive the expert routing decisions across tissue scales.

Title: Hybrid Classification for Complex and Composite Activity Recognition in Multi-User Environments
Abstract: The Human Activity Recognition (HAR) task from sensor data has yielded impressive results in recognizing elementary activities, but it has been difficult to recognize composite and multiple persons' activities due to temporal dependencies, relational interactions, and sensor-level ambiguity. In this paper, we present a hybrid approach leveraging symbolic logic for satisfying constraints, relational interaction through graph modeling, and deep learning for representing features. A probabilistic temporal grammar for activity generation, Graph Neural Networks (GNN) for relational modeling, attention based fusion for multimodal weighting, and multi-scale convolutional neural networks (CNN) together with bidirectional long-short-term memory (BiLSTM) model for temporal features constitute the proposed framework. Unlike prior methods to existing works, the proposed method employs symbolic constraints at test time to jointly learn representations and perform relational reasoning. A multi-user wearable HAR dataset incorporating hierarchical, concurrent, and interactive tasks is presented to validate the proposed approach. The results show that the hybrid approach attains an F1-score of 0.92 for atomic activities and 0.86 for composite activities, performing better than deep and classical methods. Evaluations of the approach based on its robustness against sensor failure and synchronization drifts have been done successfully. Repeated-run evaluation and effect-size analysis further support the consistency and practical magnitude of the observed improvements. The performance of the hybrid approach shows the usefulness of using all three types of components for solving the challenging problem of multi-user HAR.

Title: MSAC-TCN-Informer Multi-scale Hybrid Model-based Short-term Reliable Prediction Method Used for the PM2.5 Concentration
Abstract: With the worsening severity of air pollution, the PM2.5 concentration prediction has become a key research focus in the management and control of atmospheric pollution. Traditional deterministic, statistical, and machine learning methods often fail to extract local non-linear features and capture long-term dependencies in air quality time series data, which significantly limits their prediction accuracy. To address these challenges, this study proposes a hybrid model MSAC-TCN-Informer with ro-bustness. Firstly, a two-stage ST-GNN-PC-GAIN framework is constructed to improve data quality through spatiotemporal coarse imputation and adversarial fine refinement. Then, Multi-Scale Adaptive Convolution (MSAC) is embedded into the deep layers of Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCN), where learnable scale weights dynamically adjust receptive fields and enable adaptive extraction of multi-scale local temporal patterns. Moreover, to facilitate the transition from local representations to global sequence modeling, a feature fusion layer integrates convolutional features with positional embeddings in a unified latent space. Finally, the ProbSparse self-attention and attention distilling mechanisms of Informer are employed to efficiently capture long-range temporal depend-encies, which enhances the prediction accuracy of PM2.5. Experimental results compared with the CNN, TCN, LSTM, RNN, xLSTM, iTransformer, PatchTST, Informer and three hybrid baselines (TCN-Transformer, CNN-Informer, GNN-Transformer) on the public air quality data from Beijing's Olympic Sports Center Station and Dong Si Station demonstrated that the proposed MSAC-TCN-Informer method achieves the best comprehensive performance with respect to all indicators. Specifically, the model achieves an R<sup>2</sup> of 0.9928, with RMSE and MAE reduced to 7.0093 and 3.8070, respectively. In addition, IA increases to 0.9982, while U1 decreases to 0.0305 on the Olympic Sports Center station. Compared with Informer, the proposed model further reduces RMSE and MAE by 43.676% and 47.527%, respectively.

Title: A Multi-modal Dual-Path Attention Fusion Network (MDPAF-Net) for Electromagnetic Fault Diagnosis of Radar Timing Control Boards
Abstract: Complex battlefield electromagnetic environments easily induce various electromagnetic susceptibility (EMS) faults in radar electronic systems. Conventional diagnostic methods rely on hand‑crafted features or single‑domain deep‑learning models. They can hardly extract valid features of non‑stationary electromagnetic interference (EMI) and suffer unsatisfactory cross‑board generalization performance. Meanwhile, most existing models cannot satisfy the dual requirements of high diagnostic accuracy and lightweight embedded deployment. To address the above problems, this paper proposes an end‑to‑end Multi‑modal Dual‑Path Attention Fusion Network (MDPAF‑Net) to realize electromagnetic susceptibility fault diagnosis for radar digital circuit boards. The time‑domain branch directly extracts transient features from raw monitoring signals, while the time‑frequency branch adopts continuous wavelet transform to characterize spectral evolution features of signals. Pyramid Split Attention (PSA) modules are introduced in both two feature‑extraction branches and the feature fusion stage to implement multi‑scale feature recalibration and adaptive cross‑modal weighting. The proposed model is validated on the EMS dataset of radar timing‑control boards collected under controlled conducted‑interference injection, achieving a diagnostic accuracy of 97.1 ± 0.2 %. Comparative and ablation results validate MDPAF‑Net’s effectiveness, with its compact dual‑branch structure and low‑overhead PSA modules supporting lightweight online diagnosis on radar embedded devices. Cross‑domain tests on display‑control and data‑processing boards yield accuracy above 86.1% without fine‑tuning, with cross‑board generalization validated for homogeneous radar circuit boards. This work provides a quantifiable, lightweight, and reasonably general technical solution for high‑precision EMS fault detection and active electromagnetic protection of radar systems under complex electromagnetic interference environments.

Title: A Morphology-Aware Swin Transformer Approach for Classifying the Air Permeability of Knitted Fabrics: TexSwin
Abstract: Air permeability is a critical functional property of knitted fabrics because it directly affects thermal regulation, moisture management, and ventilation efficiency, and wearing performance. Conventional air permeability measurements provide reliable physical values, but they require dedicated measurement instruments, multiple test replicates, and strictly controlled testing conditions, which limit their suitability for rapid industrial screening. This study proposes TexSwin, a morphology-aware Swin Transformer framework for automatic air permeability classification using microscopic, knitted fabric images. Instead of relying only on numerical permeability intervals, the original twelve classes are reorganized into seven morphology-consistent categories according to pore distribution, loop density, and structural similarity. This taxonomy reduces visual ambiguity between adjacent classes and makes the learning problem more consistent with textile structure. The framework was evaluated using 900 microscopic RGB images acquired from 45 knitted fabric structures. The data were divided into 720 training images, 90 validation images, and 90 independent test images. Oversampling was applied only to the training set to reduce class imbalance, while the validation and test sets remained unchanged. TexSwin was benchmarked against representative convolutional and transformer-based architectures, and ablation, cross-validation, computational complexity, and explainability analyses were performed. Under the final 40-epoch training protocol, TexSwin achieved 91.11% validation accuracy and 92.22% independent test accuracy. On the independent test set, the model obtained a macro-F1 score of 0.8258, a weighted-F1 score of 0.9127, a macro-average ROC-AUC of 0.9865, and a weighted-average ROC-AUC of 0.9829. Five-fold cross-validation further confirmed robustness, yielding an average accuracy of 95.75% with a standard deviation of 1.60%. Grad-CAM visualizations showed that the model focused on physically meaningful regions, including pore boundaries and loop intersection zones. These findings indicate that integrating textile morphology with hierarchical transformer-based representation learning provides an accurate, interpretable, and computationally efficient framework for automated air permeability assessment.

Title: Empathy, embodiment, and expanded auditory performance in the age of AI
Abstract: This article explores empathy through experimental sound art and digital performance, drawing on over three decades of practice spanning industrial music, spatial sound, and biofeedback technologies. It asks how embodied listening can generate empathic encounters beyond visual representation and narrative identification. Focusing on EEG-driven installations and immersive multi-channel performances, including work with 4DSOUND and CMMAS, it examines how physiological data, spatialisation, and perceptual feedback loops create conditions for shared sonic presence. Machine learning and self-generative processes are considered as mediators of these encounters, with attention to their aesthetic potential and ethical limitations. Grounded in sound studies, affect theory, and critical posthumanism, the article develops sonic empathy as a situated, bodily, and relational process rather than a measurable emotional outcome. Its practice-as-research approach combines iterative biofeedback mapping, spatial composition, audience response, accessibility-led adjustment, and reflexive documentation. The discussion addresses algorithmic bias, sensory overload, unequal access, and the risks of affective manipulation. It argues that digital performance can support empathic listening when technological mediation remains intelligible, participation accommodates difference, and listeners retain agency in negotiating the encounter.

Title: Template-assisted Contrastive Learning of Task-oriented Dialogue Sentence Embeddings
Abstract: Learning high quality sentence embeddings from dialogues has drawn increasing attentions as it is essential to solve a variety of dialogue-oriented tasks with low annotation cost. Annotating and gathering utterance relationships in conversations are difficult, while token-level annotations, e.g., entities, slots and templates, are much easier to obtain. Other sentence embedding methods are usually sentence-level self-supervised frameworks and cannot utilize token-level extra knowledge. We introduce Template-aware Dialogue Sentence Embedding (TaDSE), a novel augmentation method that utilizes template information to learn utterance embeddings via self-supervised contrastive learning framework. We further enhance the effect with a synthetically augmented dataset that diversifies utterance-template association, in which slot-filling is a preliminary step. We evaluate TaDSE performance on five downstream benchmark dialogue datasets. The experiment results show that TaDSE achieves significant improvements over previous SOTA methods for dialogue. We further introduce a novel analytic instrument of semantic compression test, for which we discover a correlation with uniformity and alignment. Our code is available at https://github.com/minsik-ai/Template-Contrastive-Embedding.

Title: Neuro-structured supervised approach for heat and mass transfer in Sisko ternary nanofluid systems
Abstract: This research introduces a new neuro-structured supervised system to study heat and mass transfer in a non-Newtonian Sisko ternary nanofluid model (NSTNM). The method we are suggesting combines nonlinear autoregressive exogenous (NARX) neural networks with Levenberg–Marquardt intelligent networks (LMINs), resulting in a hybrid NARXLMINs architecture that is capable of accurately mimicking the nonlinear boundary layer behavior. Using similarity transformations, the main partial differential equations are changed into ordinary differential equations and then solved numerically by the Adam method in Mathematica, producing a reference dataset. On the other hand, MATLAB is used for neural network implementation and training. The novelty of this study is in the combination of stochastic AI-based learning and deterministic numerical methods to effectively model complicated ternary nanofluid systems which have superior thermal conductivity and mass transfer performance than ordinary mono and hybrid nanofluids. The study shows that major physical parameters greatly affect how velocity and temperature are distributed, thereby enhancing our understanding of the thermophysical properties of Sisko fluids. The developed model could be very useful in a wide range of applications such as high-tech thermal management systems, biomedical transport processes (for instance, drug delivery at targeted sites and nanofluids based on blood), energy systems, and industrial technologies for enhancing heat transfer. The findings verify that the combined AI method delivers accurate, stable, and low-time-consuming solutions; hence, it is a potential instrument for tackling complex nonlinear fluid flow issues.

Title: Quantum concept music from categorical quantum mechanics: musical incarnation of entanglement
Abstract: We initiate the development of a new language and theory for quantum music, to which we refer as Quantum Concept Music (QCM). This new music formalism is based on Categorical Quantum Mechanics (CQM), and more specifically, its diagrammatic incarnation Quantum Picturalism (QPict), which is heavily grounded on ZX-calculus. In fact, QCM is naturally inherited from CQM/QPict, given that the category-theoretic nature of the latter allows for varying underlying models, to process theories of real-world phenomena like music. Adopting a relational view of quantum theory—which is implicit in CQM/QPict—at QCM’s heart is the explicit notational representation of relations that exist within and between the key concepts of music composition, performance, and automation. QCM also enables one to directly translate quantum phenomena into music compositions in a both intuitively obvious, rigorous, and mechanical manner. Following this pattern, we propose a conceptual way of writing scores for musicians interacting like a Bell-pair under measurement, and outline how it can be live performed. While most of the Western classical music notation has heavily relied on linear representation of music–which does not always adequately capture the relational features of music–our approach is distinct by making the relational dimensions of music first-class citizens, augmented with quantum-native features. This quantum-based technique not only influences the music at the profound level of composition, but also has a direct impact on a live performance, and also provides a new template for automating music, e.g., in the context of AI-generation. Altogether, we initiate the creation of new music formalism that is powerful and efficient in capturing the interactive nature of music, both in terms of internal and external interactions, and goes beyond the boundaries of Western classical music notation, which allows to use it in many different genres and orchestrations.

Title: Environmental Taxes and Emissions: The Moderating Role of the Shadow Economy, AI, and ICT in OECD Countries
Abstract: Environmental taxes have received considerable attention as a fundamental policy for environmental regulation and sustainable development. However, empirical evidence found the contradictory relations between environmental taxation and emissions among OECD countries. This paper is aimed to analyze whether environmental taxation moderate the net effect of the shadow economy, AI adoption, and ICT penetration on CO<inf>2</inf> emissions in OECD countries. Limited by the availability of dataset, this paper chose 20 OECD countries and employed the fixed-effects model with clustered standard errors model and cross-sectional augmented autoregressive distributed lag model to check their relationships. Findings show that environmental taxes consistently reduce environmental emissions, underscoring their effectiveness as a policy tool for OECD economies. In contrast, the shadow economy worsens environmental performance, although its interaction with environmental taxes demonstrates that tax policy can partially offset the distortions caused by informality. AI adoption increases environmental quality, and interaction with environmental taxes further strengthens this effect, suggesting that AI can strengthen tax effectiveness. ICT shows no significant direct impact on environmental performance. However, its interaction with environmental taxes could reduce the emissions, indicating that tax outcomes vary with technological structure. This interaction indicates that ICT yields environmental benefits only when supported by strong fiscal frameworks. These results highlight that environmental taxation play a key role in reaching emission targets as a conditional policy tool rather than a universally effective instrument. Its performance depends on tax design, enforcement capacity, and the broader structural context, including informality and technological development. It contributes to the literature by offering empirical evidence on double dividend hypothesis and showing how fiscal instruments and technological progress interact with each other in reducing environmental emissions. The results imply that tax design should be aligned with country-specific and technological conditions to enhance policy effectiveness. Integrating environmental taxes with digital transformation strategies is important for mitigating environmental emissions of OECD countries.

Title: Deliberate practice in the age of artificial intelligence: how AI-assisted practice supports self-regulated learning and expert performance development in conservatory musicians
Abstract: Introduction – Deliberate practice is central to expert performance development, yet the conditions under which practice produces sustained gains remain contested. AI-assisted music practice applications provide adaptive feedback, intelligent scheduling, automated error detection, and performance analytics, potentially supporting deliberate practice. This study examined whether engagement with AI-assisted practice applications is longitudinally associated with expert performance development among conservatory musicians through self-regulated learning (SRL). Methods – A three-wave longitudinal study was conducted over a 16-week academic semester with a target sample of 600 conservatory musicians. Of these, 512 completed all three waves (85.3%). Temporal associations among AI-assisted practice engagement, SRL, and instructor-rated musical performance were examined. Results – Significant longitudinal associations supported the proposed pathway. Greater engagement with AI-assisted practice applications was associated with subsequent SRL, which was in turn associated with later instructor-rated musical performance. These findings are consistent with a mediating role of SRL in the association between AI-assisted practice engagement and expert performance development. Discussion – AI-assisted practice applications may support expert performance development by fostering self-regulatory processes conducive to deliberate practice. However, because the study was observational rather than randomized and involved heterogeneous AI applications rather than a standardized intervention, the findings should be interpreted as longitudinal associations rather than causal effects. AI-assisted practice applications are therefore best conceptualized as pedagogical supports that facilitate conditions for deliberate practice rather than as deliberate practice itself.

Title: Development and Implementation of an AI-based Evaluation Framework for Competency Assessment in Music Education Programs
Abstract: The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has necessitated a paradigm shift in music education competency assessment. This study developed and evaluated an AI-based evaluation framework for music education students using a Research and Development (R&D) design. The research was conducted in three phases: 1) needs assessment from 28 stakeholders, 2) framework development and validation by 9 experts, and 3) implementation with 32 senior music education students. Results showed a high demand for AI competency, particularly in adaptability (ⴳ = 4.59). The final framework comprises 5 dimensions and 14 primary indicators, validated by experts with high appropriateness (ⴳ = 4.51). Empirical implementation confirmed that the framework effectively assesses student competencies, with students achieving high performance across all domains (ⴳ = 2.79 on a 3.00 scale). This framework provides a robust tool for higher education institutions to integrate AI into music teacher training.

Title: Audio Strips Network (ASNet) and Amalgamated Audio Features (A2F): A Synergistic Approach for Audio Source Separation
Abstract: Audio source separation refers to the procedure of decomposing a mixed audio signal into its constituent components. This technique enables numerous applications, including creative music production, educational tools, karaoke, transcription, and music analysis. Despite the recent success of deep learning-based source separation techniques, these techniques often do not perform very accurately and do not provide high-quality separation of sources when many contain complex combinations in their mixtures. Source separation techniques generally rely on temporal or spectral features for analysis, which does not fully capture the complex dynamics of audio signals. To address these limitations, this paper proposes the amalgamated audio features (A2F), a hybrid representation combining temporal and spectral features. Then, the audio strip network (ASNet) is proposed, a novel framework designed to achieve clean and precise separation of individual audio sources with enhanced performance. ASNet utilizes A2F to separate sources more effectively. The model is trained and evaluated on the MUSDB, DSD100, and MUSDB18-HQ datasets, a benchmark for music source separation, and its standard measures, such as the signal-to-distortion ratio (SDR) and signal-to-interference ratio (SIR), are used to examine performance. ASNet achieves enhanced separation performance with SDR values of 12.63 for drums, 11.42 for vocal, 12.01 for bass, and 11.14 for other, and SIR values of 9.57 for drums, 9.61 for vocal, 9.66 for bass, and 9.67 for other. This advancement benefits musicians through high-quality remixing and creativity while aiding researchers in improving deep learning and hybrid audio processing models.

Title: Two-Stage DOA Estimation with Multi-Channel Attention Residual Network and Maximum Likelihood: A Multi-Feature Fusion Approach
Abstract: As a pivotal research direction in array signal processing, Direction-of-Arrival (DOA) estimation has been extensively applied in radar systems, wireless communications, and target tracking scenarios. Conventional subspace-dependent algorithms (represented by MUSIC and ESPRIT) tend to exhibit notable performance deterioration under adverse scenarios including low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), insufficient snapshots, and coherent signal environments. Meanwhile, pure deep learning (DL)-based estimation schemes are restricted by grid discretization errors in grid-based inference and limited diversity of spatial feature representations. To tackle these limitations, this paper presents a two-stage DOA estimation framework that integrates a Multi-Channel Attention Residual Network (MCARN) with Maximum Likelihood (ML) optimization. In the initial coarse estimation stage, the MCARN leverages six complementary feature inputs—namely the real and imaginary components, amplitude and phase spectra of the array covariance matrix, fourth-order cumulants, as well as the beam spectrum within the angular span of [−60°, 60°]—to fully mine spatial and statistical characteristics, enabling robust coarse DOA prediction and effectively shrinking the subsequent search domain. In the refinement stage, the ML estimator employs the coarse estimation results as prior information to conduct high-precision local searching, which removes grid quantization errors and further enhances estimation accuracy. Numerical simulation results validate that the proposed method surpasses classic subspace approaches and state-of-the-art DL-based estimators in both estimation accuracy and robustness under low SNR and single-snapshot conditions. Furthermore, it attains an excellent tradeoff between computational efficiency and estimation performance, exhibiting promising practicability for real-time engineering applications.

Title: Ultra-Short-Term Photovoltaic Power Forecasting Based on the Moirai Time Series Foundation Model
Abstract: Photovoltaic power forecasting is of great significance for power system dispatch and renewable energy integration. Traditional deep learning methods typically require collecting large amounts of historical data for independent training at each PV site, which incurs high computational costs and lacks flexibility when faced with newly grid-connected plants or changes in data input formats. The development of time series foundation models provides a new technical pathway to overcome this dilemma. This paper systematically evaluates the zero-shot generalization capability of the Moirai time series foundation model for ultra-short-term PV power forecasting tasks. In contrast to conventional full-scale training methods, Moirai keeps model weights completely frozen during the inference stage, requiring no gradient updates or fine-tuning. It can directly process historical sequences of arbitrary length and flexibly incorporate multiple types of exogenous covariates. This study designs evaluation cases from three dimensions: input sequence length, covariate combinations, and cross-site generalization. Experimental results demonstrate that Moirai exhibits stable forecasting performance across different input configurations and site scenarios under the zero-shot setting. The findings of this paper validate the applicability of general-purpose time series foundation models in the field of renewable energy forecasting.

Title: Toward Responsible and Privacy-Preserving Generation of Inpatient Clinical Discharge Notes Using Large Language Models
Abstract: Writing discharge notes (DNs) is a time-intensive task in inpatient care that contributes substantially to physician workload and burnout. Large language models (LLMs) offer potential opportunities to automate clinical documentation. However, concerns regarding accuracy, reliability, data privacy protection laws and data governance, and compliance with healthcare privacy remain. This study evaluated the performance of locally deployed, domain-adapted LLMs for generating German-language DN in internal medicine. In this retrospective study, electronic health record data from a Swiss tertiary care hospital were used. Clinical information from 3 inpatient scenarios served as input for the 3 open source LLMs (Mixtral 8×7B, Mixtral 8×22B, and LLaMA 3.1 70B). Zero-shot prompting, 4-shot in-context learning, and supervised finetuning using QLoRA were compared. Generated DNs were evaluated using automated metrics, blinded physician assessment with direct comparison of all relevant clinical information using the modified Physician Documentation Quality Instrument, and additionally an LLM-as-a-judge framework and a Turing Test. Across all evaluation methods, the fine-tuned Mixtral 8×7B model achieved the best overall performance compared with prompting-based approaches and larger nonspecialized models. Simpler cases consistently received higher-quality ratings. Physician inter-rater agreement was low, highlighting the challenges of objective quality assessment for clinical documentation. In a Turing Test, physicians were unable to reliably distinguish artificial intelligence-generated from clinician-authored DNs, performing at chance level, demonstrating that high-quality DN generation is feasible using locally deployed LLMs within secure hospital infrastructures. Domain-specific fine-tuning substantially improves performance and may enable practical deployment. Future work should address further hallucination mitigation, robustness across medical specialties, and real-world integration.
