Title: The Classical NCT Dataset: Collection of Non-chord Tone Annotated Score Data for Music Analysis
Abstract: This paper describes a newly constructed dataset of non-chord tones designed for applications in computational music analysis. Western music is fundamentally grounded in harmony theory and adheres not only to harmonic principles but also to grammatical conventions governing non-chord tones. However, non-chord tones have received limited attention in computational music research, which is probably due to the scarcity of available data. To address this gap, the Classical NCT Dataset is constructed by systematically analysing non-chord tones in the scores of 57 renowned classical compositions in collaboration with three music theory experts using a dedicated web-based analysis tool. Through statistical analysis of the dataset, the importance of non-chord tones in music information processing and their consistency with music theory were verified. Furthermore, in preparation for future dataset expansion, the problem of identifying tone types for each note from musical scores and harmonic information was formulated using both a Bayesian classifier and a deep learning model (Transformer), and their performance was compared. While the Bayesian classifier demonstrated superior performance, the results revealed that performance depends on the sample size of each class. The Classical NCT Dataset is expected to contribute to automatic music composition and music analysis systems.

Title: Carbon price forecasting through an interpretable CEEMDAN-CNN-BiGRU-Attention hybrid framework: evidence from China and the European Union carbon markets
Abstract: Against the backdrop of accelerating global carbon neutrality efforts, carbon markets have become important policy instruments for achieving emission reduction targets. However, their complex pricing mechanisms and pronounced nonlinear and nonstationary characteristics continue to challenge accurate forecasting. To address these issues, this study develops a hybrid forecasting framework integrating Complete Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition with Adaptive Noise (CEEMDAN), a convolutional neural network (CNN), a bidirectional gated recurrent unit (BiGRU), and an attention mechanism. CEEMDAN is used to reduce mode mixing and reveal multiscale price dynamics, while the CNN-BiGRU structure extracts local and bidirectional temporal features. The attention mechanism further assigns adaptive weights to informative temporal representations. SHapley Additive exPlanations are employed to quantify the contributions of explanatory variables, and a dynamic risk warning module is incorporated to identify abnormal price movements. The empirical analysis uses daily carbon emission allowance prices from the European Union market and eight regional pilot markets in China from 1 January 2014 to 13 August 2024. The results show that the proposed framework improves forecasting accuracy and stability across heterogeneous carbon markets. The interpretability analysis further reveals substantial regional differences in the effects of energy prices, financial market conditions, policy uncertainty, public sentiment, and environmental indicators. In addition, the 95th-percentile warning mechanism identifies abnormal price fluctuations in several regional markets. Overall, the proposed framework integrates forecasting, interpretability, and risk monitoring and provides analytical support for carbon market participants and regulatory authorities.

Title: Drone-Based Iot and Machine Learning Framework for Real-Time Factory Air Pollution Monitoring and Long-Term Prediction
Abstract: Monitoring air pollution around industrial facilities remains challenging because fixed monitoring stations can only provide measurements at specific locations. This study presents a drone-based air-quality monitoring framework that integrates UAV-mounted gas sensors with IoT communication, cloud processing, and machine learning. The developed payload measures CO<inf>2</inf>, CO, NO<inf>2</inf>, NO, and O<inf>2</inf>, along with temperature and GPS position, at a sampling rate of 1 Hz. The measurements are transmitted through a 4G LTE network to an AWS-based backend for storage and processing. A zoning approach is then applied to divide the monitored area into Green, Yellow, and Red zones according to WHO and NAAQS reference limits. For pollution prediction, Linear Regression, Random Forest, and LSTM models were evaluated using a 30-day Gaussian Plume simulation dataset containing approximately 2.6 million records. The LSTM model achieved the best overall performance, with an RZ of 0.94 and an RMSE of 3.21 ppm for CO<inf>2</inf>. The MAPE remained below 6.2% across the monitored pollutants. The resulting zone maps indicated that the higher-pollution regions were mainly concentrated within approximately 800 m of the simulated emission source. However, the current evaluation is based on simulated data and does not yet represent measurements from an operating industrial facility. Field testing with real sensor measurements and reference instruments is therefore required to assess the performance under actual conditions. The results nevertheless demonstrate the potential of combining UAV sensing, IoT connectivity, and machine learning for spatial air-quality monitoring and pollution forecasting.

Title: Music singing emotion classification and recognition method based on deep representation learning
Abstract: This paper proposes a music performance emotion classification and recognition method based on deep representation learning to improve accuracy. Firstly, an emotional vocabulary system is constructed, and feature parameters such as range, intensity, and rhythm are extracted based on mathematical modelling. Secondly, a multi-layer neural network model is constructed through deep representation learning to select the acoustic features with the highest correlation with emotional terms for encoding and dimensionality reduction. A deep learning architecture is designed that includes a dynamic input layer, embedding layer, convolutional layer, and maximum sentiment term pooling layer. Finally, unsupervised pre training and feature concatenation strategies are adopted to automatically mine and classify complex emotional patterns in music singing. The experimental results show that the proposed method achieves an accuracy of 90 to 98 in extracting emotional features of music singing, and a classification recognition accuracy of 97.32 to 99.74 .

Title: Detail-Enhanced High-Resolution Warping-Only Field Transforms for Particle Image Velocimetry
Abstract: Particle image velocimetry (PIV) is a technique for nonintrusive flow field measurement. Constrained by the cost volume component, existing deep-learning-based PIV methods face inherent bottlenecks in high-resolution scenarios. On the one hand, it is difficult to bear the memory load caused by high-resolution features and has to rely on multiple downsampling to use low-resolution features for modeling, resulting in the loss of small-scale flow details. On the other hand, the memory consumption when training and estimating high-resolution PIV images increases exponentially. Images with resolution above 2k ×2k cannot be estimated directly, and the block estimation-result stitching strategy is adopted, which further destroys the physical consistency of the flow field during stitching. To address these issues, we propose the detail-enhanced high-resolution warping-only field transforms (DH-WAFT), a PIV-oriented optical flow estimation method optimized for high-resolution scenarios. DH-WAFT employs a feature extraction method tailored for small targets, which further eliminates redundant noise and reduces memory consumption. A multisource feature fusion module based on a residual network is designed to model the spatial correlation between large-scale flow fields and small-scale particles. A detail complement branch with dynamic weight is introduced to adaptively compensate the microdisplacement information in different resolution scenes. DH-WAFT is trained on publicly available synthetic PIV data and evaluated on both synthetic and experimental datasets, demonstrating superior accuracy and performance. On the 256 × 256 synthetic dataset, the average endpoint error (AEPE) of DH-WAFT is relatively reduced by 57.4 % compared with RAFT256-PIV and 47.3 % compared with Twin-PIVNet. In addition, this study also conducts spatial resolution experiments, which confirms that DH-WAFT is able to retain the fluid structure at a finer scale. More importantly, DH-WAFT shows excellent performance when dealing with high-resolution experimental data, covering 512×512, 1k ×1k, and 2k ×2k levels. Finally, DH-WAFT carries out the necessary ablation experiment discussion on accuracy, memory consumption, and inference latency.

Title: Development of a Multi-Instrument System for Reproducible Hyperspectral Imaging
Abstract: While machine learning has seen huge success in standard image analysis, its application in critical domains like forensic science and material analysis is hindered by a lack of consistent, high-dimensional spectral data. The creation of such datasets is currently limited by the challenges of co-registering data across disconnected instruments and guaranteeing measurement consistency. This paper presents the design, implementation, and validation of a comprehensive measurement system that integrates high-resolution RGB, visible-range hyperspectral, and near-infrared hyperspectral cameras into a unified, automated platform. Beyond the hardware integration, the system features a custom software suite that enforces a standardised measurement protocol through real-time feedback on geometric alignment and illumination uniformity. The system's performance was validated through a Gage Repeatability and Reproducibility (Gage R&R) user study. Results demonstrate that the software-guided protocol enables operators to achieve high luminance uniformity (> 83%) and quantifiable geometric precision. By formalising the acquisition methodology and quantifying operator uncertainty, this work provides a scalable solution for generating the verifiable, 'ground truth' multi-modal datasets required to advance trusted machine learning models.

Title: Clinically Interpretable Prediction Models of Stroke Functional Outcomes: A National Cohort Study of Adults in Inpatient Rehabilitation Facilities in the United States
Abstract: Objective: To predict self-care and mobility function at discharge from inpatient rehabilitation for adults with stroke using only variables from the Inpatient Rehabilitation Facility Patient Assessment Instrument, which are mandated in the United States by the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services. Design: Retrospective cohort study. Setting: Inpatient rehabilitation facilities in the United States. Participants: National sample (N=43,745) of adults with a primary diagnosis of stroke who were admitted to inpatient rehabilitation facility in FY2023. Interventions: Not applicable. Main Outcome Measures: Section GG self-care and mobility subscales. Results: We used random forest regression, an ensemble machine learning approach that trains multiple models and combines their predictions to improve overall performance. We then created global summary trees from the random forest models to visually represent the outcomes and aid in clinical interpretation. After data cleaning and quality checks, 39,870 records were available for analysis. Records were divided into training (n=26,580), validation (n=6645), and test (n=6645) datasets. Each model included 29 predictors. Random forest models explained 58% (root-mean-squared error=5.6) and 62% (root-mean-squared error=13.3) of the total variation in self-care and mobility outcomes, respectively, when applied to the test split. In both summary trees, the respective functional measure at admission was the strongest predictor. Bladder and bowel incontinence were strong predictors of both self-care and mobility outcomes at discharge. Conclusions: The results show that standard data elements from mandatory Medicare reporting can generate robust, clinically interpretable prediction models of self-care and mobility function at discharge from inpatient rehabilitation for adults with stroke. Application of such models in practice can inform treatment planning and early discharge preparation to support personalized rehabilitation approaches.

Title: OmniFysics: Towards Physical Intelligence Evolution via Omni-Modal Signal Processing and Network Optimization
Abstract: The autonomous evolution of networked AI systems relies heavily on robust environmental perception. However, physical understanding remains brittle in current models because key physical signals are visually ambiguous and sparsely represented in web-scale data. To bridge the gap between data-centric learning and knowledge-based physical rules, we present OmniFysics, a compact omni-modal network that unifies signal processing and understanding across images, audio, video, and text. To enable autonomous optimization and inject explicit physical knowledge, we construct a dynamic physical data engine. Within this engine, FysicsAny acts as an adaptive mechanism that produces physics-grounded supervision by mapping salient objects to prototype-conditioned, physically plausible physical-attribute priors via hierarchical retrieval and physics-law-constrained signal verification. Concurrently, FysicsOmniCap distills web videos utilizing advanced audio-visual cross-modal signal processing, generating high-fidelity data pairs that emphasize dynamic physical cues. We optimize the OmniFysics network through staged multimodal alignment and evolutive instruction tuning, integrating latent-space flow matching for generation and an adaptive intent router for efficient execution. Experiments demonstrate that this evolutive optimization paradigm not only achieves competitive performance on standard multimodal benchmarks but also significantly advances physics-oriented evaluations.

Title: A deep neural network for CrIS cloud detection and transfer to HIRAS via implicit contrastive learning
Abstract: Accurately identifying whether a field of view of satellite hyperspectral infrared sounders is clear or cloudy is critical for geophysical parameter retrieval and meteorological applications. In this study, a deep neural network is developed for cloud detection in Cross-track Infrared Sounder (CrIS) data and subsequently transferred to the High-spectral Resolution Infrared Atmospheric Sounder (HIRAS) onboard the Fengyun (FY)-3D satellite. Specifically, a deep convolutional neural network is designed for CrIS cloud detection, leveraging the cloud mask products from the collocated Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS) onboard the same platform as labels for supervised learning. To mitigate the inherent discrepancies between CrIS and HIRAS observations, an implicit contrastive learning strategy is introduced to facilitate model transfer to HIRAS. The proposed model achieves an overall accuracy of 93.32% on the global CrIS data test set, demonstrating highly consistent performance across daytime (94.30%)/night-time (92.34%) and land (93.24%)/ocean (93.36%) samples. Evaluations using HIRAS data indicate robust transferability, despite underlying differences in instrument calibration and noise characteristics. Case studies further illustrate the model’s capacity to reliably capture cloud features across diverse atmospheric conditions. Furthermore, the implicit contrastive learning significantly improves detection performance for challenging samples in complex environments, such as regions affected by haze or sun glint.

Title: A Seven-Year Higher-Order Ambisonics Recording Corpus: Dataset, Methodology, and a Co-Located Spherical Microphone Array Comparison
Abstract: Research in spatial audio quality assessment, spatial machine learning, and immersive production is constrained by the scarcity of diverse, well-documented Higher-Order Ambisonics (HOA) recordings: existing public datasets are dominated by 1st-order, synthetic, or speech-only material. This paper presents an openly available seven-year HOA recording corpus comprising 23 sessions captured between April 2019 and January 2026 across concert halls, churches, studios, and outdoor environments, with musical content ranging from solo piano to 60+ performer ensembles. The corpus was captured primarily with a Zylia ZM-1 (19 MEMS capsules, 3rd order), with comparative material from a Harpex Spcmic (84 capsules, 5th order) and a Saramonic SR-VRMIC (4 electret capsules, 1st order); all recordings are provided in B-format using the AmbiX (ACN/SN3D) convention. A co-located comparison of the three arrays under matched acoustic conditions shows that capture systems of the same nominal Ambisonics order deliver different per-order energy: the ZM-1 exhibits 27.4 dB of energy rollofffrom 0th to 3rd order, against 8.4 dB for the Spcmic (paired difference 19.0 dB), a property of each array with its proprietary encoder, not of the hardware alone; re-encoding the deposited ZM-1 capsule signals with open encoders moves its delivered 3rd-order energy over a range of about 41 dB. We document the full recording and signal-processing methodology, measured room-acoustic parameters for the primary venue (RT60 = 1.97 s), and integrated-loudness quality metrics for all 74 rendered files. The corpus and metadata are released under a CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license, and the reproducible analysis pipeline under CC BY 4.0.

Title: Consideration Data Augmentation Using Frequency Characteristics for Vocal Separation in Monaural Music Source Signals
Abstract: In recent years, with the widespread adoption of music streaming services and video-sharing sites, there has been growing demand for approaches in music production that are both low-cost and easy to implement. However, single-track recording with a single microphone results in all parts being recorded as a mixed signal, which limits the flexibility of post-recording editing. To address this issue, sound source separation technology utilizing deep learning has garnered significant attention. However, separation accuracy tends to decline when dealing with sound sources that overlap in frequency bands or harmonic structures, such as vocals and guitars. Therefore, in this study, we focused on single-track recordings captured with a single microphone and applied a sound source separation method based on Conv-TasNet to music signals in order to separate the vocal component from the mixed audio. In particular, we applied data augmentation that alters the frequency characteristics of the guitar signal to increase the diversity of guitar timbres, thereby aiming to improve the model's generalization performance under conditions of frequency overlap with the vocals. In our experiments, we compared the separation performance with and without data augmentation. The results confirmed that using the proposed data augmentation improved vocal separation performance.

Title: Reliability, quality, and readability of large language models in carpal tunnel syndrome: A comparative cross-linguistic, cross-sectional observational study
Abstract: Background: AI-based chatbots are increasingly used for health information, while cross-linguistic studies suggest that response performance may vary by language. Given the high prevalence of carpal tunnel syndrome (CTS), this study evaluated the reliability, quality, patient education suitability, and readability of AI-generated responses to CTS questions in English and Turkish. Materials and methods: Seventeen patient-centered CTS questions were directed to ChatGPT<sup>®</sup> (GPT-5 Mini), Gemini<sup>®</sup> 3 Flash, and Claude<sup>®</sup> 4.5 Sonnet, using zero-shot prompting across 102 independent sessions in English and Turkish. Responses were evaluated for reliability, quality, and patient education using mDISCERN (MD), Global Quality Score (GQS), and the Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool (PEMAT). Readability was assessed via Flesch Reading Ease (English) and Ateşman Index (Turkish). Friedman and Wilcoxon tests with Bonferroni correction were applied. Results: Significant inter-model differences were observed in English across all metrics (p < 0.05), with Gemini achieving higher MD and PEMAT scores than ChatGPT and Claude (p < 0.01). Cross-language differences were observed in mDISCERN scores, while Gemini showing a significant difference in favor of English (r = 0.93; p < 0.001). None of the models met recommended readability levels in either language. Conclusion: AI-generated CTS information varied by model and language. Differences in MD scores should be interpreted cautiously because this instrument partly reflects the provision of references and does not directly assess factual clinical accuracy. None of the evaluated models achieved recommended readability levels for patient education. These findings support the use of AIs as supplementary rather than standalone sources of CTS-related patient information.

Title: Aboveground Biomass Estimation of Indian Sundarbans Using Machine Learning Based SAR-Optical Synergistic Approach
Abstract: This study targets the Indian Sundarbans, the world’s largest tidal mangrove forest, to improve aboveground biomass (AGB) estimation by integrating multi-source remote sensing data with machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) techniques. Optical data from Sentinel-2 Multispectral Instrument (MSI) and Landsat-8 Operational Land Imager (OLI) were combined with C-band and L-band Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) products. Various vegetation indices, radar metrics, polarimetric decompositions, textural features, and transformed bands were extracted. Field measurements from 200 plots in the Sundarban Biosphere Reserve served as ground truth points. The Feed Forward Deep Neural Network (FFDNN) model using L-band SAR and optical synergy achieved the highest accuracy (R²=0.82, RMSE = 36.12 Mg/ha, MAE = 30.59 Mg/ha). The XGBoost model also showed strong performance (R² >0.70), producing consistent spatial AGB maps and performing best with C-band data, highlighting algorithm-sensor dependencies. The findings support enhanced forest carbon stock assessments, inform conservation strategies like REDD+, and contribute to global climate goals such as the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and the Paris Agreement.

Title: Evaluation of a Quantized 1D-CNN for Real-Time ECG Arrhythmia Classification on a Low-Power Embedded System
Abstract: This paper details the methodology for adapting a deep learning model for a resource-constrained environment, focusing on post-training integer quantization to reduce memory footprint and computational load. It presents the design, implementation, and performance evaluation of a networked embedded system acting like a computational node to support a local wearable device in the arrhythmia classification using a lightweight 1D-Convolutional Neural Network (1D-CNN) on an ESP32-S3 microcontroller. In this architecture, the embedded board operates as a low-cost network node that offloads computations the wearable cannot perform locally, and the reported latency accounts for both data transmission and inference. The system's capabilities are evaluated using the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database. Performance metrics were measured directly on the target hardware, demonstrating a classification accuracy of 96% with a consistent inference latency of approximately 51 ms per cardiac cycle. This corresponds to a processing throughput of nearly 20 classifications per second, validating the system's suitability for real-time, beat-by-beat analysis. The results validate the feasibility of deploying accurate, low-latency cardiac measurement and analysis instruments on low-cost, lowpower embedded platforms.

Title: Three-Dimensional Evaluation of Mandibular Asymmetry in Adult Violin and Viola Players: A Prospective Cone-Beam Computed Tomography Study
Abstract: Long-term violin and viola performances involve sustained asymmetric loading of the craniofacial skeleton; however, their association with 3-dimensional mandibular asymmetry has not been well characterized. This prospective study aimed to evaluate mandibular asymmetry using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) in adult violin and viola players who have undergone prolonged intensive musical training since childhood. We prospectively included 20 adult violin and viola players, enrolled in or who graduated from the College of Music, Seoul National University. Participants underwent standardized questionnaire-based assessments, including playing history, practice characteristics, and playing-related musculoskeletal symptoms. Three-dimensional CBCT images were reconstructed following standardized reorientation. Bilateral mandibular morphology was evaluated using linear measurements (condylion-gonion, mandibular notch-gonion, and gonion-menton distances), hemimandibular volume, and asymmetry indices (AI). Associations between mandibular asymmetry and questionnaire-derived playing-related variables were analyzed using univariate regression analyses. Handspan measurements were collected as secondary outcome measures to evaluate skeletal laterality associated with prolonged unilateral hand training, providing an additional indicator of musculoskeletal adaptation beyond the craniofacial skeleton. Three-dimensional CBCT demonstrated right-sided predominance in the condylion-gonion distance, mandibular notch-gonion distance, and hemimandibular volume. The gonion-menton distance showed a small, nonsignificant, left-sided predominance. All hand measurements showed a left-sided predominance. No playing-history variable was significantly associated with directional side differences. Adult violin and viola players exhibited characteristic 3-dimensional mandibular asymmetry, with a right-sided predominance of the ramus and hemimandibular volume, accompanied by left-sided hand-span dominance. These findings suggest that prolonged asymmetric mechanical loading during intensive musical training may contribute to adaptive skeletal laterality.

Title: AI-Based Preprocessing and R-Squared Weighted Federated Aggregation for Robust Healthcare Signal Imputation
Abstract: Federated learning is an emerging paradigm for collaborative model training in healthcare applications where sensitive patient data cannot be centralized due to privacy concerns; however, missing values in physiological signals remain a major challenge, often leading to degraded model accuracy and unstable convergence. To address this issue, this work presents an AI-based preprocessing framework that combines advanced imputation methods, including K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Autoencoder reconstruction, and Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN), with classical baselines such as mean and median imputation. Building on this preprocessing stage, this study proposes a novel R-squared weighted aggregation strategy that dynamically scales clients’ contributions based on their prediction quality. The experiments were conducted on BIDMC physiological datasets with missingness rates ranging from 0.1 to 0.5 across multiple federated clients. Results show that weighted aggregation converges to lower RMSE and MAE than classical FedAvg, especially in the early rounds where high client heterogeneity exists. The proposed method adapts to client quality, thereby providing robust convergence and stability, resulting in balanced performance. These results demonstrate that combining AI-based preprocessing with R-squared weighted aggregation effectively improves the reliability of federated learning in healthcare IoT systems. The proposed approach presents a scalable and feasible solution for real-world scenarios where data incompleteness and client heterogeneity are inevitable.

Title: Machine Learning-Based Multiclass Classification of Benign Vocal Fold Lesions Using Acoustic, Clinical, and Patient-Reported Features
Abstract: Objective: To develop and evaluate a multiclass random forest classifier for distinguishing among five types of benign vocal fold lesions using acoustic and phonatory parameters, patient-reported outcomes (PROs), demographic characteristics, and occupational voice demands. Methods: This retrospective study included 217 adults with confirmed diagnoses of vocal fold nodules, vocal fold polyps, intracordal cysts, Reinke’s edema, or sulcus vocalis at a tertiary otolaryngology center. Features included five acoustic parameters (fundamental frequency, jitter, shimmer, maximum phonation time, s/z ratio), three PRO instruments, the voice handicap index, voice-related quality of life, and reflux symptom index (RSI), and demographic and occupational variables. A class-weighted random forest classifier was evaluated using stratified five-fold cross-validation with bootstrap-derived 95% confidence intervals; multinomial logistic regression and linear support vector machine served as comparators. Results: The random forest classifier outperformed the comparator models, achieving accuracy of 0.576, balanced accuracy of 0.476, macro-F1 of 0.479, and a macro-averaged area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.76. The highest class-level F1 scores were observed for sulcus vocalis (0.703) and vocal fold polyps (0.625); intracordal cysts showed the lowest recall (0.111), reflecting acoustic overlap with vocal fold polyps. Top 2 accuracy was approximately 74%. Fundamental frequency, RSI, and maximum phonation time were the highest-ranked predictors. Conclusion: A multidimensional random forest framework incorporating acoustic measures, PROs, and occupational voice demand demonstrated potential for classifying benign vocal fold lesions. Acoustic parameters alone may not adequately distinguish among these lesions, and the inclusion of patient-reported data may improve model performance. A top 2 accuracy of 74% supports utility as a pre-endoscopic decision-support tool.

Title: Heat transfer and flow characteristics of multi-layer manifold microchannel heat sinks
Abstract: To address the bottlenecks of high heat flux and large-area chip heat dissipation caused by the development of artificial intelligence and ultra-large-scale integrated circuits, this paper proposes and systematically evaluates three novel multi-layer manifold microchannel (MMC) cooling structures: rectangular (RMMC), square (RTMMC), and cylindrical (STMMC) fin arrays. A three-dimensional numerical model is established to analyze the thermal transfer efficiency, flow resistance, and temperature field distribution characteristics under heat load levels ranging from 50 W/cm<sup>2</sup> to 250 W/cm<sup>2</sup> and various inlet flow rates. The results show that RMMC exhibits the best comprehensive heat dissipation performance, achieving lower average temperature and higher temperature uniformity. STMMC has the lowest pressure drop, but poor heat transfer capacity and temperature uniformity. RTMMC shows strong heat transfer potential at high flow rates. The findings of this study offer a theoretical foundation for the optimal design of liquid cooling structures for large-area chips such as high-performance computing (HPC), GPU, and AI accelerators.

Title: Prediction of revision adenoidectomy in pediatric patients: a 10-year retrospective study
Abstract: Objective – This study aimed to identify risk factors for revision adenoidectomy in children and to develop and validate a clinical model for individualized risk prediction to support clinical decision-making. Methods – A total of 222 patients were selected via a nested case-control design from a source cohort of 16,457 children who underwent adenoidectomy at Children's Hospital of Soochow University. The dataset was randomly split into a training set and a validation set at a 7:3 ratio. Independent predictors were identified through univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses, and seven predictive models were constructed for comparison. The final model's performance was evaluated based on its discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, AUC), calibration (calibration plot), and clinical utility (decision curve analysis, DCA). Results – Multivariate analysis identified six independent risk factors for revision adenoidectomy: adenoid size, surgical instrument type, concurrent tonsillotomy during the initial surgery, allergic rhinitis, otitis media with effusion, and perioperative antibiotic use. Among seven compared models, the logistic regression model showed the best discriminative ability with an AUC of 0.921 in the validation set. A nomogram and a freely accessible web application were developed to facilitate bedside risk calculation. Conclusion – This study provides the first validated clinical prediction model for revision adenoidectomy in children. The model demonstrates excellent performance and can help clinicians accurately identify children at high risk of needing a revision surgery.

Title: Spatiotemporal Deep Learning for Robust Depression Severity Classification in Clinical Settings
Abstract: Depression is among the most prevalent and disabling mental health disorders worldwide, yet its clinical diagnosis still depends largely on subjective self-report instruments and expert judgment, which are difficult to scale and prone to inter-rater variability. Automated, objective assessment of depression severity from observable behavior could substantially extend access to screening, but most existing video-based approaches rely on static images or shallow temporal modelling and are validated on small or demographically homogeneous datasets, limiting their clinical generalizability. We propose a deep learning model that classifies depression severity from facial videos. It is evaluated on a real clinical dataset of 177 participants, including healthy controls and patients with mild, moderate, and severe depression. The framework couples a ConvNeXt-Tiny spatial backbone, enhanced with Squeeze-and-Excitation and Convolutional Block Attention modules, with a 256-unit Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network applied frame-wise through a time-distributed design to model the temporal dynamics of facial behavior. Severe class imbalance is mitigated through weighted categorical cross-entropy and targeted data augmentation, and patient-level stratification is enforced so that no participant contributes frames to both the training and evaluation splits. Under participant-level five-fold cross-validation, the proposed model achieves strong classification performance across all four severity levels, attaining 82.7% accuracy, a macro-averaged F1-score of 78.9%, and a macro-averaged AUC of 0.917 on held-out participants, and outperforming the strongest single-backbone baseline (Swin Transformer, 71.2% accuracy) by 11.5 percentage points. We further examine the validation protocol and the role of strict patient-level separation in interpreting these results, situating them against the leakage risk inherent in densely sampled video. The proposed framework offers a lightweight, behaviorally grounded, and reproducible approach to automated depression severity assessment, with direct relevance to scalable clinical screening.

Title: DIVERSITY, EQUITY, AND INCLUSION IN ORGANIZATIONS: A FRESH VIEW THROUGH GRANULAR INTERACTION THINKING THEORY
Abstract: Aim/Purpose This article introduces the Granular Interaction Thinking Theory (GITT) – a sociopsychological theory grounded in an information-processing perspective – to offer a novel lens for understanding diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) in organizations. Background DEI policies are vital instruments for addressing social inequality within organizations. However, the growing backlash against DEI efforts and inconsistent empirical outcomes highlight the need for deeper theoretical inquiry. Methodology Conceptual development. Contribution GITT complements established social (e.g., Social Identity Theory, the Information and Decision-Making Perspective, and Intersectionality Theory) and philosophical theories (e.g., Epistemic Injustice, Justice as Fairness, and Discourse Ethics) by providing an information-theoretic framework for effectively managing informational diversity and entropy. Findings Existing frameworks often overlook a crucial dimension: the informational dynamics of diverse organizational systems. GITT–DEI Framework conceptualizes diversity as expanding informational inputs, equity as enabling fair access to influence, and inclusion as facilitating reciprocal exchange and integration. While well-designed DEI initiatives enhance adaptability, creativity, and long-term value by expanding informational diversity, they also raise informational entropy. If left unmanaged, the increasing entropy can lead to higher energy and resource demands, potentially undermining organizational coherence and performance. The framework proposes an optimal entropy zone bounded by the Capture Threshold and the Sufficiency Threshold, within which meaningful plurality is preserved without exceeding organizational processing capacity. Recommendations Organizations can apply the framework through five interrelated mechanisms: for Practitioners filtering, weighting, integration, feedback, and monitoring. Informational inputs should be evaluated using transparent, context-sensitive, and contestable criteria, while AI-supported processes should remain explainable, auditable, and subject to meaningful human oversight. Recommendations The GITT-DEI Framework opens avenues for empirical validation and for new for Researchers DEI metrics. Future researchers can use the framework to estimate the actual optimal entropy zone for an organization or to simulate decision-making under varying levels of diversity and process structures to identify optimal configurations. The Equitable-channel, Entropy-zone, and Feedback-correction propositions derived from the framework can be translated into empirical research. Impact on Society More transparent and inclusive organizational informing processes may support fairer, more accountable, and better-informed decisions. In public organizations, such improvements may contribute to more responsive public services and greater consideration of diverse stakeholder knowledge. Future Research Future studies should empirically estimate the Capture and Sufficiency Thresholds and test whether decision processes within the proposed optimal entropy zone exhibit less informational exclusion and overload. Longitudinal, experimental, and simulation studies could examine how channel accessibility, weighting rules, feedback mechanisms, processing capacity, and AI assistance shape entropy trajectories and organizational outcomes.

Title: Correlations Between Master Adaptive Learners’ Characteristics and Anatomy Performance in an Active and Game-based Anatomy Learning
Abstract: Master Adaptive Learners (MALs) can adjust their learning strategies to overcome challenges, a key trait for success in complex subjects like anatomy. This study explored the correlation between MAL characteristics—curiosity, motivation, growth mindset, and resilience—and anatomy performance in an active, game-based learning environment. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 246 first-year medical students at Hasanuddin University in 2022. The anatomy course used blended, active learning, and game-based learning methods. MAL traits were measured using validated Indonesian-language instruments: the Curiosity and Exploration Inventory-II, Academic Motivation Scale short form, Growth Mindset Scale, and Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale. Anatomy performance was assessed through a comprehensive final exam. Non-parametric Spearman's rank correlation was applied due to non-normal data distribution. Students achieved a high average score (mean = 76.7, standard deviation (SD) = 16.2). Most MAL traits showed no significant correlation with performance: curiosity, motivation, and resilience (p > 0.05). However, growth mindset demonstrated a weak but significant positive correlation (r = 0.26, p < 0.001). In conclusion, while active learning may support student success regardless of MAL traits, the growth mindset was modestly linked to better performance. Curriculum strategies that cultivate a growth mindset may enhance learning outcomes in anatomy education.

Title: Improved point cloud segmentation algorithms for in situ individual plant phenotyping and weight prediction of Chinese cabbage plants using UAV imagery
Abstract: With the advancement of precision agriculture and modern breeding techniques, large-scale, efficient, and in situ acquisition of plant phenotypic data has become a critical challenge in research. Traditional manual measurement methods are inefficient and struggle to meet the demand for high-throughput phenotypic data in modern breeding. Consequently, this study proposes a method based on low-altitude drones and three-dimensional (3D) point cloud analysis to achieve in situ, nondestructive phenotypic extraction and weight prediction for individual Chinese cabbage plants. First, RGB images are captured in the field using unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). Large-scale 3D point clouds are reconstructed through structure from motion with multiview stereo technology. Subsequently, an enhanced graph convolutional neural network (AW-GNN) is proposed, integrating wavelet convolution, adaptive graph structure learning, and attention mechanisms to improve the accuracy and robustness of point cloud semantic segmentation. Building on this foundation, a morphology-guided watershed clustering algorithm is introduced. High-density segmentation of individual plants can be achieved in crowded environments by integrating two-dimensional canopy height maps with 3D point cloud spatial information. Based on the segmentation results, 3D phenotypic parameters, such as plant height, canopy width, and volume, are extracted. Individual plant weight prediction models are constructed using machine learning methods, including support vector regression (SVR) and random forest. Experimental results demonstrate that AW-GNN achieves an Intersection over Union (IoU) of 91.63% in point cloud semantic segmentation, significantly outperforming existing mainstream models. Morphological watershed clustering effectively mitigates undersegmentation and oversegmentation problems encountered by traditional methods under dense plant conditions. For individual plant weight prediction, the SVR model delivers optimal performance with a validation set R<sup>2</sup> of 0.8691 and root mean square error of 0.2810 kg. This study demonstrates the feasibility of achieving individual plant phenotyping and weight prediction in large-scale in situ scenarios using a UAV platform and improved point cloud segmentation algorithms, thereby providing an effective technical approach for high-throughput plant phenotyping analysis and digital breeding decision-making.

Title: Damage Assessment of PC Beams by Integrating Multi-scale Features of Visible and Invisible Crack Images
Abstract: Prestressed concrete (PC) bridges are widely used in the road network and often suffer structural damage such as cracks during service. Timely and effective assessment of these damages is crucial for ensuring bridge operation safety. Cracks serve as a visual manifestation of structural damage. Utilizing digital image technology for multi-faceted characterization of cracks and establishing their intrinsic relationship with structural damage states represents an effective approach for rapidly evaluating structural conditions. Accordingly, a multi-feature characterization method integrating explicit geometric texture features and implicit multifractal features of crack images was proposed in this paper, constructing a feature system with forty-five quantitative indicators. Through static failure tests of PC beams with different corrosion levels, images of the entire crack propagation process were systematically collected. Combined with the load-bearing ratio (as a damage factor), a damage prediction dataset containing 113 valid samples was established. Using various machine learning algorithms, this study systematically compared modeling performance under three feature engineering strategies: combined features, explicit features only, and multifractal features only. The consistency of model performance across different test beams and the generalization capability across structures were evaluated. Results show that features extracted from crack images correlate clearly with the damage factor, with explicit features exhibiting more pronounced correlations. Multifractal spectrum parameters and generalized fractal dimensions evolve regularly with increasing load, showing distinct distribution characteristics in intervals of positive and negative weight coefficients, which validates the effectiveness of the proposed multi-scale crack quantification system. Across all strategies, the MLP model achieves superior robustness in modeling the damage factor. The combined feature strategy achieves significantly better prediction accuracy than any single-feature strategy. Models show strong consistency across different test beams, with minor influence from individual sample variations. In structural-level transfer experiments, the combined feature strategy exhibits the best generalization ability, significantly outperforming the explicit-feature-only strategy, indicating that multifractal features provide valuable supplementary information in cross-structure prediction. The proposed explicit-implicit multi-scale feature fusion framework effectively reveals the intrinsic relationship between crack evolution and structural damage, offering a reliable approach for intelligent crack identification and quantitative damage assessment of highway bridges.

Title: Music Genre Classification Algorithm Based on Multi-Scale Fusion
Abstract: In the era of music streaming, the vast volume of digital music resources renders manual classification impractical. Although deep learning has achieved significant advances in music genre classification tasks, existing methods still face challenges such as insufficient feature extraction, low classification accuracy, loss of temporal sequence information, and limited dataset sizes. This study addresses these challenges in several ways: first, to tackle the problem of varying music durations affecting classification accuracy, log-Mel spectrograms are generated from segmented audio data; second, to improve classification accuracy on small datasets, we propose HybridNet, a deep learning model that employs a deep multi-scale fusion module to extract richer feature information. Subsequently, to further mitigate the loss of temporal information, we introduce a bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) layer resulting in the Bi-HybridNet model, which captures key sequential information in both forward and backward directions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves 86.92% accuracy on the FMA-small dataset, indicating improved classification performance over classical models. This study provides a practical technical solution for music genre classification, offering certain reference values in feature extraction and temporal modeling.

Title: Analysis and division of full-band errors in optical surfaces
Abstract: Precisely separating full-band surface errors is a cornerstone of high-performance optical manufacturing and testing. However, traditional methods rely on subjective frequency band definitions and manual filtering, which leads to inconsistent evaluation standards and introduces analysis errors. Meanwhile, existing data-driven methods mechanically fit noisy manual labels, lacking physical consistency. To address this issue, this paper presents a scale-adaptive physics-aware deep learning framework powered by a dual-domain physics-aware network, which extracts error features by imposing physical constraints in the frequency domain: a specifically shaped spectral domain selective attention mechanism is designed for a low-frequency error with a deterministic spectral envelope; an adaptive learnable spectral gating is designed for mid-frequency error with randomness and anisotropy. Experiments indicate that this network outperforms conventional models under adopted evaluation metrics and exhibits physics-constrained extraction behaviour. This helps mitigate measurement noise and subjective variability introduced by manual filtering, yielding results with improved spectral and physical consistency. Furthermore, it eliminates the reliance on high-performance computing hardware, thereby enabling millisecond-level real-time inference on a standard computer, which greatly facilitates practical engineering deployment. Based on these findings, this study proposes a generalised frequency band division method based on normalised spatial frequency, providing a normalised-frequency-based method for a more consistent cross-scale and cross-instrument frequency band error division.

Title: XAI-BDPH-Net: Explainable Hybrid Deep Learning for Transparent Personalized Healthcare and Clinical Decision Support
Abstract: To develop a framework called XAI-BDPH-Net, a hybrid explainable AI model combining SHAP (SHapley Additive Explanations) and LIME (Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations) for healthcare analytics that gives transparent predictions and decision support in the context of personalized healthcare. XAI-BDPH-Net consists of a Deep Neural Network (DNN) encoder, a Bidirectional LSTM (Bi-LSTM) for modeling temporal EHR, a weighted ensemble fusion layer, and XGBoost gradient boosting. SHAP gives a global and local feature importance explanation whereas LIME gives an instance level interpretable approximation. The framework is tested on 9,500 multimodal patient records (MIMIC-III, UCI Heart Disease, Pima Diabetes, NHANES), and it is split into 80% train and 20% test; 5- fold cross validation is used as well. Baselines: LR, RF, XGBoost standalone, DNN, Bi-LSTM, BDPH-Net (without XAI).XAI-BDPHNet overcomes the critical black-box limitation of deep learning in clinical settings by mathematically grounded explanations at both a global (population-level) and local (patient-level) scale, which allow clinicians to have confidence and take action on the AI recommendations. The combination of SHAP and LIME guarantees that all predictions and its respective research come with clear feature attributions, facilitating data-driven decision-making and regulatory alignment with FDA AI/ML guidelines and EU AI Act requirements. XAI-BDPH-Net achieves Accuracy = 97.14%, Precision = 96.87%, Recall = 97.02%, F1 = 96.94%, AUC-ROC = 0.9841, Specificity = 97.31%, MCC = 0.9341 outperforming all baselines: LR (76.34%), RF (84.12%), XGBoost (87.23%), DNN (89.41%), Bi-LSTM (91.87%), BDPH-Net-NoXAI (93.12%). This framework correctly classifies 1,841 of 1,900 test cases with just 59 misclassifications (3.1% error rate). The significant potential of XAI-BDPH-Net for explainable AI to aid non-communicable disease management contributes to the UN Sustainable Development Goal 3 (Good Health and Well-being), while its integration of AI to assist in early risk stratification of noncommunicable diseases holds promise for reducing premature death rates among the population, thereby addressing the UN Sustainable Development Goal 10 (Reduced Inequalities).

Title: Temporal Prediction Alignment for Short-Duration Acoustic Scene Classification
Abstract: Short-duration acoustic scene classification must infer a recording-level environment from a local excerpt with potentially incomplete or unrepresentative evidence. We characterize the resulting local-global disagreement and variation among sibling segments as temporal prediction mismatch. To address this problem, we propose the Temporal Prediction Alignment Framework (TPAF) with two complementary training objectives. Event-Invariant Adversarial Training discourages excessive encoding of duration-sensitive event variations, while Global Context Distillation guides each short-segment prediction with a frozen teacher that observes the paired full recording. A fixed pair of baseline reference models defines Cross-Duration Prediction Discrepancy (CDPD) and Within-Recording Prediction Variability (WRPV), enabling the same validation-derived difficulty groups to be used for every method. On the TAU20 benchmark, CDPD and WRPV show strong correlation with recording-level segment error. For 1-second inputs, TPAF improves accuracy from 59.41% to 64.59% and gains 8.51 percentage points on recordings with high mismatch, while preserving performance on the low-mismatch group. Gains of 2.85-5.18 points across three lightweight backbones and 2.47-5.18 points across three datasets demonstrate transfer beyond one architecture or collection protocol. Across 0.5-5-second inputs, TPAF provides the strongest advantage on short, high-discrepancy, and high-variability recordings.

Title: Transformer-Based Earthquake Magnitude Forecasting Through Spatiotemporal Feature Analysis in Urban Disaster Management Systems
Abstract: Contemporary urban areas need advanced analytical instruments together with strong computational technologies to improve their ability to handle emergency situations during disasters. The ability to predict earthquakes continues to be a major obstacle because seismic events occur randomly throughout various geographical and geological environments. The paper describes a Transformer-based regression model that uses geographic coordinates and focal depth and time features from 1,084,832 seismic events between 1990 and 2023 to predict earthquake magnitudes. The proposed approach is evaluated against three models, which include linear regression and decision trees and random forests, through a stratified 70/15/15 trainvalidation-test split. The Transformer model tests produced results of R2=0.9999 and RMSE=0.006. on the untested data. The study details dataset features and validation methods and performance-boosting factors, which include spatiotemporal clustering, while providing essential research areas for regional testing across different locations. The study provides a usable instrument for earthquake danger assessment, which smart city disaster management systems need.

Title: Assessing the Impact of AI Adoption and Intellectual Property Strength on Firm Performance: Evidence from Bangladeshi Software Companies
Abstract: The present study empirically investigates the relationship between Artificial Intelligence (AI) Adoption and Intellectual Property (IP) Strength and its impact on firm performance in software industry of Bangladesh. The Resource Based View (RBV) theoretical approach led to the formulation of two hypotheses which have been tested with the collected data through survey from 51 respondents from the software industry in Bangladesh. The instruments used were five-point Likert scales which were used to operationalize all constructs, and Multiple Linear Regression (MLR) was used in testing the hypotheses. The results indicate that AI Adoption is a significant and strong predictor of firm performance ( = 0.809, p < 0.001), as the overall model accounts for 72.9% of the variance in firm performance (R<sup>2</sup> = 0.729, Adjusted R<sup>2</sup> = 0.718, F(2,48) = 64.64, p < 0.001). The bivariate correlation results showed that IP Strength was positively correlated with firm performance (r = 0.532, p < 0.001), but this did not turn out to be significant in the multivariate model ( = 0.075, p = 0.414). All constructs exhibited good to excellent internal consistency (Cronbach s a: AIA = 0.894, IPS = 0.795, FP = 0.884) for the reliability analysis. The findings indicate that AI is a strategic asset, a VRIN asset, and that the current situation of IP enforcement in the software industry in Bangladesh is weak. This study presents first empirical evidence that can explain the relationship between the adoption of AI and IP strength impacting the firm performance in the context of software industry in Bangladesh together and gives some guidelines to the firm strategy and technology policy.

Title: Machine Learning-Based Prediction of Student Placement Outcomes Using Academic and Skill Indicators
Abstract: Graduate employment has become an important concern for universities as they attempt to improve career outcomes among their students. Traditional evaluation assessment systems mainly use academic measures like grade point averages (GPA), which in most cases lacks to reflect the multifaceted of the correlation between academic performance and skill-based factors that would affect the results of the placement. The increasing availability of educational data provides machine-learning practices with the new opportunities and possibilities of the analysis of the student characteristics and the employment ability outcomes prediction in a more effective way. This study presents a machinelearning-based predictive model, that aims to predict student placement outcomes using academic and skill-based measures. The model includes preprocessing of data, feature engineering, and predictive modeling that are integrated in a logical machinelearning pipeline. Supervised learning classification algorithms, including Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, and Decision Tree, are compared to understand their performance in the prediction of the outcomes of the placement and compared with each other based on evaluation values and validation metrics. Model performance was evaluated using stratified cross-validation and standard classification metrics. These results mean that evidence-based solutions can give universities a more accurate view of trends in employability, enable more data-oriented decision-making in institutions of higher learning, and assist in formulating more useful plans to enhance graduate career preparedness.

Title: Spectral-Spatial Group Attention Transformer for Palm Tree Mapping in Arid Environments: A Case Study on Al Ain Municipality Hyperspectral Data
Abstract: Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) offers spectral resolution unlike any other, allowing the material to be separated with fine details which is important in remote sensing. In dry land such as the United Arab Emirates, precise mapping of palm trees is critical in management of agriculture, food security and monitoring environment. Nevertheless, the dimensionality of HSI data is high, spectral variations, and small labeled samples are major challenges to the traditional classification technique. In this paper, a new deep learning architecture, the Spectral-Spatial Group Attention Transformer (SS-GAT), is proposed with specific applications in the palm tree strong pixel-wise classification based on hyperspectral data. The proposed model combines the approach of a multi-scale 3D convolutional neural network (CNN) to obtain shallow spectral-spatial features, the approach of a new group attention mechanism, which divides feature embeddings into heads to learn long-range dependencies and discriminative semantic information to a minimum expensive overfitting. The framework is tested against a special dataset of hyperspectral data collected on palm tree farms in AI Ain, UAE and supplied by the AI Ain Municipality. It uses an elaborate preprocessing pipeline, which comprises atmospheric correction with a physics-based model and data augmentation. The experimental performance shows that SS-GAT has a state-of-the art performance, with an overall accuracy (OA) of 98.72 per cent and Kappa coefficient of 0.983 which is significantly higher than the performance of baseline models, including SVM, 3D-CNN and the standard Transformer models. The value of each architectural element is proven with the help of rigorous ablation studies and the strength of our method is proved with the help of statistical significance tests. This work does not only introduce a high-precision instrument of palm tree inventory, but also sets a new methodological standard of HSI classification of the complex agricultural landscape.

Title: Computer Vision-Based Stroke Lesion Detection and Prognosis Prediction Using Deep Learning
Abstract: In this paper, a novel hybrid Swin Transformer and convolutional neural network (CNN) encoder-decoder, called StrokeDL-Net, is proposed for accurate multimodal brain MRI lesion segmentation and a temporal multi-modal fusion network, called ProgNet, is proposed for 90-day functional outcome prediction via the modified Rankin Scale (mRS). StrokeDL-Net overcomes the drawbacks of pure convolutional methods, especially for small and diffuse lesion detection, by combining local convolutional feature extraction with global shifted-window self-attention, augmented with an auxiliary penumbra estimation module. ProgNet fuses imaging biomarkers (segmentation), features from temporal evolution of MRI from acute and 24-hr follow-up scans, and structured clinical parameters using a cross-modal transformer attention mechanism. Extensive experimental evaluation on ISLES 2022, ATLAS v2.0, BraTS 2021, CQ500 and a proprietary clinical cohort (ISCHEMIA) achieves the Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) of 89.4%, sensitivity of 0.93, HD95 of 4.3 mm and mRS prediction accuracy of 87.3%, significantly outperforming all the baseline methods. The ablation studies verify the role of each component of the architecture. This framework constitutes a readily deployable clinical decision support system for acute stroke management. Beyond raw performance metrics, we validated StrokeDL-Net and ProgNet for clinical interpretability and generalizability across heterogeneous scanner vendors, field strengths and acquisition protocols, ensuring robustness to real-world data variability. Gradient-weighted class activation mapping confirmed consistent localization of model attention to clinically relevant infarct cores and penumbral tissue. Inference time was less than 12 seconds per case on average on standard clinical hardware, highlighting the practical feasibility of the framework to be integrated into the emergency stroke workflow.

Title: Analyzing Digital Transformation's Effect on Teaching Faculty Performance in Higher Education from Infrastructure to Impact
Abstract: Reports say that higher education institutions (HEIs) are all going through the digital transformation (DT) in an its infrastructure, processes, and the analytics. One thing that affects how the successfully instructors accomplish its jobs is the tools it use. Its abilities, workload, and the support networks are some of the other thing that determine how well the teachers accomplish its professions. There is a lack of the consensus in a studies about the the specific components of the DT that most significantly enhance teacher effectiveness, as well as the impact of the factors such as the technostress and the institutional support on this enhancement. A cross-sectional, multi-institution study (≈ 350 faculty) uses a validated 5-point instrument capturing of DT maturity (infrastructure, proces digitizating, analytics capability, training of intensity), mediators (digital pedagogy competence, technostress), moderator (institutional support), and the outcomes (course design quality, delivery effectiveness, assessment innovating, student satisfaction). Reliability/validity are assessed via CFA; hypotheses are tested with the PLS-SEM and the bootstrapped paths, plus multi-group analysis by age and it discipline and the checks for a common-method bias. DT maturity has shown a positive, significant effect on teaching performance (β ≈ 0.41, p<0.001), explaining of ~43% of the variance. Digital pedagogy competence partially mediates the effect (indirect β ≈ 0.18), while technostress negatively impacts performance (β ≈ - 0.22). Institutional support moderates both the pathways, strengthening of competence effects and the buffering of technostress. Training of intensity and the analytics capability emerge as the strongest DT predictors. Findings indicate that targeted faculty development, streamlined LMS processes, and it data-informed teaching yield measurable gains without exacerbating of workload.

Title: Rhythm Without Errors: Chain-of-Thought Reasoning and Embodied AI for Adaptive Personalized Music Training
Abstract: We introduce a foundational framework for deploying robust embodied AI tutors in adaptive, personalized music training that leverages chain-of-thought reasoning to represent rhythmic learning as an emotion-aware instructional loop in which timing deviations are detected and corrected during practice. We propose a flexible, hybrid multimodal architecture that integrates embodied agents, chain-of-thought planners, and affect-aware components to support the learner’s trajectory from basic kinesthetic sensing to precise rhythmic performance. By fusing diverse interaction channels—including physiological affective signals, proprioceptive motor feedback, gestural rhythm trajectories, and gaze-derived attention measures—the system forms a rich cognitive-affective representation of the student together with the agent’s explanatory reasoning. Engineered to scale to large learner populations, the platform employs hierarchical representation learning to separate salient affective indicators from sensory-cognitive developmental stages. We adapt a resilient, error-aware routing protocol inspired by Dijkstra’s shortest-path algorithm to generate individualized "perception-to-mastery" instructional pathways that reduce cognitive load, strengthen emotional engagement, and preserve pedagogical fidelity. To handle the complexity of high-dimensional inputs from multimodal sensors (such as facial affect trackers, electrodermal sensors, and tactile actuators), a spatiotemporal feature distillation module eliminates redundant channels while isolating latent markers of instructional flow and systemic anomalies. These distilled features are embedded into a probabilistic latent manifold that captures unique emotional-motor signatures for individual learners. A central component of our approach is an affect-sensitive affinity network that identifies cohorts of learners with similar trajectories across the instructional ecosystem. Such cohorts illuminate common learning pathways and suggest targeted kinetic supports and durable emotional scaffolding strategies that are robust to AI-driven instructional drift. Finally, a ranking-based recommendation engine combines localized affective cues with cohort-level patterns to produce actionable, reliable feedback recommendations for the embodied tutoring agent. Evaluated on a dataset of over 1 million multimodal rhythmic practice records, the architecture attains an 18% reduction in RMSE for proficiency forecasting, validating its ability to provide tailored, chain-of-thought-informed guidance that reduces uncorrected timing errors relative to baseline methods.

Title: ChatGPT Health and ChatGPT Plus in Urogynecology: A Blinded Comparison of Response Quality, Guideline Concordance, and Safety
Abstract: Introduction and Hypothesis: ChatGPT Health is a health-focused conversational artificial intelligence (AI) environment, but its performance in patient-oriented urogynecology has not been directly compared with standard ChatGPT using both validated quality assessment and objective guideline-based criteria. We hypothesized that ChatGPT Health would provide higher patient-facing response quality while maintaining comparable guideline concordance and safety. Methods: Twenty-four guideline-informed patient queries covering common urogynecological and lower urinary tract concerns were submitted independently to ChatGPT Plus and ChatGPT Health on 14 August 2026. Forty-eight responses were anonymized and independently evaluated by five blinded clinicians using the validated Quality Analysis of Medical Artificial Intelligence (QAMAI) instrument, a prespecified five-element guideline-concordance checklist, and a safety scale. Blinded head-to-head preference was assessed secondarily. Prompt-level paired comparisons used Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Results: Median guideline concordance was 100% for ChatGPT Health and 98% for ChatGPT Plus (p = 0.298). ChatGPT Health had a higher blinded five-domain QAMAI subtotal (25.0 vs 24.2; p = 0.026) and greater clarity (p = 0.020), completeness (p = 0.016), and usefulness (p = 0.033), with all three remaining significant after correction for false discovery rate. Accuracy did not differ (p = 0.453). No clinically meaningful safety concerns were identified in 240 ratings. ChatGPT Health was preferred in 47.5% of 120 assessments, ChatGPT Plus in 18.3%, and no meaningful difference was reported in 34.2%. Conclusions: Both platforms generated highly accurate, guideline-concordant, and safe responses. ChatGPT Health showed advantages primarily in clarity, completeness, usefulness, and overall quality of patient-facing communication rather than objective concordance of clinical content.

Title: An Ultra-Wide-Tuning Differential Active Inductor-VCO with Triode-Mode Loss Compensation for Aerospace Applications
Abstract: This paper presents a high-performance, differential active inductor (AI)-based voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) implemented in 90 nm CMOS technology. The proposed design satisfies the Size, Weight, and Power (SWAP) requirements for aerospace radar, frequency-agile RF front ends operating in the L and S bands, radios, telemetry, navigation, instruments, and other aerospace electronic systems that require wideband frequency synthesis. It employs a compact, modified gyrator-C topology using forward transconductors biased in saturation to replace bulky passive spiral inductors, while providing an unprecedented 187.07% frequency tuning range (0.167 GHz to 4.999 GHz) with both coarse and fine-tuning mechanisms. The key novelty of our work lies in utilizing the transistor M<inf>9</inf> as a triode-operated, voltage-controlled tunable loss compensator (V<inf>c1</inf>), providing independent control of the Quality Factor (Q) and frequency without any redesign or resizing of the layout. Further, a triple-transistor feedback network with local resistive feedback generates a controlled negative resistance, which compensates for parasitic losses of the transistors, yielding a nearly ideal inductive behaviour with a high-Quality factor (Q) of 2136 (post-layout at 4.898 GHz) and an inductance of 121.8 nH (post-layout at frequency 7.24 GHz). Post-layout simulations show excellent phase noise (− 83.83 dBc/Hz at 1 MHz) and a Total Figure of Merit (FoM<inf>T</inf>) of − 163.32 dBc/Hz, along with robust frequency convergence at 140 °C, with extreme miniaturization and a core area of only 0.00447 mm<sup>2</sup>. This monolithic solution offers superior spectral purity and robustness to process variations, providing a highly efficient RF front-end for the next generation of aerospace platforms.

Title: Embodied algorithms in vocal performance: Kinesthesis 2.0 and the transformation of player–instrument–algorithm assemblages
Abstract: Abstract – This article examines Kinesthesis 2.0, an interactive system that transforms gesture and facial expression into real-time vocal processing through algorithmic integration. Drawing on over two decades of compositional practice for theatre, dance and film, we analyse how machine learning, gesture recognition and audio processing configure player–instrument–algorithm assemblages. The analysis is grounded in vocal embodiment rather than in the voice as a discrete signal: vocal sound emerges through knowledge cultivated in sustained practice, which the system extends through gestural control and algorithmic mediation. Case studies from three theatrical productions, including human–AI co-improvisation with Somax2, examine how algorithmic systems reconfigure performer agency and embodied experience while revealing productive tensions between human expressivity and computational interpretation. The methodology is qualitative and practice-based, combining technical analysis, structured performer observation and artistic reflection; observations derive from sustained artistic practice rather than controlled experimentation. The research contributes to ongoing discussions in electroacoustic and embodied performance practice by proposing that computational mediation becomes experientially seamless not through technical simplification but through cultural depth: rooting algorithmic gesture vocabularies in embedded cultural tradition allows performers to internalise the system as an extension of practice rather than as an external tool.

Title: Transfer learning-based acoustic anomaly detection for automotive actuators
Abstract: We propose MTDF (Morlet-based Transfer Deep-SVDD), a one-class anomaly-detection framework for automotive actuators. MTDF converts motor vibration signals into acoustic-style time-frequency images (Morlet continuous-wavelet scalograms), extracts deep representations via transfer learning (VGG19), and detects anomalies with Deep-SVDD. On real-world actuator data, MTDF delivers balanced test performance (normal F1 = 74.3%; abnormal F1 = 92.9%) and remains robust to noise and cross-condition shifts, indicating suitability for in-line manufacturing monitoring.

Title: AI in Special Language Education: A Case Study of ChatGPT Utilization among Jordanian Students with ADHD
Abstract: This study carried out a quantitative analysis to investigate the use of ChatGPT in teaching English vocabulary to students with ADHD in Jordan. The sample consisted of 100 students with ADHD from 40 schools. The data were collected using three instruments. A pre-test and post-test assessed students’ vocabulary proficiency level over six months to evaluate students’ vocabulary development. A questionnaire was constructed to evaluate students’ attitudes toward using ChatGPT, while another questionnaire was administered to 20 English teachers from participating schools to measure the impact of ChatGPT and the challenges of integrating it into the educational environment. The assessment tests revealed an improvement in students’ vocabulary performance. The students’ questionnaire indicated that students with ADHD perceived ChatGPT as an effective tool for learning vocabulary, particularly due to the immediate feedback. The teachers’ questionnaire revealed that teachers considered ChatGPT as a valuable instructional tool. Teachers highlighted the main barriers to its effective implementation, such as limited resources and insufficient teacher training. The study concluded that ChatGPT has substantial potential to enhance English vocabulary learning among students with ADHD, but adequate educational support and teacher training are required.

Title: Predicting music preference using deep learning on electroencephalogram and audio features
Abstract: In this paper, we aimed to verify the practical contribution of Electroencephalography (EEG) information in music preference prediction. To this end, Null Electroencephalogram (Null EEG), in which temporal information was disrupted, was used as a control condition, and a controlled comparison between EEG and Null EEG was conducted using the same model architecture. The results showed that the EEG based model showed consistent performance improvements compared to Null EEG, confirming that EEG signals substantially contribute to music preference prediction. Furthermore, in comparison with the acoustic feature based model, the EEG only model demonstrated higher performance, while the model combining EEG and acoustic features achieved the best overall performance. Finally, an Region of Interest (ROI) ablation experiment was conducted to explore the contribution of different brain regions to music preference prediction, revealing that the occipital and frontal regions were strongly associated with music preference prediction. Overall, this study demonstrates the role of EEG information in predicting individual music preferences and suggests the potential of its complementary use with acoustic features.

Title: Validating Municipal Infrastructure-Stress Indices Against Measured Traffic: Load Ratios Destroy the Signal, and Network Topology Restores It
Abstract: Municipalities increasingly convert open GIS (geographic information system) data into a single composite infrastructure stress index, a 0-100 score per neighborhood, built by combining several map-derived measurements, used to flag areas for engineering review or capital investment. These indices are rarely checked against anything actually measured. We close that gap using 118 North Carolina DOT traffic sensors in Fuquay-Varina, NC, as an independent, instrument-measured outcome the index was never built from. A published stress index performs no better than chance at its own task, flagging the town's busiest roads, scoring an AUC (area under the ROC curve, a 0-to-1 measure of ranking accuracy where 1.0 is perfect and 0.5 is a coin flip) of just 0.481, and a recall (the fraction of genuinely busy roads it actually caught) of 0.29, barely above the 0.25 one would expect from guessing at random. Here is why it fails. The index's two heaviest-weighted components (60% of the total) are both ratios, such as building count divided by street length, meant to measure crowding. Instead, busy areas have proportionally more of both quantities, so the division cancels the exact pattern that predicts traffic, even though each quantity alone is informative. Re-tuning the weights does not fix this, because the flaw is which quantities are combined, not how they are balanced. The index also correlates negatively with nine years of measured traffic growth, so using it for early warning would misdirect attention. The fix uses free data the town already has: road functional class (e.g., highway vs. side street) and betweenness centrality (how many shortest routes between locations pass through a given road) predict traffic far better. Combined with gradient boosting (a machine-learning method that builds many small decision rules and combines them), this roughly doubles detection performance (AUC 0.818, recall 0.61).
