Title: Learning in cardiac surgery—Practice-oriented and critical guides on the application of large language models
Abstract: Medicine is in a state of continuous change and the technological progress has repeatedly reformed its culture, training pathways and epistemic practices. Large language models (LLM) represent the most recent of these transformations and with the lifelong learning touch on a core area of the medical self-conception. This article is aimed at cardiac surgeons in advanced training as well as medical specialists, who would like to systematically use LLM for their own learning. Based on the concept of calibrated trust we argue that neither blind acceptance nor categorical rejection of artificial intelligence (AI) is appropriate but a situation-dependent trusting behavior oriented to the verifiable performance of the instrument. Both positions have consequences. The uncritical outsourcing of the clinical reasoning weakens, inhibits or falsifies learning, whereas the general waiver negates the benefits. The guiding action is the principle of “test then trust”. The article describes the unique basic set-up of an LLM, discusses the benefits and limits of personalization, including data protection and copyrights, and mediates a structured method of the correct prompting with a focus on active learning. The intrinsic value of traditional learning processes is emphasized and practical examples for use are given. The text should be understood as didactic recommendations, not as clinical guidelines.

Title: Adaptive teaching assistance model combining generative AI and big data analytics
Abstract: The lack of personalized teaching resources and real-time evaluation in music education severely limits teaching effectiveness and cannot meet the diverse artistic expression needs of learners. Therefore, this paper proposes an adaptive teaching assistance model that combines generative artificial intelligence with big data analysis. This paper uses a cross modal transformer (CMT) to align performance audio with symbol score features, and employs a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) reinforcement learning framework to convert learners' performance features into reward signals to generate dynamic content. At the same time, this paper conducted a quasi experimental technical validation for 12 weeks, involving 120 undergraduate students majoring in music (60 experimental students and 60 control students); the experimental group received feedback generated by the system, while the control group received traditional guidance. The results showed that the peak cosine similarity between the generated practice trajectory and the skill level of learners at the primary difficulty level was 0.962 ± 0.014, and the system's error detection recall rate for complex rhythm errors was 91.2% ± 1.8%. After 300 training iterations, the cumulative expected return of the PPO mechanism remained stable at 95.12 ± 1.23 (average∼0.79 per step). The learning trajectory of the experimental group was significantly steeper than that of the control group, as evidenced by the significant group time interaction [β = 0.52, 95% CI (0.31, 0.73)], providing statistical support for the model's potential to accelerate short-term skill improvement. These findings suggest that the proposed closed-loop system provides a promising algorithmic framework for personalized feedback in music education, but educational statements should be interpreted within the scope of testing conditions and technical proxy indicators reported.

Title: Development of an Accelerometer-Based Silent Speech Interface Robust to Head Motion Artifacts Using a Reference-Free Denoising Autoencoder
Abstract: Silent speech interfaces (SSIs) employing three-axis accelerometers can provide an effective communication modality for individuals who experience difficulty producing audible speech. However, the accuracy of such systems tends to degrade markedly when users move their heads (e.g., nodding or turning) during silent speech, thereby reducing their reliability in practical scenarios. Apart from constraining users to maintain a fixed head position during silent articulation, no effective solution to this problem has been proposed. To overcome this limitation, we developed a head motion artifact-robust SSI that incorporates a novel denoising autoencoder (DAE) integrating a convolutional neural network with a bidirectional long short-term memory network. To train the DAE, users are required to complete a brief training session consisting solely of head movements without articulation. The key innovation lies in the training strategy: we augmented the training data for the DAE by generating artificial artifacts, enabling the DAE to learn to suppress various motion-induced distortions while preserving genuine articulatory features, so that the classifier—trained on artifact-free data—can operate reliably even when its input contains head-motion artifacts. Evaluations with ten participants over six recording sessions showed substantial performance improvements, with the signal-to-artifact ratio increasing by 1.23 dB (from −1.12 to 0.11 dB) and classification accuracy rising from 56.0% to 82.3%. To our knowledge, the accelerometer based SSI implemented in this study is the first to demonstrate robust performance under head motion-artifact conditions, highlighting its potential in real-world assistive communication applications.

Title: Real-Time Audio-Visual Emotion Detection for Human-AI Interaction
Abstract: In this study, a multimodal emotion recognition framework is proposed that recognizes human emotions based on speech and facial expression cues obtained from two databases: the CREMA-D and RAVDESS databases. Audio cues are represented by MFCC, Mel-spectrogram, and chroma features, whereas visual cues are represented by EfficientNet-based convolutional networks applied to facial frames. The temporal dependencies of these cues are modeled using BiLSTM networks, whereas audio-visual cues are fused using a gated cross-modal attention mechanism. The Transformer encoder is used for capturing contextual relationships between audio-visual cues, whereas the final layer is used for emotion classification among six classes: anger, disgust, fear, happiness, sadness, and neutral. The model is trained using the Adam optimizer and categorical cross-entropy loss functions, whereas accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and the confusion matrix are used for performance evaluation of the proposed model. The performance of the proposed model is found to be better than existing baseline models CNN, CNN+LSTM, CNN+BiLSTM, and CNN+BiLSTM+attention, whereas the proposed model achieves an accuracy of 91%. The system also offers an emotion-based chatbot that can be used for intelligent humancomputer interaction systems.

Title: A method for identifying urban flood inundation based on single-temporal remote sensing imagery
Abstract: Rapid mapping of urban flood inundation is critical for emergency response and decision-making. However, existing methods often rely heavily on multi-temporal data or deep learning models, limiting their timeliness and computational efficiency. This study proposes an automated method for mapping urban flood inundation from a single post-event image acquired by the Sentinel-2 Multispectral Instrument. The method adopts a three-stage framework comprising spectral-index-based segmentation, morphological-feature-based separation, and spatial-topological assessment. It was evaluated using three flood events in Zhengzhou, China; Manville, United States; and Porto Alegre, Brazil. Independent validation yielded overall accuracies of 0.9985, 0.9371, and 0.8834; precision values of 0.6719, 0.6771, and 0.8229; and F1-scores of 0.8037, 0.7001, and 0.7615, respectively. The extracted flood extents were further compared with those obtained using two conventional approaches and were generally consistent across the three study areas. Agreement F1-scores ranged from 0.694 to 0.870 relative to pre- and post-flood change detection based on the modified normalised difference water index, and from 0.603 to 0.866 relative to newly inundated area extraction using the European Commission Joint Research Centre permanent surface-water mask. On an experimental platform equipped with an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin, processing the Porto Alegre, Manville, and Zhengzhou scenes required 24.3, 2.68, and 19.8 s, respectively. These quantitative results indicate that the proposed method can identify major urban flood inundation areas under diverse geographical and hydrological conditions. Requiring only a single post-event multispectral image, no model training, and no high-performance computing, the method provides a lightweight solution for rapid urban flood inundation mapping and resource-constrained applications, including onboard satellite processing.

Title: The Reversed Turing Test: Measuring Superhuman AI Performance Beyond Imitation
Abstract: For more than seven decades, Alan Turing’s imitation game has shaped how the AI community discusses machine intelligence, although it was never a psychometric instrument. AI systems now outperform humans in strategic games, scientific prediction, and pattern recognition, achievements better described as domain-specific superhuman performance than as general intelligence unless a novelty condition is enforced. This paper argues that imitation-based evaluation is misaligned with such systems and introduces the Reversed Turing Test (RTT), which asks whether a machine can be identified precisely because its performance is measurably superhuman. The test combines a standardized superhuman index (SI), expressed in standard-deviation units relative to a human reference sample, with a panel of judges whose identifications are verified against the performance evidence. The paper provides a formal definition of the RTT, a taxonomy of novelty types with verification methods, a worked example in protein structure prediction, and a pre-registered text-generation study (n = 500; composite SI ≈ 3.2; 90% identification accuracy grounded in stylometric cues), interpreted as superhuman stylometric performance rather than superhuman intelligence. The RTT is compared against established benchmarks, its philosophical limits are stated, and implications for trust, creativity, governance, and evaluation design are discussed.

Title: Performance evaluation of large language models in bladder cancer patient education Q&A: a cross-sectional study
Abstract: Background – Bladder cancer ranks among the most prevalent urological tumors worldwide, with its global incidence continuing to rise steadily. Although patient education materials (PEMs) play a crucial role in enhancing disease comprehension and supporting joint clinical decision-making, current online resources frequently surpass the readability thresholds recommended for the general public. Large language models (LLMs) hold promise for health communication, yet no systematic assessment has been conducted regarding their feasibility and trustworthiness specifically for bladder cancer patient education. Objective – This study aimed to systematically benchmark five leading LLMs in producing question-and-answer content for bladder cancer science popularization, with a particular focus on readability, informational quality, and appropriateness for patient education. Methods – In this cross-sectional simulation study, 20 common patient questions covering five disease domains were compiled. On January 15, 2026, each question was submitted identically to five publicly available LLMs (Doubao, DeepSeek, Kimi, Gemini, and ChatGPT). Readability was evaluated using seven conventional metrics. Two independent pharmacists, blinded to model identity, rated the responses using the Chinese version of the Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool for print materials (C-PEMAT-P) and the Global Quality Score (GQS). Additionally, two independent clinical specialists assessed factual accuracy and alignment with the Chinese Bladder Cancer Diagnosis and Treatment Guidelines (2024 edition) employing a 4-point scale. Cohen’s kappa was used to determine inter-rater reliability. Results – ChatGPT, DeepSeek, and Doubao outperformed Kimi and Gemini on both C-PEMAT and GQS (all P < 0.001), indicating superior understandability, actionability, and overall quality. Across all models, median C-PEMAT scores ranged from 8 to 10, suggesting broadly acceptable suitability for patient education. Readability varied significantly by content domain, with treatment-oriented texts showing the highest complexity. ChatGPT achieved the best alignment with clinical guidelines. No model produced harmful advice or directly contradicted guideline recommendations. Traditional readability measures correlated weakly with GQS, whereas C-PEMAT showed a moderate positive correlation (r = 0.34). Conclusion – Current mainstream LLMs demonstrate initial potential for generating educational content on bladder cancer, albeit with considerable heterogeneity across models. Disease-specific evaluation instruments for patient education materials are more effective than general readability formulas in reflecting perceived quality. Our results advocate for a prudent, assistive role of LLMs in health communication under a human-AI collaborative model.

Title: Predicting grade≥2 chemotherapy-induced myelosuppression in older patients with colorectal cancer receiving first-line chemotherapy: a multi-algorithm consensus approach using 9 routine parameters to develop and validate an explainable boosting machine
Abstract: Objective　Older patients with colorectal cancer undergoing first-line chemotherapy are prone to myelosuppression, which can lead to treatment delays, dose adjustments, and adverse outcomes such as infection and bleeding; however, individualized risk prediction tools with external validation remain lacking. This study aimed to identify routine clinical predictors using a multi-algorithm consensus strategy, construct and compare risk prediction models for grade ≥2 chemotherapy-induced myelosuppression in this population, and evaluate the external generalizability and clinical utility of the leading model. Methods　In this retrospective cohort study leveraging data from two hospitals, we adopted a predictive model development and independent external validation design. A total of 553 older patients receiving first-line chemotherapy were enrolled, including 442 from Guang'anmen Hospital (development cohort) and 111 from Gansu Provincial Cancer Hospital (external validation cohort). The primary endpoint was grade ≥2 myelosuppression per Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events version 5. 0 (CTCAE v5. 0). Nineteen candidate predictors underwent consensus selection via least absolute shrinkage and selection operator logistic regression, the Boruta algorithm, and random forest permutation importance, with final core predictors determined by bootstrap inclusion frequency and prespecified clinical retention rules. Nine models were constructed: conventional logistic regression, LASSO logistic regression, elastic net logistic regression, random forest, extreme gradient boosting, categorical boosting, radial basis function support vector machine, linear discriminant analysis, and explainable boosting machine (EBM). Five repeated 10-fold stratified cross validation generated out-of-fold predictions in the development cohort, and locked models were applied to the external validation cohort. Model performance was assessed by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC), Brier score, calibration intercept, calibration slope, Hosmer-Lemeshow test, and decision curve analysis. Results　The incidence of grade ≥2 myelosuppression was 26. 2% (116/442) in the development cohort and 27. 0% (30/111) in the external validation cohort (P>0. 05). Nine core predictors were selected: albumin, carcinoembryonic antigen, carbohydrate antigen 19-9, carbohydrate antigen 125, body surface area, tumor location, chemotherapy cycle, chemotherapy regimen, and age-adjusted Charlson comorbidity index. The EBM was identified as the leading model based on balanced discrimination, calibration, and interpretability. In the development cohort, EBM achieved an out-of-fold AUROC of 0. 720 (95%CI: 0. 676 to 0. 772), AUPRC of 0. 421, Brier score of 0. 176, calibration intercept of 0. 035, and calibration slope of 0. 778, with no significant miscalibration (Hosmer Lemeshow P=0. 087). In external validation, EBM yielded an AUROC of 0. 714 (95%CI: 0. 595 to 0. 834), AUPRC of 0. 641, Brier score of 0. 164, calibration intercept of 0. 155, and calibration slope of 0. 778, though calibration remained suboptimal (P< 0.001). At the optimal threshold of 0. 28 derived from the development cohort, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, and F1 score in the external validation cohort were 0. 667, 0. 741, 0. 488, 0. 857, and 0. 563, respectively. Decision curve analysis indicated superior net benefit over treat-all or treat-none strategies across threshold probabilities of 0. 06 to 0. 48 (development cohort) and 0. 18 to 0. 60 (external validation cohort). Interpretation revealed albumin as the strongest contributor, followed by carcinoembryonic antigen, carbohydrate antigen 19-9, and carbohydrate antigen 125; lower albumin, smaller body surface area, ≥5 chemotherapy cycles, and the FOLFIRI regimen were associated with increased risk, while tumor markers exhibited nonlinear associations with predicted risk. Conclusion　Nine routine clinical parameters selected by a multi-algorithm consensus strategy enable construction of a prediction model for grade ≥2 myelosuppression during first-line chemotherapy in older patients with colorectal cancer. The finalized EBM model demonstrates moderate discrimination and clinical net benefit in both development and external validation cohorts but exhibits residual calibration drift externally. It may serve as an adjunctive tool for clinical risk stratification rather than a standalone decision making instrument at this stage.

Title: The Impact of Dataset Diversity on Generalization in Multimodal Violence Detection Models
Abstract: The increasing deployment of surveillance systems in public spaces has created a growing need for intelligent methods that can automatically detect violent incidents and support timely intervention. While recent deep learning approaches have shown promising performance in video-based violence detection, many existing systems rely primarily on visual cues and are often trained on limited or homogeneous datasets, which can restrict generalization in real-world environments. In this work, we investigate the impact of dataset characteristics on the behavior and generalization of multimodal violence detection models. We propose an audio-visual violence detection framework that combines visual and acoustic representations using an attention-based fusion mechanism to enable context-aware decision-making under challenging conditions. The framework is evaluated on the Real Life Violence Situations (RLVS) dataset after filtering samples with invalid or low-quality audio, resulting in an audio-visual subset of 894 videos. Experimental results show that the visual-only model achieves the highest F1-score on this dataset, indicating strong visual discriminability in RLVS, while the multimodal model provides competitive performance and improved robustness in visually ambiguous scenarios. To improve transparency in security-critical settings, we further incorporate Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) techniques, including Grad-CAM, attention visualization, and audio feature attribution, to interpret modality contributions and highlight salient decision regions. The findings emphasize that dataset characteristics strongly influence the relative benefit of multimodal fusion and highlight the importance of explainable multimodal learning for reliable violence detection in real-world surveillance applications.

Title: Real-Time Implementation of Adaptive Noise Cancellation using DSP and Machine Learning Algorithm
Abstract: Real-world speech communication is severely degraded by background noise originating from traffic, industrial machinery, and other environmental sources. Conventional adaptive noise reduction methods based on Digital Signal Processing (DSP) are computationally efficient and amenable to real-time processing; however, they exhibit limitations in suppressing complex, non-stationary noise components. Machine learning (ML) techniques, by contrast, have demonstrated strong noise-modeling capability but are often computationally intensive and data-hungry, which constrains their applicability in real-time and embedded deployments. This paper proposes a hybrid speech enhancement framework that integrates adaptive filtering using the Least Mean Squares (LMS) algorithm with a supervised autoencoder neural network. The LMS filter performs initial noise reduction by canceling correlated noise components with low computational overhead. The autoencoder subsequently refines the LMS output by learning residual noise patterns that are not amenable to conventional DSP suppression alone. The LMS learning rate (μ = 0.01) and filter order (N = 32) were empirically optimized to balance convergence speed and steady-state error under real-time constraints. To address generalization to unseen noise types, the autoencoder was evaluated on noise classes excluded from training, confirming its robustness through acceptable SNR degradation. Performance is assessed using SNR improvement, Mean Squared Error (MSE), and Perceptual Evaluation of Speech Quality (PESQ) metrics, and validation employs the NOIZEUS and VCTK-Demand standard speech enhancement benchmarks as well as real-world recordings.

Title: OmniDance: Multimodal Driven Dance Video Generation with Large-Scale Internet Data
Abstract: Music-driven dance video generation aims to synthesize expressive human motion that is temporally aligned with music while maintaining high visual fidelity. Despite recent progress, existing methods still struggle to generate dance videos that simultaneously exhibit expressive motion and high visual quality. This limitation primarily arises from two factors: (1) Dataset. The lack of large-scale and high-quality datasets and effective data collection pipelines specifically tailored for dance video generation; and (2) Method. The absence of principled framework-level solutions for effectively integrating music as a complementary conditioning signal into the Video Generation Foundation Models. To address the dataset limitation, we introduce CIPE-Dance, a large-scale Internet-sourced dance video dataset, equipped with Choreograph Informed text annotations and constructed via a Progressive Expert pipeline. To the best of our knowledge, CIPE-Dance is the largest dataset for dance video generation to date, comprising 300k high-quality clips (over 400 h) and covering diverse dancers, environments, and dance genres. To overcome the method limitation, we propose OmniDance, a framework-level recipe for integrating music into a TI2V foundation model without sacrificing its original controllability or visual fidelity. Motivated by the complementary roles of text (low-frequency semantics) and music (high-frequency temporal dynamics), OmniDance co-designs a depth-aware specialization model architecture, an anchored easy-to-hard curriculum learning strategy, and modality-specialized time-dependent CFG strategy, achieving unified TI2V/MI2V/MTI2V generation. Extensive experiments on the CIPE-Dance dataset demonstrate that OmniDance achieves state-of-the-art performance across TI2V, MI2V, and MTI2V tasks, while exhibiting robust multimodal integration capability. Project is available at https://github.com/AMAP-ML/OmniDance.

Title: Bridging the Distance: Studies in Rural Innovation Ecosystems as Human-Centered Work Systems
Abstract: Occupational Applications Rural innovation ecosystems are often perceived as abstract regional constructs, but they can be understood as work systems in which farmers, entrepreneurs, intermediaries, and local institutions collaborate to generate new products, services, and processes. This paper introduces the Rural Innovation Ecosystem Framework (RIEF), a diagnostic instrument that classifies system elements into six categories: knowledge generation, entrepreneurial actors, intermediaries, governance, resources and infrastructure, and community and culture. Practitioners can use RIEF to identify bottlenecks that increase cognitive workload or coordination cost-such as inadequate digital infrastructure or weak governance-and to design interventions that support people at work. Intermediaries can be reconceived as human-system integrators that reduce coordination burden, while governance structures can be tuned to enhance role clarity, trust, and decision quality. The framework helps managers and policymakers create safer, more effective rural work systems by aligning technological and social investments with human capabilities. Technical Abstract Background. Rural regions worldwide struggle to translate local knowledge and resources into innovation due to limited infrastructure, fragmented governance, and dispersed actors, while digital technologies, sensing systems, and AI-enabled decision support are simultaneously reshaping rural work. Existing innovation-ecosystem frameworks rarely treat rural regions as work systems or emphasize human-system performance. Purpose. This paper introduces the Rural Innovation Ecosystem Framework (RIEF) and positions it within the occupational ergonomics and human factors domain. The objective is to reinterpret rural innovation ecosystems as human-centered work systems and to provide a diagnostic instrument that highlights the interplay between human capabilities, organizational structures, and digital technologies. Methods. A hybrid systematic and integrative literature review covered 105 unique references on rural innovation, work systems, and organizational ergonomics published between 2010 and 2025. Searches were conducted in Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar using Boolean strings combining each RIEF category with rural and human-factors terms. Articles were screened by two coders against four inclusion criteria; snowballing identified additional sources; an evidence-tier rubric (A-D) protected the framework's load-bearing claims from low-quality outlets. Results. RIEF articulates six interdependent categories and five propositions describing their interactions. Cross-category synthesis surfaced three findings: intermediaries function as human-system integrators with disproportionate leverage on rural work performance; governance quality outweighs raw resource volume in shaping outcomes; and digital infrastructure amplifies-but does not by itself produce-innovation. Integration with Paul O'Brien's structural-economic view of startup ecosystems sharpens the diagnostic value of the framework by adding optionality, density, and cultural risk tolerance as upstream conditions. Conclusions. Reframing rural innovation ecosystems as work systems foregrounds the human-factors implications of digital transformation. RIEF provides researchers a structure for empirical testing and practitioners a diagnostic tool for evaluating rural projects and designing interventions that align technology, organizational structures, and community culture with human capabilities.

Title: A Comprehensive Survey on Contactless Sensors for Healthcare and Human-Centric Applications
Abstract: In the past few years, contactless sensing technology has become one of the leading instruments for healthcare and human-centred intelligent systems. Contactless sensors have a lot more benefits over the traditional sensors that need contact as they can function even without being in direct contact physically, at a safe distance, and they're being a non-contact makes them more hygienic and natural for human use. Besides, these systems are being fuelled by people's increasing wish for smart healthcare and other solutions, such as remote patient management, pandemic preparedness, and Ambient Assisted Living (AAL), to name a few. This article presents an exhaustive review of contactless sensing technology and its real-life applications. Many sensing methods are discussed and compared, like camera-based sensing, radar/microwave, infrared ultrasonic, wireless communication, hybrid combinations, etc. Among the main application areas explored were the health-related uses of contactless sensing - for example, monitoring vital signs such as heart rate, breathing and blood pressure, identifying diseases, elderly care, patient monitoring and human activity recognition. In addition, the use of contactless sensing for gesture based human machine interaction has been discussed, enabling users to operate home appliances, assistive devices and even mobile phones without any physical contact. Besides, recent data-driven analysis method, novel computational techniques paving the way for more efficient sensor array designs, processing capabilities have together contributed to the feasibility of several contactless sensing systems with excellent performance about accuracy and robustness. Though, some commercial and even more non-trivial designs are still confronted with the real-time problems mainly related to environmental and setup sensitivity, privacy concerns calibration large scale deployment, etc. This article pointed out such challenges and possible research focus leading to the development of advanced, intelligent and trustworthy next-gen contactless sensing systems.

Title: HEDRA-IDS: A Hierarchical Edge-Driven Residual Attention Framework for SDN-Enabled Intrusion Detection in Wireless Sensor Networks
Abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) deployed in mission-critical environments are facing an escalating spectrum of cyber threats, particularly Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) floods, sinkhole routing subversions, and selective-forwarding intrusions. Conventional centralized intrusion detection architectures impose untenable communication overhead and processing latency on resource-constrained sensor nodes. In this paper, HEDRA-IDS a Hierarchical Edge-Driven Residual Attention Intrusion Detection System that fuses Software-Defined Networking (SDN) programmability with a novel multi-scale residual attention neural architecture deployed across three cooperative tiers: intra-cluster edge nodes, gateway aggregators, and a cloud-resident SDN controller. HEDRA-IDS introduces a Temporal-Spatial Residual Attention Block (TSRAB) that simultaneously learns short-burst anomaly signatures and prolonged slow-rate attack patterns without gradient vanishing. Experiments conducted on the WSN-DS benchmark and a self-generated heterogeneous testbed comprising 120 Raspberry Pi Zero W sensors, a Floodlight SDN controller, and Open vSwitch data-plane elements demonstrate that HEDRA-IDS achieves a weighted detection accuracy of 98.76%, a macro F1-score of 0.9821, and a mean detection latency of 4.3 milliseconds surpassing all contemporary baselines by at least 1.9 percentage points while reducing false-positive rates to 0.73%. The proposed framework additionally incorporates an adaptive flow-rule synthesis mechanism that autonomously installs mitigation rules into SDN OpenFlow switches within one control-plane round-trip time, eliminating manual intervention. Ablation studies confirm that each architectural component contributes meaningfully to overall performance, and k-fold cross-validation (k=10) substantiates the absence of overfitting. HEDRA-IDS is thus a compelling candidate for practical deployment in industrial IoT, smart-grid metering networks, and battlefield sensor grids.

Title: Rainfall Prediction in Lakshadweep Using Deep Learning-Based Time Series Model
Abstract: Prediction of weather patterns are important factors in many areas including agriculture, disaster management, coastal planning, and in fisheries. It is very important to forecast and provide usable information about these events, as many of the coastal areas of island regions such as Lakshadweep, typically have a lack of available weather monitoring instruments.The vast amount of ever-changing, highly non-linear parameters and wide geographic range of these islands make traditional statistical forecasting methods unreliable because they cannot effectively capture these parameters at a time scale that matches the rapid changes in atmospheric conditions. Therefore, during this research study an alternative approach using deep learning was pursued as a means to accurately forecast future weather conditions for smaller isolated island.Recurrent neural network(RNN) model was developed to accurately learn the long-term temporal dependencies between the meteorological variables to enable a trained model to provide usable forecast predictions. Performance of the developed model was examined with standard metrics Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and multiple accuracy metrics. Model attained a classification accuracy of 76.64%, having low RMSE of 0.045 and MAE of 0.031. Experimental findings indicated that the model used in this research is able to discover the seasonal changes over time in the Lakshadweep, weather variables better than any of the traditional weather forecasting techniques. The final conclusion of this research is that deep learning models can effectively be applied to make reliable weather predictions on a smaller scale, such as in small island regions.

Title: Fusion-Based Multimodal Depression Detection Using Machine Learning on Textual, Vocal, and Facial Cues
Abstract: Depression is a pervasive psychiatric condition that affects over 280 million people globally, but it is mostly underdiagnosed and largely due to the existing screening tools that are highly contrarian, which is based on subjective selfreporting techniques such as the Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9). In this regard, automated mental-health screening based on the artificial intelligence methodology provides a promising avenue to improve the commencement of detecting the symptomatology of depression. In this respect, this paper presents MindScan a multimodal depression risk screening system that combines three behavioral media - conversational text sentiment, vocal prosody, and facial expression and is based on a browser platform. The system receives textual responses provided by the user in a chatbot conversation, processing them in a neural model (client-side) in order to extract prosodic features using microphone audio and a continuous depression risk scale, and provides a categorical risk classification (Low, Moderate, High) using weighted multimodal machine learning. To test the effectiveness of this methodology, we created artificial data consisting of 2,000 samples with simulations of multimodal behavior features that aimed to recreate realistic clinical distributions and to include cross-modal inconsistencies; three supervised machine-learning models were that is, Logistic Regression, Random Forest and a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) neural network, were trained and evaluated on both classification and regression levels, including Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-Score, RMSE, MAE and R2. Empirical evidence proves that MLP model seems to perform the best, as it has an accuracy of 97.2% and F1-score of 97.2% hence offers the best performance when compared to head start models and literature presented unimodal models. These results highlight the fact that multimodal analysis of behavior coupled with nonlinear machine-learning models significantly enhance automated depression detection.

Title: AGA-ANET: A Fully Attentional Activation Network with Adaptive Global Attention for Single Channel Speech Enhancement
Abstract: Recent developments in speech enhancement algorithms based on deep learning have benefited significantly from attention mechanisms, which have emerged as a cornerstone for achieving state-of-the-art performance. This paper introduces a novel approach for speech enhancement by proposing an adaptive global attention based fully attentional Network (AGA-ANet). Rather than using conventional RNNs like LSTMs or GRUs for sequence modeling, we introduce a novel S-TCN based adaptive global attention network positioned between the encoder and decoder. To enhance sequence modeling, multiple groups of squeezed TCNs are incorporated within the framework. Following the S-TCNs, an adaptive global attention (AGA) module is introduced to dynamically aggregate all output featuremaps, ensuring flexible and effective feature integration during sequence modeling. The AGA is designed to integrate various intermediate feature maps based on the global context, ensuring that relevant features are emphasized during the sequence modeling process. Additionally, AGA-ANet incorporates an attention activation within the encoder-decoder, transforming it into a fully attentional network. This allows the model to prioritize relevant high-level features during the earlier stages of processing. Experimental evaluations on the Commonvoice dataset highlight the effectiveness of the proposed approach. For the Commonvoice dataset, AGA-ANet achieves substantial improvements over the noisy mixture, the model demonstrated significant improvements in the quality of speech by 3.37 for seen noises and improved intelligibility by 89.17% under the same circumstances.

Title: A Comprehensive Review of Assistive Communication and Emotion-Aware Systems for Hearing-Impaired Users
Abstract: Assistive communicative systems and emotion conscious systems are essential in enhancing accessibility and interaction as well as social inclusion to people with hearing and speech impairments. The recent achievements of deep learning and multimodal technologies resulted in the dramatic improvement of gesturing recognition, speech processing, emotion recognition, and assistive interfaces. The paper includes the review and comparative analysis of the available research methods dealing with assistive communication and emotion-aware systems data, which are classified into assistive communication models, text- and speech-based recognition, image-based emotion recognition strategies, and multimodal emotion-aware systems. The analysed studies indicate that unimodal systems are computationally efficient but tend to be less robust and generalize better in comparison to multimodal systems that use vision, speech, text, and physiological indicators to improve their performance and gain a better understanding of the situations. Nevertheless, issues of limited availability of data, environmental sensitivity, imbalance of modalities, interpretability, and scalability in the real-world conditions have not been solved yet. According to the analysis, the existing research trends include the focus on multimodal fusion, attention mechanisms, explainable artificial intelligence, and real-time implementation. This survey is pointing at major constraints and future research directions of building scalable, explainable, and user-centric assistive communication systems that can be reliably used in the real world.

Title: AI-Powered IoT-Based Early Fire Detection with Multimodal Sensor Fusion and Acoustic Suppression
Abstract: Conventional fire detectors react only once smoke or heat has built up, by which time a fire may be established. This paper presents an AI-powered IoT system that detects fire earlier by listening for the acoustic signature of incipient combustion - the crackle and pop of igniting material - and confirms it by fusing the sound with temperature, smoke, and gas sensors, all on a low-cost Raspberry Pi edge device. A convolutional acoustic classifier over MFCC features identifies fire sounds at 97.0% accuracy; multimodal fusion of that classifier with the environmental sensors raises detection to 99.3% accuracy (F1 0.976) and halves the false-alarm rate to 0.4%, and - critically - suppresses the cooking false alarms that defeat smoke detectors, because the sensors confirm what the microphone hears. A ROC AUC of 0.995 and per-noise robustness tests (speech, traffic, machinery, television, cooking) substantiate the reliability the original work only asserted. The system also includes an experimental acoustic-suppression stage; rather than claim untested flame extinction, this paper presents a physics-based model showing that 30-60 Hz waves are the effective band and that roughly 107 dB is needed to disrupt a small flame, with the explicit caveat that physical trials and the safety of high sound-pressure levels remain future work. With a specified CNN, dataset, IoT architecture, edge-performance budget, and comparison against existing detectors, the system is a credible contribution to intelligent fire safety.

Title: Fine-Grained Detection of Forceps Tips and Joints in Laparoscopic Videos for Surgical Skill Analysis
Abstract: In this study, we propose an automatic detection method for forceps tips in laparoscopic surgical videos using a deep learning-based object detection model. To enable more fine-grained analysis of surgical instrument motion, we extend the detection target to include not only forceps tips but also joints. We employ YOLO11 and evaluate its performance across multiple model sizes. The proposed method is evaluated using a public dataset (m2cai16-tool-locations) and a self-constructed dataset consisting of 412 videos collected from simulated training environments. The dataset includes detailed annotations of both forceps tips and joints, enabling comprehensive evaluation. Detection performance is assessed using precision, recall, F1 score, and mean Average Precision (mAP). Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high detection accuracy for both tip and joint regions. These results indicate that fine-grained detection of surgical instrument components is feasible and provides a foundation for future surgical skill analysis based on motion and interaction patterns.

Title: Sound Classification and the Impact of Feature Fusion and Optimizers on Classification Performance of Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: Rapid urban population growth has lead to the increase of traffic congestion, which raises concerns about environmental impacts, noise pollution, and traffic safety. Accurate and reliable vehicle tracking is a crucial step in order to support efficient traffic management and data informed urban planning. Although computer vision-based systems are widely used, their performance deteriorates in low-light conditions and often raises privacy concerns when used in sensitive locations. Acoustic Traffic Monitoring (ATM) offers an alternative with low deployment costs, insensitivity to lighting changes, and applicability in areas where cameras are inconvenient or limited. This study investigates the possibility of vehicle type classification using audio recordings of passing vehicles. The focus is on the four core categories: cars, trucks, motorcycles, and non vehicle recordings. In this study, the MVD dataset is used to develop robust feature extraction pipelines and train deep learning models for acoustic vehicle type classification. The time domain signals are converted to time frequency representation and the Mel Spectrogram and Mel frequency Cepstral Coefficients are generated which are used to train the convolutional neural network. The results highlight key differences in the modeling behavior of MFCC and Mel spectrogram features and as well as their combination with statistical features extracted from the data. By demonstrating strong performance with computationally efficient models, this work contributes to the development of standardized, scalable ATM systems and advances research on privacy-preserving, sensor-friendly alternatives to vision-based traffic monitoring.

Title: TRACE: Temporal Reconstruction with Aligned Context Explanations for anomaly detection in building energy systems
Abstract: Anomaly detection in building management systems (BMS) presents two challenges: context-agnostic thresholding, in which a single global threshold cannot simultaneously accommodate high-load weekday peaks and low-load weekend periods, and unfaithful temporal attribution, in which explanation maps are decoupled from the underlying detection signals. This paper proposes TRACE (Temporal Reconstruction with Aligned Context Explanations), a unified framework that addresses both challenges within a single training objective. TRACE conditions the reconstruction encoder on cyclic temporal embeddings and calibrates anomaly thresholds independently per operational group, suppressing systematic false alarms without requiring separate context-specific models. Two complementary regularization terms shape temporal attention: an alignment loss that couples attention weights to the per-timestep reconstruction error, and a sparsity loss that concentrates attribution on the most informative timesteps. At inference, TRACE produces a detection decision alongside a two-dimensional attribution map identifying anomalous timesteps and responsible sensor channels. Experiments on two public benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach. On the Building Data Genome Project 2 (BDG2), TRACE achieves an F1-score of 0.767 and AUC-ROC of 0.845, reduces Context-FPR by 50% relative to LSTM-AE, and surpasses GradientSHAP in both Faithfulness@6 (0.401 vs. 0.340) and Stability (0.592 vs. 0.493). On the Secure Water Treatment (SWaT) dataset, where occupancy-driven daily patterns are absent, performance gains proportionally decrease, confirming that the benefit of context conditioning scales with the strength of the periodic occupancy structure in the data.

Title: AI Based Automatic Speech Assessment and Personalized Therapy for Aphasia Patients
Abstract: Aphasia is a neurological condition that affects an individual's ability to speak and understand language. Accurate analysis and evaluation of patient speech are essential for effective rehabilitation. In this study, an artificial intelligencebased speech therapy system is proposed to support aphasia rehabilitation. Speech samples are collected through structured tasks and processed using preprocessing techniques such as noise removal, silence removal, and normalization to enhance audio quality. Feature extraction is performed using Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC), pitch, and signal energy to capture speech characteristics. Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) is employed to convert speech into text, while acoustic and language models are used to manage variations in pronunciation and word sequences. Furthermore, Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques are applied to identify missing words, grammatical errors, and pronunciation mistakes. The system provides rulebased feedback by mapping detected errors to appropriate speech therapy exercises. In addition, longitudinal analysis is conducted to evaluate patient performance across multiple sessions and track progress over time. The proposed system improves the efficiency and accuracy of speech evaluation in aphasia rehabilitation, reduces manual effort, and provides structured feedback for continuous patient improvement.

Title: Q-LEAP: Millisecond Hyperdimensional Optimization for Full-Spectrum Optical Metamaterials
Abstract: Optical metamaterials exhibit superior optical performance, yet their high-dimensional design problems impede efficient global optimization. In this study, we introduce Quantum‑driven Learning and Exploration for Advanced Photonic metamaterials (Q-LEAP) that integrates material screening, property calculation and quantum-accelerated structural design. By incorporating a factorization machine (FM) algorithm and leveraging the quantum tunnelling effect of quantum annealing, we efficiently explore a vast solution space of containing 2<sup>108</sup> candidates, with a single optimization step completed in 2.56 ms, attaining an objective value that reaches 85.83% of its theoretical limit. To jointly evaluate runtime cost, sampling efficiency, and optimization effectiveness, we define normalized efficiency index on a natural‑log basis. Q‑LEAP reaches 21.77 × 10<sup>−2</sup>, approximately 40 times that of the best conventional method (0.55 × 10<sup>−2</sup>). Furthermore, we combine first‑principles calculations with a physics‑informed residual machine learning (PRML) method to predict frequency‑dependent dielectric functions. While density functional perturbation theory spectra are truncated at the phonon cutoff frequency, PRML overcomes this by using the Lorentz oscillator model as physical guidance, ensuring the high‑frequency extrapolation obeys the underlying oscillator dynamics. The Q-LEAP constitutes an efficient design strategy for de novo optical metamaterials, with quantum‑driven optimization delivering a substantial speedup. This speedup can be transferred to high‑dimensional problems in other domains.

Title: Agri-Detect: A Multi-scale Adaptive Fusion Network for Robust Citrus Leaf Disease Detection
Abstract: Citrus diseases, such as Huanglongbing (HLB) and canker, pose a significant threat to the global citrus industry, causing annual production losses of 20–30%. While deep learning models like YOLOv5 offer a promising alternative to manual inspection, they often struggle with the significant intra-class scale variation of disease symptoms and the presence of complex backgrounds. This paper proposes Agri-Detect, an enhanced detection framework built upon YOLOv5, to address these challenges. We introduce three key architectural improvements: (1) a Weighted Bi-directional Feature Pyramid Network (BiFPN) replaces the default PANet to resolve semantic inconsistencies across feature scales through an efficient, weighted information flow; (2) an Adaptively Spatial Feature Fusion (ASFF) module is integrated to act as a soft-gating mechanism, filtering conflicting spatial information across feature maps and enhancing scale-invariance; and (3) a Minimum Point Distance IoU (MPDIoU) loss function is employed to provide a more holistic and stable geometric optimization target for bounding box regression. We validate our model on a challenging real-world dataset of citrus leaf diseases. Ablation studies demonstrate that the combined improvements yield a significant performance gain over the baseline YOLOv5, increasing the overall mAP@0.5 from 92.1% to 98.3%. Our work provides a robust and accurate solution for automated plant disease detection, paving the way for more effective crop management.

Title: Simultaneous retrieval of 13 phytoplankton pigments from Sentinel-3 OLCI using convolutional neural networks and transfer learning
Abstract: Phytoplankton pigment concentrations retrieved from ocean color satellite observations provide key information on marine ecosystem composition and biogeochemical cycling. Although Machine Learning (ML) approaches have been applied to multi-spectral sensors such as the Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) and the Sea-Viewing Wide Field-of-View Sensor (SeaWiFS), no study has systematically exploited the specific band configuration of the Ocean and Land Colour Instrument (OLCI) onboard Copernicus Sentinel-3 for the simultaneous retrieval of multiple diagnostic pigments. This study presents the first systematic benchmark of five ML architectures: Random Forest (RF), eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGB), Dense Neural Network (DNN), one-dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory Network (BiLSTM) for retrieving 13 pigments of interest to the ocean color community from OLCI-equivalent multi-spectral radiometry. Training and evaluation rely on 185 co-located in situ remote-sensing reflectance and High Performance Liquid Chromatography (HPLC) pigment measurements collected across optically diverse European waters (Mediterranean Sea, Black Sea, Atlantic, and English Channel) within the BiOMaP programme. A novel two-phase Deep Learning (DL) training strategy is introduced, in which pigment-specific modules are first trained independently and subsequently concatenated into a joint multi-output model, preventing dominant, easily retrieved pigments from degrading performance for rarer accessory ones. To extend the methodology to operational satellite products, a transfer learning strategy based on fine-tuning is applied and explicitly benchmarked against training from scratch on a global matchup dataset. Additionally, a spectrally reduced version (5 central wavelengths) is developed and validated for compatibility with the Copernicus-GlobColour and European Space Agency’s Ocean Colour Climate Change Initiative datasets, enabling application of the multi-pigment retrieval framework to a 26-year continuous satellite record. Results indicate that CNN consistently outperforms all other architectures across all evaluation metrics, achieving coefficients of determination of 0.70–0.93 and mean absolute percentage errors of 25–55% across the 13 target pigments, close to the approximate 20% average percent differences of published inter-laboratory HPLC measurement round-robin experiments. The fine-tuned model systematically outperforms the from-scratch version across all 13 pigments, with mean absolute percentage errors generally lower than 70% and approximately 20-25% smaller than those obtained when training from scratch, and a coefficient of determination (R <sup>2</sup>) decreasing by approximately 0.2 relative to the in situ baseline versus a decrease of 0.3 for the from-scratch model. The spectrally reduced model retains comparable in situ performance and similar transfer learning advantages after fine-tuning. These results provide a quantitative demonstration of the value of high-quality regional in situ radiometry as a pre-training foundation for global satellite pigment retrieval. Together, these findings demonstrate the strong potential of OLCI-based CNN models for operational multi-pigment retrieval across current and future satellite missions and for long-term climatological analysis.

Title: Adapting AI-Based Medical Imaging Techniques for Forensic Gunshot Residue Analysis Using Infrared Thermography
Abstract: Forensic analysis of gunshot residue is crucial for criminal investigations, but traditional methods face limitations, particularly on challenging surfaces like textiles. Infrared thermography offers a promising non-invasive alternative. This study explores the feasibility of adapting artificial intelligence techniques, commonly used in medical imaging, to analyze thermal patterns of gunshot residue. A pilot dataset comprising 133 thermograms from controlled firearm experiments was used to develop a series of predictive models. Our approach ranged from baseline machine learning classifiers using extracted features to advanced deep learning architectures. We evaluated transfer learning with ResNet-18 and EfficientNet-B0 models and implemented a multi-task learning framework to simultaneously predict shooting distance, firearm type, and ammunition type. The results demonstrate that baseline models using extracted features significantly outperform those using image data. Deep learning, particularly the fine-tuned ResNet-18, showed superior performance in regression and classification tasks. Utilizing infrared thermograms and extracted features, the multi-task model yielded the most promising results, achieving a classification accuracy of 0.81 for binned shooting distance, 0.76 for weapon type, and 0.71 for ammunition. This work confirms that integrating AI with infrared thermography is a robust and viable methodology for gunshot residue analysis, offering a potential pathway to a faster, objective, and non-destructive tool for forensic science.

Title: Demand Forecasting for Audio Products and Musical Instruments
Abstract: Accurate demand forecasting is essential for inventory planning in retail environments characterized by heterogeneous product portfolios and highly variable sales patterns. This study evaluates six forecasting approaches - SARIMA, Prophet, Random Forest, XGBoost, LSTM, and SVR - using 79 months of sales data from an anonymous distributor of musical instruments and audio equipment. Exploratory analysis revealed a strongly concentrated demand structure, with only 22 references (1.4% of the catalog) accounting for 80% of total units sold. Forecasting experiments were conducted on the highest-volume reference using a strict temporal hold-out strategy and multiple accuracy metrics, including RMSE, MASE, and sMAPE. Prophet achieved the best overall performance (RMSE = 955 units, MASE = 0.45, sMAPE = 24.8%), while all evaluated models outperformed the naïive seasonal benchmark. The effect of dimensionality reduction was further assessed through PCA. PCA reduced the feature space from 11 to 9 dimensions while preserving 95% of the variance and improved Random Forest performance to RMSE = 957 units and MASE = 0.39, the best result among the tabular models, whereas LSTM performance deteriorated under the same transformation. These contrasting outcomes indicate that the benefits of dimensionality reduction are model-dependent. The results demonstrate that forecasting accuracy is strongly influenced by the temporal structure of the series and by the interaction between feature representation and learning algorithm.

Title: Coherent DOAs Estimation via Muti-Task Network Enhanced Sparse Variational Bayesian Method
Abstract: Direction of arrival (DOA) estimation is a crucial component of array signal processing. Classical DOA estimation algorithms, such as the multiple signal classification (MUSIC) and the estimation of signal parameters via rotational invariance techniques (ESPRIT), typically perform angle estimation under the assumption that sources are mutually independent of each other, which is often violated in practice due to the effects of, e.g., multi-path, leading to the coherent nature of sources at the receiver. To address this problem, this paper proposes a joint scheme integrating deep learning networks and sparse variational Bayesian (SVB). Specifically, the proposed method first utilises a deep learning network to extract angle features from the received signals, yielding the correlation relationships between sources and coarse estimates of DOA. Subsequently, accurate DOA estimation is achieved via SVB. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively cope with the impacts of complex gain errors and signal multipath effects, and its performance outperforms that of the traditional MUSIC algorithm.

Title: COMSYS Hackathon-6: VoiceHack Hack the Fake, Save the Real
Abstract: The COMSYS Hackathon-6, 2025 was a rigorous and intellectually engaging challenge organized by the COMSYS Educational Trust, Kolkata, in conjunction with the 4th International Conference on Data, Electronics and Computing (ICDEC-2025). The primary objective of this competition was to establish a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating and comparing the effectiveness of modern machine learning and deep learning approaches for deepfake audio identification. The Hackathon specifically targeted real versus fake audio detection, gender-aware deepfake analysis, and robust subject identification under short-duration and potentially degraded audio conditions. The competition was designed to promote advancements in audio-centric Artificial Intelligence systems capable of operating reliably in real-world environments, where recordings may be noisy, compressed, truncated, or intentionally manipulated. To achieve this, three curated datasets - SoundSniff, GenderGlitch, and MimicMap - were developed, each aligned with a specific task. The challenge featured supervised and semi-supervised learning tracks, low-parameter constraints, and weighted multi-task evaluation, emphasizing generalization, efficiency, and deployability. This report presents a detailed overview of the Hackathon objectives, datasets, problem formulations, evaluation protocol, and participating teams, followed by discussions on challenges and research implications in robust deepfake audio detection. The developed datasets and benchmark performance are available at https://github.com/praetorian2710/Comsys-Hackathon-6.

Title: MARS and ETMS: A Large-Scale Dataset and Ship-Size Sensitive Detection Method in Maritime Applications
Abstract: Real-time and accurate detection of ships is an essential requirement to improve marine vehicle collision avoidance and security for autonomous ship navigation. In this paper, we propose a practical large-scale detection dataset for marine ships (MARS), to handle the data requirements of ship detection tasks by considering background diversity, ship categories, ship sizes, viewpoint changes, and marine waves, etc. Furthermore, a lightweight anchor-free network called the enhanced training-time-friendly network (TTFNet) for marine ships (ETMS) is proposed, which achieves excellent detection performance for medium and small sized vessels. In particular, we first reconstruct the backbone structure and then make features perform adaptive weighted fusion in the neck structure to provide more abundant feature representations with a lightweight network. Second, a coordinate alignment compensation (CAC) module is proposed to solve the misalignment problem regarding the optimal location of different branches in the head structure, and the corresponding refinement loss is set to achieve consistency optimization. Our thorough experimental findings consistently prove that ETMS surpasses other ship detection methods, achieving an impressive 82.7 AP.5:.95 on SeaShips(7000) and 69.2 AP.5:.95 on MARS. These results highlight the effectiveness of ETMS for ship detection tasks. The application of deep learning in marine surveillance is of great significance for enhancing marine transportation safety and improving port traffic management efficiency.

Title: Enhanced Streaming Joint ASR and Disfluency Detection via Synthetic Data Generation
Abstract: The Disfluency Detection (DD) task has mainly been solved as a post-processing stage following Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems. This two-stage pipeline requires two separate models to handle these tasks independently, resulting in higher inference latency and additional inference overhead, and the disfluency detection task does not use the rich acoustic information in the audio that could aid in more accurate inference. To address these limitations, we propose a streaming joint model built upon the WeNet framework. By utilizing a shared encoder-decoder network, our model simultaneously performs streaming automatic speech recognition and disfluency detection, facilitating cross-task representation learning while achieving low latency and lightweight inference. However, training such a joint model requires multi-label datasets that contain parallel audio, transcripts, and explicit disfluency annotations, which are scarce and difficult to obtain. To overcome this data bottleneck, we propose a Double-Sided Label Augmentation (DSLA) method to construct a multi-label dataset: generate corresponding disfluent versions of news text by systematically introducing perturbations into fluent news text, and then use a pre-trained Text-to-Speech (TTS) model to generate audio from these disfluent versions. Experiments on the Switchboard test set show that the proposed model achieves competitive performance, while the double-sided label augmentation strategy effectively alleviates the data scarcity bottleneck, further enhancing the performance of the model and enabling it to significantly outperform baseline models.

Title: Heterogeneous Knowledge Distillation for Automatic Chord Recognition: A Dual-Path Multi-Teacher Framework
Abstract: Automatic chord recognition (ACR) is a fundamental task in music information retrieval (MIR) that aims to extract chord progression sequences from audio signals. While deep neural networks have become the dominant approach for ACR, different architectures exhibit distinct advantages: CNNs excel at capturing local harmonic features, BLSTMs effectively model medium-range temporal dependencies, and Transformers capture long-range global context. However, each architecture has inherent limitations that constrain overall performance. This paper proposes a novel multi-model advantage fusion method that systematically integrates the complementary knowledge of these three architectures through a dual-path knowledge fusion mechanism. The proposed approach employs feature-level fusion to inherit the core feature extraction capabilities of each base model and output-level fusion to absorb their decision logic and semantic knowledge. By training a unified Transformer-based fusion model using knowledge distillation from CNN, BLSTM, and Transformer teacher models, our method achieves simultaneous modeling of local harmonic details, medium-range temporal dependencies, and long-range global context. Experimental results on two public datasets demonstrate that the proposed fusion model significantly outperforms individual base models and simple ensemble methods, achieving root accuracy of 83.27% and major/minor accuracy of 82.19%. The dual-path fusion mechanism proves effective, with both feature-level and output-level fusion contributing to performance improvements.

Title: Advancing Multi-Speaker Audio Deepfake Detection through Chunk-Based Evidence Aggregation
Abstract: Audio deepfakes generated by modern text-tospeech (TTS) AI systems pose significant risks to the integrity of all types of digital communications. While most detection methods focus on short and single-speaker utterances, realworld audio often involves longer recordings with diverse and complex characteristics, including multi-speaker conversational content and even partially manipulated content. In this work, we study chunk-based aggregation strategies for audio deepfake detection across heterogeneous datasets including both single and multi speaker settings. We present a systematic empirical study of two complementary chunk-based aggregation methods: (i) Local Evidence Aggregation (LEA), which uses overlapping segmentation of audio clips with Top- K scoring to emphasize the most suspicious segments, and (ii) Global Evidence Aggregation (GEA), which uses non-overlapping segmentation of audio clips with voting to capture the overall consistency of spoof characteristics. Experiments on ASVspoof 2019 logical access (LA), PartialSpoof, ASVspoof5, and MsCADD (a multi-speaker conversational audio deepfakes dataset) show that aggregation strategy significantly impacts detection performance. We found that LEA is more effective for localized manipulations, while GEA performs better when spoof artifacts are consistently distributed across the audio. These results highlight the importance of aligning evidence aggregation strategy with data characteristics for robust real-world deployment especially for complex deepfakes with multiple speakers or partial deepfakes.

Title: Affective Computing Deep Learning Framework: Emotion Recognition and Music Suggestion via Convolutional Neural Network
Abstract: This paper proposes an all-inclusive deep learning framework for facial emotion recognition (FER) along with music recommendation systems to improve the user experience in affective computing. The system performs real-time FER from webcam video using three CNN architectures: a custom CNN, ResNet50V2, and VGG16. Detections of emotions are mapped to a set of playlists for music recommendation specific to the emotions. Facial detection uses Haar Cascade classifiers, and the system categorizes emotions into the following seven classes: anger, disgust, fear, happiness, neutral, sadness, and surprise. Emotionally categorized music tracks are retrieved from Spotify playlists in CSV format for quick access. Everything is integrated into a web application based on Flask which supports the real time emotion detection and music play features. Model performance is evaluated with confusion matrices, classification reports, and training-validation curves. The web interface outputs demonstrate the functionality of the music recommendation system, confirming the integrated framework works effectively in real time.

Title: Development of a PCR-based technique for genotyping UGT1A1 gene and distribution of rs3064744 alleles in the Russian population
Abstract: Background – Accurate determination of tandem thymine-adenine (TA) repeat numbers in the UGT1A1 promoter region (rs3064744) is essential for diagnosing Gilbert’s syndrome and personalizing therapy with toxic agents like irinotecan and atazanavir. However, traditional polymerase chain reaction (PCR) assays face severe limitations due to the AT-rich sequence and overlapping melting temperatures (Tm) of the highly homologous 7TA and 8TA alleles. In this context, melting curve analysis (MCA) employing fluorophore-quencher systems has emerged as a promising alternative. The purpose of this study was to develop a novel genotyping approach combining optimized aPCR-MCA analysis with an automated classifier to overcome the limitations posed by the differentiation of highly homologous alleles and to demonstrate its practical application, providing the distribution of rs3064744 genotypes across four regional cohorts of the Russian population. Methods – A specialized Dual Head 1D-convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) ensemble with Test-Time Augmentation (TTA) was developed. The model was trained and internally validated on 1, 620 engineered plasmid samples, and independently evaluated on an external clinical test set of 440 unique patient genomic DNA specimens. Real-time PCR was performed on CFX96 and DTprime platforms. Additionally, population-wide screening was conducted on 997 archival clinical samples from Moscow, Sakha (Yakutia), Dagestan, and Rostov regions. Results – While 5TA and 6TA alleles were easily separated, absolute Tm distributions of 7TA and 8TA alleles overlapped significantly, and non-uniform Tm shifts of 0.8 °C–1.4 °C occurred across platforms. Conventional absolute Tm thresholding was therefore inadequate. By assessing relative morphological curve divergence against co-amplified 7TA/7TA and 7TA/8TA reference anchors, the 1D-CNN ensemble neutralized instrument noise. It achieved 100% accuracy on internal validation and 100% concordance (440/440) with clinical reference pyrosequencing. Population screening revealed that Dagestan, Yakutia, and Rostov cohorts closely align with the European population. Rare 5TA and 8TA alleles were detected at low frequencies in Yakutia and Moscow. Conclusion – Combining LNA-modified aPCR-MCA with a comparative 1D-CNN model successfully circumvents thermodynamic limitations and eliminates human operator bias. This integrated system offers an accessible, high-throughput, and clinically valid solution for routine UGT1A1 pharmacogenetic testing.

Title: Distorted Realities: Classifying Extreme Vocals Between Harmony and Noise – A Machine–Human Evaluation of Vocal Confusion Patterns
Abstract: Extreme vocal techniques like growling and shrieking are common in metal and related genres, giving the music a characteristic intensity. Although widely used, these techniques have received limited attention in Music Information Retrieval (MIR) and musicology, particularly in fine-grained categorisation. Their niche status and marginalisation have led to limited representation in digital music libraries. Since current classification systems prioritise dominant subgenres due to a lack of detailed vocal categorisations, extreme vocal styles are often oversimplified or misrepresented, hindering tagging, retrieval, and analysis. Automation could enable consistent and nuanced vocal annotation, supporting the technical goals of MIR and analytical aims of musicology. Foregrounding vocal technique as a classification axis contributes to a richer understanding of vocal performance and genre formation. To assess machine learning as a reliable alternative to human judgment, this study developed a coarse frequency-based qualitative taxonomy from interviews with 11 extreme vocal practitioners and compared human and machine performance using the Extreme Metal Vocals Dataset (EMVD), including a listening test with 158 expert participants. Perceptual results achieved 76.2% Unweighted Average Recall (UAR), while a Support Vector Machine (SVM) model trained on ComParE features achieved a UAR of 90% on average, using singer-independent 3-fold group cross-validation. Feature group, ablation, and human prediction analyses suggest that the human-machine gap reflects differences in cue prioritisation and classification performance. Results illustrate the feasibility of machine learning to annotate vocal styles, while showing that human confusion patterns remain informative for category boundaries. This highlights how MIR methods could facilitate analysis of underrepresented genres.

Title: Predictive Forecasting of Consumer Purchase Intention in Voice Commerce: A Reproducible Benchmark of Classical, Deep and Generative AI Under a Common-Method-Variance Constraint
Abstract: Voice commerce is projected to grow rapidly, yet model comparisons in this literature typically tune a favoured method against default baselines on a single data split, and rarely examine whether the accuracy they report depends on how the constructs were measured. We evaluate eighteen methods - ten classical learners, four deep tabular architectures, three tabular generative models, and a few-shot large-language-model predictor - on an experimental dataset of 902 consumers in a 3 × 2 between-subjects design crossing voice-assistant identity with message valence, giving every model the same search budget on the same folds, with paired significance tests and multiplicity correction. Because predictors and outcome are elicited from the same respondent in a single instrument, we define predictor eligibility on measurement grounds and restrict the models to constructs measured independently of the outcome's own instrument section; contrasting that set against the full candidate set locates 20.6% of the apparent accuracy in common method variance rather than in predictive signal (cross-validated R<sup>2</sup> of 0.756 against 0.599). Three conclusions follow. Complexity is not the binding constraint: ElasticNet leads at R<sup>2</sup> = 0.6007 and Ridge follows at 0.5987, no model attains a Holm-corrected significant advantage over Ridge, and nine of the ten learners fall within 0.0101 R<sup>2</sup> of one another - less than a quarter of the fold-to-fold standard deviation - while the tree ensembles carry train-test gaps nine times larger and a serialized footprint 1334 times bigger for no gain, the deep architectures reach at most R<sup>2</sup> = 0.5587, and the LLM predictor trails a linear model on identical inputs. Measurement dominates modeling: the eligibility contrast is fifteen times larger than the spread between learners, and on the full candidate set the same protocol reverses the ranking of the linear and ensemble families. The signal is thin and cheap: 16 acceptance and anthropomorphism constructs suffice, and the 16-item emotional battery is removable for 0.0035 R<sup>2</sup>, which makes not collecting it the strongest available safeguard against emotion-based targeting. We recommend that predictive studies on self-reported constructs report the eligibility contrast alongside accuracy, and that practitioners deploy a penalized linear model on a dozen items rather than an ensemble whose cost is measured and whose gain is not.

Title: Advancing Self-Supervised Spoofed Audio Detection through Auto-Labeled Linguistic Cues
Abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI)-generated content (deepfakes in particular) are considered to be a major threat that can lead to fraud and the spread of incorrect information. The focus of generative AI research has largely been on advancements in content generation, with less attention given to detection of AI generated content with malicious intent, particularly for AI generated audio deepfakes. Although foundation models (such as HuBERT and XLSR-Wav2vec) offer powerful representations for detecting spoofed audio, they suffer from limitations in explainability and slow extraction speeds, which affect scalability. Prior research has integrated sociolinguistic expertise to identify phonetic and phonological cues in spoken English for spoofed audio detection. This approach, while successful, was limited in scale as it relied on the labeling of linguistic features by domain experts. In this paper, we propose a novel model to auto-label expert-informed phonetic and phonological cues through deep-learning based representations fine tuned with domain expert input. As such, using the fine-tuning method with expert-informed features, we scale this interdisciplinary approach and demonstrate its benefits in enhancing explainability and optimizing resource utilization (consumed time) for utilizing foundation models in large-scale applications. For example, when considering XLSR-Wav2vec-ResNet18 as one of the most recent baselines, in our proposed cost efficient ensemble setup, we achieved 31% to 63% time reduction in audio deepfake detection (scalability) across the tested datasets. Additionally, the algorithmically encoded linguistic features enhanced the explainability via reverse engineering (explainability). Our proposed method is a multi-view approach as it takes advantage of not only deep representations, but also human expert-informed phonetic and phonological aspects of natural speech. In summary, our approach supplements Self Supervised Learning models by reducing required time and increasing the explainability of audio deepfake detection.
