Title: Voice-Based Gender Detection Using Deep Learning: a Comprehensive Review
Abstract: Voice Gender Recognition is an extremely challenging task which has been included in both Voice Feature Analysis and Natural Language Processing. This review paper presents an overall review of the deep learning methods that have been used to perform Voice Gender Classification by analyzing the various methodologies relating to the deep learning methods for Voice Feature Extraction and Voice Gender Recognition. The authors reviewed the vocal features (pitch & modulation) and the feature extraction methods (MFCCs and Spectrograms) and how the architectures from the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) can be employed to improve the performance of the voice-based systems. The experimental results demonstrate that the employment of the deep learning methods in both the feature extraction and voice gender recognition tasks have improved significantly the performance of the voice-based systems. In addition, the study demonstrated that employing the deep learning method can dramatically increase the accuracy and efficiency of the voice-based systems. Overall, the results indicate that the advancements of the Artificial Neural Networks and the new models are significant factors in the advancement of this area. This review will serve as a valuable reference source for researchers and practitioners in the area of Real-World Gender Recognition, especially to improve the Human Machine Interaction. Additionally, the results of the review illustrate that there is still need for additional advancements to the Deep Learning Methods to take full advantage of the capabilities of the current technology. However, additional research is required to close the research gap between the current state-of-the-art and the performance of the current audio systems.

Title: AI-enhanced learning tools: impact of information quality characteristics on perceived ease of use analyzed with PLS-SEM and NCA
Abstract: Purpose – The purpose of this paper is to explore how the four dimensions of informational quality characteristics – accuracy, comprehensiveness, relevance, and timeliness – shape learners' perceptions of the ease of use of information in AI-enhanced learning environments. The study seeks to deepen understanding of how the quality of AI-generated instructional content influences students' ability to engage with, interpret, and apply information effectively. By extending the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) to comprise informational attributes, the paper aims to clarify which informational quality characteristics make AI-supported learning more intuitive, cognitively efficient, and pedagogically meaningful. Design/methodology/approach – A total of 197 responses were collected among undergraduate and graduate business students at a mid-sized Canadian university during the winter of 2024. The respondents were at least 18 years old. The researchers developed a survey instrument whose questions originated from prior research. SPSS and Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) with the Importance-Performance (IPMA) and Necessary Condition Analysis (NCA) were utilized as statistical techniques. Findings – The results indicate that comprehensiveness is the only significant determinant of perceived ease of use of information in AI-enhanced learning environments. IPMA identifies comprehensiveness as a high-importance but underperforming factor, suggesting that improvements in this area would most enhance usability. NCA further reveals that both comprehensiveness and relevance are essential, must-have conditions for ease of use. In contrast, accuracy and timeliness exert limited influence on perceived ease of use. Originality/value – This study extends the explanatory scope of TAM by incorporating informational quality characteristics as antecedents of perceived ease of use in AI-enhanced learning contexts. It is among the first to combine PLS-SEM, IPMA, and NCA to distinguish between determinant and must-have predictors of usability. The findings highlight that the comprehensiveness and relevance of AI-generated information – rather than its accuracy or timeliness – are the key factors shaping learners' perceptions of ease of use.

Title: The Effect of Artificial Intelligence Applications on Employee Retention and Turnover in Higher Education Institutions
Abstract: This study aims to investigate how artificial intelligence (AI) impacts employee retention and turnover at the University of Babylon. Since Iraqi universities have been experiencing extreme challenges for years related to employee retention, it is critical to analyze the role of AI as a solution to address these issues. In order to conduct the study a descriptive-analytic-quantitative methodology was employed. A survey instrument was developed based on 50 items and categorized into three areas: organizational culture, AI and employee turnover. 150 Technical and Administrative Staff members of Administration College and Humanities Colleges at the University of Babylon participated in the study by randomly completing an anonymous survey instrument. Statistical methods were applied to analyze 146 returned surveys. Findings show that AI is positively contributing to the development of employee retention strategies and reduction of turnover rates. Specifically, AI technologies, decision support technology and intelligent automation are impacting employee behavior in the form of intent to quit, employee job satisfaction and job stability. Overall, results indicated that AI is directly affecting all aspects of employee turnover as identified by the independent variable and clearly demonstrates the need for academic institutions to apply AI to their Human Resource Practices strategically. This research ends with recommendations to increase funding for AI based systems in universities and to organize efforts to create a productive organizational culture. Additionally, it recommends providing educational programs to help employees understand the advantages of AI and to strengthen workforce stability and the institution’s overall performance.

Title: The Fingerprint PAD Exposimeter (X-FPAD): A Visual Framework for Evaluating Generalization to Unseen Attacks
Abstract: Generalization to unseen Presentation Attack Instruments (PAIs) remains the primary bottleneck of fingerprint Presentation Attack Detection (PAD). State-of-the-art detectors operate as opaque classifiers, leaving practitioners without actionable guidance for dataset composition and vulnerability assessment. We propose X-FPAD (Fingerprint PAD Exposimeter), an interpretability-driven framework that projects deep fingerprint features into a deterministic two-dimensional latent space governed by a radial-angular geometry: bona fide samples are anchored at the origin, each known PAI occupies a dedicated angular sector, and radial distance encodes deviation from authentic skin. The geometry is enforced natively during training through a compound radial-angular loss. We validate X-FPAD on two optical sensors (Green Bit, Dermalog) through a three-phase protocol. Unseen PAIs are first mapped onto the known materials that govern their representation; those materials are then removed from the training set and four PAD architectures are retrained from scratch, one of them designed for generalization to unseen attacks. To establish that the resulting APCER degradation is specific to the materials the manifold names, rather than a generic cost of training on less data, the predictions are checked against an exhaustive leave-one-material-out sweep in which every training material is removed in turn: every predicted dependency shifts in the direction the manifold assigns it, while removing a material it reports as unrelated leaves performance within run-to-run variation in nine of every ten cases. The same attribution, run forward, tests the dataset-composition claim directly: adding the material the manifold recommends recovers 18.4 APCER points, 87% of what the best available candidate would have given, against 52% for an uninformed choice among the same candidates. X-FPAD is thereby supported as a cross-architecture diagnostic tool for informed dataset composition and vulnerability auditing.

Title: Mood-Aware Music Classification and Recommendation Using Machine Learning
Abstract: In modern digital world, music plays a role far beyond entertainment—it supports emotional expression, mental well-being, and social connection. However, with countless tracks on streaming platforms, listeners often struggle to find songs that fit their mood. This work proposes a mood-aware Music Recommendation System that uses machine learning and audio signal analysis to deliver personalized suggestions. With Random Forest classifiers, songs are categorized into moods like happiness, sadness, anger, fear, and neutral, and its performance is evaluated not only via accuracy, but also precision, recall, and F1 score, along with confusion matrices to analyze class-by-class prediction quality and achieved 88% accuracy. We also compare our Random Forest method to Support Vector Machine, a Convolutional Neural Network, evaluate its performance and implement a similarity-based recommendation engine for tracks that are musically and emotionally similar. The system combines signal processing, supervised learning and feature engineering in a Streamlit interface and is flexible enough to be implemented on a data science-oriented platform such as Spotify. Use cases for the system include music streaming, mental health, therapy, fitness, education, and smart homes, setting the stage to emotionally smart music.

Title: Signal Singularity Analysis for Robust Deep Audio Splicing Detection and Localization
Abstract: Deep learning has achieved strong performance in utterance-level audio anti-spoofing, yet spliced or partially manipulated speech remains difficult to detect because only short manipulated segments are embedded within otherwise realistic speech utterances. Building on prior singularity analysis for audio splicing, this work constructs a wavelet-reconstructed singularity detection feature (SDF) and employs a dedicated encoder to extract a discriminative SDF embedding. The resulting embedding is concatenated with linear frequency cepstral coefficients (LFCCs) and processed by a Light Convolutional Neural Network (LCNN) and a sequence model to capture both local boundary artifacts and temporal dependencies for frame-level detection. In addition, auxiliary supervision is applied to the SDF branch during training to encourage more discriminative SDF representations. Experiments on the HAD benchmark show consistent improvements over LFCC-based baselines, while results on the unseen split and under additive-noise conditions further support the effectiveness of the jointly trained SDF embedding under the evaluated conditions.

Title: An Efficient Deep Learning Framework for Gastric Cancer Detection Based on Improved DenseNet and Bio-Inspired Optimization
Abstract: Early diagnosis and successful treatment planning, Gastric Cancer (GC) detection and categorization from medical imaging is important. This paper presents a sophisticated architecture for computer-aided diagnosis with the use of Improved DenseNet tuned Ant Colony Optimization (ACO). The input data is fed to Non-Local Means (NLM) filter it is used in the pre-processing step to efficiently reduce image noise whereas maintaining minute structural details that are crucial for diagnosis. Fuzzy K-Means (FKM) clustering is then used to the improved image for reliable segmentation, securing that cancerous and non-cancerous zones are accurately separated using fuzzy membership functions. Histograms of Orientated Gradients (HOG) features are extracted to capture texture and edge-based discriminative information to characterise the segmented regions. An Improved DenseNet model improves feature propagation and gradient flow through modified dense connectivity, is then used to classify these features. The ACO algorithm is used to improve convergence performance and further optimise the classifier's parameters. Results from experiments show that proposed structure attains higher precision, recall, accuracy as well as F1-score of 94%, which becomes a potent instrument for automatic and dependable GC detection from medical imaging data.

Title: AI-Automation Tooling in Computer Engineering Education: Mixed-Methods TAM/UTAUT Evidence for a General Acceptance Attitude
Abstract: As generative AI and low-code workflow platforms become routine in software practice, a key educational question is whether the next generation of computer engineers will accept these tools as useful, usable, and worth sustained engagement. This paper reports a mixed-methods, cross-sectional study of undergraduate computer engineering students' acceptance of AI-automation tooling - instantiated via the workflow automation platform n8n across three identically scripted workshops in Thailand (n = 103). A 12-item, five-point Likert instrument mapped to six TAM/UTAUT constructs - Performance Expectancy (PE), Effort Expectancy (EE), Behavioral Intention (BI), Self-Efficacy (SE), Hedonic Motivation (HM), and Output Quality (OQ) - was complemented by inductive thematic analysis of open-ended feedback. Analyses combined ordinal reliability estimation, bootstrap confidence intervals, non-parametric tests, multiple-comparison-controlled correlations, polychoric dimensionality diagnostics, a common-method-bias check, and between-session comparisons. Acceptance was favourable across all six constructs at large effect sizes - PE strongest, HM weakest - and dimensionality diagnostics revealed that canonical TAM/UTAUT sub-facets collapse into a single general acceptance factor in this short-form post-workshop context, a methodologically and theoretically consequential finding. Qualitative themes converged with the quantitative profile on usefulness and enthusiasm but diverged on output quality, surfacing a small reliability-concerned subset. Findings support cautious curricular integration of AI-automation tooling in undergraduate computing education and identify three theory-grounded instructional levers: instruction-sequencing scaffolds, self-efficacy supports, and trust-calibration interventions.

Title: A Noise-Robust Melody Transcription Model Optimized for Humming Signals Using AI
Abstract: Humming is a natural and very effective method for musicians and composers to communicate musical thoughts and ideas, but hummed melodies are very difficult to develop into fully functional musical compositions because of differences in performance accuracy and tempo. Recent progress in artificial intelligence has opened a new horizon for melody extraction and music composition from hummed audio signals. The paper describes a musically intelligent system for melody extraction and music composition from hummed audio signals where a hummed audio signal is used to extract musically coherent features and develop them into a musically coherent composition. Sound feature extraction, melody transcription by deep learning, and generative music modeling are combined to remove the disparity between unstructured vocal queries and organized musical responses. Various machine learning strategies are adopted to address the noise, pitch variation, and rhythmic irregularities that come with humming signals. Researchers use the proposed approach to validate its efficiency and effectiveness for correctly conveying melodic intentions and generating musically valid output responses that can be returned either as audio or as symbolic musical representation to support music creative tasks like music composition tools, creative applications, and hum-to-search applications

Title: Intelligent Reading Recognition Method Based on Deep Learning for Liquid Crystal Digital Display Instruments Real-Time Data Towards Smart Manufacturing
Abstract: Real-time and accurate information acquisition is the key support for smart manufacturing, which can provide timely and effective data for production decision-making, quality control etc. Various types of instruments are used for measurement and detection in product production process of smart manufacturing shopfloor, most of which are liquid crystal digital display (LCDD) instruments. However, many LCDD instruments currently lack communication interfaces for data transmission and collection, and data reading and recording still depend on manual work, which leads to problems such as low efficiency, high error-proneness and poor real-time performance. To solve the above problems, the requirements for reading recognition of LCDD instruments real-time data in the context of smart manufacturing is analyzed, and taking into account actual industrial scenarios such as illumination, tilt, complex background, scale variation and data frequency variation. A deep learning-based intelligent reading recognition framework for LCDD instruments real-time data is proposed. A string region detection model for LCDD instruments real-time data based on YOLOv4-tiny is constructed to realize the rapid positioning and segmentation of instruments reading display regions. A string recognition method for LCDD instruments real-time data based on Convolutional Recurrent Neural Network (CRNN) is proposed. Experimental results verify that the proposed method can effectively realize intelligent, accurate reading recognition of LCDD instruments real-time data.

Title: Responsible Generative AI Governance in Enterprise and Healthcare Environments
Abstract: This study delves into key policy issues required for the regulation of Generative AI in high-stakes domains such as enterprise management and clinical health care. As more and more organizations deploy large language models in their tools and systems for automation, decision support, or patient care, questions of data privacy, algorithmic bias, and transparency in decision-making processes are crucial. A curated data set of 397 cases of AI failures and successes in different corporate and medical departments is used in this study. We are employing mixed methods (qualitative risk assessment instruments and quantitative performance measures) to analyse the effect of governance arrangements on the operational effectiveness and ethics. Our findings indicate that decentralized governance of data can lead to increased risks in managing data, and that data governance with a human-in-The-loop can significantly enhance data diagnostics and compliance to company policies. The study offers a blueprint for action for policymakers on the need to adopt effective guardrails to balance innovation with safety. The identified key bottlenecks in generative systems' integration are extracted from the technical logs and policy documentation in the dataset. Finally, it is important to emphasize that a multidisciplinary governance approach should be promoted, considering the ethical transparency and institutional accountability aspects, and a permanent and dynamic monitoring of the generative technologies should be maintained in professional contexts, due to the natural dynamism of these technologies.

Title: Implementation of machine learning for wind speed retrieval from HY-2B altimeter
Abstract: This study presents a novel machine learning algorithm for wind speed retrieval using the Haiyang-2B (HY-2B) altimeter. To construct a high-fidelity reference dataset, a wind field over the Northwest Pacific Ocean with a spatial resolution of 0.05° and an hourly temporal resolution was hindcast by the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model for the period from 2022 to 2024. Data from multiple active and passive sensors, specifically the Haiyang-2 (HY-2) constellation, the advanced scatterometer (ASCAT), the soil moisture active passive (SMAP) radiometer and the Advanced Microwave Scanning Radiometer 2 (AMSR-2), were assimilated into the WRF simulation. Validation of the atmospheric simulations against moored buoy observations yielded a root mean square error (RMSE) of 2.06 m/s, a correlation coefficient (r) of 0.73 and a scatter index (SI) of 0.42. Subsequently, the normalized radar cross section (NRCS) and significant wave height (SWH) from the HY-2B altimeter were collocated with the simulated wind speeds to train four machine learning models, namely the light gradient boosting machine (LightGBM), random forest (RF), eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) and residual network (ResNet). The ResNet model demonstrated superior performance, achieving an RMSE of 1.60 m/s, an r of 0.86 and an SI of 0.32. This significantly outperforms the operational HY-2B product, which exhibited an RMSE of 2.52 m/s, an r of 0.69 and an SI of 0.50 when validated against independent moored buoy observations in 2025. These results indicate that the proposed algorithm substantially enhances the accuracy of altimeter-derived wind speeds. Furthermore, when applied specifically to tropical cyclones (TCs), the method demonstrated robust capabilities by achieving an RMSE of 4.72 m/s, an r of 0.84 and an SI of 0.44.

Title: Pilot study comparing operating room workflow and team ergonomics in robotic-assisted versus navigated total knee arthroplasty
Abstract: Background: Robotic-assisted systems have been developed to improve the accuracy and reproducibility of total knee arthroplasty (TKA). While outcomes have been widely studied, the effects of these systems on intraoperative workflow and surgical team workload have received less attention. The aim of this study was to compare procedural setup, efficiency, workload, and ergonomics between the VELYS robotic-assisted solution (VRAS) and computer-navigated TKA (NAVI). Methods: Twenty patients who underwent primary TKA performed by a single surgeon, using a single implant type, were enrolled in this research (10VRAS, 10NAVI). Procedural efficiency was assessed by reference to an AI-backed process digital twin platform. Workload was evaluated using NASA-TLX questionnaires, objective ergonomic measures (power tool holding times, retractor holding times, and leg holding times), and a tray analysis. Results: The mean total operating room (OR) time was 69.4 min for the VRAS group and 72.9 min for the NAVI group, with no significant difference. The preparation (22 min) and the breakdown times (12.6 vs.11.7 min) were equivalent. The skin-to-skin times averaged 34.3 min for the VRAS group versus 38.9 min for the NAVI group. NASA-TLX scores revealed significantly lower mental, physical, and temporal demands, reduced effort and frustration, and better perceived performance of the surgeon in the VRAS group (p < 0.05). The instrument burden was similar, 5 trays (21.5 kg) for VRAS and 4 trays (20.9 kg) for NAVI. The objective workload was reduced for the VRAS group, with shorter power tool holding (2.7 vs. 7.7 min, p < 0.001), retractor holding (7.8 vs. 13.0 min, p = 0.01), and leg holding times (3.4 vs. 4.7 min, p = 0.02). Discussion: Compared with navigated TKA, robotic assistance did not prolong overall OR time and was associated with lower measured NASA-TLX scores. These findings suggest that robotic-assisted TKA may offer workflow and ergonomic advantages, although further studies with larger samples are needed to confirm these preliminary observations. Level of evidence: Level 4, retrospective study.

Title: AI-Enabled Participatory Marketing: A Bibliometric Analysis and Research Agenda
Abstract: Aim/Purpose This study addresses the structurally skewed measurement of performance outcomes in the rapidly expanding AI-enabled participatory marketing literature. This paper aims to map the intellectual structure of this field, to measure the amount of outcome-related research in six performance domains and to identify the gaps that should guide the next cycle of empirical investment for the field. Background This fragmentation makes it harder to compare studies, carry out meta-analytic synthesis, and for practitioners to predict what outcome dimensions will be most reliably influenced by investments in AI marketing. Bibliometric analysis offers a reproducible, data-driven tool for unlocking the structural distribution of this research in an expanding, technology-intensive corpus. Methodology Following a three-stage sequential screening process (criteria: publication date 2015 or later; peer-review status; and substantial treatment of AI marketing or participatory marketing outcomes), a final corpus of 467 records (2015–2026) was constructed. We applied four complementary bibliometric methods: 1. publication trend analysis; 2. source and author analysis; 3. keyword co-occurrence network analysis; and 4. performance outcome mapping protocol with domainspecific lexicons. Contribution This paper aims to provide the following: (1) what is, to the authors' knowledge, the first comprehensive bibliometric map of AI-enabled participatory marketing research organized around a six-domain performance outcome framework; (2) a quantitative distribution of outcome coverage revealing overrepresented areas (efficiency: 40.3%; stakeholder trust: 38.5%) and a critical empirical gap (market reach: 8.4%); and (3) a six-direction research agenda based on bibliometric evidence rather than researcher judgment to rebalance the field's methodological portfolio. Findings Five thematic clusters were identified (% of 467-paper corpus; multi-assignment permitted): AI and Data Infrastructure (37.3%); Digital Marketing Strategy (33.0%); Stakeholder and Participatory Engagement (58.9%); Organizational Dynamics and Leadership (30.0%); and Performance and Competitive Outcomes (60.0%). The corpus grew at a CAGR of 23.3% (2015-2024), with a YoY growth of 192.6% in 2024. Recommendations for Practitioners AI marketing managers should prioritize the following: (1) longitudinal measurement frameworks that track ROI and competitive advantage over 3–5 year cycles; (2) GIS-enabled and cross-national market reach metrics as primary KPIs, not secondary correlates; (3) context-adapted AI deployment models for emerging-market settings; (4) systematic adverse-outcome monitoring protocols (privacy, algorithmic bias, stakeholder exclusion); (5) an integrated AI Marketing Performance Index (AMPI) encompassing all six outcome domains; and (6) multi-group analysis of industry and firm-size boundary conditions before scaling AI marketing investment. Recommendations for Researchers Priorities are (1) longitudinal panel designs that track competitive advantage over a 3-5 year period; (2) market reach as the primary dependent variable using GIS and cross-national instruments; (3) studies of the emerging market context with adapted measurement instruments; (4) negative outcome and failure-mode studies; (5) an integrated AI Marketing Performance Index; and (6) moderator studies using multi-group structural equation modelling. Impact on Society As AI marketing systems scale globally, their structural bias toward documenting best-case performance scenarios while ignoring adverse outcomes – privacy breaches, algorithmic bias, stakeholder exclusion – has direct societal consequences. The research agenda proposed here seeks to produce corrective evidence that supports equitable and transparent AI governance in marketing contexts. For the informing science and knowledge management community, these findings underscore the urgency of developing structured, multi-domain performance frameworks that can distinguish value creation from value extraction in AI-intensive environments. Future Research Six directions are proposed. Most urgent are studies of longitudinal competitive advantage, market reach as primary outcome, and systematic mapping of negative/paradoxical outcomes. Medium term priorities are integrated performance index and cross national emerging market studies. With the corpus going beyond 250 annual publications, computational text analysis and co-citation network analysis should be based on this bibliometric base.

Title: Robotic Surgery in Gynecology: Current Indications, Clinical Applications and Future Perspectives
Abstract: Robot-assisted surgery represents a significant advancement in minimally invasive gynecologic surgery and has become increasingly established in clinical practice over recent years. Technological innovations such as three-dimensional visualization, enhanced instrument dexterity and improved ergonomics enable more precise performance of complex surgical procedures. In benign gynecology, robotic surgery demonstrates particular advantages in challenging clinical scenarios, including advanced endometriosis, large uterine size and obesity. In gynecologic oncology, it is well established in the management of endometrial cancer, where minimally invasive approaches are associated with reduced perioperative morbidity while maintaining comparable oncological outcomes. The introduction of the sentinel lymph node concept has further contributed to reducing surgical morbidity. Despite these advantages, limitations remain, particularly with regard to costs, infrastructural requirements and the fact that evidence is still limited for certain indications. The successful implementation of a robotic program requires structured training, standardized workflows and close interdisciplinary collaboration. Future developments, especially the integration of artificial intelligence for intraoperative support, may further enhance robot-assisted surgery and strengthen its role in gynecologic practice.

Title: Comparing Clinical and Machine Learning Approaches for Cardiac Mortality Risk Prediction
Abstract: Current mortality risk for patients with heart failure relies on clinical scores such as Meta-Analysis Global Group in Chronic Heart Failure (MAGGIC), which do not incorporate cardiac monitoring data or machine learning. In this study, we examine the performance of machine learning models on clinical, electrocardiographic, and laboratory features for prediction of cardiac mortality due to sudden cardiac death or pump-failure death. We rely on a publicly available dataset collected from the MUerte Subita en Insuficiencia Cardiaca (MUSIC) study cohort, consisting of 992 heart failure patients with clinical data, chest X-rays, 20 -min high-resolution electrocardiograms (ECGs), and 24-hour Holter ECG monitoring. Five machine learning algorithms (XGBoost, CatBoost, Gradient Boosting, Random Forest, and Logistic Regression) were trained on 92 to 132 variables representing patient history, physical examination, laboratory testing, ECG parameters, and echocardiographic data, with class weighting explored across all models. Using 11 variables available in the dataset, we also calculated modified MAGGIC scores as a clinical baseline, producing an AUC score of 0.710. All machine learning models achieve an AUC score of at least 0.721, with class-weighted XGBoost demonstrating the highest AUC score of 0.777. The performance demonstrates risk prediction improvements from electrocardiographic and Holter monitoring data beyond traditional clinical variables. These findings support a complementary approach to clinical decision-making where traditional risk scoring and machine learning models enhance risk stratification for chronic heart failure patients.

Title: Time-Varying RIS-Aided MUSIC: A Snapshot-Enhanced System for High-Resolution DOA Estimation
Abstract: With the rapid rise of reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS), metasurface-enabled sensing and localization are becoming key enablers for next-generation wireless systems due to their ultra-large apertures, low-cost hardware, and programmable electromagnetic control. However, most existing metasurface-based localization methods rely on beam scanning or fingerprinting, leading to limited angular resolution and poor adaptability, while classical MIMO subspace methods (e.g., MUSIC) can achieve super-resolution but require relatively high SNR, are constrained in target resolvability by the number of RF channels, and incur high hardware/computational costs as channel count grows. To bridge this gap, we propose a spatiotemporally coded MUSIC approach that exploits time-varying RIS coding to synthesize a high-dimensional virtual array from a small number of RF chains, thereby improving resolvability and robustness without the cost burden of large-scale MIMO. We have implemented a prototype using a 1-bit phase-quantized RIS, and experimentally demonstrated its superior DOA estimation performance consistent with theoretical predictions. Experimental results demonstrate significant gains in angular resolution, and low-SNR robustness over existing metasurfacebased localization schemes and conventional MUSIC baselines. This approach delivers a cost-effective solution for high-quality Wireless sensing in low-altitude economy, integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) and embodied artificial intelligence.

Title: An Algorithm for Fault Feature Extraction and Identification in Electric Energy Metering Systems Based on Time–Frequency Analysis
Abstract: Accurate defect detection and diagnosis in electric energy metering (EEM) systems are critical for maintaining dependable electricity measurement and reducing financial losses in power utilities. Traditional fault detection systems frequently fail to detect transient anomalies and complex disruptions in metering signals, resulting in erroneous diagnoses and system inefficiencies. Furthermore, conventional approaches struggle with noise, non-stationary signals, and overlapping fault patterns, limiting their practical utility. The goal of this research is to develop a robust fault feature extraction and identification system for electric energy meters by combining advanced time–frequency (TF) analysis, machine learning (ML), and optimization techniques. Real and simulated metering signal datasets representing various fault types are used. Data preprocessing includes denoising with the wavelet transform, and signals are normalized using min–max normalization to enhance signal quality. TF feature extraction methods, such as short-time Fourier transform (STFT) and wavelet packet decomposition (WPD), are employed to capture both temporal and spectral characteristics of the signals. For classification, the tug war optimized extreme gradient refined random forest (TWO-EG2RF) model combines the strengths of random forest (RF) for feature robustness, extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) for learning complex patterns, and tug war optimization (TWO) to optimally tune model parameters, maximizing detection accuracy. The proposed TWO-EG2RF model is effective in the discrimination of the normal and faulty conditions and detection of the type of faults. Simulation results demonstrated superior performance, with an accuracy of 97.02%, an MAPE of 0.3512, an RMSE of 0.0092, and an MAE of 0.0085, confirming the capability of the proposed model to reliably identify and categorize faults in EEM and highlighting its effectiveness. The research suggests that integrating time–frequency analysis with optimal ML models yields a highly reliable solution for defect identification in EEM systems, allowing utilities to maintain measurement accuracy while reducing operational inefficiencies.

Title: The relationship between interdisciplinary learning motivation and learning burnout among university music majors in the context of AI-assisted music education: the mediating role of perceived learning load
Abstract: Introduction – University music majors increasingly encounter AI-related learning tasks while managing instrumental or vocal practice, ensemble rehearsals, theory coursework, performance assessment, and teaching preparation. This study examined the relationships among autonomous interdisciplinary motivation, pressure-driven interdisciplinary motivation, perceived learning load, and learning burnout in this combined learning context. Methods – Anonymous cross-sectional questionnaire data were collected from a convenience sample of 237 first- to third-year music majors at one university. The data were analyzed using reliability estimation, confirmatory factor analysis, Pearson correlation analysis, hierarchical regression, and Bootstrap testing with 5, 000 resamples. Results – Autonomous interdisciplinary motivation was associated with lower learning burnout, whereas pressure-driven interdisciplinary motivation was associated with higher learning burnout. Perceived learning load accounted for part of the association between pressure-driven interdisciplinary motivation and learning burnout, indicating a significant cross-sectional indirect effect through students' appraisal of time, energy, task density, and competence demands. Autonomous and pressure-driven interdisciplinary motivation was nearly independent in the sample. The four-factor measurement model also provided preliminary support for treating autonomous motivation, pressure-driven motivation, perceived learning load, and learning burnout as distinct constructs. Discussion – The findings suggest that the psychological consequences of AI-related learning among university music majors depend not only on exposure to AI tools but also on students' reasons for participation and their appraisal of the resulting learning demands. Supporting autonomous engagement and managing additional learning load may help reduce burnout in AI-assisted music education.

Title: Generative AI-Driven Engineering Deliverables for Cross-Functional Engineering Workflows
Abstract: With the rapidly evolving organization functioning, digital integration, and wide-ranging cross collaborations, it is imperative to have an efficient, and dedicated tool for expeditious generation of engineering deliverables such as documentation, and performance metrics of innovative products. Title: System Analysis of Remote Sensing Tools: Modeling, Optimization, and Synthesis
Abstract: Remote sensing technology refers to the collection of technical tools, methods, and methodologies used to acquire information about objects that are beyond the direct reach of a measuring instrument. Understanding these objects begins with the construction of various models, encompassing both the modeling of the object of study and the tools developed for its remote sensing. In the current landscape of remote sensing, modeling activities span several domains. These include assessing the performance of remote sensing satellites, simulating radiometric and spectral channels, modeling remote sensing system signals with atmospheric effects taken into account, and developing models of observed entities such as soil, oceans, and the atmosphere. Additionally, modeling extends to the application of artificial intelligence and computational methods for analyzing space imagery. Research in the field of remote sensing also involves optimizing both the models of the technical sensing instruments and the models of the observed objects and related processes. This article presents a methodology for the modeling, optimization, and synthesis of remote sensing systems. The proposed parametric optimization method is based on the following general principles: (1) identifying at least three subsets of key parameters within the system; (2) introducing a control function in the form of a mode relationship between two parameters from different subsets, followed by its optimization. As a practical example, the paper considers the procedure for determining the extreme operating mode of a LIDAR-based remote sensing system by calculating the optimal mode function for the parameter relationship. In principle, depending on the defined objective functional and control function, the proposed method allows for the identification of two extreme modes of operation: if the objective functional is maximized, the resulting mode is deemed optimal; if minimized, the mode is considered undesirable and should be avoided in the operation of the remote sensing system.

Title: Privacy-Preserving Bathroom Activity Recognition Using mmWave Radar and Machine Learning for Assistive Living
Abstract: Monitoring daily living activities is important for eldercare, assistive living, and health monitoring applications. Traditional monitoring systems often rely on cameras or wearable devices, which may raise privacy concerns or require active user participation. This study presents a privacy-preserving approach for recognizing common bathroom hygiene activities using a millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar sensor. The system uses the Texas Instruments AWR6843AOPEVM radar module mounted at the corner of a bathroom near the washbasin mirror area to capture motion patterns during activities such as hand washing, tooth brushing, and face washing. Radar data were collected from four participants with heights ranging from 5'4'' to 5'6''. The dataset consists of 154 radar recordings, including 54 face washing, 50 hand washing, and 50 tooth brushing recordings, each with a duration of 30 seconds. The recorded radar data were processed by decoding the TI mmWave TLV packets and extracting point-cloud information including spatial coordinates and velocity. From the decoded point clouds, a set of 36 statistical features describing spatial distribution, motion dynamics, temporal behavior, and signal quality were extracted for each recording. Several machine learning classifiers, including Random Forest, XGBoost, Support Vector Machine, and K-Nearest Neighbors, were evaluated using stratified 5-fold cross-validation. Experimental results show that the Random Forest classifier achieved the best performance with an accuracy of 98.71% and a weighted F1 score of 0.9869. The results demonstrate that mmWave radar point-cloud data combined with statistical feature extraction can effectively distinguish between bathroom hygiene activities. Because mmWave radar does not capture visual images, the proposed approach provides a privacy-friendly alternative to camera-based monitoring systems, making it particularly suitable for sensitive environments such as bathrooms. The proposed system shows strong potential for future applications in eldercare monitoring, assistive living, and smart home health monitoring systems.

Title: FEEL: AfNIRS–EEG Emotion Dataset and Benchmark Library
Abstract: We present FEEL, a multimodal EEG– fNIRS dataset and benchmark library for emotion recognition. Specifically, the FEEL dataset contains synchronized EEG and fNIRS recordings from 34 participants while they listened to 38 affective music clips, and it also provides rich annotations including discrete emotion labels, dimensional ratings, and liking scores. Based on this dataset, we systematically evaluate representative fusion strategies at the signal-level, feature-level, and decision-level, and we conduct these evaluations using both traditional machine learning methods and deep learning models under subject-dependent, cross-subject, and cross-music evaluation settings. The experimental results show that neurovascular coupling features derived from EEG and fNIRS achieve the highest classification accuracy in subject-dependent evaluations, whereas multimodal fusion approaches do not consistently outperform single-modal methods across all evaluation scenarios, and different fusion strategies exhibit distinct performance characteristics across evaluation scenarios. Finally, we integrate FEEL into the LibEER benchmark framework with extended support for fNIRS and EEG–fNIRS multimodal inputs, providing a standardized benchmark with baseline results for reproducible and systematic multimodal emotion recognition research.

Title: A Novel you Only Listen Once (YOLO) Machine Learning Platform for Automatic Detection and Characterization of Heart Sounds: Feasibility Study in Healthy Subjects
Abstract: Accurate detection of S1 and S2 heart sounds is critical for automated auscultation and downstream diagnosis. Most existing models require ECG synchronization or manual labels, which limit real-world deployment. In this study, we developed a fully automated supervised You Only Listen Once (YOLO) pipeline to classify heart sound events beat-by-beat using only PCG recordings from the publicly available CirCor DigiScope dataset. After bandpass filtering and normalization, 250 ms audio windows centered on annotated midpoints were extracted. Each segment was represented using a 70-dimensional feature vector combining cepstral, spectral, chroma, and wavelet features. We trained three supervised classifiers-Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and HistGradientBoosting-on a 60/20/20 split of the data. Model performance was evaluated and reported for standard metrics along with match rate for ground truth. HistGradientBoosting achieved the best performance with 0.81 accuracy, 0.88 AUC, and 0.98 match rate on the test set. These results suggest that high-quality beat-level annotation of PCG recordings can be achieved using efficient, interpretable models without the need for reference signals.

Title: Neuromorphic Speech Noise Suppression Using a Conductance-Based Spiking Autoencoder with STDP Learning
Abstract: This paper presents a Spiking Autoencoder Cortex Circuit (SACC) for speech denoising under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions. The proposed framework combines sparse spike-based encoding, adaptive threshold regulation, and a lightweight neural decoder within a compact neuromorphic architecture. Unlike conventional deep learning approaches that rely on stacked layers and dense activations, SACC emphasizes biologically inspired sparsity and homeostatic control to stabilize neural activity while preserving speech structure. Experimental evaluation across multiple speech segments demonstrates consistent SNR improvements of approximately 6 dB on average, with moderate variability across input conditions. Signal-level waveform comparisons and spectrogram analysis indicate that the model effectively suppresses broadband noise while maintaining dominant speech components. Neural mechanism analysis further shows stable population rate dynamics and adaptive threshold behavior, preventing excessive firing and supporting sparse representation. The objective of this work is not to claim state-of-the-art performance, but to explore a structured spiking design that links neural dynamics to measurable signal reconstruction gains. The results suggest that sparse cortical-inspired encoding combined with adaptive regulation can provide a viable foundation for energy-efficient speech denoising systems. Future work will extend evaluation to larger datasets and investigate deployment on neuromorphic hardware platforms.

Title: Opportunistic Osteoporosis Screening from Routine Knee Radiographs Using a Deep Learning–Based Texture-Branch Cross-Attention Network
Abstract: This study systematically investigates the impact of architectural components on deep learning–based osteoporosis screening using knee radiographs from a single-center archive. A total of 580 posteroanterior and lateral knee radiographs (normal: n = 389; osteoporosis: n = 191) were included. ImageNet-pretrained backbones (ResNet50V2, VGG16, and DenseNet121) were progressively extended with texture channel packages, dual-stream (global + texture) cross-attention fusion, ordinal-aware supervised contrastive loss, and input-conditioned learnable test-time augmentation (L-TTA). All models were evaluated by fivefold stratified cross-validation using the out-of-fold area under the ROC curve (OOF AUC). TBA-Net v1 achieved the highest performance (OOF AUC = 0.8727), exceeding the strongest baseline VGG16 (0.8497) by 0.0230 AUC and ResNet50V2 (0.8101) and DenseNet121 (0.8092) by 0.0626 and 0.0635 AUC. Ablation analysis demonstrated that the texture branch, cross-attention mechanism, and contrastive loss reduced performance when introduced sequentially, but produced a synergistic effect when jointly optimized; a Shapley decomposition showed that this gain arises from the interaction between components rather than from any component alone. L-TTA Net (OOF AUC = 0.8427) generated clinically interpretable attention patterns. At the current dataset scale, performance plateaued at approximately 0.87 OOF AUC, indicating that further improvements are constrained by sampling variability rather than architectural complexity. Architectural components in small medical imaging datasets should be evaluated within a holistic optimization framework rather than in isolation, and learnable test-time augmentation weights provide interpretability beyond predictive performance. The framework is positioned as a triage aid for prioritizing densitometry referral rather than as a substitute for it.

Title: A Deep Learning Detection Method for Power Operation Violations Based on Illumination Decoupling and Improved YOLO Under Complex Weather Conditions
Abstract: To address object detection degradation caused by strong reflections and backlighting in post-snow winter power operations, this paper proposes a safety detection method based on illumination decoupling and an improved YOLO network. First, the algorithm achieves illumination decoupling in the luminance channel via CIE LAB color space conversion and CLAHE, reducing glare and restoring shadow details. Second, the YOLO network is deeply reconstructed: a dense feature-weighted fusion neck network (Dense Neck) is designed to aggregate multi-scale features for weak target perception, and a Focal-EIOU loss function is introduced to resolve sample imbalance from illumination distortion. Finally, integrating spatio-temporal topological constraints with a temporal sliding window filter enables robust reasoning of continuous dynamic violations. Experimental results show that the model achieves a mean Average Precision (mAP@0.5) of over 97.8% under complex light pollution with excellent real-time edge-device performance.

Title: Capto: End-To-End Assurance for LLM Training and Inference in Datacenters
Abstract: Modern datacenters run LLM training and inference across multi-GPU clusters, where bottlenecks in application, compute, and network layers make it difficult to consistently meet SLEs such as response time, collective communication rate, and Job Completion Time. We present Capto, a SaaS-based framework for continuous end-to-end assurance of on-prem LLM workloads that treats these jobs as first-class distributed systems across application, GPU, and network tiers. Capto instruments ML frameworks, collective communication, and inference transfer libraries to collect fine-grained cross-layer telemetry, directly tying GPU-to-GPU communication and RDMA flows to SLE compliance instead of isolated metrics. By correlating application iteration times, KV-cache transfers, GPU health, and network congestion in a temporal dependency graph, Capto detects performance anomalies where they appear and localizes where they originate along the end-to-end path. Building on this, Capto combines statistical causality tests with LLM-driven reasoning to turn raw anomalies into ranked, actionable root-cause hypotheses that reduce time to mitigation for issues such as network congestion or GPU stress, enabling assured operation of datacenter-scale AI.

Title: Research on the Retrieval Method of 2-D Ocean Wave Spectra from Spaceborne SAR Based on Physical Feature Modulated U-Net
Abstract: Spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR), owing to its high resolution, wide coverage, and all-weather, all-Time observation capabilities, has become a core instrument for the dynamic monitoring of 2-D ocean wave spectra on a global scale, holding significant strategic importance for ocean dynamic research and navigation safety. However, due to the azimuth cutoff phenomenon caused by the velocity bunching effect, extracting complete ocean wave spectra from SAR image spectra is extremely difficult. To address the challenges posed by this nonlinear imaging mechanism, this article proposes a deep learning model modulated by physical features, named Wave-PMUNet. With U-Net as the backbone architecture, this model innovatively introduces the featurewise linear modulation mechanism to integrate key physical parameters, such as the azimuth cutoff wavelength, radar incidence angle, and normalized radar cross section, into the neural network. In this study, a dataset is constructed using 10 289 spatiotemporally collocated pairs of Sentinel-1 Wave Mode (WV) cross spectra and the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts fifth-generation reanalysis wave spectra. Experimental results demonstrate that without the need for a first-guess spectrum, the Wave-PMUNet model improves the retrieval accuracy and similarity index of the omnidirectional ocean wave spectra compared to the traditional generative adversarial network, as well as mainstream baseline and other representative deep learning models. Specifically, the spectral similarity index (Ω) reaches 0.29, and the root-mean-square error is 0.208 m for significant wave height, 0.618 s for mean wave period, 1.597 s for peak wave period, and is reduced to 31.299 for peak wave direction, indicating competitive overall performance in ocean wave spectra retrieval. This study not only demonstrates the potential of the Wave-PMUNet model in wave spectra retrieval but also indicates that the introduction of auxiliary physical features can enhance the neural network's ability to understand the complex SAR-wave imaging mechanism. It provides a potential technical reference for spaceborne SAR ocean wave spectrum retrieval, which may contribute to improving the accuracy of global marine meteorological forecasting.

Title: RAPID: Quantile-CFAR and Persistence-Confirmed Graph-Domain Sensor Fault Detection and Localization
Abstract: Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) are widely used in environmental monitoring, industrial supervision, and smart infrastructures, where neighboring sensors often observe spatially correlated physical fields. In such graph-structured sensing systems, bias, drift, and intermittent faults can destroy spatial consistency and contaminate downstream decisions. This paper presents RAPID, a graph-domain fault detection and localization framework for single-dominant sensor malfunctions. RAPID sequentially couples a specified polynomial graph high-pass filter, a historical residual, leave-one-out robust scale normalization, an empirical quantile-CFAR threshold, and persistence confirmation; localization then follows from the maximum residual component. Unlike graph-residual detectors with fixed calibration and graph-neural predictors that require offline training, RAPID is causal, training-free, and explicitly specifies its filter, buffer initialization, quantile convention, and decision rule. Under a locally fault-free, slowly varying, and weakly dependent reference window, the empirical quantile provides approximate candidate-level false-alarm control; a dedicated calibration experiment quantifies the finite-window deviation from the target and the additional reduction produced by persistence. Monte Carlo experiments with statistical, machine-learning, and graph-neural baselines further cover gradual and intermittent faults, graph-construction and weighting sensitivity, runtime and memory, topology mismatch, multi-fault stress, and semi-synthetic validation on public temperature measurements. The results show strong detection and localization performance with low confirmed false-alarm rates and modest online computational cost.

Title: Development and External Validation of an Explainable Machine Learning Model to Identify Positive Dysphagia Screening Results in People with Dementia: A Multicenter Cross-Sectional Study
Abstract: Objective: To develop and externally validate an interpretable machine learning model for identifying the likelihood of a positive Standardized Swallowing Assessment (SSA) result in people with dementia, particularly in settings where instrumental swallowing assessments are not readily available. Methods: Candidate variables included demographic, physical, oral-health, and mental health variables routinely available in clinical practice. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression was used for variable selection. Four machine learning models were developed and compared: logistic regression, support vector machines, random forest, and AdaBoost. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, calibration, and decision curve analysis. SHAP analysis was applied to enhance model interpretability. A web-based likelihood assessment tool was developed to estimate the individual probability of a concurrent positive SSA result. Results: All four models showed good discrimination. AdaBoost achieved an AUC of 0.918 in internal cross-validation and AUCs of 0.900 and 0.889 in the domain and temporal external validation cohorts, respectively, with sensitivities ranging from 0.879 to 0.901. Since sensitivity was prioritized for case finding, AdaBoost was selected for model interpretation and online-tool development. SHAP analysis ranked body mass index as the leading contributor to the AdaBoost output, followed by number of teeth, eating ability, dietary type, and Clinical Dementia Rating score. Conclusion: The model showed good performance for identifying people likely to have a concurrent positive SSA screening result. The web-based tool may support case finding and referral for further swallowing assessment, but it should not be used as a standalone diagnostic or prognostic instrument. Prospective and geographically diverse validation is required before routine clinical implementation.

Title: Empirical mode decomposition based CNN prediction model for speech emotion classification using Mel scale spectrograms
Abstract: Studies on emotion recognition systems from speech signal are comprehensively assessed in the purview of developing Human-Computer Interface (HCI) models. Traditionally, HCI models offer significant contribution into the psychological states of individuals, serving as crucial psychic response for HCI applications. Majority of the existing works in literature concentrate on classifying emotional states with several spectral and Cepstrum features using ANN and RNN based classification for various data sets. Despite that, the results are found to be comparatively low for RAVDESS dataset. Furthermore, only limited studies focus on using 3D time frequency images for predicting Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) models. In light of these aspects, the proposed work aims at recognizing the speech emotion with seven different states using deep neural net with Empirical mode decomposition (EMD).In the initial phase, the raw speech signals are decomposed into 5 different Intrinsic Mode Functions (IMFs) and are analysed in time, frequency and energy. Subsequently, all the five oscillatory modes are transformed into linear scale and Mel scale spectrograms using short time frequency transform and auditory filter banks. These spectrograms are fed as input to three different pre-trained models namely AlexNet, GoogLeNet and ResNet-50 and evaluated for all IMFs both in linear and Mel Scale. Ablation studies are also carried out with controlled baselines viz. Mel/ Linear scale spectrograms without EMD and classical Machine Learning classifiers for fair comparison. The experimental results record an improved performance in accuracy for IMF1 + Mel scale spectrograms + ResNet-50 classifier with 76.38% and linear scale of 74.25%. Additionally, 5- fold cross validation analysis is also carried out for generalizing the model and the results are reported. In comparison to the other approaches used in literature for categorizing RAVDESS dataset, the proposed method found to yield better results.

Title: Machine learning-based solar radiation prediction across heterogeneous climatic zones using NASA POWER data: a case study in Nigeria
Abstract: Accurate prediction of solar radiation is essential for renewable energy planning, climate analysis, and agricultural productivity. Solar radiation data are required for the evaluation of solar power generation potential and crop water requirement computation, which is almost unavailable due to insufficient instrument for its measurement in many locations of the developing nations. Studies that applied several kernels of the Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) for the prediction of solar radiation are scarce. This study evaluates the performance of several machine learning models for solar radiation prediction across three climatic regions in Nigeria: Kano, Ibadan, and Onne. These locations represent distinct ecological zones ranging from the semi-arid savanna in northern Nigeria to the humid coastal rainforest in the southern region. Meteorological data used in this study were obtained from the NASA (National Aeronautics and Space Administration) POWER. Two machine learning approaches—Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) and Support Vector Machine (SVM)—were applied using different kernel configurations to predict solar radiation. Model performance was evaluated using standard statistical error metrics including Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), Mean Squared Error (MSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Normalized Root Mean Square Error (NRMSE), and the coefficient of determination (R<sup>2</sup>). The results show that Gaussian Process Regression models generally produced the most accurate predictions across the study locations. In particular, the Exponential GPR model demonstrated the best performance in the humid regions of Ibadan and Onne, with RMSE values of 1.46 and 1.36 MJ.m<sup>2</sup>.d<sup>−1</sup>, respectively. Conversely, the Fine SVM model achieved the best prediction accuracy in Kano, recording the lowest RMSE value of 2.16 MJ.m<sup>2</sup>. d<sup>−1</sup>. These differences are attributed to variations in regional climatic conditions, where the relatively stable atmospheric conditions in the dry northern region favor SVM models, while the complex and highly variable atmospheric processes in humid regions are better captured by probabilistic models such as GPR. Overall, the findings highlight the importance of selecting appropriate machine learning models based on climatic characteristics when predicting solar radiation. The results provide useful insights for improving solar energy resource assessment and environmental modeling in Nigeria and similar tropical regions.

Title: Application of the Unsupervised Machine Learning in the Color Quality Control and Grading for Polymers
Abstract: The color quality control of general-purpose polystyrene productions is assessed by visual inspection currently in industry. In order to overcome the limitations of this method and find a more scientific and robust way to classify the color grades of plastic samples, a new approach is explored. We first discuss several unsupervised machine learning clustering algorithms and analyze their advantages and drawbacks. The major color measurement methods are also evaluated. A device is proposed to measure the color temperature and illuminance of plastic samples. These measured color characteristics have the ability to recognize the subtle difference in color, overcoming the limitations of existing color measurement instruments. Based on these measured quantities, six unsupervised clustering algorithms are applied to verify the performance of clustering including K-Means, Spectral clustering, Agglomerative clustering, BIRCH, Bisecting K-Means, and Gaussian mixtures model. Five different metrics are used to evaluate clustering results. The obtained clustering regions basically match well with the reference labels. The results demonstrate that unsupervised clustering can effectively support color quality control and grading in plastic manufacturing.

Title: A Dynamic Sensitivity Assessment Continual Learning Framework for Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Bearing
Abstract: In the practical industry, constructing a comprehensive training dataset for bearing degradation data is exceptionally challenging due to prolonged collection cycles and diverse degradation modes, which hinders the engineering implementation of deep learning-based remaining useful life (RUL) prediction methods. To address the aforementioned limitations, this article establishes a novel continual learning framework named dynamic sensitivity assessment continual learning framework (DSACL) for RUL prediction, with core innovations including omni-dimensional dynamic convolution (ODConv) and sensitivity assessment. The ODConv strengthens multi-scale feature extraction capabilities through a multi-dimensional attention mechanism, while sensitivity assessment prevents alterations to importance weights through assessing the sensitivity of output functions to parameter variations. Meanwhile, a novel RUL prediction neural network model based on ODConv is constructed for the neural network model of DSACL. Experimental validation on the XJTU-SY dataset demonstrates that DSACL surpasses state-of-the-art methods in prediction performance. Moreover, the introduction of a forgetting mechanism achieves an effective balance between model capacity and prediction accuracy.

Title: EMBC Special Issue: PhyNet: A Physiology-Constrained Monotonic Neural Network for Safe and Explainable Blood Glucose Forecasting
Abstract: Objective: Deep learning (DL) has become state-of-the-art for blood glucose (BG) forecasting in type 1 diabetes (T1D). However, its black-box nature raises safety and reliability concerns regarding its use for therapeutic decision-support. This study aims to: (1) highlight potential risks associated with standard DL-based BG forecasting, and (2) address them with PhyNet, a physiology-constrained monotonic neural network. Methods: Two large-scale datasets (T1DEXI and MetaboNet, 848 subjects in total) were used to develop PhyNet-which enforces physiological consistency through a multi-branch structure and weight constraints-and compare it against six DL baselines (convolutional, recurrent, and transformer-based architectures). Models predicted BG levels up to 90-minute ahead using continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) data, carbohydrate intake, and insulin dosing, and were assessed for: (i) predictive accuracy with standard metrics, and (ii) adherence to physiological principles (i.e., carbohydrates increase BG, insulin lowers it) using explainable AI. Specifically, we evaluated model-predicted responses to varying carbohydrate and insulin intakes, and generated counterfactual explanations to identify model-recommended actions for avoiding adverse events. Results: At a 30-minute horizon, predictive accuracy was similar across models (RMSE: 19.39-21.00 mg/dL; Time Gain: 10.45-13.35 min). Despite this, only PhyNet consistently captured the physiological effects of carbohydrates and insulin, yielding 0% unsafe recommendations versus up to 64.3% for baselines. Conclusion: Standard DL models can achieve state-of-the-art performance while failing to respect physiology, posing clinical risk. PhyNet preserves accuracy while enhancing physiological fidelity, supporting safer integration into T1D technologies. Significance: Evaluating physiological consistency alongside predictive accuracy is essential for responsible clinical translation of DL-based BG forecasting.

Title: Investment Risk Management in Stock Markets: An AI-Based Approach
Abstract: This contribution investigates issues of investment risk management in stock exchanges and innovative methods of their management, supplemented by artificial intelligence (AI)․ The focus of the study is on quantitative metrics for measuring investment risk, including potential losses under extreme market conditions, the variability of returns, and downside exposure, as well as other statistical indicators that provide insight into portfolio performance and stability. The methodology for the strategic management of investment risks encompasses diversification, hedging, portfolio analysis techniques, and the utilization of derivative financial instruments. It is suggested to incorporate these techniques with scenario simulation and stress testing for the purpose to analyze and evaluate high-impact situational and short-term processes that can have a substantial impact on financial markets. The proposed investment management strategy is based on automation integrating artificial intelligence tools. This approach is flexible and adaptable to investors’ resources, strategic goals, and different financial market situations, making it unique. This strategy optimizes and disciplines investment portfolios by considering risk-return ratios and managing systemic and non-systemic risks. In addition, the approach contributes to the structural formation of the investment decision-making process and reduces the influence of subjective factors. This facilitates the continuous monitoring of risks and the timely adjustment of the portfolio structure in response to evolving market conditions. The proposed approach to investment management on stock exchanges can be useful for further scientific research in this area, as well as for specialists working in financial markets.

Title: Machine learning algorithms to predict digital skills in university teaching staff.
Abstract: Background: The digital transformation of higher education has intensified the need to assess and enhance the digital competencies of university faculty. This study analyzed the effectiveness of various machine learning algorithms in predicting levels of faculty digital competence based on socio-educational variables. The objective was to develop an advanced predictive model, applied to faculty members from the State University of Milagro and the Technical University of Manabí. Methods: A quantitative approach was adopted, with a cross-sectional correlational design. Digital competencies were measured using the internationally validated DigCompEdu Check-In instrument, structured across six core dimensions. In the predictive phase, nine supervised machine learning algorithms were trained and evaluated: logistic regression, decision trees, random forest, gradient boosting, k-nearest neighbors, support vector machines, stochastic gradient descent, artificial neural networks, and Naive Bayes. The models were trained using a dataset comprising 5,148 observations, and their performance was assessed using standard classification metrics: area under the ROC curve (AUC), accuracy, F1-score, sensitivity, and Matthew’s correlation coefficient (MCC). Results: Gradient boosting, random forest, and neural network models demonstrated superior predictive performance, particularly at advanced competence levels (B2 and C1). Significant associations were identified between academic level, age, gender, and digital competencies. Logistic regression and Naive Bayes showed limitations in identifying low competence levels (A1), while intermediate levels were often overestimated across several models. Conclusions: The findings confirm that machine learning algorithms can accurately predict university faculty digital competencies. Advanced models outperformed traditional ones, especially at higher competence levels. It is recommended to incorporate contextual variables and validate the models in diverse educational settings.

Title: A Sentinel-3 Foundation Model for Ocean Color
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) foundation models (FMs), pretrained on massive unlabelled datasets, have the potential to drastically change AI applications in ocean science, where labeled data are often sparse and expensive to collect. In this work, we describe a new FM using the Prithvi-EO vision Transformer (ViT) architecture, which has been pretrained to reconstruct data from the Sentinel-3 Ocean and Land Colour Instrument (OLCI). We evaluate the model by fine-tuning on two downstream marine Earth observation tasks. We first assess model performance compared to current baseline models used to quantify chlorophyll concentration. We then evaluate the FM's ability to refine remote sensing-based estimates of ocean primary production. Our results demonstrate the utility of self-trained FMs for marine monitoring, in particular for making use of small amounts of high-quality labeled data and in capturing detailed spatial patterns of ocean color whilst matching point observations. We conclude that this new generation of geospatial AI models has the potential to provide more robust, data-driven insights into ocean ecosystems and their role in global climate processes.

Title: Performance-based frailty tools capture distinct risk phenotypes in kidney transplant candidates: A comparative analysis of the FRAIL scale and short physical performance battery
Abstract: Frailty predicts adverse outcomes in kidney transplant candidates, but it remains unclear whether different frailty tools identify the same or distinct at-risk patients. In this retrospective cohort study, 953 kidney transplant candidates listed between 2018 and 2022 underwent frailty assessment using both the Fatigue, Resistance, Ambulation, Illnesses, Weight Loss (FRAIL) scale screening and the Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB) screening test. In a subset with available computed tomography scan imaging, body composition was analyzed using artificial intelligence-based tools. Frailty prevalence differed by instrument: 6.2% using the FRAIL scale screening vs 24% using the SPPB screening test. Waitlist mortality occurred in 9.5% (91/953) of candidates. Both tools independently predicted waitlist mortality (FRAIL scale screening test: adjusted hazard ratio, 2.38; 95% CI, 1.34-4.20; P = .003 and SPPB screening test: adjusted hazard ratio, 1.66; 95% CI, 1.07-2.60; P = .025). The SPPB screening test-defined frailty showed stronger associations with posttransplant outcomes, including longer hospital stays and 30-day and 1-year readmissions. A computed tomography scan analysis revealed that SPPB screening test-defined, but not FRAIL scale screening test-defined, frailty was associated with lower muscle density and increased visceral adiposity, suggesting a mechanistic basis. The FRAIL scale screening test and SPPB screening test captured distinct dimensions of frailty with complementary strengths. The FRAIL scale screening test better reflected symptom burden and candidates at risk for waitlist mortality, whereas the SPPB screening test was more closely associated with posttransplant complications. Results support systematic use of both instruments to optimize risk stratification and identify candidates who may benefit from targeted prehabilitation.

Title: Automated assessment of the nature of scientific inquiry (NOSI) using machine learning and transformer-based language models
Abstract: Background: Effective assessment of the nature of scientific inquiry is foundational to scientific literacy but is constrained by the resource-intensive, manual scoring of open-ended instruments such as the Views About Scientific Inquiry. Purpose: We addressed this challenge by developing and validating a comparative machine learning framework to automate and standardise the evaluation of Views About Scientific Inquiry responses responses from 503 Turkish pre-service teachers. Design/Methodology: We employed a feature-based Random Forest regression model and a deep contextual transformer-based BERTurk classification model using 5-fold cross-validation. Results: The Random Forest model established a reliable and stable methodological baseline, demonstrating strong predictive alignment with expert scores and minimal variability across repeated validation runs. Conversely, the BERTurk model, despite showing high initial potential, experienced a severe, non-reproducible collapse in performance during systematic stability tests. Conclusions: This outcome highlighted significant operational fragility under conditions constrained by limited data and a morphologically complex language. This comparative analysis reveals a critical methodological tension in educational artificial intelligence: model stability and interpretability must take precedence over peak performance for responsible application. The Random Forest framework offers a transparent, scalable solution for the automated, highly consistent assessment of the nature of scientific inquiry and serves as a diagnostic tool for identifying specific linguistic and conceptual difficulties in scientific reasoning.

Title: Integrating MR dynamic radiomics and clinical parameters for machine learning-based prediction of short-term response to induction chemotherapy in nasopharyngeal carcinoma
Abstract: Background and purpose – Accurate prediction of short-term response to induction chemotherapy (ICT) in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) remains a critical unmet clinical need. We aimed to construct a multimodal, interpretable machine learning (ML) framework integrating MR dynamic radiomics (delta radiomics) with clinical parameters to predict ICT response. Methods – A multicenter retrospective study enrolled 216 pathologically confirmed NPC patients from two institutions (Xiangyang No. 1 People’s Hospital and Xiangyang Central Hospital, January 2015–September 2024; training cohort n=151, test cohort n=65) and an independent external validation cohort of 87 patients (Affiliated Hospital of Hubei University of Chinese Medicine, February 2017–June 2024). A Delta Radscore was computed from 2, 637 candidate features extracted from paired pre- and arterial-phase post-contrast enhanced T1-weighted imaging (CE-T1WI) MRI, quantifying intratumoral microvascular dynamics. After two-stage feature selection (intraclass correlation coefficient [ICC] ≥0.80 stability screening followed by least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO)–random forest ensemble), eight ML algorithms—XGBoost, CatBoost, support vector machine (SVM), k-nearest neighbors (KNN), and Logistic Regression, etc—were systematically evaluated. SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analysis provided model interpretability. Independent clinical predictors were identified via uni- and multivariable logistic regression and integrated into a dynamic nomogram. Results – Multivariable logistic regression identified five independent predictors: T stage (OR = 4.29, 95% CI: 1.43–12.82, P = 0.009), lymphocyte count (OR = 2.08, 95% CI: 1.07–4.05, P = 0.031), lactate dehydrogenase (LDH; OR = 1.02, 95% CI: 1.01–1.03, P<0.001), Dynamic Rad_Score (OR = 0.65, 95% CI: 0.57–0.76, P<0.001), and Music Therapy and Psychological Counseling score (MTPC; OR = 0.33, 95% CI: 0.16–0.68, P = 0.026). XGBoost achieved the best performance across all cohorts: training AUC = 0.962 (95% CI: 0.937–0.998), test AUC = 0.861 (95% CI: 0.767–0.954), and external validation AUC = 0.926; significantly outperforming logistic regression (DeLong P<0.05). The nomogram C-index was 0.876, with a calibration Brier score of 0.082. SHAP analysis ranked Dynamic Rad_Score (mean |SHAP|=0.219), MTPC (0.199), LDH (0.177), and T stage (0.156) as the four most impactful predictors. Decision curve analysis confirmed net clinical benefit of XGBoost across threshold probabilities of 20%–85%. Conclusion – An XGBoost-based multimodal interpretable model integrating MR dynamic radiomics with clinical parameters effectively predicts short-term ICT response in NPC, providing a quantifiable, explainable decision-support tool to guide individualized treatment strategies.
