Title: Enhancing Geostationary Supercooled Water Cloud Identification Using Hyperspectral Infrared Sounder Measurements
Abstract: Supercooled water clouds (SWCs) play an important role in cloud radiative effects, precipitation processes, and aviation safety. Accurate SWC discrimination from passive geostationary observations remains difficult because SWCs are liquid clouds under subfreezing conditions and are influenced by atmospheric background conditions. Although reanalysis products such as ERA5 can provide useful atmospheric background fields, their latency limits near-real-time monitoring. To address this issue, this study investigates whether same-platform hyperspectral infrared observations from FY-4B/geostationary interferometric infrared sounder (GIIRS) can provide effective atmospheric-state constraints for SWC identification without relying on reanalysis inputs. A deep-learning framework, termed graph-based spectral ensemble network (GSE-Net), is developed by combining FY-4B/advanced geostationary radiation imager (AGRI) and GIIRS hyperspectral infrared observations for SWC identification. Within GSE-Net, spectral graph compressor (SGC) refines and compresses GIIRS spectra, while Bi-FiLM bidirectionally modulates spectral and AGRI scene features before fusion. Using CALIPSO as the reference, the proposed framework achieves a mean SWC F1 score of 89.33%, improving upon AGRI-only retrievals by 10.41 percentage points and outperforming AGRI+ERA5. In addition, the SGC further improves SWC identification performance over directly using uncompressed GIIRS observations. The results demonstrate that geostationary hyperspectral infrared observations can provide useful atmospheric-state constraints for SWC identification and serve as a practical alternative for near-real-time applications.

Title: Intelligent Identification of Ocean Surface Rainfall from CFOSAT Scatterometer Observations
Abstract: The China-France Oceanography Satellite scatterometer (CSCAT) provides up to 16 multiangular normalized radar cross-section (NRCS) slices, which serve as rich information sources for high-quality ocean surface wind retrieval. However, rainfall can alter backscattering characteristics and consequently degrade the accuracy of wind retrieval. Therefore, accurate rainfall identification is of critical importance. In this study, various machine learning models integrated with different intelligent optimization algorithms are developed for CSCAT rainfall identification. Through systematic comparative evaluation, the optimal models are identified. Furthermore, the impacts of the number of valid NRCS slices, observational position within the swath, and polarization on the performance of the optimal models are investigated. In addition, the effects of classification probability threshold, rain-rate threshold, and CSCAT measurement instability on performance are discussed to support practical applicability. The results demonstrate that the eXtreme Gradient Boosting model optimized by Ant Colony Optimization (ACO-XGB) and the light gradient boosting machine model optimized by particle swarm optimization (PSO-LGBM) achieve better performance among all candidate models. Specifically, ACO-XGB exhibits superior discriminative capability (AUC = 0.9382) and a lower false positive rate (FPR = 0.0368), whereas PSO-LGBM shows better performance in reducing the false negative rate (FNR = 0.1973). By fully exploiting the multiangular and dual-polarization observations of CSCAT, the proposed models achieve effective rainfall identification and maintain robust performance under varying observational conditions, rendering them suitable for operational applications.

Title: A Ku-Band Photonic-Based Cloud and Precipitation Radar
Abstract: Emerging radio frequency (RF) photonic technology enables tunable, ultrawideband, and low-phase-noise RF signal generation and downconversion with reduced instrument size, weight, and power (SWaP). To demonstrate its application in atmospheric remote sensing, a prototype RF-photonic-based Ku-band (13.9 GHz) cloud and precipitation radar was developed. This letter describes the system architecture, hardware implementation, and performance evaluation of the radar, and presents measurement results from observations of a thunderstorm system.

Title: Resource-Aware Closed-Loop Multiextended Target Tracking Method in MIMO Radar via Deep Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: Multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar, as an advanced measurement instrument, has received extensive attention for its ability to form multiple beams and achieve high-precision multitarget tracking. As the resolution of MIMO radar improves along with the advancement of measurement science, it has become feasible to accurately measure and estimate extended targets occupying multiple resolution cells, including their shape, size, and orientation. However, radar resource allocation is the key factor in determining the measurement performance of MIMO radar. Therefore, this article proposes a cognitive MIMO radar measurement method based on adaptive resources, aiming to acquire high-information measurements and optimize state estimation of dynamic multiextended target tracking (METT) under resource constraints. The core of the method consists of a cognitive control framework in an actor-critic (AC) variant of deep reinforcement learning (DRL), called the twin delayed deep deterministic (TD3) policy gradient. The aim is to adapt the transmitting power of each MIMO radar beam according to the feedback information of the tracking recursion period, thereby reducing measurement uncertainty. To that end, the posterior Cramér-Rao lower bound (PCRLB) characterizes the theoretical minimum variance of unbiased estimators, representing the minimum uncertainty achievable by the measurement system. The PCRLB of the extended target, conditioned on actually achieved measurements, is derived and utilized to design the reward function that guides the DRL agent to learn a strategy aimed at maximizing measurement quality. The resulting optimal strategy enhances estimation accuracy for extended target multifeature information. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed method is superior to other benchmark methods in improving the performance of worst case target tracking.

Title: AI-driven passenger experience monitoring in railway operations: a Reddit-based NLP analysis of service failures, sentiment and operational priorities
Abstract: Purpose – This study develops an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven framework for using passenger-generated social media discourse as a complementary source of operational intelligence in railway service quality management. It examines whether Reddit discussions can reveal dimensions of passenger experience that are not adequately captured by official performance indicators. Design/methodology/approach – Using the official Reddit API, the study collected 61, 328 documents published between July 2024 and July 2026 across five railway communities. The framework combines lexicon-based classification into seven theory-informed service failure categories with non-negative matrix factorization topic modelling, VADER sentiment analysis, lexicon-based emotion detection and robust regression. Findings – Delay-and-disruption discourse showed the highest proportion of negative documents, while safety discourse generated the greatest negativity intensity and visibility; comfort and cleanliness and ticketing and refunds were the most frequently discussed dimensions. Affective intensity and public engagement proved partially independent: delay and ticketing posts attracted significantly less engagement than average, safety, comfort posts significantly more. The index ranked comfort, cleanliness, staff, communication, ticketing and refunds as leading improvement priorities, with ticketing, delay dominating British, comfort dominating US discourse. Research limitations/implications – Findings rest on self-selected Reddit communities and rule-based instruments validated internally rather than against human gold labels; they indicate digitally expressed passenger concerns, not representative estimates of the passenger population. Practical implications – Operators and regulators can use the framework as a low-cost, continuously updated instrument complementing official performance indicators. Its extension into an early-warning system is set out as a design proposition requiring prospective validation against operational incident data, not as a capability demonstrated here. Social implications – This study highlights social media as a democratic space for public accountability in transit management. By amplifying organic passenger discourse, the framework empowers commuters whos daily lived experiences, such as comfort, cleanliness and communication issues, are often overlooked by rigid official KPIs. Recognizing these grievances underscores how transit quality directly impacts public trust, equity and socio-economic well-being. Furthermore, addressing regional variations in passenger concerns helps operators design more inclusive services. Ultimately, integrating this digital feedback into policy ensures that vital public infrastructure better aligns with the diverse safety, accessibility and comfort needs of the communities it serves. Originality/value – The study demonstrates how large-scale passenger discourse can be transformed into actionable railway service intelligence by integrating theory-informed classification, affective analysis, engagement modelling and a multidimensional operational priority measure.

Title: Reframing AI Music Today
Abstract: Debates on AI-generated music often treat recent systems as an unprecedented break, reviving anxieties about authorship, labour, and originality. This article offers a different perspective. Contemporary generative tools are understood here as the latest configuration in a long history of redistributing musical work across humans, devices, and formal procedures. Rather than presenting a comprehensive timeline, this article develops a genealogy through selected scenes, including musical automata, combinatorial paper algorithms, early rule-based computer composition, and machine learning. These cases are used to track how musical intelligence and creative agency have been repeatedly relocated, moving from mechanical performance to rule-following and from symbolic representations to statistical learning. This article argues that the distinctive shift introduced by prompt-driven systems lies less in claims of autonomous machine creativity than in the interface as a site of composition. Music-making becomes an iterative practice of specification, selection, and revision shaped by negotiation and curation under platform conditions. By treating AI music as a socio-technical reorganization of practice, this article contributes to the history of computing by using music as a case through which to examine changing relations among formalization, representation, interface, and human-machine collaboration.

Title: Prediction tools to prioritise hospitalised adult patients at risk of drug related problems: An umbrella review
Abstract: Risk prediction tools assist pharmacists to identify and prioritise hospitalised patients at risk of drug-related problems (DRPs) requiring clinical review. This umbrella review identifies existing risk prediction tools, summarises their performance, and highlights factors important for prioritising hospitalised adults at risk of DRPs for clinical review. A systematic search of three bibliographic databases from January 2010 to March 2024, identified systematic reviews that qualitatively or quantitatively examined patient- and/or medication-related factors in risk prediction or prioritisation models or tools for adult inpatients at risk of DRPs. Extracted data included citation, review type, number and date range of primary studies, population, setting, outcomes, and key risk factors. Risk prediction tools were summarised by country, sample size, performance metrics (discrimination, sensitivity, calibration), number of risk factors, and external validation. All extracted data was checked by a second reviewer. The standardized Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal instruments were used to assess the quality of eligible studies. Twenty systematic reviews met our inclusion criteria, of which 18 were of sufficient quality for synthesis. Selected articles covered 171 unique primary studies and 32 risk prediction tools, of which 12 demonstrated acceptable or good discrimination of which four also had good calibration. Two tools showed the highest potential for future clinical use based on their performance metrics and external validation data but would benefit from further validation in diverse populations. Commonly reported risk factors for DRPs were psycholeptic medications (reported in 13 systematic reviews), age, comorbidities and reduced renal function (n = 12 reviews). Based on the reviews included, no tools appear to be yet suitable for routine clinical practice due to limited external validation, calibration and unclear risk factor definitions; however, some show promise for further development and testing. Data on existing risk prediction tools and risk factors provides a foundation for refining or automating current models, for instance via machine learning approaches that can iteratively incorporate risk factors to ease use and improve prediction of DRPs within specific clinical settings.

Title: Cross-Instrument Calibration Transfer in LIBS Using Hybrid Spectral Harmonization and Deep Spectral Migration
Abstract: Laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) is a powerful analytical technique widely used for rapid elemental analysis and material classification due to its minimal sample preparation and near-real-time detection capability. Despite the increasing availability of LIBS spectral libraries, their effective reuse across different instruments remains challenging because of instrumental variability. Existing calibration transfer methods fail to capture nonlinear spectral discrepancies between instruments. To address these limitations, this study proposes a framework termed Hybrid Spectral Harmonization and Deep Spectral Migration (HSH-DSM) for cross-instrument spectral transfer in LIBS. The proposed approach integrates physically motivated spectral preprocessing with data-driven deep learning to reduce cross-instrument discrepancies. Then, a local intensity harmonization strategy is applied to correct local spectral response differences. Finally, a deep spectral migration model based on a tunable multilayer perceptron (MLP) is trained to learn the nonlinear mapping between a source domain and a target domain. Experimental results demonstrate strong spectral reconstruction performance. The model achieves coefficients of determination (R<sup>2</sup>) of 0.999 for calibration, 0.990 for validation, and 0.983 for independent test data, indicating accurate cross-instrument spectral translation. To further evaluate the practical effectiveness of the framework, the performance evaluation on unseen target-domain samples yields 97.8% precision, 97.5% recall, and 97.5% F1-score, demonstrating promising classification capability. These results confirm that the proposed HSH-DSM framework effectively mitigates cross-instrument spectral discrepancies while preserving discriminative spectral features. The proposed strategy provides a promising approach toward instrument-independent LIBS spectral libraries and facilitates reliable deployment of LIBS-based analytical models across heterogeneous instruments.

Title: Developing validity arguments for artificial intelligence-based assessment: Balancing affordances and threats
Abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used to generate, score and interpret educational assessment, yet these applications are being adopted in a largely unregulated environment. This creates a paradox: Whereas AI systems used in clinical care are subject to formal scrutiny for safety, performance and monitoring, AI systems used to inform consequential decisions about learner progression and future clinical practice are not. Existing validity frameworks remain useful but may not fully account for AI-specific threats. Methods: We conducted a state-of-the-science conceptual review examining validity for AI-based assessment through Kane's four inferences: scoring, generalisation, extrapolation and implications. We integrated conceptual and empirical literature from medical education and adjacent AI evaluation fields to identify major threats, evidence needs and practical implications for defensible AI-based assessment use. Results: AI introduces distinct validity threats across the inferential chain. For scoring, key risks include construct contamination, prompt instability and limited explainability. For generalisation, domain shift, rater culture differences and temporal drift threaten reproducibility across settings and time. For extrapolation, AI may alter the construct being assessed, making explicit construct definition essential to defensible interpretation. For implications, risks include subgroup inequities, automation bias, deskilling, weak accountability and erosion of academic integrity. Across these inferences, we identified seven cross-cutting mechanisms that can operate as either threats or affordances depending on design and governance. Conclusions: Validity for AI-based assessment should be approached as ongoing governance of a sociotechnical system rather than one-time validation of a static instrument or assessment process. Defensible adoption requires explicit validity arguments, auditability, multi-site evaluation and continuous consequence monitoring that is aware of the specific AI affordances and threats.

Title: Development of an Online Visibility Prediction System for Highways Based on RK3588
Abstract: Under conditions of low visibility on highways, achieving reliable real-time visibility prediction is of great significance for ensuring driving safety. Therefore, this paper designs a distributed online prediction system based on an embedded platform. This system uses the RK3588 as the core processor to complete data interaction and model prediction functions; it is equipped with high-performance visibility meters and six-element meteorological sensors to perceive the meteorological information of the surrounding environment from multiple angles; it adopts LoRa wireless communication technology to achieve interaction between visibility data and remote terminals. A dual-branch deep learning architecture visibility prediction algorithm is designed, which processes the visibility time series and multi-source meteorological data separately; finally, the trained model is transplanted to the RK3588 platform, and the NPU is accelerated for inference through the RKNN C API, and the rolling time window mechanism is used to support continuous rolling prediction. The prediction results of this system are in good agreement with the actual visibility change trend, with an RMSE of 0.086, an MAE of 0.047, and an MAPE of 0.119; in terms of performance, the average inference delay per single query is controlled within 12 ms, the CPU usage is stable below 20%, and the memory overhead does not exceed 100 MB, fully meeting the dual requirements of low latency and lightweight resources for online prediction in the edge computing environment.

Title: Poster: A Lightweight Acoustic Anomaly Detection Framework for Industrial IoT Edge Monitoring
Abstract: Acoustic sensing provides a practical way to monitor machinery in industrial IoT applications. However, acoustic anomaly detection (AAD) in real-world deployment still faces challenges from noise interference, domain shifts, and limited computing resources on edge devices. This paper presents a lightweight AAD framework for industrial IoT edge monitoring. First, a local time-frequency weighted representation module is designed to capture local temporal variations and emphasize informative frequency components from Mel spectrograms. Then, a lightweight ensemble learning module is proposed to progressively refine the decision results with multiple machine learning classifiers. Experiments on the DCASE 2022 Task 2 benchmark and a real-world power transformer dataset show that the proposed framework achieves competitive detection performance with low computational cost, indicating its potential for resource-constrained industrial edge monitoring.

Title: From Sound to Species: A Modular Acoustic Sensor for Biodiversity Monitoring
Abstract: Passive Acoustic Monitoring (PAM) is widely used for biodiversity assessment and environmental monitoring of wildlife and soundscapes. Long-term field deployments require sensing platforms that are compact, low-power, robust, and cost-efficient while remaining flexible for future extensions.This work presents a modular embedded acoustic sensing platform for autonomous environmental audio recording. The system separates power management, processing and data logging, and audio acquisition into dedicated subsystems connected through standardized interfaces. Audio is acquired via I<sup>2</sup> S with DMAbased buffering and periodically stored on an SD card using burst-based writing to improve energy efficiency.Evaluation includes power measurements across sampling rates from 8 kHz to 192 kHz, field deployment with automated bioacoustic analysis, and a comparison with established PAM devices. Results show that storage operations dominate energy consumption, and that duty cycling significantly improves overall energy efficiency. The proposed sensing platform provides high-quality recordings suitable for automated acoustic inference and achieves competitive hardware performance while offering greater modularity, lower cost, and improved extensibility compared to many commercial PAM alternatives.The platform provides a foundation for future low-power edge AI processing and standardized wireless communication interfaces for distributed environmental monitoring.

Title: The impact of sectoral policies and policy mixes on low-carbon innovation ‘take-offs’: an analysis of 18 countries 2001–2022
Abstract: Climate policy is a critical driver of low-carbon technology (LCT) innovation; however, prior studies pay insufficient attention to the combined effects of multiple policies. Addressing this deficiency, we combine machine learning with causal inference to endogenously detect sector-specific LCT ‘takeoffs’ in 18 major LCT nations from 2001–2022, systematically evaluating the impacts of over 1,600 policy interventions. Results show that some climate policy interventions act as key triggers for takeoffs in LCT innovation, with synergistic policy mixes forming the primary impact mechanism. In aggregate, market-based instruments (MBI), especially subsidies, serve as the foundational lever for innovation; non-market-based instruments (NMBI), notably performance standards, provide essential complementarity; and targets & governance (T&G) enhance long-run credibility and implementation capacity. At the sectoral level, the buildings sector exhibits the highest responsiveness to policy; its dispersion of agents yields a more diffuse and diverse composition of effective interventions. Electricity tends to favour complex ‘MBI + NMBI + T&G’ packages tailored to its capital-intensive, incumbent-dominated structure. Industry displays the mildest response, with cost sensitivity leading to a profile dominated by pricing and subsidies. In transport, the most effective interventions are dominated by ‘subsidy + targets’ combinations. This study suggests a general policy synergy pathway defined as ‘MBI as drivers + differentiated NMBI aligned with sectoral characteristics as complements + T&G as amplifiers’, which provides strong empirical evidence and practical guidance for designing LCT innovation policies.

Title: Attention-Augmented Hybrid CNN-BiLSTM Framework for High-Performance Bangla Handwritten Digit Recognition: An Empirical Study on NumtaDB
Abstract: Recognizing handwritten Bangla digits reliably remains a hard problem in document digitization because of pronounced intra-class variation, visually similar digit pairs, and inconsistent writing instruments across millions of writers. Standalone CNN models excel at extracting local texture but cannot model holistic structural dependencies, while recurrent networks rarely incorporate attention-guided feature selection for isolated digit recognition. We propose a unified end-to-end framework that chains three convolutional blocks for spatial feature extraction, two stacked Bidirectional LSTM layers for sequential context encoding, and a soft attention mechanism that dynamically weights the most discriminative spatial positions before classification. Trained from scratch on NumtaDB the largest public Bangla digit benchmark and evaluated on 10,807 held-out test samples, the model attains a test accuracy of 99.06% and a macro-averaged F1-score of 0.9906, outperforming all compared methods without relying on pretrained weights or external data. These results confirm that combining spatial, sequential, and attentive reasoning within a single trainable architecture yields a strong and practical baseline for Bangla OCR systems.

Title: Attention-Based Multi-Time-Scale Aggregation Network for Short-Term Load Forecasting
Abstract: Precise short-term load forecasting (STLF) is pivotal to household-level demand management and distribution-side operation, yet remains challenging due to the coexistence of fine-grained fluctuations and long-range periodicities across multiple temporal scales. This paper proposes an attention-based multi-time-scale aggregation network (MTAN), a unified end-to-end architecture that integrates heterogeneous neural encoders tailored to three temporal resolutions: a bidirectional long short-term memory network (Bi-LSTM) captures hour-level sequential dynamics, a two-dimensional convolutional neural network (2-D CNN) extracts intra-day spatial regularities, and a three-dimensional convolutional neural network (3-D CNN) mines volumetric inter-day and inter-week dependencies. The scalar branch outputs are projected into scale tokens and adaptively fused through a lightweight multi-head self-attention mechanism, enabling dynamic cross-scale weighting and scale-level diagnostic interpretation. Extensive experiments on a publicly available individual household electric power consumption dataset demonstrate that MTAN mostly outperforms five representative baselines (ARIMA, Bi-LSTM, 2-D CNN, 3-D CNN, and Informer) across ten direct forecasting horizons from 0.5 to 5 hours. The model achieves an average mean squared error (MSE) performance gap of merely 1.36% relative to the best-performing method at each horizon, validating the effectiveness of multi-scale aggregation for short-term household load forecasting while acknowledging that broader system-level generalization requires additional datasets.

Title: Comparison of physician-authored and artificial intelligence-generated after-visit summaries: A blinded comparative study
Abstract: Background: After-visit summaries (AVSs) are essential for a safe hospital discharge, yet are often written above literacy levels, omit key information, and are produced under substantial clinical time pressure. Large language models (LLMs) offer a potential solution, while performance and safety in real clinical workflows remain uncertain. Objective: To compare the quality, understandability, actionability, and safety of LLM-generated versus physician-authored after-visit summaries for hospitalized patients. Methods: We conducted a retrospective, blinded comparison of physician-authored AVSs and LLM-generated AVSs for 50 adults discharged from the University of California San Diego Health hospital medicine service in 2023. The physician-authored hospital course served as source text for generating AVSs using GPT-4 and Gemma 3n 2. Both were prompted to produce sixth-grade level, patient-centered AVSs. Five attending physicians independently evaluated each AVS using the Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool (PEMAT) for understandability and actionability and the AVSrubric, an instrument assessing accuracy, comprehensiveness, clarity, consistency with the medical record, tone and empathy, and potential for harm. Results: LLM-generated AVSs had higher PEMAT scores than physician-authored AVSs (understandability: 85.5% (GPT-4), 87.5% (Gemma), and 66.1% (physician-authored); actionability: 70.9% (GPT-4), 74.1% (Gemma) vs. 56.7% (physician-authored); all p <.001). On the AVSrubric, LLM-generated AVSs received higher ratings than physician-authored AVSs across all domains with GPT-4 demonstrating significantly higher in all five, while Gemma showed significant improvements in clarity, readability, tone, and empathy. Conclusions: In this blinded evaluation, LLM-generated AVSs were clearer, more comprehensive, and more empathetic than physician-authored AVSs and were associated with lower physician-rated potential for harm. A physician-in-the-loop LLM workflow may improve discharge communication while reducing clinician burden and warrants prospective evaluation.

Title: Reducing Mis-triage in Emergency Departments (RemEDy): Protocol for Improving Triage Accuracy Through Real-time Evaluation and Artificial Intelligence
Abstract: Background: Mis-triage represents a global concern, with reported rates ranging from 15% to 33%. Understanding its causes and contributing factors is essential for ensuring patient safety. Currently, available studies have mainly focused on evaluating triage systems rather than investigating the human factors affecting triage performance. A major limitation in triage evaluation studies is the lack of standardized criteria to assess patient acuity and the absence of a clear consensus on how to measure triage accuracy. Most studies rely on retrospective data, which often fail to capture real-life clinical complexity. Therefore, the underlying causes and consequences of mis-triage remain partially understood. Objective: This study aims to improve triage by defining the optimal triage evaluation process and identifying clinician-, patient-, and system-level factors that compromise its accuracy and safety. Methods: Reducing Mis-Triage in Emergency Departments (RemEDy) will be a 4-phase, mixed methods project conducted across 7 Swiss emergency departments. The first phase will focus on developing a standardized triage evaluation instrument, combining evidence from a scoping review of triage evaluation processes, workshops with triage clinicians using design thinking methodology, and a modified Research and Development–University of California Delphi involving international experts and patient representatives. The second phase will prospectively implement this instrument in real time within a multicenter observational cohort study to evaluate triage performance; quantify mis-triage; and identify predictors at the patient level (eg, demographics), clinician level (eg, training), and system level (eg, crowding and length of stay). The third phase will focus on designing and validating an artificial intelligence–based decision support tool, applying multimodal models that integrate real-time triage data to enhance acuity prediction and minimize human error. The fourth phase will develop and evaluate a targeted training program, guided by the Capability, Opportunity, Motivation, and Behavior model, to strengthen triage accuracy and mitigate cognitive biases. Results: The project was funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation in March 2025 (grant 10004535). At submission, the scoping review is ongoing and expected to be completed in early 2026. Development and piloting of the triage evaluation instrument will take place in 2026. A multicenter cohort study is planned between October 2026 and June 2027. The intervention study is scheduled between October 2027 and December 2028. Final results are expected in 2029. Conclusions: The RemEDy project addresses key limitations of current triage research, including the lack of standardized evaluation methods. By combining expert and clinician consensus; real-time assessment; and multilevel analysis of patient-, clinician-, and emergency department–level factors, RemEDy is expected to provide a more comprehensive understanding of mis-triage and its causes. RemEDy will establish a novel framework for real-time triage evaluation and inform the development of targeted training programs with the potential to improve triage accuracy, safety, and equity.

Title: MUSIC-CAR: A Multi-Label Complex Health-Related Activity Recognition Dataset from Smartphone Sensors
Abstract: Automated recognition of complex activities (CA), such as making a sandwich while talking on the phone, offers crucial insights into daily routines for context-aware applications like patient monitoring. While machine learning models effectively recognize simple activities (SAs), identifying CAs composed of sequential, interleaved, or concurrent SAs remains challenging, hindered by a dearth of suitable public datasets. To address this gap, we introduce a comprehensive, publicly available dataset called MUSIC-CAR for MUltilabel Sequential, Interleaved, and Concurrent Complex Activity Recognition. Collected from 47 participants using two smartphones, one wrist mounted to mimic a smartwatch and the other in a pants pocket, MUSIC-CAR provides IMU sensor data for 9 CA types (e.g., cooking). It uniquely features multi-level labels, containing coarse CA labels and fine-grained SA labels for 30 constituent SAs, capturing their complex relationships (sequential, concurrent, interleaved) within CAs. Our evaluation establishes baseline performance for Complex Activity Recognition(CAR), with XGBoost achieving the highest F1-score of 58.8%. This performance, significantly lower than typical SA recognition scores, demonstrates the inherent difficulty of multi-label CAR from IMU data. MUSIC-CAR represents a valuable resource for the ubiquitous computing and health communities, enabling researchers to develop and evaluate more sophisticated approaches for recognizing complex activities.

Title: Prompting Africa, hearing the West: generative AI music, sonic data coloniality and the future of culturally accountable musical intelligence
Abstract: Generative music systems are being increasingly recognised as adaptable creative technologies that can generate entire compositions, vocal components, instrumental layers, and stylistic variations based on text prompts, uploaded audio, and customised model conditioning. This article contends that such assertions necessitate thorough examination when pertaining to African music and the varied musical traditions, hybrid practices, and performance contexts encompassed by the term. The concern is not that modern AI music systems are incapable of producing outputs that mimic African music. They frequently represent Africanness using recognisable sonic markers such as dense percussion, chant-like vocals, generic “Afro” grooves, pentatonic colour, ululation, and tropicalised production. However, they do not adequately capture the performance systems that render specific African musical practices culturally, linguistically, and socially comprehensible. Utilising African musicology, music information retrieval, decolonial AI, dataset criticism, and digital cultural heritage, this article articulates the notion of sonic data coloniality to analyse the processes through which musical cultures are collected, classified, abstracted, trained, generated, and monetised within disparate technological frameworks. It further posits cultural competence, rather than purity, as the suitable criterion for evaluating AI-generated African music. The article presents a framework for musicological evaluation that is based on prompts and reference audio. This framework encompasses generic prompts, culturally specific prompts, expert prompts, and source-conditioned workflows, utilising rights-cleared African recordings. It posits that evaluation should consider vocality, tone-language relationships, rhythm, groove, microtiming, instrumental idiom, call-and-response, dance implications, social functions, consent, and benefit-sharing. The article asserts that African music ought to be integrated into AI systems not as a homogenised continental sound but rather through the distinct traditions, hybrid practices, performance expertise, and cultural authorities that imbue it with significance.

Title: A Clinically Grounded Review of Medical Image Classification: Quantitative Insights into CNNs, Vision Transformers, and Hybrid CNN-ViT Models
Abstract: Medical image classification has advanced substantially with convolutional neural networks (CNNs), Vision Transformers (ViTs), and hybrid CNN–ViT architectures, yet clinical translation remains limited by dataset dependency, inconsistent evaluation practices, and insufficient external validation. This review provides a clinically grounded comparative synthesis of these model families across diverse medical imaging modalities. A structured literature review was conducted across PubMed, IEEE Xplore, Scopus, and Web of Science for studies published between 2016 and 2025. Following predefined eligibility criteria, 81 studies were included in the qualitative review, of which 74 contributed to a dataset-aware descriptive quantitative aggregation. The quantitative synthesis was therefore restricted to descriptive aggregation; a formal meta-analysis was not performed because of substantial methodological heterogeneity and insufficient reporting of study-level variance information across the included studies. CNN-based models demonstrated the most consistent performance, achieving the highest weighted accuracy (0.934) and weighted recall (0.901). ViT-based models achieved competitive weighted accuracy (0.906) and recall (0.893), particularly for OCT and X-ray imaging, but appeared more sensitive to dataset scale and quality. Hybrid CNN–ViT models achieved a weighted accuracy of 0.814 and weighted recall of 0.698, with the greatest performance variability. Only 10 of the 81 reviewed studies (12.3%) reported independent external validation, while calibration and other clinically relevant evaluation measures were inconsistently reported. CNNs provide a robust baseline for medical image classification, whereas ViT- and hybrid-based architectures offer complementary strengths under appropriate data and training conditions. However, limited external validation and inconsistent reporting indicate that strong retrospective performance should not be interpreted as evidence of clinical readiness. Future research should prioritise externally validated, interpretable, and clinically deployable AI systems supported by standardised evaluation practices.

Title: Large-Sized Micropillars Enable Superior Performance MXene/PDMS Piezoresistive Sensors Toward Accurate Musical Tone Recognition
Abstract: Here we present a flexible MXene/polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) piezoresistive sensor featuring large-sized micropillars (hundreds of micrometers), which promote continuous stress transfer and dynamic interfacial contact evolution, thereby alleviating the intrinsic trade-off between sensitivity and detection range. The PDMS micropillar arrays are fabricated using laser-ablated through-hole molds. The micropillar tips preferentially deform under subtle stimuli, whereas the base layer is progressively engaged under increasing loads. This hierarchical deformation mechanism enables continuous resistance modulation over a broad pressure range. Consequently, the sensor delivers a sensitivity of 103 kPa<sup>−</sup><sup>1</sup> over a wide detection range of 0.6–588 kPa, together with fast response/recovery times (6/20 ms) and robust cyclability (10,000 cycles). Beyond physiological monitoring, the sensor further enables acoustic-vibration detection from the Erhu, a traditional Chinese bowed instrument. Assisted by a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN), a pitch recognition accuracy of 97.5% is achieved. This work provides a structural design strategy for high-performance piezoresistive sensors and establishes a new paradigm for intelligent recognition and acoustic-based human–machine interfaces.

Title: Time Series Foundation Models for Financial Forecasting: A Multi-Paradigm Benchmark on Fixed Income and FX Instruments
Abstract: Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) have recently demonstrated strong zero-shot forecasting performance on standard benchmark datasets, yet their effectiveness on financial time series remains insufficiently understood. We evaluate four pretrained TSFMs (Chronos, TimesFM, Lag-Llama, and Time-LLM) alongside a self-supervised architecture trained from scratch (TS-JEPA) against statistical, machine learning, and deep learning baselines on 19 fixed-income and FX instruments across multiple forecasting horizons and training regimes. The results show that zero-shot TSFMs do not outperform a Random Walk baseline, while increasing the amount of training data across heterogeneous market regimes does not improve forecasting performance. A capacity-controlled analysis further indicates no consistent benefit from LLM backbones, with evidence of negative transfer in fully trained settings. In addition, probabilistic TSFMs improve distributional sharpness but degrade calibration, whereas latent-space objectives without external pretraining fail to enhance noise robustness. These findings suggest a substantial mismatch between generic TSFM pretraining distributions and the statistical properties of financial markets, which are characterised by low signal-to-noise ratios, non-stationarity, and regime shifts. Overall, the results indicate that financial forecasting continues to favour simple domain-aligned models over large pretrained architectures. To our knowledge, this study represents the first multi-paradigm benchmark for TSFMs in fixed-income and FX forecasting tasks.

Title: Metrologically Grounded Graph-Augmented Multimodal AI for Surgical Video Documentation in Smart Healthcare Environments
Abstract: The increasing availability of surgical videos, electronic health records, sensor streams, and clinical notes creates new opportunities for precision healthcare in smart hospitals and connected living environments. Yet, transforming these heterogeneous data into clinically useful documentation remains difficult. Current multimodal systems often provide limited traceability between visual evidence, biomedical concepts, uncertainty information, and generated clinical text. This extended abstract outlines a research direction that builds on an implemented surgical-video report-generation pipeline based on visual-temporal transformers and large language models. The proposed extension introduces a metrologically grounded clinical event graph, where instruments, actions, anatomical targets, phases, confidence scores, model versions, and generated report sentences are represented as auditable graph entities. A metrological layer records calibration, provenance, uncertainty propagation, and human validation, while retrieval-augmented language models synthesize structured reports constrained by graph evidence. Preliminary results from the existing surgical-video pipeline on CholecT50 support the feasibility of the approach, showing strong object detection and captioning performance, including calibrated predictions and semantically coherent clip summaries. The originality of the contribution lies in reframing surgical documentation as a traceable graph-and-LLM process rather than as isolated caption generation, making the approach relevant to trustworthy clinical decision support, operating-room analytics, postoperative reporting, training, and telemedicine.

Title: Small Footprint, Big Intelligence! SAGE: Agentic Governance for Energy-Aware, High-Performance LLMOps
Abstract: The rapid proliferation of Large Language Models (LLMs) has introduced critical operational and environmental challenges, as model training and inference consume enormous computational resources and generate substantial carbon emissions that conflict with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy), SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure), and SDG 13 (Climate Action). However, LLMOps workflows remain largely manual, fragmented, and reactive, while the Artificial Intelligence (AI) industry lacks autonomous, intelligent systems capable of self-governing both operational efficiency and environmental accountability in real time. This work presents SAGE (Sustainable Agentic Governance Engine), a novel dual-agentic AI framework in which two purpose-built autonomous agents operating with goal-directed reasoning, environmental perception, adaptive decision-making, and inter-agent coordination collaboratively govern the entire LLM deployment lifecycle. The first agent, the Optimization Agent, functions as an autonomous orchestrator that continuously perceives pipeline states, reasons over resource utilization patterns, and executes self-optimizing actions for pipeline tuning, model serving configurations, dynamic resource allocation, and cost reduction through a closed-loop feedback mechanism eliminating human-in-theloop bottlenecks and enabling proactive, rather than reactive, operational governance. The second agent, the Green AI Agent, operates as an autonomous environmental auditor for LLMs that independently instruments, collects, and evaluates computational efficiency indicators including FLOPs, energy consumption (kWh), latency at P50/P95, throughput, inference speed, and CPU/GPU/RAM utilization alongside carbon footprint (CO2. emissions) externalities, autonomously mapping these metrics against SDGs 7, 9, and 13 through standardized sustainability scoring. Critically, SAGE agentic architecture enables both agents to communicate, share contextual state, and trigger cross-agent optimization loops whereby the benchmarking agent's sustainability assessments directly inform and constrain the Optimization Agent's resource allocation decisions, creating an emergent, co-adaptive governance system that neither agent could achieve in isolation. By grounding LLMOps in agentic AI principles of autonomy, reactivity, proactivity, and social coordination, SAGE transforms sustainability from a post-hoc audit concern into an embedded, agent-driven, real-time governance mechanism, reframing LLM operations as a socio-technical responsibility aligned with global climate commitments, a convergence of agentic AI, sustainable computing, and responsible AI that remains significantly underexplored in current academic and industrial research. The framework provides a reproducible, scalable pipeline for the responsible deployment of LLMs in realworld, resource-constrained edge environments. Title: A Reflective Classifier Integrating Explainable AI and Deep Learning for Alzheimer’s Disease Detection
Abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD), a neurodegenerative condition impacting more than 55 million individuals worldwide, necessitates prompt and precise diagnosis to facilitate timely therapeutic interventions. Although deep learning algorithms have demonstrated potential in the analysis of neuroimaging data, their inherent "black box" characteristics hinder clinical confidence. This paper presents the reflective classifier, a saliency-guided rectifier framework that incorporates explainable AI (XAI) methodologies into the training regimen of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to improve both diagnostic precision and interpretability. By employing Grad-CAM as an intrinsic facet of the model's architecture rather than as a post-hoc analytical instrument, the model attains state-of-the-art accuracies of 91.68%, 98.50%, and 98.40%, respectively, surpassing the performance of ResNet50, DenseNet121, and Inception-v3.

Title: Application of seismograph observation data in low-altitude aircraft signal identification
Abstract: Seismographs are highly sensitive and broadband instrument designed for detecting and recording seismic waves. In recent years, seismographs have been widely applied in the field of traffic monitoring, demonstrating significant potential, particularly for monitoring low-altitude aircraft. Radar, the traditional tool for aircraft detection, provides accurate and real-time capabilities in locating aircraft position, speed, and flight direction. However, it has limitations in detecting low-altitude aircraft, flexibility, susceptibility to terrain masking, and accuracy under extreme weather conditions. To overcome these limitations, researchers have explored various alternative methods for low-altitude aircraft detection, including infrared, imaging, and acoustic detection. Nevertheless, these methods also face challenges related to cost, weather susceptibility, detection range, and environmental noise.To address these challenges, this paper proposes a real-time recognition method for low-altitude aircraft, based on seismographs and deep learning technology. Leveraging the high precision and anti-interference capability of seismographs and integrating deep learning techniques, the method employs a lightweight MobileNetV3 network model for training, achieving automated identification of low-altitude aircraft signals. Furthermore, the vibrational frequency characteristics of the observed aircraft signals, inverted over time, yielded key flight parameters. The accuracy of these derived parameters was validated through comparison with flight trajectory data.The proposed method exhibits real-time performance and high recognition accuracy for low-altitude aircraft identification. Simultaneously, benefiting from the portability and ease of deployment of seismographs, the method is adaptable to complex environmental application requirements. It offers a feasible technical solution for the field of air traffic monitoring.

Title: Evaluating Pre-Trained Audio Models for Activities of Daily Living Recognition
Abstract: This study evaluates seven state-of-the-art sound recognition models: YAMNet, PANNs, VGGish, AST, PaSST, BEATs, and ConvNeXt-Audio for their suitability in audio-based Activities of Daily Living (ADL) recognition within smart living environments and assisted living applications. Unlike prior work focused on developing new architectures, our objective is to identify the most suitable pre-trained model for integration into an ADL summarization system under realistic indoor conditions. All models are evaluated under a unified protocol on three representative datasets: ESC-50, Kitchen20, and CHiME-Home, covering both single-label and multi-label domestic sound recognition scenarios. In addition to performance metrics, we analyze acoustic characteristics that favor different architectures, examine how pre-training data influences results, and identify which ADL-relevant sounds present challenges across models. We provide objective efficiency measurements, including FLOPs, memory footprint, and inference latency, alongside parameter counts to characterize practical deployment trade-offs. The results suggest that transformer-based models (BEATs, AST) achieve the highest recognition accuracy, while CNN-based ones (PANNs, ConvNeXt-Audio) offer better computational efficiency. The analysis further shows that overlapping sounds and multilabel environments remain challenging for several model families and that pre-training data heterogeneity partially explains observed performance gaps. These findings provide practical guidance for selecting robust and scalable audio recognition components in real-world ADL monitoring applications.

Title: Analysis of the Effectiveness of Acoustic Feature-Based Models in Music Track Classification
Abstract: This paper presents a comparative study of two approaches to multi-label music classification: an end-to-end one-dimensional convolutional neural network trained directly on raw MP3 waveforms and a dual-stream long short-term memory network operating on engineered acoustic features extracted from the time and frequency domains. Both models were evaluated on a preprocessed subset of the MagnaTagATune dataset, in which related and synonymous annotations were consolidated to reduce label redundancy. The raw-audio CNN achieved the higher classification accuracy of 93%, compared with 89% for the feature-based model, but required approximately 10 hours to complete 100 training epochs and exhibited a tendency toward overfitting. In contrast, the dual-stream LSTM completed the same training procedure in approximately 30 minutes, corresponding to an approximately twenty-fold reduction in training time. These results indicate that end-to-end learning can provide moderately better predictive performance, whereas carefully selected acoustic features offer a substantially more computationally efficient alternative. The feature-based approach may therefore be better suited to resource-constrained, latency-sensitive, or embedded applications, while raw-audio models remain preferable when classification performance is the primary objective.

Title: AIN Surgical: A Low-Cost Framework for Synthetic Data Generation in Surgical Robotics Using High-Fidelity Clinical Simulation
Abstract: The advancement of surgical robots depends on big data to train artificial intelligence systems that do vision and control, but achieving real data from real surgeries is difficult due to privacy limitations and the high cost of data preparation and the difficulty of accessing various medical cases. This paper suggests a framework for generating high-fidelity synthetic data using Unity3D software to simulate realistic surgical environments for robotics. This framework includes 3D modeling for organs, realistic physical interactions and environment randomization algorithms to increase the diversity of data. These data are used to train AI models to detect surgical instruments, segmentation, and decision making. The latest studies show that the synthetic data generated by Unity3D can improve the performance of the models and make them more reliable, sometimes surpassing real data in some cases. This work clarifies the ability of merging synthetic data with simulation using game engines and artificial intelligence to accelerate the advancement of autonomous surgical robots. Our result shows that the proposed framework achieves comparable performance to human navigation, with only a 13.85% difference in task completion time.

Title: From Time Domain to Frequency Domain: A Music Deepfake Detection Model Based on Multi-Branch Convolutional Neural Network
Abstract: With the rapid advancement of deep learning and generative models, AI-generated music has seen widespread adoption across both industrial and artistic domains. However, critical challenges regarding copyright attribution and detectability remain urgent. This paper proposes an end-to-end AI audio detection and scoring model based on a Multi-Branch Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). We extract eleven categories of features spanning the time domain, frequency domain, and acoustic statistics. These features are modeled via five parallel branches and subsequently fused for discrimination, thereby achieving robust music deepfake detection. Furthermore, we design various perturbation and adversarial processing techniques to evaluate the model's robustness. Branch contribution analysis is also conducted to reveal the model's dependencies on time-domain envelopes and formant structures. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves an accuracy of 89% and maintains stable performance under most mild-to-moderate perturbations, exhibiting high robustness in comprehensive scoring even under strong perturbations. The proposed method features low computational cost and good scalability, making it generalizable to fields such as speech spoofing detection and environmental sound recognition.

Title: Explainable CNN-based bottleneck diagnosis in human–cobot manufacturing using process heatmaps: An operations and quality management perspective
Abstract: Human–cobot collaborative manufacturing, positioned at the core of the Industry 5.0 paradigm, increases the stochasticity of production systems through human variability, safety-related stops, and resource-sharing constraints. In such environments, rapid identification of dominant bottlenecks and their root causes is critical to operational resilience, production-management responsiveness, and preserving the human-centric character of operations. This study proposes an explainable bottleneck-diagnosis framework based on convolutional neural networks (CNNs) that leverages process heatmaps derived from a discrete-time flow-line simulation model inspired by the digital twin concept. Each simulation run is encoded as a three-channel heatmap (queue length, station busy state, and downtime), yielding a compact spatio-temporal “process fingerprint” suitable for imagebased representation learning. We consider a six-class taxonomy: balanced operation, bottleneck caused by human fatigue, bottleneck caused by cobot performance degradation, bottleneck caused by safety stops in a human–cobot cell, bottleneck caused by cobot failure, and supply delays (line starvation). On a balanced dataset of 1,500 synthetic samples, the CNN achieves a test accuracy of 0.938 (macro-F1 = 0.938; 95% Wilson confidence interval for accuracy: 0.898–0.963). An ablation study shows that multi-channel heatmaps improve accuracy by 0.10 compared with queue-only heatmaps. Explainability is operationalised using Gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM), which consistently localises station–time regions associated with queue build-up and downtime patterns, providing process engineers with evidence that can be translated into corrective actions. The results indicate that simulation-generated heatmaps can support transparent and scalable bottleneck analytics for human–cobot manufacturing, enabling rapid prototyping prior to deployment on shopfloor data and providing an evidence-based decision-support instrument for operations and quality management. The framework also clarifies the shop-floor data required for deployment and proposes a staged implementation path for real-factory decision support.

Title: Explainable Machine Learning for Parkinson's Disease Detection from Speech Signals: A Comparative Evaluation of Classical Models
Abstract: Neurological disorders can alter speech in multiple ways, affecting voice quality, pitch variation, and articulation. In Parkinson's disease, early signs such as reduced loudness, monotone speech, breathiness, and vocal instability are commonly observed, making speech a useful indicator for early discernment. In light of these changes, this study compares three machine learning models - SVM, Random Forest, and XGBoost - using the UCI Parkinson's Speech Features dataset. Among them, XGBoost shows better performance in identifying Parkinsonian speech patterns. The analysis is carried out using key acoustic features namely jitter, shimmer, MFCCs, RPDE, DFA, and pitch-related measures. SHAP is further applied to interpret the model, helping to pick out the most influential features in the prediction.

Title: Stress Identification from Facial Thermal Images using FTS-Net
Abstract: Stress detection using facial thermal imaging offers a non-contact, physiologically meaningful alternative to conventional stress assessment methods. However, there are no publicly accessible facial thermal datasets specifically labelled for stress, and current methods that rely on handcrafted features or conventional convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are unable to capture long-range spatial relationships or subtles temperature fluctuations across facial areas. To overcome these constraints, this research proposes the Transformer-based Facial Thermal Stress Network (FTS-Net), a unique deep learning architecture for stress detection from facial thermograms. The Kotani Thermal Facial Emotion (KTFE) is utilised with anger and neutral classes. Based on psychophysiological correlations, the anger and neutral emotion classes are used as proxies for stressful and non-stressful circumstances. FTS-Net combines multi-scale convolutional feature extraction with an attention mechanism to emphasize physiologically significant regions such as the forehead, periorbital, and nasal areas, while a transformer encoder captures global spatial dependencies and contextual thermal relationships across the face. The novelty of this work lies in integrating transformer-based global modeling with attention-guided thermal feature learning for stress inference from facial thermograms under weak supervision. According to experimental results, FTS-Net achieves better classification performance than standard networks such as ResNet, DenseNet, Inception, and Xception. The suggested approach provides a practical and noninvasive way to detect stress in applications related to affective computing and healthcare.

Title: Non-Contact Speech Classification Using MOF Based Humidity Sensors and Machine Learning
Abstract: Conventional speech recognition depends on acoustic signals, leaving it prone to interference from background noise, privacy risks, and poor performance in constrained environments. Our approach introduces a non-contact system for classifying spoken commands like "Yes"and "No"through humidity sensing paired with machine learning models. A metal organic framework (MOF) sensor is used that detects current variations produced by humidity changes during speech. We developed a robust signal processing and feature extraction pipeline to pull out key time domain metrics, such as peak amplitude, rise time, and area under the curve. A stacking classifier integrating decision Tree, SVM, and XGBoost with logistic Regression gives an accuracy of 92.7%. Overall, this research establishes a low power, silent, contactless alternative for voice interfaces, suitable for assistive technology, underwater communication, and areas demanding high privacy.

Title: Support Vector Machine-Artificial Neural Network Hybrid Model for Condition Monitoring of Electrical Machines
Abstract: Condition monitoring of electrical machines has garnered continuous study attention for more than thirty years, especially concerning spinning electrical machinery. Previously, operators meticulously monitored machine performance; however, this practice has diminished with the introduction of rapid-response digital protection mechanisms. This study, grounded in the author's expertise and current literature, concentrates on online monitoring techniques, with minimal attention to variable speed drives and a preference for conventional machines over contemporary topologies. Data preparation utilises the DWT to efficiently identify and extract unique signal patterns. SVM-ANN are employed for classification, exemplified by a binary decision problem of fault versus no fault classification in early-stage virtual screening. The findings validate that DWT is an effective instrument for feature extraction in condition monitoring. Moreover, SVM exhibits superior performance with diminished standard error in comparison to ANN. SVM-ANN model consistently surpasses alternative methods with an accuracy of 96.06% regardless of training data volume, neural network techniques, or descriptor types. The amalgamation of wavelet-based methodologies with machine learning models demonstrates significant efficacy in the Condition Monitoring of Electrical Machines, facilitating dependable fault detection and enhanced predictive capabilities, while underscoring the necessity for further research on contemporary machine designs and variable speed applications.

Title: A Multimodal Interface for Enhancing Communication Accessibility with Bi-Directional Interaction Among Individuals with Hearing and Speech Impairments using Deep Learning
Abstract: Communication barriers remain critical for individuals with hearing and speech impairments, particularly when both participants do not share a common communication mode. This paper presents a reproducible multimodal bidirectional communication interface that integrates convolutional neural network (CNN)-based sign language recognition, speech-to-text conversion, text-to-speech synthesis, and GIF-based sign representation retrieval within a unified assistive framework. Visual signs are captured using a 640×480 camera at 30 fps and processed through a CNN trained on 5,240 labeled gesture images covering alphabetic, numeric, directional, and common communication signs. Spoken input is recorded at 16 kHz and mapped to text and sign representations using a repository of 1,320 GIF-based signs. Experimental evaluation using 4,860 bidirectional trials produced 4,417 successful translations, corresponding to 90.88% overall translation reliability. The system achieved 88.62% gesture recognition score, 90.71% speech transcription score, 91.00% macro-precision, 90.50% macro-recall, and 90.73% macro-F1 across multimodal evaluation. Real-time testing showed an average gesture inference time of 32.6 ms and end-to-end interaction latency of 184.7 ms. These results demonstrate that the proposed interface can support practical two-way communication between speech users and sign-language users while maintaining measurable recognition accuracy, computational responsiveness, and accessibility benefit.

Title: Robust Deep Learning-enabled Framework for Skin Cancer Segmentation and Classification using Trans-MobileUnet++ and Multi-Dilated Attention based ResNeXt
Abstract: Skin cancer occurred when the abnormal cells multiply, which often results in prolong expose to Ultra Violet (UV) rays. Skin cancers are frequently due to high expose to sunlight and ranges from harmless skin lesions to invasions tumors. Early identification and accurate diagnosis are essential for boosting the visual examination based on the expert's evaluations. To solve these issues, an innovative deep learning model is developed, which provide more efficient and early detection. Thus, an enhanced skin cancer segmentation and classification framework is developed using deep learning, which helps to tackle the current issues by enabling early classification. At first, the image is taken from standard data sources. The developed model segments the collected images using Trans-MobileUnet++ (Trans-MUnet++), integrating U-Net++ skip connections, a lightweight MobileNet backbone, and transformer-based feature extraction. This architecture lowers computing complexity, improves feature representation, and improves lesion boundary identification. By resolving data scarcity and class imbalance without raising training costs, it guarantees precise, effective, and scalable skin cancer segmentation. The segmented images are classified using Multi-Dilated Attention based ResNeXt (MDA-RNeXt). Multi-Dilated Attention increases sensitivity to both minor and large lesion patterns by capturing spatial data at many scales. ResNeXt leverages residual connections and grouped convolutions to effectively learn hierarchical representations. While the gated shared weighted paired attention dynamically balances global and local interactions and selectively controls data flow to minimize irrelevant features and enhance discriminative representations, the integrated ResNeXt provides precise and reliable skin cancer classification. In the final stage, the designed model generates skin cancer categorization, which its performance is then evaluated against baseline models, demonstrating superior accuracy and the overall effectiveness.

Title: Depression Detection using Speech Emotion Recognition: Comparative Analysis of Models
Abstract: Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) has gained significant attention for its ability to make human-computer interactions more natural and supportive, particularly in applications such as mental health monitoring and intelligent assistant systems. In this work, examine the effectiveness of different deep learning approaches using four widely used datasets: SAVEE, RAVDESS, CREMA-D, and DAIC-WOZ. The models evaluated include Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM), and hybrid architectures that combine CNN with BiLSTM or BiGRU, along with attention mechanisms to better focus on important features. also explore the impact of using reduced feature sets and introduce a confidence- and risk-based strategy to enhance prediction reliability. The results reveal that model performance differs across datasets, largely due to variations in data complexity. The MLP model achieved the highest accuracy of 95 on the SAVEE dataset, while hybrid models showed stronger performance on more complex datasets like DAIC-WOZ. In contrast, the CREMA-D dataset produced comparatively lower results, indicating its challenging nature. Overall, the study highlights that integrating multiple model techniques with feature selection and attention mechanisms can improve the accuracy and robustness of emotion recognition systems, making them more suitable for real-world use.

Title: Predicting AI-Integrated Performance from Perceived AI Literacy Among Senior High STEM Learners
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become a cornerstone of modern STEM education, requiring students not only to understand AI conceptually but also to demonstrate competence in applying it to authentic academic tasks. However, most existing studies rely on perceived AI literacy without validating whether these perceptions accurately reflect students' demonstrated capabilities. This study investigated the relationship between perceived and performance-based AI literacy among Grade 12 STEM students enrolled in an Integrated Challenge-Based Learning Program (ICBLP). A predictive-correlational design was employed using two validated instruments: the Perceived AI Literacy Scale (PALS) and the AI Written Work (AIWW) performance assessment. Results revealed strong reliability across perceived literacy domains (α=.814) but weaker internal consistency for demonstrated literacy (α=.474), indicating domain distinctiveness. Correlational analysis showed minimal alignment between perceived and actual competence (r =.134, p>.05). Hierarchical regression indicated that perceived literacy explained only 11.9% of variance in AI-integrated performance, while cluster analysis identified three distinct AI literacy profiles, revealing disparities between confidence and capability. These findings highlight that AI literacy must be assessed through both perceptual and authentic performance measures. The study contributes to emerging AI educational frameworks by proposing a dual-assessment model and emphasizing differentiated instruction to support diverse AI literacy trajectories.

Title: A Hybrid Deep Learning Approach for Speech Emotion Recognition
Abstract: This manuscript proposes a classification model of speech emotion conditions by FM (feature map) integrated with TCN and the pretrained CNN (convolutional neural network) of the speech databank. The work consists of four essential steps. Firstly, it receives MFCC (Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients) and gammatone cepstral coefficients (GFCC) in the incidence domain, as well as log-Mel spectrograms in the time-incidence domain. Secondly, based on the features, the next stage starts the training process through TCN and the other audio MobileNet network (YAMNet), respectively. A third step is the FM combination using canonical correlation analysis (CCA), stationary wavelet transforms (SWT), and principal component averaging with fuzzy c-means (FCMPCA). The above processes make it possible to use the TCN and YAMNet fusion models, and FM fusion (FMF) models to create an effective speech emotion recognition model. Finally, a comparison of classification of the AI-Hub speech emotion dataset, and the RAVDESS, TESS, and Emo-DB datasets is presented. The investigational results proven that the suggested model yielded better performance than prior studies across most datasets.

Title: Machine Learning-based Investigation of Structure-Breakdown Relationship in BOPP
Abstract: Polypropylene (PP) films serve as the core dielectric medium for high-voltage dry-type DC capacitors. However, the nonlinear structure-property relationship between their multi-scale microstructure and macroscopic breakdown performance remains elusive. In this study, a generalized structure-property dataset transcending processing boundaries was constructed by integrating samples prepared via uniaxial stretching and biaxial orientation (BOPP). Based on the support vector regression (SVR) algorithm, a high-precision breakdown strength prediction model (R<sup>2=</sup> 0.95) was established, and the contribution weights of multi-scale structural parameters were quantified via SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis. The results reveal that for biaxially oriented polypropylene (BOPP) films, the breakdown performance is synergistically regulated by crystallinity, melting point, crystallite size, and ash content. The melting point and crystallinity play dominant roles in the breakdown mechanism. Notably, crystallinity exhibits a significant percolation threshold effect at 52%, above which the formation of a dense crystalline network effectively enhances the breakdown strength. Furthermore, fine crystallite size and low ash content were identified as key factors for achieving high breakdown strength. Based on these findings, a comprehensive regulation strategy of “purification, grain refinement, and crystallization enhancement” is proposed. This work elucidates the microstructural origins of the breakdown performance of PP films, providing a theoretical basis and methodological reference for accelerating the development of next-generation high-energy-density capacitor films.

Title: From Perception to Performance: Artificial Intelligence, Student Motivation, and Learning Strategies of Students in Metro Manila, Philippines
Abstract: This study explores the relationship between students' perceptions of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and their motivation and learning strategies within higher education institutions in Metro Manila. Grounded in the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), the research investigates how perceived impact, usefulness, and actual use of AI influence student engagement and academic behaviors. Using a correlational design, data were collected from 385 college students through a structured survey adapted from validated instruments. Descriptive and inferential statistics, including Spearman's rank-order correlation, were employed to analyze the data. Findings reveal that students generally perceive AI positively, especially for homework assistance and distance learning. While AI is embraced as a supplementary tool, students remain cautious about replacing traditional educational methods. Motivation scores indicate strong academic drive, though test anxiety and confidence in handling difficult material show variability. Learning strategies are well developed, with students demonstrating effective study habits and metacognitive approaches; however, visual aids and persistence during periods of boredom are less frequently used. The study highlights the potential of AI to enhance personalized learning, support self-regulation, and foster academic success. However, ethical concerns, digital literacy gaps, and infrastructural limitations, particularly in the Philippine context, pose challenges to widespread adoption. These insights underscore the need for balanced integration of AI in education, promoting responsible use while maximizing its motivational and pedagogical benefits.

Title: Self-Supervised Deep Learning for Early Detection of Voice Pathologies
Abstract: Voice disorder detection systems have traditionally relied on manually annotated acoustic datasets, which require significant effort from clinical experts and speech-language pathologists. The increasing availability of large-scale unlabeled voice recordings offers new opportunities for more scalable learning approaches. A self-supervised deep learning model based on a combined CNN-BiLSTM architecture is proposed for the automatic recognition of voice disorders. To characterize voice signals, the proposed method combines CNN-based spectral feature extraction with BiLSTM-based temporal sequence modeling. Performance evaluation on the experimental dataset yields an accuracy of 98.3%, suggesting that self-supervised representation learning provides a powerful solution for automated voice pathology analysis. These findings suggest that self-supervised methods can significantly enhance automated voice disorder detection and support early clinical diagnosis using diverse and large-scale voice data.

Title: Bridging Perception and Practice: Assessing AI Literacy Among Grade 12 STEM Students
Abstract: In the Philippine education landscape, where emerging technologies like artificial intelligence (AI) are transforming how students learn, assessing their AI literacy is both a timely challenge and an essential step toward future-ready learning. This study examined the relationship between perceived and demonstrated AI literacy among Grade 12 STEM students enrolled in the Integrated Challenge-Based Learning Program (ICBLP). Using a descriptive-correlational design, two instruments were employed: the AI Literacy Questionnaire (AILQ) to measure students' self-reported literacy and the AI Written Work (AIWW) task to evaluate demonstrated competence. Data from 95 students aged 16-18 were analyzed using descriptive statistics, correlation, and group comparisons. Results revealed that students possessed high demonstrated AI literacy (M=4.67, SD=0.34) but only moderate perceived literacy (M=3.63, SD=0.61), indicating a gap between confidence and performance. The weak, non-significant correlation (r=0.134, p>0.05) suggested that the two scales assess distinct dimensions of literacy. Component analysis showed strong ethical and affective literacy but weaker behavioral consistency, while gender analysis revealed females' strength in applied and ethical domains and males' higher perceived cognitive literacy. Findings underscore the multidimensional nature of AI literacy and highlight the ICBLP's effectiveness in fostering reflective, ethical, and applied AI competence. The study recommends integrative, gender-responsive, and challenge-based pedagogies that bridge perception and practice, preparing learners to engage with AI critically, responsibly, and humanely.
