Title: Long-Distance Detection of Gas Leakages by Narrowband Ultrasonic Sensing and Multidistance Fusion Supervised Learning Method
Abstract: Reliable detection of gas leakages is essential for ensuring the safety of energy storage and transportation systems, minimizing economic losses, and protecting public welfare. Although acoustic wave detection enables noncontact monitoring and performs well across different gases and environments, it remains constrained by a weak ability to capture long-distance leakage signals and by limited detection accuracy. This study proposes a gas leakage long-distance detection technology based on narrowband ultrasound sensing and a multidistance fusion supervised learning method to address these limitations. In particular, a narrowband ultrasound detection apparatus with a sound concentrator is designed to capture the acoustic signals of leakages. Following feature extraction, a local mean weighted K-nearest centroid neighbor classifier based on multidistance fusion (LMWKNCN-MD) is proposed for leakage detection. Datasets are collected in laboratory and factory environments for evaluating the performance of the apparatus and the proposed method. The detection apparatus successfully detects leakage sources up to 10 m away using a fully noncontact and nondestructive method under test conditions of 0.3 MPa pipe pressure and a Φ 0.1-mm leakage orifice. The experimental results indicate that the proposed method has a 4.3 % higher detection accuracy compared to the attention-based local mean K-nearest centroid neighbor classifier (ALMKNCN) in the air leakage dataset. This study holds promise for broad industrial prospects offering improved safety in gas storage and transportation.

Title: Assessing the Influence of Video Games on Academic Success Through Machine Learning Techniques
Abstract: This study assesses the influence of video game engagement on the academic success of first-year students enrolled in an introductory programming course using supervised machine learning techniques. Specifically, it examines how gaming frequency, daily and weekly gaming duration, and preferred game genres relate to students' study practices, behavioral wellness, and academic outcomes. A quantitative predictive research design was employed, involving 640 first-year students. Data were collected through validated survey instruments and academic records. The survey captured gaming-related variables and two behavioral indicators: the Study Habit Index (SHI), which represents learning routines and academic discipline, and the Behavioral Wellness Index (BWI), which reflects motivation, stress management, and emotional balance.Academic success was operationalized through a rule-based performance classification derived from academic records, categorizing students into High, Average, and Low performance groups. Gaming and behavioral variables were used as predictors in three supervised machine learning models: Decision Tree, Random Forest, and Support Vector Machine. Model performance was evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation, while K-Means clustering was applied as an exploratory technique to identify natural student groupings. Among the supervised models, the Decision Tree achieved the highest overall cross-validation performance, followed by Random Forest as a strong ensemble benchmark, while Support Vector Machine provided a nonlinear comparison model.The findings indicate that study habits have a stronger association with academic success than gaming exposure alone. Gaming hours showed minimal direct relationship with academic performance, suggesting that time spent playing video games is not, by itself, a dominant predictor of student achievement. Instead, academic success is better explained by combined behavioral patterns involving study discipline, wellness, self-regulation, stress, and motivation. The study demonstrates the potential of machine learning in educational analytics by integrating gaming and behavioral indicators to support early identification of academically at-risk students and guide evidence-based interventions that promote balanced learning, wellness, and academic improvement.

Title: Research on Dance Movement Generation based on Semantic-Aware Physics - Guided Dance Generation Framework
Abstract: Dance movement generation plays a crucial role in improving choreography, virtual reality, digital entertainment, human-computer interaction and animation by directly synthesizing accurate dance performances synchronized with music. However, traditional dance movement generation methods particularly depend on convolutional neural networks, transformer-based architectures and recurrent neural networks, they frequently outcomes the limited semantic understanding of inadequate modeling of long-term choreography, dance movements, poor adaptability across different dance styles and the physically generation unrealistic body poses. In addition, conventional deep learning-based methods often face difficulties in accurately incorporating modeling emotional characteristics and multimodal musicmotion information of music and preserving biomechanical reliability during dance generation. To overcome these challenges, the proposed Semantic-Aware Physics-Guided Dance Generation Framework (SPGDGF) is developed for dance movement generation. Firstly, multimodal dance data, such as music signals, skeletal motion sequences, dance style labels, body joint coordinates and choreography annotations, are gathered from public dance datasets, online dance video databases and motion capture repositories. Moreover, preprocessing techniques include missing pose completion, music-motion temporal synchronization, feature normalization and data augmentation are applied to improve learning stability and data quality. The Semantic Dance Representation Encoder captures discriminative semantic movement demonstration, while the Emotion-Aware Music Encoding Module models rhythm, emotional characteristics and tempo from music signals. Further, the Hierarchical Choreography Learning Network extracts long-term temporal dependencies across dance sequences. Subsequently, Physics-Guided Motion Refinement Module and adaptive multimodal feature fusion and allows realistic dance movement generation by ensuring choreography consistency, biomechanical plausibility and music-motion synchronization. Experimental results represent the proposed SPGDGF framework achieves improved performance compared with conventional dance generation methods in terms of Fréchet Inception Distance FID of 0.31, dance generation accuracy, music-motion synchronization, choreography consistency, motion diversity and biomechanical realism, thereby virtual performers, assisting choreography and AI-assisted dance generation systems.

Title: Application Boundaries of AIGC Music Generation Technology in Media Content Production
Abstract: With the advantages of efficiency and customization, Generative Artificial Intelligence (AIGC) music generation technology is reshaping the logic of music supply in media contents creation, and is already applied on a large scale to the short video, advertisement, film and television scene. However, issues including violation of training data, copyright controversy on generated contents, and unbalanced industrial ecology. Based on the principles of copyright law and the practice of the media industry, this paper defines the application boundaries of AIGC music generation technology from three aspects: scenario adaptation, functional performance, and ethical compliance, and analyzes the practical challenges in the application of the technology, including the dilemma of copyright ownership, the difficulty in determining infringement, the absence of industry standards, and the lag of policy regulation. Based on the existing policy demands, in this work we propose a multiple-layered regulation framework including law-making optimization, technological fixes, private sector cooperation, and judicial evolution. These are the main areas of contribution: (1)the presentation of a three-dimensional framework (scenario, function, ethics) for defining application boundaries;(2) A systematic analysis of four major real-world dilemmas;(3) A four-in-one integrated regulatory system of "law - judiciary - industry - technology"was constructed. This study provides theoretical support and practical paths for the compliant application of AIGC music generation technology and the high-quality development of the media industry.

Title: Deep Learning Approaches for Lung Cancer Classification: Assessing CNN Performance using Saliency Maps and Grad CAM on CT Imaging
Abstract: Lung cancer remains among the leading causes of mortality in the world and CT imaging is one of the crucial instruments of early diagnosis. These scans however are time consuming and prone to error in case they are manually interpreted. We use a dataset of 364 lung CT images in this study, as they have been obtained in an Iranian hospital comprising of 238 cancerous and 126 noncancerous patients, which are accorded with labels by a specialist in pulmonology. We test five different convolutional neural network designs, under the same preprocessing, augmentation and training regimes to give an equal evaluation opportunity. To solve the issue of class imbalance and low number of samples, data augmentation methods were used to increase the size of the data threefold to enhance model generalization. To make the decisions of the models more interpretable, saliency maps and Grad Cam were employed to visualize the decision-making of the models, where attention was paid to the clinically relevant areas, including tumor areas in cancerous scans and ground glass opacities in noncancerous images. The results of the experiment suggest that NASNet Mobile demonstrates excellent performance, with the highest level of test accuracy of 99.94. These results indicate that it is more effective in classifying lung cancer. In general, this paper delivers a multimodal comparison, solid data augmentation approaches, and interpretable visual features that enhance clinical confidence. It leads to the development of automated lung cancer detection, as well as offering a scalable solution that can be deployed in resource constrained settings.

Title: Biomechanics-Constrained Adaptive Optimization of Motion Performance via Music Emotion-Aware Computational Modeling
Abstract: To address the lack of deep coupling between music emotion perception and biomechanical constraints in real-time optimization of motion performance, this paper proposes an adaptive motion performance optimization framework based on music emotion perception under biomechanical constraints. This framework constructs a quintuple model (S, E, A, T, R), where S is the biomechanical state space including joint angles, angular velocities, joint torques, ground reaction forces, muscle fatigue indices, and injury risk markers; and E is a three-dimensional continuous emotional state space based on pleasure, arousal, and dominance, along with its temporal dynamic features. Methodologically, a music emotion event detection method based on generalized likelihood ratio and autoregressive models is proposed. A signal-to-noise ratio weighted phase-locked loop algorithm is used to extract auditory event-related potential waveforms, which are then mapped to the continuous emotional state space through a learnable encoding network. Regarding the optimization strategy, a maximum entropy reinforcement learning framework is constructed, and a composite reward function integrating task performance, injury risk assessment, and emotion-motor coupled rewards is designed. The experimental platform integrated a Vicon 3D motion capture system, a Kistler 3D force table, a Delsys surface electromyography system, and a real-time computing workstation. Forty-eight healthy adults were recruited to complete treadmill exercise experiments under three conditions (no music, random music, and adaptive optimization). Results showed that the proposed music-based emotional event detection method improved the F1 score by 8.68 percentage points compared to the baseline method using a hidden Markov model. The signal-to-noise ratio weighted phase-locked loop algorithm improved the principal component retention rate by 14.32 percentage points under high noise conditions. Emotional state decoding achieved a mean absolute error of 0.182 and a correlation coefficient of 0.846 in pleasure prediction. Compared to the no-music control group, the adaptive optimization group showed a 9.22% reduction in steady-state oxygen uptake, an 8.87% improvement in exercise economy, a decrease in the coefficient of variation of oxygen uptake to 4.76%, and a decrease in the respiratory quotient from 0.912 to 0.886, corresponding to an approximately 36.8% fat-based energy supply ratio.

Title: Comparative Evaluation of Anomaly Detection Algorithms for PM2.5 Air Quality in Bogotá, Colombia
Abstract: Air pollution from particulate matter (PM) is an issue to be considered by all governments worldwide, in the pursuit of improving the quality of life for the population. In Colombia, the government has led the use of instruments such as the 2021 Air Quality Strategy, through which compliance with regulations is sought. For the authorities in Bogotá (Colombia), the most important pollutants to consider are PM<inf>10</inf> and PM<inf>2.5</inf>. This research develops a study to accurately forecast the behavior of pollutants, with the purpose of preventing the population’s exposure to high levels of PM. This paper presents a comparison of anomaly detection algorithms to identify outliers in air quality data, particularly PM<inf>2.5</inf>. The data used was collected hourly from air quality monitoring stations in Bogotá from 2014–2019. The methodological design includes the implementation of synthetic outlier data, processing of time series, selection of statistical methods, and models based on artificial intelligence (AI). Finally, a comparative study is conducted based on performance metrics. The experimental results show that the statistical method (SARIMAX) presents high accuracy in identifying normal data. Regarding AI-based models, the SR and CNN models show higher performance metric accuracy for identifying outliers. The SR model is accurate for detecting anomalous data from a computer vision perspective, as it combines saliency maps and convolutional neural networks. The CNN model forms a conceptual description of inputs based on historical data patterns. The results can be improved by adding a CNN configuration layer, as done in classical clustering methods, or even an auto-encoder. The main idea is to implement CNN solely as a feature extractor.

Title: A Web-Based Mental Health Assessment Framework using Natural Language Processing Techniques
Abstract: Mental illnesses like depression, anxiety, stress, and so on have become more widespread, and this has necessitated the availability of assessment tools that are readily available, scalable, and automated. The paper will offer a web-based mental health risk assessment system that utilizes the latest technology of Natural Language Processing (NLP) in real-time to analyze textual information provided by users. The offered system incorporates a hybrid deep learning framework with the relation of DeBERTa, BiLSTM, and XGBoost to promote the contextual comprehension, sequential emotional pattern identification, and effective classification of the performance. First, text input by the users is received with a secure web interface and processed with general NLP preprocessing methods, such as tokenization, lemmatization, and sentiment normalization. To extract deep semantic relationships in the text, DeBERTa is used to extract contextual embeddings. Such embeddings are also trained in the form of a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) network in order to capture emotional dynamics and linguistic reinforcing relations. Fused feature representation, sentiments, and linguistic indicators are input into an XGBoost classifier to predict mental health in multi-class. There is a weighted risk scoring system used to measure the level of severity and provide tailored feedback. It is experimentally tested on standard mental health text data sets that the proposed hybrid framework is more effective than the traditional machine learning and standalone transformer models in terms of accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. The architecture is scalable to the deployment of a web system, which is guaranteed to perform in real-time, secure data, and privacy of users. The suggested framework offers a solid and smart instrument to identify the risk of mental health early and help intervene in time and to promote the development of digital health care.

Title: AI-Driven Predictive Maintenance Framework for Industrial IoT Systems using Google Cloud
Abstract: Analytical preservation has become an vital strategy in Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) locations for enlightening equipment reliability, dropping unforeseen machine failures, and enlightening trade productivity. This paper suggests an AI-driven predictive maintenance framework using the Google Cloud AI Platform for smart monitoring and fault estimate of engineering refining machines. Three machine learning algorithms, namely Random Forest, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Artificial Neural Network (ANN), are practical and assessed to classify potential equipment letdowns before disappointment occurrence. Among the manufacturing models, the XGBoost classifier achieved the highest prediction accuracy of 99.18% with strong accuracy, recall, and AUC performance, on behalf of superior ability in early fault finding and analytical analytics. The grouping of Google Cloud AI services allows walkable model training, cloud-based supply, real-time specialist care, and efficient data organization for smart manufacturing applications. New results show significant improvements in upkeep efficiency, decrease in working downtime, and lower upkeep costs associated with traditional sensitive conservation approaches. Title: Power Plant Efficiency Prediction Using MrMiMaxG Feature Selection and Consensus Voting Mechanism
Abstract: Efficiency assessments in steam power plants frequently face challenges due to high dimensional sensor data that is plagued by significant noise, multicollinearity, and fluctuating feature importance. Traditional Feature Selection techniques typically operate independently and yield inconsistent sets of features. To overcome this issue, this paper introduce MrMi-MaxG, a consensus driven ensemble Feature Selection framework that combines Mutual Information, mRMR, Recursive Feature Elimination, and Genetic Algorithm using a voting approach. Besides the dataset from the power plant operations, the efficacy of this technique was also evaluated using the benchmark dataset Communities and Crime from UCI Machine Learning. The experimental findings indicate that MrMiMaxG can drastically decrease feature dimensionality by as much as 91.8% on the benchmark dataset, all while achieving an R<sup>2</sup> value exceeding 0.99 and a WPPS score of up to 93.87% for calculating BE values and 90.88% for NPHR. An analysis of time complexity reveals substantial improvements in computational efficiency, with the model training taking place 9 times faster (a 900% enhancement) and inference being 1.5 times quicker when compared to models that do not implement Feature Selection. By using the risk oriented Weighted Penalty Performance Score (WPPS) metric for evaluation, the framework delivers a scalable, energy efficient, and secure approach for large-scale industrial analytics.

Title: Noise-Suppressed Transformer-based Voice-to-Text for Accurate Multilingual Speech Recognition in Noisy Environments
Abstract: This study aims to design and implement a noise-suppressed, transformer-based voice- to-text system that can accurately recognize multilingual speech in challenging noisy conditions. The experimental setup consists of two comparative groups, both evaluated using multilingual speech datasets recorded under noisy conditions. Group 1: It represents the baseline system, which employs a conventional RNNoise-based automatic speech recognition (ASR) model without any noise suppression techniques. A total of 1,000 audio samples are used for its evaluation. Group 2: It corresponds to the proposed approach, which integrates noise-aware processing with an RNN-Transformer-based ASR architecture for multilingual speech transcription, also tested on 1,000 audio samples. The proposed noise-suppressed RNN-Transformer-based ASR system achieved a higher average transcription accuracy of 96.01%, surpassing the existing RNNoise-based system, which attained an accuracy of 86.58%. In addition to improved accuracy, the proposed model exhibited greater consistency, with a lower standard deviation of 3.05 compared to 4.12 for the baseline system. The findings demonstrate that the RNNoise-Transformer-based speech recognition system performs considerably better than the conventional RNNoise model, attaining an accuracy of 96.01% while lowering the word error rate to 5.8%. The system demonstrated effective real-time operation with an average latency of 160 ms and maintained stable performance across varying noise levels.

Title: Nurse-Led Ambient AI Scribe for Patient Safety Incident Investigation Reports (Project NARRATE): Retrospective Pre-Post Comparative Document-Quality Study
Abstract: Background: Patient safety investigation reports support organizational learning only when they are complete, usable, and sufficiently detailed. Conventional free-text reports are often inconsistent and may omit information needed for review and learning. Project NARRATE (Nursing AI-Refined for Accurate Transcription of Events) is a nursing-led ambient artificial intelligence workflow that uses prompts aligned with the World Health Organization Minimal Information Model for Patient Safety Incident Reporting and Learning Systems, Situation-Background-Assessment-Recommendation output, and visible missing-information cues to support structured supervisor reporting. Objective: This study aimed to compare the completeness and narrative quality of conventional and NARRATE-period supervisor investigation reports for falls and medication administration-related incidents. Methods: We conducted a retrospective pre-post document-quality study at a tertiary academic medical center in Singapore. We reviewed 150 deidentified completed supervisor investigation reports: 75 conventional reports from June to August 2025 and 75 confirmed NARRATE reports from January to March 2026. NARRATE use was voluntary, and recorded use represented approximately 40% of eligible postimplementation reports. Two blinded reviewers rated reports using a World Health Organization (WHO)–aligned completeness checklist and an adapted 8-domain Physician Documentation Quality Instrument (PDQI). Report-level comparisons were adjusted for repeated reports by the same supervisor using random-intercept linear mixed-effects models. A stratified 60-report plain-paragraph rerating examined whether visible structure influenced ratings. Results: All 150 reports were analyzed. Unadjusted mean WHO total completeness was 11.81 (SD 3.39) for conventional reports and 13.61 (SD 2.54) for NARRATE reports; the unadjusted difference was 1.80 points, and the cluster-adjusted mean difference was 1.95 (95% CI 0.91‐3.00; P<.001). The adapted PDQI mean was 3.61 (SD 0.52) and 4.13 (SD 0.34), respectively; the unadjusted difference was 0.52 points, and the cluster-adjusted mean difference was 0.53 (95% CI 0.37‐0.69; P<.001). In the plain-paragraph sensitivity analysis, the completeness advantage remained (adjusted mean difference 1.70, 95% CI 0.27‐3.14; P=.02), as did the adapted PDQI mean advantage (adjusted mean difference 0.25, 95% CI 0.06‐0.43; P=.009). Explanation, organization, and comprehensibility remained significantly higher after deformatting; actions were borderline (P=.05), and synthesis, internal consistency, and fairness/balance were not statistically significant. Conclusions: Among voluntary early adopters, NARRATE use was associated with more complete reports and higher adapted PDQI mean scores after accounting for supervisor clustering. Because recorded use represented approximately 40% of eligible postimplementation reports and users self-selected, findings may reflect adopter and supervisor characteristics. Results support the structured workflow as a whole, not any single AI component, and do not demonstrate downstream patient-safety effects. Confirmatory evaluation under broader adoption with a concurrent, reliably classified comparison group is needed.

Title: MODELLING IMPACT OF HYBRID METHODOLOGY ON PERFORMANCE OF IT-ENTERPRISES
Abstract: Purpose. To develop and empirically verify a model-based approach to assessing the impact of a hybrid project management methodology on the performance of software development enterprises, taking into account the level of managerial maturity and the moderating role of artificial intelligence tools. Methodology. The study is based on an original survey of 93 Ukrainian IT enterprises (2026) and combines cluster analysis (the k-means algorithm with the silhouette quality criterion), multiple regression modelling (OLS), the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) with verification of the consistency of expert judgements (CR <0.1), and three-level scenario modelling. The enterprise typology is constructed by level of managerial maturity through the aggregation of managerial, engineering and business indicators. Findings. A typology comprising three enterprise types is empirically confirmed: start-up, established Agile practices, and mature enterprise level. The regression model (R<sup>2</sup>=0.957) revealed a statistically significant effect of the presence of a project management office, CI/CD maturity and AI readiness on the composite project performance index (PPI). The transformation of the management system is substantiated through three scenarios: baseline, formalisation of the hybrid methodology, and integration of artificial intelligence tools. An adaptive PPI structure with differentiated subindex weights and assessment time horizons is proposed; the projected performance gain falls within the range of 10-40 %, peaking at highly mature enterprises. Originality. A multi-level model for assessing the impact of a hybrid project management methodology has been developed and empirically verified which, unlike descriptive maturity models, combines an enterprise typology based on managerial maturity, an adaptive composite PPI indicator and a four-stage scheme for transforming management practices. The model operationalises the non-linearity of the transition between maturity levels while accounting for the moderating role of AI tools and the resource constraints of the enterprise. Practical value. The proposed model is intended to serve as an analytical instrument for substantiating managerial decisions concerning the adoption of a hybrid methodology and the integration of artificial intelligence at software development enterprises. Its application delivers a predictably positive economic effect through the reduction of losses, revenue growth and an increase in the intangible value of assets, and provides a quantitative rationale for investment decisions by demonstrating positive NPV and IRR.

Title: Spoken Response-Based Automatic Screening of Suicidal Risk Among Adolescents
Abstract: Automatic detection of suicidal risk has become the need of the hour, especially for adolescents. This study presents a suicidal risk classification system. The database utilized in this work is introduced in the 1st SpeechWellness Challenge organized in 2025. It comprises participants' spoken responses to three distinct tasks. The provided baseline systems are based on both conventional and advanced deep-learning models. The implemented deep learning model has provided better detection performance. In this study, we explore three distinct hand-crafted feature sets and their fusion at the decision and feature levels to implement a light-weight suicidal risk classification system. We also proposed a simple method that address the limitation of the baseline conventional model. Moreover, the detection is performed at the segment level, and the impact of different input segment lengths is analyzed. The results show that our proposed method outperformed the baselines on the development set in terms of accuracy. On the test set, our submissions are found to be better than the baselines in terms of recall metric.

Title: Physical Therapy and Health-Promoting Interventions Featuring Artificial Intelligence–Generated Music
Abstract: Artificial intelligence–generated music (AI-music) has emerged as an innovative adjunctive modality for pain management within physical therapy, offering adaptive, personalized auditory stimulation that aligns with patients’ physiological and emotional states. This literature review synthesizes current evidence on the effectiveness of AI-generated and AI-personalized music in rehabilitation contexts, with emphasis on pain modulation, psychological regulation, motor performance, cognitive functioning, and patient engagement. A narrative synthesis approach was used to evaluate studies identified through literature review, focusing exclusively on measurable therapeutic outcomes. Findings indicate that AI-generated music provides comparable analgesic effects to traditional music interventions, with enhanced benefits linked to real-time personalization and patient preference alignment. Strong evidence supports superior reductions in anxiety and stress, which indirectly mitigate pain and improve tolerance for therapeutic activity. AI-adaptive rhythmic structures further facilitate motor recovery by enhancing entrainment and movement synchronization, while interactive and feedback-based systems significantly improve motivation and adherence. Cognitive effects are variable but promising, particularly in neurological populations. Long-term outcomes remain under-studied, and current research lacks standardized evaluation frameworks, while ethical considerations—including privacy, data use, and clinician readiness—present practical barriers to implementation. AI-generated music demonstrates substantial potential as an adjunct to physical therapy pain management, offering multi-dimensional benefits that support both physical and psychological aspects of rehabilitation.

Title: Prediction and Quantification of Stress in the Workplace by Utilizing Machine Learning Approaches
Abstract: The prevalence of mental health problems has become a very common phenomenon during recent times, social media has become a much more popular platform through which people are expressing their psychological suffering. This paper shows a detailed machine learning model of predicting and estimating workplace stress, which addresses the increasing mental health epidemic where 81 percent of employees are affected by stress and 22.8 percent of adults are fighting mental illness. It created a hybrid multi-criteria meta-learner classifier by combining 4 heterogenous datasets, i.e., the OSMI Mental Health in Tech Surveys (2021–2022), the Sleep Health and Lifestyle Dataset and the CDC Diabetes Health Indicators Dataset, a total of 64,875 instances. It employed several supervised learning algorithms such as Logistic Regression, K-Nearest Neighbour, Decision Tree and Random Forest and then stacked them together using stacking methods. Performance of individual algorithms has been on a gradual increasing trend, the best results were produced by Logistic Regression with a accuracy of 92.64, KNN with a accuracy of 92.58, Decision Tree with an accuracy of 92.26 and the best among these was the results of the Random Forest with an accuracy of 94.97. The higher performance was sustained in the ensemble Stacked Model with accuracy rate of 94.97 as well as precision rate of 94.43, recall rate of 94.97 and F1-score stands at 94.34. The model outlined herein is effective in showing potentials of the ensemble machine learning methods in predicting stress at the workplace with over 94% accuracy in various measures of performance and high predictive capability that surpasses single algorithms. The paper is a validated instrument in identifying early stress in the work environment and proactive organisational responses to establish healthier workplaces by data-driven mental healthcare.

Title: Performance of Large Language Models in Oral Cancer Patient Education: An Evaluation of Reliability, Readability, and Patient Communication Quality
Abstract: Background: As society is increasingly depending on large language models (LLMs) for health-related questions, it is essential to objectively evaluate the quality and accessibility of the oral cancer information they provide. Although LLMs occupy a growing space in digital health communication, it remains unknown whether the information they generate is both reliable and easy to read. Objective: The purpose of this study was to evaluate the reliability and readability, respectively, of the responses generated by four mainstream LLMs (ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, and DeepSeek) to questions related to oral cancer. Specifically, the present authors aimed to evaluate the reliability of responses to common oral cancer questions and assess whether the readability of responses meets established expectations. Methods: Twenty-two commonly asked, patient-orientated oral cancer-related questions were developed through two predefined phases: Google Trends analysis and expert consultation with specialists in oral oncology. Each question was entered as an independent single-turn prompt into four LLMs: ChatGPT-5, Gemini 2.5, Perplexity Pro, and DeepSeek v3.2. The primary outcome was information reliability and quality, assessed using four standardized instruments: the DISCERN questionnaire, the Ensuring Quality Information for Patients (EQIP) tool, the Journal of the American Medical Association (JAMA) benchmark criteria, and the Global Quality Scale (GQS). The secondary outcome was readability, assessed using six established indices: the Automated Readability Index, Flesch Reading Ease Score, Gunning Fog Index, Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level, Coleman-Liau Index, and Simple Measure of Gobbledygook. Results: Significant differences were observed among the four LLMs in DISCERN, EQIP, and JAMA scores (all P < 0.001), whereas no significant difference was found in GQS scores (P = 0.440). Perplexity Pro achieved the highest mean DISCERN score (46.36 ± 4.70), EQIP score (85.00 ± 0.00), GQS score (4.05 ± 0.58), and JAMA score (1.00 ± 0.00). However, all models produced responses above the recommended sixth-grade readability level. The mean FKGL scores ranged from 12.65 ± 3.07 for ChatGPT-5 to 15.65 ± 3.36 for Perplexity Pro, and the mean FRES scores ranged from 37.50 ± 14.27 for Perplexity Pro to 52.59 ± 12.47 for Gemini 2.5. Conclusion: Current LLMs may support oral cancer patient education, but their use remains limited by variable information quality, insufficient transparency, and poor readability. Although Perplexity Pro performed better on several reliability-related metrics, no model showed consistently high performance across all dimensions or met recommended readability standards. Future LLM-based patient education tools should prioritise verifiable sourcing, guideline-based accuracy, risk communication, and plain-language adaptation.

Title: Fusing Spectral Intelligence with GeoAI: Machine Learning and Evolutionary Computing for Sustainable Soil Monitoring
Abstract: Long-term food security, climate resilience, and environmental preservation all depend on healthy soil. Traditional soil testing methods are accurate, but they present significant limitations: they are subjective, expensive, and create lab waste, which makes them challenging to scale and environmentally unsustainable. This work addresses a significant need in soil health evaluation: the necessity for real-time, non-invasive instruments. The current research established an innovative framework that integrates Laser-Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy (LIBS) with machine learning and geospatial analysis to provide accurate soil diagnostics in agricultural and industrial contexts. The goal is to develop a system that can utilise data to deliver accurate, scalable, and location-specific information regarding pollutants, nutrients, and soil composition. The methodology comprised several distinct phases. First, the LIBS data was mitigated by noise reduction, choosing features, and dimensionality reduction. Then, supervised and ensemble machine learning techniques were employed for the classification of spectral data. Finally, a multi-resolution GeoAI approach was employed to combine LIBS results with satellite images. The system design uses deep learning and genetic models to enhance regional predictive accuracy and combine data from the ground with data from satellites. The method works effectively to locate heavy metals, quantify both major and minor nutrients, and link the initial LIBS elements data with satellite plant indices and reflection patterns. The users may use this technology to manage nutrients, build high-resolution maps of soil, and estimate the probability of that the soil will become polluted, minimizing environmental impact. Field spectroscopy, machine learning, and remote sensing are all employed in this work to provide a tool that can be used in many ways and is highly extensible. This facilitates enhanced land stewardship. Consequently, AI-enabled toolsmay assist stakeholders in making decisions that will help with digital green efforts, environmental preservation, and make farming more precise.

Title: Edge-Deployed Vision Transformer Model for Automated Keratoconus Classification in Corneal Imaging
Abstract: Keratoconus is a non-inflammatory disease that results in bilateral, asymmetric, and progressive ectasia, characterized by corneal thinning, which often remains untreated from the time of diagnosis. A major factor in accounting for this delay has been the enormous reliance on traditional diagnostic tools, which commonly require expensive instruments. In this paper, we present an edge-computing mobile application for the automatic classification of keratoconus using a Vision Transformer (ViT) model. Images of the eye are captured laterally using a smartphone and then transmitted to a cloud server for analysis. ThingsSentral, which is hosted in the cloud, means that the AI model can be deployed and accessed remotely. The presented method provides a workflow that can sort input images into two classes, keratoconus or normal, and offers user-friendly functionality. The performance was tested using different learning rates with two optimizers (SGD and Adam) to compare. By learning at a learning rate of α = 0.005, the SGD optimizer achieved the best performance, yielding training accuracy of 96.67% and validation accuracy of 95.60%, with low training and validation losses (0.0986 and 0.2088, respectively). By contrast, the best performance was achieved for Adam at α = 0.001, achieving training accuracy of 96.55%, validation accuracy 98.90%, with corresponding losses of 0.0790, 0.0782. Adam was somewhat sensitive to changes in learning rate and showed significantly lower results at α = 0.005 and α = 0.01. The proposed edge-cloud framework displays how lightweight, smartphone-based deep learning applications can improve keratoconus screening in practical, particularly remote, resource-limited clinical situations.

Title: Perceived Generative AI risks and behavioral vulnerabilities: understanding cognitive and emotional pathways
Abstract: Purpose – Tools of generative artificial intelligence (Gen AI) have gained immense significance recently, particularly in higher education. While these tools enhance educational efficiency, there are still unanswered questions about the challenges of incorporating this technology into learning processes and its effects on academic outcomes, despite its promise to improve academic work. The purpose of this research is thus to address this gap by developing and validating a comprehensive scale covering perceived risks of Gen AI – such as hallucinations, dysfunctional AI use behavior and biases – and measuring their impact on students' academic performance. Design/methodology/approach – The study develops a scale through a three-step process. The study used a mixed-method approach to develop a scale on risks associated with Gen AI. The first step involved qualitative interviews to arrive at themes, followed by thematic analysis. Data were collected from students of diverse backgrounds and were subjected to exploratory factor analysis and confirmatory factor analysis. Lastly, we applied structural equation modeling using AMOS to validate the hypothesized relationships. Findings – The results indicated significant impacts of hallucinations, dysfunctional AI use behavior and biases on students' attitudes and perceived productivity, which in turn influence their academic performance. Originality/value – To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this study is the first to develop and validate a reliable scale to measure the challenges students encounter when using Gen AI tools and the associated risks. Drawing on the theory of epistemic risk, this study conceptualizes hallucinations, dysfunctional AI usage behavior and biases not merely as technical flaws but as epistemic predispositions that affect users' ability to improve their academic performance when interacting with Gen AI. Hence, this research translates and extends the theory of epistemic risk by converting abstract constructs into measurable instruments that can be validated across diverse contexts.

Title: Training the public health workforce for generative AI: validation of the Italian Chatbot Usability Questionnaire
Abstract: Introduction – Artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming increasingly relevant for public health practice. However, scalable training models and validated usability instruments for AI chatbots are still limited in non-English contexts. We aimed to (i) assess AI knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) among a sample of Italian public health professionals, and (ii) translate, culturally adapt, and psychometrically validate an Italian version of the Chatbot Usability Questionnaire (CUQ-IT) by applying it to a workshop-developed vaccination counseling chatbot. Methods – We conducted a three-phase study during the 57th Italian National Congress of Hygiene, Preventive Medicine and Public Health (Italy, October 2024): (i) use of an Italian translation and adaptation of the CUQ within a cross-sectional KAP survey; (ii) a 90-min theoretical-practical workshop with guided prompt engineering and collaborative development of a Custom GPT for vaccination counseling (VaxSense), followed by supervised interaction; (iii) post-workshop usability evaluation with CUQ-IT and psychometric testing. Construct adequacy was assessed using KMO and Bartlett's test. Internal consistency was estimated with Cronbach's α. Associations between KAP and usability ratings were explored. Results – Of 150 workshop attendees, 87 returned questionnaires (58%); 86 were eligible for KAP analyses, and 77 completed CUQ-IT for usability evaluation. Participants (mean age 35.9 ± 8.7; 55.8% females) reported moderate AI knowledge (mean 2.74 ± 1.05/5), positive attitudes (3.87 ± 0.73/5), and limited routine use (2.88 ± 1.11/5). CUQ-IT showed good sampling adequacy (KMO = 0.81) and significant item correlations (Bartlett's χ<sup>2</sup> (120) = 515.36, p-value <0.001). Internal consistency was high overall, with Cronbach's α = 0.881. The mean CUQ-IT usability score for VaxSense was 66.60 ± 15.29 (range 18.75–95.31). Participants with higher AI knowledge, more positive attitudes, and more frequent AI use tended to assign higher usability scores. Conclusion – In our sample of Italian public health professionals, moderate baseline AI knowledge, positive attitudes, and limited routine use of AI emerged, while the workshop-developed vaccination chatbot achieved overall good usability. The significant gender differences observed in both self-rated AI knowledge and usability scores indicated that “AI readiness” may be uneven, even within trained professional groups, underscoring the need for inclusive capacity-building strategies. In the public health sector, training should be framed as a component of safe implementation: strengthening the ability to critically appraise outputs, recognize common failure modes, mitigate bias and equity risks, and apply privacy-by-design principles. CUQ-IT demonstrated robust psychometric performance and represents a standardized tool to benchmark chatbot usability in Italian settings. Future work should confirm its measurement structure in larger samples and assess whether targeted training may reduce capability gaps and support appropriate and sustained use of AI in public health practice.

Title: Cost-Aware Multiwindow Ensemble Decision Support for Nonstationary Foreign Exchange Markets
Abstract: Financial markets are strongly nonstationary, making short-horizon foreign exchange decision support sensitive to estimation windows, feature design, and transaction costs. This paper proposes a transparent multiwindow ensemble framework in which interpretable multiregression experts use rolling-statistic features computed over different lookback windows. Time-scale diversity is combined with a supervisory layer that converts recent cost-aware utility scores into expert weights and selects execution thresholds on a meta window. The utility criterion is based on net pips after transaction costs and includes penalties for drawdown and turnover, while the execution rule incorporates volatility gating and minimum holding constraints. The framework is evaluated on synchronized one-minute quotes for 16 major currency pairs using a nonoverlapping walk-forward protocol. The benchmark set includes lag-based machine-learning models, LSTM, Transformer, Echo State Network, Bayesian model averaging, dynamic model averaging, stacking, and alternative multiexpert aggregation rules. In the main fixed-horizon experiment with τ = 15 minutes, the proposed utility-weighted ensemble achieves the highest mean Sharpe ratio of 1.085 and a mean net profit of 312.3 pips. The results support utility-calibrated time-scale diversification as an auditable approach to FX decision support under nonstationarity.

Title: The Impact of Large Language Model Integration on Cognitive Load and Metacognitive Strategies
Abstract: The integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) into educational and professional cognitive processes is transforming the ways in which individuals process information, make decisions, and regulate cognitive activity. Despite the rapid proliferation of LLM-based tools, their impact on cognitive load and metacognitive strategies remains insufficiently explored from an empirical perspective. The present quasi-experimental study aims to examine how the integration of LLMs influences intrinsic, extraneous, and germane cognitive load, as well as the planning, monitoring, and evaluation of one's own cognitive activity. The study involved 124 participants, divided into an experimental group (LLM integration) and a control group. The research instruments included the NASA-TLX cognitive workload scale, the Paas Cognitive Load Scale, and the Metacognitive Awareness Inventory (MAI). Statistical analysis incorporated ANCOVA, Structural Equation Modeling (SEM), and mediation analysis. The results demonstrate a statistically significant reduction in extraneous cognitive load when using LLMs (p < 0.01), accompanied by a redistribution of cognitive resources toward germane cognitive load. At the same time, structural changes in metacognitive monitoring were observed, including the strengthening of planning strategies and external regulation mechanisms. A mediation effect of cognitive load was identified in relation to the influence of LLM use on task performance. The present study contributes to the development of distributed cognition theory and Human-AI Interaction research by proposing an empirically grounded model of cognitive integration of LLMs in professional activity. Thus, the results of structural modeling confirm the hypothesis that the impact of LLMs on performance is primarily mediated through the redistribution of cognitive load and the activation of metacognitive regulatory mechanisms.

Title: Design and Teaching Practice of Virtual Simulation Experiment for Testing Ultra-High-Speed Electro-Optic Modulation Chips for Optoelectronic Information Major
Abstract: Objective Conventional experimental teaching methods for ultra-high-speed electro-optic modulation (UHS-EOM) chip testing face multiple challenges, including high equipment costs, expensive consumables, significant operational risks, and stringent requirements for cleanroom environments. These constraints severely limit the scalability of such experiments in undergraduate education. To address this issue, this paper designs and develops a virtual simulation-based experimental system for testing UHS-EOM chips. The system constructs corresponding 3D simulation models based on actual devices and chip structures. With reference to optical chip testing platforms, virtual simulation experiments are designed to cover key performance parameters of thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN)-based UHS-EOM chips, including half-wave voltage, electrical parameter, and electro-optic bandwidth test systems. Furthermore, an integrated online and offline hybrid teaching and assessment model encompassing “teaching–learning–practicing–evaluating” is introduced, enabling comprehensive experimental instruction across the full chain of “theory–design–fabrication–testing”. This approach provides scalable practical training in optical chip testing for undergraduate students in optoelectronics, while also offering a new pathway for pre-research technical training for graduate students entering relevant scientific laboratories. With the widespread application of 5G technology and the comprehensive deployment of large-scale artificial intelligence models, there are increasing demands for the speed and efficiency of information processing. The national strategy explicitly emphasizes deepening industry-academia-research collaboration in talent cultivation, encouraging relevant universities and research institutes to accelerate the training of innovative talents to meet the urgent needs of the optical chip industry. As a core component for achieving ultra-high-speed, large-capacity optical communication and optical computing, ultra-high-speed electro-optic modulator chips rely critically on their testing processes, which constitute one of the key manufacturing steps. For students in optoelectronic disciplines, mastering the knowledge and skills related to ultra-high-speed electro-optic modulator chip testing is essential for engaging with cutting-edge scientific research and adapting to the future development of the optoelectronic information industry. As such, training in UHS-EOM chip testing is not only a vital component of the innovative experimental curriculum for undergraduates but also a fundamental skill for graduate students entering related research laboratories. However, traditional experiments face significant limitations, including high costs, the need for ultra-precise experimental control, and lengthy operational procedures. These constraints restrict traditional offline UHS-EOM chip testing to research laboratories, severely hindering its application in large-scale innovative talent training. To address these challenges, we have designed and developed a virtual simulation teaching system for TFLN UHS-EOM chip testing. The testing content covers key performance parameters of UHS-EOM chips, such as half-wave voltage, electrical parameters, and electro-optic bandwidth. By integrating multi-dimensional innovative teaching methods, this system aims to cultivate students’ ability to solve optical chip testing challenges, enhance the quality of innovative talent cultivation in optoelectronic information disciplines, and better support the national strategy for strengthening the optoelectronic information industry. Methods This experimental teaching methodology adhered to the core concept of “promoting practice through virtual means and refining virtual simulation through practical application”. It established a comprehensive, closed-loop pedagogical framework encompassing “theoretical construction–virtual simulation–field practice–comprehensive evaluation”. The implementation began with a hybrid approach combining offline lectures and flipped classroom sessions to systematically impart core theoretical knowledge, including principles of optical communication, optical waveguides, and the operational mechanisms of TFLN modulator chips, supplemented by thematic seminars and debates. Concurrently, a virtual simulation platform for testing UHS-EOM chips was introduced, enabling students to deepen their understanding of testing procedures and instrument operation. To further facilitate the transfer of competence, students engaged in field practice at optoelectronic enterprises or collaborative laboratories, where they received guidance from industry mentors on chip testing processes and performed hands-on, high-precision tasks such as fiber-waveguide coupling and high-speed GSG radio frequency probe alignment in research laboratory settings, thereby bridging the gap from virtual cognition to practical skills. Finally, systematic assessment of learning outcomes was conducted through comprehensive experimental reports and multi-dimensional evaluations, forming an integrated “teaching–learning–practicing–evaluating” closed-loop system that effectively enhanced students’ comprehensive innovation and practical capabilities in the field of optical chip testing. Results and Discussions The technical architecture of this virtual simulation system was modeled and simulated based on the UHS-EOM chip testing platform of the Optical Waveguide Hybrid Integration and Micro-Nano Optoelectronic Devices Research Laboratory at Jinan University. It innovatively incorporated two critical virtual operation modules: fiber-waveguide manual coupling and manual alignment and electrode contacting using high-speed GSG radio frequency probes. Additionally, it integrated an online-offline hybrid teaching model that combines “instruction–learning–practice–evaluation” into a cohesive four-in-one pedagogical approach, supported by a multi-dimensional teaching assessment mechanism. Specific survey results indicated that over 95% of students provided positive evaluations (strongly agree and agree) for this virtual simulation experimental teaching. Furthermore, after virtual simulation training, the average total scores for the two practical experimental operations—fiber-waveguide manual coupling and high-speed GSG radio frequency probe alignment and electrode contact—improved from 85 to 94 points. The experimental duration was also reduced from over three class periods to within two class periods. Conclusions Starting from the necessity and advancement of developing a virtual simulation system for UHS-EOM chip testing, this paper elaborates on the platform’s process design, experimental content (including half-wave voltage, electrical parameters, and electro-optic bandwidth testing), and the corresponding experimental teaching model. Through the integrated teaching practice of “instruction–learning–practice–evaluation” involving both instructors and students, positive results have been achieved. This virtual simulation experimental teaching system not only effectively reduces experimental costs and supports large-scale teaching implementation, filling the gap in virtual simulation teaching for high-speed optical chip testing, but also helps broaden students’ perspectives on UHS-EOM chip testing processes, laying a crucial skill foundation for their future employment or further studies in research laboratories. This design contributes to cultivating innovative talents that meet the needs of scientific research and industrial development in the field of optoelectronic information, and holds positive significance for advancing the progress of the optoelectronic information industry.

Title: Artificial Intelligence and Big Data as a Key Driver of Digitalization in Natural Resource Management in Central Asian Countries
Abstract: The digitalization of natural resource management is becoming a key factor in enhancing the sustainability of socio-economic development under conditions of global environmental threats and increasing anthropogenic pressure. For the countries of Central Asia, characterized by a high dependence on water and land resources, the transboundary nature of water systems, and institutional fragmentation in governance structures, the implementation of digital transformation is of particular relevance. The aim of this study is to provide a comprehensive scientific assessment of the potential of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Big Data technologies in advancing the digitalization of natural resource management in the region. The methodological framework integrates satellite-based Earth observation data, climate reanalysis datasets, hydrological monitoring records, and administrative data within a Data Lake-Lakehouse architecture. Machine learning and deep learning methods, including ensemble models and recurrent neural networks, were employed for analysis and forecasting, complemented by explainable AI tools (SHAP). Spatio-temporal validation and uncertainly assessment ensured the robustness and reliability of the obtained results. The findings demonstrate that intelligent models significantly improve the accuracy of hydrological and climatic forecasting compared to traditional statistical approaches, while also identifying high-risk zones of water scarcity, land degradation, and desertification. Spatial analysis of land-use change and NDVI dynamics confirmed substantial land cover transformations driven by the combined effects of climatic and anthropogenic factors. The application of SHAP analysis enhanced model transparency and enabled the linkage between key contributing factors and policy-relevant management decisions. Within the discussion framework, a roadmap for implementing digital platforms for natural resource governance is proposed, along with practical recommendations at both national and regional levels. The results confirm that digitalization of natural resource management based on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence can serve as an effective instrument for strengthening resilience, adaptability, and policy coherence in Central Asian countries.

Title: We don’t care how much you sweat: An epistemic framework for behavioral and brain science laboratory infrastructure
Abstract: For decades, behavioral and brain research has advanced by isolating single variables or brain regions to study behavior and performance. However, it has become increasingly clear that reductionist methods struggle to capture the complex, dynamic, and context-dependent nature of human behavior. Developments in data analysis and artificial intelligence now enable unprecedented insights into complex datasets. Yet, while different strands of reform literature have advanced how we theorize, measure, and analyze, the infrastructural conditions under which data are generated, the laboratory, have received comparatively little conceptual attention. Here, devices are often siloed, proprietary, or limited to aggregated outputs, thereby constraining the questions that can be addressed. In this paper, we offer an epistemic framework for reasoning about laboratory infrastructure at the scale of the whole laboratory, understood not as a collection of individual instruments but as an integrated infrastructure in which multiple hardware systems co-exist, communicate, and jointly support the questions a research group can ask. Conceptually, we think of measurements in three epistemic layers: the surface layer (raw numeric outputs, e.g., from an electrodermal sensor), the proxy layer (physiological or behavioral subsystems, e.g., sweat gland activity), and the target layer (emergent phenomena or constructs such as working memory capacity, arousal or effort). These layers are epistemic in that they describe how meaning is inferred from signals and the type of losses and mismatches that can occur at or between them; e.g., when we study arousal or effort, we don’t care about sweat gland activity per se, but rather as an imperfect intermediate proxy. We derive from these layers a practical rating scheme across seven infrastructure properties: signal digitization, signal fidelity, temporal alignment, real-time access, interoperability, transparency, and flexibility. Researchers can use these to evaluate and optimize their laboratory across modalities. Our framework complements existing modality-specific standards and community-developed integration tools by providing a shared decision logic at the scale of the lab as a whole.

Title: Predicting Educational Outcomes Using Artificial Intelligence
Abstract: In the context of the digital transformation of education and the rapid expansion of online learning systems, the problem of early prediction of educational outcomes has become strategically important. Modern approaches to educational data analysis, such as Educational Data Mining (EDM) and Learning Analytics, enable the development of highly accurate predictive models. However, many of these models operate as “black boxes,” limiting the transparency of decision-making processes and reducing trust among educators and educational administrators. In this regard, Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) is increasingly recognized as a key instrument for improving the interpretability, ethical compliance, and practical applicability of machine learning models in education. The objective of this study is to develop and interpret a predictive model for student academic performance using XAI methodologies. The research applies a comparative analysis of Random Forest, XGBoost, and neural network algorithms, combined with interpretability techniques including SHAP, LIME, and Partial Dependence Plots (PDP). The study is based on a comprehensive educational dataset that includes academic performance indicators, demographic characteristic s, and digital behavioral metric s extracted from Learning Management Sy stem (LMS) platforms. The findings indicate that gradient boosting models provide the highest predictive accuracy (ROC-AUC > 0.89). However, the integration of SHAP analysis enables the identification of key predictors of academic performance, including LMS interaction intensity, prior academic achievements, and behavioral engagement patterns. The interpretability analysis also reveals nonlinear relationships between study time investment and final academic performance. The practical significance of the study lies in establishing a methodological foundation for the development of transparent early-warning systems for academic risk detection, which can support evidence-based decision-making in educational institutions. The results further highlight the importance of integrating algorithmic fairness and AI ethics principles into educational analytics systems.

Title: Multi-Step Ahead Traffic State Prediction Using a Stochastic Residual Long Short-Term Memory and Temporal Dilated Attention Mechanism
Abstract: Accurate multi-step prediction is crucial for anticipating future traffic conditions, but existing models frequently encounter performance degradation due to external noise and error accumulation over longer prediction horizons. This study presents a multi-step-ahead traffic state prediction model that combines stochastic residual long short-term memory (SResLSTM) networks with a temporal dilated attention (TDA) mechanism to address these challenges. The SResLSTM architecture mitigates vanishing or exploding gradient issues, facilitates learning long-term temporal dependencies, and improves network training efficiency. It also incorporates Gaussian noise with the inputs to enhance the model's robustness. The TDA mechanism comprises multi-scale causal convolutions, multi-head attention, and gated residual fusion to enhance the model's prediction accuracy by dynamically assigning relevant weights to different time steps, thereby capturing the temporal variability essential for precise multi-step prediction. This research also proposes a Fourier denoise filter (FDF) using a learnable frequency-domain denoising technique to suppress high-frequency noise from the input data. The proposed model was evaluated using three benchmark traffic flow and speed datasets: the PEMS, PEMS-BAY, and METR-LA datasets. Extensive experiments demonstrated good performance improvements across different prediction lengths on all three datasets compared to the baselines, such as a 6.97%, 10.16%, and 0.55% enhancement in terms of mean absolute error, root mean squared error, and (Formula presented.) score, respectively, for a prediction horizon of 60 min based on the PEMS-BAY dataset. It also demonstrated enhanced robustness to rare events, random sensor dropouts, and adversarial attacks of various magnitudes. However, the model requires moderate computational resources, with a training time of 491.22 s on the PEMS dataset and a larger convergence time than the baselines. Additionally, the good outcomes of the conducted generalizability test on the European road freight transport flow dataset further verified the proposed model's worthiness.

Title: Faculty Members’ Acceptance of Digital Knowledge Management through AI-based Learning Management Systems in Universities according to the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology
Abstract: This study aimed to investigate the degree of faculty members’ acceptance of digital knowledge management through Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based Learning Management Systems (LMS) in Jordanian universities, based on the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT). The researchers adopted a descriptive-analytical approach to assess the effectiveness of AI-based LMS as an independent variable on the dependent variable of digital knowledge management. A questionnaire was used as the primary data collection instrument and was distributed randomly through Google applications to a sample of 320 faculty members from universities in northern Jordan. The study results indicated that faculty members exhibited a high level of acceptance of digital knowledge management through AI-based e-learning systems. Furthermore, the findings revealed that key UTAUT constructs—performance expectancy, effort expectancy, social influence, and facilitating conditions—had a significant positive impact on faculty members’ intention to use AI-based LMS for digital knowledge management. The researchers recommend encouraging faculty members to integrate AI applications into educational management, particularly in digital knowledge management, while considering theoretical models such as UTAUT to enhance adoption and implementation.

Title: Towards optimised perishable inventory systems: integrating time-temperature indicators with deep reinforcement learning
Abstract: Time-Temperature Indicators (TTIs) can improve the control of perishable temperature-regulated products in cold-chain operations. Companies monitor product quality and temperature over the full cold-chain process, and TTIs provide visual signals indicating product freshness. This study develops a periodic-review temperature-sensitive perishable inventory model that integrates TTIs and Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) within a high-dimensional Markov decision process. We implement Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) to learn ordering policies that capture multi-period inventory aging and demand uncertainty. Through numerical experiments, we compare PPO against a base-stock policy and a projected inventory level policy in TTI-enabled and non-TTI settings. PPO achieves the highest mean performance overall and in almost all tested configurations, with the PPO advantage increasing as deterioration becomes faster. Comparing systems with and without TTIs shows profit gains up to about 45%. The value of TTI information depends on deterioration rate, green/yellow demand mix, and whether replenishment responds to the green/yellow stock mix. TTIs are more beneficial when the deterioration-generated stock mix is close to demand. Profit may decrease when this alignment breaks down, either because too many items move to yellow while demand remains mainly green, or because yellow demand arises before enough stock has moved from green to yellow.

Title: Developing and validating a domain-specific instrument for measuring physical education teachers’ acceptance of artificial intelligence: the AI-PEQ
Abstract: Introduction – The growing integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into educational settings has created an urgent need for psychometrically validated instruments capable of measuring educators' acceptance of AI-enhanced tools within specific disciplinary contexts. In Physical Education (PE), this need is particularly acute; despite the proliferation of AI-supported technologies such as motion capture systems, biomechanical feedback platforms, and adaptive performance analytics, no validated domain-specific scale existed to assess PE teachers' acceptance of such tools before this study. This paper reports the development and psychometric validation of the AI in Physical Education Questionnaire (AI-PEQ), a new instrument designed to measure PE teachers' acceptance of AI across five theoretically grounded constructs: AI Awareness, Perceived Educational Value, Ethical Considerations, Perceived Curriculum Integration Feasibility, and Behavioral Intention. Methods – Drawing on the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT), item generation followed a systematic, literature-informed procedure. The instrument was subsequently subjected to Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA) and Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA), with reliability assessed through Cronbach's alpha and composite reliability indices. Data were collected from a sample of 230 in-service PE teachers in Egypt. Results – Findings confirmed a robust five-factor structure with satisfactory model fit, strong internal consistency across all subscales, and evidence of convergent, discriminant, and criterion-related validity, including significant correlations with established TAM and UTAUT reference scales and predictive associations with self-reported AI use behaviors. Discussion – The validated AI-PEQ provides researchers and practitioners with a reliable, context-sensitive tool for diagnosing barriers and facilitators of AI adoption in PE, thereby enabling evidence-informed professional development and institutional planning. The study contributes to the emerging scholarship on technology-enhanced physical education by providing the field's first validated instrument for measuring AI acceptance and offers a replicable methodological framework adaptable to other specialist education contexts.

Title: The economics of evolutionary programming
Abstract: In this paper, we present an economic model of evolutionary computation technologies, highlighting how alternative propertization and liability mechanisms shape the balance between “exploration” and “exploitation” in evolutionary research. We consider two interrelated effects of evolutionary experimentation: (i) the positive externalities that occur when superior mutations enhance performance, benefitting all subsequent implementations of the algorithm; (ii) the negative externalities that arise when inferior mutations cause harm. Our analysis reveals that experimentation reaches the optimal stopping point only with a combined use of propertization and liability instruments. If intellectual property frameworks fail to propertize benefits from evolutionary processes, limiting liability may be a second-best means of encouraging experimentation.

Title: Interpretable machine learning for hikikomori screening: The adaptive HRI-15
Abstract: Hikikomori, or prolonged social withdrawal, is an issue of global relevance. The HRI-15 is a brief tool for its assessment. This study enhances its utility by adding clinical thresholds to identify risk and person-centered clinical profiles, and by developing a machine-learning(ML)–based computerized adaptive test (CAT) to enable rapid screening. Data from a national survey of Italian adolescents (N = 8,755) were used to conduct ROC analysis and latent profile analysis (LPA). The findings indicated that a score of ≥ 42 achieved optimal classification performance, and four profiles with distinct meanings and systematic differences in anxiety, depression, impulsivity, and risk behaviors were identified. A multivariate conditional inference tree was estimated to develop an ML-based adaptive version of the instrument. The CAT reduced administered items by 53% (7.03/15), accurately reproducing full-length scores (r = .77–.997) and the corresponding classification; alignment was assessed with latent transition analysis (entropy = .96). The procedure was integrated into an application supporting administration, scoring, and reporting (score, risk, profiles, graphs). Combining a cross-validated cutoff and clinically useful profiles with CAT and its automated administration and reporting application strengthens triage and personalization, enabling large-scale, multidomain screening and earlier intervention for hikikomori risk.

Title: Enhancing Demand Fulfillment in Metal-Mechanical MSEs Using DDMRP and Holt-Winters with ML Residual Correction
Abstract: Peru's metalworking MSEs face significant demand fulfillment challenges. CREATEM S.A.C., an automotive spare parts manufacturer, achieves only 47.99% OTIF - well below the 80% industry benchmark - resulting in annual losses of S/ 103,145.40. Since MYPEs make up 99.2% of the enterprises in the metalworking sector, which contributes 11.2% of the national manufacturing GDP, it is critical to optimize their management. The issue has been tackled in earlier studies using forecasting and techniques like DDMRP. Regarding the resources accessible to micro and small businesses, these instruments are constrained. To enhance demand fulfilment, the model combines machine learning algorithms with forecasting techniques like Holt-Winters, exponential smoothing, etc. with the DDMRP approach. Over an eight-month period, simulations were used for validation. The primary outcome was a MAPE of less than 20% and an increase in OTIF to 88%. The outcomes show that the concept works well for enhancing the sector's ability to meet demand.

Title: Signer-Independent Indian Sign Language Recognition Via Deep Vision Transformers
Abstract: Real-time sign language recognition and translation systems can often suffer from degraded performance when exposed to new, unseen signers due to differences in hand morphology, skin tone, motion dynamics, and the style of signing. These challenges severely limit the ability to deploy the system across heterogeneous user populations. In this work, we propose a signer-independent, real-time Indian Sign Language recognition and translation framework, which translates gestures directly into text and speech. The proposed architecture integrates pose-based skeletal feature extraction along with appearance normalization with adversarial feature disentanglement and spatiotemporal Transformer modelling to facilitate robust generalization across diverse signers. Our architecture uses a dual-stream input: a pose stream, encoding geometric motion as hand, facial, and upper body key points, while an appearance stream captures the non-manual cues from RGB frames. The extensive data augmentation and adaptive normalization mimic the signer diversity of the real world. Moreover, a gradient reversal adversarial branch adds invariance to the signer identity of the learned embeddings. It is further enhanced by the contrastive loss function, which aligns the representations of identical signs across subjects. The core neural architecture is based on a spatiotemporal Transformer encoder decoder that decodes the sequential features into textual glosses, synthesized into speech using a TTS module. Extensive experimental evaluation on strictly signerindependent protocols demonstrates superior recognition accuracy, robustness to visual variation, and low latency in inference, therefore underlining the framework for real-world applications in inclusive communication for the Deaf and Hardof-Hearing community.

Title: Comparison of Traditional Machine Learning Models and Large Language Models for Multi-Label Text Classification on X (Twitter)
Abstract: Social media platform X (Twitter) is a major source of public information across domains such as technology, education, and health. However, its short and informal text poses challenges for natural language processing (NLP). This study applies a Large Language Model (LLM)-based approach for multi-label text classification on X (Twitter) data covering six domains: Artificial Intelligence and Technology, Education, Music and Film, Sports, Health, and Finance. Data were collected via the Twitter API using keyword filters, followed by preprocessing steps including text normalization, URL removal, and language detection. The baseline models-KNN, Naïve Bayes, and Random Forest-used TF-IDF features and were compared with LLMs through zero-shot and fine-tuning approaches. Experimental results show that fine-tuned LLMs significantly improved accuracy and generalization compared to traditional models. However, among all tested models, Random Forest achieved the best performance with an Micro-F1: 0.612, Macro-F1: 0.568, Hamming Loss: 0.096, making it the most effective model in this study. These findings highlight the potential of LLMs and traditional machine learning integration for real-time public conversation analysis on social media.
