Title: AI-Assisted Analysis of Guzheng Performance Body Movements: Innovation Through Motion Recognition Technology
Abstract: This study investigates the application of motion recognition technology in guzheng performance training and evaluates its potential for improving the preservation, standardization, and innovation of traditional instrumental performance. An MPU9250 inertial sensing system was deployed at 13 key body nodes to collect multidimensional motion data, including acceleration, angular velocity, and magnetic field intensity. Quaternion modeling, Euler-angle conversion, preprocessing, and coordinate transformation were used to construct a body-movement dataset for guzheng performance and to characterize key action features. Experimental validation was conducted through both motion capture simulation and teaching practice. In the simulation test, the average recognition accuracies for three performers were 74.42%, 73.77%, and 64.45%, respectively, indicating that the proposed approach can effectively capture the initial stages of performance movements, although accuracy decreases in later frames because of cumulative errors. Processing times ranged from 490.00 s to 566.57 s. In the teaching experiment, students trained with motion recognition assistance outperformed those receiving traditional instruction, particularly in expressiveness, spatial awareness, endurance, and rhythmic performance. The results demonstrate that motion recognition technology can provide objective evaluation, visualized feedback, and personalized guidance for guzheng training, offering a feasible technical path for the digital preservation and intelligent development of traditional Chinese music performance.

Title: Improvement of Spatial Non-Uniformity of Pulse-Dilation Framing Camera Using SPLANF
Abstract: The pulse-dilation framing camera (PDFC) serves as a critical ultrafast diagnostic instrument in inertial confinement fusion (ICF) experiments, where its imaging performance is significantly degraded by axisymmetric non-uniform magnetic fields. This degradation induces severe spatial non-uniformity (SNU), characterized by blurred fine structures and a pronounced spatial variation in stripe contrast. While conventional hardware-based optimization strategies offer partial mitigation of SNU, they often entail increased system complexity, high implementation costs, and the risk of introducing additional disturbances. Recent advances in deep learning have opened new avenues for image restoration and fusion; however, most existing approaches rely on local blur kernel assumptions and thus fail to adequately address the non-local, globally continuous blurring effects arising from the three-dimensional helical trajectories of photoelectrons in PDFC. Therefore, developing a deep fusion framework capable of adaptively correcting SNU in a label-free manner holds substantial theoretical significance and practical engineering value—both for enhancing the spatial resolution of PDFC systems and for advancing intelligent ultrafast diagnostics through data-driven methodologies. This paper proposes stripe-perception with location-aware nested architecture for image fusion (SPLANF), a novel self-supervised learning model designed to address SNU in PDFC imaging. Built upon a U-Net backbone renowned for its effectiveness in image-to-image translation tasks, SPLANF features a nested fusion framework that integrates a dual-input encoder (DIE) for multi-scale feature extraction and a single-input decoder (SCD) for coherent image reconstruction. The model incorporates two specialized attention modules tailored to distinct aspects of the degradation process. The stripe-perception attention module (SPAM) is specifically engineered to recover orientation-sensitive stripe patterns obscured by anisotropic blur. It employs a dual-path convolutional structure operating in horizontal and vertical directions to explicitly extract directional features, thereby enhancing the discrimination and reconstruction of high-frequency structural details crucial for resolution assessment. The second module, the location-aware attention module (LAAM), addresses the spatial variability of image degradation. By combining global height-wise and width-wise pooling with channel interaction mechanisms, LAAM dynamically generates spatial weight maps that encode the position-dependent intensity of blur, effectively modeling the non-uniform response across the image plane induced by magnetic field gradients. A key advantage of SPLANF lies in its self-supervised training paradigm, eliminating the need for paired ground-truth data—a major practical limitation in experimental settings. The model is optimized end-to-end using a composite loss function composed of a pixel-level loss term and a structural similarity loss term, weighted by a coefficient γ. Empirical evaluation determines the optimal balance when the weighting coefficient is set to 5000. To enhance generalization and domain-specific feature learning, training leverages a hybrid dataset: the diverse MS-COCO public dataset is combined with a custom-built dataset containing 47 real captured PDFC images and 20000 synthetically generated local stripe patches. These synthetic samples are carefully designed to simulate the physics-driven degradation characteristics of the PDFC system, ensuring alignment between learned features and actual imaging conditions. Comprehensive experimental evaluations demonstrate that SPLANF achieves significant improvements in both visual quality and quantitative performance metrics. In terms of local detail recovery, the model successfully restores the originally degraded 5 lp/mm stripe patterns. At representative positions D₁, D₂, and D₃, the mean modulation (MMD) increases from baseline values of 1.1, 3.3, and 1.8 to enhanced levels of 3.3, 8.4, and 7.6, respectively, indicating effective contrast restoration. For global spatial uniformity, the range of gradient standard deviation (GSD) narrows from 6.53–43.75 to 11.64–39.77. More importantly, the total variance of gradient standard deviation (TVGSD) decreases from 87.37 to 49.71, confirming suppression of both localized and systemic non-uniformities. Ablation studies validate the complementary roles of SPAM and LAAM: when used independently, SPAM enhances central-region textures but performs poorly at image boundaries. In contrast, LAAM improves edge-awareness but sacrifices central detail fidelity. Only their joint integration delivers balanced, high-fidelity restoration across the entire field of view. Comparative analysis against state-of-the-art fusion algorithms—including deep perception enhancement-multi exposure fusion (DPE-MEF), image fusion convolutional neural network (IFCNN), low-rank representation network (LRRNet), unsupervised unified image fusion network (U2Fusion), and self-supervised mask-optimization fusion (SMF)—reveals that SPLANF achieves superior restoration performance, particularly in off-axis regions such as D₃. This marked advantage underscores its unique capability to model the underlying physics-informed, spatially variant degradation mechanism, surpassing generic methods that lack explicit structural and positional awareness. This study presents SPLANF, a self-supervised deep learning framework that effectively corrects SNU in magnetic focusing PDFC imaging through the synergistic integration of stripe-perception and location-aware attention mechanisms. Without requiring ground-truth labels, the model achieves adaptive and accurate SNU correction, yielding substantial improvements in both visual clarity and quantitative metrics such as MMD and TVGSD. These results systematically confirm its superior restoration capability. SPLANF establishes a new technical pathway for image quality enhancement in ultrafast diagnostics, overcoming the limitations of hardware-centric solutions and conventional algorithmic approaches. It also lays a solid theoretical and experimental foundation for integrating deep learning with physical priors in precision imaging systems. Future work will focus on three directions: lightweight model design for real-time deployment, construction of a multi-modal evaluation framework for comprehensive performance assessment, and refinement of physics-informed synthetic data generation to further improve model robustness, practicality, and cross-scenario generalization.

Title: Cross-Domain Drone Audio Classification: A Comparative Domain Transfer Study
Abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) pose security concerns due to potential malicious use. Audio-based detection systems provide effective solutions, but face significant domain shift challenges in real-world deployment, which compromises their generalization capability across different domains in practical deployments. To tackle the domain shift problem, this study proposes a comprehensive domain adaptation framework evaluating five methodologies for drone detection across-domains: baseline machine learning (ML) such as SVM, baseline deep learning (DL) such as neural networks, enhanced ML with maximum mean discrepancy (MMD), DL integrated with MMD, and Domain advanced neural networks (DANN). The framework employs 234-dimensional feature extraction encompassing MFCCs, mel-spectrograms, chroma features, spectral characteristics, and temporal properties across source domains (FT2D, HPSS, RepetSim) and target domain (Public dataset). The system addresses class imbalance through SMOTE-Tomek resampling and incorporates four-fold augmentation techniques (Gaussian noise, time stretching, pitch shifting, volume variation) to enhance cross-domain transfer. MMD enables explicit domain alignment through multi-scale kernel computation and adaptive instance weighting, while DANN employs adversarial training with gradient reversal for domain-invariant feature learning. This study shows that MMD-enhanced ML outperforms (16-21%) baseline methods by 48-83 percentage points, achieving 99.75% accuracy in five-fold cross-validation. To verify the superiority and stability of our approach, paired t-tests were conducted. The results show significant improvements (p¡0.001) for both MMD+Aug ML and MMD+Aug DL compared with baseline, confirming consistently more efficient performance.

Title: Intelligent quantification of piano performance quality via bidirectional long short-term memory networks
Abstract: Piano performance evaluation is a key component of music education, yet traditional teacher-based assessment is limited by subjectivity, inconsistent standards, delayed feedback, and poor scalability, motivating the need for an objective, automated scoring method. This study proposed a bidirectional long short-term memory network (BiLSTM) with an attention mechanism for automatic piano performance scoring. Five features, including pitch, rhythm, dynamics, pedal usage, and expressiveness, were extracted from MIDI data and reduced from 142 to 100 dimensions before model input. BiLSTM captured bidirectional temporal dependencies, while attention highlighted critical segments for five-level classification. Experiments on 10,000 MIDI samples achieved 0.873 accuracy under five-fold cross-validation, with precision, recall and F1-score of 0.865, 0.858 and 0.861, respectively. Ablation results showed improvements over LSTM (0.081) and BiLSTM (0.031), confirming the effectiveness of attention and strong generalisation on unseen pieces (≥ 0.851).

Title: Large language models versus expert clinicians in optimizing Chinese patient education materials for temporomandibular disorders: a mixed-methods study integrating readability, accuracy, actionability, and cultural adaptability
Abstract: Objective – To evaluate the performance of large language models (LLMs) and expert clinicians in optimizing Chinese patient education materials (PEMs) for temporomandibular disorders (TMD) across readability, accuracy, actionability, and cultural adaptability, and to determine whether a human-AI collaboration model can achieve an optimal balance among these dimensions. Methods – Fifteen TMD education topics were selected through a Delphi consensus process. Four groups of PEMs were generated: original texts (Group A), LLM-rewritten texts (Group B, Claude Opus 4.6), clinician-rewritten texts (Group C), and human-AI collaboration texts (Group D). Blinded assessments were conducted by a professional panel (n = 3) and a health literacy-stratified patient panel (n = 6). Readability was measured by sentence length and common character proportion, accuracy by 5-point expert ratings against standardized checklists, actionability by the PEMAT instrument, and cultural adaptability by qualitative thematic analysis. Prompt sensitivity was tested across three distinct styles. Results – LLM-rewritten texts demonstrated significantly shorter sentences (21.1 vs. 33.9 characters, p < 0.001) and substantially higher actionability (95.6% vs. 16.7%, p < 0.001) compared with original texts. Clinician-rewritten texts achieved the highest accuracy (4.48 vs. 3.23, p < 0.001) but low actionability (46.7%). The human-AI collaboration model matched clinician accuracy (4.49, p = 1.000) while preserving LLM actionability (95.6%), with 72% less clinician time. Sensitivity analysis confirmed actionability robustness under empathetic and authoritative prompts but attenuation under a concise prompt. Qualitative analysis identified four cultural adaptability themes, with LLMs excelling in terminology localization and behavioral structuring but showing limitations in TCM conceptual depth. Conclusion – The human-AI collaboration model represents a promising and balanced approach for producing Chinese TMD patient education materials, combining LLM strengths in structural optimization with expert clinician oversight for accuracy and cultural appropriateness.

Title: Development and validation of an interpretable machine-learning-based model incorporating time-weighted variables for predicting intensive care unit mortality in patients with cardiac arrest: A retrospective study
Abstract: Background: Cardiac arrest (CA) remains a critical medical emergency characterized by high mortality rates despite the advancements in resuscitation and intensive care. The heterogeneous and evolving clinical course of patients with CA hinders early and accurate prognostication. We aimed to construct and externally validate a predictive model for 28-day intensive care unit (ICU) mortality in patients with CA by leveraging time-weighted clinical data and traditional and machine-learning approaches including extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), gradient boosting with component-wise linear models (Glmboost), random forest (RF), generalized linear models with elastic net regularization (Glmnet), and multivariate Cox regression. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed adult patients with CA from three large-scale ICU databases: eICU Collaborative Research Database (training cohort, n = 1,077), Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV v3.1), and MIMIC-III Clinical Database CareVue subset v1.4 (combined validation cohort, n = 368). Time-weighted averages (TWA) of clinical parameters—including the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS), vital signs, and arterial blood gas indices—were computed over the first three ICU days. Variable selection was performed using the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression, followed by multivariable Cox regression analysis. Five prognostic models—Glmboost, XGBoost, RF, Glmnet, and Cox regression—were developed and evaluated using C-index, time-dependent area under the curve (AUC), Graf score, and decision curve analysis. Model interpretability and time-varying effects were examined via SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and Piece-wise exponential additive mixed model (PAMM). Results: Nine independent predictors of ICU mortality were identified, with TWA Glasgow Coma Scale (TWA-GCS) (hazard ratio: 0.75, 95% CI: 0.71–0.78, P < 0.01) and duration of mechanical ventilation (hazard ratio: 0.72, 95% CI: 0.69–0.75, P < 0.01) showing the strongest associations. In external validation, the Glmboost model showed the lowest Graf score. SHAP analyses underscored TWA-GCS and duration of mechanical ventilation as the most impactful variables. PAMM analysis revealed an increasingly protective temporal effect of higher TWA-GCS values. Subgroup analysis showed 28-day ICU mortality rates of 76%, 57%, and 32% in patients with low (< 4), moderate (4–10), and high (> 10) TWA-GCS scores, respectively (P < 0.01). Conclusion: Incorporating time-weighted clinical data significantly improves ICU mortality prediction in patients with CA. Glmboost showed the best calibration/error-related performance based on Graf score while demonstrating comparable discrimination, with TWA-GCS identified as a key prognostic factor.

Title: Subseasonal forecasts of the MJO and convectively coupled equatorial waves in ACCESS-S2 and GraphCast: A multi-year analysis
Abstract: The Madden–Julian Oscillation (MJO) and convectively coupled equatorial waves are fundamental drivers of tropical precipitation variability at subseasonal-to-seasonal (S2S) time-scales, yet their accurate prediction remains challenging for S2S forecasting systems. This study evaluates the predictive skill of two contrasting approaches—the dynamical Australian Community Climate and Earth-System Simulator–Seasonal version 2 (ACCESS-S2) and the machine-learning (ML)-based GraphCast—in forecasting the MJO, equatorial Rossby (ER), Kelvin, and mixed Rossby–gravity (MRG) waves across the Tropics. Using 38 years of hindcast data (1981–2018) with 42-day lead times, we apply wavenumber–frequency filtering techniques to precipitation and assess forecast performance against observed precipitation estimates from the Multi-Source Weighted-Ensemble Precipitation (MSWEP). Although the evaluation period overlaps with GraphCast's training data (1979–2021) and may favor its performance, it enables assessment across decades of climate variability and highlights the core strengths and limitations of each modeling approach. Our results reveal distinct complementary capabilities between the two models: ACCESS-S2 demonstrates better skill for longer-time-scale phenomena, maintaining meaningful correlations ((Formula presented.)) for MJO forecasts up to 21 days over the Maritime Continent during boreal summer (April–September) and the Indian Ocean during boreal winter (October–March) and between 9 and 16 days for ER waves across different tropical basins. In contrast, GraphCast shows better performance for shorter-time-scale wave prediction, achieving 6–9 days of skill, defined as (Formula presented.), for Kelvin waves and 4–8 days for MRG waves. However, both models systematically underestimate precipitation amplitude across all wave types, particularly over the Maritime Continent and Pacific regions. Phase-speed biases, in contrast, remain small (below 20%), suggesting that forecast degradation is driven primarily by loss of wave coherence rather than propagation errors. These findings highlight complementary capabilities that could inform hybrid ensemble forecasting strategies for improved S2S equatorial wave and tropical precipitation predictions.

Title: Interpretable multimodal machine learning for injury risk stratification in adolescent athletes: integrating kinematic, physiological, and load data with SHAP/LIME explainability
Abstract: Adolescent athletes (aged 13–18 years) face significantly elevated lower-limb injury risk compared to adult populations due to immature neuromuscular control, while existing injury risk assessment methods are broadly limited by single-modal reliance, insufficient model interpretability, and a lack of dedicated research targeting youth populations. This study proposes an interpretable multimodal machine learning framework that integrates three data modalities—kinematics, physiology, and training load—via feature-level concatenation, based on a cross-sectional multimodal dataset of 320 fully anonymised adolescent athletes comprising 12 feature variables acquired under standardized protocols using internationally recognized instruments, including Vicon optical motion capture, AMTI force platforms, Polar H10 heart rate monitors, Supersonic Imagine Aixplorer ultrasound elastography, and Catapult GPS trackers. Through 5-fold stratified cross-validation, the comprehensive performance of five traditional and five modern/deep machine learning models was systematically compared in a binary injury risk stratification task. Experimental results demonstrate that logistic regression achieved the best overall performance [Accuracy = 86.9%, AUC-ROC = 0.965, F1 = 0.866, Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) = 0.742]. Dual interpretability analysis was further conducted on the optimal model using a SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) linear explainer and a Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME) local explainer; both methods consistently identified peak hip adduction angle (mean |SHAP| = 2.208), ankle dorsiflexion range of motion (1.426), and dynamic knee valgus angle (1.359) as the most critical injury risk predictors (Spearman ρ = 0.93), in high agreement with established biomechanical findings in sports medicine. An ablation analysis of modality contributions demonstrated that the tri-modal integration achieved a substantive AUC gain over single-modality configurations, supporting the value of multimodal feature integration. We note explicitly that the binary risk label was derived from a clinically-informed weighted composite of the input features rather than from prospective injury follow-up; the framework therefore performs risk stratification with respect to this composite, and validation against true prospective injury outcomes remains an important next step. This study provides an interpretable technical framework for standardized, digitized, and stratified injury risk assessment in adolescent athletes, with important potential for clinical translation and sports injury prevention practice.

Title: Depression Detection in Speech Using Wav2Vec 2.0 Feature Extraction
Abstract: Depression, a common and highly disabling mental health condition, is known to impair emotional and cognitive functioning. Traditional diagnostic techniques are frequently time-consuming, subjective and not available in resource-limited settings. This work takes advantage of new capacity in audio signal processing and self-supervised learning to investigate a novel framework for automatic depression detection with vocal biomarkers. The approach employs Wav2Vec 2.0 to extract discriminative speech embeddings from the DAIC-WOZ dataset and presents multiple deep learning pipelines- e.g., MLP, CNN, LSTM and an ensemble of CNN + MLP for binary prediction of depression. The audio data is preprocessed by stripping away interviewer speech, silences and noise, afterward segmented to chunk-frames to overcome class imbalance. Our experiments demonstrate that the CNN + MLP ensemble can achieve a high accuracy of 95%, and balanced precision-recall scores for both classes, warranting its consideration as a potential candidate for usage in practical mental health monitoring systems. This study highlights the feasibility of using self-supervised feature learning methods alongside deep models for large-scale, non-invasive screening of depression.

Title: Depression and Anxiety Screening for Pregnant Women and General Users Using AI Speech
Abstract: This specific research is a reaction to the increasing worry over undiagnosed cases of anxiety and depression in pregnant women a major public health issue that may have an impact on the health of expectant mothers and their developing offspring. Self-administered questionnaires which are subjective, time consuming and often unavailable in rural areas are used in the present screening process. In this study an artificial intelligence system that analyzes speech signals to identify mental health issues is used to provide an objective approachable and intelligent screening tool. In order to identify salient speech characteristics, the screening approach necessitates the submission of audio samples via uploaded files or microphones followed by feature extraction utilizing sophisticated audio signal processing. While a distinct deep learning model recognizes emotions from voice signals, a recurrent neural network model learns temporal patterns in speech using voice datasets from sadness and anxiety. With two distinct interfaces for regular users and expectant mothers, the system incorporates a sizable language model to produce tailored mental health recommendations and insights depending on the identified results. High performance is demonstrated by experimental assessment which achieves 98.2 percent accuracy for emotion recognition and 97.5 percent accuracy for the classification of anxiety and depression. The suggested system comes to the conclusion that speech-based AI can successfully offer trustworthy, in-the-moment mental health screening and helpful advice.

Title: Lightweight Parkinson's Detection from Spontaneous Speech Using Dominant-Speech Filtering
Abstract: Early detection of Parkinson's disease (PD) is critical for effective clinical management, yet initial symptoms are often mild and difficult to identify. Speech irregularities emerge as early non-motor biomarkers in up to 90% of patients, providing a non-invasive avenue for scalable screening via mobile devices. This study proposes a lightweight, diarization-free architecture using dominant-speech filtering on the MDVR-KCL dataset of smartphone conversational recordings to isolate patient voice from noise and interlocutors via energy-based thresholds, enabling efficient mobile deployment. 24 interpretable acoustic features (jitter, shimmer, HNR, MFCCs, formants, pitch, intensity) were fused with PCA-compressed wav2vec2 embeddings and fed to an SVM model at 3-second segment and patient-level scales. Segment-level achieved 97.0% accuracy, 94.7% recall, and 98.8% precision via 5-fold cross-validation (CV), while patient level aggregation yielded 91% accuracy and 77.8% recall. Patient-level Leave-One-Subject-Out cross-validation (LOSO-CV) further confirmed robust generalization, achieving 89% accuracy, 94.4% precision and 80.6% PD recall across 73 unseen patients, demonstrating stable between-subject performance with minimal drop (-2%) from 5-fold results. This compact pipeline enables reliable, real-time PD screening from spontaneous speech on resource-limited mobile devices.

Title: Read and Tell - Speech Dataset for Scripted and Spontaneous Scenarios
Abstract: The growing need for robust and ethically balanced speech datasets is becoming increasingly critical in the development of voice-based AI systems or biometric authentication. In this paper, we present a novel speech corpus, Read and Tell (RaT), comprising recordings from 120 speakers, balanced by gender, and diversified in age and language. Each participant contributed approximately five minutes of read speech and five minutes of spontaneous speech (ten minutes in total per speaker), recorded using various mobile phones in comparable acoustic environments. The dataset enables a systematic comparison of speaking styles and their influence on model performance. We evaluate the corpus in three core tasks: speaker verification, gender classification, and age group classification. Our experiments present significant differences in model behavior depending on speech style. The proposed dataset is a valuable resource for researchers aiming to evaluate and benchmark speech technologies that are robust, fair, and representative of real-world usage conditions. By combining demographic balance, multilingual coverage, and two distinct speaking styles within a compact, well-documented design, RaT fills a critical gap as an evaluation set for testing speech technologies under realistic, style-mismatched, and demographically diverse conditions. The dataset, available for research under license, offers a challenging benchmark to drive progress in robust, fair, and inclusive speech processing.

Title: Fake Audio Detection in Multiple Languages Using Generative AI
Abstract: The growing number of high-quality, digital generated via sound synthesis methods has a large impact on the security of digital communications and the people who use them. The following study describes an innovative framework for the detection of 'artificial' or 'Deep fake' audio recordings that identifies and differentiates real and Deep fake utilizing sound signal processing methods (both traditionally) and utilizing primarily deep learning methods. The Deep Learning model utilizes observable characteristics of both authentic and synthetic audio file types (e.g., Melspectrograms, Melfrequency cepstral coefficients, MFCCs, temporal characteristics, spectral characteristics) to measure how many features from the original, 'non-deepfaked' digital audio file were created as a result of generating that digital audio 'file'. The previously described observable characteristics are used to train/validate two primary types of Deep Neural Networks: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN's) and Bi-directional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM's). In this study, I utilized both the CNN's and BiLSTM's to develop a new, innovative hybrid architecture capable of recognizing the spatial (spatially) and temporal (temporally) dimensions present in real and artificial speech audio files. The Deep fake audio detection framework that I developed based on the hybrid CNN and BiLSTM architecture was trained on three distinct benchmark data sets: ASVspoof, WaveFake, and FakeAVCeleb, by examining their performance in relation to the overall benchmarking methodology. On average, across the complete training benchmark set, my deep fake audio detection framework achieved an overall accuracy of 95.4%. Detection of deepfake audio using the deepfake audio detection framework developed during this research effort was successful in detecting deepfake audio samples. However, no deepfake audio samples were detected with a greater than required accuracy than the required accuracy threshold was established. The results and capabilities demonstrated by the deepfake audio detection framework demonstrate that the framework is capable of performing voice authentication, monitoring calls for audio or audio/video calls at call centres, assisting with the forensics of digital audio evidence, and ultimately assisting in establishing credible trust in the integrity of digital audio-based communications.

Title: Multi-Task Arabic Speech Modeling for Secure Voice Commands
Abstract: The rapid advancement of generative artificial intelligence has made voice cloning a serious threat to biometric security systems. This paper presents a multi-task architecture designed to secure Arabic voice command systems against advanced neural voice cloning attacks, especially those generated by the XTTS-v2 model. This approach extends the spoofing detection paradigm by proposing a framework based on speaker identification, which is better suited to multi-user environments, while integrating voice command recognition within a unified multi-task setting. We evaluate two self-supervised learning (SSL) models, HuBERT and Wav2Vec2, each combined with a temporal attention mechanism to jointly perform spoofing detection, speaker identification, and Arabic voice command recognition. Experiments are conducted on a balanced Arabic dataset of 3,200 samples, comprising real voices and synthetic voices generated by XTTS-v2 with stochastic variability, to simulate realistic attack conditions. Results show high performance in command recognition (98.14%) and speaker identification (98.12%). For spoofing detection, the system achieves an accuracy of 89.38% and an Equal Error Rate (EER) of 7.25% for Wav2Vec2 and 7.88% for HuBERT, highlighting the superior performance of Wav2Vec2. These findings show that SSL-based multi-task architectures provide an effective solution for developing secure and robust Arabic voice control systems.

Title: Stammering Detection with Streaming TDNN and Log Mel Acoustic Features
Abstract: Stammering is one of the disorders that brings about a lack of speech fluency and a decrease in the social interaction skills of the affected individual. It is generally described as the occurrence of speech disfluencies such as repetitions, prolongations, and involuntary pauses in the speech of the person. The paper presents a clever system for the identification of stammering through the use of a Streaming Time Delay Neural Network (TDNN) combined with log Mel acoustic features for the accurate and instant disfluency classification in spoken language. The proposed TDNN model, in contrast to regular speech recognition systems that rely on static input windows, sequentially processes audio frames in a streaming manner; thus, it can capture both short- and longterm temporal dependencies without a significant computational cost. The approach takes log Mel spectrograms of the raw speech signals so that the most relevant spectral information is retained, and at the same time, the method is resistant to background noise and speaker variations. The features are then input to the streaming TDNN, which generates a binary output indicating either fluent or stammered speech segments. The new method can reach very high detection accuracy levels with a low latency, and it can be considered to outperform both in terms of precision and inference speed the baseline convolutional and recurrent models. The experiments demonstrate that the performance of the stammering detection system can be dramatically enhanced through the combination of temporal context modeling and acoustic feature learning. Moreover, the compact design of the system enables it to be implemented on the edge devices and mobiles for speech therapy, early diagnosis, and assistive communication purposes.

Title: Machine learning integration of thermal liquid biopsy and clinical biomarkers for pancreatic cancer diagnosis and prognosis: A retrospective cohort study
Abstract: Background: Pancreatic cancer continues to be one of the most challenging malignancies to diagnose and treat, and it is often detected at an advanced stage owing to asymptomatic early phases and limitations in current diagnostic tools, highlighting the need for improved diagnostic methodologies. Methods: We aimed to evaluate the potential for integrating information from thermal liquid biopsy (TLB) thermograms with clinical biomarkers to improve the diagnosis and prognosis of pancreatic cancer. Serum samples from 381 Danish patients with pancreatic cancer and 325 patients referred with non-organ specific signs and symptoms of cancer, but without confirmed cancer after clinical and computed tomography evaluation, were analyzed. TLB thermograms provided information on the partial excess heat capacity of the serum as a function of temperature. Three classification models were constructed using machine learning algorithms based on variable selection with penalization, applying cross-validation and resampling techniques: iClin Model (age, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group Performance Status, carbohydrate antigen 19.9, and C-reactive protein), iTLB Model (discordant pairs of temperatures from thermograms), and iTLB + iClin Model (discordant pairs of temperatures and clinical data). Results: The iClin Model achieved high diagnostic performance, with a validation area under the curve (AUC) of 0.95 ± 0.01 for differentiating symptomatic controls from patients with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), but showed no significant association with overall survival (OS). The iTLB Model showed limited diagnostic performance, with a validation AUC of 0.59 ± 0.03, but was associated with OS in patients with PDAC. The combined iTLB + iClin Model preserved high diagnostic performance, with a validation AUC of 0.95 ± 0.02, sensitivity of 96.20%, specificity of 91.20%, positive predictive value of 90.48%, and negative predictive value of 96.59%. For early-stage PDAC, the iTLB + iClin Model achieved an AUC of 0.93 (95% CI: 0.89–0.98), compared with 0.96 (95% CI: 0.95–0.98) for stages III–IV. Conclusion: This study demonstrates the potential of combining specific clinical biomarker information with advanced techniques such as TLB, to improve the accuracy of pancreatic cancer diagnosis and prognosis.

Title: A deep learning-based approach combining technical indicators and market sentiment for multi-timeframe cryptocurrency investment decision support
Abstract: To help navigate the volatility of cryptocurrencies, this study proposed a leakage‑free deep learning approach utilizing over 50 technical indicators as well as the Crypto Fear & Greed Index (FGI) to forecast movement for five major cryptocurrencies; BTC, ETH, BNB, XRP, and SOL. For evaluation, the research used daily time series data from January 2018–April 2025 and tested six different neural network approaches and several traditional machine learning baselines using TimeSeriesSplit for a strict cross‑validation methodology. In addition, class imbalance was addressed by utilizing cost‑sensitive learning to evaluate the models’ performance using both macro F1 scores and Sharpe ratios adjusted for transaction costs. The results of my analysis show that the best horizon for forecasting is asset specific, where CNNs performed the strongest at horizons ranging from 15 days to 30 days. Additionally, it was found through an ablation study that incorporating sentiment provided a ‘sentiment premium’ for altcoins (+3.28% F1 score for ETH) while Bitcoin remained technically driven. Overall, this risk‑aware model will provide a solid decision‑making platform within the rapidly changing world of digital asset markets.

Title: Can AI singing retain users? Examining how experience, ethical acceptance, and affective engagement shape continuance intention
Abstract: Introduction – With the increasing integration of artificial intelligence into digital music applications, AI singing has emerged as a novel form of human–AI interaction in mobile karaoke platforms. Despite its growing popularity, limited research has examined the psychological mechanisms underlying users’ sustained engagement with AI singing, particularly from perspectives integrating affective experience and ethical perception. To address this gap, the present study aims to investigate the technological, affective, ethical, and agency-related factors influencing users’ continuance intention toward AI singing. Methods – Grounded in research on technology acceptance and psychological engagement, this study develops an extended framework incorporating Perceived Agency (PA), Ethical Acceptance (EA), and Affective Engagement (AE) to better explain users’ responses to AI-generated singing experiences. A total of 460 valid responses were collected through a survey, and structural equation modeling (SEM) was employed to test the proposed relationships. Results – The findings indicate that Performance Expectancy (PEF), Effort Expectancy (EE), Perceived Enjoyment (ENJ), Ethical Acceptance (EA), and Affective Engagement (AE) significantly and positively influence continuance intention. In contrast, Perceived Agency (PA), Perceived Innovativeness (PI), and Social Influence (SI) do not show significant effects. Discussion – The results suggest that sustained engagement with AI singing is shaped not only by functional evaluations, but also by emotional experience and ethical perception. This study contributes to research on psychological engagement in AI-enabled music interaction and provides practical implications for the design and optimization of AI singing applications.

Title: Classification of Assamese regional songs using a hybrid model of machine learning and deep learning
Abstract: Purpose – The purpose of the study on Regional music serves as a vital medium for preserving cultural identity, traditions and collective memory. In Assam, a state in Northeast India, musical forms such as Bihu, Borgeet, Goalpariya, Kamrupi and Naam represent the region’s diverse cultural and spiritual heritage. Despite their significance, systematic computational studies on Assamese regional music remain scarce. Design/methodology/approach – This paper presents an approach for automatic classification of Assamese regional music using a hybrid deep learning and machine learning technique. Audio recordings were transformed into spectrograms to capture both frequency and temporal features of the signals. Findings – A hybrid CNN + KNN model was developed, which yielded an accuracy of 0.71, with precision of 0.76, recall of 0.71 and F1-score of 0.70. The hybrid model demonstrated a balanced performance across evaluation metrics, indicating improved generalizability. Originality/value – To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this study contributes to music information retrieval (MIR) and digital heritage by being one of the first systematic attempts to classify Assamese regional music through artificial intelligence-driven methods. The proposed framework can support digital archiving, recommendation systems and cultural preservation, ensuring that Assamese traditions are safeguarded in the digital era.

Title: Technological Advances that Shape Practice Towards Better Teaching and Learning Experiences in the Study of Music
Abstract: Arts and humanities educators have been urged in recent years to remain attentive to the political, economic, and ideological forces shaping their institutions, their work, and their students’ expectations. The arts landscape continues to face challenges such as global pandemics, online learning, and changing student populations. In continuing to be mindful and engage with teaching and learning as a collective, we must persevere and share both our successes and challenges in the arts and humanities teaching and learning space. At Sydney Conservatorium of Music (SCM), at the University of Sydney, Australia, we have a workforce of expert musicians who mentor tertiary music students within a variety of disciplines including music composition, performance, musicology, etc. In their roles as practice-focused educators, these musicians have significant experience of teaching and learning, yet many have had no opportunities to engage in formal training as higher music educators. In order to provide formal training as an essential component of an academic’s growth and development, institutions have established short-term postgraduate programs, such as the Graduate Certificate in Educational Studies (Higher Education). We present two examples of how this formal training has led to significant innovations within our faculty’s teaching practice. The importance of encouraging arts practitioners to engage in this training has established a framework of excellence in our tertiary music institution and challenges music educators to refocus on the significance of teaching and learning in music degrees globally.

Title: Contractual standardisation and AI readiness in maritime governance: evidence from maritime contract-type analytics
Abstract: Charterparty markets differ not only in cargo type but in the institutional structures governing how contracts are drafted, standardised, and reproduced. Drawing on institutional theory, this study treats maritime contract types—from standardised instruments such as waybills and bunkers to bespoke voyage charters and offshore agreements—as distinct contractual environments, and asks whether they differ systematically in readiness for AI-assisted document analytics. A corpus of 1,783 maritime legal documents was classified using a Legal-BERT multi-label classifier, evaluated through five-fold cross-validation repeated across three seeds, with contract-type-level area under the precision–recall curve (AUPRC) as the primary indicator of AI readiness. Performance varied substantially, from 0.281 for voyage charters to 0.916 for contracts of affreightment (global micro-F1 = 0.569), confirming that maritime document environments are not equally ready for AI-assisted analytics. The expected mediation pathway through textual regularity was not supported (Spearman ρ = 0.027, p = 0.924), indicating that the operative mechanism extends beyond textual homogeneity to label specificity, vocabulary exclusivity, and inter-document scope coherence. The findings carry practical implications for maritime governance institutions, standard-form bodies, and organisations deploying AI tools in contract review.

Title: Methodological development of a pneumatic artificial muscle-driven left ventricular simulator using interpretive structural modeling
Abstract: Mock circulation systems can replicate a wide range of cardiac operating scenarios, such as cardiovascular diseases, particularly muscular dysfunctions. These systems are operated by sophisticated control algorithms which require complex driver and data acquisition systems, whereas animal models raise ethical concerns. Therefore, there is a need for novel testbeds to overcome the challenges in the existing systems. The aim of this study is to develop a less complex and realistic left ventricular (LV) simulator. The Interpretive Structural Modeling (ISM) approach was utilized to evaluate different left ventricular actuation methods and materials. ISM revealed that the most suitable method to actuate the LV is using the pneumatic artificial muscles and latex rubber. The performance of the new LV simulator was evaluated for healthy and diseased conditions at 50, 60, 70 and 80 bpm heart rates. The experiments revealed that the beating LV simulator can generate average flow rates of up to 2.25 L/min. The actual human LV-like wall motion was also verified by the twisting angle on the apex of the beating LV simulator with 21 degrees of rotation and 11 mm of apex shortening. The prototyped beating LV simulator is a promising preliminary platform and may reach actual human LV’s hemodynamic and cardio-mechanical performance with further improvements.

Title: AI-based Respiratory Illness Detection using Voice Signals (Cough, Speech, and Breathing Analysis)
Abstract: Respiratory illnesses such as COVID-19, asthma, and bronchitis continue to pose a major global health burden. In many regions, these conditions remain underdiagnosed due to the high cost of diagnostic equipment and the shortage of trained medical personnel, which contributes to delayed treatment and avoidable mortality. At the same time, smartphones and laptops equipped with built-in microphones are now widely available, enabling the routine recording of cough, speech, and breathing sounds in everyday settings. Recent research has shown that these audio signals, when represented as spectrograms, contain discriminative patterns that can be exploited by machine learning models through systematic feature extraction and embedding learning. Despite this progress, most existing approaches are limited in scope. They typically focus on a single disease, rely on small or restricted datasets, and use audio recorded under controlled or quiet conditions, which limits real-world applicability. In response, this paper proposes an AI-based framework for the classification of multiple respiratory illnesses, with a focus on COVID-19, asthma, and bronchitis, using cough, speech, and breathing recordings. The framework integrates three publicly available datasets to capture diverse diseases, devices, and recording environments. Audio signals are resampled, normalized, denoised, and segmented before extracting log-mel spectrograms and handcrafted features such as mel-frequency cepstral coefficients. Baseline classical models are compared with a multi-branch convolutional neural network that processes each modality separately and fuses learned representations for final prediction. The system is intended as a clinician-in-the-loop decision support tool, evaluated using subject-stratified cross-validation and clinically relevant performance metrics, to support realistic and supervised deployment.

Title: A Lightweight Edge Deployable Deep Learning Framework for Speech-Based Pain Classification across Heterogeneous Datasets
Abstract: Automatic pain assessment from speech is an emerging approach for non-invasive and objective healthcare monitoring. However, many existing methods are evaluated on single datasets or under controlled conditions, which limits their robustness under diverse real-world conditions. This paper presents a lightweight, end-to-end deep learning framework for speech-based pain level classification that explicitly targets multi-dataset robustness assessment. The proposed approach uses log-Mel spectrograms with an EfficientNetV2B0 backbone to learn discriminative acoustic features without relying on handcrafted feature engineering or multi-stage pipelines. The model is evaluated on heterogeneous datasets, including clinical recordings, controlled experimental data, and a merged dataset representing diverse conditions. Experimental results show competitive performance, achieving up to 77.8% accuracy in four-class classification, 71.7% in three-class classification, and 87.7% in binary pain detection on the merged dataset. Compared with previous works, the approach achieves competitive performance, with stronger results in clinical and reduced-class settings. The model was also converted using TensorFlow Lite to enable efficient edge deployment with minimal performance degradation and reduced computational cost, supporting future deployment in mobile and edge-based healthcare applications.

Title: Machine Learning-Based Clustering of Global Labor Markets Using Unemployment Profiles
Abstract: The problem of global unemployment is currently an urgent challenge in the development of the world’s economy, but the traditional classification methods still cannot fully analyze the inadequacies and complexities of this problem. The research gap due to the use of ML analysis for clustering has not been paid attention to, so the data can be considered as under-exploited. Therefore, in this paper, we focus on analyzing unemployment data collected from 187 countries in the period of 2014 to 2024 based on four key features: overall mean rate, overall standard deviation, gender gap, and youth-adult gap. We combine the K-means and Hierarchical clustering methods to cluster countries with common economic characteristics, then the Gradient Boosting model is applied as the main model to make predictions about future trends in each cluster. We identify the analysis results that highlight five distinct country clusters with mean unemployment levels ranging from 4.93% to 29.91%. Notably, structural disparities persist, with the average cluster gender gap and youth-adult gap in the labor force reach up to 15.18 and 27.54 percentage points, respectively. Furthermore, the cluster-specific forecasting performance also achieves RMSE in the 0.48–2.21 range and MAE of 0.32 to 2.01. In addition, cluster-specific forecasting of 2025–2030 indicates that there will be a path-based trend of forecasting, which means that vulnerable clusters will continue to experience structural stress without forming major developments. After all, this study highlights the fact that, unless structural changes are implemented, the fragile economies risk stagnation in the long term. The suggested clustering framework is, therefore, a crucial instrument that can be used by policymakers in order to shift towards generic answers to the question of precision-based strategies, which will guarantee the creation of a more inclusive and sustainable labor market development process.

Title: Multimodal Deep Learning-Based Anomaly Action Recognition in Multiple Physical Security Domains
Abstract: This paper proposes a multimodal deep learning system for anomaly action recognition across multiple physical security domains using RGB video, depth video, and audio streams. The proposed system recognizes nine types of anomaly actions in three representative environments: construction sites, urban buildings, and industrial facilities. For spatio-temporal video understanding, RGB and depth video streams are analyzed using a modified R(2+1) D network, while audio signals are processed using CLAP-based semantic audio embeddings. The multimodal outputs are integrated through a confidence-weighted fusion module to improve robustness under diverse environmental conditions. Experimental results show that the server-based model achieves an average anomaly action recognition accuracy of 87.33% with a NetScore of 63.35, while the lightweight model achieves 81.78% accuracy with a NetScore of 65.03. These results demonstrate that the proposed system provides an effective balance between recognition performance and computational efficiency for practical multimodal anomaly action recognition in edge deployment.

Title: Supervised Source Separation and Multimodal Fusion of Heart-Lung Sounds
Abstract: Reliable classification of cardiopulmonary abnormalities from digital auscultation remains challenging due to spectral overlap between heart and lung signals, class imbalance, and limited acoustic variability in existing datasets. This work presents an integrated evaluation pipeline combining time-frequency preprocessing, heart-cycle segmentation, deep convolutional neural networks, prototype-based inference, and classical machine learning applied to deep embeddings. Experiments were conducted using a manikin-generated dataset containing overlapping heart-lung recordings across six lung and four heart sound categories, partitioned into distinct training, validation, and test sets. Results demonstrate modest baseline performance on mixed spectrograms, with a peak test accuracy of 0.833, dominated by over-prediction of normal breath sounds and nearzero recall for minority lung pathologies. Heart-cycle segmentation introduced temporal structure and improved per-cycle validation accuracy to 0.856, while file-level aggregation achieved 0.754 validation and 0.812 test accuracy, indicating enhanced sensitivity to arrhythmic and conduction features. Prototype-based classification achieved 0.843 validation and 0.833 test accuracy, confirming partial separability in deep latent space despite feature entanglement. Logistic regression on deep embeddings yielded 0.800 test accuracy, demonstrating that the learned representations lacked strong linear discriminability. Dimensionality-reduction analyses using t-SNE and UMAP revealed persistent cluster overlap between heart and lung manifolds, underscoring limited modality disentanglement. Collectively, these findings highlight that naive acoustic separation alone remains insufficient for robust multimodal auscultation analysis, and that dataset realism, spectral integrity, and temporal attention modeling are critical for clinical deployment. The proposed pipeline offers a reproducible benchmark and identifies key architectural and data-centric directions for advancing intelligent cardiopulmonary diagnostics.

Title: S.C.O.R.E: A Multi-Modal Artificial Intelligence Framework for Neurocognitive Assessment via Semantic Analysis and Behavioral Biometrics
Abstract: The growing incidence of neurodegenerative illnesses calls for accurate and accessible cognitive evaluation instruments. Conventional approaches such as the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) have limited scoring criteria and lack objective behavioral analysis. This paper introduces S.C.O.R.E. (Systematic Cognitive Observation and Recognition Engine), a preventive neuro-cognitive assessment platform that transforms the traditional analog Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) into a multi-modal, paperless intelligent system. Our method utilizes a Neural Semantic Scoring Engine based on Sentence-BERT (SBERT) for flexible, context-aware response evaluation, while incorporating behavioral biometrics through Deep Autoencoders and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to identify motor-cognitive changes via typing dynamics. These features are combined using XGBoost and Random Forest classifiers in an ensemble pipeline, with SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) for clinical interpretability. Preliminary validation demonstrates an accuracy of 94.2% in identifying cognitive health statuses, establishing S.C.O.R.E. as a powerful tool for early screening and clinical decision support.

Title: Performance Enhancement of Dolphin Sound Classification via Data Augmentation
Abstract: Reliable identification of dolphin vocalizations is essential for effective marine acoustic monitoring. Limited and imbalanced datasets often constrain classification performance. This study investigates the impact of systematic data augmentation on dolphin sound classification using both classical machine learning and deep learning approaches. Acoustic data from 12 dolphin species were converted into time-frequency representations. Augmentation was performed using techniques such as pitch variation, time stretching, noise injection, and amplitude scaling to simulate real-world acoustic variability. A range of classifiers, including Support Vector Machine, K-Nearest Neighbors, Random Forest, Logistic Regression, Naive Bayes, and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), were evaluated under both non-augmented and augmented conditions. The results reveal that data augmentation is not uniformly beneficial across all models. It exhibits a strong dependence on the underlying classification approach. While probabilistic models such as Naive Bayes show performance degradation due to violated feature assumptions. Deep learning and instancebased methods benefit significantly from augmented data. In particular, the CNN achieves the highest accuracy of 97.8%, demonstrating improved robustness and generalization. These findings highlight the importance of model-aware augmentation strategies for developing reliable dolphin acoustic classification systems.

Title: A Non-Prosthetic Assistive System for Persons with Hearing Losses: Design and Experimental Investigation
Abstract: Hearing impairment affects hundreds of millions of people worldwide and limits their ability to perceive critical environmental sounds. Conventional assistive devices, such as hearing aids and cochlear implants, mainly focus on sound amplification and provide limited contextual or spatial awareness. This paper presents a wearable, non-prosthetic assistive system that integrates environmental sound recognition, sound source localization, and real-time speech-to-text transcription within a unified framework. The system uses a multi-microphone array and an embedded platform to process audio in real time through preprocessing, feature extraction, and machine learning-based inference. Extracted information is delivered through a web-based interface and haptic alerts to support intuitive inter-pretation of surrounding acoustic events. The paper presents the system design, hardware integration, software architecture, and experimental evaluation of its main components. Results demonstrate the feasibility of combining semantic and spatial audio understanding within a single assistive platform to improve safety, communication, and environmental awareness for hearing-impaired users.

Title: Stability-Aware Preprocessing for Audio-Visual Speech Processing
Abstract: Audio-visual speech processing (AVSP) systems offer a compelling framework for robust speech analysis in adverse and unconstrained environments; however, their deployment in real-world conditions remains challenged by uncontrolled variability in audio and visual inputs. Factors such as environmental noise, illumination changes, spatial misalignment, and temporal inconsistency introduce instability that is frequently addressed through increasingly complex model architectures, while preprocessing is often treated as a secondary implementation step. This paper presents a unified, stability-aware preprocessing pipeline that reframes preprocessing as a primary design layer operating entirely prior to learning and inference. The proposed framework systematically conditions audio and visual streams through modality-specific normalization and explicit cross-modal consistency enforcement, yielding statistically coherent and temporally aligned representations. By constraining input variability and suppressing nuisance factors unrelated to speech content, the preprocessing stage emphasizes task-relevant structures and reduces the burden placed on downstream models, enabling lightweight yet effective learning behavior. The pipeline is designed to be architecture-agnostic and applicable across diverse audio-visual datasets, supporting consistent model behavior without reliance on dataset-specific preprocessing heuristics. Rather than pursuing task-level performance optimization, this work adopts an observational evaluation perspective to examine how principled preprocessing influences learning stability, convergence behavior, and robustness under realistic operating conditions. The findings position unified preprocessing as a foundational mechanism for building efficient, reproducible, and scalable AVSP systems suitable for real-world deployment.

Title: A music style recognition system by multi-task LSTM and its application in Orff music pedagogy
Abstract: In order to solve the bottleneck problems of subjective evaluation and lagging teaching feedback in traditional music education, this study proposes a bidirectional long-short-term memory (BI-LSTM) multi-task learning framework that integrates harmonic/percussive source separation (HPSS) preprocessing technology. The system provides real-time quantitative teaching feedback according to students' performance by decoupling the characteristics of melody flow and rhythm flow. The international free music archive (FMA) dataset was used for technical benchmarking, and a three-week Orff teaching intervention experiment was conducted for 60 primary school participants. The experimental results showed that the system achieved 94.5 F1 score. Verified by analysis of variance (ANOVA), the accuracy of the students' discrimination of music styles was significantly improved from the initial benchmark value of 65.4 to 91.2 after intervention. The model system proposed in this study provides an objective and stable technical paradigm and decision support for the interactive mode of intelligent music education.

Title: Antibiotic mixture exposure in meconium affects child neurodevelopment via altering early-life gut microbiome and metabolome
Abstract: Previous evidence has established associations of antibiotic exposure in early life with neurodevelopmental disorders. However, previous studies have often relied on self-reported or record-based exposure measures that may not accurately reflect internal fetal exposure, and few have integrated prenatal exposure biomarkers with infant microbiome, metabolome, and longitudinal neurodevelopmental data. This study included 300 mother-infant pairs from the Shanghai Maternal-Child Pairs Cohort. Meconium samples were used to quantify concentrations of 18 antibiotics using high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC). Neurodevelopmental outcomes were assessed using Ages and Stages Questionnaires (ASQ) at 2, 6, 12, and 24 months of age. Multi-omics profiling of 6-month fecal samples was conducted, employing 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing and HPLC-based metabolomics. Linear and logistic regression models, negative binomial regression, interpretable machine learning algorithms, metabolome-wide association/pathway analyses and high-dimensional mediation modeling were used. Our study population demonstrated predominant exposure to three antibiotics: chlortetracycline, penicillin, and chloramphenicol. Each interquartile range (IQR) increase in meconium-measured antibiotic burden was associated with a lower total ASQ score at 6 months (β = −4.49, 95% CI: −7.14 to −1.86) and lower scores across all five developmental domains (βs ranging from −0.53 to −1.11; all P < 0.05). Each IQR increment of antibiotic burden was also associated with greater odds of belonging to the lower-score group of total ASQ trajectory (OR = 1.20, 95% CI: 1.04, 1.42) and the lower-score group of personal-social trajectory (OR = 1.13, 95% CI: 1.01, 1.28). Exploratory high-dimensional mediation analyses identified Lactobacillus and 2-(14,15-epoxyeicosatrienoyl) glycerol (2-14,15-EG) as candidate intermediates in the association between meconium-measured antibiotic burden and neurodevelopment. Our study suggested that higher meconium-based biomarkers of intrauterine antibiotic burden were significantly associated with lower neurodevelopmental outcomes in early childhood, with the strongest inverse associations observed at 6 months. Lactobacillus and 2-14,15-EG were identified as potential mediator biomarkers. These hypothesis-generating findings require independent replication, longitudinal temporal validation, and experimental studies before causal mechanisms or microbiota-targeted interventions can be inferred.

Title: CNN-transformer hybrid deep learning method for suppressing interference fringe noise
Abstract: Tunable Diode Laser Absorption Spectroscopy (TDLAS) technology often faces the problems of interference fringe overlap and phase shift, leading to target signal distortion. Traditional digital filtering and existing deep learning models are often limited to local smoothing when dealing with dynamic distorted noise that has frequency aliasing with real signals, which easily causes signal feature loss or absorption peak clipping. To address this challenge, a novel hybrid denoising architecture (New CNT) based on Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Transformer is proposed in this paper. This model uses CNN to accurately extract local waveform distortion features and combines the multi-head self-attention mechanism of Transformer to filter global background noise. To accelerate model convergence and avoid invalid training, an equivalent data optimization strategy is adopted, which relies on a smaller-scale training set to enable the model to obtain an additional performance gain of 4.42 dB while significantly reducing the total training overhead by 19%. In addition, the Monte Carlo phase perturbation technology is introduced into the training data to simulate actual working conditions, and a joint loss function (including weighted mean square error, Pearson correlation coefficient, and peak missing penalty) is innovatively designed, which effectively overcomes the peak shaving phenomenon during denoising and maintains the similarity of physical waveforms. The simulation results show that the average signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the mixed signal with envelope distortion noise is increased by 44.60 dB with the New CNT model, respectively, and exhibits extremely high accuracy and stability in the evaluation indicators of Peak Height Error (PHE) and Relative Standard Deviation (RSD). This study provides a reliable deep learning solution for TDLAS systems with high timeliness, high precision, and strong robustness.

Title: Development of Explainable Audio-Based Deep Learning for Gender-Aware Dysarthria Classification
Abstract: Dysarthria is a motor speech disorder characterized by impaired articulation, reduced speech intelligibility, and abnormal prosodic patterns. Although deep learning methods have shown promising performance in automatic dysarthria detection, most existing studies formulate the task as binary classification and overlook gender-dependent acoustic variability. In addition, the lack of interpretability in deep learning models remains a significant challenge for clinical adoption. This study proposes an explainable audio-based deep learning framework for gender-aware dysarthria classification. The proposed system employs a standardized preprocessing pipeline consisting of resampling, normalization, silence removal, and fixed-length segmentation. Log-Mel spectrograms are extracted to capture discriminative time-frequency characteristics of dysarthric and non-dysarthric speech and are subsequently processed using a convolutional neural network (CNN). The framework performs four-class classification: Male Dysarthria, Female Dysarthria, Male Non-Dysarthria, and Female Non-Dysarthria. To improve robustness and reduce overfitting, several augmentation strategies, including time stretching, pitch shifting, additive noise injection, and SpecAugment, are incorporated. Furthermore, Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) techniques, namely Grad-CAM and saliency mapping, are integrated to visualize discriminative spectral regions influencing model predictions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed gender-aware framework improves classification performance compared to conventional binary approaches while providing clinically interpretable insights into dysarthric speech characteristics. The proposed framework offers a transparent and robust approach for automated dysarthria assessment and has potential as a decision-support tool for speech-language pathologists and clinical researchers.

Title: Aircraft Approach Type Recommendation Based on Weather Conditions Using Supervised Learning
Abstract: The approach and landing phases are the most critical stages in flight operations, where ATC is required to make fast and accurate decisions, especially under changing weather conditions. This study develops a supervised learning-based recommendation system for landing approach types by leveraging real-time data from D-ATIS and RVR at six major airports in the United States. Among the tree-based models, Random Forest achieved the best performance. The tree-based model achieved the highest average macro precision, recall, and F1-score of 0.82, 0.92, and 0.86 respectively. For kernel-based models (SVC), the best result was obtained with the polynomial kernel, achieving average precision, recall, and F1-score of 0.75, 0.92, and 0.79. In addition, Explainable AI (XAI), specifically SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) is used to observe feature importance of both tree-based and kernel-based models. The SHAP results shown that both models mostly rely on airport-related features for instrument-based landing approaches.

Title: RamanLLM: Reprogramming Frozen Large Language Models for Raman Spectral Analysis
Abstract: Raman spectroscopy provides molecular fingerprints that can detect disease-related biochemical changes, but its deployment in clinical settings is limited by fluorescence interference, instrument variability, and the scarcity of labeled biomedical datasets. In this work, we present RamanLLM, a framework that reprograms a pretrained large language model (LLM) for Raman spectral analysis without full model retraining. The proposed approach represents each spectrum as a sequence of local spectral segments, which are projected into the LLM embedding space through a lightweight reprogramming layer and combined with task-specific prompt tokens. This allows the frozen transformer to model both local spectral structures and long-range dependencies across the signal, leveraging pretrained sequence modelling capabilities while keeping training cost low.RamanLLM is evaluated on multiple real-world Raman datasets covering both regression and classification tasks. For regression, on the Interference dataset involving analyte prediction in 3-component mixtures, RamanLLM achieves the best performance for urea (RMSE = 4.86, R2 = 0.99), outperforming Random Forest (RF) (RMSE = 5.81) and CNN (RMSE = 6.09), and improves over RF for lactate prediction (RMSE = 4.65 vs 5.19). For classification, RamanLLM achieves 98.5% accuracy on a 4-class cancer dataset, 98.8% on a 5-class bacterial dataset, and 93.2% on a 30-class dataset, remaining competitive with CNN-based models. These results show that frozen LLMs can be effectively adapted to spectroscopy data, providing a flexible and parameter-efficient alternative to task-specific deep learning models, particularly in settings with limited data and varying experimental conditions.

Title: Scale: Sensitivity-Aware Federated Unlearning with Information Freshness Optimization for Mobile Edge Computing
Abstract: Federated Unlearning (FU) is emerging as a powerful tool that enables the selective removal of client data to effectively address data contamination and meet strict privacy regulations in mobile edge computing (MEC) systems. Although FU has recently drawn attention in the AI community, existing approaches suffer from low unlearning precision and lack temporal information reflection, which results in suboptimal forgetting performance. To address these issues, we propose SCALE, a dual-level unlearning framework combining historical contribution analysis with information freshness-aware adaptive sparsification. Our framework first employs a historical contribution-based layer sensitivity analysis to identify layers most influenced by target clients, then performs fine-grained unlearning through adaptive sparsification at the weight subgroup level to balance information freshness with forgetting effectiveness. Through theoretical analysis, the proposed framework demonstrates the convergence properties and acceleration advantages. Our experiments and testbed results demonstrate superior unlearning effectiveness compared to state-of-the-art baselines, with significantly improved forgetting performance.

Title: Comparative Analysis of ARIMA and LSTM Models for Forecasting ETF Closing Prices and Trading Volume
Abstract: Accurate forecasting of financial time series is essential for supporting investment decision-making and portfolio management. Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs), as highly liquid financial instruments, require reliable predictions of both closing prices and trading volumes. This study compares conventional statistical approaches, namely Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) and Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average with Exogenous Variables (ARIMAX), with multiple deep learning frameworks based on Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) architectures, including Vanilla LSTM, Bidirectional LSTM, and Stacked LSTM, for forecasting ETF closing prices and trading volumes. The empirical analysis uses multivariate QQQ ETF data from February 2019 to February 2024 obtained from Yahoo Finance. Model performance is evaluated using Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE), and the Diebold-Mariano (DM) statistical test. The results show that ARIMAX achieved the best overall forecasting performance, indicating that incorporating trading volume as an exogenous variable improves short-term ETF forecasting accuracy. ARIMA also produced competitive results under limited historical data conditions. Among the deep learning approaches, Vanilla LSTM outperformed Bidirectional and Stacked LSTM architectures. The findings suggest that statistical approaches remain robust and computationally efficient for short-term ETF forecasting, while LSTM-based models provide advantages in learning nonlinear temporal relationships in financial time-series data.

Title: Local electrostatics governs tryptophan oxidation and enables rational stability engineering in antibodies
Abstract: Oxidation of tryptophan (Trp) residues in therapeutic antibody complementarity-determining regions (CDRs) can impair binding affinity, stability, and developability, yet the molecular determinants of site-specific susceptibility remain incompletely understood. Here, we present a structure-informed machine learning framework trained on Trp oxidation profiles from 187 monoclonal antibodies to identify the physicochemical drivers of oxidation risk. Beyond solvent accessibility, the dominant known predictor, we identify local residue-level electrostatic potential (Epot) as a strong independent modulator: negatively charged microenvironments markedly increase oxidation susceptibility. A two-parameter model combining only solvent accessibility and Epot achieves 79% classification accuracy, approaching the 84% performance of full-feature ensemble models, and correctly classifies all 10 CDR Trp sites in a blind validation panel of eight clinical-stage IgG1 antibodies. Leveraging the long-range nature of electrostatic effects, we show that targeted distal charge-altering mutations, without direct modification of the oxidation-prone Trp, reduce oxidation rates by approximately 50% in four of five re-engineered antibodies, with binding affinity preserved in two. In a clinically relevant anti-CD33 antibody where the critical CDR Trp oxidizes at 97% and Trp-to-Phe substitution abolishes binding, iterative electrostatic optimization yielded variants with up to ~50% oxidation reduction, including one single-point-mutation variant achieving 27% oxidation reduction at only 1.4-fold affinity cost, substantially outperforming direct Trp substitution. Redox replica-exchange molecular dynamics simulations provide mechanistic support, revealing an 88 mV increase in Trp reduction potential upon distal charge-reversing mutations. Together, these results establish local electrostatics as a predictive, tunable, and mechanistically grounded handle for rational antibody engineering, and provide a practical framework for simultaneously optimizing oxidation stability and antigen-binding function.

Title: ENEC: A Lossless AI Model Compression Method Enabling Fast Inference on Ascend NPUs
Abstract: The rapid scaling of Large Language Models presents significant challenges for their deployment and inference, particularly on resource-constrained specialized AI hardware accelerators such as Huawei's Ascend NPUs, where weight transfer has become a critical performance bottleneck. While lossless compression can preserve model accuracy and reduce data volume, existing lossless compression algorithms exhibit extremely low throughput when ported to the Ascend NPUs. In this paper, we propose ENEC, a novel lossless compression method specifically customized for AI model weights and optimized for Ascend Neural Processing Units. ENEC adopts a block-based fixed-length encoding scheme and incorporates a series of optimizations: bit-width quantization with hierarchical halving bit-packing, vectorized branch-free integer transformation, and dependency-decoupled intra-segment scan. Experimental results demonstrate that ENEC outperforms existing state-of-the-art NPU compressors in both compression ratio and throughput. Compared to leading GPU solutions, ENEC achieves a 3.43× higher throughput than DietGPU and a 1.12× better compression ratio than nvCOMP. By reducing weight transmission overhead, ENEC significantly improves end-to-end inference performance, achieving up to a 6.3 × speedup. On Ascend NPUs, ENEC is the first open-source lossless compression algorithm for model weights that achieves performance comparable to state-of-the-art GPU compressors, offering an effective solution for deploying large-scale AI models.
