Title: Hybrid Machine Learning and Multimodal Fusion Techniques for Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Systematic Review
Abstract: Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA) is a typical sleeping disorder, characterized by constant interruptions to breathing during the sleep that causes severe health-threatening conditions of heart diseases, intellectual retardation, and inadequate living conditions. The conventional diagnostic instruments, e.g., polysomnography (PSG) are accurate, but expensive, time-consuming and must be adopted in a specific, specialized hospital setting, therefore, they are not universal. In the recent years, machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) models were a popular research topic in the detection and severity prediction of automated OSA on the basis of such physiological indicators as electroencephalogram (EEG), electrocardiogram (ECG), and oxygen saturation (SpO2) and clinical features. The paper will present a review of conventional machine learning, deep learning, and novel hybrid and multimodal detecting methods of OSA. One of the classical algorithms such as Support Vector Machines, Rand Forest and gradient boosting algorithms have been reported to be effective with handcrafted features but the deep learning algorithms and models such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) have been reported to be quite useful in extracting features automatically using raw biomedical signals. Nevertheless, personal models are usually constrained to reflect both local trends and long-term time trends. In order to overcome these issues, the recent research directions are concentrated on hybrid architectures incorporating CNN, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Transformer-based models, as well as multimodal strategies of data fusion, which involve physiological signals, and clinical characteristics. These methods are much better in detecting, being robust and extrapolating across datasets. This review evaluates the performance of different models in terms of standard evaluation metrics, mentions all essential difficulties such as data imbalance and model interpretability, and provides prospective research such as explainable artificial intelligence, wearable-based real-time monitoring, and customized healthcare systems. The research draws the conclusion that hybrid multimodal deep learning models serve as an up-and-coming solution to the reliable and scalable OSA detection and severity evaluation.

Title: Acoustic Leak Detection Based on Multi-Feature Representation and Weighted Soft-Voting Fusion
Abstract: To address the challenges of complex environmental noise, significant variations in pipeline operating conditions, and a low proportion of leak samples in acoustic leak detection for real water supply networks, this paper formulates pipeline leak recognition as an acoustic anomaly detection and binary classification problem. A machine-learning-based acoustic leak detection method using multi-feature representation and weighted soft-voting fusion is proposed. The experimental data were collected from real water supply networks in Tianjin using a noise correlator, covering acoustic pipeline states under different pipe diameters and materials. First, the raw audio signals are denoised, normalized, and sliced into fixed-length segments. Then, two complementary feature representations are constructed. The first representation consists of MFCC, first-order delta MFCC, second-order delta MFCC, and spectral statistical features, which are used to train XGBoost and SVM models. The second representation is the Log-Mel spectrogram, which is used to train a CRNN model. Finally, a weighted soft-voting strategy is adopted to fuse the predicted probabilities of the three models and obtain the final leak decision. Test experiments show that the proposed fusion model achieves an accuracy of 0.9920, a precision of 0.9366, an F1-score of 0.8636, and an AUC of 0.9868, outperforming the individual models in overall performance. The results indicate that handcrafted acoustic statistical features and deep time-frequency features are complementary, and that the proposed machine-learning fusion method can improve the stability of acoustic anomaly detection and leak recognition in real water supply network scenarios.

Title: Development and Optimization of Knowledge Graph for Human-Machine Interaction Interface of Intelligent Voice Systems
Abstract: In today’s rapidly advancing technological era, the field of artificial intelligence is booming at an astonishing rate, showcasing boundless innovative vitality and enormous potential for development. Title: SURGE Phase 1: An AR/VR-Based Deep Learning Framework for Surgical Scene Analysis
Abstract: Traditional surgical training is constrained by the cost, accessibility, and limited repeatability of cadaveric dissection. To address these challenges, we introduce SURGE (Surgical Training via Unified Reinforcement and Guidance Environment), a framework that merges AI-driven surgical analysis with an immersive Augmented and Virtual Reality (AR/VR) training module. The system integrates a deep learning component for real-time surgical scene understanding including instrument segmentation and procedural workflow analysis with an interactive AR/VR interface developed in Unity 3D for simulated surgical tasks. This interface provides an immersive appendectomy simulation, featuring high-fidelity anatomical models, interactive labelling, and collision-based surgical actions to replicate key procedural steps. Our implementation demonstrates high performance in analysing open surgery video data (achieving a tool mAP of 0.72 and phase recognition precision of 0.88 on the EgoSurgery dataset) and successfully renders a stable, interactive training environment. SURGE aims to establish a scalable and cost-effective platform that enhances surgical skill acquisition through a combination of AI-driven analytics and hands-on virtual practice.

Title: Study on AI-Based Ultra-Low-Rate Speech Coding Objective Quality: A Comprehensive Comparison
Abstract: AI-based ultra-low-rate speech codecs have advanced rapidly in recent years; however, the absence of standardized evaluation benchmarks has made it difficult to objectively compare competing approaches. This paper presents the first comprehensive, multi-dimensional objective evaluation of five representative AI-based ultra-low-rate speech codecs, namely EnCodec, DAC, LongCat-Audio-Codec, Mimi, and BigCodec, across nine objective metric scores spanning six metric families on a unified Chinese-English speech corpus. The nine metrics cover signal fidelity, perceptual quality, speaker similarity, and composite evaluation dimensions. The experimental results reveal a clear performance hierarchy. BigCodec achieves the highest scores across all nine metrics, outperforming all other codecs with its large-scale single-codebook architecture at a bitrate of merely 1.04 kbps. LongCat ranks second with its semantic-acoustic decoupled architecture at the lowest bitrate of 0.87 kbps, followed by Mimi in the middle tier using a Split-RVQ design. EnCodec and DAC, despite their multi-codebook RVQ structure at 1.5 kbps, yield substantially inferior results. Three overarching insights are derived: model capacity and codebook efficiency are the dominant factors for ultra-low-rate performance, the number of RVQ layers is not a reliable performance predictor, and semantic-acoustic integrated encoders offer a viable architectural paradigm at extremely low bitrates. These findings provide empirical guidance for both researchers and industry practitioners in selecting and designing speech codecs for ultra-low-rate applications.

Title: Automated Subtitle Generation in Videos Using AI and FFmpeg

Title: Primal - Dual Proximal Policy Optimization for Constrained Offloading and Scheduling of Multi-User Periodic DAG Tasks in MEC
Abstract: Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) enables latencysensitive IoT applications to execute computation near end devices, but online offloading and scheduling remain challenging when multiple users periodically generate directed acyclic graph (DAG) workflows under heterogeneous edge resources, time-varying wireless links, and explicit feasibility requirements such as deadline-miss and battery-safety constraints. In such multiuser dynamic environments, fixed-penalty reward shaping is often difficult to calibrate across different workload conditions and user scales, which may lead to either insufficient constraint enforcement or overly conservative policies. To address this issue, we propose a structure-aware and constraint-aware reinforcement learning framework for constrained multi-user periodic DAG scheduling in MEC. The proposed policy first uses graph-based DAG encoding to capture workflow topology and node-level dependency information, and then introduces a constraint-aware fusion mechanism that conditions task representations on urgency, congestion status, battery condition, and dual-induced feasibility pressure. In this way, constraint information participates in forward decision making directly, rather than affecting learning only through rewardlevel penalization. On top of this policy architecture, we further develop a weighted behavior cloning (WBC) warm start and a primal-dual proximal policy optimization (PD-PPO) procedure to improve early feasible exploration and regulate long-term constraint satisfaction. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves a better cost-feasibility trade-off than heuristic and representative reinforcement learning baselines. In particular, it attains lower system cost while satisfying the prescribed miss-rate and batterysafety thresholds, and maintains favorable performance under different user scales and workload conditions, demonstrating its effectiveness for constrained online scheduling in MEC systems.

Title: New Progress of Polarization-Spectral and Spatial Multifunctional Optical Imaging Technology
Abstract: Significance Polarization-spectral multidimensional optical information hybrid imaging represents a burgeoning class of ultra-compact and multifunctional imaging modalities. By synergistically integrating spectral and polarimetric dimensions, this technology transcends the limitations of conventional imaging systems that primarily capture two-dimensional spatial intensity. It facilitates a more nuanced detection of multifaceted optical information while maximally preserving the spatial resolution of the target, thereby holding significant implications for intelligent perception and representing a novel frontier in computational imaging. This review systematically elucidates the fundamental principles, technological advancements, and future trajectories of this rapidly evolving field. The significance of this research domain is rooted in the inherent limitations of traditional optical imaging, which largely neglects the rich spectral and polarimetric signatures carried by light waves. Spectral information provides crucial insights into material composition and state, serving as a cornerstone for applications in remote sensing and material identification. Conversely, polarization information is intimately linked to a target's surface morphology, texture, illumination angle, and structural properties, offering distinct advantages in object discrimination, stress analysis, and biomedical diagnostics. The fusion of these dimensions into a single imaging modality—hyperspectropolarimetric imaging—enables the simultaneous acquisition of spatial (x, y), spectral (λ), and full-Stokes polarization data. This creates a high-dimensional descriptor of the observed scene, unlocking unprecedented capabilities for advanced characterization and analysis. Progress The core challenge lies in efficiently encoding and decoding these four tightly coupled dimensions onto a standard intensity-only detector. To address this, various technical architectures have been developed, which can be systematically categorized into four principal frameworks based on their information multiplexing and acquisition strategies. The first category encompasses DTD-SPI architectures. Operating on a principle of sequential scanning, these systems perform temporal modulation across both spectral and polarimetric dimensions independently. Typically reliant on components like AOTFs or rotating waveplates, they achieve high-precision decoupling of Stokes parameters and spectral information. While offering advantages in system simplicity, straightforward reconstruction algorithms, and high data fidelity—making them suitable for static laboratory analyses and material characterization—their fundamental trade-off is between acquisition time and information dimensionality. This results in protracted acquisition times, poor temporal resolution, and extreme sensitivity to motion artifacts, rendering them unsuitable for dynamic or real-time applications. The second category, SP-TD SPI, adopts a compromise by parallelizing spectral acquisition while retaining temporal modulation for polarization. This architecture typically combines a spectrometer or snapshot hyperspectral imager with a time-sequential polarization modulator. Systems like those based on Fourier-transform spectrometry with Wollaston prisms or ferroelectric liquid crystals exemplify this approach. By compressing the acquisition cycle compared to DTD-SPI, these methods offer improved temporal efficiency and are better suited for scenarios like solar observation or environmental monitoring. However, the reliance on sequential polarization measurements still introduces the potential for motion-induced artifacts between frames, limiting true snapshot capability and posing challenges for long-term system stability due to mechanical or active components. The third category, PP-TD SPI, inverts the previous compromise by enabling parallel snapshot acquisition of polarization information while scanning spectrally over time. This architecture leverages technologies like DoFP polarimeters or aperture-separation techniques to capture multiple polarization states in a single exposure. The spectral dimension is then obtained via a tunable filter or a Fourier-transform spectrometer. Techniques such as FTCS fall under this umbrella, where polarization information is encoded onto distinct carrier frequencies within an interferogram. This approach significantly enhances the frame rate and consistency of polarization measurements, making it ideal for observing dynamic polarization phenomena in industrial inspection or atmospheric science. Nevertheless, it remains constrained by the sequential nature of spectral acquisition, facing an inherent trade-off between spectral resolution and total measurement time, and thus cannot achieve instantaneous full-spectrum capture. The fourth and most advanced category is SSPI. Representing the forefront of the field, SSPI architectures achieve true single-exposure, simultaneous acquisition of all four dimensions through a deep integration of optical encoding and computational imaging. This paradigm employs three primary technological routes: 1) FDM, where thick birefringent elements encode polarization information onto spectral carrier frequencies within a single interferogram or spectrum, as pioneered by channeled spectropolarimetry and its evolution in systems like the polarization-difference interference imaging spectrometer. 2) SDM, which utilizes subwavelength nanostructured surfaces to spatially modulate the light field. By carefully designing the phase and polarization response of meta-atoms, a single metasurface can simultaneously perform spectral filtering and polarization splitting, focusing different polarization-spectral channels onto distinct regions of the detector, as demonstrated in spatial multiplexing metalenses for full-Stokes imaging. 3) CIS, which employs coded apertures or random encoders to physically mix the multidimensional information onto the detector. Sophisticated inverse algorithms, particularly deep learning-based neural networks, then serve as high-dimensional decoders to robustly reconstruct the full data cube from the undersampled measurements. SSPI systems offer unparalleled advantages in temporal resolution, system stability, and light throughput, making them uniquely suited for capturing ultrafast dynamic events, such as missile plume detection, combustion diagnostics, and transient biological processes. However, this performance comes at the cost of significantly increased complexity in optical design and reconstruction algorithms, which often involve computationally intensive, noise-sensitive processes with inherent trade-offs between spatial, spectral, and polarimetric resolutions. Conclusions and Prospects The evolution of polarization-spectral imaging clearly demonstrates a trajectory from purely time-sequential methods towards architectures with increasing parallelism, ultimately culminating in snapshot-capable systems. This progression is fundamentally driven by the relentless pursuit of higher temporal resolution, enhanced system stability, and complete information capture. Current research is focused on achieving an optimal balance between spatial, spectral, and polarimetric resolutions, system complexity, and real-time performance. Future developments will be propelled by two key directions. First, the integration of metasurfaces and photonic integrated circuits promises to drive miniaturization, multifunctional integration, and the development of robust, chip-scale instruments. Second, the synergistic combination of artificial intelligence and computational imaging will further enhance encoding efficiency and reconstruction fidelity, and enable intelligent, context-aware decision-making. These advances are poised to propel polarization-spectral imaging from specialized laboratory setups towards widespread deployment in real-world applications, including biomedical diagnostics, industrial quality control, environmental remote sensing, and advanced security and defense systems.

Title: Air Quality Forecasting in Indian Smart Cities Using Artificial Intelligence and Supervised Ensemble Learning Models
Abstract: Public health and environmental sustainability are seriously threatened by the increasing levels of air pollution in India’s cities. Especially in the context of smart cities, accurate air quality forecasting has become crucial for pollution control and policymaking. In order to forecast the Air Quality Index (AQI), this study suggests an AI-based framework that makes use of supervised ensemble machine learning models. This study assesses ensemble learning methods—Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and XGBoost—and compares them to conventional models using multi-year, real-time environmental data from various Indian smart cities. According to the results, ensemble approaches provide better prediction performance in terms of precision, dependability, and flexibility, which makes them useful instruments for intelligent urban environmental management.

Title: AI- Powered Dynamic Music Composition System using LSTM and Transformers

The LSTM part of the system captures the temporal dependencies amongst note sequences, and the Transformer uses the auto-attentionances to capture better global cohesiveness. Title: Hybrid Machine Learning and Deep Learning Approach for Minimum Airfare Prediction
Abstract: Airfare prediction is a challenging task due to dynamic pricing mechanisms, limited real-time visibility into fare updates, and nonlinear demand-supply interactions. This paper focuses on Minimum Fare Prediction: forecasting the lowest airfare a route will reach within the next three days so that users can decide whether to buy now or wait. We propose a hybrid framework that integrates gradient-boosted tree ensembles (XGBoost and Histogram Gradient Boosting Regressor) with temporal neural architectures (1D-CNN, LSTM, and a CNN→LSTM hybrid) trained on a unified feature space. The models are trained and evaluated on a proprietary Pateh.com dataset of approximately 49.7 million flight search records collected over 480 days, one of the largest corpora analyzed in airfare prediction research. Each instance corresponds to the minimum observed daily fare for a specific origin-destination route, enriched with 20 engineered features including calendar descriptors, lagged fares, and rolling 3-day minimum prices. To evaluate practical usefulness, we introduce Regression Weighted Accuracy (RWA), a tolerance-based metric that rewards predictions within a ±10% band of the true price and penalizes larger deviations. Using a time-series cross-validation scheme with 12 folds, our hybrid CNN→LSTM model achieves higher RWA than existing baselines such as k-nearest neighbors, gradient boosting, and bagging regression trees on a key route (IFN-DXB), and reaches up to 0.60 RWA on selected high-traffic routes. The approach is currently being A/B tested within Pateh's production system to provide "buy now vs. wait"recommendations and display the predicted minimum fare for the next three days.

Title: Structured Contextual Deep Learning for Channel Estimation in UAV-OFDM Systems Under Beam Squint and Doppler Effects
Abstract: Reliable channel estimation (CE) in unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs)-assisted orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) systems is fundamentally challenged by mobility-induced Doppler dynamics and frequency-dependent beam squint, which jointly distort pilot observations and reduce channel coherence across subcarriers. These impairments limit the effectiveness of conventional model-based estimators and increase retransmissions, thereby degrading spectral and energy efficiency. This paper develops a structured UAV-assisted OFDM framework that explicitly captures Doppler-induced phase evolution and wideband spatial distortion. Least-squares (LS) estimation and a genie-aided minimum mean square error (MMSE) equalizer are employed as analytical references, where the latter serves as an ideal upper performance bound. Building upon this foundation, we introduce a physics-informed contextual deep learning formulation that refines LS estimates by exploiting cross-subcarrier frequency correlation. The proposed hybrid architecture, termed CRDBA-Net, integrates dilated residual convolution, bidirectional sequential modeling, and attention-based subcarrier weighting to capture multi-scale frequency structure and mobility-driven variation. Extensive bit error rate (BER) evaluations demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently outperforms classical and representative learning-based baselines across a wide signal-to-noise ratio range and under severe Doppler and beam-squint conditions, while approaching genie-aided MMSE performance without requiring prior channel statistics or matrix inversion. The results highlight the potential of structured deep learning to enhance reliability and computational efficiency in high-mobility green UAV communication networks.

Title: Piano Hand Posture Detection Using MobileNetV3 and LSTM on Raspberry Pi 5
Abstract: This study addresses the challenges of piano pedagogy by developing an automated hand posture classification and real-time feedback system. While traditional music education relies on the physical presence of an instructor to correct technical flaws, students often struggle with maintaining ergonomic integrity during solo practice. The proposed system utilizes a spatial-temporal deep learning architecture, integrating MobileNetV3 for efficient spatial feature extraction and Long Short-Term Memory networks for temporal sequence analysis. Hardware implementation is centered on the Raspberry Pi 5 platform paired with a wide-angle camera module to capture a top-down perspective of the performer's hand. The model was trained on a custom-built dataset focusing on the distinction between proper curved finger orientation and improper postures such as flat fingers or dropped wrists. Experimental results demonstrate a testing accuracy of 98.33 percent and a precision of 98.39 percent, proving the effectiveness of the hybrid model in a localized computing environment. The system provides immediate auditory feedback to the user, offering an accessible technological solution to prevent repetitive strain injuries and support technical development in beginner and intermediate piano learners.

Title: Optimized Ensemble Learning with Metaheuristic Feature Selection for Early CKD Diagnosis
Abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a progressive disease and its health-related implications are serious and, in this case, it is mandatory to diagnose the disease at a very early age and in exact manner to render clinical care. This paper presents a hybrid predictive model, which combines the science of sophisticated preprocessing, metaheuristic feature selection, ensemble learning, and automated hyperparameter optimization. A pre-processing of the CKD dataset available in the UCI Machine Learning Repository was done to deal with missing values, class imbalance with SMOTE and outliers with the Interquartile Range. A Swarm Intelligence Optimization (SIO) methodology, a hybrid of Ant Colony Optimization and Particle Swarm Optimization, was used to determine the most informative features with particular gravity, albumin, sugar, hemoglobin and hypertension along with dimensionality reduction and maintaining predictive relevance. The features have been selected were fed into a hybrid ensemble model (AXgC) of AdaBoost, XGBoost and CatBoost are created by taking advantage of the complementary capabilities of boosting algorithms. Hyperparameter tuning with optuna gave the optimal model performance of 96.00% accuracy, 97.92% precision, 95.00% recall, F1-score of 94.92 and AUC of 0.9983. The establishment of comparative analysis with related literature proves that AXgC is a strong, and explainable method of classifier that is superior to individual classifiers and traditional feature selection techniques. The suggested framework provides relevant and interpretable instrument to detect early CKD and it can be used to facilitate personalized treatment planning and informed decision making. Further studies can be taken in the future in this direction to longitudinal data and heterogeneous populations to improve the generalizability and practical application.

Title: Personalized Serious Games for ADHD: A Systematic Review and Evidence Synthesis
Abstract: Approximately 5-7% of children globally experience ADHD, a neurodevelopmental disorder manifesting through difficulties in sustained attention, excessive motor activity, and impaired impulse control. Game based digital interventions have emerged as engaging therapeutic tools, with adaptive personalization proposed to amplify clinical benefits by tailoring task parameters to each user's cognitive profile. We conducted a systematic synthesis of 20 investigations examining adaptive game-based interventions for pediatric and adolescent ADHD populations, spanning publications from January 2011 through August 2024. Our multi database search strategy (five databases) yielded 72 distinct records, with 20 ultimately satisfying eligibility requirements following full text screening. Adaptive features predominantly implemented through artificial intelligence and machine learning algorithms encompassed dynamic difficulty adjustment, individualized performance feedback, and customized reward timing. Relative to fixed difficulty comparison conditions, adaptive interventions produced modest to moderate gains in attentional capacity and working memory performance, alongside variable but predominantly favorable impacts on symptom ratings. User engagement remained uniformly elevated across studies, while treatment emergent adverse effects occurred infrequently. Nevertheless, evidence certainty was constrained by methodological limitations including modest sample sizes, insufficient assessor blinding, and heterogeneous outcome instrumentation resulting in moderate to high bias risk across the corpus. Adaptive game-based platforms thus constitute a provisionally encouraging supplementary approach within multimodal ADHD treatment, particularly for augmenting cognitive capacities. Subsequent investigations should emphasize adoption of uniform assessment instruments, extended monitoring periods, explicit algorithmic documentation, and methodologically robust designs conducive to independent replication and quantitative pooling.

Title: Algorithmic justice and ethical governance in artificial intelligence: a conceptual insight and further research suggestions
Abstract: Purpose – The growing use of algorithmic decision-making has generated a raging scholarly and policy debate on the ethical dimensions of artificial intelligence (AI). Researchers call for the creation of ethical governance systems – including regulatory frameworks, transparency platforms, algorithmic audit systems and accountability mechanisms. Yet, there is limited conceptual understanding of how algorithmic justice principles could be systematically embedded in those governance frameworks. This study aims to develop an integrated framework that explains the ethical challenges associated with AI and how governance mechanisms and algorithmic justice principles can be leveraged to promote responsible and equitable AI deployment. Design/methodology/approach – The study uses a conceptual literature analysis grounded in a structured thematic synthesis of 23 scholarly papers published between 2016 and 2026, focused on AI ethics, algorithmic bias, algorithmic justice and responsible AI governance. The selection process was guided by transparent inclusion and exclusion criteria, consistent with PRISMA 2020 principles. Findings – The synthesis shows that algorithmic decision-making systems produce unintended ethical consequences – including algorithmic bias, lack of transparency and poor accountability mechanisms – when deployed in socially sensitive environments. A distinctive conceptual outcome is the insufficiency of technical fairness interventions in the absence of robust institutional governance, calling for a systemic, governance-first approach wherein algorithmic justice principles are embedded as foundational institutional requirements. Research limitations/implications – This conceptual study opens avenues for empirical research on the ethical challenges of algorithmic decision-making across sectors such as finance, health care, public administration and digital governance. Future research should examine how algorithmic risks manifest in specific institutional contexts and evaluate multi-stakeholder governance models. Practical implications – Regulatory bodies and policymakers should design comprehensive frameworks that foster ethical AI management – encompassing transparency, accountability and fairness requirements. Algorithm impact assessments and auditing systems should become standard governance instruments before AI deployment in socially sensitive domains. Social implications – Embedding algorithmic justice within governance structures is a social justice imperative. When AI systems reproduce historical biases without adequate oversight, they deepen structural inequalities and undermine democratic inclusion. Equitable access to fair and transparent algorithmic decision-making is essential for preserving the rights of marginalised communities. Originality/value – This study advances the existing literature by developing an integrated conceptual framework that systematically embeds algorithmic justice principles within institutional governance structures. Uniquely, it positions institutional governance as the primary mediating mechanism between abstract ethical commitments and the actual ethical performance of AI systems, bridging technology ethics theory and socio-technical systems theory. It distinguishes itself from existing frameworks by incorporating organisational meaning-making and posthumanist perspectives on algorithmic authority.

Title: Deep Neural Network for Jianzi Pu Super-Resolution: Algorithm Design and Performance Analysis
Abstract: Due to hardware limitations of acquisition equipment, existing ancient Guqin tablatures suffer from widespread image degradation and blurriness in notation characters. This study focuses on three representative natural image super-resolution models (FSRCNN, EDSR, and ESRGAN), comparatively verifying their super-resolution performance on non-natural images like Jianzi Pu. Title: Deep Learning-based Few Shot Reverberation Estimation Algorithm and Hardware Co-optimization Framework for Real-time Live Music Signal Acquisition
Abstract: To address the issues of insufficient reverberation modeling accuracy and limited real-time performance in real-time live music signal acquisition under complex acoustic environments, this study proposes an original deep learning-based few-sample reverberation parameter estimation algorithm and a hardware/software co-optimization framework. At the methodological level, a unified model integrating prototype metric learning and continuous parameter regression is constructed. This model extends few-sample classification capabilities to continuous acoustic parameter estimation tasks. At the modeling level, a three-channel complex time-frequency feature model containing real, imaginary, and amplitude information is constructed based on short-time Fourier transform, and energy normalization is used to improve cross-sample distribution consistency. In the feature extraction stage, an improved ResNet structure integrating global context modeling and local attention enhancement is designed. Subsequently, a prototype metric learning mechanism is introduced to construct an embedding space, characterizing acoustic similarity through class center distance, and combining probability mapping to achieve continuous regression of multiple parameters such as reverberation time (T60), direct-to-reverberation ratio (DRR), and absorption coefficient. Simultaneously, a joint dereverberation and beamforming model based on convolutional MLDR-WPE is constructed. At the system implementation level, this test proposes a heterogeneous computing architecture based on STM32, FPGA, and edge GPU, and constructs a task scheduling model oriented towards latency and power consumption. Simultaneously, a structured activation pruning strategy based on Top-K importance selection is designed to reduce inference overhead. Experiments are conducted using a hybrid dataset constructed from 48 hours of real music data and 12,000 simulated room impulse responses, evaluated under 1-shot to 10-shot settings. Results show that the proposed method achieves a T60 estimation MAE of 0.094, a DRR estimation RMSE of 1.73, and a correlation coefficient PCC of 0.89 under 10-shot conditions. In comparison, this result represents a MAE reduction of approximately 25.9% compared to the MAML method. In the speech enhancement task, STOI and PESQ are improved to 0.87 and 2.68, respectively. At the system level, the post-processing latency is reduced from 95 ms to 41 ms, and power consumption is reduced from 4120 mW to 2135 mW. Structured pruning further reduces inference overhead by approximately 38%.

Title: Myers-Briggs Type Indicator Personality Prediction from Reddit Post Using an Integrated Hybrid Model of Naïve Bayes and Random Forest Machine Learning
Abstract: MBTI (Myers-Briggs Type Indicator) personality assessments serve as essential tools to evaluate how well a person fits into particular job roles. Traditional personality tests collects data through self-reported questionnaires which tend to be long and prone to personal biases. Machine Learning-based personality prediction automation solves the limitations of traditional methods. This research will develop a hybrid model using Naïve Bayes and Random Forest to improve accuracy and performance in predicting the MBTI personality test. Training and testing will use a dataset of posts from Reddit. Reddit serves as an excellent data source because it can reflect an individual's personality in the digital world with little to none filters. The dataset will be preprocessed and used to train the models. The models will be combined using the weighted average method. The performance will be evaluated using the F1 score and accuracy metrics. The result, hybrid model achieved a remarkable 95% accuracy for the Intuition/Sensing (N/S) trait. However, the Judging/Perceiving (J/P) trait remains a challenge, revealing a clear trade-off where Random Forest maximizes accuracy (64%) while Naïve Bayes maximizes F1-score (50%). This study concludes that while hybrid models effectively scale to long-form text, the optimal weighting strategy is trait-dependent, with "Abstract"traits (N/S) favoring Ensemble methods and "Structural"traits (J/P) requiring Probabilistic balancing.

Title: Two-Dimensional Acoustic Source Localization in DAS Systems Using Physics-Informed Neural Networks
Abstract: Objective Distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) technology has emerged as a powerful tool for acoustic source localization due to its high sensitivity and long-range monitoring capabilities. By utilizing fiber-optic cables to detect the minute changes in Rayleigh backscattering signals caused by acoustic disturbances, DAS can offer high-resolution, continuous, and large-scale spatial monitoring. Traditional localization algorithms, however, often struggle in real-world applications, especially under noisy conditions or in complex environments. These algorithms tend to suffer from poor noise robustness and limited adaptability, affecting the accuracy and stability of the localization process. The main objective of this research is to address these limitations by proposing a novel approach that incorporates a physics-informed neural network (PINN) into the DAS-based acoustic source localization framework. This approach aims to improve the localization accuracy and robustness of DAS systems, particularly under challenging conditions involving noise and signal variability. Methods The proposed method integrates the time difference of arrival (TDOA) model, a well-established physical model for acoustic source localization, into the neural network training process. In previous work, the physical model is directly coupled with the neural network during backpropagation, which often leads to numerical instability, such as gradient explosion. To overcome this issue, the current study introduces a decoupled embedding strategy, where the physical model is embedded into the neural network without being involved in the gradient computation during training. This strategy ensures stable and efficient convergence while retaining the advantages of physical model integration. In this study, a phase-sensitive optical time-domain reflectometry (φ-OTDR) system is used to validate the proposed method. The φ-OTDR system, with a spatial resolution of 4 m and a coverage area of 25 m², generates a dataset of 6570 samples, simulating real-world acoustic disturbances. The network takes raw DAS waveforms as input, predicting the distances between the acoustic source and several sensor probes. These predicted distances are then fed into the TDOA-based physical model to estimate the location of the source. Unlike traditional methods, which directly rely on data-driven approaches to extract the localization information from raw signals, the proposed method benefits from the inclusion of a physical model that guides the neural network’s learning process and improves its generalization capabilities. Results and Discussions The experimental results indicate that the proposed PINN-based localization framework significantly outperforms traditional data-driven models in terms of both localization accuracy and robustness to noise. The average localization error of the PINN-based method is found to be 4.19 cm, a 37.74% reduction over the traditional data-driven neural network methods. Furthermore, the robustness of the model is tested under various noise conditions, including Gaussian white noise (signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 10 dB) and background noise (SNR of 11 dB). The PINN-based approach shows a reduction in localization error by 27.4% and 54.3%, respectively, demonstrating its superior noise robustness compared to data-driven models. The results are illustrated in several figures that quantify the performance of the proposed method. For instance, Fig. 3 compares the error distributions of the PINN-based model and the data-driven model, showing that the PINN-based model results in a more concentrated error distribution along the y-axis, thus achieving higher localization accuracy. Similarly, Fig. 4 depicts the cumulative distribution of localization errors, revealing that the PINN-based model consistently produces lower errors across the entire range of test samples. Specifically, at the 80% cumulative probability mark, the PINN model achieves an error of 0.027 m, while the data-driven model reaches 0.152 m, indicating a significant advantage in terms of accuracy. In addition to accuracy, the proposed model also excels in terms of robustness and generalization, particularly in noisy environments. Fig. 6 and Fig. 7 show that, under various noise levels, the PINN-based model consistently delivers lower errors compared to the data-driven model. This advantage is most evident in low SNR conditions, where the traditional model’s performance degrades significantly, whereas the PINN model maintains stable and reliable results. These figures highlight the importance of incorporating physical knowledge into the learning process, which allows the model to perform better under complex and uncertain noise conditions. One of the key innovations of this work is the decoupled embedding strategy, which addresses the gradient instability issues encountered when the physical model is directly coupled with the neural network. By keeping the physical model static during training, the method avoids common pitfalls such as gradient explosion and ensures more stable convergence. This improvement is particularly crucial in acoustic localization tasks, which are sensitive to noise and environmental changes. Additionally, the use of physical constraints as soft regularizations helps the network focus on physically feasible solutions, further enhancing its generalization ability. Conclusions In conclusion, this paper presents a novel PINN-based framework for acoustic source localization in DAS systems, which effectively combines the advantages of deep learning and physical modeling. The proposed method significantly improves localization accuracy, reducing the average localization error by 37.74% compared to traditional data-driven models. Moreover, the framework demonstrates robust performance under noisy conditions, with localization errors decreasing by up to 54.3% in challenging noise environments. These results suggest that the integration of physical models into the neural network training process provides a powerful tool for improving the accuracy and robustness of DAS-based localization systems. The PINN-based framework offers a promising solution for real-world deployment of DAS systems, particularly in complex acoustic environments where traditional methods struggle. By leveraging both data-driven techniques and physical knowledge, this approach paves the way for more reliable and efficient acoustic source localization in large-scale, distributed sensing systems. Future research focuses on extending this framework to three-dimensional localization tasks and exploring its potential in a wider range of applications, including structural health monitoring, environmental monitoring, and security surveillance. The ability to seamlessly integrate physical models into deep learning systems offers a generalizable approach that can be adapted to other inverse problems in complex sensor networks.

Title: Resource-Efficient Multimodal Large Language Models for Context-Aware Hate Speech Detection
Abstract: Social media platforms rely on automatic hate speech detection for content moderation. Many online posts are multimodal, meaning they contain more than one form of data; they could be a mix of audio, images, videos, or text. Memes, a combination of an image paired with a short text, need contextual understanding from both modalities to comprehend the full meaning. While state-of-the-art Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have strongly filtered out the content with great accuracy, heavy computational resources are needed to run these models, which limits practical deployment. This study investigates whether resource-efficient MLLMs with fewer than four billion parameters are worth deploying by comparing their performance with a unimodal text-only baseline. Qwen2-VL-2B, Granite-Vision-3.2-2B, and DeepSeek-VL2-Tiny are fine-tuned using Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (LoRA) for hate speech detection and evaluated on the MMHS150K dataset. The primary metric used for the results is the Macro F1-score and accuracy. Qwen2-VL-2B had the highest Macro F1-score of 0.643, outperforming the unimodal text-only LSTM baseline of 0.605. The results show that a resource-efficient MLLM can outperform a unimodal model for multimodal hate speech detection.

Title: Benchmarking Models Under Data Scarcity Using Synthetic Datasets
Abstract: Benchmarking machine learning models typically assumes access to large, representative evaluation datasets. In privacy-constrained settings such as enterprise document processing, this assumption often fails: evaluation data is sensitive, user-owned, and difficult to share, making data scarcity a structural constraint rather than a temporary limitation. As a result, comparative model evaluation is frequently performed on small or proxy datasets, raising concerns about the reliability of benchmark conclusions.This paper examines whether synthetically generated datasets can serve as evaluation benchmarks under such constraints. Rather than focusing on absolute performance, we study whether synthetic benchmarks preserve relative model behavior observed on real data. We propose a task-conditioned synthetic benchmarking framework and instantiate it in the context of document image enhancement, generating paired clean and de-graded document images under controlled variation in content, layout, and degradation processes.Using six architectures spanning four architecture families - encoder-decoder networks, dilated convolution models, feature pyramid networks, and attention-based hybrids - evaluated across four synthetic variants, we analyze the conditions under which synthetic benchmarks preserve model rankings. Our results show that pairwise model orderings are reliably pre-served when performance gaps exceed approximately 1 dB Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR), while rankings become unstable when models perform within 0.5 dB of each other. These findings identify both the potential and the boundaries of synthetic benchmarks as evaluation instruments, providing practical guidance for responsible model comparison in data-scarce, privacy-constrained environments.

Title: The Impact of Negative Perceptions of Generative AI on Engineering Students’ Academic Performance
Abstract: The integration of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) into higher education has intensified debates surrounding academic integrity, cognitive skill erosion, and educational equity, particularly within engineering education. While existing literature frequently assumes that negative student perceptions of GenAI undermine academic performance, empirical evidence directly testing this assumption remains limited. This study examined the relationship between engineering students’ negative perceptions of GenAI and their academic performance using a cross-sectional quantitative correlational design. Data were collected from 380 undergraduate engineering students at a public university in the Philippines. Six theoretically grounded dimensions of negative perception (i.e., academic integrity concerns, devaluation of human effort, challenges to higher-order thinking, data security risks, fears of skill erosion, and digital divide concerns) were measured using a validated survey instrument (McDonald’s ω = 0.953). Academic performance was operationalized using cumulative grade point average (GPA). Pearson correlation and hierarchical multiple regression analyses were conducted. Results revealed no statistically significant relationships between any dimension of negative GenAI perception and academic performance. Regression models demonstrated minimal explanatory power, indicating that students’ skepticism toward GenAI we’re not found to be significantly associated with academic performance within the scope of the variables measured. These findings challenge deterministic narratives that portray negative AI perceptions as direct impediments to student achievement. The study contributes empirical evidence to debates on AI in engineering education by demonstrating that student skepticism may reflect ethical and epistemic awareness rather than disengagement or diminished competence. The findings support pedagogically grounded and context-responsive approaches to GenAI integration, aligning with Sustainable Development Goal 4 (Quality Education) and Sustainable Development Goal 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure), particularly in promoting inclusive, ethical, and evidence-informed educational innovation.

Title: Artificial intelligence-based expert trajectory guidance in an ex vivo robot-assisted renal wound suturing training model
Abstract: Introduction – Renorrhaphy is one of the most technically demanding steps in robot-assisted partial nephrectomy, requiring expert-level suturing to ensure adequate hemostasis and long-term renal function preservation, yet acquiring such proficiency requires extensive practice under expert supervision. Although artificial intelligence has been increasingly applied to perioperative surgical care, its potential to learn expert operative patterns from standard surgical video and translate them into real-time visual guidance for surgical training remains largely unexplored. Here we developed and evaluated an artificial intelligence framework that learns expert suturing trajectories from standard endoscopic video and provides intraoperative visual guidance for renal wound suturing training. Methods – A multicenter expert trajectory dataset was constructed from robot-assisted partial nephrectomy procedures performed at two medical centers, supported by a standardized data pipeline comprising 28-class scene annotation, temporal phase labeling of complete suturing actions, and sliding-window trajectory sampling. Building on these data, we developed a Scene-Aware Transformer that integrates instrument motion with surgical scene context to predict future trajectories, and prospectively evaluated the resulting guidance system in a pilot ex vivo porcine kidney feasibility training study involving 24 novice trainees. Results – The dataset comprised 18, 515 annotated frames, 806 complete suturing actions, and 24, 897 valid trajectory samples. On the independent held-out institutional test set, the model achieved an average displacement error of 34.25 pixels and a final displacement error of 52.54 pixels, with an end-to-end inference latency of 32.7 ms under laboratory computational conditions. In the prospective training study, novice trainees who received expert trajectory guidance significantly outperformed the unguided control group across six of eight performance measures by the final assessment, and maintained their advantage during unguided evaluation sessions. Discussion – These preliminary findings suggest that artificial intelligence-derived expert trajectory guidance may support short-term skill acquisition for renal wound suturing. As the prospective training component was a single-institution feasibility study without long-term retention or clinical transfer assessment, larger multicenter randomized trials are warranted before broader integration into surgical training curricula.

Title: Deep Learning-Assisted Personalized Piano Teaching in Blended Learning Environments
Abstract: Piano teaching has long relied on in-class instruction and teacher experience, leaving after-class practice poorly monitored and inefficient. To address this gap, this study integrates deep learning into personalized piano teaching within a blended learning environment, and constructs a closed-loop model: performance data collection—feature recognition—individual diagnosis—tiered intervention—dynamic feedback. A 12-week controlled experiment is conducted in a university piano course, with indicators including rhythm stability, pitch accuracy, fluency, musical expressiveness, self-regulation, and practice behaviors. Results show that deep learning does not replace teachers but provides full-process traceable diagnosis, effectively identifying individual differences and improving personalized intervention efficiency. This study offers implications for technology-supported blended learning and personalized instruction in higher arts education..

Title: Explainable Deep Learning for Automated Classification of Skeletal and Tumor Pathologies in 3D Volumetric Medical Imaging
Abstract: Accurate identification and classification of 3D mesh data in medical imaging are crucial for various clinical and research applications, including surgical planning, anatomical analysis, and disease diagnosis. In recent years, the application of deep learning techniques to medical imaging has gained significant traction, particularly in the analysis of 3D mesh data. This study presents a comprehensive explainable AI-based deep learning framework for classifying tumorous and skeletal structures in 3D medical data. The models, including CNN, ResNet-18, VGG-16, and EfficientNet-B0, are trained and evaluated on MedShapeNet, a large-scale dataset comprising over 100,000 3D medical shapes spanning bones, organs, vessels, muscles, and surgical instruments. A robust preprocessing pipeline is developed to transform raw Stereolithography (STL) neuro-anatomical structures into normalised feature vectors, ensuring consistent representation across varying mesh complexities. A multifaceted model evaluation approach is employed, combining quantitative metrics with advanced visualisation techniques to gain insight into the model’s decision-making processes. Experimental results show that the VGG-16 model achieved the highest test accuracy of 99.15% and an F1 score of 99.16%, closely followed by ResNet-18 with an accuracy of 98.87%. These findings highlight the effectiveness of VGG in improving deep learning performance for medical mesh classification tasks.

Title: A Web-Enabled AI System for Real-Time Piano Fingering Optimization in Music Education
Abstract: Traditional piano fingering instruction often suffers from low efficiency and limited personalization. To address these limitations, the authors present a web-enabled AI system that supports real-time, adaptive fingering guidance in educational settings. The system fuses Musical Instrument Digital Interface (MIDI) data and three-dimensional finger joint tracking to model both musical and ergonomic dimensions, and it employs a hybrid graph neural network and reinforcement learning framework to generate comfortable, accurate fingering suggestions. A confidence-based difficulty adjustment strategy and miniature haptic feedback create a closed-loop learning experience, while cloud–edge deployment ensures responsiveness and privacy. Evaluated through technical performance, electromyography fatigue, cognitive load, and motivation metrics, the system significantly improves students' consistency, engagement, and satisfaction—without increasing teacher workload. This work offers a scalable, AI-driven approach to skill-based music education.

Title: Video Segmentation of Deformable Instruments in Ultrasound-Guided Interventional Surgeries for Structural Heart Diseases
Abstract: The increasing incidence of structural heart disease has emerged as a significant global health challenge. Recently, ultrasound-guided interventional techniques have demonstrated the potential to replace traditional treatment methods due to their advantages, including the absence of radiation risks and the ability to provide real-time monitoring during surgeries. This study addresses challenges in instrument identification caused by factors such as low imaging resolution, variable instrument morphology in different sections, and the tendency for instruments to disappear or become obstructed. To tackle these issues, we propose a deep learning-based method for Video Instance Segmentation (VIS). The proposed method consists of three key components: 1) A frame-level detector extracts features from each image frame and generates queries for object instances. 2) A model architecture integrates the spatial feature extraction capabilities of convolutional neural networks with the temporal modeling capabilities of transformers, utilizing a windowed attention mechanism to capture inter-frame dependencies. 3) A multi-video segment joint memory learning mechanism is introduced, which stores historical query features in a shared memory bank. This enhances tracking robustness, particularly when instruments disappear or deform. Experimental results show that the model achieves an Average Precision (AP) of 40.640, significantly surpassing the performance of other mainstream VIS models. This method effectively improves the accuracy of instrument recognition and tracking stability in ultrasound images, thereby enhancing the safety and success rate of interventional surgeries. It also contributes to the promotion of this advanced surgical technique.

Title: The Scale for AI Literacy in Health Care Workers: Development and Validation
Abstract: Background: AI is increasingly embedded in health care systems; yet, validated instruments for assessing AI literacy among health care workers remain limited. Existing measures are often designed for students or general populations and may not adequately reflect competencies required in health care practice. Objective: This study aimed to develop and validate the Scale for AI Literacy in Health Care Workers (SAIL-HCW), a new instrument designed to assess AI literacy across domains relevant to health care practice. Methods: A 3-phase instrument development study was conducted. In Phase 1, conceptual domains were identified through a literature review, and an initial item pool was generated. In Phase 2, content validity was assessed by 4 subject-matter experts, and face validity was evaluated with 26 health care workers. Feedback from both groups informed item refinement. In Phase 3, psychometric testing was conducted using survey data from health care workers in a single health care organization. A total of 425 participants completed the survey. The dataset was randomly split into 2 subsamples for exploratory factor analysis (n=212) and confirmatory factor analysis (n=213). Model fit was evaluated using unidimensional, correlated-factor, higher-order, and bifactor models. Reliability was assessed using Cronbach alpha and McDonald omega. Item performance was examined using corrected item-total correlations (CITC), item discrimination analysis, and inter-item correlations. Construct validity was assessed using prior AI training, frequency of AI use, and self-rated AI literacy. Results: Phase 2 feedback from experts and health care workers supported the proposed domain structure and informed item refinement, including revision of wording and removal of redundant items. The final SAIL-HCW consists of 14 items across 7 domains, including AI concept, data fluency, AI evaluation, AI in practice, ethics and regulation, AI in system, and continuous learning. In Phase 3, the bifactor model showed the best fit compared with alternative models (comparative fit index and Tucker-Lewis index>0.93; root-mean-square error of approximation<0.06; standardized root-mean-square residual<0.05), indicating a general AI literacy factor alongside domain-specific factors. Internal consistency for the total scale was high (Cronbach α=0.937; ω=0.938). Domain-level reliability ranged from 0.635 to 0.797. All items significantly discriminated between high- and low-scoring groups (P<.001), with CITC values ranging from 0.570 to 0.785. Construct validity was supported, with higher SAIL-HCW scores observed among participants with prior AI training, higher frequency of AI use, and higher self-rated AI literacy (all P<.001). Conclusions: The SAIL-HCW provides initial evidence of validity and reliability for assessing AI literacy among health care workers. Findings suggest that AI literacy may be represented as a general construct with additional domain-level components. The scale may be useful for research and educational evaluations, although further validation in other settings is required.

Title: A lightweight alignment-aware DBNet for surgical instrument code detection
Abstract: Reliable detection of engraved surface codes on surgical instruments is essential for end-to-end traceability, yet remains challenging in practice because metallic reflection, motion blur, scale variation and weak textures often hinder stable localization. Here we present LA-DBNet, a lightweight detection framework built on DBNet for this task. The model uses MobileNetV4 with LiteFPN to reduce complexity while preserving multi-scale feature representations. To better capture the elongated structure and edge features of engraved codes, we introduce a Directional Edge Collaborative Alignment (DECA) module to improve cross-scale feature alignment, and embed an Efficient Channel Attention (ECA) mechanism in the high-resolution feature layer to enhance responses relevant to the target and suppress noise caused by reflections. We further incorporate a region-weighted consistency learning strategy during training to improve robustness to degraded samples. On our surgical instrument code dataset, LA-DBNet achieves an F1 of 95.8%, improving DBNet by 3.6 percentage points, while reducing parameters to 3.35 M and reaching 33.6 FPS. On ICDAR2015, it attains an F1 of 86.1%. These results show that LA-DBNet improves detection performance while substantially reducing model size and maintaining efficient inference in surgical instrument code detection.

Title: Clinical cognition in the age of cardiovascular AI
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly entering cardiovascular medicine through electrocardiography, imaging, wearable monitoring, risk prediction, heart failure management, and clinical decision support. Its value, however, should not be judged only by technical accuracy, speed, or computational sophistication. Cardiovascular care requires clinicians and teams to convert multimodal, longitudinal, incomplete, and context-dependent information into action under uncertainty. This Perspective argues that AI should be understood not as a replacement for clinical intuition, but as a cognitive instrument that reshapes how cardiovascular teams perceive, prioritize, reason, decide, communicate, and learn. Building on dual-process theories of clinical reasoning, the manuscript proposes that AI can support both rapid pattern recognition (System 1) and slower analytic reasoning (System 2), while also creating new vulnerabilities when automation bias, alert fatigue, poor explainability, dataset shift, hidden inequity, or responsibility drift distort judgment. The central standard should therefore move from algorithm-centered performance to accountable intelligence: AI that is accurate, explainable, locally validated, equitable, auditable, monitored across its lifecycle, and embedded within explicit clinical governance.

Title: Cloud Detection of OMPS Nadir Mapper Radiance Data Using Deep Learning Techniques
Abstract: The ozone mapping and profiler suite-nadir mapper (OMPS-NM) is a key satellite instrument for retrieving and analyzing ozone concentrations in both the total column and different atmospheric layers. Given the relatively large footprint of the OMPS-NM sensor, accurately detecting cloud-contaminated fields of view (FOVs) at the subpixel scale is essential for both calibration/validation efforts and the direct assimilation of sensor data record (SDR) radiances into numerical weather prediction (NWP) models. To address this challenge, a novel subpixel cloud detection model has been developed using deep learning techniques. The model is trained using reference cloud information from the visible infrared imaging radiometer suite (VIIRS), which is collocated on the same satellite platform as OMPS-NM. The training dataset consists of globally matched NOAA-21 OMPS-NM and VIIRS measurements, which are randomly selected from different months in 2024 to capture a wide range of atmospheric and surface conditions. For each OMPS-NM footprint, the collocated VIIRS cloud mask is used as the ground truth to train a deep neural network (DNN) on the corresponding OMPS-NM spectral signatures. To reduce model complexity and improve efficiency, the OMPS-NM radiance spectra are transformed into principal components (PCs), with only the top 14 PCs used as input features. The model's performance is evaluated globally against the VIIRS-derived cloud mask. Results show a strong spatial agreement between the model predictions and VIIRS cloud data, achieving a high global mean detection accuracy of 89%. Regionally, the model performs slightly better over oceans (90%) than over land (87%). Further comparison with the operational OMPS-NM effective cloud fraction (ECF), derived from NOAA's total ozone product, demonstrates that the deep learning model is significantly more effective at identifying subpixel clouds that are often missed by the operational method. This enhanced detection capability highlights the model's potential for improving the accuracy and reliability of OMPS-NM science products.

Title: Multimodal Deep Learning for Human Fatigue Detection and Classification Using Speech and Text Modalities
Abstract: Automated detection of human fatigue is of critical importance for a wide range of applications including occupational safety, driving safety, and human performance monitoring. While existing fatigue detection systems predominantly rely on image processing and physiological signal-based approaches, the rich acoustic and linguistic information available in speech signals remains largely underexplored. In this study, we propose a multimodal deep learning framework for binary fatigue classification (energetic vs. fatigued) using speech signals. A purpose-built dataset was constructed via neural speech synthesis under controlled acoustic parameters and prosodic disfluency injection to simulate energetic and fatigued speaking conditions. Three multimodal fusion strategies - Early Fusion, Mid Fusion, and Late Fusion - are evaluated, each combining acoustic features (Mel-spectrogram and handcrafted audio descriptors) with linguistic features derived via automatic speech recognition (ASR) followed by a BERT language model. An audio-only CNN+MLP baseline (82.5% accuracy) is also provided for comparison. Under a speaker-dependent evaluation protocol, the Late Fusion model achieves the highest AUC-ROC of 0.978 with 94.7% accuracy. We further evaluate generalisation through a speaker-independent split, where Late Fusion achieves 85.4% accuracy, and through a noise-robustness analysis at multiple SNR levels. These findings establish that speech-based multimodal approaches offer a powerful and complementary alternative to camera-dependent and physiological methods for fatigue detection.

Title: Robustness design and analysis of airborne visual perception based on deep ensemble learning
Abstract: The visual perception function based on machine learning is crucial for enhancing situational awareness or autonomous flight capabilities of aircraft in complex environments，and its performance has significant impact on flight safety. However，the inherent probabilistic nature of machine learning techniques poses substantial challenges to meeting airworthiness safety objectives，thereby hindering their application in airborne systems. To address this issue，a robustness-oriented design method for airborne visual perception based on deep ensemble learning is established. First，a highly representative dataset is generated based on the operational design domain，and a K-fold cross-validation method based on CW-SSIM is proposed to improve the independence between the training and validation sets with limited data. Second，based on the YOLO architecture，depthwise separable convolution is introduced，and three optimized base learners are designed to address different detection needs through multi-scale feature fusion，en⁃ hanced focus on small object detection，and fine-grained feature extraction. Finally，an ensemble learning method is designed using a weighted adaptive fusion strategy to dynamically adjust the weights of base learners，thereby improv⁃ ing the model accuracy and robustness. Experimental results show that the ensemble learning model outperforms de⁃ tection box fusion algorithms such as NMS and WBF. When the IoU is not less than 0. 7，the ensemble model im⁃ proves the average P-value，R-value，and F1 score by at least 11. 36%，2. 06%，and 6. 78%，respectively，com⁃ pared to a single model. When the IoU is no less than 0. 75，the AP value increases by at least approximately 3%. These results indicate that proposed method significantly enhances target detection accuracy and robustness in com⁃ plex environments，effectively reducing false positives and missed detections，and provides technical assurance for the safe flight of aircraft.

Title: A Machine Learning Framework for Malicious URL Detection with LabVIEW-Based Visualization of Phishing Attacks
Abstract: The rapid growth of phishing campaigns and malicious web services has transformed URLs (Uniform Resource Locators) into a primary attack vector in modern cyber threats. Traditional blacklist-based filtering and simple pattern-matching techniques are often unable to keep pace with the evolving landscape of URL obfuscation strategies. This paper proposes a machine learning framework for malicious URL detection, complemented by a LabVIEW-based virtual instrument that visualizes and simulates phishing attacks. A focused taxonomy of phishing URL manipulation techniques is developed, including sound squatting, combo squatting, homograph attacks, typo squatting, subdomain squatting and TLD (Top-Level Domain) squatting, and representative examples for each category are illustrated within the virtual instrument. This interactive environment allows users to explore how small lexical and structural changes in URLs can bypass naive security filters. On the detection side, lexical and statistical features are extracted, such as URL length, character entropy, special symbol density, subdomain depth and brand-similarity indicators and several supervised machine learning models are evaluated for binary classification of benign versus malicious URLs. Experimental results show that tree-based ensemble methods outperform linear baselines, achieving high detection rates with low false-positive rates. Finally, potential avenues are outlined for integrating the proposed framework into real-world security workflows and for using it as an educational tool to demonstrate both the mechanics and the risks of phishing attacks.

Title: Advances in the integration of near-infrared spectroscopy and artificial intelligence for food quality and safety assessment
Abstract: Near-infrared spectroscopy (NIR) has been widely adopted in food quality and safety assessment owing to its inherent advantages— including rapid analysis, non-destructive measurement, and operational simplicity—that enable high-throughput, real-time, and on-site monitoring without sample preparation. However, NIR measurements are inherently susceptible to experimental interferences— such as ambient temperature fluctuations, optical path variations, and inconsistencies in solid sample mass— leading to spectral instability. Moreover, the technique suffers from intrinsic limitations, including a low signal-to-noise ratio, broad and overlapping absorption bands, and poorly resolved characteristic peaks. In recent years, the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) has offered robust, data-driven solutions to enhance the accuracy, sensitivity, and robustness of NIR-based analysis. The integration of AI algorithms with NIR enables efficient extraction of latent patterns from complex, high-dimensional spectral data—thereby substantially improving predictive performance and analytical reliability. This AI-enhanced NIR paradigm has emerged as a prominent and rapidly expanding research frontier. This review first articulates the foundational methodological framework underpinning NIR-AI integration, then provides a critical synthesis of representative applications in non-destructive food quality and safety assessment— spanning meat and poultry products, cereal-and oilbased foods, and liquid beverages—with explicit attention to algorithmic rationale, validation rigor, and quantitative performance metrics. It further critically examines key methodological challenges and practical constraints in real-world implementation—such as spectral variability across heterogeneous food matrices, limited generalizability of AI models to unseen production batches, and the scarcity of standardized, publicly accessible NIR-AI benchmark datasets—and concludes with a forward-looking perspective on translational pathways toward routine deployment, including instrument-algorithm co-design, regulatory validation frameworks, and edge-AI-enabled portable systems. Collectively, this synthesis aims to inform evidence-based research prioritization and accelerate the adoption of NIR-AI solutions in food safety governance and quality control practice.

Title: Development of the Digidiadem digital application for telemedical self-examination of speech and memory with self-assessment using artificial intelligence for quick detection of cognitive disorders – study protocol
Abstract: Aim: With the growing number of older adults and the declining number of younger specialists, assessment of memory and language functions in-person will become increasingly challenging. Digital applications will therefore gain importance, yet such tools are currently lacking in the Czech Republic. The aim of this study is to present the methodology of a unique digital application designed to independently examine and automatically evaluate memory and language functions in a home environment without the presence of an administrator. Methods: The Digital Diagnostics of Dementia, with the acronym Digidiadem derived from the initial parts of the words, is based on tasks that can be administered in the form of a structured interaction with a computer. It includes sentence learning and recall, scene description and recall of information from the scene, naming and recall of 20 pictures, names of animal, and repetition of pseudowords. This will be followed by in-person assessment using standardized instruments: the Repeatable Battery for the Assessment of Neuropsychological Status (RBANS), the Mississippi Aphasia Screening Test (MAST), and the certified tests Amnesia Light and Brief Assessment (ALBA) and Picture Naming and Immediate Recall (PICNIR), along with mood and functional independence questionnaires. The study will include cognitively normal individuals without neuropsychiatric history and with normal RBANS scores, as well as patients with mild cognitive impairment and mild dementia. Digital and in-person test results will be correlated and subsequently compared using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Results: Scores from the in-person battery will characterize cognitive performance across groups and at the same time verify the concurrent validity of the Digidiadem. The discriminative validity of the Digidiadem application will be evaluated using inferential statistics and AUC analysis. Conclusion: The project will result in a modern digital application, the Digidiadem, intended for self-assessment of memory and language functions across various settings. Automated self-evaluation using artificial intelligence methods will provide users with information about their cognitive functions and enable convenient detection of cognitive impairment.

Title: Early Detection of Heart Disease Using Hybrid Ensemble Learning: Comparative Analysis of XGBoost-LightGBM
Abstract: Cardiovascular disease is one of the leading causes of mortality in the world, which requires attractive and efficient screening instruments to support the risk stratification of the population. This research compares four different computational models such as Stacked Autoencoder coupled with a Random Forest (SAE+RF), a hybrid gradient-boosting model with XGBoost and LightGBM, a meta-learning Stacking Classifier, and a Voting Classifier, using an 8,763-record clinical dataset available on Kaggle. The results of the experiments show that the XGBoost-LightGBM hybrid has the best generalization at 96.05% test accuracy, followed by the Stacking Classifier (89.05%), Voting Classifier (88.75%), and SAE+RF architecture (73.45%). These results prove the hypothesis that heterogeneous fusion significantly overcomes the individual learner. The suggested methodology provides a non-invasive, scalable, administration of cardiac risk assessment tool in early stages, which has accurate diagnosis to decrease disease-related mortality because of timely clinical intervention.

Title: Resilient Unsupervised Deep Learning for Data Denoising via Noise-to-Semiclean Training
Abstract: Seismic data denoising is crucial for improving signal quality in both passive seismic monitoring and active subsurface exploration, enabling more reliable interpretation. In this work, a novel unsupervised deep learning approach with robust learning is proposed for denoising seismic data. The method begins by transforming the seismic data into a 2-D representation. This transformation extracts localized time–frequency features that capture the signal’s frequency variation over time. To enhance the robustness of the deep neural network’s learning process, a self-noise cancellation stage based on vector space projections is incorporated. This allows the network to learn sparse representations of the signals, achieved through a specifically tailored loss function. Comparative evaluations demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a strong denoising performance, with an average signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) improvement of 15 dB, by effectively learning sparse features. Benchmarked against other unsupervised methods, it consistently shows superior performance. Extensive experiments on synthetic, pseudosynthetic, and field datasets further validate its effectiveness in significantly enhancing the SNR of seismic data. The proposed framework is validated on passive seismic data and shows strong potential for extension to active seismic scenarios, as well as to general signal enhancement applications, including audio signal processing, biomedical, wireless communications, and radar systems.
