Title: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Detection Using Machine Learning and Lung Sound Analysis
Abstract: COPD is a persistent respiratory illness which leads to airflow obstruction and difficulty in breathing, and usually goes unnoticed till later on in life. Traditional diagnostic procedures including spirometry and CT scans involve costly equipment and certified personnel, and thus, it is challenging to make an early diagnosis particularly in the rural and resource constrained regions. As an answer to this challenge, this project suggests a machine learning-based system of lung sound analysis early COPD detection. The system enables users to capture and store respiratory sound signals and preprocess them to extract all pertinent acoustic features by eliminating noise and using Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC). A Deep Belief Network (DBN) is used to classify these features to differentiate COPD and non- COPD. The trained model is combined to a web-based application which gives result of prediction and the degree of confidence. The further option of a health questionnaire, doctor recommendations according to the location, precautionary information, and awareness chatbot make the site more usable and accessible to healthcare. The use of conventional performance indicators, including accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, confusion matrix is experimentally proven to show that the proposed system can deliver reliable and accurate COPD detection. The solution is a low-cost, non- invasive, and scalable way of performing early screening and remote respiratory health monitoring and is part of the enhanced management of the disease and early medical intervention.

Title: Electricity Consumption Forecasting Using Deep Learning Algorithms
Abstract: Forecasting electricity demand will be an essential instrument in energy systems of the future, as it enables optimal power allocation, facilitates load regulation, and supports sustainability planning at the strategic level. This work brings a single deep learning framework that is capable of short-term electricity consumption prediction. The Household Electric Power Consumption data set was employed for model creation and testing. The original time-series data have been converted to hourly intervals and were made more informative through the introduction of lag-based and rolling statistical feature engineering for the preservation of temporal dependencies. Six progressive architectures ConvLSTM, CNN-LSTM, CNN-TCN, LSTM-XGBoost, TCN-XGBoost, and ConvTCN were trained and tested by RMSE, MAE, MAPE, and R<sup>2</sup> criteria. The experimental results reveal that the CNN-LSTM architecture outperforms other models in predictive performance, achieving an RMSE of 0.555 kW and an R<sup>2</sup> value of 0.556. The interplay of convolutional feature extraction with sequential learning is largely responsible for the outstanding forecasting accuracy achieved, thus enabling more reliable and intelligent demand management in future smart grids.

Title: Advancing Antibacterial Research: Predictive Modeling of Gracilaria verrucosa Extracts Using Machine Learning
Abstract: The increasing need in new antibacterial agents has prompted an increased effort to identify bioactive compounds within the marine environment e.g. Gracilaria verrucosa. In our work, we used predictive modeling methods to estimate the antibacterial potential of G. verrucosa extracts on a machine learning basis. Three models were trained and tested on experimental antibacterial datasets with the use of the Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Regression (SVR) and Elastic Net Regression (ENR) models. Of these, RF was the best performer with an accuracy of 93.8, precision of 92.9, recall of 92.2, and F1-score of 92.5, compared to both the SVR (87.1% accuracy) and ENR (81.2% accuracy). RF has been demonstrated to be the most dependable model to predict antibacterial activity because of the ensemble-based character of this interaction that provides effective management of nonlinear biological interactions. These results underscore the possibility of machine learning as a powerful screening instrument of marine algal extracts to minimize the use of laborious in vivo methods and expedite the process of identifying novel therapeutic leads.

Title: Deployment of Quantized Deep Noise Suppression on Real-Time Edge Platforms
Abstract: Many audio devices benefit considerably from noise suppression algorithms, including hearing aids, earphones, and headsets. In recent years, with the advent of artificial intelligence in several applications, neural network-based denoising algorithms have also become essential in the audio signal processing field. However, many of the previously mentioned devices target embedded systems, i.e., architectures with limited computational resources. This paper addresses the challenge of efficient deployment of neural networks on embedded devices while meeting tight real-time constraints. In this paper, we extend our previous work on integrating NeuralCasting with the Patmos time-predictable processor, providing a WCET analysis and comparing the performance against state-of-the-art AI frameworks (TensorFlow Lite and ONNX Runtime) for deployment on embedded systems and other hardware platforms (RaspberryPi).

Title: Research on Intelligent Recognition Algorithm for Visual Inspection Data of Measuring Instruments Based on Deep Learning
Abstract: This paper proposes an intelligent recognition algorithm (MIF-Net) for visual inspection data of measuring instruments based on deep learning. The algorithm focuses on instrument area localization, dial structure analysis, key visual element enhancement, and intelligent reading regression. It constructs an end-to-end recognition framework consisting of a lightweight visual encoder, a multi-scale scale perception module, a pointer-scale relationship modeling module, and an uncertainty-constrained reading decoder. First, an improved convolutional visual backbone is used to extract local texture and global structural features of the instrument image. Second, the multi-scale scale perception module enhances the response of fine-grained scale lines, digit characters, and pointer edges. Third, a pointer-scale relationship modeling mechanism is introduced to jointly encode the pointer direction, scale distribution, and instrument range, thereby improving reading stability in complex backgrounds. Finally, uncertaintyconstrained loss is used to adaptively adjust the weights of lowquality image samples, reducing the negative impact of reflective, blurred, and occluded samples on model training. Experimental simulations constructed a visual inspection dataset for metrology instruments, including mechanical pointer meters, digital display meters, and hybrid display meters, and compared it with methods such as ResNet, YOLOv8-CR, CRNN, and Swin-Reader. The results show that MIF-Net achieves superior performance in terms of instrument type recognition accuracy, reading recognition precision, and robustness to complex interference, with an overall recognition accuracy of 98.37% and an average reading error reduced to 0.41%FS, representing improvements of 2.16% and reductions of 0.23%FS compared to the best comparison algorithm, respectively. Even under reflective, tilted, occluded, and lowlight conditions, the algorithm maintains an average recognition accuracy of 95.84%, indicating that this method can effectively improve the intelligent recognition capability of visual inspection data for metrology instruments, providing reliable technical support for automated metrological verification and industrial intelligent inspection.

Title: Semantic Navigation and High-Precision Autonomous Docking for Mobile Robots in Nuclear Medicine Environments
Abstract: The deployment of autonomous mobile robots in nuclear medicine examination rooms presents a confluence of navigational and control challenges. Unlike standard hospital corridors or warehouse logistics environments, these specialized facilities are characterized by highly unstructured spatial constraints, the presence of hazardous ionizing radiation. These physical limitations severely restrict the available free space, amplifying the difficulties associated with the non-holonomic kinematic constraints of differential-drive robotic platforms. To address the dual requirements of semantic spatial awareness and millimeter-level positioning, this comprehensive research report details a novel, integrated framework for semantic navigation and coarse-to-fine autonomous docking. The proposed system introduces a Multi-Layer Semantic Grid Map architecture that fuses geometric occupancy, deep-learning-derived semantic classifications stabilized by a Bayesian Dirichlet distribution update mechanism, and a continuous radiation field estimated via an obstacle-aware Gaussian Process Regression model. For path planning within these highly restricted spaces, an advanced hybrid framework is deployed, coupling an Improved Hybrid A∗ global planner with a Pose Auxiliary Point Timed Elastic Band local optimizer, supported by Kalman Filter-based dynamic obstacle tracking. Finally, to ensure collision-free, high-precision instrument manipulation, a Nonlinear Model Predictive Control based Hybrid Visual Servoing strategy is formulated. This controller integrates a parallel PI compensator to eradicate mechanical steady-state errors and employs an asymmetric time-varying performance function to rigorously enforce FOV constraints during the terminal docking phase. Experimental results confirm a 91.7% improvement in docking precision.

Title: Competition-and Timeliness-Aware Adaptive Asynchronous Aggregation for Federated Learning in Edge-Assisted Vehicular Networks
Abstract: Federated learning in edge-Assisted vehicular networks must perform distributed model training under high vehicle mobility, heterogeneous computing capabilities, and dynamically fluctuating wireless links. Conventional synchronous federated learning suffers from excessive waiting latency, whereas ordinary asynchronous federated learning can alleviate synchronization blocking but fails to sufficiently exploit the heterogeneity in vehicle mobility, data scale, and computing capability. Existing mobility-Aware asynchronous federated learning (MAFL) incorporates vehicle-state information into the asynchronous framework; however, its aggregation stage still relies on fixed parameters and therefore lacks fine-grained adaptivity. To address these limitations, a competition-and timeliness-Aware adaptive asynchronous aggregation method is proposed. In the original MAFL environment, a state-Aware adaptive aggregation weight is first designed by jointly considering training delay, communication delay, participation frequency, and data scale, thereby replacing the fixed aggregation parameter with a dynamically adjustable one. For multi-vehicle upload competition under limited uplink resources, queueing delay and update-deadline margin are further introduced to construct a competition-and timeliness-Aware aggregation mechanism. The experimental results showed that, in the non-competitive environment, the proposed method achieved higher test accuracy and lower loss than the fixed-parameter baseline. Under upload competition, as the competition intensity increased, the proposed method exhibited better training stability and smaller performance degradation. These results indicate that jointly incorporating vehicle-state heterogeneity and update timeliness into the aggregation design, while allowing the aggregation parameter to adapt dynamically, provides an effective way to improve asynchronous federated learning in vehicular networks.

Title: Prompt Engineering for Empowering Audio Large Models in Interference Recognition: Strategy Optimization and Zero-Shot Scenario Adaptation
Abstract: Cross-modal Large Audio-Language Models (LALMs) demonstrate strong zero-shot reasoning in general audio understanding, but their robustness in noisy environments is limited. In a zero-shot 'prompt + post-processing matching' setting, Qwen2-Audio achieved only 13% category similarity on the FSD50K dataset - far below the $0.30-0.49 \text{mAP}$ of specialized audio-text alignment models like CLAP[1]. This paper proposes three progressive prompt strategies: 'establishing interference awareness', 'supplementing background information via Sound Event Classification (SEC) for targeted filtering', and 'guiding precise differentiation through Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning'. Experimental results show the CoT-based strategy delivers optimal performance, increasing overall recognition accuracy by 13.0% and high-interference scenario accuracy by 20.4%. This work provides a lightweight, reusable engineering solution for LALMs in uncontrolled zero-shot environments.

Title: Training Set Synthesis for Bioacoustic Denoising: A Case Study with Mice
Abstract: Bioacoustic recordings are often degraded by ambient noise, which complicates the analysis of weak or noise-overlapped vocalizations. Convolutional neural networks, particularly U-Net architectures, have shown strong denoising performance in speech and music processing. However, their application for denoising bioacoustic signals is limited by the scarcity of clean training data. To address this, we propose a training set synthesis approach and develop a supervised denoising model that predicts a complex ratio mask in the time-frequency domain. The model leverages ridges, or frequency contours, that represent the fundamental frequency together with one or more harmonic partial components of vocalizations. These ridges are used both for the synthesis of training set and for the design of a loss function that assigns higher weights to the ridge regions (ridge-guided loss function). This weighting step helps the network better preserve vocalization details during denoising. As a case study, we evaluate our approach using ultrasonic vocalization (USV) recordings of house mice, which are widely studied in behavioral biology and neuroscience. In field recordings, the proposed method enhances tracking of fundamental and harmonic partial ridges compared to previous signal-processing approaches. In addition, a classifier trained on denoised data improves USV classification on out-of-sample, noisy recordings from wild and domesticated mice compared to classifiers trained on noisy recordings. The proposed method also substantially improves the scale-invariant signal-to-distortion ratio on synthetic testing data across a wide range of input signal-to-noise ratios. While focused on USVs, the proposed approach is broadly applicable to other bioacoustic signals with trackable ridges, and thus enables ridge-based training set synthesis and denoising.

Title: Physics-Informed Deep Autoencoder for Real-Time Array Calibration on High-Mobility Platforms
Abstract: With the widespread application of array on various mobile platforms, time-varying amplitude and phase errors have become critical factors affecting the performance of array signal processing. Existing deep learning-based calibration methods predominantly rely on supervised learning with explicit error labels, which are impractical for rapidly time-varying errors in real-world scenarios. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a novel self-supervised deep autoencoder framework that treats array calibration as a data reconstruction problem without requiring prior knowledge of error parameters. A dedicated deep neural network is designed for channel-wise error correction, employing a dual-driven learning mechanism that utilizes both unperturbed (ideal) data and perturbed (error-contaminated) data. Based on the principle of minimizing the mean square error between desired outputs and the ideal model, the algorithm extracts hidden features of the array manifold and achieves effective correction of time-varying amplitude-phase errors. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm can effectively correct time-varying errors in each channel. When random time-varying amplitude errors of $pm 80 %$ and phase errors of $pm 5°$ are present, both in-phase and quadrature data errors are reduced to within $4 × 10-4$, respectively. Furthermore, when the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is greater than or equal to 0 dB, the MUSIC algorithm's direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation accuracy using the corrected data is essentially consistent with that of error-free data, verifying the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

Title: Dual-input deep learning system for microbial identification from blood agar plates
Abstract: Objective: The morphological classification of microbial cultures and colonies requires specialized knowledge and experience; therefore, automation in this field remains limited. This study examines the feasibility of automating the identification of pathogenic microbial species from colony images of cultured microorganisms. Methods: Two distinct image datasets were constructed for 10 clinically relevant species: a colony image dataset, consisting of individual colony images cropped, and a tile image dataset, generated by dividing entire images of the culture plate into tiles. Separate ResNet-50–based models were trained in each dataset, and their outputs were integrated to evaluate the classification performance. Training was conducted using 10,048 colony images and 23,003 tile images collected from 418 strains, and performance was assessed with five-fold cross-validation (K = 5). Results: The colony image model achieved a sensitivity of 0.934 and a specificity of 0.993, while the tile image model achieved a sensitivity of 0.918 and a specificity of 0.991. Integration of the two models into an ensemble model further improved performance, yielding a sensitivity of 0.955 and a specificity of 0.995 when tested on 76 independent strains. Conclusion: The ensemble model approach provides high accuracy and robustness, suggesting its potential technical contributions to microbial identification in clinical microbiology laboratories.

Title: Remotely Sensed Data-Driven Deep Learning Assimilation for Wave in China Seas
Abstract: This letter proposes a U-shaped network (Unet)based postprocessing data-assimilation framework to improve hourly significant wave height (SWH) hindcasts from the finite-volume community ocean model (FVCOM)–simulating waves nearshore (SWAN) in the China Seas. Unet is trained with 2024 SWH observations from Jason-3, Haiyang-2 (HY-2), and the surface waves investigation and monitoring (SWIM) instrument onboard the China–France Oceanography Satellite (CFOSAT), and applied to the 2014–2023 hindcasts. Validation against buoy observations during 2022–2023 shows that Unet reduces the root-mean-squared error (RMSE) from 0.65 to 0.53 m and increases the correlation coefficient (Cor) from 0.84 to 0.86. Unet also outperforms residual Unet (ResUNet), the Kalman filter (KF), and ensemble optimal interpolation (EnOI), whose RMSEs are 0.58, 0.63, and 0.64 m, respectively. Monthly mean SWH from the assimilated fields shows positive tendencies during 2014–2023, demonstrating the framework’s potential for regional decadal-scale variability analysis.

Title: Music Genre Classification Using Dual-Branch Feature Fusion of Mel-Spectrogram Embeddings and Acoustic Statistical Descriptors
Abstract: Music genre classification is a fundamental task in music information retrieval, audio signal processing, recommendation systems, and digital music resource management. Mel-spectrogram-based deep models have been widely used for this task because they can learn discriminative time-frequency representations. However, they may not fully capture global acoustic properties related to timbre, harmony, rhythm, energy, and tonality. This study investigates whether acoustic statistical descriptors provide complementary information to Mel-spectrogram deep embeddings for music genre classification. A dual-branch feature fusion framework is proposed, in which a ResNet18-based branch extracts log-Mel spectrogram embeddings and an MLP-based branch encodes acoustic descriptors, including MFCC, Chroma, spectral centroid, zero-crossing rate, RMS energy, tempo, and Tonnetz. Experiments were conducted on FMA-small and GTZAN under a unified preprocessing, training, and evaluation protocol. The proposed model achieved an accuracy of 0.732±0.011 and a macro-F1 of 0.703±0.014 on FMA-small, and an accuracy of 0.881±0.009 and a macro-F1 of 0.861±0.010 on GTZAN. Compared with traditional classifiers, CNN-based models, residual networks, CRNN, lightweight CNN models, and transformer-style spectrogram baselines, the proposed model produced modest but consistent improvements. Although the performance gains over strong spectrogram-based baselines are moderate, the improvements are stable across repeated runs and are supported by descriptor-level, error-structure, and feature-space analyses. Descriptor-level ablation, fusion-strategy comparison, confusion-reduction analysis, and feature-space visualization further showed that acoustic descriptors improve genre separability when integrated with Mel-spectrogram embeddings. These findings suggest that dual-branch feature fusion provides an effective and interpretable strategy for medium-scale music genre classification.

Title: Cross-Dataset Feature Discriminability in Static Malware Detection: A CVFR-Based Study Across Four Heterogeneous Benchmarks
Abstract: Static malware detection with machine learning relies critically on which features are extracted from Portable Executable (PE) binaries. Most prior work evaluates feature selection on a single benchmark, leaving open whether features generalize across heterogeneous datasets. We investigate crossdataset feature discriminability by quantifying the consistency of important features across heterogeneous malware datasets. We introduce Cross-Validated Feature Ranking (CVFR), a lightweight wrapper that aggregates Random Forest (RF) feature importance across repeated cross-validation runs to attach perfeature confidence intervals and a stability score (SNR) to an otherwise standard ranking. CVFR is not a new feature-selection algorithm and is not claimed to improve accuracy; it is positioned as the uncertainty-quantification instrument that enables the cross-dataset discriminability study. RF, Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), LightGBM, and One-Class SVM are evaluated under a two-level stratified crossvalidation protocol (25 repeated evaluations) with within-fold SMOTE on four PE-header benchmark datasets: EMBER, BIG15, Malicia, and BODMAS. RF achieves the highest F1 and AUC-ROC on every dataset (mean 98.72% F1, 0.998 AUC), consistently outperforming MLP across all 25 fold-seed pairs (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, p<0.0001), and remaining best or tied against a competitive LightGBM gradient-boosting baseline. An ablation study confirms that CVFR achieves predictive performance comparable to single-run impurity ranking and permutation importance, while additionally providing uncertainty estimates for feature importance at lower computational cost than permutation importance. Jaccard analysis reveals limited feature overlap (7.9-27.6%) among independently collected datasets, while datasets sharing the same extraction schema (EMBER and BODMAS) reach 83.8% overlap. Transfer experiments show that the high-overlap pair (EMBER↔BODMAS, 83.8% Jaccard) experiences larger F1 degradation (20-36 pp) than the low-overlap pair (BIG15↔Malicia, 8-13 pp), suggesting that feature-space overlap alone is insufficient to predict transferability and that temporal distributional shift may exert a stronger influence on cross-dataset generalization. Because the transfer analysis covers only two dataset pairs (two seeds each) that co-vary simultaneously in feature overlap, temporal collection gap, and class balance, this transfer observation is hypothesis-generating rather than statistically conclusive. Subject to that caveat, the findings indicate that feature importance should be validated separately for each target dataset and that successful cross-dataset deployment is likely to require explicit domain adaptation, even when datasets share the same feature-extraction schema.

Title: Estimating Lake Water Level in Ice-Influenced Proglacial Lakes: A Comparative Study of Machine Learning and Satellite Altimetry in Chilean Patagonia
Abstract: This study compares three machine learning (ML) models [long short-term memory (LSTM), random forest (RF), and XGBoost] and four satellite altimetry missions (J3, S3B, S6, and SWOT) for estimating water levels in Lake Gray, Chilean Patagonia (2012–2025). XGBoost achieved the best ML performance (RMSE = 0.11 ± 0.02 m, Kling–Gupta efficiency (KGE) = 0.9684 ± 0.0084), while Sentinel-6 provided the highest altimetric accuracy (RMSE = 0.07 m). SWOT captured the full hydrological variability (IQR = 0.78 m), which was nearly identical to in situ records, outperforming traditional altimeters (J3 and S3B). Tree-based methods and SWOT best reproduce observed distributions. The combined use of ML for long-term reconstruction and modern altimetry for high-precision monitoring offers a reproducible, proof-of-concept framework for remote, ice-influenced proglacial lakes.

Title: Efficient deep mood-based Hindustani raga music recommendation using facial emotion expressions
Abstract: Music recommendation is considered as a solution, and the performance is degraded with prediction error. Title: Explainable Transformer-Based Speech Emotion Recognition Using Benchmark Datasets
Abstract: Although Speech Emotion Recognition plays a critical role in human-computer interaction, the opaque "black box"nature of deep learning models poses significant challenges for reliability and interpretability. This study utilizes a hybrid SER system based on Explainable Artificial Intelligence, combining high accuracy and transparency. The methodology involves extracting contextual features from raw audio signals using the Wav2Vec 2.0 architecture and processing them with a multilayer Transformer classifier. The model was trained and tested on the IEMOCAP dataset and evaluated on the RAVDESS dataset. Experimental results showed that the model performed successfully in its in-domain with 66.91% WA and 70.30% UA. However, in cross-dataset tests, performance decreased to 31.70% WA due to domain shift. A comprehensive XAI analysis was conducted to improve transparency into the model's decision-making process. While the quantitative effects of features on prediction were determined using the SHAP method, the model's temporal focal points in the audio signal were visualized using attention-weight analysis. The analyses revealed that the model could distinguish emotions such as "anger"with high confidence, especially by focusing on high-energy segments and sentence-end intonations. This study provides a methodological contribution to the literature by demonstrating that both high performance and interpretability can be offered together in SER systems.

Title: A Voting-Based Deep Learning Ensemble Framework for Monkeypox Skin Lesion Classification
Abstract: Monkeypox is a recently identified i nfectious disease that mainly spreads through close contact with infected individuals or exposure to contaminated surfaces. A visible skin rash is one of its primary symptoms. However, diagnosing monkeypox based only on appearance is difficult b ecause its visual features are similar to other skin-related illnesses such as measles and chickenpox. Although laboratory techniques like PCR and antigen testing are considered reliable, they are not always practical in low-resource regions due to their dependence on costly instruments, trained professionals, and longer testing durations. This article provides an automated deep learning method that uses medical images to classify monkeypox and related skin disorders in order to get around these restrictions. Four categories are included in the dataset utilized in this study: measles, chickenpox, monkeypox, and normal skin. A 70:15:15 split is used to separate the photos into training, validation, and testing sets. Hard and soft voting ensemble techniques are used to combine the predictions of three pretrained convolutional neural network models: ResNet-18, EfficientNet-B0, and DenseNet-121. To improve training efficiency a nd r educe c omputational cost, techniques such as transfer learning, GPU-based processing, and mixed-precision training are utilized. Evaluation criteria such as accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, F1-score, and AUC-ROC are used to gauge model performance. Consistent with previous ensemble-based learning studies, the experimental analysis shows that ensemble techniques perform better than individual models, with soft voting yielding the best overall outcomes.These results show that the suggested framework can be a reliable and effective method for detecting monkeypox. Monkeypox and other seemingly similar skin conditions can be quickly, non-invasively, and automatically screened for with the established technology.

Title: Lightweight Multi-Cue Fusion Network for Deepfake Audio Detection
Abstract: The emerging threat of audio deepfakes generated by sophisticated text-to-speech and voice conversion techniques has the potential to compromise the security of voice biometrics, call center security, and audio-based authentication systems. The difficulty of detecting audio deepfakes has been attributed to the subtle, attack-dependent, and highly channel- and device-variant dependent nature of the features, which has been observed to degrade the performance of the existing audio deepfake detection systems. In spite of the promising results obtained by the existing deep learning-based countermeasures, it has been observed that a large percentage of the existing audio deepfake detection systems rely on a single representation of the features. In order to address the challenges of the existing audio deepfake detection systems, we propose a lightweight multi-cue audio deepfake detection system. The proposed system utilizes the features of the spectrogram and statistical features of the audio signal. The proposed system utilizes a CNN model, a handcrafted cue vector, and a fusion network. The framework is optimized and tested using the widely used ASVspoof 2019 protocols, specifically the LA and PA protocols, with the use of traditional performance measures such as Equal Error Rate (EER) and minimum tandem Detection Cost Function (min-tDCF). Title: Explainable AI in Sales Forecasting: Interpreting Machine Learning Models for Business Decisions
Abstract: Sales forecasting becomes important in order to inform corporate goals, how resources should be utilized and to achieve profitability. The paper presents an Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) framework, which uses ensemble regression models with interpretability methods to provide predictive analytics with high accuracy and complete transparency. The paper factors Gradient Boosting, XGBoost, Light GBM, Random Forest, and CatBoost models, the last being optimized with randomized hyperparameter tuning, and evaluated with the help of MAE, RMSE and R<sup>2</sup>. CatBoost model performed best in this scenario with an R<sup>2</sup> = 0.9936 much better compared to the traditional algorithms such as Support Vector Regression (SVR), Decision Tree (DT), ARIMA and Linear Regression (LiR). Ablation study is the one that confirms, again, the absolute necessity of the purposely created features. The generated framework, in addition to forecasting the best level of accuracy, also offered transparency and actionable insight, therefore, a valuable, ethically-conscious instrument of data-driven business strategy.

Title: Performance Enhancement of Heart Sound Classification Using Ensemble Machine Learning Techniques on PCG Signals
Abstract: The classification of heart sound signals from phonocardiogram (PCG) has become one of the important noninvasive techniques for early detection of cardiovascular abnormalities. But how good the signal is, how much background noise is present, and how complex the murmur patterns are have a huge impact on diagnostic accuracy. In this paper, an ensemble framework for machine learning system is proposed to enhance the performance of heart sound classification with PCG signals. To increase the robustness of classification and to minimize the uncertainty of prediction, a combination of classifiers with Random Forest, Gradient Boosting and XGBoost was proposed. The PCG recordings first go through some preprocessing steps, such as normalization, segmentation, filtering and noise reduction, to enhance the quality of the features and signal clarity. Later, discriminative temporal and spectral features are extracted from different components of the heart sound including S1, S2 and murmurs. The ensemble learning approach can harness the best of each of the classifiers to attain better accuracy, precision, recall and generalization ability than individual machine learning models. Experimental assessment shows that the proposed framework is able to deal with the noisy PCG in an effective manner and improves abnormal heart sound detection performance. The framework provides an efficient and robust solution that could be applied in intelligent cardiac diagnostic systems and realtime healthcare monitoring applications.

Title: Zero-Shot Large Language Models for Preliminary Prediction of PTSD Symptoms From Clinical Interview Transcripts: Grands modèles de langage sans exemple pour la prédiction préliminaire des symptômes de TSPT à partir de transcriptions d'entrevues cliniques
Abstract: Background: Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is common yet frequently underdiagnosed, in part due to barriers to systematic screening and the reliance on self-report instruments. Large language models (LLMs) have shown promise in extracting clinically relevant information from unstructured language, but their ability to infer item-level PTSD symptom severity from clinical interviews remains unclear. Methods: Using the Distress Analysis Interview Corpus—Wizard of Oz (DAIC-WoZ), we analyzed 100 semi-structured clinical interview transcripts paired with item-level PTSD Checklist—Civilian Version (PCL-C) scores. Six LLMs (DeepSeek 3.1, Claude Sonnet 4, LLaMA 4 Scout, GPT-4o, GPT-5, and Gemini 2.5 Flash) used zero-shot prompting to predict all 17 PCL-C items. Performance was assessed for binary symptom endorsement (≥3 vs. < 3), 5-point Likert prediction, and DSM-IV symptom-cluster analyses using accuracy, F1 score, and Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC). Results: For binary prediction, Claude 4 achieved the highest mean accuracy (0.705; 95% CI, 0.681-0.728), followed by DeepSeek 3.1(0.699; 95% CI, 0.675-0.724) and Gemini 2.5 (0.698; 95% CI, 0.677-0.718). For Likert prediction, DeepSeek 3.1 performed best (accuracy = 0.438; 95% CI, 0.401-0.475), only modestly above the majority-class baseline (0.399; 95% CI, 0.355-0.443). Performance varied by symptom domain, with re-experiencing and hyperarousal symptoms generally predicted more accurately than avoidance/numbing symptoms. Across models, predicted item-level symptom patterns showed a meaningful alignment with observed PCL-C responses despite reduced accuracy in fine-grained severity estimation. Conclusion: Zero-shot LLMs’ performance was insufficient for clinical application in predicting PTSD symptoms from semi-structured interview transcripts. While models showed some ability to capture overall symptom patterns, performance varied across domains and remained limited for fine-grained severity estimation. Given these constraints and the non-trauma-specific nature of the dataset, findings should be interpreted as preliminary, with only modest differences observed between models. Plain Language Summary Title: Can Artificial Intelligence Identify PTSD Symptoms from Conversations? A Study Using Clinical Interview Transcripts Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is a common mental health condition, but it is often missed in clinical settings. Screening usually relies on questionnaires that patients must complete themselves, which may not always happen due to time, stigma, or discomfort discussing trauma. Researchers are exploring whether artificial intelligence (AI) could help identify PTSD symptoms from conversations instead. In this study, we tested several advanced AI systems, known as large language models, to see if they could estimate PTSD symptoms based on written transcripts of clinical interviews. These interviews were not specifically designed to assess trauma, which makes the task more challenging but closer to real-world situations. We compared the AI predictions to participants' own questionnaire responses about their symptoms. We found that the AI models were somewhat able to recognize general patterns of PTSD symptoms, especially more visible ones like sleep problems or distressing dreams. However, they struggled with more internal or less obvious symptoms, such as avoidance or emotional numbness. Overall, their accuracy was moderate and not reliable enough for clinical use, particularly when trying to estimate how severe symptoms were. Importantly, differences between the AI models were small, and none performed well enough to replace existing screening methods. These findings suggest that while AI may have future potential as a supportive tool, it is not yet ready to be used for diagnosing or screening PTSD on its own. Further research using better data, improved methods, and real clinical settings is needed before this approach could be considered for practical use.

Title: Automated Traffic Surveillance and Oversight: Legal Limits of Personal Data Processing by Public Authorities in the Republic of Croatia
Abstract: The deployment of video surveillance, automatic number plate recognition (ANPR), and electronic toll collection systems enables public authorities to systematically collect and process road users' personal data. As processing by public authorities is typically grounded in legal obligation or the performance of tasks in the public interest rather than individual consent, ensuring transparency, clear legal bases, defined retention periods, and adequate security safeguards (including anonymization/pseudonymization) becomes particularly critical. This raises significant concerns regarding lawfulness, proportionality, and purpose limitation. This paper presents a normative legal analysis of the regulatory framework governing personal data processing in automated traffic control and surveillance systems in the Republic of Croatia. It examines the application of the GDPR, the Croatian Act on its Implementation, the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights, and relevant EU instruments such as the ITS Directive, Directive 2016/680, and the AI Act, with particular attention to the distinct legal regimes applicable to ordinary video surveillance, ANPR systems, and AI-based biometric technologies. The paper identifies regulatory gaps and legal risks, and emphasizes the need for clear legal bases, transparency, accountability, and proportionate use of technology to ensure effective protection of fundamental rights under EU and national law.

Title: AI-Driven Classification of Personality Items: A Study on Large Language Models
Abstract: This study investigates the effectiveness of large language models (LLMs) in classifying items that evaluate the Big Five personality dimensions, focusing on performance variations across traits and comparing local and cloud-based models. Five Natural Language Processing (NLP) models were used to classify 385 personality items, employing three levels of detail in prompt design. The results indicate that larger generative models, such as ChatGPT-4o and Gemini 1.5 Pro, outperformed smaller models in terms of accuracy, both for the five personality factors and overall. However, the Llama 3.1 model, run locally, showed adequate results for judge-based analyses, offering a viable alternative for those prioritizing data privacy. The study highlights the potential of LLMs as complementary tools in the development of psychological assessment instruments.

Title: Neural Decoding of Music Effects on Mental Fatigue States
Abstract: We investigate the neural mechanisms through which music influences mental fatigue using electroencephalography (EEG) and deep learning. We collected EEG data from 49 participants during periods with and without musical auditory stimulation, categorized by mental fatigue status based on standardized questionnaires. Following preprocessing and feature extraction, we implemented three deep learning architectures (Convolutional Neural Network [CNN], Gated Recurrent Unit [GRU], Long Short-Term Memory [LSTM]) to decode and classify four distinct conditions: with/without music and with/without mental fatigue. The GRU model achieved superior classification performance (96.92% accuracy), followed closely by LSTM (96.03%), while CNN showed significantly lower performance (58.97%). The high decoding accuracy demonstrates that music exposure produces distinctly identifiable neural patterns that can be differentiated from those associated with mental fatigue. The superior performance of recurrent architectures highlights the importance of modeling temporal dependencies in EEG data associated with these cognitive states. Our findings provide neural evidence supporting music's potential as an intervention for mental fatigue and establish a foundation for developing personalized music-based strategies to enhance cognitive well-being.

Title: Anomaly-aware electric vehicle charging and battery storage management using smart-meter data and a GCN-BiLSTM autoencoder
Abstract: This research develops a smart meter-based residential energy management system that uses advanced deep learning to detect anomalies in electricity consumption data and optimize power usage in homes with electric vehicles and battery storage. The proposed framework addresses the limitations of traditional smart meters, which usually measure and transmit power consumption but do not actively identify abnormal readings or support intelligent energy scheduling. Smart meter data from 900 households are used to design and evaluate the model. The anomaly detection module is based on an autoencoder that integrates Graph Convolutional Networks and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory networks. This structure enables the system to learn both the relational and time-dependent behavior of household energy consumption. Missing values and abnormal readings are detected by comparing original and reconstructed consumption patterns. The corrected smart meter data are then applied to a multi-objective power management strategy that controls EV and battery charging/discharging, reduces peak demand, lowers grid energy consumption, and improves the use of renewable energy sources. The results show that the proposed method achieves high anomaly detection performance and provides better energy cost reduction than conventional approaches. Therefore, the study offers a practical framework for reliable, economical, and sustainable residential energy management.

Title: Predicting Station Occupancy of Bike-Sharing System During Events: Insights from Lisbon
Abstract: Technological advancements have enabled the large-scale collection of bike-sharing systems (BSS), providing valuable opportunities for city planners and operators to optimize services and improve decision-making. As a soft mobility mode, BSS plays a critical role in promoting sustainable and reliable urban transportation. However, research remains limited regarding how such data can be used to evaluate the impact of city events on BSS usage and to enhance station occupancy prediction. To address this gap, this study uses Lisbon, Portugal, as a case study to investigate the influence of events on BSS usage, focusing on hourly station occupancy rates and, for the first time in the city, integrating event data into BSS prediction models. By integrating weather conditions and event data, we apply state-of-the-art machine learning algorithms, such as Random Forest, Gradient Boosting Tree, and Extreme Gradient Boosting, to predict occupancy levels. The goal is to evaluate model performance, analyze prediction error patterns, and contribute to more efficient resource allocation and management of BSS during urban events. Results show that an XGBoost model enriched with an occupancy-change feature and historical demand data delivers the most accurate station-level occupancy predictions, revealing distinct usage patterns between sports and music events and across station locations, and provides actionable insights to support targeted, time-sensitive bicycle rebalancing during high-impact event days. The study provides a benchmark methodology that can be used in other urban contexts, enabling smart cities’ advancements.

Title: HIL-MDF: A Human-in-the-Loop Multimodal Deepfake Detection System
Abstract: The rapid advancement of deepfake technology creates a critical threat to the integrity of digital media, necessitating the development of detection technologies that are both robust and transparent. This paper proposes a novel Human-In-The-Loop Multimodal Deepfake Detection (HILMDF) system that integrates both audio and visual modalities, utilizing explainable artificial intelligence methods to provide reasoning behind the classification, and enhance human understanding of the system. The system utilizes a mid-level fusion architecture combining an EfficientNet-B0 backbone with a 1D convolution to extract spatiotemporal visual embeddings, and a specialized 2D Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for processing audio Mel-Spectrograms. To address the black-box nature of deep learning methods, three Explainable AI (XAI) techniques were applied (Saliency maps, Integrated gradients, and Layer-Grad-CAM) to provide an interpretable visual representation of the explanation behind the model reasoning. To present these explanations, an interactive decision support interface is introduced to facilitate human verification in the detection loop. Experimental evaluation was carried out using the multimodal deepfake dataset FakeAVCeleb, and the system achieved an accuracy of 89.75%, significantly outperforming unimodal baselines and standard ensemble methods.

Abstract: The growth of solar power has become one of the most prospective sources of renewable energy in meeting global sustainability objectives due to the minimal environmental effects and ability to use it in large scale. Abstract: This study uses Natural Language Processing (NLP) and machine learning techniques to explore lyrics-based music genre classification. Title: Effects of Virtual Reality–Based Physical Exercise Interventions on Behavioral, Executive Function, and Motor Outcomes in Children and Adolescents With Autism Spectrum Disorder: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
Abstract: Background: In addition to core behavioral symptoms, children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) frequently exhibit impairments in executive function and motor performance. Although virtual reality (VR)–based physical exercise interventions are increasingly used in ASD rehabilitation, evidence regarding their multidimensional effects remains limited. Objective: This study aimed to systematically review the effects of VR-based physical exercise interventions on behavioral outcomes, executive function, and motor performance in children and adolescents with ASD. Methods: PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) 2020 guidelines were followed. PubMed (National Library of Medicine), Embase (Elsevier), Web of Science, Scopus (Elsevier), and other databases were searched from inception to May 7, 2026. Eligible studies included randomized and nonrandomized trials involving participants aged 6‐18 years with ASD. The interventions consisted of VR-based exercise programs involving physical activity participation, including active video games, motion-sensing interactive training, and augmented reality–based exercise training. Risk of bias was assessed using Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2; Cochrane Bias Methods Group) and Risk of Bias in Nonrandomized Studies of Interventions (ROBINS-I; Cochrane Bias Methods Group), and certainty of evidence was evaluated using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) framework. Random-effects meta-analyses were conducted using Hedges g standardized mean differences (SMDs). Results: A total of 15 studies involving 439 children and adolescents with ASD were included; among them, 9 studies were eligible for meta-analysis. Behavioral outcomes were reported in only 3 studies. Owing to substantial heterogeneity in study designs and assessment instruments, we did not conduct a meta-analysis for these outcomes. Current evidence suggests inconsistent effects on social interaction and stereotyped behaviors. VR-based physical exercise interventions may improve executive function (SMD 0.75, 95% CI 0.32‐1.18; I<sup>2=0.0%</sup> P=.01; GRADE moderate). However, the prediction interval crossed the line of no effect (−0.12 to 1.63). VR-based physical exercise interventions were associated with improvements in motor performance (SMD 1.08, 95% CI 0.08‐2.08; I<sup>2=74.3%</sup> P=.04; GRADE low). However, the wide prediction interval suggests substantial between-study variability (−1.31 to 3.47). Conclusions: Current evidence suggests a relatively consistent positive effect of VR-based physical exercise interventions involving physical activity participation on executive function in children and adolescents with ASD. However, substantial uncertainty remains regarding their effects on motor performance and behavioral outcomes. Unlike previous reviews that primarily focused on general VR interventions, social skills training, or single functional outcomes, this systematic review specifically examined the multidimensional effects of VR-based physical exercise interventions. The findings suggest that VR-based physical exercise interventions may be implemented as adjuncts to conventional exercise or rehabilitation programs rather than as stand-alone interventions. Future large-scale, high-quality randomized controlled trials with larger sample sizes, standardized intervention reporting, and long-term follow-up are needed to further clarify the optimal implementation conditions and underlying mechanisms of different forms of VR-based exercise training.

Title: EXPLORING WORKFLOW PATTERNS IN TWO HYBRID ENGINEERING TEAMS
Abstract: Aim/Purpose This article reports an exploratory case study that examines workflow perceptions in two hybrid engineering teams comprising 26 professionals, focusing on temporal experience, meeting character, and engagement. Background Hybrid work configurations pose coordination challenges for distributed teams, yet the hybrid context remains understudied, particularly in terms of temporal coordination and synchronous communication. Methodology Following an exploratory case study design, we conducted semi-structured interviews with four team leaders and administered a six-item categorical questionnaire to 26 team members. A modified C4.5 decision tree algorithm was applied to organize response patterns for interpretive purposes, though severe limitations from the small sample size and unvalidated measures are acknowledged. Contribution Three response patterns and one outlier emerged (n= 1), with sense of time and meeting character appearing as the most differentiating variables. Extracted patterns from decision trees serve as a foundation for describing a provisional profile. Three provisional profiles were observed: a subgroup reporting temporal acceleration alongside task-focused meeting preferences (n=4); a subgroup reporting awaiting-completion states with task-focused preferences (n=17); and a subgroup reporting connection-oriented meeting preferences (n=4). These profiles are offered as tentative, sample-bound observations. We introduce preliminary terminology to describe workflow dynamics and apply a machine learning algorithm in a new context, as an exploratory pattern-organization tool. No claims of generalizable patterns are made due to the absence of performance measurement and comparison groups. Findings The observed patterns suggest possible directions for further studies on temporal experience, meeting character, and informing processes in hybrid work settings. These patterns require extensive validation before offering reliable guidance for practice. Recommendations The managers and team leaders may find it useful to reflect on temporal experifor Practitioners ence, meeting structure, and information flow in hybrid teams, but the present study does not provide validated intervention principles or managerial guidance. Recommendations The interpretations were made on a small data set that depends heavily on the for Researchers specificity of the team’s common language and may serve as a basis for researching new concepts of group engagement patterns in a business environment. Larger datasets, along with the application of contemporary machine learning methods, could be used to uncover hidden patterns in qualitative data. Impact on Society This study contributes to ongoing discussion about hybrid work by drawing attention to underexplored issues of temporal coordination and meeting function, but it should not imply direct societal impact or reliable practical guidance. Future Research Future research with larger datasets, validated instruments, performance measurement, and cross-context replication is essential, positioning this study as hypothesis-generating groundwork for understanding temporal dynamics in hybrid teams.

Title: AI Utilization and Planning Performance in Civil Engineering: Design, Scheduling, and Resource Planning
Abstract: The research focuses on the potential for, and perceptions of, using artificial intelligence in relation to key processes in the construction sector, such as design, resource planning, and project delivery time. The study is grounded in a survey of civil engineering professionals, examining the level of AI adoption and its impacts in terms of the range of tools used, intensity of use, and the capacity to integrate AI into established procedures and workflows, particularly with respect to processing efficiency, quality, and re-source utilization. After defining the survey instrument and verifying its content validity, we analyze relationships between AI use and its implications for planning, in the context of expected outputs for project design and the delivery of time- and material-related commitments. Our underlying assumption is that greater use of AI will be associated with higher design efficiency and improved planning performance in civil engineering (H1–H2). We further hypothesize that these effects will be more pronounced depending on firm size and/or project scale (H3). The aim of the research is to ana-lyse AI adoption and its impacts on the processes under review, and to pro-vide civil engineering professionals with relevant, research-based conclusions and evidence-informed.

Title: A 3-dimensional Resnet model for assessment of drug efficacy in 3D cancer models using optical coherence tomography
Abstract: Ninety percent of drugs fail during clinical trials, mainly due to lack of clinical efficacy. Recent developments in in vitro models such as 3D tumor heterospheroids have led to improvements in failure rates, but the relative lack of standardized evaluation methods for 3D cultures limits their utility in high-throughput screening. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) shows significant promise for high-throughput screening of 3D models; however, the optimal classification model and key image features for assessing drug efficacy in OCT images of spheroids has yet to be explored in detail. In this study, we investigate whether OCT combined with machine learning methods can be used to identify biomarkers of drug efficacy in 3D tumor spheroid models. We further compare the performance of two different models to determine the optimal configuration for accurate classification. Volumetric OCT images were acquired of co-cultured HT29 spheroids treated with 3 different concentrations of cisplatin. A two-dimensional multi-view ResNet model and a three-dimensional ResNet model were used to classify the images and to identify key image features associated with each group. Differences between spheroids treated with different concentrations of cisplatin are clearly visible in the OCT images. Our model was able to classify the images based on cisplatin concentration with 71.9% accuracy using the 2D multi-view model and 91.2% accuracy using the 3D model. Key features in the 3D model significantly improved the model accuracy. These results underscore the possibility that OCT could be used for high-throughput screening of drugs using 3D in vitro models and highlight key identifying features for further investigation.

Title: Artificial Intelligence as a Regulatory Agent: Chinese Philosophical and Anthropological Perspective
Abstract: The article continues the authors’ inquiry into the theory of consciousness and the transformation of this concept within the contemporary communicative environment, aiming to elaborate in detail the problem of the normative agency of artificial intelligence (AI) in the context of the Chinese Confucian tradition. Divergent approaches to understanding the moral status of artificial systems have emerged within the Western philosophy of AI ethics and the Russian philosophical-anthropological tradition. At the same time, Chinese Confucian normativity, grounded in the categories of ritual, virtue, and sincerity, offers a distinct model for integrating AI into the socio-moral order. The paper provides a comparative analysis of these approaches: Western theories of information ethics and distributed agency, the Russian philosophy of consciousness and thoughtactivity, and Confucian role ethics. It examines how AI can function not merely as an instrument but as a normative agent capable of sustaining ritual harmony through the performance of social roles. Based on a comparison of Chinese and European principles of AI governance, it is demonstrated that fundamental differences underlie their external similarities: Western discourse is anchored in the values of autonomy and individual rights, whereas Chinese discourse relies on harmony, the collective good, and state governance. It is also shown that, within the context of integration into all spheres of education, industry, and science, contemporary AI can be regarded as a normative agent in a restricted sense, through the fulfillment of roles and the maintenance of ritual normativity. A promising direction at present is the synthesis of the Western idea of the legal protection of the person and the Eastern idea of harmony, which opens the possibility of forming an ethics of composite subjectivity for humans and AI. The proposed concept entails a new philosophical-anthropological framework for understanding human-machine interaction, in which responsibility and moral action are distributed within a hybrid system while preserving the priority of human consciousness and virtue.

Title: A Hybrid Deep Learning and Machine Learning Framework for Classifying Assamese Music Genres
Abstract: A number of current music genre categorization systems have centered around Western music and worldwide popular languages, with local and culturally diverse genres remaining neglected. There are significant difficulties in automatic detection of genres in such areas, including the lesser availability of annotated datasets and feature extraction issues related to linguistic and musical diversity. This paper proposes a hybrid model integrating deep learning architectures (LSTM, BiLSTM) and ensemble machine learning algorithms (Random Forest, XGBoost) to predict Assamese music genres-a low-resource, high-culture domain. A handpicked dataset of more than 10,000 songs across 12 varied Assamese genres was compiled and thoroughly investigated using statistical and temporal audio features. Experiments show that BiLSTM best solves these problems with superior accuracy and confirm that sequential deep learning models are appropriate for detecting regional music style. The model improves scalable and accurate regional music classification, encouraging digital preservation and discovery.

Title: Enhanced Pneumonia Classification in Chest X-Rays Through Explainable AI and Deep Learning Interpretability
Abstract: Pneumonia continues to be a major global health concern, particularly affecting susceptible populations such as infants, young children, and older adults. Radial diagnosis is very important to receive proper treatment and to reduce the possible complications. Despite the widespread use of chest X-rays (CXR) as a first line imaging test to diagnose pneumonia, their interpretation may be challenging and subject to human error. This work presents a new deep learning-based method to enhance the process of detecting pneumonia in CXRs with the use of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and Explainable AI (XAI). They used a number of pre-trained models, such as InceptionV3 (94% accuracy), MobileNetV2 (95%), NASNet (94%), ResNet152 (86%), Xception (93%), and a hyperparameter-tuned version of MobileNetV2, with the highest accuracy of 98%. Saliency maps were used to increase the visual interpretability and assist to highlight the most important areas to use in the diagnostic process. XAI inclusion enhances not only transparency but also clinical validation. In general, the suggested solution has shown good medical performance and is a reliable and interpretable instrument to assist clinicians, especially in a resource-constrained setting.

Title: Machine learning analysis of the association between psychosocial risks and burnout syndrome in mining workers
Abstract: Introduction – Burnout syndrome represents a critical issue in occupational health, particularly in high-demand contexts such as mining, where physical, environmental, and psychosocial risks converge and affect workers' wellbeing and job performance. In this context, the study objective is to analyze the association between psychosocial risk factors and burnout syndrome among mining workers in Moquegua, Peru. Methods – A quantitative, analytical cross-sectional study with a non-experimental design was conducted. The study population consisted of 65 workers from a mining unit in Moquegua, Peru. Given the complete accessibility of the target population, a census approach was adopted, and all eligible workers were included in the study (N = 65). Validated instruments were used, including the SUSESO/ISTAS21 questionnaire for psychosocial risks and the Maslach Burnout Inventory. Data analysis involved descriptive and correlational statistics, multiple linear regression, and machine learning techniques. Results – The findings revealed significant associations between psychosocial factors particularly social support, leadership, and work–family conflict (double presence) and burnout. All analyzed factors demonstrated significant associations capacity, with double presence emerging as the most influential predictor. Furthermore, machine learning analyses identified relevant burnout-related patterns within the analyzed dataset, highlighting their effectiveness in identifying burnout-related patterns. Discussion – Burnout in mining is a multifactorial phenomenon influenced by organizational and psychosocial conditions. The results support the use of machine learning as an useful tool for identifying psychosocial risk patterns that may support prevention strategies, contributing to improved occupational health strategies in high-risk industrial settings.

Title: Machine Learning in Robotic-Assisted Surgery: A Systematic Review and Multi-Task Intelligence Framework
Abstract: Robotic-assisted surgery (RAS) has significantly advanced modern healthcare by improving surgical precision, minimally invasive procedures, and patient outcomes. The integration of machine learning into robotic surgical systems introduces new capabilities such as automated tissue analysis, surgical phase recognition, skill assessment, and semiautonomous task execution. However, challenges related to data scarcity, explainability, real-time processing, and regulatory compliance continue to limit widespread clinical deployment. This paper presents a hybrid study combining a systematic literature review of machine learning in robotic-assisted surgery with the design and empirical evaluation of the proposed Multitask Surgical Intelligence Network (MSIN). The framework integrates deep learning techniques for instrument detection, tissue segmentation, surgical phase recognition, and motionbased skill assessment within a unified surgical intelligence platform. Experimental findings demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves high performance across multiple surgical intelligence tasks while supporting real-time analysis suitable for robotic surgical environments. The study also highlights the importance of explainable and safety-aware AI models for clinical integration. All reported results were obtained using five-fold cross-validation on publicly available benchmark datasets (Cholec80, JIGSAWS, JHU-ISI, M2CAI16, and AutoLaparo), with task-specific baselines trained under identical data splits and hardware conditions to ensure fair comparison. The paper identifies major research gaps and outlines future directions including federated surgical learning, foundation model adaptation, low-latency surgical AI systems, and regulatory-compliant autonomous surgical intelligence. The proposed framework provides a scalable foundation for nextgeneration intelligent robotic surgery systems.

Title: AI-Based Adaptive Deep Learning Noise Cancellation in Hearing Aids
Abstract: Hearing aids equipped with current noise control techniques produce poor speech clarity when there is other noise. Conventional acoustical techniques for controlling unwanted noise generally need to have no movement of the noise source which limits their effectiveness. A new noise-cancellation approach using artificial intelligence (AI) assistance for smart hearing devices is proposed and developed. It uses a very lowpower, lightweight neural network and a Digital Signal Processing (DSP) algorithm to provide improved separation between speech and noise, resulting in higher speech-to-noise ratio (SNR), while minimizing processing latency. The success of the application of this technology has shown improvements in performance and suitability of the devices to function in real conditions.

Title: Predicting Students' Academic Performance and Psychological Readiness Toward ChatGPT Use Using NLP and Machine Learning
Abstract: The increasing use of ChatGPT in higher education has created new opportunities and concerns regarding academic performance, psychological readiness, and responsible artificial intelligence use among students. This study developed an NLP-driven machine learning framework for predicting students' academic performance and psychological readiness toward ChatGPT use in academic work. A total of 853 undergraduate students participated in the study through a structured survey and open-ended response instrument. The structured data captured academic indicators, ChatGPT usage behavior, AI self-efficacy, learning motivation, academic anxiety, ethical awareness, self-regulated learning, and AI dependency, while the unstructured responses were processed using Natural Language Processing techniques. Bag-of-Words, TF-IDF, sentiment analysis, lexical indicators, and topic-based features were extracted and integrated with the structured variables to form a unified predictive feature matrix. Four supervised machine learning models, namely Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine, Random Forest, and XGBoost, were evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Results showed that XGBoost achieved the highest performance, obtaining 84.20% accuracy and 83.10% F1-score for academic performance classification, and 81.90% accuracy and 81.20% F1-score for psychological readiness classification. SHAP-based explainability analysis identified AI self-efficacy, verification behavior, AI dependency, study hours, responsible AI use, and learning motivation as the most influential predictors. The findings indicate that students' academic and psychological outcomes in ChatGPT-assisted learning are influenced not merely by frequency of use but by confidence, verification practices, responsible engagement, and dependency tendencies. The proposed framework provides a data-driven basis for designing AI literacy interventions and learner support strategies in higher education.

Title: Analysis of Student Competencies in the Digital Era: Based on Accounting Student Perceptions
Abstract: The advancement of technology has significantly transformed the roles and functions traditionally associated with accounting, thereby necessitating revisions to the academic curriculum to align with these evolving demands. In this context, the present study aims to investigate the disparity between accounting students’ perceptions regarding the importance of digital-era competencies and the extent to which higher education institutions contribute to the development of these skills. This study employed a quantitative descriptive research design, utilizing a questionnaire as the primary data collection instrument. The research population comprised students from four universities. Data were analyzed using the Wilcoxon test. The findings reveal that students place a high level of importance on both technological and soft skills relevant to the digital era; however, they perceive the universities’ efforts to enhance these competencies as insufficient. This perception is corroborated by the results of the Wilcoxon test, which indicate a statistically significant gap between student expectations and institutional performance in skill development. Future studies are encouraged to explore the accounting curriculum by evaluating the required soft skills and technical competencies, such as big data analytics, fundamental programming, and the application of artificial intelligence and emerging technologies in accounting education.

Title: Seizing the means of machine listening/ learning and agentic AI: creative practices with conTorchionist and vibe composing
Abstract: This article addresses the challenges posed by the hegemony of commercial, “black-boxed” Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools in musical creation, aiming to counteract the alienation inherent in Software as a Service (SaaS) platforms. Drawing on the concepts of mechanology and technodiversity, we advocate a critical and inventive engagement with technology through the appropriation of machine-listening and learning infrastructures. To this end, we present conTorchionist, an open-source, nomadic, and cross-platform library built upon libtorch, designed to bridge the gap between non-real-time research (Python) and real-time performance environments (Pure Data, Max, SuperCollider). Furthermore, we introduce the concept of ‘vibe composing’ as a methodology within research-development-creation and practice-based research in music, where the coding of algorithms assisted by agentic AI constitutes a fundamental poetic gesture. This approach is exemplified through two musical works, second nature (2025) and Eutrópia III (2025), which demonstrate how the development of idiosyncratic technical objects can engender unique aesthetic outcomes, ranging from spectral spatialization to neural control of latent spaces. Finally, we reflect on how seizing these technical means allows artists, particularly in the context of the Global South, to assert epistemic and technical sovereignty, fostering an ecology of invention that resists the standardization of the algorithmic age.

Title: AI-Powered Mobile Application for Supporting Mental Wellness in Children
Abstract: Children often struggle to express their emotions verbally, making early detection of mental health issues challenging and limiting timely intervention. This research proposes an AI-powered mobile application designed to support children's mental well-being through multimodal emotional analysis and personalized interventions. The significance of this study lies in addressing the lack of accessible, child-friendly, and culturally relevant digital mental health solutions, particularly for Sinhala-speaking users, while reducing dependence on subjective expert interpretation. The proposed system integrates four main components, including a culturally grounded therapeutic story generator using a GRU-based deep learning model, an emotion analysis module for children's drawings utilizing DenseNet121 and YOLOv8 with colour and spatial feature extraction, an emotion-aware music recommendation and adaptive puzzle game powered by EfficientNet-based facial emotion recognition, and a Sinhala voice-first mood prediction system using fine-tuned XLM-RoBERTa.Experimental results demonstrate strong performance, including improved contextual coherence and adaptive therapeutic storytelling capabilities, 79% accuracy in drawing-based emotion classification, 87% accuracy in emotion-aware music recommendation, and 96% accuracy in Sinhala text-based mood prediction, along with improved user engagement through personalized storytelling and adaptive feedback mechanisms. The system further enhances interpretability by generating parent-friendly emotional reports using large language models. In conclusion, this research contributes a comprehensive, multimodal, and culturally adaptive AI solution for supporting children's mental health, enabling early emotional detection, improved communication, and scalable intervention through an engaging mobile platform.

Title: Ensemble Learning for Coronary Heart Disease Detection: A Machine Learning Approach
Abstract: Coronary Heart Disease (CHD) has remained one of the foremost causes of death in the world, and thus, there is a need to ensure that there are dependable early diagnosis mechanisms that would aid clinicians in making decisions at the right time. The rapid development of electronic health records and sensor-based medical data has presented more opportunities in predictive analytics in healthcare than ever before. However, the sensitivity, complexity, and scale of health data require robust analytical models and a safe and reliable data processing system. In this respect, machine learning (ML) methods have become effective instruments in deriving significant patterns of heterogeneous healthcare data. This study hypothesizes an ensemble learning framework that is used in the early identification of CHD. The proposed ensemble model is more accurate and stronger in predictions than any of the individual models by incorporating several ML classifiers. The study provides a scalable method to prevent cardiovascular diseases, and the model may help healthcare professionals to identify high-risk patients at an early stage and, thus, implement interventions in time and enhance patient outcomes. Experimental results demonstrate that the ensemble model outperforms conventional ML models, highlighting its effectiveness as a supportive diagnostic tool for CHD prediction.

Title: TLN-YOLO: A Robust YOLOv8-Based Model for High-Precision Bird Nest Detection on Transmission Lines
Abstract: Bird nests on transmission lines are typical external hidden dangers that easily cause line short circuits, insulator flashover, and unplanned tripping accidents, seriously threatening the safe and stable operation of power grids. Existing deep learning-based detection methods still have prominent limitations: low detection accuracy for small and concealed nests, high missed and false detection rates in complex corridor backgrounds, and difficulty in balancing detection accuracy and real-time inference performance. To address the above challenges, this paper proposes Transmission Line Nest-YOLO (TLN-YOLO), a high-efficiency bird nest detection model based on the YOLOv8 baseline. First, an Enhanced Semantic and Receptive Field (ESRF) module is designed to replace the original Spatial Pyramid Pooling Fast (SPPF) module in the backbone, which effectively retains high-level semantic information of bird nest targets and suppresses complex background interference. Second, a modified Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) is integrated into both the backbone and neck networks, which enhances the network's discriminative feature learning for bird nest targets via joint channel and spatial attention weighting, and strengthens the multi-scale feature fusion capability of the model. Finally, Depthwise Separable Convolution (DSC) is introduced to replace standard convolution for downsampling in the neck, which reduces the computational complexity of the model without obvious accuracy loss. Experimental results on the self-built transmission line bird nest dataset show that TLN-YOLO achieves 83.5% precision, 72.8% recall, and 81.7% mAP@0.5. Compared with the baseline YOLOv8 model, the mAP@0.5 of TLN-YOLO is increased by 8.4 percentage points, while maintaining an inference speed of 146 FPS, which fully meets the real-time detection requirements of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV)-based transmission line inspection. This work provides a lightweight, high-precision, and edge-deployable technical solution for intelligent power grid inspection, and offers a valuable reference for the application of YOLO-series models in complex industrial defect detection scenarios.
