Title: Pediatric Wrist Fracture Detection Using Hybrid Model
Abstract: Effective and timely diagnosis of pediatric wrist fractures is essential for proper clinical management, although it is still hard to fulfill because of low fracture patterns, the anatomy of growing bones, and radiologists' increasing workload. The development of deep learning frameworks mainly single-stage object detection models like YOLO, has opened up the possibility of real-time and automatic fracture detection from X-ray images. Nevertheless, the reliability of the current models is still questionable as they are not applicable to clinically balanced pediatric datasets. In this paper, we present a new hybrid deep learning model that combines EfficientNet-based classification and YOLOv8-based localization to enhance the detection of pediatric wrist fractures. Initially, the system employs EfficientNet with transfer learning to classify wrist radiographs as fractured or non-fractured. Images identified as fractured are then passed to YOLOv8, which draws precise bounding boxes around the fracture locations. The proposed approach has been validated on the GRAZPEDWRI-DX dataset, it outperformed standard YOLOv8 variants in terms of detection performance. The proposed approach was validated on the GRAZPEDWRI-DX dataset, achieving a recall of 90.96 %, precision of 95.59 %, 94.99% mAP@50 for fracture localization-significantly outperforming standard YOLOv8 variants while maintaining real-time inference. The hybrid system has been very effective in reducing the number of false positives and in making the localization of lowcontrast fractures typical for pediatric radiographs easier. The findings convey that hybrid attention-enhanced deep learning models can be trusted as Computer-Assisted Diagnosis instruments for detecting pediatric wrist fractures, thus helping radiologists working in busy clinical environments.

Title: EmoTraceNet: Leveraging Residual Emotional Traces for Robust Audio Deepfake Detection
Abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence and generative models has enabled the creation of highly realistic synthetic speech, giving rise to deceptive audio deepfakes. Specifically, Emotional Voice Conversion (EVC) poses severe security risks by manipulating the emotional prosody of an utterance to bypass psychological defenses while strictly preserving linguistic content and speaker identity. Existing Audio Deepfake Detection (ADD) systems exhibit significant vulnerabilities against EVC attacks, primarily due to extreme emotional imbalances in current public datasets and an inability to decouple emotional features from spoofing artifacts. To address these limitations, we first introduce DeepEmo, a large-scale, emotionally balanced audio dataset encompassing the latest EVC generative models. Furthermore, our empirical analysis reveals that current EVC algorithms struggle to entirely disentangle source emotions, leaving identifiable emotional traces. Motivated by this emotion trace hypothesis, we propose EmoTraceNet, a novel dual-branch framework integrating a spoofing detection branch and an auxiliary emotion classification branch. By employing a cross-task attention fusion mechanism, EmoTraceNet explicitly captures the residual emotional traces as well as generative artifacts. Extensive experiments on the DeepEmo and EmoFake benchmarks demonstrate that our proposed approach achieves state-of-the-art performance (3.06% EER on DeepEmo). Notably, EmoTraceNet exhibits superior cross-domain generalization, robust cross-emotion detection capabilities, and strong resilience against acoustic noise compared to existing baselines.

Title: MarsMTFormer: A Unified Multitask Transformer for Martian Surface Detection and Instance Segmentation
Abstract: Martian surface understanding plays a crucial role in planetary geoscience, supporting autonomous rover navigation and geological interpretation in deep-space exploration. However, existing deep learning methods for Martian surface analysis are typically designed for single tasks and fail to exploit shared representations across terrain detection and segmentation. Although a few multitask frameworks incorporate auxiliary geometric cues, they lack the capability for unified instance-level recognition and fail to handle the extreme scale variations and heterogeneous task imbalances inherent to Martian terrains. In this study, we propose MarsMTFormer, a unified multitask transformer framework for Martian surface object detection and instance segmentation. To address the large-scale variations and sparse contextual information in Martian terrains, we design a gated global context enhancement decoder, which introduces compact global semantic tokens and employs an adaptive gating mechanism to selectively inject scene-level context into query representations, resulting in more stable and discriminative features. Moreover, the severe long-tailed distributions of Mars data lead to heterogeneous imbalance across detection and segmentation tasks, posing significant challenges for unified multitask learning. To overcome this, we develop an adaptive multitask weighted sampling strategy that dynamically balances training by jointly modeling category frequency and task-specific performance feedback, enabling coordinated optimization across detection and segmentation tasks. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MarsMTFormer delivers competitive performance on the MarsScapes and SynMars-TW datasets.

Title: Research on Transmission Line Acoustic Monitoring Technology Based on Distributed Acoustic Sensing
Abstract: Monitoring acoustic signals in the vicinity of transmission lines can effectively identify bird activities, mechanical construction, and lightning events within transmission corridors, providing support for bird hazards and external damage early warning, as well as lightning localization. Through theoretical modeling combined with simulation experiments, this study proposes an acoustic monitoring method for transmission lines based on optical ground wire (OPGW) and distributed acoustic sensing (DAS). First, by establishing models for acoustic wave propagation, acoustic-induced vibration, strain transfer, and DAS acoustic sensing, a quantitative theoretical model and the correlation between far-field acoustic source signals and optical fiber phase parameters are constructed. Second, a transmission line simulation test platform was built to experimentally investigate the acoustic sensing performance of OPGW. This validates the effectiveness of the proposed theoretical model, quantifies the acoustic pressure sensitivity (APS) and frequency response characteristics of the optical cable, and explores the impact of environmental wind speed on its acoustic sensing performance. On this basis, combined with field tests on a 220 kV transmission line, the applicability of the model to actual line scenarios is further discussed. Finally, the accuracies of different deep learning models in the task of transmission line bird song signal recognition are comparatively analyzed. The experimental results indicate that the phase response of the optical cable decreases rapidly with the increase of the acoustic source frequency. The APS is -109.67± 0.68 dB re 1 rad/μ Pa under a 100 Hz signal excitation, and drops to - 149.72 ± 2.30 dB re 1 rad/μ Pa at 5000 Hz. Furthermore, utilizing deep learning models can effectively identify bird activities on transmission lines, with the maximum recognition accuracy reaching 96.83%. This study provides a theoretical foundation and experimental validation for distributed acoustic state perception in transmission corridors.

Title: Transfer Learning-Enhanced Leaf Area Index Retrieval From Landsat Surface Reflectance Data
Abstract: In recent years, artificial neural networks (ANNs) trained on data simulated by radiative transfer models (RTMs) have demonstrated substantial potential for estimating vegetation biophysical parameters. However, substantial biases persist between ANN-based estimations and actual values because of model simplifications, discrepancies between simulated and real-world scenarios, and uncertainties in input parameters. In this study, a transfer learning-enhanced inversion method is proposed for retrieving leaf area index (LAI) from Landsat surface reflectance data by integrating a physical model with LAI ground measurements. Using a deep belief network (DBN) as the base model, the optimal hyperparameters are first determined through a Bayesian optimization algorithm (BOA); then, the DBN is pretrained using a dataset simulated by the PRO4SAILT model to construct a source model. All the parameters of the source model are subsequently fine-tuned to construct a fine-tuned model using carefully quality-controlled sparse LAI ground measurements provided by the implementing multiscale agricultural indicators exploiting sentinel (IMAGINES) and validation of European remote sensing (RS) instruments (VALERI) projects. During the fine-tuning process, regularization constraints are introduced to mitigate parameter overfitting, and a robust 10-fold cross-validation (CV) method is used to verify the performance of the fine-tuned model. The fine-tuned model is then applied to retrieve LAI values from Landsat surface reflectance data. The results demonstrate excellent agreement between the retrieved LAI values and those from the LAI reference maps from the IMAGINES and VALERI projects, with performance significantly outperforming the source model and SNAP software. This method effectively combines the advantages of RTM simulations and LAI ground measurements, offering a viable physical-model-based solution to mitigate the domain shift that occurs between simulated data and satellite observations.

Title: From Close Reading to Distant Reading: Generative AI and the Construction of a New Methodology for Literary Analysis
Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GAI) has recently emerged as a novel analytical instrument in the digital humanities, gradually reshaping both the conceptual foundations and practical configurations of literary research methods. Large language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT, with their capacities for rapid text generation, topic detection, and semantic mining, extend traditional practices of close reading toward the broader horizon of distant reading. This shift enables researchers to uncover latent intertextual patterns and macro-level cultural trends, and to explore new links between literary imaginaries and contemporary media circulation. However, the adoption of GAI also raises critical challenges. Most LLMs are trained predominantly on Western corpora, and their performance in cross-lingual analysis—especially for Chinese literary texts—remains under-examined. Furthermore, many literary scholars lack a deep understanding of the technical architecture and operational logic of LLMs, which can lead to interpretive bias, methodological misuse, and an uncritical reliance on AI-generated outputs. Problems such as cultural bias, loss of contextual nuance, and semantic distortion may thus go unnoticed. In response, this paper advocates for the establishment of clearly defined, guided conditions and systematic usage guidelines for GAI-assisted literary research. The study proceeds in three steps: (1) it analyzes how GAI reconfigures the theoretical underpinnings and methodological frameworks of literary studies; (2) it examines, through concrete cases, the practical difficulties encountered by literary scholars when using GAI tools; and (3) it proposes an operational framework and normative procedures that enable innovative yet responsible integration of GAI into literary analysis while safeguarding core humanistic values.

Title: Ensemble learning model evaluation for multi-horizon stock price forecasting: Performance and interpretability
Abstract: Stock market forecasting is a high-priority activity in financial decision-making and helps both investors and institutions in figuring out future price movements of stocks in a volatile and uncertain environment. Precise stock price prediction has always posed a challenge due to nonlinear temporal dependencies and influence by several economic factors, which also limit the scope of traditional statistical and single model learning techniques. This research intends to establish a robust multi-step-ahead forecasting framework for making precise Nifty Fifty index price predictions. In this context, this paper proposes an ensemble-driven Deep Learning (DL) approach where comprehensive data preprocessing with Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE) is integrated with multiple Machine Learning (ML) and DL models, including a Deep Neural Network (DNN) as the main predictor. The developed model reports 0.99853 as the R-squared value and 0.00675 as the Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) in one-step-ahead forecasting. For multistep-ahead forecasting, the model reports 724.37 RMSE values for 1-day, 920.02 for 3-day, and 2228.28 for 7-day time horizons while maintaining consistent trend behavior. The results demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed framework in modelling intricate market dynamics and establish this model as a significant instrument for short-term and medium-term stock price prediction.

Title: An Investigation of Prompt Engineering and Fine-Tuning Using Quantized Low Rank Adaptation for Medical Calculator Implementation on MedCalc-Bench
Abstract: Providing quality healthcare is a key goal of governments worldwide. There are enormous challenges, including the high cost of medical care, timeliness of treatments, and the optimization of available resources. The use of AI is emerging as a key technology to address some of these challenges. We focus on the use of clinical calculators, which are a key component in decision-support systems. We aim to automatically compute patient vitals from unstructured clinical notes to enhance workflow efficiency. However, this task remains an open challenge for language models. We investigate two complementary strategies for medical score calculation using the Qwen3-4B-Instruct small language model on eight rule-based calculators from the MedCalc-Bench benchmark: CHA2DS2-VASc, Centor, HEART, PERC, and SIRS. First, we develop a two-stage structured prompt that decomposes each task into entity extraction followed by rule application. Second, we apply supervised fine-tuning with QLoRA (4-bit NormalFloat quantization and low-rank adapters), attaining 60.0% accuracy on the same evaluation set. Comparative analysis reveals that structured prompting outperforms QLoRA fine-tuning on this subset, while fine-tuning yields superior format adherence and reduced hallucination. We also found that roughly half the SIRS test cases in MedCalc-Bench have incorrect labels, artificially limiting how well any model can perform. We determined that our model performance is insensitive to LoRA rank and learning rate within tested ranges. These findings offer practical guidance for deploying small language models in resource-constrained clinical AI settings.

Title: Comparative Evaluation of Machine Learning Models for Audio and Lyrics-Based Music Emotion Recognition
Abstract: Music emotion recognition (MER) plays a significant role in human-computer interaction and recommender systems. In this study, we conduct a comparative evaluation of machine learning models for MER within the dimensional Arousal-Valence framework. We explore three main approaches to emotion recognition in music: acoustic features, lyrical features, and their combination via early fusion. We first train regression models to predict continuous Arousal and Valence values using acoustic features, lyrical embeddings, and their early fusion. The predicted values are subsequently mapped into four emotion quadrants based on Russell's circumplex model. Model performance is then evaluated using classification metrics, including Accuracy, Precision, Recall, and F1-score, computed on the derived quadrants. We compare Logistic Regression, Ridge, SVM, Random Forest, K-NN, and XGBoost on the PMEmo2019 dataset. Experimental results show that the early fusion approach achieved the best overall performance, with k-Nearest Neighbors reaching an accuracy of 0.734 and an F1-score of 0.723. In contrast, audio-only and lyrics-only modalities performed moderately, while linear models consistently underperformed across all experimental settings.

Title: Cross-Domain Emotion Prediction and Speech Synthesis for the Kazakh Language
Abstract: This work presents a cross-domain system for emotion prediction and speech synthesis in Kazakh, a low-resource language in AI research. By fine-tuning the ai-forever/mGPT-1.3B-Kazakh model for emotion prediction from text inputs and integrating it with the facebook mms-tts-kaz model, we generate emotionally expressive speech. Leveraging the KazEmoTTS dataset, our approach demonstrates high emotion prediction accuracy and enhanced naturalness in synthesized speech, bridging a critical gap in Kazakh language resources. The proposed model predicts emotions from text and selects an appropriate fine-tuned text-to-speech (TTS) model to generate expressive speech corresponding to the predicted emotion. Evaluation results demonstrate effective emotion classification performance and improved perceptual quality of synthesized speech. This research provides an essential step towards improving AI-driven emotional expressiveness in Kazakh, with potential applications in virtual assistants, conversational AI, and accessibility tools.

Title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning as Strategic Instruments of Cybersecurity Risk Management in Digital Transformation
Abstract: Digital transformation has fundamentally reshaped the cyber-threat landscape, compelling organisations to rethink how they identify, assess, and mitigate risk. This paper investigates AI and ML as strategic facilitators of cybersecurity risk management and makes three original contributions. First, introduce the Cybersecurity Risk Framework (CRF) Score a composite index aggregating four entropy-weighted sub-dimensions (Detection Velocity, Accuracy Quotient, Scalability Index, and Governance Score) that quantifies organisational AI security maturity on a reproducible [0], [10] scale. Second, synthesise and quantify the performance advantages of five ML paradigms (supervised, unsupervised, deep learning, reinforcement learning, and NLP) across primary security use-cases. Third, validate the CRF Score against cross-industry data via OLS regression, establishing that each one-unit score improvement is associated with a 12.4% reduction in mean breachlifecycle duration. Results show that AI-enhanced environments achieve CRF Scores 2.0-2.8 × higher than traditional counterparts, with technology and financial services sectors leading. The paper concludes with a governance-grounded three-phase implementation roadmap calibrated to the NIST AI RMF.

Title: Constraint-Guided SUS Inference from Natural Language Feedback
Abstract: The System Usability Scale (SUS) remains widely adopted due to its psychometric grounding, low administration cost, and well-established normative benchmarks [7, 17]. However, conventional survey-based administration faces practical limitations at scale, including self-selection bias, respondent fatigue, and operational costs that grow with user base size [6, 8]. Naturally occurring user feedback—app reviews, support tickets, discussion forums—contains linguistically encoded signals of usability perception that machine learning models can extract at scale [1, 4]. Yet existing approaches treat the task as sentiment classification or thematic categorization, operating independently of formal psychometric instruments. This independence introduces an underexplored validity risk: unconstrained neural models may generate predictions that violate the structural properties of SUS—item polarity, inter-item consistency, and score range boundaries—while remaining statistically plausible. Evidence from adjacent domains confirms that statistical performance and psychometric coherence can diverge substantially [15, 16]. We propose a neuro-symbolic framework that addresses this risk directly. Neural components interpret natural language feedback; symbolic layers encode the structural constraints of SUS as explicit, enforceable rules within the inference process [5]. Rather than replacing SUS, the approach preserves its psychometric foundations while enabling large-scale usability assessment from naturally occurring feedback.

Title: A Guideline-Concordant Chatbot Framework for Structured Colorectal Cancer Screening: Multistage Feasibility Study
Abstract: Background: Colorectal cancer (CRC) screening relies on structured risk assessment and guideline-concordant communication, which remain challenging to implement consistently in real-world practice. Digital tools based on large language models (LLMs) may support such workflows, but their feasibility and safety in structured screening contexts have not been well evaluated. Objective: This study aimed to develop and evaluate a guideline-concordant chatbot framework for structured CRC screening. Methods: A multistage feasibility study was conducted. In phase 1, baseline performance of contemporary LLMs was assessed using 14 standardized CRC screening questions and validated expert-rated instruments. In phase 2, structured prompt versions were iteratively optimized based on screening guidelines and expert feedback and tested using simulated user scenarios. In phase 3, the optimized chatbot was evaluated in 50 screening-eligible adults to assess feasibility, safety, and guideline concordance. Results: In phase 1, both LLMs demonstrated satisfactory performance in responding to standardized CRC screening questions, with DISCERN instrument for AI-generated content scores of 12.02 (SD 0.30) for GPT-4o and 13.36 (SD 0.26) for DeepSeek-V3, Global Quality Score scores of 3.96 (SD 0.10) for GPT-4o and 4.39 (SD 0.08) for DeepSeek-V3, Natural Language Assessment Tool for AI scores of 21.41 (SD 0.34) for GPT-4o and 22.73 (SD 0.27) for DeepSeek-V3, and Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool adapted for AI outputs scores of 0.900 (SD 0.016) for GPT-4o and 0.906 (SD 0.015) for DeepSeek-V3. In phase 2, iterative prompt optimization significantly improved all 6 expert-rated dialogue evaluation dimensions (all P values <.001). In phase 3, the optimized chatbot successfully collected complete CRC screening risk information and generated guideline-concordant screening recommendations for all participants (N=50). No unsafe or inappropriate outputs were identified. Conclusions: This study demonstrated the feasibility, preliminary safety, and guideline-concordant performance of a structured chatbot framework for CRC screening communication under the study conditions. Beyond patient education, the proposed framework may support key components of the CRC screening workflow, including risk information collection, risk stratification, and generation of guideline-concordant screening recommendations. Further prospective studies are needed to evaluate the framework’s impact on patient-centered outcomes, screening uptake, and clinical effectiveness.

Title: Lightweight Structure Design of Crossover Equipment Based On Deep Learning and Topology Optimization-Control Integrated Algorithm
Abstract: Background: Lightweight structures often neglect closed-loop control needs, leading to designs that are stiff yet costly to actuate. Methods: We propose a joint framework that couples a CNN-based topology prior with SIMP refinement and an explicit control-performance term derived from a reduced state-space model; the CNN supplies near-optimal initial layouts, while the optimizer balances mass, compliance, and control effort via tunable weights. Results: Across canonical beams and an application-scale component, the method achieved up to 22% mass reduction versus a SIMP baseline, retained ≥90% target stiffness, satisfied 96% of stress constraints, and reduced iterations to convergence; control proxies (actuation energy/closed-loop cost) improved consistently, evidencing structure-control co-design benefits. Concluding Remarks: Integrating learning priors with physics optimization and control metrics yields lighter, easier-to-control structures and faster solve times. The framework is general and supports sensitivity studies over weights and constraints to guide engineering trade-offs.

Title: An Attention-based Multi-Modal Deep Learning Framework for Intelligent Thyroid Disease Diagnosis and Prediction
Abstract: Hypothyroidism, and Thyroid Disease are some of the serious health issues that afflict individuals in different regions of the world and therefore they need the right and timely diagnostic solutions to prevent the occurrence of severe metabolic and oncological complications. The conventional diagnostic techniques based on clinical examination, biochemical tests and imaging have a shortage of predictability, results interpretation latitude and subjectivity. To overcome these inadequacies, this study proposes an advanced multi-modal diagnostic model, which is an artificial intelligence-based diagnostic model. To begin with, Clinical Textual Data undergoes Clinical Textual Normalization and De-identification (CTND) in order to eliminate noise, normalize medical terminologies and ensure patient confidentiality whilst adaptive resizing, intensity normalization, speckle noise removal, and contrast enhancement are pre-projects on the thyroid ultrasound images to enhance the visual quality of the images. Then, textual information is analysed to obtain contextual and semantic characteristics using the BERT-Driven Clinical Text Intelligence Model (BD-CTIM), and ultrasound images are analysed to obtain deep spatial features. To locate the most informative representations, a Cross-Modal Attention Fusion Algorithms (CMAF-A) is employed to selectively and efficiently choose and combine features to end up with a single multi-modal feature. A combination of the attributes is classified in a Deep Multi-Modal Softmax Classification Network (DMMSCN) in a manner that can properly distinguish between hypothyroidism, hyperthyroidism, thyroid cancer and normal cases. The suggested model improves the detection performance and is more effective than the current ones. The thyroid dataset is used for the experiments and comprises 3772 records to evaluate the proposed approach's efficiency. Furthermore, the given framework is evaluated with the help of the standard performance measures including accuracy, precision, recall and F1-score, and the results of the experiment show that the given framework is much more efficient than the traditional and single-modes diagnostic models. In general, the proposed system is a proper, scalable, and smart instrument to enhance the diagnosis of thyroid illnesses and clinical decisions.

Title: Hybrid ConvNeXt-Swin Transformer Ensemble for Multiclass Kidney Lesion Classification from 2D CT Images
Abstract: An analysis with the computed tomography (CT) scan is crucial in identifying the condition of the kidneys and providing the right treatment method to the patient; nonetheless, the challenges of manual analysis may serve as a bottleneck in the clinical practice. To counter this challenge, we have designed a new deep learning model which we would apply to the categorization of kidney Tumors in multiple classes in an automated fashion. It is not based on our work on a single-architecture model and the hybrid ensemble to capitalize on the strengths of two state-of-the-art neural networks: the ConvNeXt-Tiny and the Swin-Tiny Transformer. The critical idea was to join the impressive ability of ConvNeXt to detect the local textures on a small scale with the possibility of Swin Transformer to perceive the overall and high-level view of the image. This model was tested and trained using publicly available CT-KIDNEY-DATASET which consisted of four classes: Normal, Cyst, Tumor and Stone. We have been pleased with the results of our experiments and believe that the ensemble can classify well and is also robust on unseen test data. Our Research demonstrates that one of the best approaches to combining convolutional and transformer style approaches is to create a powerful diagnostic instrument capable of actually changing the workflow of radiologists and the consistency of characterizing kidney Tumors.

Title: Genetic Algorithm Based Deep Time Series Similarity Searching Approach for Acoustic Fingerprinting
Abstract: With the exponential growth in music consumption, the demand for robust audio identification systems has intensified, especially for copyright detection and content-based retrieval. Acoustic fingerprinting, which identifies audio using unique spectral features, is a core technique in this domain. In this study, we propose a novel Deep Time Series Similarity Searching (DTSSS) framework for audio fingerprinting, leveraging a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)-based Siamese Neural Network. A key innovation of this work is the integration of a Genetic Algorithm (GA) to optimize hyperparameters critical to model performance. To enhance robustness, audio degradations such as noise, pitch, and tempo alterations were applied during data augmentation. The proposed system significantly outperforms the Shazam algorithm, achieving an accuracy of 64.44% compared to Shazam’s 21.22% on the same dataset of degraded audio. This result highlights the potential of combining deep learning with evolutionary optimization for high-fidelity, real-world audio retrieval systems.

Title: Infant Cry Sound Analysis and Classification with the Help of Machine Learning to Detect Early in Infancy
Abstract: Infant cry is a crucial first signal of communication that contains indicators of physiological needs and possible health issues. Title: DoA Estimation Based on Deep Learning-MUSIC Hybrid Algorithm with Fluid Antenna for Closely Spaced Signals
Abstract: Fluid antenna (FA) has emerged as a highly promising candidate in wireless communications, attributed to its exceptional design flexibility and enhanced degrees of freedom (DoFs). This paper addresses the challenge of direction-of-arrival (DoA) estimation for closely spaced signals under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and limited snapshot conditions. To tackle this issue, a dual-driven FA system is proposed, which synergistically integrates data-driven and model-driven paradigms. Drawing inspiration from the Toeplitz algorithm, a deep neural network (DNN)-based multi-layer perceptron (MLP) architecture is developed to learn the mapping relationship between input covariance matrices and labeled covariance matrices. To ensure the output covariance matrices are compatible with subsequent subspace-based search procedures, a constrained forward computation function is designed. Furthermore, a dual-constrained loss function is formulated to balance the numerical precision and structural consistency of the output covariance matrices. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves significant performance improvements over conventional DoA estimation algorithms in terms of estimation accuracy.

Title: A Lightweight YOLO11n Method for Steel Surface Defect Detection Based on Weak-Class-Aware Classification Loss Weighting
Abstract: Steel surface defect detection for edge deployment requires both lightweight inference and reliable recognition of weak or hard-to-learn defect categories. To address this issue, this paper proposes a lightweight YOLO11n method based on weak-class-aware classification loss weighting. Using the NEU-DET dataset and the Ultralytics YOLO11n framework, the proposed strategy keeps the detector architecture, parameter count, and inference pipeline unchanged, and introduces class-aware positive-sample weighting only during training for the weak classes crazing and rolled-in_scale. Specifically, the original binary cross-entropy term in the classification branch is replaced with a weighted BCEWithLogitsLoss, thereby strengthening supervision for weak classes without altering the deployed model. Comparative experiments involving high-resolution input, a P2 detection layer, P4-PSA enhancement, CLAHE preprocessing, weak-class oversampling, targeted augmentation, and larger teacher models show that these alternatives either fail to consistently surpass the baseline or are less suitable for deployment. Multi-seed experiments further show that the proposed strategy yields only slight but repeatable positive changes in the overall metrics and a relatively more stable gain for rolled-in_scale, while preserving the lightweight characteristics of YOLO11n. Therefore, the method should be viewed as a low-overhead training-stage refinement rather than a substantial performance boost.

Title: A Reliability-Weighted Demand Planning Model for AI Datacenter Infrastructure Under Vendor-Assessed Yield Uncertainty
Abstract: The artificial intelligence workload is growing exponentially, which has increased the need to have specialized data center infrastructure, such as gpus, server modules, power distribution systems, and liquid cooling devices. The current study offers a new framework of reliability-weighted demand planning that incorporates the vendor-evaluated yield uncertainty in the forecasting and procurement decisions of AI data center constructions. The model suggested scales supplier reliability by using the historical yield performance measurements, supplier quality scores and risk measures and then integrates the reliability indices into baseline demand projection using weighted adjustment mechanism. Experimental validation on the Advanced Semiconductor Supply Chain Dataset shows that there is substantial increase in predictability of the accuracy of the forecasts, and availability of the supply as well as predictability of the timeline of the deployment was much higher than the traditional methods of planning. The findings show the delay in infrastructure deployments is decreased by 23.7 % and the implementation of procurement efficiency is increased by 31.4 % and at the same time the costs of buffer inventory are lowered by 18.9 %. The reliability-weighted model offers the data center operators better supply assurance and allocation strategies in the case of vendor yield variability, and helps to achieve more resilient and cost-effective AI infrastructure deployment.

Title: Artificial Intelligence Pilot Vision: Contextual Cockpit Readout for VR/MR Training
Abstract: The rapid adoption of virtual and mixed reality technologies (VR/MR) in pilot training has led to an increased use of eye tracking as an objective source of information about visual attention, situational awareness and workload. However, conventional gaze visualizations, such as heatmaps, primarily indicate where a trainee looked while providing limited information about what cockpit data were visually accessible at the moment of fixation. This paper presents the detection stage of a broader artificial intelligence (AI)-driven framework designed to infer cockpit information accessibility directly from image-based eye-tracking recordings without requiring simulator APIs or proprietary avionics interfaces. The proposed approach operates purely on image inputs, supporting portability across different VR/MR ecosystems and potential applicability in both virtual and physical cockpit environments. The complete framework combines real-time cockpit instrument localization with subsequent semantic readout modules for instrument interpretation, including OCR for digital displays, regression-based estimation for analog gauges, and classification of binary indicators. The present work focuses exclusively on the detection stage. A dataset of 2,750 annotated cockpit frames covering 21 instrument classes was created from high-resolution flight simulator recordings using a semi-automatic annotation workflow. To reduce temporal data leakage, the dataset was partitioned using a temporally separated train-validation strategy. Two state-of-the-art object detectors, YOLOv7 and RT-DETRv2, were trained and evaluated for real-time cockpit instrument detection. Both models achieved an mAP@0.5 exceeding 0.99, while RT-DETRv2 achieved superior localization performance with an mAP@0.5:0.95 of 0.855 compared to 0.780 for YOLOv7. Inference benchmarks on commodity GPU hardware (NVIDIA RTX 5060 Ti) demonstrated real-time operation for both models, with TensorRT-accelerated latency of 2.3 ms for RT-DETRv2 and 3.3 ms for YOLOv7 at FP16 precision, well within the 90 fps performance budget of VR/MR training systems. The results demonstrate that accurate real-time cockpit instrument detection is feasible on standard gaming GPU hardware and suitable for integration into future gaze-aware pilot training frameworks.

Title: CAREER CRAFT: AI-Based Intelligent Guidance
Abstract: Integrating several guidance services into one digital ecosystem, a single intelligent platform named Career Craft was created to streamline and improve the career development process of students and professionals. The system brings together the key instruments, including resume creation, talent evaluation, job suggestion, job interview preparation, and cover-letter creation, into a single platform, and there is no necessity to depend on career fragment assets. Title: Random Forest-Based Prediction of Microgrid Power Quality With Hybrid Energy Storage Systems
Abstract: The growing incorporation of renewable energy sources and electric vehicle (EV) charging stations into microgrids presents issues in sustaining steady power quality due to inconsistent output and unpredictable demand. This paper introduces a predictive framework using Random Forest (RF) to anticipate power quality in microgrids integrated with Hybrid Energy Storage Systems (HESS). The model is trained and assessed via dataset of 2, 5 0 0 operating records of microgrid systems, each categorized by power quality as Low, Medium, or High. The RF model had an overall classification accuracy of 99.20 %, indicating robust predictive efficacy. Analysis of feature significance revealed that the state of the storage system and the parameters of power flow substantially affect power quality results. The model demonstrated consistent performance across many environments, including residential, business, and public spaces, underscoring its adaptability. These findings highlight the capability of machine learning methods to improve microgrid dependability, facilitate proactive energy management, and maintain consistent power quality across diverse operating settings. The proposed framework provides a pragmatic instrument for operators to enhance the efficiency of hybrid energy storage systems and provide superior power supply in contemporary microgrid settings.

Title: ML-Based Real-Time Multimodal Confidence Assessment System for Communication Skill Development
Abstract: The dependability of measuring the confidence of an individual on interpersonal communication is a major challenge, which is always dependent on subjective human judgement and thus presents incongruent results due to prejudice. This paper suggests a new real-time multimodal system of automated confidence evaluation using the live speech and facial behavioural patterns. It has a dual-stream architecture (speech confidence, MFCCs, head pose, prosodic characteristics) and a facial confidence architecture (eye-contact dynamics, head pose, expression dynamics). A system of weighted embeddings (0.7 speech, 0.3 facial) is used to obtain a continuous score of confidence on a scale of 0 - 1 0 0. To overcome the lack of ground-truth confidence labels in available datasets, affective state-to-estimated confidence levels are simulated with the help of IEMOCAP and AffectNet. The system provides a real-time performance and a latency of less than 500 ms with a fusion accuracy of 94.2 per cent and F 1 of 0.94. A Confidence Stability Index (CSI) is used to measure the model calibration. The pipeline is tested using offline metrics and real-time user experiments which form a scalable basis of objective communication coaching.

Title: AI-Driven Intelligent Data Acquisition Architecture Using NI DAQ for Real-Time Sensing, Analytics, and Automation
Abstract: Many traditional data acquisition (DAQ) tools only transform a sensors' output and do nothing else to aid in understanding a system, responding to variables, or achieving automated control functions. As a result, they do not function efficiently in a factory, hospital, or smart city. These environments require a system to function at a high level, integrating precise, real-time, and context-aware data. This paper describes a reconfigured data acquisition framework that employs National Instruments (NI) DAQ hardware, which is intended to operate not just as a measurement interface, but as an intelligent processing layer. The proposed system incorporates advanced signal conditioning, multisensor feature extraction, and real-time modeling to detect and diagnose performance degradation and faults in real-time during data acquisition. The system adaptability, decision autonomy, and predictive maintenance capabilities across several domains are the result of a seamless integration of NI DAQ modules and architectural inference capabilities. As more channels are added, experimental results show an increase in accuracy of measurements, quicker response times, and adaptability of the system on a continual basis. The inclusion of more advanced capabilities into the DAQ workflow not only enhances the ease with which individual users can understand a system, but also increases efficiency, reliability, and overall system performance.

Title: Hybrid Temperature Control System: Embedded PID with Sensor Diagnostics and ML-Driven Forecasting
Abstract: This paper presents an Arduino-based temperature control system integrating a Proportional-IntegralDerivative (PID) algorithm with real time data visualization and machine learning (ML) capabilities. The control setup employs a MAX6675 thermocouple sensor interfaced with an Arduino Uno and an AC dimming circuit using a TRIAC for precise heat regulation. In addition to conventional PID control, a Streamlit based Python dashboard was developed for real-time monitoring, data analytics, and predictive modeling. A comparative analysis among LM35, RTD (PT100), and thermocouple sensors was performed to evaluate measurement accuracy, response time, and electromagnetic interference (EMI) immunity. Supervised ML models including Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Linear/Logistic Regression were trained on time- series temperature data. The Random Forest model achieved an R2 value above 0.95 for regression tasks and over 9 0% accuracy in classification of controller states (ON/OFF). Experimental results demonstrate that thermocouples deliver superior performance in TRIAC based thermal control circuits. The study highlights how integrating smart predictive models with conventional PID control enhances adaptability, robustness, and intelligence in hybrid hardware, software temperature regulation systems. This approach establishes a foundation for developing future intelligent thermal management and energy efficient control applications.

Title: PhonIA: A Web-Based Human–Machine Cooperative System for Accessible Vocal Health Monitoring
Abstract: Voice disorders represent a significant occupational risk for professionals who rely on their voice as a primary working tool, including teachers, singers, and broadcasters. Early detection and continuous monitoring of vocal alterations remain challenging due to the limited accessibility of specialized clinical assessment and the absence of objective, preventive tools suitable for regular use. This study presents the development and evaluation of PhonIA, a web-based computational application designed for the analysis, monitoring, and early identification of vocal pathologies through acoustic signal processing and machine learning techniques. The system integrates Digital Signal Processing (DSP) methods with supervised learning algorithms to extract and analyze clinically validated acoustic parameters, including fundamental frequency (F0), jitter, shimmer, and Harmonic-to-Noise Ratio (HNR). Parameter extraction was implemented using the Praat Parselmouth library and validated through direct comparison with the Praat software, demonstrating high numerical concordance. Classification models – including Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest, and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) – were trained and evaluated using the Advanced Voice Function Assessment Databases (AVFAD), comprising 709 labeled voice recordings (healthy and pathological). Two experimental configurations were tested: (1) a baseline model using classical acoustic features and (2) an optimized model incorporating additional acoustic and contextual attributes with hyperparameter tuning. Results showed substantial performance improvements in the optimized configuration, with XGBoost achieving the best overall performance (accuracy = 86.5%), demonstrating strong sensitivity and balanced classification between healthy and pathological voices. Feature importance analysis confirmed the central role of jitter- and shimmer-related parameters in pathological voice discrimination. The proposed system demonstrates that combining clinically interpretable acoustic measures with optimized machine learning models provides a robust and scalable solution for vocal health screening and longitudinal monitoring. PhonIA represents a promising assistive tool for preventive vocal care, with potential applications in telemedicine, clinical triage, and professional voice management.

Title: Deep Learning-Based Framework for Rapid Screening for Type 2 Diabetes Onset in Healthcare Applications
Abstract: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) is a widespread chronic metabolic disease, which has become a most important health and financial burden, and that is why there is imperative to have effective early diagnostic options. The explosion of diverse healthcare data provides new vistas of predictive modeling, but the traditional approaches to diagnostics and the traditional methods of machine learning are still confined in terms of their ability to identify nonlinear and complicated relations. The paper introduces a deep learning-based framework of early T2DM detection through the combination of advanced neural designs and data preprocessing and interpretation. Various models are tested such as ensemble classifiers, Convolutional neural networks (CNNs), Autoencoders (AEs), and a Temporal Inception Perceptron Network (TIPNet) based on various clinical, demographic, and lifestyle characteristics. To deal with the problem of class imbalance, adaptative synthetic oversampling algorithms are used, whereas explainable artificial intelligence tools like LIME and SHAP are used to improve the transparency of the model. The experimental findings of independent testing and 1 0-fold cross-validation show that the proposed framework can have better predictive performance, and its accuracy and significant enhancement of F1-score, recall, and AUC. The results support the framework effectiveness as a smart clinical decision-support instrument in terms of early diagnosis and individual care.

Title: AI-Powered Road Accident Severity Prediction Using Ensemble Learning on Large-Scale Traffic Data
Abstract: Predicting the severity of road accidents before or immediately after they occur can improve emergency response and traffic infrastructure planning. This paper presents a machine learning study using the US Accidents dataset (2016-2023), covering 7.7 million records from 49 states, to classify each accident into one of four severity levels. Three ensemble models-Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Random Forest (RF), and Gradient Boosting (GB)are trained alongside two linear baselines, Logistic Regression and a Support Vector Machine via SGD. The pipeline includes temporal and geospatial feature engineering, weather normalization, and infrastructure risk scoring, with an 80/20 stratified split and standard feature scaling. Cost-sensitive learning via XGBoost's scale-pos-weight pa-rameter is employed to address extreme class imbalance. XGBoost achieved the highest weighted accuracy of 91.24% (weighted F1: 0.912; macro F1: 0.46; balanced accuracy: 0.61); Random Forest reached 89.85%. Linear models plateaued near 68%, confirming non-linear separability. Geographic coordinates and road infrastructure variables are the dominant predictors, confirmed via SHAP analysis. Severe class imbalance limits minority-class recall even with cost-sensitive training; ADASYN-based remediation is discussed as a key future direction.

Title: PCAUSE: A Web-Based Machine Learning Tool for PCOS Pre-Assessment Using Non-Invasive Features
Abstract: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) is a frequently encountered endocrine dysfunction affecting women of reproductive age. There is an associated heightened risk for gynecologic malignancies with PCOS and as such, would require early recognition to allow prompt institution of therapeutic measures. It is worth mentioning that the combination and severity of symptoms can vary substantially among women with PCOS, making early recognition challenging. Given the heterogeneity of PCOS symptoms, there is increasing interest in machine learning approaches that capitalize on non-invasive attributes. After a thorough preprocessing technique applied to a publicly available PCOS dataset from a machine learning repository, including data cleaning, multicollinearity mitigation, and class imbalance handling via Borderline SMOTE and mutual information feature selection, nine machine learning classifiers in four model configurations with hyperparameter tuning via GridSearchCV to optimize model performance were evaluated for PCOS prediction. k-Nearest Neighbors enhanced with both Borderline SMOTE and mutual information feature selection came out as the best performing algorithm, attaining the utmost sensitivity (0.86), vital for timely recognition and bringing down false negatives, with very good specificity (0.88) and AUROC (0.90). The best model was also integrated with an explainability functionality using Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations offering transparent, actionable insights. Lastly, a web-based prototype application (PCAUSE) was created to provide an automated preliminary tool aimed at determining PCOS risk harnessing only noninvasive clinical and lifestyle factors. Assigned to be clinically adjunctive and user-friendly screening instrument, PCAUSE fills the gap by permitting women and assisting healthcare workers in early risk recognition - particularly in resource-deficient scenarios.

Title: Deep Learning-Based Maneuvering UAV Tracking in Multi-User Uplink ISAC Systems
Abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) offers a promising paradigm for low-altitude unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) surveillance by leveraging existing cellular infrastructure. However, tracking highly maneuvering UAVs using uplink reference signals in multi-user ISAC systems remains challenging. On one hand, conventional motion models often fail to capture complex UAV dynamics, leading to severe motion model mismatch. On the other hand, noisy user equipment positions result in measurement model mismatches and can degrade the performance significantly. To tackle these challenges, we propose a learning-aided extended Kalman filter for robust 3D position and velocity tracking. The method combines a neural prediction module that learns UAV maneuvers and a neural update module that adaptively corrects the innovation covariance to handle parametric uncertainties. Our proposed signal processing pipeline, which incorporates clutter suppression, parameter estimation via MUSIC and the iterative adaptive approach, and the learning-aided tracker, is validated in realistic ray-tracing scenarios with diverse UAV trajectories. Results demonstrate that our scheme significantly outperforms baseline methods in tracking accuracy and robustness while reducing computational complexity.

Title: MX-AI: Agentic Observability and Control Platform for Open and AI-RAN
Abstract: Future 6G radio access networks (RANs) will be artificial intelligence (AI)-native: observed, reasoned about, and re-configured by autonomous agents cooperating across the cloud-edge continuum. We introduce MX-AI, the first end-to-end agentic system that (i) instruments a live 5G Open RAN testbed based on OpenAirInterface (OAI) and FlexRIC, (ii) deploys a graph of Large-Language-Model (LLM)-powered agents inside the Service Management & Orchestration (SMO) layer, and (iii) exposes both observability and control functions for 6G RAN resources through natural-language intents. On 150 realistic operational queries, MX-AI attains a mean answer quality of 4.1 / 5.0, and 100 % decision action accuracy, while incurring only 8.8 secs end-to-end latency when backed by GPT-4.1. Latency is reduced to 1.3 secs when utilizing lama3.2:3b-q4 approaching near-real-time loops. Thus, it competes human experts performance, validating its practicality in real settings. We publicly release the agent graph, prompts, and evaluation harness to accelerate open research on AI-native RANs. Title: MIMO Spatial Multiplexing in Wireless Networks-on-Chip in the Terahertz Band
Abstract: We investigate the application of MIMO spatial multiplexing to enhance the capacity of wireless chip-to-chip communication links. Chip-scale environments present unique advantages: the propagation environment is static and potentially fully known, allowing for the pre-computation of coding weights and optimization of antenna placement. Moreover, the rich multipath and near-field characteristics at this scale enable effective spatial multiplexing, overcoming the limitations of conventional time-frequency resource division. This is particularly critical for meeting the high-throughput demands of emerging applications such as big data centers, artificial intelligence, virtual reality, and augmented reality. In this work, we explore this novel setting using ray-tracing-based modeling to accurately capture the complex propagation behavior within typical chip geometries. We validate our modeling approach through full-wave electromagnetic simulations using Ansys HFSS. By analyzing the resulting channel matrices, we evaluate the achievable MIMO capacity under different settings and demonstrate the feasibility and performance potential of spatial multiplexing in highly confined and deterministic chip-scale environments.

Title: EGO: Enhancing GPU Observability using eBPF
Abstract: Modern high-performance computing applications, including machine learning and scientific workloads, increasingly rely on graphics processing units (GPU) to meet their computational demands. Current GPU monitoring solutions confront critical limitations, often trading granular observability for efficiency or vice versa. While emerging kernel space technologies such as extended Berkeley packet filters (eBPF) have demonstrated low-overhead metric collection in network monitoring, their adaptation to GPU telemetry has remained largely unexplored. This paper presents eGO (eBPF for GPU Observability), a novel framework for GPU performance monitoring in cloud-native environments that captures fine-grained metrics with minimal resource contention. Our approach instruments GPU kernels, memory operations, and scheduling events using eBPF's in-kernel programmability. Extensive experimental evaluations on Chameleon Cloud bare-metal testbed reveal that eGO minimizes CPU overheads by 18× over conventional tools, and reduces instruction processing by over 130× during complex workloads. Furthermore, by eliminating polling, eGO captures events on average 118 ms earlier than nvidia-smi. Our evaluations demonstrate that eGO significantly enhances operational efficiency and measurement granularity, while also extending observability with comprehensive telemetry for identifying microsecond-scale bottlenecks in CUDA workloads for cloud operators.

Title: TraPos: A Transformer-Based Localization Framework for Next-Generation Mobile Networks
Abstract: In multipath-rich indoor environments, accurate localization remains a challenging task, as bandwidth-limited signals require high-resolution algorithms for precise parameter estimation. To address this challenge, we introduce TraPos, a transformer-based framework for indoor localization. The network is trained and evaluated on 5G channel measurements collected with a software-defined radio (SDR) platform. The datasets were acquired using an automated guided vehicle (AGV), with spatial uniformity ensured through grid-based filtering. As a baseline, TraPos is compared to a state-of-the-art joint angle-delay Multiple Signal Classification (MUSIC) algorithm. Results show that TraPos outperforms the super-resolution method in both angle of arrival (AOA) and time difference of arrival (TDOA) estimation. Title: Benchmarking deep learning pipelines for surgical instrument segmentation in endoscopic spine surgery: cross-dataset evaluation under deployment-realistic conditions
Abstract: Purpose: Automated surgical instrument segmentation is a prerequisite for AI-assisted guidance in endoscopic spine surgery. Deployment-realistic comparisons of foundation-model and conventional deep learning architectures — accounting for the detector dependency of bbox-prompted models — remain lacking. Methods: Seven deep learning pipelines were evaluated for binary instrument segmentation: U-Net, Attention U-Net, U-Net++, SegFormer-B0, DeepLabV3+, nnU-Net, and a fully automatic two-stage foundation-model pipeline (MedSAM2-Tiny segmentor + YOLOv8-nano detector). Strict patient-level data splitting was applied across two independent datasets (SNUBH biportal, n = 56 patients; SEA uniportal, n = 60 patients) with three-tier testing (internal, temporal external, cross-dataset external) and two training variants (biportal-only; combined biportal–uniportal). Results: With biportal-only training, the fully automatic foundation-model pipeline ranked last on cross-dataset external testing (DSC 0.776; 0.737 under a strict empty-mask convention), about 9% points below DeepLabV3+ (0.865). The same MedSAM2-Tiny segmentor reached DSC 0.946 with ground-truth bounding-box prompts, leaving a 16.9-point oracle-to-deployment gap driven by detector domain mismatch: 61% missed detections and 39% box-localization error. With combined training, all seven pipelines exceeded DSC 0.94; nnU-Net was highest (0.978), and the foundation-model pipeline (0.962) was not significantly different from SegFormer-B0 (0.960) or DeepLabV3+ (0.958) after Bonferroni correction, although the small external sample does not establish equivalence. The improvement was driven primarily by detector rather than segmentor learning, and all seven main pipelines except the nnU-Net 5-fold ensemble met the 30 frames-per-second real-time threshold. Conclusions: Foundation-model two-stage pipeline performance depends critically on detector training data coverage; once the segmentor approaches its oracle ceiling, detector domain coverage becomes the limiting factor for fully automatic deployment. When combined training is feasible, foundation-model and conventional architectures converge to comparable accuracy, although these rankings are specific to the datasets studied and require validation on independent cohorts. Reporting deployment DSC alongside the ground-truth bounding-box upper bound is recommended for future surgical-segmentation benchmarks.

Title: High-performance gas measurement systems—bridging the gap between sensors and analytics
Abstract: In gas measurements, there is inherent competition between sensors and analytical systems, often made difficult by a lack of understanding of approaches and constraints from both sides. Title: Localized Federated Learning for Personalized Music Recommendations: Implementation and Evaluation on Android
Abstract: This work introduces the design and implementation of a privacy-centric music recommendation system based on federated learning methods running on Android devices. Traditional music recommendation systems are based on centralized storage of data, which infringes heavily on user privacy. We overcome these threats by allowing personal recommendations without retaining user data on central servers. We model a Neural Collaborative Filtering (NCF) using TensorFlow Lite and train it locally on user interaction history, providing only model updates—and not raw data—to a central server for aggregation. This federated architecture preserves privacy while maintaining recommendation quality through coordinated model tuning. Our system demonstrates the practical feasibility of privacy-preserving personalization in mobile systems, presenting a working alternative to the traditional centralized data approach. Performance tests compare our federated approach with baseline strategies, highlighting its capacity to produce accurate recommendations without sacrificing privacy. This work presents a blueprint for applying federated learning in consumer apps, facilitating ethical AI adoption in personalized services beyond music streaming.

Title: Enhancing Prostate Cancer Detection Accuracy in MRI-Guided Biopsy Using Q-HyCVT-Net
Abstract: Accurate detection techniques remain essential in addressing prostate cancer as a major health issue because they provide early diagnosis and treatment planning capabilities. The effectiveness of traditional MRI-guided biopsy techniques faces challenges because it fails to perform accurately when detecting lesions and extracting features from them. Q-HyCVT-Net represents the combination of deep learning techniques along with quantum computing principles to build better instruments for detecting prostate cancer. The Q-HyCVT-Net utilizes a QIFE module featuring QWT and QEM to extract high-dimensional spatial and textural MRI scan features. The integration of Hybrid CNN-Vision Transformer (AM-CV) uses area-specific spatial feature analysis from CNN and far-reaching contextual competence from ViT to develop a comprehensive representation of prostate irregularities. The HQC operates as the final stage of classification by uniting QKL and QDTs to produce more reliable predictions and lower the number of erroneous positives. The Q-HyCVT-Net achieves superior performance than standard deep learning methods in MRI dataset evaluations conducted on Prostate and PI-CAI benchmarks. The methodology reaches 98.2% accuracy alongside 97.9% sensitivity and 98.5% specificity which demonstrates higher performance than standard CNNbased radiomics together with standalone Vision Transformers. The medical community trusts the system more by using explainable AI (XAI) techniques which produce visual model prediction explanations by showing both saliency maps and feature attribution analytics. The Q-HyCVT-Net constitutes an innovative system for MRI Page Route Due to demonstrated excellence in diagnostic precision through quantum-based quantitative assessments combined with deep learning technologies. The model shows high potential for real-world clinical use because of its exceptional performance alongside its interpretability features and its reliable decision-making capacity which leads to more precise and early prostate cancer detection.

Title: Edge-to-Cloud Iot Framework for Real-Time Urban Noise Mapping and AI-Driven Acoustic Classification
Abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of an end-to-end Internet of Things (IoT) framework for real-time urban noise mapping and intelligent acoustic classification. Traditional noise monitoring relies on expensive, static sound level meters that lack spatial granularity. To address this, we propose a mobile crowdsensing architecture where smartphones act as ubiquitous sensory nodes. Audio samples and GPS coordinates are captured via a cross-platform Flutter mobile application and transmitted via the lightweight MQTT protocol to a Dockerized backend. An automated Python-based consumer pipeline processes incoming streams, extracting core acoustic features including Root Mean Square (RMS) amplitude, Zero-Crossing Rate (ZCR), and Spectral Centroid. Audio is then passed through an AI-driven classification engine utilizing the YAMNet deep learning model to categorize sound sources into distinct classes such as Speech, Traffic, and Silence. Classified, geolocated data is stored in InfluxDB, a high-performance time-series database, and visualized on a live interactive web dashboard using Leaflet.js and Grafana. Additionally, Google Gemini AI generates automated acoustic forensics reports for government authorities. Experimental results show classification confidence exceeding 88% and total system latency under 600 ms.

Title: Human Skin Disease Detection Using Deep Learning
Abstract: Skin diseases are global health concern require accurate and efficient diagnostic methods; Dermatologists often face challenges due to low lesion contrast and visual similarities between affected and healthy skin. To address this, we propose a computeraided diagnostic model using image preprocessing techniques to enhance the features extraction process and reduce the noise. Data augmentation is also used to enhance the learning accuracy of the classifier and then the performance of the proposed model. The Proposed Solution provides wider access to an automated system to classify skin diseases using deep learning as a convenient, fast, inexpensive diagnostic tool that will lower misdiagnosis rates and help provide timely treatment. Preferred framework implies that a highly varied dataset of dermoscopic images would be gathered and prepared to be used by the model, then trained on strong machine and deep learning models to perform multi-class classification. Experimental results showed that the performance of the methodology using deep learning Vision Transformer model overcomes the literature review methods and achieved 98% accuracy for 5-class classification and 93% accuracy for 10-class classification which proves its consistency in different complexities. Moreover, the model is hosted as a convenient web application, which allows performing image uploads and getting real-time predictions of the diagnosis. The effectiveness of the system has been empirically verified, which suggests its prospect as a convenient instrument of dermatological analysis.

Title: Inferring Attention and Concentration from Gameplay Interaction Data Using AI-Based Learning Analytics
Abstract: Game-based learning environments generate rich streams of interaction data that capture learners’ behavioral patterns in ways traditional static assessments cannot. Within Human-Computer-Interaction (HCI) research, however, the use of educational games as instruments for assessing cognitive skills such as attention and concentration remains limited. This study presents a predictive learning analytics framework that models gameplay interaction behaviors as proxies for underlying attention-related subskills through human-AI interaction. The framework is grounded in an in-house educational game designed by the GameIT studio to elicit measurable indicators of attention, including task completion patterns, response timing, error frequency, and progression across difficulty levels. The empirical dataset comprises 74 gameplay sessions from six learners, with 24 features capturing progress, performance, mistakes, and time spent across easy, medium, and hard tasks. Initial statistical analysis revealed consistently high task progress alongside meaningful variability in performance efficiency, motivating predictive modeling of attention profiles. To address the small and imbalanced dataset, a Conditional Generative Adversarial Network (CGAN) was employed to generate synthetic gameplay data conditioned on performance categories. Three supervised learning models were evaluated: Random Forest, AdaBoost, and k-Nearest Neighbors. Ensemble methods substantially outperformed distance-based approaches. Random Forest achieved 97.5% accuracy with balanced precision and recall, whereas AdaBoost exceeded 99% accuracy in identifying high-attention learners. From an HCI perspective, the findings demonstrate how fine-grained interaction data can enable explainable, non-intrusive cognitive assessment, supporting adaptive feedback and early intervention in child-focused digital environments.

Title: A Trust-Aware Structural Model for Secure AI-Enabled Cloud E-Learning Systems
Abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and cloud computing into higher education has transformed e-learning platforms into complex socio-technical ecosystems. Although cloud-enabled Education-as-a-Service (EaaS) architectures enhance scalability and accessibility, and AI-driven analytics support personalization and predictive feedback, sustainable learning outcomes depend on behavioral adoption dynamics and perceived cybersecurity assurance. To address this challenge, an integrated structural framework is developed to examine how Cloud/EaaS Capability and Data-Intelligence Capability influence Adoption (grounded in UTAUT), which in turn drives E-Learning Success. Cybersecurity Trust is conceptualized as a moderating boundary condition shaping the strength of the adoption-outcome relationship. Beyond theoretical integration, the study introduces a layered secure architecture aligned with the structural logic and proposes a validated measurement instrument designed for empirical assessment using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The resulting framework offers a coherent perspective for understanding how intelligent capability, scalable cloud infrastructure, and governance-oriented security mechanisms jointly determine sustainable performance in AI-enabled educational environments.

Title: Autonomous Road Surface Distress Detection for Laser Crack Measurement System
Abstract: Localizing and identifying pavement damage types are crucial for road condition inspection. The Laser Crack Measurement System (LCMS) is widely used in the road inspection industry due to its ability to capture high-quality road surface images, producing reliable damage detection results, particularly for cracks, patches, and potholes. However, automated distress detection using these images remains constrained because of the cost of LCMS-equipped instrument and the limited public availability of their image data. Additionally, existing AI-based methods for detecting only cracks, patches, and potholes are prone to errors, often mis-classifying other un-trained abnormal pavement features as cracks or patches. Furthermore, the significant size differences between these two types of distress frequently lead to false results when detecting them simultaneously. To address these issues, the current study introduces a two-step system integrated with LCMS for detecting multiple pavement distress types, including crack, joint, patch, pothole, and sealed crack. The system employs automated segmentation models leveraging machine learning and deep learning techniques, represented by the Random Forest (RF) model and the U-Net model, respectively. The preliminary results demonstrate a significant improvement in detecting multiple distress types. Quantitatively, the U-Net model outperforms the RF model, demonstrating an approximate improvement of 78%, 89%, and 78% for large, medium, and small features segmentation, respectively. The U-Net model also exhibits more stable inference performance with new images, attributed to its convolutional neural network architecture. The outcomes of this study contribute to advancing methodologies in computer vision applications for pavement inspection and provide practical insights for pavement engineering.

Title: A multi-objective portfolio optimization model incorporating sentiment analysis of quarterly reports and LSTM-based price prediction
Abstract: Sentiment analysis (SA) of natural language text has become as a powerful instrument for enhancing financial market predictions. Quarterly reports from companies, in particular, offer a rich source of data for sentiment analysis, providing key insights into a company‚Äôs performance, strategic actions, and future prospects. These reports can significantly influence investor decisions regarding asset investments. Notwithstanding the potential, prior research has not investigated sentiment analysis concerning these resources in portfolio optimization. To fill this void, we propose an innovative three-stage approach to constructing stock portfolios. In the first stage, we perform sentiment analysis on companies‚Äô quarterly reports using the FinBERT model to assess the sentiment surrounding each company. In the second stage, we utilize a Long-Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model for forecasting future prices, which enables the calculation of expected returns and the covariance matrix. In final stage, we present a three-objective portfolio optimization model that incorporates risk, return, and sentiment-derived trend features. We solve this model using the Weighted Goal Programming (WGP) method. Our results indicate that the proposed model effectively supports portfolio optimization. Moreover, the model is implemented using data from companies that are part of the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA), and findings demonstrate high accuracy, confirming the practical potential of the proposed approach.

Title: A Unity-Based Experimental Instrument for Studying AI-Based Decision Support in Dynamic Visual Search Tasks
Abstract: Investigating human-AI collaboration in visual search requires experimental paradigms that balance ecological validity with methodological control. We present a Unity-based scene generator that creates dynamic aerial emergency scenarios with parametric control over scene complexity, AI reliability, and cueing characteristics. A validation study (N=44) examined detection performance across three conditions (manual control, 75% AI reliability, 95% AI reliability) and two levels of complexity. Results confirmed that the instrument meets Gray’s criteria for methodological utility. The complexity manipulation yielded large effect sizes with significant interactions. The reliability manipulation replicated established compliance-reliance asymmetries and trust calibration patterns. An unexpected finding was equivalent accuracy between low and high AI reliability groups despite a 20%-point reliability difference. Signal-detection analysis revealed that participants compensated for AI errors when those errors were visually verifiable, suggesting error verifiability as a boundary condition for the reliability-performance relationship. Using the generator, researchers can systematically examine human-AI interaction in dynamic visual search while analyzing relevant measures.

Title: Deep Learning in Finance: Review, Implementation and Analysis
Abstract: Deep Learning (DL) has significantly transformed the financial sector by enabling more accurate predictions, trend forecasting, and risk assessment. This paper explores an in-depth review of the diverse applications of DL across key financial domains, including market prediction, portfolio optimization, credit scoring, macroeconomic forecasting, risk management, and exchange rate estimation. The analysis categorizes financial use cases based on the underlying DL models employed, distinguishing DL from traditional Machine Learning (ML) approaches that often suffer from limitations in handling complex, non-linear financial data. By addressing these shortcomings, DL offers superior performance and greater adaptability in dynamic market environments. In addition to theoretical insights, this paper presents the implementation and quantitative analysis of DL-driven predictions for various financial instruments such as future gold price, Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) price, bitcoin price, and US$ (USD) price which highlights how economic factors influence these outcomes. The comprehensive review along with prediction and analysis of these financial instruments aims to provide researchers and practitioners with a structured understanding of Deep Learning’s capabilities and evolving role in modern finance.

Title: RICA: A Reconfigurable In-Sensor Computing Architecture with Parallel Weight Distribution for Versatile Edge Vision
Abstract: The conventional von Neumann architecture, which separates image sensing and processing, creates a data transfer bottleneck that limits the performance and energy efficiency of intelligent vision systems at the edge. While in-sensor computing (ISC) has emerged as a promising solution to mitigate this issue, existing designs often sacrifice architectural flexibility for efficiency, making them ill-suited for the diverse and evolving kernel sizes required by convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and patch embedding layer of vision transformers (ViTs). Moreover, many reconfigurable architectures rely on slow, serial weight-loading mechanisms that introduce a critical latency overhead. To address these limitations, this paper presents a reconfigurable ISC architecture (RICA) with a parallel weight distribution and readout system, comprising: (i) a scalable, reconfigurable crossbar unit (RCU) array, (ii) a reconfigurable weight distribution (RWD) scheme for parallel multi-scale kernel loading, (iii) a coordinated kernel shifting (CKS) mechanism for seamless inter-RCU convolution, and (iv) a dynamic column-coupling module (DCCM)-based power-aware readout path. The proposed architecture is evaluated through post-layout simulations in a 0.18 μm CMOS process. The results indicate a projected frame rate of up to 3840 fps for a 128×128 resolution, with an energy efficiency of 3.10 TOPS/W and up to 4.77 TOPS/W at 4K resolution. Compared with the reference design, the proposed architecture provides an estimated frame rate improvement of 33% for large kernels (e.g., 11×11, s=4), while reducing power consumption by 18-32% across configurations. By combining broad reconfigurability with high efficiency, RICA provides a versatile platform for next-generation edge AI vision systems.
