Title: ERP users intention to use artificial intelligence and automation instruments in Romanian businesses
Abstract: This article proposes an original analysis of the perception of users of integrated enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems regarding the adoption and use of Artificial Intelligence systems and automation tools. Building on previous results from established theories such as Unified Theory Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTUAT), Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), the study addresses a particularly research question: why do some companies benefit from process robots, predictive analytics and intelligent automation, while others fail to capitalize on their investment? Based on 388 valid responses to a questionnaire from the users of an ERP system which is used by more than 40,000 companies, the methodology used in this research employs the PLS-SEM structural equation model. The results are interesting in the specific context of the adoption of AI and automation tools within the ERP systems, highlighting the significant influencing factors: performance expectancy, effort expectancy, social influence and job relevance. Perceived trust has an influence only in the case of the adoption of automation tools, while the moderation analysis highlighted the robustness of the model across the entire population. Based on the results obtained, theoretical and practical implications are presented, as well as future directions.

Title: A Blockchain-Enabled Digital Twin Framework for Sustainable Portfolio Optimization
Abstract: Investments in green are gaining importance in terms of matching the finance-led growth with environmental sustainability. Nevertheless, the existing green financial instruments are not capable of being transparent, real-time checked, and auto-compliant and are therefore founded on inefficiencies and decreased investor trust. A new system that will implement a combination of Digital Twin technology and Blockchain to develop better green portfolio administration. Digital Twins offer live tracking of asset performance, like its carbon offsets and efficiency, whereas Blockchain offers nondestructive verification, and compliance with smart contracts is enabled. With a multi-source collection of power systems, green bonds, and environmental indexes, the proposed system achieved an accuracy of 93.8% portfolio returns, 91.2% carbon offset verification, and 96.1% environmental compliance score. Also, the latency of smart contracts was lowered to 94 ms, and AI-based rebalancing led to a 14.3% lift in risk-adjusted returns. The combined strategy can increase data traceability, smart decision-making, and create a solid foundation of sustainable financial ecosystems by connecting environmental performance with financial responsibility.

Title: Real-Time Guitar Chord Recognition via FPGA-accelerated Wavelet Analysis
Abstract: This paper presents a hardware-accelerated implementation for real-time Automatic Chord Recognition (ACR) of guitar audio based on wavelet analysis. To address the inherent time-frequency resolution trade-offs of Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) based spectral analysis, a custom high-resolution wavelet convolution pipeline on Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) logic was implemented. This architecture utilizes Morlet wavelets with bins centered around musical notes across multiple octaves, allowing for the direct extraction of chromatic features from guitar audio. To acquire a sparse time-frequency representation, a Synchrosqueezing Transform (SST) is applied in real-time. The second half of this work evaluates the performance of various classification methods applied to the resulting features. Several approaches are compared, ranging from simple template-matching to more sophisticated machine learning models to identify the optimal balance between recognition accuracy and computational efficiency for live guitar performance.

Title: PsyScale: A Collaborative Human-AI Framework for Theory-Driven PsychQuestionnaire Design
Abstract: Designing valid psychological questionnaires requires deep domain expertise and substantial resources, yet shortages in qualified psychometricians create bottlenecks when practitioners need instruments for emerging phenomena or diverse populations. While Large Language Models (LLMs) offer potential support, unconstrained generation often lacks psychometric rigor. This paper introduces PsyScale, a collaborative Human-AI framework that addresses the cold start problem by generating high-quality initial drafts for expert refinement. The framework employs theory-driven sub-attribute decomposition as a coordination mechanism, enabling domain experts to define construct structure while LLMs generate item content within those constraints. We validated PsyScale on 857 anonymized counseling transcripts with ground-truth scores for OCEAN personality traits, anxiety, and depression. Results demonstrate that decomposition significantly enhances convergent validity compared to unstructured generation. While performance on dynamic clinical states remains modest, PsyScale provides a scalable methodology for interdisciplinary teams to accelerate instrument development through structured Human-AI collaboration.

Title: Line Spectrum Feature-Guided Deep Convolutional Network for Low-SNR Underwater DOA Estimation
Abstract: Direction of Arrival (DOA) estimation is a crucial task in underwater target detection. However, both data-driven and model-driven algorithms can be regarded as threshold detection based on the signal energy in the direction of the wave vector. In complex underwater environments characterized by low Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) and limited snapshots, performance significantly degrades. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a line spectrum feature-guided deep convolutional network (LSF-CNN). Unlike traditional deep learning methods that directly input the covariance matrix, our approach utilizes the radiated noise generated by naval ships during forward movement for target recognition, which exhibits certain frequency domain characteristics. Specifically, we design a feature extraction module to identify the main line spectrum components from the Power Spectral Density (PSD) and construct a Line Spectrum Enhanced Covariance Matrix (LSE-CM). This matrix serves as a robust input feature map for a multi-layer Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), which learns spatial features while suppressing broadband noise. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed LSF-CNN achieves superior estimation accuracy compared to the classic MUSIC algorithm and standard CNNs, particularly under severe noise conditions (e.g., SNR below -10 dB), showing great potential for robust underwater target localization.

Title: An AI-Based Tool for Training Facial Emotion Recognition and Production in Patients with Schizophrenia: Development and Preliminary Results
Abstract: Schizophrenia is a psychiatric disorder characterized by cognitive and social impairments, including difficulties in recognizing and expressing facial emotions. Considering the critical role of social cognition in the functioning and quality of life of individuals with schizophrenia, a web-based computational tool grounded in artificial intelligence and affective computing techniques was developed and preliminarily evaluated to train the recognition and production of facial emotional expressions. The system integrates automated facial expression analysis to provide objective performance scores, supporting structured emotional skills training. The instrument was developed following usability principles suitable for the target audience and employs images and audio stimuli to promote engagement. It was evaluated with four patients receiving specialized outpatient care using structured tests. Additionally, specialist clinicians conducted an independent assessment. The results indicated higher accuracy in recognizing positive emotions and provided preliminary feasibility indications of the tool as a complementary resource for AI-assisted social cognition training. Qualitative analysis provided indications of favourable user acceptance and preliminary expert validation. Despite the limited number of participants, the findings provide preliminary exploratory indications of the tool’s potential and support recommendations for refinement and broader evaluation in future studies. This study does not aim to demonstrate clinical efficacy, but rather to explore feasibility and interaction patterns in a pilot setting.

Title: Advancing Speech Emotion Recognition: A Comprehensive Evaluation on the TESS Dataset
Abstract: Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) is essential for emotion-sensitive human-computer interaction systems. This paper seeks to perform a systematic and structured assessment of classical machine learning models and deep neural architectures for speech emotion recognition on the TESS dataset. Imposes uniform data partitions, feature pipelines and training protocols to facilitate an equitable comparison. Conventional classifiers, including SVM, Decision Tree, and Random Forest, attain a peak accuracy of 75.08%. Conversely, deep learning models exhibit significantly enhanced performance, with CNN reaching 97.50% and LSTM achieving 98.75% test accuracy. A comprehensive analysis demonstrates that the LSTM outperforms CNN-based spectral modelling by more effectively capturing temporal dependencies in emotional speech. These results demonstrate the significance of temporal representation in SER and offer empirical evidence into model selection in evaluation settings that are reproducible and constrained.

Title: An Interpretable Multi-Modal Deep Learning Framework for Ischemic Stroke Risk Prediction
Abstract: Ischemic stroke is a killer and also a major cause of long-term disability in the world, and attempting to prevent it early and correctly is of essence in the provision of preventive care. Conventional risk assessment tools tend to use clinical scores and independent data about the patient, where the multi-faceted and interactive nature of the neuroimaging, clinical history, and demographic variables may be missed. In order to fill this gap, we present a multi-modal deep learning framework that can be interpreted to predict the individualized risk of ischemic stroke by combining heterogeneous patient data. Convolutional neural networks (ResNet18) are used to identify structural and lesion-related characteristics of brain images, and transformer-based models are used to identify the temporal trends and patterns of progression of longitudinal electronic health records. Fully connected networks are used to process structured clinical and demographic variables to produce meaningful embeddings. These multi-modal representations are subsequently combined together to create one unified predictive model that is used to produce individual stroke risk scores. Explainable AI methods to guarantee clinical trust can emphasize important brain areas and major clinicaldemographic characteristics that affect each prediction. Experimental testing indicates that the suggested methodology is better at predictive performance, which is more precise and understandable than the single-modality models. The framework provides a clinically relevant and data-driven instrument to help prevent early ischemic stroke by assessing that risk and making proactive decisions and individualized prevention choices.

Title: Spur Gear Fault Diagnosis Using Deep Learning with Wavelet Feature Attention and Spike Encoding
Abstract: This paper presents a diagnostic framework integrating Wavelet Spectral Feature Attention and Spike Encoding with convolutional neural network classification for spur gear fault diagnosis. The methodology is validated using the XJTU Spur Gearbox dataset acquired at 15 Hz and 20 Hz shaft rotational speeds across five fault severity levels. Wavelet Spectral Feature Attention emphasized fault-sensitive frequency regions through adaptive scale weighting, followed by neuromorphic spike encoding to preserve discriminative temporal patterns. Classification performance was evaluated under same-speed and cross-speed scenarios. Same-speed evaluation achieved high diagnostic accuracy, demonstrating strong fault discriminability when training and testing conditions matched. Cross-speed generalization maintained robust performance despite operational speed variation between training and testing phases. The methodology demonstrated effective fault identification across all severity levels with minimal generalization gaps indicating adaptability to operational changes. Feature representations from wavelet-based spectral enhancement and spike-based temporal encoding contributed to consistent and reliable fault classification under variable operating conditions.

Title: Spectral-Aware Graph Pre-training and Prompt Tuning Framework for Network Traffic Anomaly Detection
Abstract: With the evolution of network technologies, the scale of network traffic has grown exponentially, and at⁃ tack methods (such as protocol obfuscation and skipping connections) have become increasingly covert and complex, pos⁃ ing unprecedented challenges to traditional detection methods. Although graph neural networks (GNNs) have demonstrated potential in modeling traffic topological dependencies, they generally face two major bottlenecks in real-world network se⁃ curity scenarios: first, the significant structural heterophily in network traffic graphs, where anomalous traffic tends to estab⁃ lish atypical connections with normal nodes possessing vastly different features, causing GNNs based on homophily as⁃ sumptions to fail; second, the extreme scarcity of high-quality anomaly labels, where full-parameter fine-tuning easily induc⁃ es overfitting or the negative transfer of pre-trained knowledge. To this end, this paper proposes a spectral-aware graph pre-training and prompt tuning framework tailored for network traffic anomaly detection. Abandoning the reliance of traditional graph learning paradigms on homophilic structures and massive labeled data, the core innovations of this framework lie in: (1) Introducing complementary spectral filters to jointly model low-pass signals (capturing stable communication patterns) and high-pass signals (identifying abnormal connection perturbations) for the first time during the pre-training phase, accu⁃ rately characterizing the strong heterophilic nature of network traffic from a frequency domain perspective; (2) Designing a spectral-aware contrastive learning mechanism to extract robust frequency-invariant features by maximizing representation⁃ al consistency across cross-frequency views; (3) Proposing a parameter-efficient prompt tuning strategy that, while freezing backbone parameters, utilizes learnable prompt vectors to adaptively adjust the fusion weights of high- and low-frequency channels, achieving precise transfer to downstream few-shot tasks. Experiments on three real-world network security datas⁃ ets, including CICIDS2017, CICIDS2018, and HIKARI2021, demonstrate that the proposed method comprehensively out⁃ performs existing baseline models in detection performance under sample-scarce scenarios. With a maximum improvement exceeding 20%, these results verify the robustness and practicality of the proposed method in complex and heterophilic net⁃ work environments.

Title: LogKDR: A Knowledge-Distilled Retrieval-Augmented Framework for Interpretable Log Analysis
Abstract: As a vital instrument for recording system and device operational status, logs have been widely adopted across various information systems. Log anomaly detection and root cause analysis are crucial for ensuring the reliability and security of large-scale software systems. However, current deep learning-based approaches suffer from limited interpretability, while methods relying on pre-trained models face challenges such as high computational costs and privacy concerns. To address these limitations, we propose LogKDR, a Knowledge Distilled Retrieval-Augmented framework that integrates Multi-hop Retrieval(MHR), Knowledge Distillation(kD), and Self-adaptive Active Learning(SAAL) into a unified closed-loop system. The framework introduces three key innovations: MHR constructs hierarchical contextual evidence chains across heterogeneous sources, enabling fine-grained correlation from symptoms to root causes; KD transfers reasoning capabilities from a high-capacity teacher model to a lightweight student model for efficient on-device inference; and SAAL ensures continuous model evolution under concept drift through uncertainty-driven pseudo-labeling and incremental updates. Experiments on three benchmark datasets - HDFS, BGL, and Thunderbird - demonstrate that LogKDR achieves an average improvement of 18.12% in F1-score over large models while significantly enhancing interpretability metrics(ROUGE and BLEU), attaining state-of-the-art performance. Ablation studies confirm that each component critically contributes to the framework's robustness, efficiency, and explainability in dynamic log environments.

Title: Machine Learning in Cardiovascular Disease Prediction: Current Methods and Future Directions
Abstract: As the primary cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) demand precise and expandable risk prediction models. Conventional clinical risk assessment instruments like the European SCORE model and the Framingham Risk Score depend on predetermined statistical relationships and a small number of clinical variables which frequently leads to a decreased capacity for cross-population prediction. The use of large-scale multi-modal datasets such as clinical records genetic information imaging data and biomarkers for better cardiovascular risk stratification has shown great promise in recent years thanks to machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) techniques. 22 peer-reviewed studies that were published between 2018 and 2025 are systematically examined in this review. Using databases like PubMed IEEE Xplore and Google Scholar a systematic literature search was carried out utilizing keywords like deep learning machine learning cardiovascular disease prediction and multi-modal data. Studies were accepted if they reported quantitative performance metrics and used ML/DL techniques to predict CVD. In order to facilitate safe and scalable clinical deployment future research should give special attention to standardized benchmarking explainable AI techniques ensemble learning strategies and adherence to local healthcare laws.

Title: Artificial intelligence in public procurement: Admissibility of AI-based tenders and compliance obligations for contracting authorities in light of recent administrative case law
Abstract: This article moves from two recent administrative rulings – TAR Lazio-Roma n. 4546/2025 and Consiglio di Stato n. 8092/2025 – which, for the first time explicitly, address the use of artificial intelligence systems by an economic operator in the performance of a public contract. The analysis seeks to answer three questions: whether, and under what conditions, a tender incorporating AI-based solutions is admissible in a public procurement procedure; what compliance obligations apply to the contracting authority at the offer evaluation and contract execution stages; and whether the existing regulatory framework is sufficient or whether specific legislative intervention is required. The two rulings affirm the full compatibility of AI with the principles set out in Legislative Decree n. 36/2023, provided that its use is consistent with the objectives of the procedure and positively assessed by the evaluation committee in the exercise of its technical discretion. The provisions of the Public Contracts Code, the AI Act and the GDPR, together with existing soft law instruments, provide, in the authors’ view, an adequate regulatory framework, rendering specific legislative intervention unnecessary.

Title: Application of AI-Driven and Computer System-Supported Personalized Music Learning Models in Higher Education Arts Education
Abstract: Integration of AI and computer systems in such a profound manner has pushed the art education to intelligent level in the sphere of higher education. In order to make the process of students learning music more personalized and efficient, this paper develops a personalized model of learning music that is powered by AI and assisted by computer systems. It is a model that predicts the data in students of their pitch, rhythm, and performance emotion according to the deep learning algorithms and dynamically modulates the learning path according to a learning behavior feature extraction module. The research process involves four phases (1) to create a student music learning dataset, which covers performance records and learning logs of 500 music majors; (2) to create a model of music performance evaluation using a convolutional neural network (CNN) to make individual differences; (3) to develop an adaptive learning recommendation system so as to optimize the learning content by using a reinforcement learning process; and (4) to compare the model with a manual teaching process in the experimental phase to confirm its teaching effect. The results show that the experimental group students’ scores in the music performance skills assessment increase to 94.1; learning efficiency increases to 44.3; the system recommendation accuracy reaches 91.4%. The study shows that this model can significantly improve learners’ self-learning ability and music performance level, providing a sustainable and intelligent development path for higher education art education.

Title: Addressing Dataset Imbalance in Multi-Label Image Classification Through CLIP-Guided Synthetic Image Generation
Abstract: Multi-label image classification is often a considered as a very challenging task. This challenge significantly increases when the image datasets suffer from class imbalance or limitation of labeled samples resulting with "minority classes". The lack of representation for minority classes causes biased learning and poor generalization. This paper focuses on creating a deep learning model that can identify multiple object categories from a single image. It deals with the challenge of overlapping and coexisting features within the same frame. The paper also proposes a hybrid approach where text-to-image generative models, like Stable Diffusion, produce synthetic samples for underrepresented classes. A CLIP-based semantic alignment score filters the generated images, making sure that only semantically accurate synthetic samples are included in training. The framework was tested on a multi-label dataset with ten classes that included vehicles and musical instruments. The experiments show that adding CLIP-validated synthetic images improved the micro-F1 score from 0.38 to 0.96. This improvement addresses the weaknesses related to imbalance in the baseline ResNet classifier. The results confirm that diffusion-generated augmentation significantly boosts performance for minority classes while maintaining semantic consistency.

Title: TechTheraphy: A Mental Health Support System

Title: A Unified Multimodal Intelligence Framework for Real-Time Adaptive Human State Understanding in Conversational Interfaces
Abstract: The analysis of human emotions is essential in establishing an AI system that will deal with human beings in an empathic and adaptive way. This paper describes a multimodal human state recognition system with a conversational agent that examines facial, audio and textual signals. On facial emotion recognition, EVA-Giant is better than ViT-H/14, FaceViT+, and Swin Transformer because of massive pretraining and robust visual representations. Whisper v3 Large performs significantly better than WavLM-Large, SpeechT5-Large and Wav2Vec2.0 in audio analysis, including emotion-specific acoustic variations and noisy to handle, as well as in speech analysis, where it makes sound predictions even solely on single-sample input. GPT-4 embeddings outperform RoBERTA-Large, t5-Large and DeBERTA in emotion understanding of texts, and provide rich semantic encoding. Methods of multimodal fusion were investigated, among which the Gated Multimodal Unit (GMU) was a dynamically weighting multimodality with high performance in multimodal fusion and robustness in the cases of missing data. Combining with a DialoGPT conversations interface, the system is more proficient in the quality of dialogue, empathy and understanding the context. This piece of work offers a feasible standard and perspective to create robust emotionally intelligent AI frameworks that can be used in mental health aid, adaptive learning, and human phenomenon interactions.

Title: Transforming Public Management in Morocco Through AI and Behavioral Economics: Innovations in Decision-Making and Administrative Efficiency
Abstract: In a time of digital transition and increasing citizen demands, Morocco is looking to update how it functions in order to face today’s issues. The article discusses opportunities to use artificial intelligence (AI) and behavioral economics to improve administrative performance, accountability, and citizen confidence. Automation and predictive analytics from AI can support a form of more agile governance, while behavioral economics allows for the design of policies that better reflect actual citizen behavior. The paper unites theoretical study with application-orientation in Moroccan institutions, showing how these instruments are used to improve resource allocation, to save processing time and to enforce policies adequately. The study is of a mixed-method nature (questionnaires and interviews) and will involve 100 participants from various sectors (public administration, AI experts, behavioral practitioners, and citizens). Results show that AI considerably enhances administrative efficiency (reducing delays and costs) whereas behaviorally, interventions raise citizen compliance and satisfaction. A combination of both approaches builds institutional confidence (37% more than using either approach alone). By contrast, the habitude and regional (urban versus rural) differences (those /bugs/ in closets haunt) make this impact limited. Notably, future directions in this regard include a people-centered digital transformation, context-specific implementation and upskilling of public sector workers. Limitations A small number of frontline managers were included in the study and a lack of time to evaluate long-term changes at the organizational level. Despite these limitations, Morocco has the potential to be a public modernization model – if the country incorporates AI and behavioral science, ensures a transition that is inclusive, and implements transparent governance.

Title: Deployment Readiness Assessment of Large Language Models in Power Distribution Systems: A Risk-Aware Framework
Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly being proposed for a wide range of power distribution system tasks, from fault diagnosis and state estimation to dispatch optimization and energy management coordination. However, deployment decisions in existing research are predominantly evaluated through task-performance metrics alone, overlooking the operational risks that arise when probabilistic generative systems interact with safety-critical physical infrastructure. This paper proposes the LLM Deployment Readiness Assessment (LDRA) framework, an analytical instrument that evaluates any LLM-integrated power system use case along four axes: Task Determinism Requirement (TDR), Hallucination Criticality Index (HCI), Adversarial Exposure Surface (AES), and Human-in-the-Loop Feasibility (HILF). A weighted Composite Readiness Score (CRS) maps each use case into one of three deployment zones (GREEN, AMBER, or RED), enabling structured go/nogo decisions independent of performance benchmarks. We apply LDRA to twelve representative use cases drawn from recent literature and demonstrate that four widely-studied deployments fall in the RED zone despite strong benchmark results or active research presence, revealing a systematic gap between reported performance and operational readiness. The framework provides power system engineers and AI practitioners with a shared vocabulary and a reusable analytical methodology for risk-aware LLM integration.

Title: Machine Learning Benchmarking for Industrial Power Quality Anomaly Detection: Performance, Cost, and the Limits of Class Imbalance Mitigation
Abstract: Industrial power systems are vulnerable to power quality (PQ) anomalies such as voltage sags, swells, transients, and harmonic distortions, whose detection is complicated by extreme class imbalance. This study benchmarks 13 machine learning (ML) approaches on approximately 4.5 million onesecond measurements containing 577 instrument-confirmed anomalies (0.013% prevalence, 7,851:1 imbalance ratio), recorded by a power analyser at our industrial partner's client industrial facility. The evaluated approaches include tree-based ensembles, a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network, the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) for class balancing, and novel hybrid two-stage pipelines. Stacking Ensemble and BalancedRandomForest (BRF) achieve statistically equivalent Receiver Operating Characteristic Area Under the Curve (ROC AUC) scores, while Weighted Ensemble leads on F2. Cost-based evaluation reveals a paradox: models with the highest recall incur the highest operational costs due to the volume of false alarms. Five principal findings emerge. First, metric selection determines the winning model. Second, traditional ML with class balancing matches or exceeds deep learning under extreme imbalance. Third, SMOTE is harmful at this level of imbalance. Fourth, unsupervised pre-filtering adds complexity without improving detection. Fifth, domaininformed features contribute more than algorithmic sophistication. Results are derived from a single facility and should be interpreted as a reference for comparable imbalance regimes.

Title: On the Quantization-Aware Training for Digital Semantic Speech Communications
Abstract: Semantic speech communication has recently emerged as a promising paradigm for bandwidth-efficient wireless transmission by prioritizing the semantic information. However, bridging neural semantic representations with practical digital transceivers remains an open challenge, as most existing approaches operate on continuous latent features incompatible with discrete modulation schemes. This work introduces a quantization-aware digital semantic speech communication approach that bridges neural semantic representation learning with digital signal processing pipelines. The proposed architecture integrates a neural semantic encoder-decoder with latent feature quantization, channel coding and digital modulator for transmission over wireless channels. During training, quantization-aware perturbations are incorporated to emulate discretization effects and improve robustness to digital implementation constraints. System performance is evaluated under Rayleigh and Rician fading channels across signal-to-noise ratios (SNR) ranging from 0 to 20 dB using perceptual speech quality and intelligibility metrics. Experimental results demonstrate consistent improvements in perceptual quality and intelligibility compared with non-quantization-aware semantic baselines, particularly in low-to-moderate SNR regimes. Moreover, the proposed model exhibits stable performance across multiple quantization depths, indicating that quantization-aware training (QAT) enables robust and flexible deployment of semantic communication systems in practical digital wireless environments.

Title: Performance Analysis of Speckle Filters on Sentinel-1 GRD Data for LULC Applications
Abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery is inherently affected by speckle noise. This study systematically examines the statistical foundations of five speckle filters namely Boxcar, Median, Frost, Lee, and Refined Lee and evaluates their performance for Land Use/Land Cover (LULC) classification. Sentinel-1 Ground Range Detected (GRD) data in C-band frequency (5.36 GHz) was instrument in the present study. The results indicate that imagery processed with the Refined Lee filter achieved the highest LULC classification accuracies for the SVM (OA=70%, Kappa=0.58), RF(OA=79%, Kappa=0.73), and DT (OA=83%, Kappa=0.79) classifiers. This superior performance is attributed to its enhanced edge-preserving capability, resulting from adaptive smoothing regulated by directional gradient analysis. Such edge preservation substantially reduces commission and omission errors among LULC classes. The Median filter recorded the second-highest ROC statistics across the machine learning classifiers. The research findings demonstrate that filter effectiveness is application-specific, with the Refined Lee and Median filters emerging as optimal choices for complex LULC classification tasks.

Title: Deep Learning Approaches for Multi-City Urban AQI Level Classification Using Multivariate Time-Series Data: A Comparative Study
Abstract: Accurately assessing the quality of air in urban areas is one of the key tasks to be performed as a mitigation action for environmental and public health risks deriving from atmospheric pollution. This work investigates recent approaches using deep learning for time-series classification in multi-city Air Quality Index classification based on heterogeneous data sets of urban pollution. Six pollutant concentration measurements, such as PM2.5, PM10, NO<inf>2</inf>, SO<inf>2</inf>, CO, and O<inf>3</inf>, which were collected from multiple metropolitan cities, will be combined into a single dataset and then standardized into AQI categories. In this paper, several deep learning architectures, such as CNN, RNN, LSTM, Bidirectional LSTM, and GRU, are developed and evaluated under identical conditions of pre-processing and training to model temporal dependencies and nonlinearities of air quality dynamics. Normalization of features is used to deal with variations in scale, whereas the weighted cross-entropy loss was applied to solve class imbalance problems. Accuracy and weighted F1-score are used as metrics to assess quantitative performance. The comparative analysis has shown that the recurrent and gated architectures have performed much better with respect to conventional models since those models captured sequential pollutant patterns. The proposed framework establishes a scalable and reproducible deep learning pipeline for urban AQI classification, offering valuable insights for intelligent environmental monitoring systems and data-driven smart city applications.

Title: HumToMusic: Generating Full Music from Human Humming Using AI
Abstract: In modern times, creating music has become relatively easy owing to rapid advancements in AI technology. However, there remains an outstanding challenge in converting human hums into high-quality and fully structured music. Human hums have low precision, noisy breaths, unstable rhythms, and large gaps between solo vocals and full instrumental ensemble sounds. In this paper, we propose a novel end-to-end AI model for addressing this issue. The first step involves using a CNN to detect pitch with high accuracy. Secondly, we incorporate a Large Language Model (MIDI-LLM) to compose the backing instrumentals. Finally, we apply flow-matching diffusion models along with Audio ControlNet to generate audio, preserving human emotions. The output audio is generated using BigVGAN v2 vocoder, resulting in ultra-high-quality 44.1 kHz stereo sound. Our proposed approach outperforms all previous baseline systems in terms of both speed and audio quality.

Title: Grooming Detection Using a Multimodal AI Approach for Slovak Language Environments
Abstract: This work presents an intelligent multimodal detection system for identifying online grooming in the Slovak language setting. Online grooming poses a substantial threat to minors in digital spaces. However, existing online grooming detection solutions are restricted to only English texts and have no ability to analyze voice messages. Thus, the proposed system incorporates three independent modules. They include the following: (1) a CNN-LSTM based model designed to detect synthetic voices from mel-spectrograms, (2) Whisper medium from OpenAI used for ASR, which is also multilingual, and (3) a fine-tuned XLM-RoBERTa (base) text classifier for detecting grooming online. Moreover, multimodal fusion proved to be robust by demonstrating compensatory performance in the case of failure in specific modalities. Due to its modularity, scalability, GDPR-compatibility, and cross-linguistic nature, the presented system can serve as a basis for the development of automated online protection systems aimed at safeguarding children in other low-resource European languages aside from Slovak.

Title: Al-Driven Knowledge Management System for Skill-Psychology Personalized Violin Teaching
Abstract: Traditional violin teaching is plagued by homogenization, poor adaptation to individual differences, and the inability to quantify implicit musical psychological variables. This study constructs an AI-driven “skill-psychology” dual-dimensional personalized violin teaching strategy, reconstructing three quantifiable musical psychological dimensions, and building a two-dimensional adaptive matching model and a closed-loop teaching path. A 12-week controlled experiment on 120 violin learners aged 10-18 shows the AI group achieves far higher improvement in basic and advanced skills than the traditional group, with significantly reduced performance anxiety and notably elevated learning motivation and self-efficacy. Intermediate learners report the highest satisfaction with the AI strategy, which realizes the synergy of skill training and psychological regulation and offers a feasible intelligent solution for personalized violin education.

Title: From Full-Range Spectroscopy to Rgb Indices: A Decisionoriented Evaluation of Feature Compression for Sediment Organic Matter Prediction
Abstract: Accurate estimation of sediment organic matter (OM) is essential for understanding biogeochemical processes, yet conventional laboratory methods are time-consuming and difficult to scale. Reflectance spectroscopy combined with machine learning provides a rapid alternative, but full-range spectroscopic instruments are costly and operationally complex. This study assessed whether full-range spectroscopy offers a meaningful predictive advantage over compact color-based and RGB-derived features for sediment OM estimation. Using 350 dried sediment samples from Netley Lake (Manitoba, Canada), Support Vector Regression models were developed using raw and preprocessed fullspectrum reflectance (360-2500 nm), a collective set of 15 color coefficients, and simplified RGB-based indices. Results show that spectral preprocessing yields inconsistent gains, while color coefficients and RGB indices achieve comparable or superior test performance with improved stability. These findings indicate that sediment OM signals are effectively captured by low-dimensional color features, supporting lowcost RGB-based sensing for routine monitoring.

Title: A Data-Driven Acoustic Parameter Extraction Framework for Stylistic AI Anchor Synthesis
Abstract: Although neural Text-to-Speech (TTS) technologies have reached the intelligibility benchmark, they generally have "prosodic smoothing"problems and are unable to express rich genre-driven temporal and spectral information for multi-genre professional broadcast applications. This paper introduces a quantitative feature engineering approach to deterministic acoustic priors. Through the construction of a multi-speaker expert corpus and digital signal processing, we separated the acoustic stylistic shifts driven by genre factors from the physiological characteristics of each speaker. Through statistical comparison, we identified strong norms across speakers: the speech tempo must be elongated (slowed down) and the baseline pitch predominantly elevated for political news reporting to reflect architectural solemnity, though localized individual variations in pitch inflection may exist, while the intensity must be increased (by 0.7 ~ 3.3 dB) and the speech rate needs to be accelerated (by approximately 23.7% on average) for livelihood news reporting. The Z-score method is adopted to convert absolute acoustic shifts into input condition vectors. The derived parameters yield explicit engineering constraints for tuning the variance adaptors (pitch, energy and duration predictors) in the current-generation neural TTS architecture, thus reducing the averaging effect and improving the stylistic performance of AI virtual anchors.

Title: EEG-Conditioned Emotional Speech Synthesis with Grad-TTS
Abstract: Existing emotional speech synthesis methods mainly rely on discrete emotion labels, reference speech, or speech-derived emotional cues for emotional control. Although effective, these conditioning forms still exhibit limitations in continuity, objectivity, and fine-grained emotional modeling. To complement existing emotional control strategies, this paper proposes an EEG-conditioned emotional speech synthesis framework based on Grad-TTS. Raw EEG signals are processed by an EEG emotion encoder to obtain continuous emotional embeddings, which are introduced into the speech generation process as additional conditional information. An emotion consistency constraint and a multi-task learning strategy are further incorporated to improve emotional expressiveness and generation stability. Experimental results show that EEG emotional information can be effectively integrated into diffusion-based speech synthesis. Compared with directly using raw EEG signals, structured EEG emotional representations achieve better objective and subjective performance. These results demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of EEG as a supplementary physiological condition for emotional speech synthesis.

Title: Sentinel-Math: A Framework for Neural Intent Monitoring and SafetyCircuit-Breaking Against Semantically Disguised Logical Tasks in LLMs
Abstract: As Large Language Models (LLMs) advance in complex reasoning, they increasingly exhibit "Strategic Dishonesty"against high-order attacks that wrap harmful semantics within mathematical logic. Consequently, traditional black-box filters easily fall into "Safety Hallucinations"or trigger the "Calculator Paradox"by honestly outputting dangerous parameters. To address this, we propose Sentinel-Math, a decoupled intent auditing and safety circuit-breaking framework. Pioneering a neuro-symbolic hybrid mechanism, it utilizes a Risk Sentinel for dynamic dispatching, an external symbolic engine to anchor objective logical truth, and an internal state probe (via Mechanistic Interpretability) to quantify subjective deceptive intents. Our core innovation is a 3D Orthogonal Decision Space X<inf>1</inf>, X<inf>2</inf>, X<inf>3</inf>that completely decouples contextual harmfulness, subjective deceptiveness, and objective incorrectness. This eliminates the Calculator Paradox while enabling fine-grained motive diagnosis. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that Sentinel-Math suppresses Jailbreak Success Rates on high-order benchmarks (e.g., EvilMath) below 5.0%, achieves absolute interception against explicit malicious requests, and preserves native mathematical reasoning capabilities (performance drop<0.5%), offering a paradigm for externally guided yet behaviorally endogenous honest AI.

Title: Cross-platform evaluation of LLM-generated educational texts on cardiac myxoma: quality, readability, and actionability using network analysis and latent profile analysis
Abstract: Background – Patients with cardiac myxoma require long-term follow-up, and the quality of patient education as well as the ability to recognize early symptoms may influence integrated postoperative cardiovascular and tumor-related management. Although large language models (LLMs) have been increasingly applied in medical education, cross-platform empirical evidence in this intersecting context remains limited. This study evaluated the performance and limitations of widely used LLMs in generating patient education texts for cardiac myxoma using a standardized, expert-curated educational question set. Methods – We constructed a standardized dataset of 60 expert-curated educational questions spanning the disease course of cardiac myxoma and used nine widely used LLMs to generate 540 patient education texts. Text quality, readability, and actionability were assessed using the Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool for Printable Materials (PEMAT-P), Ensuring Quality Information for Patients (EQIP-36), the Global Quality Score (GQS), and seven readability formulas. In addition, a regularized Gaussian graphical model-based partial correlation network analysis and latent profile analysis were performed to identify relationships among evaluation metrics and cross-platform text phenotypes. Results – Texts generated across platforms showed significant heterogeneity in information quality, understandability, and objective readability, whereas clinical actionability was generally low. Word count showed the strongest positive correlation with the total EQIP-36 score and occupied a central position in the network. Reading-difficulty indices were consistently negatively correlated with PEMAT-P actionability. Latent profile analysis identified three text phenotypes: moderate-quality/low-readability, high-quality/high-actionability, and low-quality/easy-to-read. Ideally suited patient education texts accounted for only a very small proportion of all outputs. Conclusions – Within this expert-curated educational question set, the current application of LLMs in patient education for cardiac myxoma is primarily limited by reading burden and insufficient behavioral guidance. Although longer outputs were generally associated with higher informational quality scores, greater syntactic complexity was associated with lower actionability of the materials. In addition, latent profile analysis suggested that only a small subset of outputs approached a more favorable quality–actionability profile.

Title: A Multi-Sensor Dataset for 3D Human Pose Estimation Using Imaging Radar
Abstract: This work focuses on 3D Human Pose Estimation (HPE) using imaging radar. We introduce DualRadarHPE, a new multi-sensor dataset containing calibrated and temporally aligned data from two widely adopted radar sensors - Texas Instruments (TI) and Bosch. The dataset includes three radar data representations from TI: raw ADC data, heatmap, and point-cloud; and point clouds from Bosch. The data was captured in both indoor and outdoor scenarios. These scenarios were designed to reflect challenges of real-world applications, such as presence of large metallic objects that can increase radar sensor noise, sensor motion, and multiple people in the scene. We overview state-of-the-art open-access datasets and benchmarks for radar-based 3D HPE and evaluate two popular point-cloud-based methods and the most recent heatmap-based method. We introduce necessary algorithmic adaptations to improve their performance. Finally, we propose a new RadarViT method that is more light-weight and outperforms the existing methods with respect to the mean per joint position error. We tested this model in outdoor conditions with and without re-training, in the presence of multiple persons, and under dynamic conditions. The dataset and the code will be made publicly available.

Title: Listening Through Temporal Windows: Multi-Scale Hierarchical Attention for Early Alzheimer Detection
Abstract: Speech is often seen as a useful source of information for studying Alzheimer's disease, but using it for early detection is still a challenge. One reason is that speech changes linked to cognitive decline do not occur at a single time scale. Some effects appear briefly, while others emerge only over longer stretches of speech. In this work, we study whether analyzing speech at multiple temporal resolutions can help address this issue. We propose a multi-scale temporal attention network that combines three pre-trained speech models, Whisper, WavLM, and TRILLSON, operating on 30 -second, 20 -second, and 1 second windows. Each time scale is processed separately using an attention mechanism that emphasizes segments carrying stronger diagnostic signals. The representations obtained at each scale are combined at a later stage to produce the final decision. To handle variable-length recordings, we apply adaptive segmentation with overlapping windows. On the ADReSSo Challenge blind test set, the system achieves an accuracy of 81.69%. This result is higher than what we observed with single-scale models and exceeds previously reported performance on the same task. When examining the feature space, we see that short-term acoustic information and longer-term speech patterns contribute in different ways. Together, they improve class separation, which supports the use of multi-resolution speech analysis for noninvasive Alzheimer's screening.

Title: Mapping personal recovery in schizophrenia spectrum disorders: an exploratory machine learning study of self-reported stage classifications
Abstract: Recovery in schizophrenia is a complex and multidimensional process involving functional, clinical, and psychological dimensions. This study aims to use machine learning (ML) to explore multivariate associations with classifications of personal recovery assessed with the Stages of Recovery Instrument (STORI). We analyzed cross-sectional data from 1, 361 individuals with schizophrenia-spectrum disorders enrolled in the French REHABase cohort, a national psychosocial rehabilitation network. Random forest models were developed using internal cross-validation on a training set and subsequently evaluated on an independent test set (70/30 split). Model performance was high in the training data (AUC = 0.997; accuracy = 94.3%) and more modest in the test set (AUC = 0.724; accuracy = 49.8%). SHAP analyses (explainable ML) were used to describe stage-associated recovery profiles based on multivariate patterns across sociodemographic, clinical, and psychological variables. Overall, the modest performance observed in the independent test set underscores the complexity of personal recovery and is consistent with partial conceptual overlap across STORI stage classifications. The Moratorium stage was characterized by higher negative self-esteem and internalized stigma, alongside lower wellbeing and positive self-esteem. Awareness was associated with mental wellbeing and negative self-esteem, with additional contributions from positive self-esteem and relational satisfaction. The Preparation stage showed less distinct profiles, with autonomy emerging as a relevant feature. Rebuilding was associated with intermediate-to-high levels of wellbeing and resilience. The Growth stage was characterized by high wellbeing, positive self-esteem, and relational satisfaction. These findings provide an integrated description of stage-associated recovery profiles and illustrate how explainable ML can be used to explore the multidimensional organization of personal recovery.

Title: Statistical Feature Selection over Self-Supervised Speech Representations for Autism Detection
Abstract: Recent advances in self-supervised learning (SSL) enable rich, high-dimensional speech representations useful for Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) detection, but their direct use is challenging when clinical data are scarce. We apply a multi-criteria statistical feature-selection framework to fused SSL embeddings: utterance-level HuBERT, Wav2Vec 2.0 and WavLM vectors are concatenated, pruned to the most informative dimensions, and evaluated under a subject-independent protocol with several classifiers - Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), Random Forest (RF), Gradient Boosting (GB), and k-Nearest Neighbors (KNN). The pipeline reduces dimensionality and improves performance; the best configuration reaches an accuracy of 91.67%. WavLM and HuBERT supply most of the discriminative signal and complement each other when combined.

Title: Prediction of biomass pyrolysis product yield based on machine learning algorithms
Abstract: To achieve targeted regulation of biomass pyrolysis products, a yield prediction and process optimization model based on machine learning was constructed. A dataset containing 578 valid samples was established by integrating literature and experimental data, and data preprocessing and feature selection were performed using boxplot and clustering algorithms. On this basis, Bayesian optimization was applied to tune four base learners, including Random Forest and Gradient Boosting Decision Tree models, and a high-accuracy yield prediction meta-model was constructed through a stacking ensemble strategy. The results showed that the coefficients of determination (R<inf>2</inf>) for biochar, tar, and pyrolysis gas yields reached 0.92, 0.90, and 0.94, respectively. Feature importance analysis using SHAP and GINI indicated that biochar yield was mainly influenced by pyrolysis temperature and carbon content, tar yield was primarily affected by lignin and hemicellulose contents, and gas yield was dominated by hemicellulose content and pyrolysis temperature. Furthermore, partial dependence plot (PDP) analysis revealed the optimal operating regions for product formation: low temperature and slow heating (500°C, HR < 20°C / min) favored biochar production, moderate temperature and short residence time (600°C, 40min < RT < 50min) promoted tar enrichment, while high temperature with moderate heating rate (>750°C, 15°C / min < HR < 25°C / min) maximized gas yield, providing an efficient predictive tool and theoretical basis for the intelligent control and industrial application of biomass pyrolysis.

Title: Deformable DETR for Automated Bone Fracture Detection in Pediatric Wrist X-rays: A Deep Learning Approach
Abstract: One of the most important clinical activities in emergency medicine and orthopedic care is the bone fracture detection. The current paper introduces a new solution based on Deformable Detection Transformer (Deformable DETR) to detect bone fractures and other anomalies on X-ray in pediatric wrist images automatically. We use the GrazPedWri-DX dataset which consists of 20,327 annotated X-ray images of pediatric wrists. Our system is a transformer-based architecture with deformable attention mechanisms that are effective in capturing multi-scale features of medical images. The system proposed identifies 9 types of anatomical abnormality such as bone fractures, bone anomalies, lesions and soft tissue anomalies. Extensive experiments show that our Deformable DETR model can be trained to have higher performance, with 94.2% average precision (AP) at IoU threshold 0.50, being better than the traditional CNN-based models (ResNet50 + SVM: 87.3% AP, EfficientNetB0 + XGBoost: 89.5% AP, VGG-16 + Random Forest: 85.8% AP). The model has strong generalization with 91.8% AP on the test set, and has clinical application with 0.48 seconds mean inference time per image. This article demonstrates the efficacy of transformer-based architectures in medical image analysis and offers a feasible instrument to help radiologists detect fractures.

Title: Alzheimer’s Prognosis from Neuroimaging Using Optimized Variational Mode Decomposition based on Brown Beer and Transfer Learning
Abstract: Purpose: Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) is a progressive, chronic disorder of the brain for which there is now no operative treatment. However, there are medications that can slow its growth. In order to stop and control the development of AD, earlier diagnosis of the disease is prototypical. Method: We propose a novel method, which is based on Brown beer optimization, integrated to overcome the issue of the VMD related to the number of modes (K) and the penalty factor (α). This optimal method was helpful in decomposing MRI images into intrinsic modes and capturing complex signal patterns of the brain. Then, transfer learning-based models were used to extract deep features from sub-band images, and feature engineering, such as dimension reduction and feature ranking, was performed on these features before feeding them to a classifier to classify healthy and affected AD images. Result: The proposed method achieved diagnostic accuracy of 97.6%, specificity of 97.4%, and sensitivity of 98.8% in distinguishing AD from healthy controls, outperforming traditional VMD and standard deep learning approaches. Progression prediction models demonstrated a correlation coefficient of 0.89 with clinical outcomes, highlighting robust prognostic capabilities. To validate the model's performance, cross-validation and Grad-CAM are employed. Conclusion: The prognosis for AD is significantly improved by BBO-optimized VMD with transfer learning, providing a scalable and precise instrument for early recognition, tracking, and individualized behavior.

Title: Prediction of University English Writing Scores using Hierarchical Multi-Scale Feature Scoring Network
Abstract: From the past decades, the increasing demand of educational technology has significantly transformed the way student performance is assessed in domain of language learning and writing evaluation. Thus, the Automated Essay Scoring (AES) systems have emerged as an efficient solution to reduce the burden of manual grading. However, the existing AES-based models suffered in independently handling of multi-scale features and lack of effective feature integration which led to restrict its ability to capture the complex essay writing patterns. Hence, this research proposes a structural unified framework namely Hierarchical Multi-scale Feature Scoring Network (HMFS-Net) to improve the hierarchical understanding and feature representation for improved essay score prediction. Initially, the input data is collected from the ASAP dataset and fed into preprocessing for lowercasing, punctuation removal, sentence tokenization and word tokenization to preserve the semantic and structural information. Then, the Word2Vec, average pooling and hierarchical averaging are employed in feature extraction to perform word-level, sentence-level and document-level representations. After that, these heterogeneous representations are fused into a single unified feature vector by using the vector concatenation and finally, the linear regression layer is incorporated to evaluate the final essay score. The proposed HMFS-Net model achieved highest Quadratic Weighted Kappa (QWK) of 0.962 than the existing Lightweight XGBoost (LwXGBoost) model.

Title: Multidimensional Evaluation Model of Emotion and Skill in Music Performance based on Artificial Intelligence Audio Analysis
Abstract: Music performance evaluation lacks automated models quantifying both emotional expression and technical skill. A multi-task model integrates wav2vec 2.0 and a Transformer encoder. From input audio, Log-Mel spectrograms feed a six-layer time-frequency convolutional network, while the original waveform feeds a pre-trained wav2vec 2.0 model. A Transformer encoder fuses the two feature sequences. The model regresses valence and arousal via confidence-weighted mean squared error, and four skill metrics pitch deviation, rhythmic stability, dynamic uniformity, timbre clarity via smoothed L1 loss. Contrastive learning with NT-Xent loss reduces annotation noise. The model achieves joint optimization of multi-task regression and contrastive learning. On the DEAM test set, mean absolute errors for valence and arousal reach 0.125 and 0.138. Root mean square errors for pitch deviation, rhythmic stability, dynamic uniformity, and timbre clarity are 0.075, 0.080, 0.090, and 0.095 respectively. The proposed framework provides a repeatable end-to-end solution for automated multidimensional music performance evaluation.

Title: Generative AI in Signal Processing Education: An Audio Foundation Model Based Approach
Abstract: Audio Foundation Models (AFMs), a specialized category of Generative AI (GenAI), have the potential to transform signal processing (SP) education by integrating core applications such as speech and audio enhancement, denoising, source separation, feature extraction, automatic classification, and real-time signal analysis into learning and research. This paper introduces SPEduAFM, a conceptual AFM tailored for SP education that fuses traditional SP principles with GenAI-driven innovations. Through an envisioned case study, we outline how AFMs can enable a range of applications, including automated lecture transcription, interactive demonstrations, and inclusive learning tools, showcasing their potential to transform abstract concepts into engaging practical experiences. This paper also addresses challenges such as ethics, explainability, and customization by highlighting dynamic, real-time auditory interactions that foster experiential and authentic learning. By presenting SPEduAFM as a forward-looking vision, our goal is to inspire broader adoption of GenAI in engineering education, enhancing accessibility, engagement, and innovation in the classroom and beyond.

Title: CNN Image Multiclass Classification with ADAM Optimizer and ReLU Warm-Up Strategy for Drone-Based Mangifera Indica L. Fruit Drop Prediction
Abstract: Precision agriculture has continuously integrated artificial intelligence and drone-based imaging systems to improve crop monitoring, disease identification, and yield prediction in high-value fruit cultivation. In Philippine Carabao mango agriculture, fruit loss is a significant challenge with substantial economic implications, often persisting due to factors such as maturity, peduncle detachment, and early-stage disease infections. This research sought to establish a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based framework for image classification to forecast fruit drop, utilizing imagery obtained from drones. The explicit objectives were to: (1) design and optimize a CNN model utilizing the Adaptive Moment Estimation (ADAM) optimizer with a learning rate ReLU warm-up strategy; (2) extract and classify visual features including color, shape, peduncle condition, and disease symptoms; (3) develop a supporting mathematical model for the CNN architecture; and (4) assess performance using standard metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. A collection of 3,500 annotated mango photos was compiled and analyzed, encompassing various ripeness stages, morphological differences, and prevalent mango illnesses, including anthracnose, bacterial black spot, and black mildew. The CNN architecture was based on a LeNet-inspired framework, augmented with ReLU activations, dropout regularization (rate =0.5), and early stopping to mitigate overfitting. Warm-up learning rate scheduling was implemented during the initial epochs to stabilize training dynamics. The model underwent training, validation, and testing utilizing a 70-15-15 distribution. The results indicated macro-averaged scores of 94.8% accuracy, 94.4% precision, 93.9% recall, and 94.1 % ~F 1-score for all tasks. Analyses of the confusion matrix demonstrated significant predictive reliability, especially with the assessment of peduncle condition and fruit ripeness. In conclusion, the suggested CNN framework successfully met the research objectives, providing a dependable, scalable, and real-time solution for predicting mango fruit drop. The use of drone vision technology offers a promising instrument for data-driven orchard management and sustainable mango cultivation.

Title: Profiling Digital Hate: A Multidimensional Measurement Approach Based on the Perspective API
Abstract: The automatic classification of digital hate is a pressing challenge, yet many existing computational models remain opaque and insufficiently evaluated as measurement tools in social science contexts. This study examines the utility of Google’s Perspective API as a measurement instrument by modeling higher-order constructs of harmful discourse (i.e., incivility and intolerance) as outcomes of multiple lower-level behavioral indicators captured by distinct API scores rather than using a single aggregate score as a proxy for complex social behaviors while enabling the evaluation of state-of-the-art black-box classifiers beyond classification metrics. Drawing on 4,000 manually annotated English-language YouTube comments in the context of the Israel-Hamas war, we test whether multiple API scores predict incivility and intolerance using generalized linear and additive models, assess classification performance across non-hateful, uncivil, and intolerant content, and benchmark a recent deep learning model. Results show that Identity Attack is a strong predictor of intolerance, whereas Insult and Profanity are indicative of incivility. While classification performance is somewhat below state-of-the-art deep learning models, our approach offers important advantages: transparency, interpretability, accessibility for non-technical researchers, and potential cross-linguistic applicability. We argue that typology-driven, multi-indicator-based classification provides a practical and theoretically grounded complement to more aggregated black-box models, particularly in human-in-the-loop workflows that can help reduce annotator exposure through pre-filtering of content.

Title: Multi-modal Features Analysis and Performance Assessment for Endovascular Surgery Skills
Abstract: Purpose: Interventional skill and assessment are essential for vascular interventionalists prior to performing clinical procedures. However, traditional surgical assessments often fail to deliver objective and accurate results. To address these issues, our study proposes a simulator and an analytical framework for evaluating endovascular procedural performance. Methods: A custom interventional operation simulator included an in vitro silicone phantom, mock circulation loop, visual module, force-sensing module, and custom software for kinematic and force data post-processing. An in vitro study was conducted to deliver medical guidewire to four target vessels by thirty interventionalists and ten medical novices. Four types of features (i.e., vascular morphological, device-vascular model interaction, kinematic and force) were obtained from the interventional tasks. An operational force prediction model was developed and trained using long short-term memory (LSTM) networks based on multi-modal feature datasets. Furthermore, features with significant differences were applied for qualitative and quantitative evaluation via support vector machine and Mahalanobis distance. Results: The well-trained LSTM model could predict the operation force, force and torque between instruments and vascular model. The qualitative assessment achieved an overall accuracy of 84.17% for two-class classification to distinguish the novice and expert attempts, and the quantitative assessment could assign effective scores for all attempts. Conclusions: This work provides an approach for the prediction and assessment of intervention performance behaviors, and results demonstrate the effectiveness of this method for promoting the development of interventional skill assessment.

Title: A Two-Stage Unified Refinement Framework With RS-Specific Priors for Remote Sensing Open-Vocabulary Segmentation
Abstract: Vision-language pretrained models, particularly CLIP, have demonstrated remarkable zero-shot transfer capabilities across various image-level tasks, catalyzing the advancement of open-vocabulary semantic segmentation (OVSS) in remote sensing (RS). However, the direct deployment of CLIP to the RS domain is inherently constrained by the profound domain shift between terrestrial and overhead perspectives, as well as the intricate geometric heterogeneities regarding scale and orientation. To circumvent these limitations, we propose CDSeg, a robust framework tailored for RSOVSS. Central to this architecture is the dual-domain feature compensation module (DDFCM), which integrates DINOv3 weights, pretrained on large-scale RS benchmarks, to augment CLIP with domain-specific semantic priors, effectively bridging the natural-to-satellite knowledge gap. Furthermore, we introduce a MambaVision-driven cross-feature fine-grained interaction module (CFFIM) to facilitate a unified refinement of spatial and category attributes, leveraging long-range dependency modeling to enhance the model's discriminative power in unseen environments. To robustly manage the complexities of diverse orientations and scales, CDSeg incorporates a direction-aware rotation strategy and a wavelet-cross-attention-enhanced module (WCAEM) for high-fidelity multiscale feature decoding. Empirical evaluations on four public benchmarks demonstrate that CDSeg achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance, while extensive ablation studies substantiate the synergistic contribution and indispensability of each component.

Title: A predictive tool incorporating frailty scores for perioperative risk assessment in patients with spinal metastasis: a national retrospective cohort study
Abstract: Background: Surgical treatment for spinal metastases is associated with high perioperative risk due to tumor burden, neurologic compromise, and limited physiological reserve. Frailty is a recognized predictor of adverse outcomes, yet most existing indices exclude key clinical variables. This study evaluated and enhanced the predictive performance of three frailty instruments—the 5-item Modified Frailty Index (mFI-5), 11-item mFI (mFI-11), and Risk Analysis Index–Administrative (RAI-A)—by incorporating five clinically relevant covariates: serum albumin, hematocrit, body mass index (BMI), spinal region, and procedure type. Methods: A retrospective cohort analysis was performed using the ACS-NSQIP database (2010–2022) to identify adult patients who underwent surgery for spinal metastases. Frailty scores and clinical covariates were analyzed using logistic regression and ensemble machine learning models. Primary outcomes were 30-day postoperative complications, readmission, and reoperation. Model performance was assessed using discrimination and reclassification metrics. Results: A total of 5,052 patients were included. Higher frailty scores were significantly associated with increased complication rates, prolonged hospitalization, higher early mortality, and lower rates of discharge to home (p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, vertebrectomy/corpectomy, thoracic or multilevel surgery, and lower preoperative hematocrit were independently associated with increased complication risk. Higher serum albumin was protective against early reoperation, while steroid use and delayed time to surgery predicted higher readmission risk. The RAI-A model performed best for complications, while the mFI-5 model showed strongest association with reoperation. Augmenting frailty indices with the five clinical covariates improved predictive performance across all outcomes. Conclusion: Frailty is a clinically meaningful predictor of perioperative risk in spinal metastasis surgery. Integrating serum albumin, hematocrit, BMI, spinal region, and procedure type with frailty indices enhances risk stratification and informs surgical planning, preoperative optimization, and patient counseling in this vulnerable population. Title: AI-based personalized sports training plan generation system: A multi-community ranking framework
Abstract: We propose a scalable hybrid multi-modal framework for personalized sports training plan generation based on diverse athlete profiling and dynamic optimization search. Designed for large-scale athletic environments, our system uncovers coherent, performance-aligned athlete communities through hierarchical feature learning. This pipeline extracts diverse biometric features—such as cardiovascular capacity, movement efficiency, and recovery patterns—enhanced by leveraging dynamic programming to identify optimal training paths for each athlete. A physiological feature selection strategy filters out less discriminative attributes, producing refined performance representations. These athlete representations are projected into a latent performance space, where each individual is modeled as a probabilistic distribution over abstract training themes, supporting precise ability differentiation. We construct a weighted athlete similarity graph from these representations, enabling large-scale community detection through advanced clustering techniques. The resulting training communities reflect shared physiological patterns—such as endurance-focused or power-oriented athletes—and reveal both macro- and micro-level performance trends. To deliver personalized training plans, a ranking module integrates individual athlete profiles with community embeddings to suggest optimal exercise regimens. This fusion of individual characteristics and group patterns enhances training effectiveness. Evaluations on a dataset of over one million training sessions confirm the system's scalability and prediction accuracy, demonstrating robustness across varied fitness levels and effectiveness in large-scale personalization scenarios.

Title: Detection of Cardiovascular Abnormalities With Heart Sounds Using Machine Learning
Abstract: Cardiovascular diseases, also commonly called as CVDs, are a leading global health burden that demands accessible and objective screening tools. Although PCGs offer a non-invasive diagnostic medium, manual interpretation is subjective and greatly influenced by the domain expert's level of expertise. This work proposes a novel, noise-aware, two-stage machine learning framework for automatic heart sound classification. The system first employs an authenticity filter to filter out spurious audio from valid heart sounds, followed by an abnormality detection module to classify heart sounds into two categories: Normal and Abnormal. A critical finding of this work is challenging conventional preprocessing; we show that standard noise reduction techniques degrade diagnostic performance significantly by removing subtle pathological cues. Evaluated on the public CirCor DigiScope dataset, our pipeline achieves state-of-the-art F1-score of 98.02% using a Random Forest classifier trained on comprehensive multi-domain feature set from raw, unfiltered data. The proposed system will be deployed as an openaccess Streamlit web application to bridge the gap between practical deployment in a clinical environment and research. The results obtained in this project validate the potential of the framework for use as a reliable automated decision support tool for cardiac screening.

Title: Automated Oral Cancer Image Classification Using MobileNetV2 for Histopathological Analysis
Abstract: Oral cancer is a major health issue worldwide, and early diagnosis is essential for enhancing patient survival rates. Histopathological analysis of oral tissue slides is the definitive method for diagnosis; yet manual evaluation is laborintensive and prone to inter-observer variability. This research introduces an automated method for oral cancer classification using MobileNetV2, a lightweight convolutional neural network, for the examination of histopathological images. The model was trained on a dataset including 1,224 H&E stained images, encompassing normal epithelium and Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma (OSCC) at magnifications of 100x and 400x. The preprocessing stages include scaling, normalization, and data augmentation to improve model performance. The MobileNetV2 model attained a classification accuracy of 99.63%, a precision of 99.75%, a recall of 99.50%, and an F1 score of 99.62% on the test set. The findings indicate that the model can proficiently differentiate between normal and malignant tissues, providing a dependable instrument for automated oral cancer diagnosis. The methodology has the potential for incorporation into mobile-assisted diagnostic systems, aiding pathologists and enhancing early detection in clinical and resource-constrained environments.

Title: AI-guided optimization of integrated waveguide polarizers with 2D reduced graphene oxide [Invited]
Abstract: Reduced graphene oxide (rGO) exhibits strong anisotropic light absorption and high compatibility with photonic integrated chips, making it a promising material for implementing high-performance on-chip polarization-selective devices. The performance of rGO integrated waveguide polarizers is highly dependent on the waveguide geometry, and achieving optimal performance requires exploring a large parameter space, making conventional mode simulation methods computationally demanding. Here, we propose and demonstrate a machine learning framework based on fully connected neural networks (FCNNs) to map the dependence of the polarizer figure of merit (FOM) on the waveguide geometry. Once trained by using a small dataset of low-resolution mode simulation results, the FCNN framework can rapidly and accurately predict FOM values across a large structural parameter space with high resolution. Results show that this method can reduce overall computing time by more than four orders of magnitude as compared to the mode simulation methods, and achieve high prediction accuracy with an average deviation (AD) below 0.05. Title: Symbolic Dastgah Classification of Persian Classical Music Using Natural Language Processing
Abstract: Music Information Retrieval (MIR) provides computational methods for music analysis; however, most existing approaches to Persian classical music rely on audio-based signal processing. This paper proposes a symbolic framework for Dastgah classification using Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques applied to MIDI (Musical Instrument Digital Interface) representations. Using the IRMA dataset of Mirza Abdollah's Radif, MIDI note sequences are encoded symbolically by mapping pitch-duration pairs to Unicode characters and treated analogously to text. SentencePiece tokenization is employed to capture recurring melodic patterns, and Word2Vec is used to learn vector embeddings of the resulting musical tokens. Fixedlength representations of entire pieces are obtained via statistical pooling over token embeddings. These representations are evaluated using classical machine learning classifiers, including Support Vector Machines, Logistic Regression, k-Nearest Neighbors, and Random Forests. Experimental results show that meanpooled representations combined with a linear SVM achieve the best performance, with an accuracy and F 1-score of 0.81 across 13 Dastgahs and Avazes. To the best of our knowledge, this work presents the first application of NLP techniques to symbolic Dastgah classification, offering a complementary alternative to audio-based approaches that aligns closely with the theoretical structure of the tradition.
