Title: Multiple machine learning models for predicting major adverse cardiovascular events in dialysis with clinical and echocardiographic parameters: a retrospective cohort study
Abstract: Background: Patients undergoing dialysis are at an elevated risk of cardiovascular events. This study aimed to develop machine learning (ML) prediction models to identify risk factors for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in dialysis patients. Materials and Methods: This retrospective study included 203 patients undergoing dialysis with a median age of 45.0 years and 64.0% male. The participants were divided into training and test sets in a 7:3 ratio. LASSO regression selected characteristic variables from patients’general information, laboratory tests, and echocardiographic parameters (including global longitudinal strain [GLS]). Eight ML models were constructed,and SHAP analysis evaluated feature importance. Results: The incidence of MACE (including myocardial infarction, unstable angina, heart failure, and cardiovascular death) in dialysis patients was 38.92%. The average follow-up period was 18 months. LASSO regression identified eight feature variables. Among the ML models, AdaBoost demonstrated superior performance, with an AUC of 0.883 (95% CI: 0.830–0.937), accuracy of 0.804, sensitivity of 0.864 and specificity of 0.762 in the training set, and an AUC of 0.809 (95% CI: 0.706–0.912), accuracy of 0.750, sensitivity of 0.90 and specificity of 0.675 in the test set. The SHAP analysis identified N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) level, estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), GLS and age as the four most important features for predicting MACE in patients undergoing dialysis (mean absolute SHAP values: 0.199, 0.176, 0.096 and 0.091, respectively). Conclusion: Elevated NT-proBNP, advanced age, reduced eGFR and impaired GLS were independently associated with an increased risk of MACE in patients undergoing dialysis.

Title: Machine Learning-Driven Cognitive Assessment Framework for Early Detection of Alzheimer's Disease Using ADNI Clinical Data
Abstract: Alzheimer disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disease that has a strong influence on memory, thinking functions as well as performing daily life functions. The timely clinical intervention of the disease and the proper management of the patient are all dependent on the early and accurate diagnosis of the Alzheimer disease. Tests of Cognitive assessment eg. Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), Alzheimer Disease Assessment Scale (ADAS-Cog) and Functional Activities Questionnaire (FAQ) are tests that are common in clinical practice to assess the cognitive decline that is a result of the presence of Alzheimer disease. Nonetheless, manual interpretations of such assessments may be difficult in relation to large clinical datasets, thus the implementation of data-driven methods that can be used to inform clinical decision-making is proposed in this study. An instrumented dataset of 9,430 samples was created based on three clinically useful cognitive measures: MMSCORE (MMSE), TOTAL13 (ADAS-Cog) and FAQTOTAL (FAQ). Group K-Fold crossvalidation was used to train the model, and patient-level dataset separation to avoid data leakage through the use of unique patient identifiers was carried out. Three machine learning models, including Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), have been created and tested with the help of several performance measures, such as the accuracy, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, and specificity. Experimental evidence indicates that cognitive assessment scores are also critically predictive in the distinction between cognitive normals and people with cognitive impairment as relates to the Alzheimer disease. The XGBoost classifier was found to have the best performance with a test accuracy of 0.80, sensitivity of 0.813, specificity of 0.776 and AUC of 0.8766, and feature importance analysis and SHAP based explanations further indicated that the most influential predictor of the risk of Alzheimer is the Functional Activities Questionnaire score, then ADAS-Cog and MMSE scores. The results demonstrate the usefulness of machine learning methods in using a small collection of cognitive predictors to determine Alzheimer disease with a high degree of reliability. As this study indicates, cognitive assessment-based predictive models may be a useful and understandable decision-support instrument to be used in the clinical environment to identify cognitive impairment in the early stages.

Title: Digitalization and renewable energy sustainability: an empirical analysis of artificial intelligence and wind power in Europe
Abstract: Renewable energy sources lie at the core of the global energy transition toward sustainable development, with wind energy playing a strategic role in the shift to low-carbon energy systems. However, the intermittent and variable nature of wind energy brings forth significant challenges in forecasting and optimization. At this juncture, artificial intelligence (AI) emerges as a critical instrument for enhancing energy efficiency, improving system reliability, and accelerating technological innovation. This study investigates the impact of AI on wind energy generation by employing a panel dataset covering 28 European countries over the period 2009–2024. The empirical strategy first tests long-run relationships through the Pedroni cointegration approach, while dynamic interactions are estimated using the ARDL model. Robustness checks are conducted via Panel FMOLS, OLS, and FGLS estimators, and their forecast performances are further compared using the Diebold–Mariano test. The Dumitrescu–Hurlin panel causality test is employed to explore the directional linkages between variables. The findings reveal that AI exerts a statistically significant and positive effect on wind energy generation, primarily through technological progress and innovation channels. Overall, the study provides empirical evidence on the role of AI in Europe’s renewable energy transition and underscores the importance of digitalization and efficiency-oriented applications in shaping future energy policies.

Title: Relevance Metric for Bird Sound Detection
Abstract: This work proposes a relevance metric strategy for automated bird vocalization detection, tested on a newly compiled dataset of annotated recordings collected from multiple rainforest fragments. Our approach combines a shallow CNN architecture with a relevance metric to better handle diverse real-world recording conditions. Our experiments were conducted using a private dataset comprising 849 samples with bird vocalizations, totaling 15,867 regions of interest (ROIs) that were labeled by experts. The marked ROIs correspond to the calls or songs of 161 different bird species. We compare our method against a traditional energy-based baseline, which achieves F1-scores of 0.42 and 0.44 when using Per-Channel (PCEN) Energy Normalization and Spectral Subtraction, respectively. By contrast, our best CNN variant, leveraging PCEN spectrograms, obtains an F1-score of 0.66. While the approach maintains consistently high precision, recall remains variable in more challenging scenarios. Overall, the results highlight that modest increases in network depth and appropriate spectrogram processing can substantially improve detection performance in complex soundscapes.

Title: Physics-Informed Modeling of Temperature Effects in Rogowski Coils for Harmonic and Complex Signal Accuracy
Abstract: Low-power instrument transformers (LPITs) are increasingly being deployed in power networks, either replacing or complementing traditional inductive instrument transformers (ITs). Although LPITs provide several advantages, they are also sensitive to a range of influencing factors. This work focuses on Rogowski coils (RCs) and investigates the impact of temperature on their performance. The analysis follows the temperature-accuracy testing procedure prescribed by current standards, with the results used to train a physics-informed deep learning model. The model is experimentally assessed for estimating the coil output over the considered temperature range and for harmonic components over a wide frequency spectrum. The proposed approach, validated on three commercial devices, enables the estimation of temperature-dependent output variations without the need for real-time thermal calibration or additional sensing hardware, thereby lowering system complexity and cost. By embedding physical knowledge into the data-driven framework, the methodology provides an interpretable model whose performance is evaluated at temperatures not used during training, within the experimentally tested range. The experimental findings confirm that combining domain knowledge with modern DL techniques can support the mitigation of one of the most critical error sources in RCs, enhancing their reliability for grid monitoring, protection, and control.

Title: SpAudiX: A Hierarchical Edge Framework for Spatial Audio Sensing and Monitoring Applications
Abstract: Distributed sensing and monitoring applications increasingly demand low-latency and scalable processing in environments where reliable cloud connectivity is limited or unavailable. These constraints are especially critical for audio-centric sensing, where signal quality is strongly affected by noise, spatial variation, and the need to correlate observations across multiple devices. This paper presents SpAudiX, a hierarchical three-layer edge computing architecture for distributed audio sensing and processing applications in remote environments. SpAudiX organizes resource-constrained edge nodes, intermediate edge servers, and a top-level edge coordinator according to physical proximity, enabling localized multi-source aggregation and scalable cross-cluster coordination. At the edge server layer, spatially co-located audio streams are processed using an AI-driven pipeline for signal enhancement, source prioritization, and noise suppression, thereby exploiting spatial redundancy without relying on centralized cloud infrastructure. To validate the proposed design, we implement a fully functional prototype and deploy it on a multi-node virtual machine testbed. Experimental evaluation using real audio samples demonstrates the feasibility of the approach and provides insights into system performance and scalability. The results show that SpAudiX enables practical, infrastructure-independent spatial audio sensing for dynamic real-world scenarios such as disaster response, environmental monitoring, and security applications.

Title: Pneumatic Measurement System Design Based on Resource-constrained Controller
Abstract: The precision of traditional pneumatic measuring instruments is limited by various error sources, making it difficult to stably break through the micrometer-level 0.5 μm bottleneck. This study explores the effectiveness of machine learning methods in compensating for complex systematic errors and achieving submicron-level pneumatic measurement. A hardware-collected dataset of pneumatic sensor voltage signals was acquired using a PCIE-1816 DAQ card (250 samples across 50 gap positions, 4000 points per sample at 2 kHz, 16-bit resolution) containing more than ten types of error sources. Three ensemble learning models—Random Forest, Gradient Boosting Tree, and Extra Trees—were trained and compared against conventional signal processing baselines including moving average filtering, Savitzky-Golay smoothing, and polynomial regression. Experimental results show that the optimal Extra Trees model achieved a mean absolute error (MAE) of 1.398 μm on the test set, significantly outperforming polynomial regression (2.602 μm), Savitzky-Golay filtering (0.385 μm), and moving average filtering (0.412 μm), with a precision improvement of approximately 1.9 times. The proportion of samples with errors within 0.1 μm increased from 12.2% to 90.2%, achieving a stable leap from micrometer-level to submicron-level precision on resource-constrained controllers.

Title: DBLAD: A Dual-Branch Lightweight Architecture with Attention-Guided Frequency-Spatial Fusion for AI-Generated Art Detection
Abstract: The rapid advancement of generative models, particularly latent diffusion models, has enabled the production of synthetic artworks that are increasingly indistinguishable from human-created art, posing significant threats to artistic integrity, copyright protection, and digital content authenticity. Existing detection approaches suffer from three key limitations: (1) heavy reliance on large-scale models such as ResNet-50 (25.6M parameters) or CLIP ViT-L/14 (428M parameters), which prohibit deployment on resource-constrained devices; (2) singledomain feature extraction that captures either spatial or frequency artefacts but not both, leading to poor generalisation across diverse generative architectures; and (3) lack of adaptive feature refinement mechanisms that can selectively emphasise the most discriminative cues within fused representations. To address these challenges, we propose DBLAD (Dual-Branch Lightweight AI Art Detector), a compact detection framework comprising three innovations: (1) a dual-branch architecture that jointly extracts spatial features via EfficientNet-B0 and frequencydomain artefacts via a lightweight DCT-based CNN; (2) an attention-guided fusion module employing the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) to adaptively weight channel and spatial information in the fused representation; and (3) a parameter-efficient design totalling only 4.42M parameters (16.9 MB), achieving a 5.7 × reduction compared to ResNet50. Experiments on the Bird et al. AI-generated art dataset demonstrate that DBLAD achieves 100% accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and an AUC-ROC of 1.0000 on the test set, while ablation studies confirm that each proposed component contributes measurably to the final performance.

Title: An Exploratory Machine Learning Classification of Contrasted Depressive Symptom Groups Using Self-reported Psychometric Measures in Mexican Undergraduate Students
Abstract: Depressive symptoms in university students are influenced by multiple psychological and contextual factors, yet they are often examined through isolated variables. This study explored whether self-reported psychometric measures could support the classification of contrasted depressive symptom groups in undergraduate students and help identify the most relevant contributing domains. Questionnaire-level scores from validated instruments assessing intrafamilial relationships, quality of life, anxiety, social skills, personality, and related constructs were used as predictors. Depressive symptom groups were defined from PHQ-9 scores using a 40–20–40 contrasted-group design. Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machines, Random Forest, and LightGBM were evaluated under stratified 5-fold cross-validation. Feature relevance was examined through normalized importance measures across models, and Principal Component Analysis (PCA) was used as an exploratory complement. Random Forest achieved the highest performance, while Logistic Regression and Support Vector Machines also showed competitive results. The most relevant predictors were not limited to anxiety, but included intrafamilial relationship variables, quality of life, social skills, and personality dimensions, suggesting that depressive symptom differentiation is associated with a broader psychosocial profile. PCA results revealed latent structure but did not improve predictive performance. These findings provide preliminary evidence that multidimensional psychometric data can support exploratory classification of contrasted depressive symptom groups and may help reveal relevant psychosocial domains for future mental health research.

Title: Evaluation of an AI-Based Mental Health Chatbot Through Multidimensional Expert Assessment: A Preliminary Study from Yucatán, Mexico
Abstract: Mental health disorders represent a growing global burden, with persistent treatment gaps driven by limited access to care, stigma, and shortages of trained professionals, particularly in low- and middle-income regions. Artificial intelligence (AI)–based conversational agents have emerged as scalable digital tools with the potential to support mental health through psychoeducation and emotional guidance. However, concerns remain regarding their ethical alignment, empathic capacity, and management of sensitive or crisis-related situations. This study presents a preliminary expert-based evaluation of an AI-powered mental health chatbot developed as an academic prototype for psychoeducational support among students in southeastern Mexico. A cross-sectional exploratory assessment was conducted with 17 independent mental health experts, who evaluated the system across four dimensions: ethical adequacy, psychoeducational quality, empathic communication, and management of sensitive situations, using a 5-point Likert scale. The overall mean score was 3.34/5 (SD = 1.07; 95% CI: 2.79–3.89) corresponding to a performance level classified as requiring adjustments. Ethical adequacy achieved the highest score (3.57/5), while psychoeducational quality (3.22/5), empathic communication (3.18/5), and management of sensitive situations (3.40/5) remained below the adequacy threshold. Internal consistency of the evaluation instrument was acceptable (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.84), with moderate inter-rater agreement (ICC range: 0.62–0.71). These findings suggest that, although the chatbot demonstrates a foundational ethical baseline, important improvements are needed in its interaction quality and handling of complex mental health scenarios. This exploratory study contributes context-specific evidence and underscores the importance of rigorous multidimensional evaluation prior to broader implementation.

Title: Classification of Burnout Syndrome Based on EEG Signals: A Machine Learning Approach
Abstract: Burnout syndrome is a multidimensional phenomenon characterized by emotional exhaustion, depersonalization, and reduced personal accomplishment, resulting from chronic workplace stress. There is an urgent need for objective screening tools. This preliminary study recorded EEG signals from 24 participants, 14 with burnout, 10 controls, classified using the MBI-GS instrument. Features were extracted using Discrete Wavelet Transform, frequency analysis, and Continuous Wavelet Transform. Classification was performed using classical machine learning Support Vector Machines, K-Nearest Neighbor, Random Forest, and deep learning models, ResNet50, and a custom CNN. The RF algorithm achieved the highest performance with an F1-Score of 0.75 at the window level and 0.81 at the subject level. Feature importance analysis from the Random Forest model identified the beta band (temporal domain) and alpha band (frequency domain) as the most significant biomarkers for classification.

Title: RTD-SLAM: A Dynamic SLAM System Integrating Real-Time Object Detection and Epipolar Geometry
Abstract: Current mainstream visual localization and mapping methods are generally built on the assumption of a static world. However, in highly dynamic real-world environments, the presence of pedestrians, vehicles, and other moving objects breaks this assumption, leading to feature matching errors or data association failures, which in turn affect localization accuracy and system robustness. To address this problem, this paper proposes RTD-SLAM, a method that integrates deep-learningbased real-time object detection with multi-view geometry for dynamic feature point rejection. Built upon the ORB-SLAM3 framework, RTD-SLAM combines the Transformer-based RealTime Detection Transformer (RT-DETR) with epipolar geometry constraints to distinguish between dynamic and static features. Dynamic features are discarded, and only static features are retained for pose estimation. Experiments on the TUM RGB-D dataset show that our method significantly reduces both absolute trajectory error and relative pose error. Compared with the original ORB-SLAM3, RTD-SLAM achieves higher localization accuracy while maintaining real-time performance.

Title: Modeling Teacher-Student Co-regulation as a Relational Process in AI-Supported Learning
Abstract: In formal education, regulation is inherently relational: teacher and student continuously adapt to one another through dynamic interaction, responding to and shaping each other’s actions over time. Despite its theoretical centrality in the learning sciences, teacher-student co-regulation has not yet been formalized as an explicit computational construct within AI-supported educational systems. AI in Education is evolving along two largely separate trajectories: student-facing systems that function as increasingly autonomous personalized tutors, and teacher-facing systems that position educators as recipients of analytics and performance indicators. This architectural divide is not merely technical. It implicitly reshapes the pedagogical relationship: learning becomes individually optimized, while teaching risks becoming observational rather than co-regulatory. This doctoral project investigates how teacher-student co-regulation can be formally represented and empirically studied as a relational process in AI-supported learning environments. It conceptualizes co-regulation as a dynamic coupling between student learning states and teacher instructional actions and examines how patterns of alignment and misalignment emerge over time using longitudinal digital trace data. A prototype system will be developed as a research instrument to operationalize this relational model and enable in-situ investigation of co-regulatory processes. By extending learner modeling from the individual to the relational level, the project introduces co-regulation as a unit of computational analysis in AI in Education and studies how its explicit representation shapes teacher-student coordination over time.

Title: Attention-based Bi-Stream network for underwater image enhancement
Abstract: Enhancing underwater images is difficult because of degradation caused to visibility, contrast, and color distortion due to scattering, light absorption in underwater environments. In this paper, we present a new multi-stream deep learning approach, UWIEn_BiAlCn to enhance underwater images. The proposed framework begins with preprocessing, then employs a Bi-Stream feature extraction networks: an Improved AlexNet with Pyramid Dilated Convolution (ImAlPDC) and an Improved CNN with Spatial Pyramid Hybrid Convolution (ImCSPHC), to capture both local and global contextual features at multiple scales. The bi-scale features generated are fused using an attention-based fusion module, ensuring optimal feature integration and relevance weighting. A subsequent decoder network reconstructs the enhanced underwater image with improved perceptual quality. Experimental results demonstrate superior performance, achieving PSNR up to 39.12, SSIM of 0.988, UIQM of 4.87, and UCIQE of 0.758 on UIEB, outperforming conventional single-stream models and existing enhancement methods across multiple benchmark datasets.

Title: DMHF-Net: Dual-Modal Hierarchical Fusion Network for RGB-IR Joint Detection of Small-Scale Targets from UAV Perspective
Abstract: Small-target detection based on uncrewed aerial vehicle aerial imagery has been widely adopted in remote sensing. However, under complex environments and varying illumination conditions, single-modal processing of small targets often suffers from weak feature representation, making effective feature extraction a formidable challenge. To address these challenges, we propose a novel multimodal remote sensing detector, namely dual-modal hierarchical fusion network (DMHF-Net). This network offers four scalable model sizes to cater to deployment requirements across diverse scenarios. The DMHF-Net leverages frequency-split receptive field dilated convolution to expand the receptive field, enabling lightweight frequency-aware feature extraction. The extracted features are fed into the modality-channel joint attention fusion module, which fuses the dual-modal features and dynamically adjusts the feature weights of each modality to output feature maps with different scales and channel dimensions. Via the global-spatial channel joint weighting module and multimodal scale influence detection head, the importance of spatial regions and individual channels is adaptively assigned, further enhancing the feature expression of small targets. After detection, critical samples are weighted in the intersection-over-union-aware weighted loss and participate in backpropagation to improve the network. Extensive experiments were conducted on improved VEDAI, RGBT-tiny, LLVIP, DroneVehicle, and M3FD datasets. Our experimental results demonstrate that the DMHF-Net achieves remarkable performance levels, with an excellent tradeoff between detection accuracy and computational cost maintained across all model variants. The results also show the superiority over other state-of-the-art object detection methods.

Title: AI-resistant and AI-resilient assessment in higher education: a systematic review of validity-grounded strategies, institutional frameworks, and equity implications
Abstract: The emergence of large language models has precipitated a fundamental disruption to higher education assessment. Conventional instruments are susceptible to AI-assisted completion, threatening construct validity across disciplines and institutional contexts. When submitted work reflects AI capability rather than student competency, the inferential chain from performance to qualification is invalidated–a problem of design rather than detection. This systematic review makes two contributions. First, it theorises and grounds the distinction between AI-resistant assessment, which seeks to prevent or impede AI access through containment, and AI-resilient assessment, which assesses genuine human cognitive performance of intrinsic educational value regardless of the AI tools that exist. Second, it synthesises peer-reviewed empirical literature, policy documentation, and sector guidance published between 2022 and 2025. A PRISMA 2020-compliant search of five databases was conducted; two independent reviewers screened all records with substantial inter-rater agreement. Forty-seven peer-reviewed studies, 23 policy documents, and 11 sector reports were included. Six evidence-based assessment categories were identified, taxonomised, and evaluated against a structured adversarial threat taxonomy. AI-detection tools are structurally insufficient as primary responses. A Six-Layer AI-Resilient Assessment Stack, grounded in multi-trait multi-method validation logic, is proposed as an integrated institutional framework. Persistent challenges include equity, reliability, faculty development, and data protection.

Title: SFMF-DETR: A Spatial-Frequency Collaborative Enhancement and Multiscale Feature Fusion Framework for Small Object Detection
Abstract: In remote sensing object detection tasks, accurately identifying tiny objects within vast and complex scenes is crucial. However, existing end-to-end frameworks face performance bottlenecks due to inadequate high-frequency detail preservation, fine-grained feature dilution during multiscale fusion, and spatial distortion from traditional upsampling. To address these issues, this article proposes SFMF-DETR, a spatial-frequency collaborative enhancement and multiscale feature fusion framework for small object detection. First, a spatial-frequency multiscale feature enhancement (SF-MFE) module is designed to augment high-frequency components of target boundaries via a dual-stream collaboration mechanism, alleviating spectral deficiency. Second, a cross-scale channel selection attention (CCSA) module implements fine-grained feature selection through adaptive weighting, preventing shallow features from being overwhelmed by deep semantics. Third, a soft-normalized upsampling alignment (SNUA) module preserves the structural integrity of tiny objects using energy normalization constraints. In addition, an Inner-SIoU loss function optimizes the regression branch through auxiliary scale strategies and direction-aware mechanisms, enhancing localization stability in dense scenarios. Experimental results on the VisDrone2019-DET, AI-TOD, and RSOD datasets demonstrate that SFMF-DETR achieves significant gains while maintaining real-time efficiency. Specifically, on VisDrone2019-DET, SFMF-DETR-R18 reaches an mAP<inf>50</inf> of 40.5% (+3.0%), while SFMF-DETR-R50 further reaches 42.1% (+3.4%). On AI-TOD, SFMF-DETR-R18 achieves 58.9% mAP<inf>50</inf> (+2.8%) with a small-object average precision (AP) of 25.7% (+1.6%), and SFMF-DETR-R50 further improves these to 60.2% mAP<inf>50</inf> and 26.5% small-object AP. On RSOD, the model reaches 98.3% mAP<inf>50</inf> (+3.3%), validating the effectiveness and generalization of the proposed framework across diverse remote sensing scenarios.

Title: Evaluating the environmental impacts of synergistic agricultural policies: a double machine learning analysis of dual-pilot reforms
Abstract: Agricultural green transformation requires policies that address pollution control and carbon mitigation within the same production process. This study investigates whether China’s Agricultural Social Services (ASS) and Policy-based Agricultural Insurance (PAI) create additional environmental gains when they operate as a coordinated policy package. Based on a balanced panel of 31 Chinese provinces from 2007 to 2023, we construct a coordinated environmental performance index that integrates carbon-reduction performance and non-point source pollution-control performance. A double/debiased machine learning framework is then used to estimate the effect of ASS-PAI coordination while allowing for high-dimensional covariates and nonlinear confounding structures. The evidence shows a steady improvement in coordinated environmental performance over time, accompanied by a more compact spatial distribution and a southeastward movement of the performance center. Provinces implementing both ASS and PAI achieve higher environmental performance than those exposed to only one policy. This result remains stable after changing model specifications, cross-fitting folds, and machine-learning algorithms. Mechanism analysis indicates that coordinated policies work partly by expanding mechanized agricultural operations and strengthening farmer cooperatives. The effect is stronger where agricultural service systems are more developed, insurance markets are less mature, grain-crop dominance is lower, and irrigation conditions are better. These findings show that production-service support and risk-protection instruments can become mutually reinforcing when they are institutionally matched. The study provides evidence for designing agricultural policy packages that help developing economies control diffuse pollution and lower production-related carbon emissions within the same production system.

Title: A XGBoost-based geophysical model function relating ocean wind and wave states for C‑band VV‑polarized SAR backscattering
Abstract: Nowadays, C-band VV (vertical–vertical)-polarized Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) ocean wind retrievals commonly rely on CMOD (C-band MODel) series geophysical model functions (GMFs). However, most existing GMFs were built based on low-to-medium resolution scatterometer data and ignore the sea‑state influence on normalized radar cross-section (NRCS). In this letter, two novel GMFs (XGB_CSARMOD_w and XGB_CSARMOD_ww) based on the machine learning technique of eXtreme Gradient Boosting are proposed to model C-band SAR backscattering in VV polarization. Here, XGB_CSARMOD_w uses wind vector and incidence angle to predict NRCS, while XGB_CSARMOD_ww additionally includes significant wave height (SWH). These two GMFs are directly constructed based on collocation between 6392 Sentinel-1A/B SAR interferometric wide images and 70 buoys from 2014 to 2023. The validation results demonstrate that both new GMFs perform better in simulating NRCS compared to traditional GMF of C-SARMOD2. After incorporating SWH, XGB_CSARMOD_ww yields the best performance, achieving a root mean square error of 1.21 dB and a correlation coefficient of 95.17% in NRCS prediction. Our new GMF that simultaneously considers wind and wave conditions provides a new pathway for synergetic retrieval accurate ocean wind and SWH from SAR images under complex sea states.

Title: SAMBA: Machine Learning-Assisted Antenna Miniaturization Via Adaptive Boundary Adjustment
Abstract: Achieving extreme antenna miniaturization while maintaining rigorous electromagnetic (EM) performance presents a formidable challenge. This letter proposes surrogate-assisted miniaturization with boundary adjustment (SAMBA), a machine learning framework designed to push antenna footprints toward their physical limits. Unlike conventional approaches that merge objectives into a single fitness function, SAMBA treats the area as a computationally inexpensive objective and EM metrics as expensive constraints modeled by machine learning method. A key innovation is the adaptive boundary adjustment strategy, which dynamically resizes the search space based on feasibility feedback to balance exploration and convergence. Furthermore, a clustering-based batch sampling technique is employed to enable efficient parallel model updating. Validation on two patch antennas demonstrates area reductions of 25.3% and 36% with negligible gain degradation, significantly outperforming conventional surrogate-assisted optimization methods under a limited simulation budget.

Title: Validation of a Generative Artificial Intelligence Learning Progression Instrument Using Item Response Theory: Unleashing the Potential of Adult Learners
Abstract: There are currently few established scales for evaluating learning progression in generative artificial intelligence (GenAI). This study validates an instrument designed to assess the progression of the GenAI concept using a diverse cohort of 635 participants in Hong Kong, including 355 adolescents (under 18) and 280 adults (over 18), comprising students, teachers, parents, and administrative staff. The findings indicate that a three-parameter logistic model provides the best fit for the instrument when compared to other Item Response Theory (IRT) models. Analysis of the difficulty, discrimination, and pseudo-guessing parameter confirms that the instrument effectively differentiates individuals with various abilities. The study’s contribution is the validated Generative Artificial Intelligence Concept Test—a practical and sensitive tool applicable for assessing GenAI learning achievements across both adolescents and adults. To evaluate educational impact, a paired statistical analysis comparing performance before and after a 30-h GenAI literacy course revealed significant learning progression because of the intervention. Both groups demonstrated notable improvements, with adults showing greater improvement than adolescents. The findings highlight an urgent need to unleash the potential of adults and prioritise GenAI literacy by deepening their understanding and application of these technologies.

Title: Synthetic Data Set for Surgical Instrument Detection
Abstract: This paper tackles the problem of surgical instrument preoperative checks using computer vision. More specifically, it investigates the creation of synthetic images to train object detection algorithms based on deep learning. The images are generated with the Blender software and using open-source CAD models to emulate the surgical instruments. This paper presents the various attempts to create a synthetic data set offering similar performances to one made of real-world images. The test performed with the YOLOv9 object detection algorithm shows mAP@50 scores of 0.94 and 0.91 for synthetic and real-world data sets respectively.

Title: Perception-Driven Complex-Domain Speech Enhancement for High-Fidelity Reconstruction
Abstract: To address the issues of detail loss, residual noise, and limited perceptual quality in speech enhancement under mid-to-high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions, this paper proposes a perception-driven training paradigm for high-fidelity speech reconstruction. Built upon the Deep Complex Convolutional Recurrent Network (DCCRN), the proposed method improves the naturalness and detail preservation capability of enhanced speech through a high-SNR-first dynamic curriculum learning strategy, a joint time-frequency perceptual loss, as well as mask refinement and Exponential Moving Average (EMA) stabilization strategies. Experimental results on the TIMIT and MUSAN datasets show that the proposed method consistently outperforms the baseline model under fixed SNR conditions, achieving an average PESQ improvement of 0.22, reaching 3.81 at 15 dB and a peak value of 3.93, while also yielding stable improvements in speech intelligibility. Furthermore, under higher SNR conditions of 25 dB and 30 dB, the model still exhibits stable performance without obvious over-enhancement or speech degradation artifacts. Spectrograms and local timedomain waveform analysis further demonstrate that the proposed method effectively suppresses residual noise in silent segments and high-frequency regions, while better preserving the main speech structure and local transient details.

Title: Siamese Network Object Tracking Algorithm Based on Spatiotemporal Multi-Scale Features and Adaptive Contour Center Weighting
Abstract: Visual object tracking is a fundamental yet challenging computer vision task crucial for autonomous systems and intelligent surveillance. Despite deep learning advancements, contemporary single-object trackers suffer severe performance degradation in unconstrained scenarios characterized by heavy occlusion, abrupt illumination variations, and severe non-rigid morphological deformations. Traditional Siamese network architectures, relying heavily on deep semantic features, irrevocably sacrifice fine-grained spatial resolution, which causes catastrophic model drift when distinguishing targets from semantically similar background distractors. To comprehensively address these issues, this research proposes a novel tracking framework integrating spatiotemporal multi-scale feature extraction with a Squeeze-and-Excitation Attention Module (SEAM). This architecture dynamically fuses shallow spatial features and deep semantic features to guarantee robust category-level discrimination. Furthermore, an Adaptive Target Contour Center Weighting (CCW) mechanism is proposed to exploit temporal inter-frame continuity. By utilizing a computationally efficient row-column scanning algorithm to extract topological boundary priors, this spatial penalization module effectively suppresses background distractor peaks. Extensive experiments on OTB2015 and VOT2018 benchmark datasets definitively demonstrate the quantitative and qualitative superiority of the proposed framework, conclusively validating its exceptional robustness, unparalleled precision, and real-time applicability in highly complex environments.

Title: A Deep YOLO-based Detection Framework Incorporating Channel Attention and Cross-Scale Feature Aggregation for Signal Modulation Classification
Abstract: To address the challenges of insufficient feature representation, limited multi-scale structural modeling capabilities, and decreased robustness under low signal-to-noise ratio conditions in signal modulation classification tasks under complex electromagnetic environments, this study proposes a deep YOLO detection framework that integrates channel attention and cross-scale feature aggregation mechanisms from a theoretical perspective. This model constructs a unified time-frequency statistical feature modeling method, structurally fusing instantaneous amplitude, instantaneous phase, and instantaneous frequency. Simultaneously, it combines bilinear time-frequency distribution and higher-order cumulants as optimizations to form a multi-dimensional joint feature representation. A cross-scale feature aggregation module is introduced into the detection backbone network, performing global optimization through multi-scale deep separable convolution and adaptive weight fusion strategies. Furthermore, a multi-channel attention and spatial neighborhood joint attention mechanism is designed. This mechanism can enhance key feature responses and suppress redundant information. Based on this, an analog generative network based on modulation consistency constraints is proposed. This network achieves feature enhancement through structure-preserving perturbation and distribution alignment loss. Experimental results on our self-constructed SMC-2026 dataset (with parameters of 198,000 samples, 11 modulation schemes, and SNR ranging from -14 dB to 22 dB) demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the comparison model in both classification accuracy and detection performance. Compared to the baseline YOLO method, the overall accuracy is improved by 6.6%, and mAP@0.5 is improved by 6.6%. Compared to the more advanced Transformer model, accuracy is improved by 7.8%, inference speed is improved by approximately 68%, and the number of parameters only increases by approximately 1.2M. Under low signal-to-noise ratio conditions, the model performance improvement reaches a maximum of 11.3%. Confusion matrix analysis shows that the false positive rates for QAM and FSK classes are reduced by 34% and 27%, respectively. The KL divergence of the generated model is 0.017. The model's GFLOPs increase by approximately 31%, while still maintaining a real-time inference capability exceeding 100 FPS.

Title: Leveraging Machine Learning for Proactive Pancreatic Cancer Diagnosis
Abstract: Pancreatic cancer is among the most fatal malignancies since it has late onset of symptoms and does not have effective diagnostic instruments at an early stage. In this paper, a proactive diagnostic framework based on machine learning is suggested, which combines clinical, biochemical, and imaging-generated characteristics to enhance the accuracy of early diagnosis. The methodology involves a pipeline which is structured by the preprocessing of the data, feature engineering and the development of supervised models by the use of Complement Naive Bayes, AdaBoost and extra trees classifiers. Ensemble learning algorithms were also used to increase sensitivity and minimize instances of misclassification and feature-importance analysis to facilitate clinical decision making. The experimental findings showed that the diagnostic performance of the ensemble models improved significantly, with the ensemble models showing an increase in sensitivity and the general accuracy as opposed to the conventional baselines. The system captured well nonlinear trends of early pancreatic anomalies and made predictable results across heterogeneous data sets. The results indicate the potential of multi-modal machine learning in overcoming the problem of early pancreatic cancer detection and present its potential as a clinical decision support system. This paper will show that by combining various patient characteristics and a strong ensemble-based classification, it may be possible to identify the high-risk cases earlier and to intervene in time and to enhance the potential patient outcomes.

Title: Calibrated AI Soft Sensors for Property Valuation under Sparse and Noisy Market Signals
Abstract: Automated Valuation Models (AVMs) typically function as point estimators, optimizing for global accuracy metrics such as Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE). However, in high-stakes domains like mortgage underwriting and real estate portfolio management, the reliability of a measurement is often more critical than the prediction itself. This paper proposes a novel framework that reframes property valuation not as a regression task, but as a design problem for an AI-assisted "soft sensor."We introduce a Deep Ensemble-based Virtual Instrument capable of quantifying measurement uncertainty arising from sparse data, market regime shifts, and strategic listing biases. We utilize a synthetic data generation framework to establish a known latent ground truth, which is not directly observable in real-world economic datasets, enabling controlled evaluation of reliability and uncertainty behavior. We demonstrate that standard ML predictors are functionally uncalibrated (15% empirical coverage for 90% confidence intervals), which we correct via post-hoc variance scaling to restore 90% coverage. Furthermore, we demonstrate a "Selective Risk"mechanism, allowing the instrument to reject low-confidence inputs, reducing RMSE by 11.8% when rejecting the bottom 50% of uncertain measurements. This establishes "Economic Metrology": applying instrumentation standards (calibration, uncertainty budgets, operating ranges) to financial estimation. The framework enables safe human-AI hybrid workflows for automated valuation.

Title: Classification of Salt–Alkali-Tolerant Rice Cultivars Using Hyperspectral Reflectance and Machine Learning
Abstract: Aiming at the problems of low efficiency, heavy workload, long cycle, and destructiveness in traditional methods for distinguishing salt–alkali tolerance among different rice cultivars, this research proposes a classification method combining hyperspectral technology with machine learning algorithms. The Analytical Spectral Devices (ASD) FieldSpec 4 hyperspectral instrument was employed to collect leaf reflectance spectral data of different rice cultivars. After removing abnormal data, smoothing, and noise reduction, the combined preprocessing method of standard normal variable (SNV) transformation and first-order derivative (FD) was applied to the original spectral data to eliminate noise and enhance subtle spectral features. Furthermore, Competitive Adaptive Reweighted Sampling (CARS) and Random Forest (RF) were separately used for feature extraction to achieve data dimensionality reduction and select key spectral features. On this basis, the performance of Back Propagation Neural Network (BPNN), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) algorithms was systematically compared. These algorithms were combined with the two feature extraction methods to construct classification models for rice cultivars’ salt–alkali tolerance. Experimental results showed that the CARS feature extraction method could more effectively extract spectral features related to salt–alkali tolerance traits. The model combining CARS with KNN achieved the best performance, with a classification accuracy of 97.14% and a Kappa coefficient of 96.88%. The hyperspectral CARS-KNN classification model for salt–alkali-tolerant rice developed in this research provides technical support for rice breeding against salt–alkali stress and establishes a methodological basis for the precise discrimination of salt–alkali-tolerant cultivars in future research.

Title: Comparative Analysis of Automata-Based and Machine Learning Approaches for Postoperative Risk Prediction in Thoracic Surgery
Abstract: Lung cancer thoracic surgery is a particularly high-risk procedure in terms of both the occurrence of postoperative complications and mortality, which requires the implementation of decision-support systems that are correct, easily understood and interpreted. Conventional statistical and Machine Learning (ML) methods have been shown to be promising for predicting one-year survival using datasets such as the Thoracic Surgery Data in the UCI repository, which include preoperative variables such as age, comorbidities, pulmonary function tests, etc. Nevertheless, they are usually not accepted clinically as they are not transparent since they are black boxes. The automata theory, specifically Deterministic Finite Automata (DFA) and rule-based state machines, provides a complementary model of clinical pathways, with explicit state transitions and rule enforcement. The automata can perform powerful data validation, detect high-risk patterns, and perform real-time patient classification through deterministic traceability by directly encoding medical logic into transitions. This review comparatively focuses on automata-based methods and ML models and highlights the relative merits of their interpretability, computational efficiency, and adherence to protocols, versus their predictive accuracy and multi-signal combination. Moreover, it makes evident the opportunities for hybrid architectures with automata-driven capabilities to improve ML predictions, thereby balancing transparency and performance. Finally, automata integration into clinical decision support offers a way to reliable, explainable, and deployable risk prediction instruments in the field of thoracic surgery to aid in achieving better patient safety and improved surgeon decision-making.

Title: On Uncertainty-Aware ML-Based Systems: A Metrology Perspective
Abstract: Uncertainty quantification is a fundamental requirement for enhancing the reliability and safety of AI solutions, particularly in applications related to measurement instruments. This paper investigates the impact of data quality on both aleatoric and epistemic uncertainties. The study employs a methodology based on a simple regression problem involving a sinusoidal signal to evaluate how different uncertainty sources affect the network performance. To do so, aleatoric uncertainty is evaluated using Monte Carlo Simulation (MCS), while epistemic uncertainty is estimated via the Monte Carlo Dropout (MCD) technique. The experiments analyse model behaviour across three distinct areas, i.e, training, interpolation and extrapolation regions. The ML performance within each region is analysed as a function of the input uncertainty and other training parameters. This work serves as an initial effort to clarify, from a metrological perspective, the relationship between specific uncertainty sources and ML performance.

Title: VWA-TCN-ADELSTM for Furnace Temperature Prediction in Regenerative Aluminum Melting
Abstract: Accurate prediction of furnace temperature is essential for optimizing energy consumption and maintaining process stability in regenerative aluminum smelting. This study proposes a hybrid deep learning model, VWA-TCN-ADELSTM, that integrates Variable Weighting Attention (VWA) to adaptively assess feature importance, Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCN) to extract multi-scale temporal features, and an Adaptive Decay-Enhanced Long Short-Term Memory (ADELSTM) network to capture long-term dependencies while modeling dynamic temporal evolution. SCADA data collected from an industrial aluminum plant were preprocessed using normalization, feature selection, and Savitzky-Golay smoothing. Experimental results show that the proposed model consistently outperforms LSTM-based baselines and other hybrid architectures in terms of RMSE, MAE, MAPE, and R<sup>2</sup>. Diebold-Mariano tests further confirm that its superior predictive performance is statistically significant. These findings provide technical support for intelligent monitoring and predictive control in regenerative aluminum smelting.

Title: Incorporating Measurement Uncertainty into Uncertainty-Aware GANs: A Metrology-Driven Approach
Abstract: Artificial Intelligence techniques are increasingly adopted in instrumentation and measurement systems to support data-driven estimation, forecasting, and decision-making. Among these techniques, Uncertainty-aware Generative Adversarial Networks (UGANs) have recently emerged as a promising framework for probabilistic modeling, as they enable both sample generation and uncertainty estimation. However, existing UGAN formulations primarily address uncertainty arising from the learning process, while largely overlooking the uncertainty associated with measured data, which is a fundamental aspect of metrology. This paper introduces a metrology-aware uncertainty GAN (UGAN-M) that explicitly incorporates measurement uncertainty into the learning and inference processes. The proposed framework separates input-driven uncertainty, derived from classical Type A and Type B uncertainty evaluation, from model-driven uncertainty learned by the network. These two contributions are combined within a probabilistic loss formulation, enabling physically interpretable uncertainty decomposition and calibrated probabilistic predictions. The proposed approach is validated through a representative case study involving short-term forecasting of electrical grid voltage and frequency. Measurement uncertainty is estimated from instrument specifications and statistical analysis of the acquired data and injected into the network as time-varying input uncertainty. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed UGAN-M achieves well-calibrated prediction intervals and improved probabilistic performance compared to conventional UGAN approaches, while maintaining comparable point prediction accuracy.

Title: Cross-Domain Generalisation in Low-Resource ASR: A Multi-Corpus Investigation of Konkani Using Wav2Vec2 and Expanded Language Models
Abstract: Building ASR systems for Konkani is difficult because the available speech datasets are limited and differ considerably in speaking style, recording quality, and conversational usage. In this work, six Wav2Vec2-based systems are evaluated using individual datasets (Shrutilipi, Rasa, and IndicVoices\_R), pairwise merged training sets, and a combined three-dataset setup. Two character-level language models, a Base LM (56k sentences) and an Extended LM (167k sentences), are used to study the effect of textual priors during decoding. Results show that while single-dataset models perform well primarily in-domain, the merged three-dataset model consistently generalises better across diverse test conditions and achieves the more stable cross-domain performance with beam-search + Extended LM.. The merged systems handle spelling variation, conversational speech, and English-Konkani mixed utterances more effectively than several of the single-dataset models. Better decoding performance is also observed when larger text resources are used during language-model decoding.

Title: The preparation gap: IHL, human–machine teaming and assurance in military AI systems
Abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems are increasingly supporting targeting, intelligence analysis and operational planning across military domains, reshaping how commanders use force through human–machine teaming (HMT). HMT offers operational advantages, but risks such as automation bias, adversarial manipulation and degraded performance pose challenges for the ability of deployers to use AI systems in compliance with international humanitarian law (IHL). This article argues that adherence to IHL cannot be deferred until hostilities arise; system design, testing, governance and training must be structured in advance to establish the conditions under which AI-enabled human–machine teams can exercise appropriate human judgement consistent with IHL obligations. The paper proposes an HMT Assurance Card, a cross-disciplinary life-cycle instrument integrating IHL obligations, civilian harm pattern analysis and AI governance frameworks into measurable standards applicable across the AI system life cycle, defence institutions and coalition environments.

Title: Abnormal Sound Detection for Microfans Based on Persistence-Guided Interpolation Resampling
Abstract: Abnormal sound detection is a critical quality control task for ensuring the performance and reliability of microfans and is of great importance for identifying potential manufacturing defects and improving product quality. Traditional abnormal sound detection methods mainly rely on manual auditory inspection, which is inefficient and subjective. Moreover, existing machine learning-based methods exhibit limited detection performance under imbalanced class distributions. To address this problem, this paper proposes an abnormal sound detection method for microfans under class imbalance. First, the acoustic signals of microfans are preprocessed, and multidimensional abnormal sound features are extracted from the processed signals. To cope with the imbalanced class distribution, a persistence-based interpolation resampling strategy is introduced. Specifically, the persistence of minority-class samples in the feature space is calculated to characterize their structural stability under neighborhood relationships. The persistence values are then used as weighting constraints to guide interpolation between neighboring minority-class samples, thereby generating synthetic samples and enhancing the model's ability to recognize abnormal sound patterns. Finally, a classification model is constructed by optimizing the hyperparameters of a support vector machine using the particle swarm optimization algorithm. Experimental results on a self-collected microfan acoustic dataset and a public dataset demonstrate that, under imbalanced conditions, the proposed method can effectively detect abnormal sounds and achieves better classification performance than commonly used detection methods.

Title: A Hybrid Critical-Path and Load-Balance Scheduling Algorithm for Efficient Task-Parallel Execution on Multi-Core CPUs
Abstract: Task-parallel scheduling on multi-core CPUs is a fundamental problem in high-performance computing, directly governing the throughput of modern data-intensive workloads ranging from scientific simulations to large-scale machine learning pipelines. Despite decades of research, existing schedulers suffer from three persistent limitations: (1) pure critical-path heuristics such as HEFT achieve short makespan but produce severely skewed core loads under heterogeneous workloads; (2) greedy minimum-completion methods such as Min-Min incur prohibitive ON2P) scheduling overhead at scale; and (3) prior load-balancing schemes lack robustness when task weights are perturbed by runtime variation. To address these limitations, we propose CP-LB, a hybrid critical-path and load-balance scheduling framework that integrates three coupled components: (1) a parameterized DAG workload model that grounds scheduling decisions in Brent's theoretical bound; (2) a hybrid priority function that linearly combines upward rank and a dynamic load-balance factor through a tunable coefficient λ; and (3) a balance-aware core selection rule that jointly minimizes finish time and load deviation. Extensive experiments on deterministic DAG benchmarks with up to 2,000 tasks and 128 cores show that CP-LB matches HEFT in makespan (<1% gap) while reducing load imbalance by 74 %, load variance by 97 %, and median makespan deviation under perturbation to 0.4%.

Title: Ensemble-Based Uncertainty Estimation for Deep-Learning Measurement Systems in Vision Applications
Abstract: Deep-learning-based vision systems are increasingly employed as measuring instruments, for example to estimate dimensional or positional quantities from images. However, such systems are typically characterized by the absence of explicit quantification of the uncertainty associated with each individual measurement. This paper presents a practical framework to treat a deep neural network as a measuring device and to estimate its uncertainty using an ensemble of object detectors. Concretely, an ensemble of ten nominally identical YOLOv12s detectors is trained on the same microscopy dataset, using the same architecture and hyperparameters but different random seeds. Each trained network is interpreted as a feasible realization of the associated measurement task. At inference time, all ensemble members are applied to the same image; their bounding boxes are clustered by Intersection-over-Union (IoU) and class label, so that each physical object is associated with a cloud of bounding boxes provided by different models. The mean bounding box of the cloud is interpreted as the measurement result, while the dispersion of the cloud provides a per-object uncertainty estimate in the image domain. A simple scalar calibration factor obtained from the microscope allows these quantities to be directly expressed in physical units. The proposed approach requires no modification of the network architecture or loss function and can be described in the language of measurement science: the bounding box is measured as the average of repeated "readings", and the spread of those readings quantifies the uncertainty.

Title: Latency-Aware Hardware-Software Co-Design of an ARM-NPU Heterogeneous Edge Architecture for Real-Time Neural Speech Intelligence
Abstract: The proliferation of voice-enabled intelligent systems has created unprecedented demands for real-time neural speech processing at the network edge. This paper presents a latency-aware hardware-software co-design methodology for ARM-NPU heterogeneous edge architectures targeting real-time neural speech recognition applications. The proposed framework addresses the fundamental challenge of orchestrating computationally intensive transformer-based speech models across heterogeneous processing elements while meeting stringent latency constraints inherent to conversational AI systems. We introduce a novel latency prediction model that characterizes the execution behavior of speech neural networks across ARM Cortex CPU cores and dedicated neural processing units (NPUs), enabling intelligent workload partitioning and scheduling. The co-design methodology encompasses three complementary optimization layers: (1) architecture-aware neural network transformation that adapts speech models to heterogeneous execution patterns, (2) a dynamic scheduling framework that minimizes end-to-end latency through predictive task allocation, and (3) memory hierarchy optimization that reduces data movement overhead between processing elements. Experimental evaluation on representative edge platforms demonstrates that the proposed approach achieves a 62.7% reduction in end-to-end speech recognition latency compared to baseline implementations, while maintaining recognition accuracy within 1.2% of the original model performance. The framework enables real-time speech processing with median latencies below 80 milliseconds for streaming automatic speech recognition, satisfying the requirements of interactive voice assistant applications.

Title: GT-Conformer: A Speech Enhancement Method Integrating Multi-Scale Features and Frequency-Adaptive Attention
Abstract: Speech enhancement is a crucial task in speech signal processing, with significant applications in speech communication and recognition. To address the trade-off between model complexity and performance in existing deep learningbased methods, this paper proposes a lightweight network based on Conformer and frequency-dependent dual-path attention. Specifically, Conformer enhances modeling of local and global dependencies, MSFF boosts feature fusion across spectral bands, and FDDPA refines attention to frequency-specific noise patterns. These are integrated by replacing the G-DPRNN in traditional GTCRN. Experiments show the model outperforms the original GTCRN in PESQ and STOI metrics, with only 30K parameters, making it suitable for real-time deployment.

Title: An NLP-Based Framework for Analyzing Online Reviews to Assess Service Quality in Local Small and Medium Food and Service Businesses
Abstract: Online customer reviews provide rich source of service quality insights, yet researchers in the Philippine context still rely mainly on survey-based SERVQUAL instruments to assess service quality. Only few studies have used NLP-based sentiment analysis to convert online review text into validated SERVQUAL dimension insights. To address this gap, this study developed a review analysis pipeline for service quality assessment in local small and medium food and service business in Northern Luzon using online reviews from Google Maps, Facebook Pages, and TripAdvisor. The study analyzed 3,754 segmented review texts, classified them as positive, neutral or negative, and mapped them into SERVQUAL dimensions: Reliability, Assurance, Tangibles, Empathy, Responsiveness, using transformer-based models for Taglish text analysis. The study benchmarked fine-tuned mBERT-base and XLM-RoBERTa-base models across epochs, batch sizes and learning rates. The results showed that mBERT-base achieved the best performance in sentiment classification, while XLM-RoBERTa-base performed best in SERVQUAL mapping as this study focuses on training performance. The analysis found that most review segments were neutral and that Reliability appeared as the most frequent SERVQUAL dimension. These findings are converted into interpretable location-level to business-level insight through a validated dashboard.

Title: Artificial intelligence-powered surgical scene analysis in minimally invasive adrenal surgery: integrated recognition of anatomy, tools and phases
Abstract: Background: This retrospective feasibility study aimed to develop an artificial intelligence–powered surgical model capable of recognizing key anatomical structures, tools, and surgical phases during minimally invasive adrenal surgery, and to assess its clinical applicability. The system has potential to enhance procedural safety and support training for adrenal operations, which are performed relatively infrequently. Methods: Video recordings from 20 laparoscopic transabdominal adrenalectomies (10 from each side; 2011–2025) were retrospectively analyzed. Surgical frames were annotated for tools, actions, anatomy, and surgical phases to build the dataset. A ResNet-50–based multi-head cross-attention network with dedicated heads for tools, actions, targets, and phases was developed. Laterality was incorporated through feature-wise linear modulation, and class imbalance was handled using weighted loss. Performance was assessed on a balanced test set using top-accuracy and mean average precision with 5-fold cross-validation. Results: A total of 10,747 frames were labeled with 53,152 annotations across 9 tool categories, 7 surgical actions, 13 anatomical targets, and 6 phases. The model achieved top-1 accuracies of 67.6% for tools, 86.2% for actions, 70.0% for targets, and 60.3% for phases. Top-3 accuracies increased to 93.8%, 94.2%, 90.9%, and 95.3%, respectively. Mean average precision values were 64.2% for tools, 62.4% for actions, 46.8% for targets, and 66.4% for phases. Conclusion: The developed model demonstrated the feasibility of recognizing surgical instruments, actions, and key anatomical structures in adrenal surgery. These results may represent an initial step toward future systems capable of automated surgical scene analysis in minimally invasive adrenalectomy.

Title: Preliminary Development of an Artificial Intelligence-Based Measurement System for Automated Feed Monitoring and Feed Weight Estimation
Abstract: This paper presents the preliminary development and experimental validation of an artificial intelligence-based measurement system for automated feed monitoring and direct feed weight estimation in the context of Precision Livestock Farming. The proposed approach relies exclusively on RGB imaging and supervised deep learning techniques to estimate feed mass, deliberately avoiding explicit three-dimensional geometric reconstruction or density-based calibration procedures typically adopted in existing solutions. A single-stage object detection and classification framework is employed to jointly localize the feed heap and infer its weight class in a single forward pass. The model is trained on a large, carefully annotated dataset covering a wide range of feed weights, with controlled quantization and extensive variability in illumination conditions and feed arrangement, in order to enhance robustness and generalization capability.Experimental results show excellent detection performance and a strong correlation between predicted and reference weights, with most estimation errors confined to adjacent quantized classes. Beyond conventional computer vision metrics, the proposed system is explicitly treated as a measurement instrument. A metrological characterization is therefore performed, including calibration for gain and offset correction and a quantitative evaluation of measurement uncertainty following ISO GUM principles [1]. The results demonstrate a near-unitary calibrated response and an expanded uncertainty compatible with the requirements of feed intake monitoring applications.Compared to camera-based 3D systems, the proposed RGB-only solution significantly reduces hardware complexity, computational burden, and deployment constraints, while maintaining high accuracy and repeatability. These features make the system particularly suitable for large-scale farm deployment and for integration within multimodal sensing platforms aimed at improving feed efficiency assessment and sustainability in livestock production systems.

Title: Deep Learning -Based Cross-Language Synthetic Voice Detection Using Audio Preprocessing with Acoustic Feature Extraction for Experimental Evaluation on Bangla with Indonesia Speech Datasets
Abstract: The task of detecting synthetic speech is to determine if the audio sample is real or synthetic. Thanks to recent developments in DN, synthetic voices are now very realistic with can be increasingly difficult to detect. While these technologies help facilitate some beneficial functions such as voice assistants with human-computer interactions, they can also carry risks of impersonation, fraud with misinformation. We introduce a framework for synthetic speech detection based on audio pre-processing with acoustic feature extraction in this paper, Noise removal, silence trimming with frequency filtering are all part of the pre-processing stage that improves audio quality. Thirty-eight audio characteristics are retrieved and provided, including pitch, energy, and spectral into a FNN for classification. The experimental findings show that the suggested model can achieve 99% accuracy for the Bangla dataset (in-domain) with 93% for the Indonesian dataset (cross-language). A performance decay is noted on cross-language testing, but the model shows good generalization. Future work will include testing of the system under noisy with real-world conditions with expansion to other languages with deployment environments.

Title: Integrating Smart Meter Data and Building Energy Modeling for Demand Response Management Using Deep Learning and Temporal Database Techniques
Abstract: This study presents an integrated residential electricity consumption forecasting method that enhances demand response (DR) management by combining anonymized smart meter data with building energy modeling (BEM) simulations. Minute-level smart meter measurements were collected over three years from 10 continuously occupied households in a community in Taiwan. Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models served as the baseline forecasting framework. To improve predictive performance, building physical characteristics, such as orientation, floor area, height, and window-to-wall ratio, together with local weather conditions were incorporated into standardized-occupancy BEM simulations to generate hourly energy-use profiles. Integrating these BEM-simulated data with measured smart meter records improved prediction accuracy for high-consumption periods by approximately 5-10% relative to the baseline LSTM framework. Beyond total household load, the smart meter data were used to identify the dominant high-power appliance type during each interval, enabling detection of events that met or exceeded a user-defined threshold. Temporal database operations, particularly coalescing, were applied to merge overlapping high-consumption episodes and pinpoint which households, appliances, and time windows exhibited the greatest community-level energy-saving potential. By extracting the earliest and latest time boundaries of these events, the framework supports targeted LSTM-based forecasting tailored to DR applications. The proposed approach provides actionable insights for DR program design, including optimal load-curtailment periods, appliance-specific intervention strategies, and coordinated energy management across households. While the results demonstrate the method's practical value for utilities and aggregators seeking to implement residential DR programs and enhance grid flexibility services, the current study represents a proof-of-concept validation; wider deployment would require further evaluation at scale before operational implementation.

Title: Robust Spectroscopic Analysis Through Image-Based Spectral Representation and Deep Learning Techniques
Abstract: Variability in instrument calibration, both between different devices and over time, remains a significant obstacle to Raman spectroscopy. Even minor shifts in wavenumber can substantially reduce classification accuracy. Traditional spectral models struggle to remain robust under such conditions, particularly due to the one-dimensional (1D) nature of spectral inputs and the absence of pretrained deep learning architectures for Raman spectra. In this study, we systematically investigate the robustness of a previously introduced spider plot–based spectral representation specifically with respect to wavenumber calibration drift in test data. In this approach, each Raman spectrum is converted into a radial spider plot in which the angle of each sector represents the wavenumber, and the color indicates the normalized intensity, enabling the use of powerful image-based deep learning models. We employed EfficientNetB7, a pretrained convolutional neural network (CNN), to classify transformed spectra. Using a dataset of 5420 spectra from six bacterial species, we introduced synthetic wavenumber shifts of ±9 cm<sup>−1</sup> to simulate realistic calibration drift in the test data. The traditional method, which combined principal component analysis with linear discriminant analysis (PCA-LDA), showed a significant drop in balanced accuracy from 0.90 to 0.77 when shifts were present. By contrast, our spider plot–based approach retained strong performance, achieving balanced accuracy scores of 0.88 without shifts and 0.83 with shifts. Although no spectral augmentation was done in the training of either classification workflow, we attribute this robustness to the rotational consistency of spider plots under spectral shift and the tolerance to image rotation in CNNs, which are pretrained on large, augmented image datasets. Our findings demonstrate the advantage of using image-based methods to mitigate the effects of calibration variability in Raman spectroscopy.

Title: An End-to-End Deep Learning Frame work for Hair and Scalp Disease Detection with Pixel-Level Localization
Abstract: The evaluation of timely hair and scalp disorder screening is challenging due to a need for experienced clinicians to visually inspect images, and/or perform invasive testing and examination. This manuscript outlines an end-to-end deep learning-based approach that can classify and localize the region of infection on scalp images. The proposed method utilizes a three network based-pipeline; a pre-trained AlexNet for rapid feature extraction and initial disease identification, a pre-trained NASNet for accurate multi-class disease classification, and a pre-trained Unet for segmentation and visualization of infected regions. The input images undergo standardization processes including resizing, noise reduction, normalization, enhancement of contrast and data augmentation to provide improved robustness to lighting variability and background clutter. A fully integrated and scalable version of this pipeline has been developed into a user-friendly web application using the Django platform to enable real-time clinical screening and interpretation. Experimental results on a large scale dataset of scalp images that have been annotated (alopecia, dandruff, folliculitis, psoriasis and normal scalp) achieved an average accuracy rate of 99.75%, with a macro and weighted precision, recall and F1-score averaging approximately 99.75%. The confusion matrix showed almost no misclassifications took place, and the one vs rest ROC curve analysis reported an area under the curve of 1.000 for each of the five classes. The results of these experiments demonstrate that the integration of complementary convolutional neural network backbones with segmentation improves both the diagnostic performance and interpretability of hair and scalp diseases assessed without invasive testing or examination. Furthermore, to increase transparency, the segmented masks are over layed on the original image, and the predicted label and confidence scores are displayed in conjunction with the masked images. Additionally, the modular design enables the ability to extend the model to new classes and larger datasets.

Title: A Hybrid CNN-BiLSTM Architecture for Emotion Recognition from Audio-Visual Inputs
Abstract: Emotion recognition is contributing significantly to improving Human-computer interaction and systems’ capabilities of interpreting the emotional state of the users. This paper introduces a multimodal deep learning architecture to simultaneously consider the influence of facial expressions and the prosody of speech signals for basic emotion classification using six emotion categories: Angry, Disgust, Fear, Happy, Sad, and Surprise. We use Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) for facial feature analysis for CK+ dataset, and employ Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) networks for the temporal sequence processing for speech based RAVDESS dataset. In order to alleviate the data imbalance and enhance the generalization ability of the model, multiple augmentation methods are adopted in two datasets. The features extracted from both modalities are then concatenated and fed into a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) for classification. Results report on the proposed multimodal model that outperforms unimodal models with that of 98.09% accuracy, in contrast to 94.36% for the facial emotion recognition and 87.84% for the speech emotion recognition model. These results verify the efficiency of multimodal fusion to boost emotion recognition performance under different conditions.
