Title: A Machine Learning-Based Calibration Method for a Wind-Speed Measurement Unit in Power-Grid Meteorological Devices
Abstract: The wind-speed measurement unit of power-grid meteorological devices plays an important role in power system operation monitoring and extreme-weather risk assessment. However, due to structural flow disturbance and varying operating conditions, the raw wind-speed measurements often exhibit systematic bias, making high-accuracy and deployment-ready calibration modeling necessary. This paper proposes a wind-speed calibration method based on a "physics baseline and residual learning". A power-law model is first adopted as the physics baseline to anchor the overall trend. Then, nonlinear bias is compensated via residual learning, where the Reynolds number is introduced as a representative physical feature to characterize operating-condition differences. An ensemble strategy is further employed to improve prediction stability. Comparative experiments are conducted using wind-tunnel calibration data. Under five repeated random 8:2 train/test splits, the proposed method achieves a test-set "RMSE of 0.1220 m/s (std 0.0115 m/s)"and "MAE of 0.0761 m/s (std 0.0021 m/s)", significantly outperforming the physics-only power-law baseline. Moreover, the empirical CDF of absolute error shows "P90 = 0.1459 m/s"and "P95 = 0.1868 m/s", confirming stable accuracy for the majority of samples. Additional analyses under different wind-speed ranges and repeated random splits further verify the robustness of the proposed method.The results demonstrate that the proposed approach effectively compensates nonlinear bias while preserving physically consistent trends, providing a practical solution for engineering deployment of wind-speed calibration in power-grid meteorological devices.

Title: Hybrid Machine Learning Approach for Real-Time Fault and Energy Theft Detection in Smart Energy Meters
Abstract: This study proposes hybrid solution that combines supervised learning classifiers, anomaly detection and signal processing feature extraction in order to determine both faults in electric meters and whether they are being tampered with. We are able to come to a conclusion using a generator-based approach, ensemble includes boosted (loss based) decision trees and non-supervised clustering techniques to decrease false-positives from a non-compliant device and obtain low latency performance appropriate for deployment at a site. The solution exploits streamed meter data and engineered features in both the time and frequency domains and uses adaptive threshold systems derived from previous load profiles. Testing against both simulated and actual datasets showed a very high degree of accuracy in detecting the fault event, low (how quickly) latency in finding when the meter fault occurred and resilient to adversarial attacks. Improvements compared to baseline detection methods demonstrate very large increases in both detection and fault isolation rates. The design was created so that there is room to grow, maintain privacy of the meters' users and comply with smart grid communication standards making it possible for utility firms to detect integrity issues and take action to minimize customer disruption and costs.

Title: Image2Biomass: Multi-Target Biomass Regression from Pasture Images with Pretrained ConvNeXt
Abstract: Accurate biomass estimation is important for pasture monitoring, grazing management, and sustainable agricultural decision-making. This paper presents an RGBonly deep learning baseline for the CSIRO Image2Biomass task, formulated as a five-target regression problem over Dry_Green_g, Dry_Dead_g, Dry_Clover_g, GDM_g, and Dry_Total_g. The proposed method employs a pretrained ConvNeXt-Tiny backbone with a lightweight multi-output regression head and is evaluated using leakage-aware 5-fold GroupKFold cross-validation with image-level grouping. On the original target scale, global weighted R<sup>2</sup> is used as the primary evaluation metric, and the model achieves a mean score of 0.5457 ± 0.0307, with a 95% bootstrap confidence interval of [0.5179,0.5687]. Out-of-fold analysis shows strongest performance on Dry_Green_g (R<sup>2</sup>=0.5990), GDM_g (R<sup>2</sup>=0.5645), and Dry_Total_g (R<sup>2</sup>=0.5597), while Dry_Dead_g and Dry_Clover_g remain more challenging. These findings indicate that a carefully designed RGB-only pipeline provides a reliable and reproducible benchmark for multi-target pasture biomass estimation, while also highlighting clear opportunities for improvement through stronger benchmarking, target-aware objectives, and multimodal extensions.

Title: Laryngeal Disease Detection Using Machine Learning
Abstract: Voice disorders are frequently underdiagnosed due to the subjective and resource-intensive nature of traditional clinical assessments. This work proposes a non-invasive, machine learning based system for early detection and classification of voice pathologies, which is particularly beneficial in settings where access to specialized clinical expertise is limited and vocal health is critical for daily communication and professional use. Using the Saarbrücken Voice Database (SVD), a two-step classification framework is designed hat first performs healthy versus pathological voice detection and then conducts multi-class classification across six clinically significant pathology categories. Audio preprocessing involves FFmpeg-based conversion and extraction of MFCCs, spectral features, jitter, shimmer, pitch, and formants. The evaluation covered several architectures, spanning classic models like Random Forest and LightGBM alongside neural network frameworks such as BiLSTM, 1D and 2D CNNs, LSTM, and hybrid CNN+LSTM setups. Results demonstrate that LightGBM achieves the best performance in binary classification, while the fine-tuned CNN+LSTM hybrid model provides superior multi-class accuracy. This pipeline lays the foundation for a realtime AI-assisted diagnostic tool for scalable clinical deployment.

Title: Scattering Imaging of Large Field-of-View Polarization Metasurfaces Integrated System (Invited)
Abstract: Objective Polarization, as a key degree of freedom of the optical field, preserves structural information that is often lost in traditional intensity imaging, particularly in strongly scattering environments. It plays a critical role in biomedical diagnosis and complex-scene perception. However, conventional scattering polarization imaging systems are typically bulky, employ complex optical paths, and rely on sequential acquisition, resulting in low efficiency and limited real-time capability. In recent years, metasurfaces composed of micro-nano structures offer a new pathway toward compact, high-efficiency, real-time polarization imaging. Nevertheless, existing lens-type metasurface polarization imagers generally adopt small-diameter and short-focal-length designs, which still require external objective lenses for image magnification and thus cannot be directly integrated with image sensors. Moreover, the small separation angles of the six polarization sub-images lead to channel crosstalk for large targets and under strong scattering conditions, which restricts the achievable field of view (FOV). Therefore, developing a large-FOV, integrated metasurface-based polarization imaging system and investigating its performance in scattering environments are essential to overcome the limitations of current bulky and narrow-FOV designs. Methods This work proposes and designs a polarization-multiplexed metasurface with a diameter of 1.2mm and a focal length of 3mm, capable of simultaneously splitting and focusing three orthogonal polarization bases onto a single image plane. Six polarization channels can be captured in a single exposure, significantly enhancing the efficiency and real-time performance of full-Stokes parameter acquisition. Three metasurface samples with sub-image separation angles of 3°, 5°, and 7° are fabricated using an aperture-shared interleaved-strip configuration. An optimized aperture is introduced, and the metasurface is directly bonded to a CMOS sensor without any external objective lens, thereby constructing a compact polarization imaging system suitable for scattering environments. The polarization measurement errors, effective FOV, and imaging characteristics of the three metasurfaces are experimentally measured and compared. Building upon this, a polarization-driven scattering-imaging neural network is developed, incorporating physical polarization constraints, adversarial learning, multi-scale convolution, and channel-attention modules to evaluate the recovery capability of different sub-image separation angles under strong scattering conditions with a transport mean free path of approximately 12. Results and Discussions Calibration using 18 input polarization states demonstrates that all three metasurfaces achieve high-accuracy full-Stokes measurements. The mean absolute errors for the 3° design are M<inf>MAE</inf>(S<inf>1</inf>) = 2.417%, M<inf>MAE</inf>(S<inf>2</inf>) = 2.681%, and M<inf>MAE</inf>(S<inf>3</inf>) = 2.776%; for the 5° design, M<inf>MAE</inf>(S<inf>1</inf>) = 2.532%, M<inf>MAE</inf>(S<inf>2</inf>) = 1.978%, and M<inf>MAE</inf>(S<inf>3</inf>) = 2.781%; and for the 7° design, M<inf>MAE</inf>(S<inf>1</inf>) = 2.523%, M<inf>MAE</inf>(S<inf>2</inf>) = 2.681%, and M<inf>MAE</inf>(S<inf>3</inf>) = 2.961%. All measurement errors are below 3%, achieving high-precision full-Stokes polarization detection. Through aperture optimization, integration of all three metasurfaces with the CMOS sensor is successfully achieved. Characterization of the imaging performance after integration shows that the effective FOVs are 5.72° for the 3° metasurface, 10° for the 5° metasurface, and 14.25° for the 7° metasurface. As the separation angle increases, the spacing between sub-images enlarges, enabling the system to capture a large FOV simultaneously. The polarization-parameter images reveal material-specific information that cannot be observed in conventional intensity imaging. In real-object imaging, the degree of polarization (DOP) and angle of polarization (AOP) variations of polarized glasses across different channels reflect their filtering characteristics; plastic spoons exhibit local polarization changes due to stress-induced birefringence under polarized illumination; and multilayer transparent tape displays distinct layer-dependent features in circular polarization degree (DOCP) and AOP images despite minimal contrast in intensity images indicating that depolarization and phase-delay effects arising from multilayer interfaces can be effectively extracted. Overall, the 7° metasurface achieves high-fidelity polarization-parameter acquisition through an expanded FOV and enhanced channel independence. Under scattering conditions, all three metasurfaces are capable of recovering polarization information after scattering, but their performance varies significantly. Due to its small sub-image spacing, the 3° metasurface exhibits stronger inter-channel interference and insufficient channel separation, resulting in partial spatial overlap under scattering. This leads to a long-tailed distribution in the total mean absolute error (E<inf>MAE,total</inf>) and samples with a low peak signal-to-noise ratio (P<inf>PSNR,total</inf>). The 5° metasurface yields more uniform reconstruction results, with improved detail fidelity and polarization consistency, as reflected by a left-shifted E<inf>MAE,total</inf> distribution and an approximately 1 dB increase in P<inf>PSNR,total</inf>. Among the three metasurfaces, the 7° design demonstrates the best spatial decoupling and anti-interference performance. Its predicted images align most closely with the ground truth, achieving the smallest E<inf>MAE,total</inf> (0.0058) and the highest P<inf>PSNR,total</inf> (37.53 dB). Conclusions This work investigates large-FOV polarization metasurfaces for imaging and reconstruction under strong scattering and proposes a fully integrated full-Stokes polarization-multiplexed metasurface system directly coupled to a CMOS image sensor. Through an aperture-shared interleaved-strip design and optimized separation angle selection, three metasurface samples with separation angles of 3°, 5°, and 7° are fabricated and systematically evaluated via simulations and experiments to assess their performance in large-FOV polarization imaging under scattering conditions. Experimental results show that the 7° metasurface achieves an effective FOV of 14.25° with polarization measurement errors below 3%. For scattering imaging, the polarization-driven deep-learning reconstruction network enables high-fidelity restoration, yielding a total mean absolute error of 0.0058 and a total peak signal-to-noise ratio of 37.53 dB, demonstrating superior anti-interference capability and reconstruction stability. Increasing the polarization sub-image separation angle within a reasonable range effectively enhances polarization preservation under strong scattering and provides a new design strategy for developing highly integrated, large-FOV, and robust polarization imaging systems.

Title: Ensemble Learning Techniques for Sentiment Classification of Student Feedback in Multidisciplinary NEP Curricula
Abstract: The application of the National Education Policy (NEP) requires the application of effective analytical instruments to measure student-driven, multi-disciplinary curriculums. This article suggests a high-performance ensemble learning model of the sentiment classification of heterogeneous student feedback. In order to handle the linguistic diversity of multidisciplinary information, we apply a pipeline, including TF-IDF vectorization and an optimized preprocessing (tokenization, lemmatization and stop-wording). The fundamental architecture uses a multi-tier ensemble approach, which is the combination of Support Vector Machines (SVM), random forests (RF), and Naive Bayes (NB), which uses both majority voting and logistic regression-based stacking to address bias of individual classifiers. Empirical findings show that the suggested ensemble settings are far much better than the individual learners on the essential performance parameters, namely accuracy, precision, and F1-score. The study shows that ensemble techniques can be scaled to handle intricate educational data sets, which can offer evidence-based support to curriculum optimization to the NEP framework.

Title: Ground Water Modeling for Analysing the Water Level of Wells Before and After Monsoon
Abstract: Groundwater is essential for supporting agriculture, home supplies, and ecosystem stability, particularly in monsoon-dependent areas like India, where surface water availability is markedly seasonal. Notwithstanding its importance, precisely forecasting groundwater levels remains a formidable challenge due to the intrinsic nonlinearity, noise, and seasonal fluctuations of hydrological systems. Traditional statistics and machine learning models often fail to adequately capture these intricate temporal-spatial dynamics, leading to diminished predictive accuracy and incorrect management insights. This paper presents a novel hybrid forecasting framework, the Polar Fox-based Sequential Neural Network (PFbSNN), which combines the optimisation efficiency of the Polar Fox algorithm with the temporal learning capabilities of a sequential neural network. The model was trained and validated using a comprehensive dataset of 2196 groundwater observations collected from 10 districts in Telangana, India, for the period 2018–2020. The procedure encompassed methodical data preprocessing for noise attenuation, feature extraction to enhance input significance, and temporal modelling using PFbSNN to forecast groundwater levels for both pre- and post-monsoon periods. The performance evaluation demonstrated that the PFbSNN achieved remarkable prediction accuracy, as evidenced by an R<sup>2</sup> value of 0.99, a Root Mean Square Error of 0.18 m, and a Mean Absolute Error of 0.05 m, significantly exceeding those of traditional and independent neural network models. The model accurately captured seasonal variations and regional differences in groundwater dynamics, demonstrating its ability to manage intricate hydrological relationships. The findings underscore the PFbSNN model as a viable decision-support instrument for groundwater monitoring, resource management, and sustainable planning in semi-arid and monsoon-influenced environments. Future endeavours will focus on expanding the model to encompass broader spatio-temporal scales, integrating climatic and land-use predictors, and evaluating its transferability across various hydrogeological contexts.

Title: Investigation of Machine Learning Algorithms for Detecting Faults in Industrial Equipment Through Sound Analysis
Abstract: The study investigates the performance of two traditional machine learning algorithms, namely Random Forest and Multilayer Perceptron Neural Network, to detect and classify the acoustic anomalies of machine tools used in the industry. The MIMII dataset (Industrial Machinery Investigation and Inspection Malfunction), which contains recordings of a hydraulic pump working normally, was the source of the data for the research. The proposed approach entails audio file pre-processing, Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs) extraction with their temporal derivatives, and model training and evaluation. The Random Forest model attained 95% accuracy within 17 seconds of training, while the MLP was able to achieve 96 % accuracy, but at the cost of 620 seconds of training time. The comparative evaluation based on the metrics and ROC curves established that the neural network had a higher recall which was indicative of its committing fewer errors in the detection of anomalies. Even though Perceptron was a demanding model in terms of computation, it was still able to leverage its strong generalization ability. The implications of this study are that it has opened up areas for further research where MFCC-based acoustic analysis together with machine learning could be used for machine defect detection. This method is at the heart of predictive maintenance and industrial monitoring systems.

Title: Large-scale Multi-objective Optimization Method Based on Adaptive Evolutionary Learning Multi-Objective Optimizer Extreme Learning Machine
Abstract: Intelligent algorithms encounter severe challenges of high-dimensional decision-making and complex objective conflicts when dealing with large-scale multi-objective optimization problems. In order to effectively solve the problem of large-scale multi-objective optimization, a large-scale multi-objective optimization method based on Adaptive Evolutionary Learning Multi-objective Optimizer Extreme Learning Machine (AELMO-ELM) is constructed by combining the adaptive optimization characteristics of AELMO (Adaptive Evolutionary Learning Multi-objective Optimizer) and the efficient function approximation ability of ELM (Extreme Learning Machine). The mathematical form of the large-scale multi-objective function is set, and ELM is used to solve the optimal solution of the objective function. Then, AELMO is used to adaptively adjust the weights to finally determine the high-quality solution set of the large-scale multi-objective optimization problem. The experimental results show that under the same experimental environment, from the perspective of the change of IGD index, the IGD of the four methods decreases with the increase of the number of iterations. The highest IGD values of the comparison methods 1 to 3 are 0.8, 0.65, and 0. The large-scale multi-objective optimization method based on AELMO-ELM decreases rapidly throughout the whole process and reaches the lowest value; from the perspective of the hypervolume index, the hypervolume of the comparison methods 1 to 3 grows slowly and has a low value, which is much lower than the designed method. This method has good performance, can efficiently process large-scale data, find better solutions, and has practical application value, especially in the field of intelligent warehousing, which can assist in multi-objective collaborative decision-making scenarios such as warehouse resource allocation and inventory management optimization.

Title: Unrelated Parallel Machine Scheduling Based on an Enhanced Whale Optimization Algorithm
Abstract: In the context of intelligent manufacturing, the unrelated parallel machine scheduling problem (UPMSP) has become an NP-hard challenge due to machine heterogeneity, task dynamics, and multi-objective conflicts. Traditional algorithms face the bottlenecks of premature convergence and insufficient adaptability. To address this issue, this paper proposes an improved whale optimization algorithm (IWOA), which achieves efficient solution through a four-dimensional strategy optimization: a discrete continuous mapping mechanism is established based on random key encoding to convert job allocation into a machine preference value optimization problem; the initial population diversity is enhanced by combining Logistic chaotic mapping, and adaptive weights are introduced to dynamically balance global exploration and local exploitation; the Levy flight strategy is embedded to avoid local optima, and job swapping mutation is used to maintain population diversity. Theoretically, a hybrid integer programming model integrating machine preference encoding is constructed to break through the performance bottleneck of traditional meta-heuristic algorithms; applicationally, a scheduling optimization system supporting dynamic constraint expansion is developed, providing a core module for manufacturing decisions. Experiments show that IWOA improves the convergence speed by 15% in a 1000 × 100 scale scenario, reduces the maximum completion time by 2.4%, and is significantly superior to the standard algorithm. Future research will focus on distributed parallel acceleration, dynamic rescheduling based on deep reinforcement learning, and collaborative optimization with digital twins, promoting autonomous decision-making throughout the intelligent manufacturing chain.

Title: Nodes, glitches and embedded algorithms: COMACROB and posthuman organology
Abstract: In this article, Composing for Acoustic Robots (COMACROB) serves as a case study on the posthuman ontology of digital instruments. COMACROB is an instrumental system composed of live coding, AI-generated symbolic music and mechanically actuated acoustic instruments, such as the Yamaha Disklavier and MIDI pipe organ. The system challenges traditional distinctions between instrument, scoring and performance. The study borrows key notions from Thor Magnusson’s organology theory, presenting COMACROB as a layered system of inscriptions. It then attempts to delineate COMACROB’s speculative realism, drawing on Actor-Network Theory (ANT) and Object-Oriented Ontology (OOO) as two complementary theoretical frameworks. ANT is employed to present how agency in COMACROB is distributed across a network of translating actions between human and nonhuman agents, whereas OOO places the focus of inquiry on the autonomy and resistance of the objects that constitute the system. At the core of the study lies the notion that algorithmic processes are not external control agents, but intrinsic functions that co-constitute the identity of the instrument. The article overall posits that COMACROB is a case of posthuman model of musical organology, according to which digital instruments are participant agents in the process of music authorship.

Title: Hybrid ARIMA-LSTM Modeling for Bitcoin Price Forecasting Using Technical Indicators
Abstract: Accurate forecasting of Bitcoin prices remains a challenging task due to the high volatility, nonlinearity, and complex temporal dynamics of cryptocurrency markets. This paper proposes a hybrid ARIMA-LSTM modeling framework for Bitcoin price forecasting that integrates statistical timeseries analysis with deep learning techniques. The autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) model is employed to capture linear trends and temporal dependencies, while a long short-term memory (LSTM) network is used to learn nonlinear patterns inherent in historical price data. To further enhance predictive performance, a set of widely used technical indicators, including moving averages, Bollinger Bands, relative strength index (RSI), and moving average convergence divergence (MACD), is incorporated through feature engineering. A parallel hybrid strategy based on regression-weighted model fusion is adopted to combine ARIMA and LSTM predictions. Extensive experiments are conducted on daily Bitcoin price data across multiple market regimes, including stable and highly volatile periods. The results demonstrate that the proposed hybrid ARIMA-LSTM approach consistently outperforms standalone ARIMA and LSTM models in terms of forecasting accuracy, particularly when technical indicators are included.

Title: “MELMA” in otolaryngology: Medical evaluation of large language model answers. Clinician-rated scoring (MELMA-Q) and web-based auditing (MELMA-W) novel tools for AI assessment
Abstract: Purpose: To propose a novel, standardized, and safety-centered tool for Large Language Models (LLMs) evaluation. Methods: The Medical Evaluation of Large Language Model Answers Questionnaire (MELMA-Q) was developed as a 30-item clinician-rated instrument spanning seven domains: Medical Accuracy/Groundedness, Clinical Reasoning/Management, Safety/Ethics/Trustworthiness, Linguistic Quality/Semantic Fidelity, Understandability/Literacy Adaptation, Usefulness/Decision Support, and Performance/Answer Behavior. The MELMA Clinical Acceptability Framework (MELMA-CAF) is a two-tier system that incorporates a non-compensatory safety gate and weighted scoring. Five standardized otolaryngology scenarios were posed to three LLMs (ChatGPT 5.2, Gemini Flash 3, DeepSeek v3.2), generating 15 responses, which were independently scored by five blinded ENT specialists. A web-based implementation (MELMA-W) operationalized rubric-based scoring and was compared with clinician ratings. Results: All responses passed Tier A safety screening. Mean total MELMA-Q scores ranged from 72.4 to 85.6 across models; inter-rater reliability was excellent (ICC 0.89; 95% CI 0.84–0.93). MELMA-W validation using paired model × domain observations showed systematically higher clinician scores (bias of 0.804 Likert points). Conclusions: MELMA-Q and MELMA-W provide a structured, safety-centered pilot framework for evaluating LLM-generated medical responses in otolaryngology; however, broader validation across larger datasets, additional raters, and other clinical specialties remains required.

Title: Enhancing Sentiment Classification Accuracy in Myanmar YouTube Comments Using a Hybrid CNN-BiLSTM Attention Model
Abstract: Comments posted on YouTube have become a valuable source of opinion mining with the swift growth of user-generated content on social media. Even though SA has already made impressive feats with the English language, computational implementation of sentiment analysis tasks with low-resource languages, including Myanmar, is still difficult, as it has a complicated agglutinative morphology and no whitespace-delimiting characters. This study suggests a strong model of classifying sentiment polarities of Myanmar posts on YouTube in terms of positive and negative polarities. Our hypothesis is that a new architecture, the Hybrid CNN-BiLSTM with Attention Mechanism (HCB-AM), will be able to surmount the distinctive peculiarities of the Myanmar script.It employs CNNs to obtain local features on n-grams and BiLSTM networks to obtain the context of long texts. It has an attention mechanism, which its aim is to concentrate on important words and not noisy words. The paper performs research on a manually annotated dataset of 9,902 comments on viral Myanmar music videos. We have done extensive preprocessing, such as syllable-based segmentation and removal of stop-words to clean up the noisy text. We made comparisons on the proposed architecture and the standard deep learning models, which are RNN, GRU, and simple LSTM. It has been demonstrated through experiment that deep learning can be highly effective in the field, and the LSTM baseline reporting an accuracy of 97%. The suggested hybrid model increases the performance even further and provides a scaling method of sentiment analysis in under-resourced languages.

Title: Enhancing Speech Emotion Recognition with Wav2Vec 2.0: A Performance Analysis on TESS
Abstract: The technology of SER (Speech Emotion Recognition) makes it likely for machines to interpret feelings and emotions like a human encounter. Using the Wav2Vec2 transformer and deep learning, this research presents a technique. It is different from the traditional approaches as it does not rely on separate acoustic feature extraction but instead, it is based on self- supervised deep speech representations. The model was tested on the TESS dataset including seven emotional categories and achieved accuracy and constancy that surpassed the classical techniques. The results showed that transformer-based models can very well capture subtle emotional cues in speech through their strong potential for applications in affective computing, human computer interaction, and emotion aware systems. The consequences determine the effectiveness of transformer based self supervised representations for speech emotion recognition on a controlled benchmark dataset.

Title: Multimodal Big Data Fusion Algorithms in Music Emotion Recognition and Accurate Annotation
Abstract: With the rapid development of digital music and the popularization of multimodal content, accurate identification and annotation of musical emotions has become a crucial foundation for intelligent music recommendation, creative assistance, and emotion computing. However, existing emotion recognition methods mainly rely on single-modal features, such as audio or lyrics, which suffer from insufficient capture of emotional expression and inaccurate category and intensity annotation. To this end, this article introduces a multimodal big data fusion algorithm that integrates audio signals, lyrics text, and performance video features through temporal alignment, unified embedding spatial mapping, and attention fusion strategy. It combines multi-task joint loss optimization to predict emotional categories and intensities, and adds modal consistency constraints to improve the accuracy and robustness of emotional annotation. The experimental results show that under the mid-term attention fusion strategy, the accuracy of emotion categories reaches 0.86, the F1 score is 0.85, the mean square error of emotion intensity decreases to 0.049, and the Pearson correlation coefficient reaches 0.81, which is significantly better than the single modal method. Compared with single modal features (audio 0.78, lyrics 0.73, video 0.70), the fusion model showed an average improvement of about 12% in accuracy and an average decrease of about 0.025-0.026 in emotion intensity prediction error, verifying the effectiveness of multimodal fusion in improving emotion recognition accuracy and detail control.

Title: Computationally Efficient Deep Learning for Automated Intracranial Hemorrhage Detection in Emergency CT Scans
Abstract: Intracranial hemorrhage (ICH) is a life-threatening neurological disorder wherein prompt and accurate diagnosis is critical for patient prognosis. In everyday clinical practice, manually interpreting computed tomography (CT) scans takes a lot of time and can be different for different people, especially in busy emergency departments. This paper introduces an automated deep learning methodology for intracranial hemorrhage detection utilizing the EfficientNet-B0 architecture, which implements compound scaling to attain an effective equilibrium among network depth, width, and image resolution. The Brain CT Hemorrhage Dataset (Kaggle) [15], which comprises non-contrast head CT scans depicting realistic class distribution, is used for training and evaluation of the proposed system. Transfer learning is used and appropriate class weighting is used to address class imbalance. Experimental results show that the diagnostic performance is strong and consistent, as shown by high accuracy, reliable sensitivity and specificity, and an excellent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve. In terms of inference time, the EfficientNet-B0 model uses much less computing power with an inference time of ~45 ms/image delivering a comparable performance. Thus, it enables real-time deployment on standard clinical hardware. The performance of the proposed model is benchmarked against classical deep learning architectures, namely VGG-16 and ResNet-50, using multiple metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, specificity, F1 score, and AUC-ROC. The model also accurately identifies most hemorrhagic cases while keeping the number of false positives low, which shows that it can be used in real-life clinical settings. This study demonstrates that EfficientNet-B0 provides a well-balanced integration of diagnostic reliability and computational efficiency, positioning it as a promising instrument for emergency triage and implementation in resource-limited healthcare environments where swift ICH detection is essential. The future work will be a multi-class hemorrhage subtype classification and multi-institutional validation for broader clinical scalability.

Title: Exam Preparation in the Age of AI: Investigating University Students' Use of Artificial Intelligence Tools
Abstract: As Artificial Intelligence instruments continue to be increasingly incorporated into the education paradigm, we review their heretofore complex effects on the study methods of university students, especially in high stakes situations like final examinations. Overall, this research provides an in-depth analysis of how AI works, in particular how ChatGPT, adaptive learning environment and intelligent tutoring system affect ability of Academics determining from managing their study efficiency, motivation, understanding. The investigation is conducted through a quantitative methodologically rigorous survey that investigates the mechanisms by which AI tools enable exam preparation and how these mechanisms enable the AI tools to enhance personalized learning, optimize temporal management, and augment content retention. However, the results also highlight some serious problems: excessive dependence, a reduction in key analytical skills, and ethically challenging uses to which they may be put. Building on these findings, this study provides a set of pragmatic recommendations to educational institutions to specify frameworks for the responsible incorporation of AI technologies ensuring that such instruments contribute to an enriching, rather than hindering, educational experience.

Title: MambaFormer: A Lightweight Fault Diagnosis Framework with Bidirectional State Space Model and Enhanced Attention Mechanism
Abstract: Despite being crucial for maintaining high reliability of rotary machines, existing approaches have been unable to strike the right balance between computational efficiency and diagnostic accuracy. In this paper, we present MambaFormer, a light-weighted deep learning approach, which incorporates bidirectional state space modeling and multi-scale attention mechanism. The network architecture involves Simplified Mamba for efficient modeling of long-range interactions, SimAM block for increasing discriminative features without any trainable parameters, and light-weighted channel attention module. Evaluation of MambaFormer on the OU bearing dataset under diverse operating conditions revealed that the proposed approach reached 97.00% accuracy with merely 0.675 million parameters and 27.19 million FLOPs, outperforming such models as MCSwin-T, ResNet18, and CLFormer. Besides, the model demonstrates balanced performance for all fault types, obtaining a J-score equal to 3.22, suggesting its high quality of feature extraction. Thus, our approach provides a good trade-off between the computational complexity and performance, which makes MambaFormer applicable for practical fault diagnosis tasks in industry.

Title: Identification of Hate Speech in Kannada Through the Use of Deep Learning Technique
Abstract: The growth of regional-language content on digital platforms has amplified the demand for automated systems capable of detecting hate speech beyond just text [1]. This project introduces a comprehensive Kannada hate speech detection system that examines audio characteristics and written text to categorize speech as hateful or benign. Unprocessed audio undergoes automatic speech transcription and translation as necessary, enabling linguistic analysis in conjunction with acoustic feature extraction [2]. Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs) are extracted from each audio sample and fed into a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), while the translated text provides an additional semantic layer to guide classification decisions. The model shows strong performance on the training data but reduced accuracy on unseen samples, indicating overfitting due to a limited dataset and inconsistencies in speech transcription quality. Despite these challenges, the system successfully establishes a functional baseline that integrates audio and text cues, demonstrating the feasibility of automated Kannada hate-speech detection and laying the foundation for future improvements using larger datasets and more advanced speech models [3].

Title: A Composite Metric for Assessing Automated Testing Tool Effectiveness: Development and Validation of TCS
Abstract: Software testing is a very important stage of a Software Development Life Cycle. The increasing demand for a qualitative and affordable software testing tool has directed to the creation of variety of automated and AI-based testing approaches. A consistent technique to evaluate their overall performance has also become a mandate. This study proposes a composite metric called Tool Capability Score (TCS), to evaluates tool performance using seven essential characteristics: Automation Level, Integration Support, Execution Speed, Reporting and Analytics, Ease of Maintenance, Test Coverage and Scalability. Secondary data from previous research on software testing tools is used in this study. The data was analyzed through statistical and comparative methods to validate the proposed evaluation framework. Spearman's correlation was used for statistical validation of the calculated TCS values, which showed excellent agreement with expert ranks. The findings show that TCS minimizes subjective bias by offering a fair, data-driven method of comparing testing instruments. The Tool Effectiveness Index, Automation Capability Index, Testing Performance Efficiency, Testing Capability Maturity Score, Composite Evaluation Index, AI Testing Intelligence Quotient, and Efficiency-Adaptability Ratio are among the other metrics that are introduced in addition to TCS. With room for future development through additional dynamic performance indicators, the study provides a verified framework that aids researchers and organisations in choosing effective testing instruments.

Title: The Landscape of Disulfidptosis in Preeclampsia Reveals a Novel 5-Gene Diagnostic Signature via Machine Learning
Abstract: Purpose: Preeclampsia (PE), a pregnancy-specific pathological condition, has shown a growing incidence over recent decades. Disulfidptosis is a newly discovered mode of programmed cell death that differs from traditional cell death pathways in its molecular mechanisms. Numerous studies have reported the association between disulfidptosis and various diseases; however, the role of disulfidptosis in the pathogenesis of PE remains unknown. Patients and Methods: This study first analyzed the expression patterns of disulfidptosis-related genes (DRGs) using the GSE75010 dataset. Based on these results, unsupervised consensus clustering was conducted specifically on the PE samples included in this dataset. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis and machine learning algorithms were utilized to identify hub genes related to PE and disulfidptosis clusters. Ultimately, the expression profiles of these hub genes were validated using the independent datasets GSE4707, GSE30186, and GSE54618, as well as quantitative PCR (qPCR). Results: 9 DRGs showed abnormal expressions in the PE samples (P < 0.05). Subsequently, two disulfidptosis clusters were identified, each with its own unique functional pathway. Among the four algorithms examined, the support vector machine delivered the most dependable predictions (sensitivity = 0.889). In addition, the genes SASH1, CST6, CCBL1, FSTL3, and SPAG4 were determined as the central genes. A diagnostic model was established using these five genes, The high-fitting of the calibration curve and the positive net benefit of the broad threshold of the DCA decision curve demonstrate that this model has potential good clinical decision-making value. Meanwhile, the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis of the external validation dataset indicates that the predictive performance of this model is excellent (AUC =1), the qPCR validation demonstrated that the differences in expression of the five genes in the PE and non-PE controls (NC) samples were statistically significant (P < 0.05). However, the area under the curve (AUC) values of the external validation all being equal to 1 may indicate a problem of overfitting. The sample size verified by qPCR is relatively small, which has statistical limitations. Conclusion: This study proposes a new diagnostic model for PE, which can serve as a framework for studying disease heterogeneity and provides a basis for understanding the role of disulfidptosis in the occurrence of PE.

Title: A Machine Learning Approach for Predicting Term and Preterm Births Using Maternal Data
Abstract: Preterm birth or the birth before completion of a full gestation of 37 weeks continues to be a significant contributor to morbidity and mortality among the newborns across the globe. It has an impact on 11 percent of pregnancies worldwide. Early detection of pregnancies that are at risk of premature birth will help in carrying out the necessary measures in good time so that the newborn babies could have better outcomes. In order to solve this problem, we developed a machine learning model to classify term and preterm births using clinical data in the real world.We gathered and tabulated an elaborate set of information based on Electronic Health Records (EHRs). Some of the variables that we targeted include maternal health indicators, prenatal care details, sociodemographic background, and clinical factors that are region-specific. We have experimented with several classification algorithms and have discovered that the Random Forest classifier would be the most reliable to us. The model produced positive outcomes. The performance measurements were accuracy of 0.90, precision of 0.90 to term births, recall of 0.99 of term classification as well as F1-score of 0.95. These findings suggest that we can successfully categorize term and preterm births by defining them by the selected maternal characteristics. This provides medical practitioners with an effective instrument of risk detection and correction at an early stage.

Title: Asymmetric Hierarchical Fusion for Visual Grounding in SAR Images
Abstract: Visual grounding on synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery aims to localize objects described by natural language expressions. However, existing SAR grounding studies remain limited to single-category scenarios and lack relational descriptions, preventing models from generalizing to realistic multi-object scenes. To address this issue, we introduce SAAVG, a new multi-class SAR visual grounding dataset built from multiple high-resolution SAR detection sources and enriched with automatically generated and manually verified referring expressions. Building upon the LQVG framework, we propose an Asymmetric Hierarchical Fusion mechanism that deepens the Vision–Language Interaction pathway through iterative cross-modal refinement, motivated by the dominant role of this pathway in visual grounding performance. We examine two variants, Shared-Weight and Per-Scale, to characterize their behavior across SAR and optical domains. Experiments on DIOR-RSVG, SARVG1.0, and SAAVG show that the Shared-Weight variant achieves state-of-the-art results on SARVG1.0 (Pr@0.5 92.01%, mIoU 83.39%), while the Per-Scale design performs better in optical imagery, revealing modality-dependent fusion dynamics. The proposed dataset and findings establish a useful benchmark and offer valuable insights into hierarchical cross-modal interaction for SAR visual grounding. The dataset will be released upon publication at: https://github.com/duongb1/SAAVG.

Title: LLM-Based Stock Price and Volatility Prediction: A Multi-Modal Deep Learning Framework Integrating Financial News Sentiment and Technical Indicators
Abstract: Stock price prediction is the most enduring problem of financial engineering because financial markets are nonlinear, non-stationary, and informationally dense. Classical models based on historical price trends and fundamentals often miss the context of qualitative financial narratives. This paper proposes FinLLM-Predict, a new multimodal deep learning framework based on Large Language Models (LLMs) and quantitative financial signals for directional price forecasting and volatility estimation. In our architecture, we combine domain-specific LLMs tuned to semantic analysis of financial news, earnings transcripts, and technical indicators based on price series via a market-responsive dynamic cross-modal attention mechanism adjusting modality contributions. Hierarchical multitask learning predicts price direction, magnitude, and realized volatility simultaneously for coordinated optimization on related objectives. Experiments conducted over a six-year horizon on the S&P 500 index show that FinLLM-Predict achieves a 12.3% improvement in directional accuracy and an 18.7% reduction in volatility prediction error over state-of-the-art baselines, and is particularly robust in high-volatility regimes. Ablation studies show that each component is needed, and attention analyses indicate that textual signals become more informative during periods of market uncertainty, consistent with economic intuition. The interpretability, performance, and adaptability of the framework make it an interesting instrument for algorithmic trading and risk management.

Title: Integrated Multi-Disease Risk Assessment for Early Healthcare Intervention Using Explainable AI
Abstract: The non-communicable chronic diseases, including diabetes, cardiovascular diseases, hypertension, thyroid and liver diseases, contribute to the current 71 % of worldwide mortality as well as 41 million deaths each year. The invasive diagnostic tools affecting early diagnosis are still a barrier to early diagnosis due to the high cost of the tests (between 300 and 1000 dollars) and their inaccessibility in resource-strained environments. In this paper, the authors have developed a multi-disease prediction system based on the ensemble machine learning algorithms to approximate the risk of five major chronic diseases by using non-invasive lifestyle and demographic factors in parallel. One large sample of 10, 877 records of patients of five disease groups was gathered and preprocessed. To provide the opportunity to predict crossdisease, nine most pertinent features were chosen: age, body mass index, smoking status, physical activity, alcohol intake, sleep duration, stress level, and family history. Five advanced algorithms, i.e. there were Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM and Support Vector Machine were implemented and stringently tested. XGBoost has the greatest result with an average accuracy of 93.8 % among the diseases, 95.2 % among diabetes, 91.4 % among high blood pressure, 96.1 % among thyroid diseases, and 88.9 % among liver diseases with an overall AUC-ROC of 0.954. The SHAP analysis showed that the most useful predictors were BMI, age, and family history with a combined predictive power of 71.3. To assess risks of multiple diseases in real-time and explainable predictions, a web-based deployment platform was created. This non-invasive screening instrument is significantly more cost-effective compared to invasive diagnostic procedures thus has tremendous potential in early intervention in primary healthcare facilities, particularly to the underserved groups.

Title: Survey on Machine Learning and Deep Learning Techniques for Stutter Detection
Abstract: Automatic stuttering detection has become a major focus in speech technology, integrating advancements in signal processing, machine learning (ML), and deep learning (DL) for reliable fluency assessment. Stuttering and disfluencies such as repetitions, prolongations, and blocks affect speech intelligibility, while manual identification by speech language pathologists remains subjective and labor intensive. This survey analyzes current ML and DL based stutter detection methods, highlighting feature extraction approaches, datasets, model architectures, evaluation metrics, and research challenges. The review traces the shift from traditional ML classifiers to modern deep neural and multimodal models, noting limitations including data scarcity and poor cross domain generalization. Traditional ML relies on handcrafted acoustic and prosodic features, pitch, energy, spectral envelopes, and temporal cues paired with SVMs, HMMs, or GMMs, but these methods struggle with feature engineering and nonlinear speech patterns. DL based architectures such as CNNs, RNNs, LSTMs, and transformer models overcome these constraints by capturing complex disfluency characteristics and long range temporal dependencies, leading to significant improvements in automatic stutter detection performance.

Title: Tracking Instrument Handling During Laparoscopic Surgical Training Using Hand Landmarks
Abstract: While laparoscopy has revolutionised surgical procedures by enabling faster recovery and reduced trauma compared to open surgery, it has a steep learning curve, requiring much practice to master the stroke mechanics required for complicated procedures. Instrumented laparoscopic surgical trainers provide a safe environment for surgeons to hone their motor skills, enabling them to perform procedures with confidence, while capturing kinematic and video data from the instruments for performance assessment. Although hand grip is known to affect force control, precision, and most efficiency, most simulators lack sensors outside of the box and cannot capture subtle variations in instrument grip. Accurately detecting such variations would allow teachers to provide more informative guidance to trainees. Leveraging MediaPipe Hand Landmarker, we propose an unobtrusive vision-based hand pose sensing framework for detecting different laparoscopic instrument grip and handling techniques during training. By clustering finger-tracking landmarks from feature vectors detected during selected instrument movements, we demonstrate that we can accurately detect two common instrument grip positions as well as different modes of axial instrument rotation that kinematics sensors cannot distinguish. Experimental results obtained using a laparoscopic simulator demonstrate that the algorithm can differentiate tool hand grip changes and two different rotation strategies with 99% accuracy, across 5 subjects. Machine learning models can leverage this new capability to provide more precise guidance to trainees on instrument handling, something current training systems cannot achieve.

Title: An AI-Driven End-to-End Multimodal Architecture for Automatic Music Plagiarism Detection
Abstract: Musical plagiarism is debated daily in courts, industry, and academia, but most automatic approaches rely on a single type of audio or textual evidence, limiting their robustness and scalability. In this paper, we propose an end-to-end architecture for detecting substantial similarity based on a multichannel analysis that integrates three sources of information: voice, instrumental accompaniment, and lyrics. The lyrics are obtained through automatic transcription with Whisper, while the signal is separated into vocal and instrumental sources with Hybrid Demucs. Subsequently, both acoustic channels are identified with acoustic fingerprints extracted with SpectroMap. To compare them, we propose two normalized similarity measures: F-Matching Score (for audio) and T-Matching Score (for text). We validate the method with three well-known case studies in the media. The results show that the multimodal approach is capable of capturing patterns consistent with human perception and known legal outcomes, offering an objective support tool without replacing expert judgment.

Title: A Speech Measurement Component for a Serious Games-Based Patient Digital Twin
Abstract: Speech and audio signals provide non-invasive access to cognitive and motor aspects relevant to therapeutic assessment. This paper presents a speech-based measurement component integrated into a serious games-based patient digital twin (DT) for therapy. The component supports audio acquisition, preprocessing, and word-level speech classification via a remotely deployed machine learning service. As a use case, a convolutional neural network-based speech classifier is integrated into a production serious-game speech therapy application and evaluated across pediatric, adult, and large-scale public speech datasets. Experimental results highlight the impact of data quality, dataset scale, and population characteristics on classification performance under realistic acquisition conditions. Our solution demonstrates the feasibility of operationalizing speech as a realtime measurement modality within an interactive DT platform.

Title: Generative AI Is Unable to Detect Audio Deepfakes: An Empirical Investigation
Abstract: In recent years, advances in synthetic speech have raised growing concerns in areas such as cybersecurity, media authenticity, and digital identity authentication. This study evaluates whether large language models (LLMs), such as Mistral, DeepSeek, LLaMA, and Gemma, can detect audio deepfakes using only textual summaries of acoustic features. To evaluate this, we extracted two balanced subsets from the ASVspoof2019-LA and SceneFake datasets. Each subset contains 2,400 audio samples (1,200 bonafide and 1,200 spoofed), giving a total of 4,800 recordings used in the evaluation. For each sample, we extracted acoustic features using both Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs) and Wav2Vec2 embeddings, which were then transformed into textual prompts. To examine how prompt engineering influences model performance, we designed and tested multiple variations of prompts on each language model. The results show that certain prompt formulations enable the models to detect spoofed audio samples with perfect recall. However, the precision remained relatively low, depending on the prompt structure, suggesting that models are susceptible to false positives despite more descriptive prompts being provided. Our findings indicate that LLMs at present are incapable of detecting audio deepfakes without domain-specific tuning, highlighting the need to develop specialized models.

Title: Interpretable Diabetes Risk Prediction using SHAP-Guided Stacking Ensemble Model
Abstract: Diabetes is a significant health issue facing the world today and its early and precise identification is necessary to avoid serious complications. In this study, we present a SHAP-driven stacking ensemble predictive control framework of diabetes risk prediction, which combines the use of Random Forest, Extra Trees, and Logistic Regression as the base models with an XGBoost meta-learner. Borderline-SMOTE is implemented to overcome the issue of class imbalance, which guarantees strong training. The stacking ensemble has the best accuracy of 91.5%, compared to the best base model, Extra Trees (88.9%). SHAP (Shapley Additive exPlanations) interpretability identifies the most important clinical and demographic characteristics, and these offer understandable information about what the model does. The suggested methodology has good predictive capability and understandable outcomes, and it will provide a useful instrument to help medical workers make wise choices related to managing diabetes.

Title: Predicting Drinking Water Safety Using Gradient Boosting Algorithm
Abstract: Access to potable water is essential for public health, and precise forecasting of water safety has gained significance owing to escalating pollution levels. This research introduces a machine learning strategy for classifying the safety of drinking water using the Gradient Boosting algorithm. The model was trained using the Kaggle drinking-water dataset, including critical physicochemical parameters such pH, hardness, solids, conductivity, turbidity, sulphates, trihalomethanes, organic chemicals, and carcinogenic markers. The dataset was organized via an 80: 20 train-test division with balanced class sampling to ensure unbiased learning. The Gradient Boosting classifier exhibited exceptional performance, with an overall accuracy of 99.75%, which underscores its proficiency in differentiating between potable and non-potable water samples. The high accuracy demonstrates the algorithm's efficacy in collecting complex feature interactions and discerning minor patterns related to water quality. The suggested system offers a pragmatic and effective alternative for automated water quality evaluation, facilitating environmental monitoring and safeguarding public health. The results indicate that Gradient Boosting may function as a dependable instrument for the early identification of dangerous water and can be included in intelligent water control and decision-support technologies.

Title: Deepfake Voice Detection Using WavLM Feature Extraction and XGBoost Classification
Abstract: Modern text-to-speech (TTS) systems can produce very natural and human-like synthetic voices following the rapid development of generative speech technologies, i.e., deepfake audio. Although these technologies offer many useful applications, they pose serious challenges for security, privacy and reliability of digital communication. Therefore, detecting speech that has been generated artificially has become an important research problem. In this paper, we propose a hybrid deepfake voice detection framework based on pretrained WavLM model for informative speech representation extraction and XGBoost algorithm for classification. Input audio signals are first cleaned and normalized. Then deep acoustic and contextual features are extracted using WavLM embeddings. The embeddings encode important speech characteristics such as spectral patterns, prosody and speaker-specific information. The extracted features are then fed to the XGBoost classifier for classifying the speech as genuine or synthetic. Authentic speech recordings in English and Tamil were collected for experimental analysis and synthetic samples were generated using Google Text-to-Speech (gTTS). The proposed framework achieved the accuracy of 93.8%, which shows the effectiveness of the framework for differentiating AI-generated speech and real human voices.

Title: AI-Driven Psychoeducational Analytics for Early Detection of Academic Risk in Colombian Schools
Abstract: This article presents the development of an academic management model integrating artificial intelligence, aimed at the early prediction of school failure risk. The study employed scientifically validated psychometric instruments, from which multi-stage databases were constructed, incorporating variables related to reading comprehension, mental health, spelling, and mathematical performance. Regression and clustering algorithms were compared with traditional linear approaches, showing a substantial enhancement in predictive performance. The proposed model is designed to support institutional data-driven decision-making and to guide timely pedagogical interventions. The findings confirm the high potential of artificial intelligence as a tool to strengthen educational inclusion, optimize academic management processes, and improve school performance in public education contexts marked by socioeconomic vulnerability. Title: Generative AI and student learning performance in medical higher education: a social cognitive theory perspective
Abstract: Purpose – This study examines the impact of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) on medical students' learning performance in higher education. Drawing on Social Cognitive Theory, it investigates the mediating roles of technology self-efficacy, perceived learning outcomes, and cognitive engagement, as well as the moderating role of fairness and ethical perceptions in AI-supported learning environments. Methods – A cross-sectional quantitative design was employed, with data collected from 326 medical higher education students in Pakistan using validated survey instruments. Structural equation modeling (SEM) with SmartPLS 4.0 was applied to test direct, mediating, and moderating relationships among the study variables. Results – The findings reveal that GAI-based technologies (GAT) exert a significant positive direct effect on students' learning performance and indirect effects through technology self-efficacy, perceived learning outcomes, and cognitive engagement. Technology self-efficacy and cognitive engagement emerged as strong mediators, while perceived learning outcomes further supported academic motivation and achievement. Moderation analysis demonstrated that perceptions of fairness and ethics significantly strengthen the positive effects of these mediators on learning performance, underscoring the importance of ethically grounded AI implementation. Conclusion – The study provides empirical evidence that GAI can enhance learning performance in medical higher education when supported by strong self-efficacy, engagement, and positive learning perceptions. Importantly, ethical and fair AI practices amplify these benefits. The findings offer practical implications for educators and policymakers seeking to integrate generative AI responsibly and effectively into medical education.

Title: Accuracy, readability, and health information quality of AI chatbot responses for patient education on intermittent fasting in chronic kidney disease: a prospective structured evaluation
Abstract: Background – Intermittent fasting (IF) represents a dietary strategy with known metabolic benefits, however its safety and applicability in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) remains poorly understood. AI chatbots’ reliability for clinical and dietary guidance in clinically complex areas remains underexplored. No study has examined AI performance on IF in patients with CKD. This study evaluated the accuracy, consistency, readability, and quality of responses generated by ChatGPT-5 and Claude 4.5 Sonnet regarding IF in CKD. Methods – Twenty-five patient-centered questions spanning seven clinical domains were developed by two board-certified nephrologists and submitted independently to ChatGPT-5 and Claude 4.5 Sonnet twice per model. Prompts were submitted under standard and unmodified user conditions without customized system instructions to represent a zero-shot evaluation that is illustrative of typical patient use. Responses were evaluated for accuracy, consistency (comparatively between responses), and appropriateness by the evaluators. Response readability and quality were assessed using the Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level (FKGL) formula and the DISCERN instrument respectively. Results – Both ChatGPT-5 and Claude 4.5 Sonnet demonstrated identical accuracy scores during the first question prompts with notable improvement upon re-prompting after 24-hours. Both models demonstrated an identical internal consistency at 90%. ChatGPT-5 produced responses at the middle school level, better aligned with the US adult health literacy benchmark, while Claude 4.5 Sonnet generated responses at the high school level. DISCERN scoring was comparable between chatbots indicative of good response quality. Both chatbots had similar performance regarding individual subdomains. Conclusions – Both chatbots illustrated clinically accurate and cautious responses to questions regarding IF in CKD. ChatGPT-5 responses were better suited to the average health literacy of the general United States adult population. Despite our findings, we do not recommend either chatbot be used as the primary source for clinical counseling regarding IF in CKD. It is important for clinicians to help to guide patients toward evidence-based clinical information.

Title: Improving heavy metal prediction using hybrid feature selection and ensemble learning with multi-source remote sensing in Red River Delta mangroves, Vietnam
Abstract: Mangrove ecosystems play a critical role in supporting coastal aquaculture by providing essential ecosystem services and reducing HM exposure to adjacent aquatic environments. Despite their importance, mangroves have declined sharply worldwide due to conversion for aquaculture and urban development, leading to substantial HM release and transport from sediments into surrounding waters. Quantitative assessment of mangroves’ capacity to regulate heavy metals remains limited, as monitoring trace-level HM concentrations over large spatial scales is technically challenging. This study presents a novel and automated ensemble learning framework for large-scale prediction of arsenic (As) and lead (Pb) concentrations in mangrove soils using multisource Earth observation data. Optical Sentinel-2 (MSI) combined with C-band SAR (Sentinel-1), and L-band SAR (ALOS-2 PALSAR-2) data were integrated with field measurements from 101 soil cores to derive complementary spectral, vegetation and soil indices, textural, and backscatter features. Multiple machine learning models were trained and systematically optimized using stacking and five-fold cross-validation within the AutoGluon framework. The weighted Level-2 ensemble consistently outperformed seven Level-1 base learners, achieving high predictive accuracy for both metals (R<sup>2</sup> > 0.75). The hybrid genetic algorithm-particle swarm optimization (GA-PSO) approach for optimal feature selection further improved performance, increasing R<sup>2</sup> to 0.816 (As) and 0.886 (Pb), while reducing RMSE to 4.266 and 6.293 mg kg<sup>−1</sup>, respectively. The proposed workflow demonstrates the added value of multisensor data fusion, feature selection, and automated ensemble learning for mapping trace-level soil contaminants in complex coastal environments. This is the first systematic, large-scale assessment of heavy metal accumulation in Vietnamese mangroves that integrates optical and multi-frequency SAR data with advanced ensemble modelling. The framework is computationally efficient, scalable, and transferable, offering a practical solution for regional to national-scale environmental monitoring and ecological risk assessment from space.

Title: Parallel Deep Learning LSTM Models for Scalable Financial Market Prediction
Abstract: Financial predictive analytics has become a common instrument in market dynamics intelligence, decision-making grounded on data, and an optimized investment strategy. In this study, it is documented that a specially developed Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, that are able to cope with sensitive temporal dependences and fluctuating market dynamics successfully. With consideration of the computationally intensive nature because of large sets of financial data as well as the computationally intensive LSTM training process, we see our high-performance solution through the context of Parallel Computing frameworks as the basis for GPU acceleration. Towards these purposes, GPU T4 accelerators made available on environments such as Kaggle and Google Colab were utilized to bring about the optimum level of computationally effectiveness. The new strategy overlays GRU's increased ability to process sequential data onto the ability of GPUs to process in parallel, significantly increasing precision of prediction and training velocity. Experimental results verify the effectiveness of the strategy, which potentially can provide real-time financial market predictions without having high computational overhead. This study offers a detailed examination of design, deployment, as well as performance evaluation of a parallel computing-enhanced model, highlighting its effectiveness in enabling scalable and efficient stock price forecasting in real-world scenarios. The results shown here form a foundation for more research on next-generation predictive analytics solutions that will address the dynamic and data-driven nature of financial markets.

Title: An Ensemble Machine Learning Framework for Encrypted HTTPS Traffic Classification
Abstract: The swift proliferation of encrypted network communication has rendered conventional deep packet inspection (DPI) methodologies unsuitable for traffic identification and security surveillance. This study proposes an ensemble machine learning framework for classifying encrypted HTTPS data based on flow-based criteria that protect user privacy. The experimental dataset comprises statistical attributes, including packet size distribution, flow duration, and inter-arrival durations, gathered from actual backbone networks. We employ these attributes to sort network traffic into six application types: live video streaming, video player, music player, file upload, file download, and website browsing. We examine the performance of Support Vector Machine (SVM), Logistic Regression (LR), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Random Forest (RF), and XGBoost. To improve the accuracy and reliability of classification, an ensemble model is created that utilizes the best features of each individual learner. The ensemble method outperforms individual classifiers in recognizing encrypted HTTPS traffic patterns, as evidenced by experimental findings that demonstrate higher accuracy, precision, and F1-score. The suggested framework is a smart, scalable, and privacy-preserving way to analyse current network data. It makes it easier to optimise networks and find intrusions in encrypted settings.

Title: A Lightweight Phase-Aware U-Net for Single-Channel Speech Enhancement in Disaster Communication Systems
Abstract: This research introduces a phase-aware deep learning approach for single-channel speech denoising that concurrently estimates magnitude and phase information in the time-frequency domain. A lightweight convolutional U-Net predicts a soft spectral mask and a residual phase correction from the short-time Fourier transform (STFT) of speech that contains noise in it. We test the system on paired clean and noisy speech data at different signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) levels, from 0 to 40 dB. PESQ, STOI, SNR, and SI-SDR are some of the objective and perceptual measures used to measure performance. The experimental results reveal that the suggested methodology works well for both medium- and high-SNR circumstances, with high speech intelligibility and perceptual quality. Title: Digital Musical Instruments, Education, and AI: Towards Enhanced Learning and Creativity
Abstract: This article explores the transformative potential of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Digital Musical Instruments (DMIs), particularly Extended Digital Musical Instruments (EDMIs), within music education. It highlights how this technological convergence can revolutionize teaching methodologies and expand creative expression. Focusing on BehCreative, a notable EDMI designed for embodied and interactive musical experiences, the paper illustrates its potential for engaging students through kinesthetic interaction, drawing upon principles of embodied cognition and motor learning. The article delves into the unique capabilities of BehCreative, including its use of motion capture and Extended Reality (XR) for real-time sound generation, and its implications for therapeutic contexts. Furthermore, it examines the multifaceted role of AI in music education, from personalized learning and intelligent tutoring to enhancing creativity and providing objective performance assessments. The synergy between AI and DMIs is presented as a means to foster adaptive feedback, collaborative practice, and the development of accessible musical interfaces like the Adaptive Use Musical Instrument (AUMI). Finally, the article critically addresses the challenges and ethical considerations of integrating AI and DMIs in education, including issues of accessibility, algorithmic bias, originality, data privacy, and the evolving role of educators. It concludes by advocating for an interdisciplinary and human-centered approach to harness these innovations responsibly, aiming to cultivate creativity and universal access to musical learning for future generations. This article is intended as a position paper that outlines theoretical opportunities and research directions for integrating EDMI/AI into music education. It does not report extensive classroom-deployment studies; rather, it draws on pilot empirical evidence (neuroimaging and exploratory interaction studies) and the broader literature to motivate future educational trials.

Title: GIS and remote sensing-based hybrid AHP–machine learning framework for flood susceptibility and risk assessment in the Wolaita Zone, Southern Ethiopia
Abstract: Flooding is a major natural hazard with significant social, economic, and environmental impacts, particularly in data-scarce regions. This study applied GIS and remote sensing–based framework integrating multi-criteria decision analysis via the analytical hierarchy process with ensemble machine-learning models to assess flood susceptibility and risk in the Wolaita Zone. Eleven flood-conditioning factors, including elevation, slope, rainfall, distance to rivers, drainage density, TWI, LULC, NDVI, soil type, geology, and curvature, were first reclassified to a common scale. These factors were then weighted using AHP and used as inputs for both standalone AHP and hybrid machine-learning models. Spatial analysis using the three models shows that moderate flood susceptibility dominates most of the area, while high-susceptibility zones are concentrated in lowlands and along river corridors. Flood risk mapping indicates that approximately 60% of the study area is at moderate risk and 31% at high risk, with very low, low, and very high-risk areas covering minimal portions. The hybrid AHP–RF model demonstrated superior predictive capability, achieving an AUC value of 0.957. These findings demonstrate that the integration of expert-derived AHP weights with machine-learning models produces accurate, high-resolution flood susceptibility and risk maps, offering a robust framework for flood mitigation and land-use planning.

Title: Transfer Learning Driven Multi-Class Weather Recognition Using Deep Residual Networks
Abstract: The visual data is necessary to estimate the weather conditions with high precision to apply it in the case of intelligent transportation system, monitoring of disasters, environmental surveillance, and smart agriculture. The conventional weather forecasting methods are based on either numerical models or sensor based systems that might necessitate special infrastructure and computing resources. As the quality of image-based weather data has become more and more accessible, deep learning has become a highly valuable instrument in automated weather classification. This paper suggests a deep learning model of weather image classification, with multiple classes based on ResNet101. This model uses image net transfer learning to feature hierarchical visual features and adapts them to various weather conditions such as cloudy conditions, rainy conditions, shine conditions, foggy conditions, sunrise condition, and snow conditions. An extensive preprocessing pipeline that includes image resizing, image normalization, and data augmentation is used to improve and increase robustness and generalization. Empirical testing of the Kaggle Weather Image Dataset proves that the suggested model provides the overall classification performance of 96.2 percent, and macro-averaged precision, recall, and F1-score are high. The findings indicate that deep residual learning is effective in feature representation of complex environmental scene classification. The suggested framework provides a practical and efficient idea of a multi-class weather recognition systems in real-life scenarios.

Title: A Comparative Analysis of Chaotic and Stochastic Compressive Sensing Matrices for MFCC-Driven Audio Classification
Abstract: In audio classification, the increasing usage of audio data has resulted in users seeking a means to classify these audio files based on a high degree of accuracy while minimizing time within an efficient manner. This article will introduce the use of the integrate Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) and Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) approach as part of a complete framework. The integration of these techniques produces robust features, and by employing stochastic (Bernoulli, Gaussian) measurements and chaotic (Logistic Hénon Map) measurements for compressing these features across three ratios of 25%, 50%, and 75%. Classification results are performed using three classifiers: Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and XGBoost, and then these three classifiers were evaluated for each ratio of compression using the parameters of accuracy, precision, F1 score, and training time. Evaluation of the classification results showed that the XGBoost classifier demonstrated the highest results for accuracy, precision, and F1 score, with an improvement of approximately 3% - 5% in comparison to the RF classifier for accuracy at this time. While the RF classifier has the advantage of training more quickly, it has the drawback of experiencing degradation in performance as the compression rate increases. SVM is accurate but has the drawback of requiring over 2× the time to train in comparison to XGBoost. Chaotic measurement results made using the Logistic Hénon matrix compared favorably with the stochastic measurements, particularly at higher compression rates, demonstrating its potential as a viable means for the efficient and highly reliable method of audio classification. Our research serves as a research pipeline that combines chaotic measurement with advanced ensemble learning techniques for the rapid and reliable classification of audio files.
