Title: Cross-Dialect Arabic Audio Deepfake Detection via One-Class Learning and Outlier Exposure
Abstract: Recent advances in speech generation helped to create fake voices for beneficial uses including entertainment and education. Although this technology was originally made for helpful uses, nowadays it is misused for harmful purposes like voice impersonation, fraud, and online attacks. Detecting audio deepfakes in Arabic is difficult because the language has many different dialects, complex pronunciation patterns, and very limited labeled data for training detection models. In this paper, we present a deep learning framework for detecting Arabic audio deepfakes using one-class learning. The model leverages multilingual speech encoder such as WavLM with an OC-Softmax head to identify patterns in authentic Arabic speech. The model has been trained on real speech from the Casablanca dataset, which includes eight dialects and then evaluated on the Arabic Audio Deepfake and ArFake datasets to test its performance. The Leave-One-Dialect-Out (LODO) method tests the model's ability to generalize to new dialects it has not seen before. Our experiments demonstrate that simple one-class learning reaches 87% accuracy but incorrectly labels many fake samples as real. Adding 5 to 10% outlier exposure during the training process greatly enhances fake detection. Our top-performing setup in the last experiment (E6) achieves 78.3% accuracy, 99.8% precision, an equal error rate (EER) of 14.8%, and a ROC-AUC of 0.9262 on the ArFake dataset under in-distribution evaluation. However, performance drops notably under zero-shot conditions involving unseen synthesis methods and dialects, highlighting an ongoing generalization gap. Our findings show that robustness in detecting fake Arabic audio is achieved by training on multiple Arabic dialects and carefully injecting a controlled outlier exposure (OE) during training. This helps in improving the generalization to unseen dialects under LODO evaluation.

Title: AI-Based Detection of Synthetic Video and Audio Media
Abstract: Recent improvements in generative AI have made it possible to make very realistic fake media, which are often called "deepfakes."These changes put digital trust, identity verification, and information integrity at great danger. We present a multimodal deepfake detection system that examines both visual and aural signals. The system has two parts: a visual detector that uses the FaceForensics++ dataset to find artifacts that show that a face has been changed, and an audio detector that uses Mel-spectrogram representations from the ASVspoof 2019 dataset to find fake speech. A weighted decision-level fusion process controlled by a parameter α combines the outputs of the two branches. The video model achieved 85.7% validation accuracy, while the audio model achieved 86.9% accuracy. The proposed fusion approach improves overall detection performance to approximately 89.6%.. The system is also tested for robustness against both visual and auditory spoofing assaults utilizing ROC-AUC, Equal Error Rate (EER), and confusion matrix analysis in addition to accuracy. The findings validate that multimodal analysis enhances detection reliability relative to unimodal systems and provides a viable methodology for real-world media forensics applications.

Title: Detecting Audio Deepfakes in the Libyan Dialect: A Stacked Ensemble Approach Using MFCCs and Mel-Spectrogram CNNs
Abstract: Audio Deepfakes (AD) are highly realistic fake audio recordings created using AI-based tools that clone human voices. Recent advances in Text-To-Speech (TTS) and Voice Conversion (VC) technologies have made it easier to generate both synthetic and imitative speech. While these technologies were designed to improve people’s lives, they have also been misused by attackers, posing significant risks to public safety. Developing effective algorithms to distinguish fake audio from real audio is therefore critical. Various machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) techniques have been created to identify Deepfake audios. However, the reliance on massive training data or excessive pre-processing introduces significant methodological challenges. This paper proposes a hybrid framework for detecting AI-generated speech, integrating a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Dense Neural Network (DNN), and an optimized XGBoost classifier within a stacking ensemble. The framework leverages key audio features such as Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs) and their derivatives, along with the average STFT spectrum and Mel-Spectrogram, extracted from the audio recordings, which were collected from real Libyan dialect and generated as Deepfake audio clips using Retrieval-based Voice Conversion (RVC) and Tacotron model. Our dataset consists of three versions containing audio clips lasting three, five, and seven seconds. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed system achieves its highest performance with five-second segments, reaching an accuracy of 98.75%, while maintaining strong performance for other durations. These results highlight the benefits of combining DL and traditional ML techniques for robust audio forgery detection.

Title: Phase-Aware Deep Learning with Complex-Valued CNNs for Audio Signal Applications
Abstract: This study explores the design and application of Complex-Valued Convolutional Neural Networks (CVCNNs) in the domain of audio signal processing, with a focus on utilizing phase information often neglected in real-valued networks. Empirical evaluations are conducted across three stages. First, CVCNNs are benchmarked on standard image datasets (MNIST, KMNIST, FMNIST), where they demonstrate competitive performance with real-valued CNNs, even under synthetic perturbations. Although our focus is audio signal processing, we first evaluate CVCNNs on image datasets to establish baseline performance and validate training stability before applying them to audio tasks. In the second experiment, we focus on audio classification using Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs). CVCNNs trained on real-valued MFCCs slightly outperform real-valued CNNs; however, incorporating phase information into the input does not lead to measurable performance gains, highlighting the difficulty of exploiting phase information without phase-aware architectural design. Finally, a third experiment introduces Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to explicitly model phase information via edge weighting, where the inclusion of phase yields measurable gains in binary and multi-class genre classification, affirming its relevance when appropriately structured. These results underscore the expressive capacity of complex-valued architectures and confirm phase as a meaningful and exploitable feature in audio processing applications. Whereas current methods show promise, future advances in phase-aware design will be essential to leverage the potential of complex representations in neural networks.

Title: Meta-Learning for Few-Shot Spectroscopic Regression under Distribution Shifts in Smart Agriculture
Abstract: Deep learning has revolutionized spectroscopic analysis, providing powerful tools for sectors such as pharmaceuticals, food quality, and agriculture. However, the practical deployment of these models is often hindered by two critical challenges: the high cost of acquiring labeled samples and the performance degradation caused by distribution shifts across different instruments, regions, or harvest seasons. In this work, we investigate few-shot adaptation for spectroscopic regression as a model-updating problem. Using the Mango dataset as a benchmark, we conduct a systematic comparison between traditional Fine-tuning (FT) and representative meta-learning frameworks, including Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning (MAML), Prototypical Networks, and Simple Neural Attentive Meta-Learner (SNAIL).Our results show that knowledge transfer between measurement conditions is essential to achieve effective adaptation under label scarcity. Meta-learning provides the clearest advantages in the most relevant few-shot regimes: at 25-shot, MAML and especially Prototypical Networks outperform conventional FT, while also showing lower run-to-run variability under limited support sizes. Although FT remains a strong baseline - and becomes increasingly competitive as the support set grows - the overall results highlight meta-learning as a more reliable strategy for low-shot recalibration under realistic distribution shifts.

Title: An Intelligent Mobile Application for Real-Time Stress Detection and Customized Mitigation Techniques Using Wearable Physiological Data: A Preliminary Study
Abstract: Stress is a critical factor impacting human performance within transportation systems, often leading to cognitive fatigue, reduced situational awareness, and increased accident risks among operators and drivers. If unmanaged, chronic stress also results in serious health conditions such as hypertension and cardiovascular diseases. In the context of smart mobility, the early detection of stress is vital for maintaining both operator’s well-being and overall system safety. While wearable devices allow for the continuous collection of physiological signals, most existing detection and mitigation systems are overly complex and lack tailored intervention strategies for mobile environments. Hence, we propose an intelligent mobile app powered by machine learning models for real-time detection and management of stress using data obtained from wearable sensors. The proposed system classifies a subject as either stress or rest based on electrodermal activity (EDA) and skin temperature (TEMP) signals, using the XGBoost model trained on the open WESAD dataset. As soon as the subject is detected in a stress condition, the mobile application will trigger a personalized relaxation response comprising soothing music, motivational messages, or guided breathing exercises. In the experiments, the XGBoost model achieved an accuracy of 91.18 %, whereas the SVM model achieved an accuracy of 94.12%, demonstrating the strong capability of both models in distinguishing between stress and rest states. This study aimed to provide an initial exploration of the potential for integrating machine learning–based stress detection with wearable technologies, supported by personalized intervention methods. Feedback was collected from five users regarding the system’s ease of understanding and the effectiveness of the personalized interventions. The responses were positive and encouraging, supporting further development and enhancement of the system.

Title: CURA: Size Isn’t All You Need-A Compact Underlying Architecture for On-Device Intelligence
Abstract: Existing on-device AI architectures for resource-constrained environments face two critical limitations: they lack compactness, with parameter requirements scaling proportionally to task complexity, and they exhibit poor generalizability, performing effectively only on specific application domains (e.g., models designed for regression tasks cannot adapt to natural language processing (NLP) applications). In this paper, we propose CURA, an architecture inspired by analog audio signal processing circuit that provides a compact and lightweight solution for diverse machine learning tasks across multiple domains. Our architecture offers three key advantages over existing approaches: (1) Compactness: it requires significantly fewer parameters regardless of task complexity; (2) Generalizability: it adapts seamlessly across regression, classification, complex NLP and computer vision tasks; and (3) Complex pattern recognition: it can capture intricate data patterns while maintaining extremely low model complexity. We evaluated CURA across diverse datasets and domains. For compactness, it achieved equivalent accuracy using up to 2,500 times fewer parameters compared to baseline models. For generalizability, it demonstrated consistent performance across four NLP benchmarks and one computer vision dataset, nearly matching specialized existing models (achieving F1-scores up to 90%). Lastly, it delivers superior forecasting accuracy for complex patterns, achieving 1.6 times lower mean absolute error and 2.1 times lower mean squared error than competing models.

Title: Deep Learning-Powered VGGNet Framework for Efficient Diagnosis and Stage Assessment of Bladder Cancer
Abstract: Bladder cancer is among the most common malignancies in the global society and there is a need to detect it with accuracy and at an early stage to enhance the prognosis of the patient. In this paper, a VGGNet-based deep learning model is proposed to achieve dependable diagnosis and classification of bladder cancer into various stages with clinical parameters. The model was trained and tested on a curated dataset and it exploited the convolutional neural network structures to extract and learn discriminative features. To measure diagnostic efficiency, performance evaluation metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, specificity, and AUC were evaluated. The proposed model had a total accuracy of 96, precision of 95, recall of 97, F1-score of 96, specificity of 95 and AUC of 0.99, which exhibited good predictive power. The confusion matrix and the ROC curve also confirmed strong classification performance. These findings emphasize the possibility of VGGNet-based framework as a reliable diagnostic instrument, which would allow clinicians to obtain early diagnosis and accurate staging of bladder cancer to plan therapy better.

Title: Interpretable Machine Learning to Predict Anxiety or Depression in Acute Ischemic Stroke after IV Thrombolysis: A Retrospective Cohort Study
Abstract: Background: Acute Ischemic Stroke (AIS) represents a prevalent cerebrovascular condition characterized by significant levels of disability and mortality. This study aimed to develop and validate a Machine Learning (ML) model designed to predict the occurrence of anxiety or depression in AIS patients following Intravenous Thrombolysis (IVT). Methods: Participants from two centers included in CNSR between March 2019 and January 2024 were randomly allocated into a training set (70%) and a test set (30%). 5 ML models (DT, LR, RF, XGBoost, KNN) were constructed utilizing selected variables. Model performance was assessed through calibration curves, AUC, accuracy, and precision metrics. Results: A total of 1,711 participants were analyzed, with 467 diagnosed with anxiety or depression. The cohort was divided into a training set comprising 1,197 patients and a testing set of 514 patients. Among 56 clinical variables, 7 key features were identified based on SHAP values: lesional site, AST, BMI, ALB, age, Apo A1, and hemorrhagic complications. The RF model demonstrated superior overall performance, achieving an AUC of 0.841, accuracy of 0.808, and precision of 0.841 in the training set. Discussion: The RF prediction model developed in this study has the potential to estimate the risk of mood disorders post-IVT in AIS patients prior to treatment, thereby facilitating clearer communication and expedited clinical decision-making. Additionally, it underscores modifiable clinical factors that may enhance patient quality of life. However, the generalizability and efficacy of the model may be constrained by the characteristics of the sample population and the variable selection process. Conclusion: The RF model presented in this study may represent a valuable instrument for evaluating the risk of anxiety or depression in AIS patients following IVT within clinical practice.

Title: A Hybrid Group Method of Data Handling–Modified Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm-Local Outlier Factor for Short-Term Load Forecasting in Microgrids
Abstract: Precision tools are required because load forecasting is essential for power system planning and optimal performance. Data machine learning techniques and data mining methods are essential instruments for evaluating data and uncovering concealed information in data. In this study, a novel approach to estimating the grid-connected micro grid load is put forth. The group method of data handling (GMDH), on which the successful approach is based, was used to estimate the load using an adaptive learning network. Using the technique of modified particle swarm optimization (MPSO), the GMDH network was developed. The major goal of providing combination techniques is to concurrently leverage single-model benefits in structuring complex systems while also overcoming single-model constraints. The MPSO algorithm is used to improve GMDH polynomial coefficients. In this paper, GMDH-MPSO combines with the local outlier factor (LOF) to account for potential outliers. The outcomes compare favourably with those of standard GMDH, the autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) approach, and GMDH taught using PSO, demonstrating the GMDH-MPSO-LOF method's tolerable efficiency. The GMDH-MPSO-LOF model with a correlation coefficient (R) value of 0.9968, mean square error (MSE) value of 0.1156, and root mean square error (RMSE) value of 0.3532 is competitive with similar algorithms.

Title: AI-Based Instrumental Music Composition for Vocal Inputs
Abstract: This paper presents a lightweight system for transforming sung vocal melodies into instrumental performances using an efficient combination of deep learning and MIDI-based processing. The proposed pipeline is designed to operate reliably on standard consumer hardware without requiring GPU acceleration, making it suitable for resource-constrained environments. The method consists of three primary stages: confidence-aware melody extraction using an optimized configuration of the CREPE model, structured MIDI mapping with lightweight harmonic analysis for chord interpretation and instrument assignment, and real-time audio synthesis via high-quality SoundFont rendering. The system emphasizes low-latency processing, robust pitch detection, and musically coherent output, even for short or expressive vocal inputs. A browser-based interface provides piano-roll visualizations and harmonic overlays that support intuitive interaction and analysis. Experimental observations indicate that the proposed approach produces stable and interpretable melodic representations suitable for educational contexts, rapid prototyping, and early-stage music composition.

Title: Deep Learning-Based Speech Enhancement using Convolutional Encoder-Decoder Networks
Abstract: In modern telecommunication systems and hearing assistive devices, background noise significantly degrades speech quality along with decrease in intelligibility. Addressing this condition is critical, as cleaner audio is a prerequisite for robust performance in downstream applications such as Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) and voice-command interfaces. This paper presents a deep learning based approach for speech enhancement, specifically targeting single-channel noise reduction. The proposed system utilizes a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) based Encoder-Decoder architecture to map noisy speech spectrograms to their clean counterparts. The model is trained on a synthetic dataset generated by mixing clean speech with urban environmental noise at varying Signal-to-Noise Ratios (SNRs) ranging from -5 dB to 10 dB. The feature extraction relies on the Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT), and signal reconstruction is achieved using the Inverse STFT (ISTFT) with the phase information obtained from the noisy input. Evaluation of the system across a validation set of unseen audio samples confirms its robustness. The model successfully reconstructs speech signals even in high-noise scenarios (SNR of -5 dB), with comparative waveform analysis showing a marked reduction in amplitude during non-speech intervals. Experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed deep learning-based method in suppressing background noise and yet preserving speech intelligibility.

Title: Cultivation of Junior School Students' Interdisciplinary Competence Based on Smart Learning Companion
Abstract: Interdisciplinary competence has become the core driving force behind technological development and talent cultivation. Title: AI-Powered Deepfake Detection System for Audio and Video Integrity
Abstract: The methods for creating Deepfakes have improved a lot in recent years. As a result, highly realistic forgery of audio-video content is difficult to distinguish from authentic ones. To fix the issues above, this work proposes a multimodal deepfake detection framework that jointly considers visual representations and speech and lip-audio synchronization. Title: An IoT-Enabled Smart Electricity Meter Integrating Advanced Analytics and Voice-Based Mobile Interaction
Abstract: Modern smart grid networks require precise energy forecasts and monitoring. Real-time visualization, billing insights, and voice-based interaction using text-to-speech and speech-to-text technologies are all offered by a Flutter-based mobile application. Title: EmoSync: Bringing Music to Life with Emotionally Choreographed 3D Characters Using AI
Abstract: EmoSync converts the evolving emotion of a song into a live performance by a 3D character in virtual reality. A neural model predicts valence and arousal from a 260-dimensional audio descriptor set at 2 Hz. The predictions are mapped to 21 prototypical emotion zones that drive facial expressions, gesture selection, and animation intensity. Among four tested architectures, a deep feed-forward network achieved the lowest error on DEAM (MAE = 0.101 for arousal, 0.105 for valence) and is used in the system. Errors concentrate in adjacent sectors of the valence–arousal circumplex, which preserves perceived plausibility. The end-to-end pipeline runs with a one-time startup buffer of about three seconds and then updates avatar behavior at 0.5-second resolution. In a within-subjects study with 21 participants, ratings increased from audio-only to light-show to character-driven conditions, with the full EmoSync setting scoring highest (mean 8.2/10). The results indicate that emotion-aware character animation can enhance music listening in VR and provide a practical testbed for music-emotion models in interactive contexts.

Title: Augmented Violin: Real-Time Sound Transformation via Gesture Recognition

Title: Adaptive Rhythm Control Optimization via Multi-Source Keyboard Performance Data Fusion for Intelligent Music Production
Abstract: This paper proposes an adaptive rhythm control optimization framework based on multi-source keyboard performance data fusion. This framework primarily addresses the challenge of rhythm modeling in intelligent music generation relying on a single modality and failing to characterize the dynamic features of performance. The method first constructs a unified multi-source rhythm representation space, encoding the symbolic layer, acoustic layer, behavioral layer, spatial layer, and control layer across modalities. Based on this, a five-dimensional fusion tensor structure is designed. This innovation enables strict alignment of multi-source data in the temporal dimension and completes temporal calibration of heterogeneous data through cross-source neighborhood consistency constraints. Furthermore, a multi-source attention fusion mechanism is introduced. This mechanism models the cooperative and conflict relationships between different modalities through interaction terms. At the rhythm modeling level, this study proposes a fusion-driven beat fingerprint function. This process characterizes the acceleration features of rhythm changes through multi-source response weighting and second-order time derivative enhancement terms. Simultaneously, cross-source consistency constraints are combined to improve the stability of multi-modal responses. At the generation and control layers, a hidden Markov rhythm dynamic model under fusion feature conditions is constructed. Simultaneously, the variational autoencoders and Wasserstein generative adversarial networks are combined to achieve rhythm latent space modeling and distribution alignment. Finally, the fused features are introduced into the reinforcement learning control framework. The experiments were conducted using the self-built multi-source keyboard performance dataset MKPD-Set. Results show that, compared to single-modal fusion methods, the proposed method reduces beat offset error (BOE) by approximately 28.2%. It also achieves significant improvements in rhythm consistency (FC) and generation diversity (GD). Even under 30% noise conditions, rhythm accuracy (RA) remains at a high level. This result demonstrates stronger robustness compared to the Transformer model (RA=0.801, BOE=39.5). Furthermore, subjective evaluation results show that the proposed method scores higher in rhythmic naturalness and expressiveness.

Title: Experimental sense-making, musicking and no control: Performing black box music instruments
Abstract: The text explores ‘Black Box Music,’ an artistic research experiment investigating human–technology relations in musical improvisation. The authors describe performances in which each musician plays an unfamiliar, complex, custom-built instrument designed by another team member. These ‘black box’ devices-ranging from AI-based systems to assemblages of analogue devices-cannot be fully understood or controlled, thus foregrounding questions of agency, sense-making, and aesthetic experience. Drawing on Actor-Network Theory, phenomenology, and philosophies of technology, the authors show how performers, instruments, and audience form a dynamic network of actants whose roles and intentions remain ambiguous. Players initially struggle to ‘read’ the instruments’ behaviour, shifting from reactive analysis toward proactive improvisation. This process blurs embodiment and alterity: the instruments alternately function as transparent extensions of the body and as quasi-autonomous others. Such ambiguity invites anthropomorphisation and even ritualised interaction, echoing historical entanglements of music, magic, and spirituality. Audience members, too, encounter indeterminate agency and must negotiate aesthetic meaning without clear attribution of sound to human or machine. The project demonstrates how complexity and unpredictability destabilise traditional notions of control, revealing improvisation as collective, participatory sense-making and highlighting the emergent, co-creative agency of both humans and technological instruments.

Title: Robustness-Oriented Explainability Analysis of the PHQ-9 Depression Scale Using Ensemble Learning under Response Perturbations
Abstract: Reliable assessment of depression is essential for early identification of high-risk individuals, yet psychometric instruments such as the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 are vulnerable to response variability and uncertainty. This study aims to analyze the robustness, redundancy, and explainability of PHQ-9-based high-risk classification rather than propose a predictive diagnostic system. The objectives are to examine structural stability of the scale, evaluate effects of realistic Likert-scale perturbations on clinically relevant metrics, and assess resilience of high-risk detection under increasing uncertainty. An Extreme Gradient Boosting classifier was trained using clean PHQ-9 responses, with binary high-risk labels derived from established clinical thresholds. Robustness was evaluated by introducing bounded ±1 Likert-scale noise into symptom responses at multiple perturbation levels during testing. Results show that perfect performance under noise-free conditions reflects deterministic scale construction, while increasing perturbation produces gradual degradation in accuracy and sensitivity. Crucially, the ability to detect high-risk individuals remained above 97%, even when response variability increased, while the rate of missed cases rose only slightly. This trend suggests that the PHQ-9 survey possesses inherent internal consistency and structural stability, ensuring dependable risk categorization even when self-reported answers vary. The findings highlight the value of stress-testing assessments through response variation - a practical and clinically relevant way to verify the reliability of mental health tools. Ultimately, this approach advocates for the cautious interpretation and functional use of PHQ-9 screening in routine medical practice.

Title: Pretrained Biomedical Foundation Models: Comparative Analysis and Practical Applications in Healthcare
Abstract: The rapid proliferation of pretrained biomedical foundation models has transformed healthcare AI, yet researchers and clinicians face persistent challenges in selecting the most appropriate model for a given application, as architectures, pretraining strategies, and computational requirements vary substantially across systems. This review provides a structured comparative synthesis of representative pretrained biomedical foundation models to support informed model selection for clinical and research applications. Seven models spanning encoderonly, decoder-only, and multimodal architectures and three pretraining strategies, continued pretraining, from-scratch pretraining, and instruction tuning, are compared across biomedical NLP benchmarks covering named entity recognition, question answering, and clinical reasoning. A multi-criteria framework evaluates each model across architecture, strategy, vocabulary type, task suitability, scale, and open-weight accessibility. Pretraining strategy and vocabulary alignment appear to be more influential factors in downstream performance than parameter count alone: from-scratch domain pretraining tends to outperform continued pretraining in several reported benchmarks, and instruction tuning has been shown to enable expert-level performance on specific clinical reasoning benchmarks (e.g., USMLE). These findings suggest that model selection should be guided by corpus-task alignment rather than scale, and that openweight alternatives can recover a meaningful fraction of closedmodel performance at lower deployment cost. Practical selection guidelines, current limitations including bias, hallucination, and computational accessibility, and future research directions are discussed.

Title: Analyzing Usage Patterns of Artificial Intelligence Tools Among Criminology Students Using Machine Learning and Behavioral Analytics
Abstract: This study analyzes the usage patterns of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools among criminology students through the integration of behavioral analytics, sentiment analysis, and machine learning techniques. A dataset consisting of 533 respondents from Region II and Region III was collected using a structured survey instrument with Likert-scale and open-ended responses. Feature engineering was applied to construct composite behavioral indices, while sentiment analysis was performed to extract attitudinal insights from textual data. The processed dataset was used to train and evaluate classification models, including Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN). The results show that the SVM model achieved the highest performance, with an accuracy exceeding 95%, precision reaching 100%, and recall values up to 100% for the Moderate class. The LDA model also demonstrated strong performance with AUC values ranging from 0.983 to 0.997, while KNN showed comparatively lower performance with recall values as low as 69% for the High class. Feature importance analysis using the mRMR algorithm identified the AI Usage Index (0.3682) as the most significant predictor, followed by usage frequency and tools used. These findings highlight the effectiveness of integrating machine learning and sentiment analysis in modeling AI usage behavior and supporting data-driven educational strategies.

Title: An Error Analysis and Benchmark on Automatic Speech Recognition for isiZulu, isiXhosa, isiNdebele, and siSwati
Abstract: Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems have achieved remarkable performance for high-resource languages but remain significantly underperforming for low-resource African languages, particularly the South African Nguni language family, isiZulu, isiXhosa, isiNdebele, and siSwati. This study presents a comparative evaluation of three leading ASR models, Whisper, Wav2Vec2.0, and SpeechBrain, on South African Nguni languages. This study evaluated pre-trained models using standardized datasets from the South African Digital Language Resources (SADiLaR), and a total of 4, 456 audio files from speakers across all four Nguni languages. Performance was evaluated using Word Error Rate (WER), Character Error Rate (CER), and error pattern analysis. Wav2Vec2.0 demonstrated a more balanced error profile performance across all languages with the lowest average WER of 1.574, followed by Whisper with 1.730 and SpeechBrain with 2.141. IsiXhosa consistently showed the highest error rates across all models, while siSwati and isiNdebele had more balanced performance. Error analysis revealed substitutions as the dominant error type, with 6 0 - 7 0 % of total errors, with SpeechBrain showing the highest insertion rates and Whisper the highest deletion rates. The study's findings indicate that while Wav2Vec2.0's semi-supervised learning approach shows promise for low-resource Nguni languages, all evaluated models demonstrate poor performance in terms of WER. This highlights the urgent need for language-specific fine-tuning and expanded training corpora.

Title: Moodify AI: An Intelligent Air-Drumming System Using Computer Vision and Artificial Intelligence for Real-Time Musical Interaction
Abstract: Traditional drum kits are expensive, bulky, and space-consuming, limiting accessibility for beginners and casual learners. This paper presents Moodify AI, a marker less, vision-based air-drumming system that uses OpenCV and MediaPipe for real-time hand-landmark extraction and a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) classifier for gesture recognition. Unlike sensor-based or wearable systems, the proposed approach requires only a standard webcam and performs velocity-based gesture detection to simulate dynamic drum intensity. Experimental evaluation shows an average gesture recognition accuracy of 92% in well-lit conditions and 87% under low-light environments, with an average latency of 150-250ms, making it suitable for real-time musical interaction. The system demonstrates a low-cost, portable, and scalable alternative to hardware-dependent virtual percussion systems while enabling expressive gesture-controlled music performance.

Title: Preoperative risk stratification for pathological upgrading in colorectal polyps using explainable machine learning: implications for screening optimization and resource allocation
Abstract: Background – Pathological upgrading in colorectal polyps, which occurs when resection specimens have a higher histological grade than preoperative biopsies, can lead to an underestimation of the severity of the disease and suboptimal treatment. Given the substantial global burden of colorectal cancer (CRC), improving preoperative risk stratification of colorectal polyps is essential for optimizing screening strategies and resource allocation in CRC prevention. Methods – Between December 2019 and December 2024, 593 patients with colorectal polyps were included in this retrospective study, undergoing endoscopic biopsy and subsequent complete resection. Clinical and endoscopic variables were gathered, and feature selection was conducted using LASSO regression and the Boruta algorithm. Repeated ten-fold cross-validation was used to develop and evaluate six machine learning models: RF, CART, NNet, LR, GBM, and XGBoost. AUC, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, MCC, and Brier score were used to assess the model's performance. A web-based calculator was developed to aid in clinical implementation, using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to interpret the optimal model. Results – Among the 593 patients, 150 (25.3%) experienced pathological upgrading. Five key predictors were identified: maximum tumor diameter, surface color, erosion, villous structure, and lesion location. With an AUC of 0.890 in the training set and 0.863 in the test set, the XGBoost model exhibited superior performance, along with strong calibration and discrimination. SHAP analysis showed that lesion location, particularly rectal location, was the most influential factor, followed by erosion and tumor size. To aid in individual risk prediction, a user-friendly online calculator was designed (available at: https://changchangzhang2001.shinyapps.io/blsj/). The calculator will remain freely accessible for at least 3 years after publication, and the source code is available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request. Conclusion – Researchers in this study devised a machine learning model that provides explanations for predicting pathological upgrading in colorectal polyps. The model serves as a useful instrument for assessing preoperative risks and aids in making decisions based on risk, potentially boosting early detection efficiency, refining endoscopic management approaches, and improving resource allocation in colorectal cancer prevention programs.

Title: Infrared Thermography Versus Clinical Assessment for Knee Joint Damage Detection in Rheumatoid Arthritis
Abstract: Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) is an inflammatory disease that advances to destroy the synovial joints, especially knee joint. Active inflammation has to be early detected to avoid irreversible joint destruction. The research paper is an analysis on the efficacy of Infrared Thermography (IRT) in the detection of knee joint inflammation among RA patients and a comparison of its performance with clinical examination, laboratory (ESR, CRP) and musculoskeletal ultrasound. A cross-sectional survey of 100 patients (70 RA patients that met the ACR / EULAR 2010 criteria and 30 healthy participants) was carried out. Those were standardized thermographic images of both knees taken in controlled environmental conditions. Thermal parameters were obtained and statistically analyzed including mean temperature, the peak temperature and the bilateral asymmetry index. The outcome demonstrated high temperatures of knee surface in RA patients when compared to the controls (p<0.001). Significant (r = 0.76) positive correlation was displayed between thermographic hotspots temperature and ultrasound-detected synovitis. IRT had an 88 percent sensitivity and 81 percent specificity in the detection of inflammatory activity. The integration of machine learning also increased the diagnostic accuracy to 91.7%. The results suggest that IRT is a dependable and non-invasive instrument free of radiation that can be used to supplement traditional clinical evaluation to identify and track inflammation in the knee joints promptly in RA.

Title: Detecting Health Misinformation: AI Solutions for Medical and Policy Content
Abstract: The dissemination of health misinformation in a short period is life-threatening to the trusting attitudes, medical decision-making, and adherence to policies. In the given research, AI-based methods of automated classifying health-related claims are offered using transformer-based language models and hybrid structures into Supports, Refutes, and Neutral categories. Various state-of-the-art biomedical NLP models have been tested such as BioBERT, RoBERTa, SciBERT, ClinicalBERT, and a fine-tuned Meta-Llama-3-8BInstruct. A lot of experiments on the HealthVer dataset prove that the Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct has a maximum performance score, with its own test accuracy of 0.8391 and the Macro-F1 score of 0.7831, which is even better than BioBERT and other models. It was found in comparative analysis that medical domain-specific transformers are of great use in credibility assessment in clinical and public-health claims. Such results indicate the possibility of sophisticated large-language model to be used as an effective instrument in fighting health misinformation on digital pillars.

Title: Real Time Sign Language Recognition with Text to Speech Integration
Abstract: One of the most important forms of communication for people with speech or hearing problems is sign language; however, its limited understanding among non signers often restricts effective interaction. This paper presents a real time Indian Sign Language (ISL) recognition system integrated with Text to Speech (TTS) conversion to address this challenge. The proposed system employs MediaPipe for accurate hand landmark detection and extracts 3D spatial coordinates as gesture features. These features are classified using optimized machine learning models, including Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Random Forest. To improve classification performance and mitigate data imbalance, the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) is applied during training. Communication is made simple and accessible by translating the identified motions into speech and text. Experimental findings show that the system attains a high level of accuracy, real time responsiveness, and robust performance under varying conditions. The proposed approach highlights the effectiveness of integrating gesture recognition with speech synthesis as a scalable assistive technology for inclusive human computer interaction.

Title: Hybrid CNN-SVM Framework for Automated Depression Detection Using Speech Analysis
Abstract: This paper presents a hybrid CNN-SVM model that is used to detect depression based on speech using the DAIC-WOZ dataset (Opensource). All audio files were processed using Librosa, SciPy and Parselmouth to remove noise and normalize audio and extract acoustic features (including some MFCCs, spectral, prosodic and energy-based acoustic features). After data preprocessing, the CNN was trained to learn depth spectral representations and SVM was trained to classify the embeddings to improve the performance of generalization. The model achieved a rate of accuracy of 69.09%, which is a 6%-8% better result than the current methods. In general, the analysis finds a value in deep learning with machine learning in the creation of noninvasive, reliable, and scalable methods of detecting depression early.

Title: Optimizing Human-Machine Interaction in BDA-AI Systems
Abstract: Despite growing scholarly interest in Big Data Analytics and Artificial Intelligence (BDA-AI) systems, empirical research lacks standardized measurement tools to assess their environmental impact. This research addresses the gap by developing an instrument that examines the influence of BDA-AI on eco-innovation (EIN) and ecological performance (EP). Building on the Technology-Organization-Environment (TOE) framework, this study introduces employee digital skills (EDS) and top management support (TMS) as key determinants of technology adoption. Following an extensive review of the literature from 2015 to 2025, a theoretical framework was constructed that encompasses six hypothesized relationships. The proposed measurement instrument comprises 37 items that measure BDA-AI, TOE framework, EP, EIN, TMS, and EDS. This research advances the environmental sustainability and technology management literature by offering researchers a robust tool for investigating how BDA-AI shapes organizational environmental practices.

Title: Enhancing Sentiment Analysis Using Targeted Preprocessing and Weighted Ensemble Learning
Abstract: Sentiment analysis serves as a stepping stone for opinion mining interpretation of textual user reviews and NLP. It is shown that text preprocessing, when combined with weighted ensemble learning, enhances binary sentiment accuracy on the IMDB movie review dataset. The methodology includes multilevel NLP preprocessing, which involves removing HTML tags, non-alphabetic symbols, and stop words, as well as stemming and TF-IDF representation. This is followed by a comparison of multiple classifiers, including Logistic Regression, Linear SVC, and Multinomial Naive Bayes. Building on these results, a custom weighted Voting Classifier was constructed to leverage the strengths of top-performing models. It was observed that the weighted ensemble classifier consistently outperformed individual classifiers, which contributes to improved overall accuracy and generalisation. It is confirmed that targeted preprocessing, when combined with weighted model aggregation, improves sentiment classification in sparse, high-dimensional text spaces and is likely to find broad applicability for similar realworld opinion mining tasks and large-scale review analytics.

Title: RHYTHM: Intelligent Music Recommendation Framework Based on Facial Affect Analysis
Abstract: The paradigm of Music Recommendation Systems (MRS) is currently undergoing a fundamental shift, transitioning from static, history-based preference models to context-aware architecture driven by the user's real-time affective state. While traditional collaborative filtering successfully captures long-term taste, it often fails to address the immediate, situational emotional needs of the listener. This paper presents a comprehensive survey and a proposed architectural framework for an Emotion-Aware Music Recommendation System (EAMRS) optimized for resource-constrained edge environments. This paper perform an in-depth analysis of current methods used in three important areas: (1) Facial Emotion Recognition (FER), where comparison of heavy models like VGG16 with lightweight ones like MobileNetV2 is done; (2) Music Mood Classification (MMC), where judgement of the performance of spectral feature engineering is made and that of deep learning hybrids working end-to-end; and (3) Psychological Emotion Mapping, where The subtle differences are highlighted between mood congruence and mood regulation. Besides, this paper elaborate on the implementation strategy which makes use of depth wise separable convolutions to get real-time inference (approx. 25ms) on standard hardware, and on the CNN-GRU hybrid model for audio analysis that has a classification accuracy of 98% which is quite high. The paper concludes by addressing the "Semantic Gap"in audio analysis and outlining future directions for multimodal fusion.

Title: AI-Driven Claims Adjudication: Optimizing Healthcare Systems with Machine Learning and Deep Neural Networks
Abstract: Healthcare claims adjudication is an important administrative process that affects the accuracy and efficiency of reimbursements in healthcare systems and prevents fraud. Growing volumes of claims, challenging billing codes, undocumented clinical records, and sophisticated fraud schemes present weaknesses in rule-based and manual adjudication. This study introduces an AI-based claims adjudication system that combines transformer-based natural language processing (NLP), ensemble machine learning, and a two-step fraud detection pipeline. The system examines the structured attributes of claims, utilization, profile of provider behavior, and contextual embeddings of clinical text to automatically perform adjudication with great accuracy and transparency. Claim classification is performed using a weighted combination of XGBoost, Random Forest, and neural network classifiers, and fraud detection is performed using a hybrid model of unsupervised anomaly detection and supervised learning. On large-scale healthcare data, experimental analysis reveals 94.7% classification accuracy, 67 percent processing time reduction, and 37 percent better fraud detection results than rule-based systems. The interpretability, regulatory compliance, computational complexity, and deployment considerations discussed in this study make the framework a scalable platform for next-generation healthcare claims processing.

Title: EN-CBAM: A Novel Deep Learning Approach For Accurate Respiratory Disease Detection
Abstract: Rrespiratory diseases are common throughout the world. Diagnostic instruments are important for the proper detection and treatment of respiratory diseases. A timely diagnosis of respiratory disease is essential. This paper investigates the performance of the deep learning model based on the EfficientNet-B0 baseline and Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM), to detect diseases such as pneumonia, COVID-19, and tuberculosis with high accuracy. The goal is to achieve an accuracy of over 90% on a dataset of chest X-ray images, which would significantly improve upon the state of-the-art results in this field. Meanwhile, more complex models like Capsule Networks and Attention-based models have achieved accuracies up to 89% and 90%, respectively. Title: Deep Learning-Driven GAN-RNN Hybrid Framework for Intelligent Speech and Listening Skill Development in EFL Learners
Abstract: Effective English as a Foreign Language (EFL) training requires exact evaluation of learners' speaking and listening proficiency'an aspect where conventional systems frequently lack the ability to adapt dynamically to individual differences. This study presents a hybrid framework that combines Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) for speech data enhancement with Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN) for the temporal modelling of learner advancement, driven by deep learning. Generative Adversarial Networks enhance the dataset by producing authentic phonetic and prosodic changes, whereas Recurrent Neural Networks identify long-term dependencies in learner voice sequences for accurate skill assessment. The system employs encoder-based feature extraction and adaptive loss synchronisation to guarantee consistent convergence and contextual precision. Comparative assessments against CNN-LSTM, BiLSTM-Attention, Transformer, and Plain RNN benchmarks reveal that the proposed hybrid attains enhanced performance with 97.8% accuracy, 97.5% F1- score, and a R<sup>2-</sup>score of 0.982. Title: Real-Time Embedded Voice Processing System on RV1126 Platform: Hybrid Signal Processing and NPU-Accelerated Neural Networks for Communication Applications
Abstract: Intelligent voice processing for remote conferencing and online education remains challenging in complex acoustic environments. Existing systems suffer from three critical limitations: (1) traditional TDOA-based localization methods exhibit degraded accuracy under reverberation and multi-path propagation, (2) purely spatial beamforming approaches fail to separate overlapping speakers with similar directional characteristics, and (3) deep learning-based separation models incur prohibitive computational costs for real-time deployment on resource-constrained embedded platforms. To address these challenges, we propose a hybrid voice processing framework that synergistically integrates spatial-temporal acoustic methods with NPU-accelerated neural architectures on the RV1126 embedded platform. Our system introduces three key innovations: (1) a cascaded TDOA-GCC-PHAT localization pipeline achieving 3.2° horizontal accuracy through adaptive phase transform weighting, (2) a delay-and-sum beamforming module coupled with LMS-based acoustic echo cancellation delivering 32dB ERLE, and (3) an INT8-quantized DPRNN deployed on the integrated NPU for real-time multi-speaker separation at 30 FPS. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate end-to-end latency of 75.4ms, noise suppression exceeding 20dB, and superior performance compared to conventional approaches, validating practical viability for intelligent conferencing applications.

Title: AI-Enabled Framework for Stock Market Prediction Using KSE-100 Index
Abstract: Financial markets serve as platforms where instruments such as equities, foreign exchange, and cryptocurrencies are traded, and accurate price prediction remains a critical challenge for traders and investors. The models evaluated include ML algorithms such as XGBoost and Random Forest, and DL architectures such as LSTM, GRU, and Transformers. Title: AI-Enabled Competency-Based Learning: An Integrated Framework for Assessment, Adaptation, and Organizational Decision Support
Abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into competency-based learning (CBL) is rapidly advancing the shift from knowledge memorization to mastery of measurable skills, with significant implications for both academic and organizational contexts. This study presents a systematic literature review of 34 peer-reviewed articles identified through a PRISMA-guided screening process in the Scopus database (2015-2025). Methodological quality was appraised using the APPRAISE-AI instrument across six evaluation domains, yielding a mean composite score of 9.82 out of 12 (median = 10.75), with 23 studies (67.6 %) classified as high quality, confirming the robustness and reliability of the evidence. Synthesizing insights on core AI capabilities, including adaptive systems, learning analytics, skill detection, explainable AI (XAI), and hybrid approaches, and their relationship with competency rubrics as the central mechanism in CBL, this study makes three contributions to the literature. First, competency rubrics are positioned as boundary objects that interface AIdriven assessment evidence with personalized and adaptive learning paths. Second, a Decision Support System (DSS) is embedded as a facilitation and governance layer, involving managers, subject matter experts, and Human Resources/Learning and Development (HR/L&D) units to ensure fairness, ethical accountability, and contextual relevance in organizational learning ecosystems. Third, a systematic translation mechanism converts technical AI metrics, including accuracy, Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and F1-score, into actionable organizational Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), encompassing time-to-proficiency, compliance index, error reduction, and learning adoption. This dual conceptual and practical contribution provides a clear roadmap for leveraging AI to support transparent, ethical, and effective workforce development in competency-based corporate learning settings.

Title: Advanced Deep Learning Framework for Highly Accurate Infant Cry Signal Classification
Abstract: Accurate infant cry signal classification is a critical aspect in infant distress root cause identification and resolution, enabling timely effective interventions. Title: Enhancing Heart Disease Diagnosis through Ensemble and Instance-Based Machine Learning Techniques
Abstract: Cardiovascular disease remains one of the major health issues affecting the whole world, and the early detection of the condition requires more sophisticated instruments to minimize the death rates. This study examines the effectiveness of machine learning (ML) in the prediction of heart disease on the UCI Heart Disease dataset, which contains 303 records of patients with 14 clinical variables. Four ML models, including Logistic Regression, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Decision Tree Classifier, and Random Forest Classifier, are adopted and tested in binary classification (presence or absence of the disease). The methodology includes a lot of data preprocessing, feature selection and correlation analysis, Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE), the training of the model with hyperparameter optimization, and the evaluation of the model with accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. The Regression (Logistic) had training accuracy of 85.12 percent and test accuracy of 81.97 percent, and KNN and Random Forest had cross-validated accuracy of 85.07 percent and 81.99 percent, respectively. Visualizations, such as confusion matrices, ROC curves, and feature importance graphs, contribute to a better understanding. Comparative analysis indicates that the strength of Random Forest and the effectiveness of Logistic Regression, feature importance shows that cholesterol, age, and ECG results are the most important predictors. This paper highlights the possibility of ML to transform the diagnostics of cardiovascular diseases and suggests the directions of future improvement along with deep learning and real-time data combination, and discusses ethical issues such as data privacy and model bias.

Title: Deep Learning-Based for Accurate Estimation of Hypertension Risk Using Health Data
Abstract: Hypertension is a common cardiovascular disorder that presents significant health hazards, including heart disease and stroke. Precise forecasting of hypertension risk is essential for timely intervention and efficient management. This paper introduces a deep learning methodology employing a Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) to assess hypertension risk based on demographic and health-related information. The model is trained on the Hypertension Risk Dataset from Kaggle, comprising 13 characteristics and a hypertension risk label. The proposed RNN model has robust prediction performance, with an overall accuracy of 95.6%. The result outcomes the efficacy of RNNs in identifying complex patterns and temporal relationships in health data, surpassing conventional machine learning methods. The results indicate that deep learning models can function as dependable instruments for early risk evaluation and individualized monitoring of hypertension. This method can mitigate difficulties, enhance patient outcomes, and facilitate improved healthcare decision-making through the implementation of timely preventative actions.

Title: Predictive Algorithms for PCOS: Harnessing Data to Uncover Hidden Risks
Abstract: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) is a highly common issue but largely ignored hormonal disorder that affects females in their reproductive age. The varied and shifting symptoms it brings sometimes make it very difficult to identify and diagnose on time. This research paper examines the use of predictive instruments with special interest in algorithms of machine learning of the ensemble type in the determination of PCOS and the presentation of hidden risk factors. Moreover, SHAP and LIME interpretation methods provided meaningful clinical insights, which are more self-assuring and open to AI-dependent diagnostic systems. Title: Oilfield Produced Water Treatment Prediction Based on Multi-Scale SE Attention-XGBoost Hybrid Model
Abstract: In oilfield produced water treatment, accurate prediction of oil content is critical for process optimization, but traditional machine learning methods struggle with complex feature interactions in small sample scenarios, while deep learning approaches require large datasets and lack interpretability. To improve the prediction accuracy in industrial applications with limited training samples, this paper proposes a Multi-Scale SE Attention-XGBoost hybrid model. We adapt the Squeeze-andExcitation (SE) attention mechanism from image processing to tabular industrial data by removing spatial pooling operations and directly learning feature importance weights, design a multi-scale architecture with different reduction ratios to capture feature relationships at multiple granularities, integrate residual connections to enhance representation and prevent overfitting, and combine SE-enhanced features with XGBoost for final prediction. Experimenting on a real-world dataset from a hydrocyclone-flotation facility, the proposed model demonstrates superior performance compared to standalone XGBoost, LightGBM, Random Forest, and MLP methods. The experiment validates the effectiveness of the multi-scale attention mechanism in identifying key process parameters, and the model can be effectively applied to oilfield water treatment optimization.

Title: Deep Learning-Based Speech Analysis for Early Detection of Alzheimer's Disease
Abstract: AD is one of the most important global healthcare challenges in the 21st century, and its early detection is of prime importance for effective intervention and treatment. This work proposes a broad, multimodal framework that leverages state-of-the-art self-supervised learning through Wav2Vec2 in the clinically validated DementiaBank speech corpus for early AD detection. Our proposed architecture integrates pre-trained Wav2Vec2 embeddings with rich linguistic features through a hybrid system that combines temporal convolutional networks with cross-modal attention mechanisms. The model processes samples of spontaneous speech from standardized picture description tasks to capture both subtle acoustic patterns and higher-level complex linguistic biomarkers of cognitive decline. Title: Comparing Baseline and Day-1 Diffusion MRI Using Multimodal Deep Embeddings for Stroke Outcome Prediction
Abstract: This study compares baseline (J0) and 24-hour (J1) diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for predicting three-month functional outcomes after acute ischemic stroke (AIS). Seventy-four AIS patients with paired apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) scans and clinical data were analyzed. Three-dimensional ResNet-50 embeddings were fused with structured clinical variables, reduced via principal component analysis (≤ 12 components), and classified using linear support vector machines with eight-fold stratified group cross-validation. J1 multimodal models achieved the highest predictive performance (AUC=0.923 ± 0.085), outperforming J0-based configurations (AUC ≤ 0.86). Incorporating lesion-volume features further improved model stability and interpretability. These findings demonstrate that early posttreatment diffusion MRI provides superior prognostic value to pre-treatment imaging and that combining MRI, clinical, and lesion-volume features produces a robust and interpretable framework for predicting three-month functional outcomes in AIS patients.

Title: SPARK- Speech Pattern Analysis for Recognizing Parkinson's Disease
Abstract: Early diagnosis of Parkinson's disease (PD), a chronic neurodegenerative disorder, can improve patient care and allow for the utilization of disease-modifying treatments. Speech degradation is also one of the quickest detectable mundane symptoms of PD and provides a viable means of detection that is non-invasive. In this paper, The SPARK (Speech Pattern Analysis for Recognizing Parkinson's disease), a novel machine learning based framework to detect PD from speech signals. Mel Frequency Coefficient Cepstral (MFCC) are extracted to represent discriminative vocal cues. Several classifiers are employed and tested such as different kernels of Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbour (KNN), Random Forest and XG boost. For enhancing stability and decreasing over fitting, ensemble methods such as voting and stacking are applied. Experimental results show that these stacking generalization ensemble models outperform all other algorithms and obtain a best accuracy of 91.23% with balanced precision and recall. The entire system is then implemented and an interface is designed using Flask such that voice can be analyzed at any time for easy screening. These results demonstrate the promise of speech-based ensemble learning as an inexpensive and scalable clinical decision support instrument for early Parkinson's disease detection.

Title: NLP-Driven Gradient Boosting Ensemble Framework for Automated Viral Genome Classification in Large-Scale Metagenomic Data
Abstract: The rapid advancement of next-generation sequencing (NGS) technologies has generated unprecedented volumes of metagenomic data, yet accurate identification of viral sequences remains a significant computational challenge. Title: A weighted multimodal fusion and deep learning framework for quantitative evaluation of music performance effects
Abstract: Music performance evaluation has long relied on subjective judgement, causing inconsistency and poor reproducibility. This study presents a quantitative framework using weighted multimodal fusion and deep learning, integrating audio, video, and motion data to assess technical and expressive performance. Title: ViT-AUDIT: Spectrogram-based Deepfake Audio Detection using Vision Transformers
Abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence has enabled the generation of highly realistic synthetic speech, raising serious concerns for voice-based authentication and communication systems. This paper proposes ViT-AUDIT, a spectrogram-based deep learning framework that leverages Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs) and multiple neural architectures, including CNN, RNN, CRNN, LSTM-GRU, and Vision Transformers (ViT). Title: Inequality-Constrained Emotional-Style Decoupling Optimization for Automatic AI-based Electronic Keyboard Music Generation
Abstract: To address the issues of high coupling between emotion and style, lack of physical performance constraints, and insufficient granularity of emotion control in current automatic music generation models, this paper proposes a groundbreaking Inequality-Constrained Emotion-Style Decoupling Optimization Framework (IC-ESDO) for automatic music generation on electronic keyboards. This framework achieves unified optimization among emotion expression, style control, and performance feasibility through the collaborative design of multimodal emotion perception, latent space decoupling modeling, and inequality constraint decoding. Methodologically, this study first constructs a multimodal emotion perception module. This module integrates EEG signals, textual emotion descriptions, and user historical preferences, learning continuous and differentiable emotion embeddings through a cross-modal attention mechanism. Subsequently, in the generative model based on OctupleMIDI extended representations, multi-channel posterior modeling of latent emotion, style, and content variables is introduced. Simultaneously, a dual decoupling mechanism is constructed using mutual information suppression terms and an adversarial decorrelation discriminator. Furthermore, the physical and logical constraints of electronic keyboard performance are formalized into a set of computable inequalities. The model embeds constraint filtering and renormalization operations at each generation step, ensuring that the generated results satisfy performance conditions such as finger spacing limits, polyphony constraints, pedal logic, and legato rules. On the experimental level, this paper constructs the E-StyleKeys-45K dataset, which contains 45,312 MIDI tracks and features multi-style and multi-emotion continuous annotations. It also conducts systematic comparisons with models such as Music Transformer, EmotionBox, Diff-BGM, Hyper-Curve Transformer, and Calliope. The results show that the proposed method reduces the Emotion Consistency Error (ECE) by approximately 34.2% compared to the best comparable model. Significant improvements are also achieved in Style Consistency (SCA) and Emotion-Style Decoupling Index (ESDI). In cross-style emotion generalization experiments, IC-ESDO maintains stable performance even with unseen emotion-style combinations. Constraint Satisfaction Rate (CSR) experiments show that the proposed method achieves over 95% across all constraint dimensions.

Title: Transformer-Based Dynamic Regional Attention Mechanism for Occluded Face Recognition
Abstract: Face recognition in occluded scenarios poses significant challenges due to partial obstructions that impair feature extraction and matching accuracy. Traditional convolutional neural networks struggle with global context modeling and robustness to occlusions. This study introduces a Transformerbased dynamic regional attention mechanism tailored for occluded face recognition. The approach leverages a pre-trained Vision Transformer for multi-scale feature extraction, integrates an occlusion detection module using a lightweight CNN to generate masks, and dynamically adjusts attention weights to prioritize non-occluded regions. Extensive experiments on the Masked Face Recognition dataset, AR Face, and FaceOcc demonstrate superior performance, achieving 98.5 % accuracy under occlusion, outperforming baselines by up to 6.5 %. Ablation studies validate the efficacy of each component, highlighting the mechanism's robustness and generalization. This work advances occluded face recognition by addressing key limitations in existing methods, offering a scalable solution for real-world applications in security and surveillance.

Title: Invited Talk: From Chip to AI Factory-A Five-Year Roadmap for Silicon Suppliers and Hyperscalers
Abstract: AI infrastructure is entering a critical scaling phase in which sustained, deployable performance is increasingly constrained not by peak compute capability, but by system-level integration across silicon, packaging, cooling, power delivery, facilities, and operations. As accelerator power density rises and heterogeneous integration accelerates, through chiplets, advanced 2.5D/3D packaging, and high-bandwidth memory (HBM) performance bottlenecks shift into memory bandwidth, power delivery networks, and thermo-mechanical interfaces. At the same time, AI deployment is expanding beyond centralized training clusters toward hybrid cloud, regional inference, and edge environments, creating a multi-topology reality that favors repeatable, serviceable reference architectures over bespoke, peak-optimized designs.This paper presents a five-year roadmap (2026-2030) for silicon suppliers and hyperscalers that reframes AI scaling around the concept of the AI factory: a co-designed system spanning chip, package, server, rack, cooling distribution, power, and facility operations. We show that junction-to-surface thermal resistance, interface stability under warpage and clamp-load variation, and manufacturability and serviceability constraints increasingly dominate achievable power density and sustained utilization. As a result, thermo-mechanical integration emerges as system architecture, rather than a secondary validation concern.The paper consolidates industry developments into six overarching themes: (i) system-level integration rules serve as a key competitive advantage; (ii) hardware-software co-design and enhanced observability drive operational efficiency; (iii) memory bandwidth and data movement represent the primary system-level expenses; (iv) thermo-mechanical enablement determines the feasibility of multi-kilowatt packages; (v) the selection of cooling technologies should align with maturity and operational risk; and (vi) considerations regarding energy, water, and carbon constitute fundamental design constraints. A gated execution framework is introduced that aligns cooling modality, interface validation, mechanical robustness, and qualification rigor with increasing power density, emphasizing extension of mature single-phase liquid cooling and KPI-driven pilots for higher-risk technologies.The central conclusion is that future AI infrastructure scaling depends less on nominal silicon advances and more on the ability to industrialize system-level integration rules, instrument the full stack, and scale through disciplined replication. Organizations that adopt this system-centric approach will achieve higher sustained utilization, lower total cost of ownership, and faster deployment velocity, while those that do not risk turning peak silicon capability into stranded or unreliable capacity.

Title: An Adaptive AI-Driven Game-Inspired Framework for Simulation-Based Personalized Pronunciation Feedback in Children
Abstract: Pronunciation learning for children with speech sound difficulties requires frequent, individualized practice that is often difficult to provide consistently in classroom or home environments. Adaptive pronunciation learning systems offer a promising direction by tailoring feedback to each learner's specific articulation patterns. This paper presents a simulation-based adaptive pronunciation framework that operates at the phoneme level and dynamically adjusts corrective feedback according to learner-specific error profiles. The system models common child pronunciation errors, such as phoneme substitution, deletion, and insertion, and evaluates adaptation strategies within a controlled experimental environment. To ground the simulation in real speech data, utterances and phoneme annotations are derived from established child language resources, including the CMU Kids Speech Corpus and child-directed transcripts from CHILDES. Model performance is assessed across simulated pronunciation trials (M=100 target words, T=5 attempts per target), measuring phoneme error rate, word error rate, and correction efficiency under varying learner profiles. The results show that adaptive feedback strategies consistently outperform non-adaptive baselines across all evaluated metrics within the simulation setting. Although the proposed framework is not deployed with live learners, the findings demonstrate the potential of adaptive phoneme-level modeling as a methodological foundation for personalized pronunciation learning systems. This work aims to support future research toward interactive, datadriven speech learning applications validated through real-world user studies.

Title: NeuroSpeechNet: Hierarchical Attention-Enhanced EEG-to-Speech Synthesis via Deep Neural Mapping
Abstract: This study introduces NeuroSpeechNet, a novel end-to-end neural framework for transforming non-invasive EEG signals into intelligible speech. The approach integrates a hierarchical attention-based feature extraction mechanism, enabling the selective amplification of speech-relevant neural patterns at both local and global levels within the EEG signal. These enriched representations are processed by a deep sequence-to-sequence model employing self-attention to capture complex temporal dependencies, thus facilitating a robust mapping from neural activity to acoustic space. The output acoustic representations are synthesized into continuous speech waveforms, fully automating the EEG-to-speech process without manual feature engineering or intermediate labels. Experimental evaluations on benchmark EEG-speech datasets demonstrate that NeuroSpeechNet achieves superior performance in terms of correlation accuracy, reconstruction error, and speech intelligibility compared to classical and recent deep learning baselines. Objective metrics show notable improvements in both feature prediction and audio quality, while subjective listening tests confirm the enhanced naturalness and clarity of the synthesized speech. Title: Employing Transfer Learning Enabled Convolution Neural Networks for Deep Fake Voice Detection
Abstract: Audio deep fakes, generated through advanced artificial intelligence (AI) techniques, have emerged as significant threats to digital communication security and privacy. This paper explores the application of transfer learning-enabled Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to detect deep fake voices, combining data from two separate datasets: DEEP-VOICE and the ASVspoof 2019 dataset. Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients were used as features for processing the audio and as input to the pre-Trained CNN models. Experimental results demonstrate the performance of four pre-Trained CNN models employed: VGG19, EfficientNetB0, MobileNetV2, and InceptionV3, with InceptionV3 achieving the highest accuracy at 95.34%. This indicates the robustness and effectiveness of transfer learning in deep fake voice detection while utilising fewer computing resources and data. Overall, this study underscores the importance of integrating advanced and efficient AI methods, such as transfer learning, to develop reliable deep fake detection systems.

Title: From Fear to Features: Deep Learning on EEG for Early Screening of Learning Disabilities in Children
Abstract: Learning disabilities are one of the most common challenges a child will face in their school-age years, and emotional issues like fear and anxiety can rob them of psychological health as well as academic success. In this train of thought, a computational neuroscientific study on LD children being afraid can be successful by using electroencephalogram (EEG) data through an emerging technology including deep learning. Publicly available EEG datasets from four children with learning disorders (recorded under resting-state and fear-evoked conditions) were used. For both frequency bands, several sources were selected according to a combination of statistical and spectral properties, and a pattern of statistical dependency between the emotionally associated neural activities was identified. To manage the lack of informative samples, synthetic samples were generated using advanced over-sampling techniques like SMOTE and ADASYN. We tried and tested a few classification models and selected the best performing deep learning model (ResNet1D) achieved impressive results with an accuracy of 99.33%, Recall of 100% and an ROC AUC score of 0.9997, which again reflects how well it can discriminate fear-related brain patterns. The findings seem to confirm a fear-specific tuning of brain dynamics in children with learning disabilities, mainly on theta and beta frequency bands, which are modernly recognized markers of higher-order cognitive and emotional dysfunctions. These findings also demonstrate the potential of EEG-biased AIs as efficient and noninvasive instruments for early screening. However, the dataset has only four real LD subjects and extensively uses synthetic augmentation so the reported performance should be considered as proof of concept and remains to be validated on larger subject-wise clinical population with real controls. This approach offers new possibilities for integrating affective neuroscience into educational diagnostics, so that it is possible to develop plans of learning specifically adapted to the emotional and cognitive requirements of each child.

Title: Enhancing Measurement Accuracy Through AI-Driven Calibration and Error Correction in RF Spectrum Analyzers
Abstract: This study investigates the application of artificial intelligence techniques, with a particular emphasis on linear regression modeling, to improve calibration accuracy and systematic error correction in RF spectrum analyzers within a metrological framework. A supervised learning approach is proposed to characterize and model the relationship between reference power levels and measured instrument responses while accounting for both systematic and stochastic measurement deviations. Experimental data were acquired under controlled calibration conditions and subsequently subjected to preprocessing and normalization procedures to ensure data consistency and model robustness. The developed regression-based correction model demonstrated strong predictive capability, reflected by high coefficients of determination and reduced residual discrepancies between reference and measured values. Furthermore, the proposed approach maintains alignment with metrological traceability principles and measurement uncertainty considerations, thereby ensuring compatibility with established calibration laboratory practices. Beyond error compensation, the integration of AI-driven modeling enables enhanced diagnostic and predictive functionalities, including automated drift detection, performance monitoring, and data-informed maintenance planning. These capabilities contribute to improved measurement reliability, operational efficiency, and instrument lifecycle management. Overall, the results highlight the potential of AI-assisted calibration strategies to advance RF measurement systems toward increased autonomy, adaptability, and real-time optimization, supporting the evolution of next-generation intelligent metrological infrastructures..
