Title: Empirical Comparison of Feature-Based and Neural Frameworks for Multilingual Emotion Detection
Abstract: Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) is essential for improving human-machine interaction in applications such as virtual assistants, telehealth, and customer service systems. Nevertheless, the application of SER in the multilingual settings is still demanding because different languages have differences in their phonetics, prosody, and cultural expression. Conventional machine learning (ML) systems utilizing handcrafted acoustic features can become especially difficult to generalize in such cases, and deep learning (DL) models can capture more intricate emotional patterns to a larger extent. The paper is a comparative analysis of both the ML and DL methods in multilingual SER in terms of performance, cross-lingual robustness, and feasibility. It has been experimentally demonstrated that model XGBoost can attain an accuracy of 95.0% on the English dataset and model CNN-BiLSTM can attain an accuracy of 83.87% on the Hindi dataset, indicating that hybrid deep learning architectures are effective in complex multilingual tasks.

Title: AuthAI: A Hybrid Feature-Optimized Framework for Authorship Verification and Style Change Detection
Abstract: Effective techniques to differentiate between machine-generated content and human-written language are essential given the rapid development of generative artificial intelligence (Gen AI) models. This paper introduces AuthAI, a comprehensive system for authorship analysis that addresses two core challenges: Authorship Verification (AV) and Style Change Detection (SCD). For AV, we present a hybrid framework built on the ELECTRA (Efficiently Learning an Encoder that Replaced Tokens) transformer, optimized using advanced feature engineering with TF-IDF and the Shuffled Frog-Leaping Algorithm (SFLA) to accurately determine if a text is human- or AI-authored. For SCD, the system employs fine-tuned BERT and ALBERT models to detect stylistic shifts within a document, identifying whether it is single- or multi-authored and locating the precise points of change. Both pipelines are integrated into a unified, GPU-optimized deep learning approach, leveraging best practices like mixed-precision (FP16) training and gradient accumulation. Deployed within an interactive Flask web application with a secure MySQL backend, AuthAI demonstrates remarkable efficacy, achieving over 90% accuracy in authorship verification and high performance in style change detection. This proven, adaptable system provides a dependable instrument for ensuring digital content authenticity, with applications in plagiarism detection, forensic analysis, and literary research.

Title: Navigating remote leadership in the age of operational hybrid work: current Issues and innovative approaches
Abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated the shift to remote work, radically altering leadership styles across the globe. As businesses move toward hybrid work models that include in-office and remote work, managers must overcome new obstacles to sustain teamwork, engagement, and productivity. This study examines how remote leadership is evolving in the hybrid era, focusing on key topics such as performance management, employee well-being, trust-building, and communication challenges. It also examines how technology, such as AI-enabled instruments and online collaboration tools, might support effective leadership. The research identifies creative methods for resolving these issues by analyzing prior studies, case studies, and interviews with business leaders across sectors. The results highlight the importance of emotional intelligence, flexibility, and fair leadership for creating cohesive, productive teams. This article provides insights into the future of leadership in an increasingly digital and flexible workplace and concludes with suggestions for leaders seeking to succeed in hybrid work environments.

Abstract: Machine Learning in the optimization of AlN/GaN MOSHEMTs (Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor High Electron Mobility Transistors) to be used in the high-power and RF switching applications. Title: AI-Based Detection of Telemarketing Call Intent and Fraud Using Short-Duration Audio Analysis
Abstract: This paper presents a novel system that leverages the capabilities of Artificial Intelligence to facilitate the early detection of the purpose of a telemarketing call as well as the probability of a scam. This system only processes the first fifteen seconds of the call. The system leverages the capabilities of the OpenAI Whisper model to facilitate multilingual speech-to-text as well as the GPT-4 model to facilitate the classification of the call. A hybrid dataset was designed to include 2,500 real telemarketing audio samples as well as 3,200 artificially generated audio samples. The system's performance was evaluated experimentally to attain accuracy of 93.5%, precision of 92.8%, recall of 94.2%, as well as F1 score of 93.5%. The performance of the system was also compared to other machine learning approaches to demonstrate the efficacy of the system.

Title: Performance Evaluation of a Hybrid DSP-Machine Learning Steering-Model Using Radar Data in Single-Target Scenarios
Abstract: We present a comparative analysis of the Steering-Model, a hybrid DSP-Machine Learning approach for Direction-of-Arrival (DoA) estimation, against the FFT-based spatial-spectrum technique and the Multiple Signal Classification (MUSIC) algorithm. FFT-based methods provide computational efficiency, yet their resolution is constrained by finite aperture and spectral leakage. In contrast, MUSIC achieves super-resolution through eigenvalue decomposition and subspace separation, but incurs high computational cost and requires accurate source-count estimation. The proposed Steering-Model introduces a learnable Steering-Layer that replaces fixed subspace separation and steering vectors with trainable real-and complex-valued weights, formulating DoA estimation as a multi-label classification task over a predefined angular grid. The architecture comprises 52,152 parameters (305 KB), employs the Wasserstein distance as the loss function, and eliminates eigenvalue decomposition and source-count estimation requirements. Evaluation on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrates that the Steering-Model achieves sharper spectral peak resolution than FFT-based methods across various SNR levels and reduces computational runtime by up to 80% compared to MUSIC. Notably, although trained exclusively on single-Target synthetic data, the model generalizes to real radar data and multi-Target scenarios, resolving sources with angular separations as small as 10° in a 12-receiver array under moderate SNR conditions. The Steering-Model offers a practical alternative that balances computational efficiency and angular resolution, suitable for embedded implementations in sensor networks.

Title: A Multimodal Wearable Assistive Device for Deaf, Mute and Blind
Abstract: Assistive technologies are essential for improving communication and mobility for individuals with hearing, speech, and visual impairments. However, many existing solutions address only a single type of disability and frequently depend on smartphones or cloud-based processing, which introduces latency, privacy concerns, and usability limitations in real-world environments. This paper presents a multimodal wearable assistive system designed to support real-time communication and navigation for users with single or combined sensory impairments. The proposed system adopts a watch-centric architecture that integrates vision-based sign language recognition, lip movement analysis, speech-to-text transcription, text-to-speech synthesis, and obstacle detection within a compact embedded platform. To satisfy the computational and energy constraints of wearable hardware, lightweight deep learning models are employed, including MobileNet-V3 for gesture recognition and a CNN-BiLSTM architecture for lip movement recognition, while speech processing is implemented using an embedded automatic speech recognition pipeline. Vision inference is executed locally on an edge AI processor to reduce communication latency and improve data privacy. The system design emphasizes edge intelligence, multimodal sensing, and hands-free interaction to enable continuous assistive support in practical environments. The proposed approach demonstrates the feasibility of integrating multiple assistive functionalities within a single wearable platform, providing a scalable and accessible solution for individuals with sensory impairments.

Title: Large Language Model–Driven Feature Weighting for Cross-Device Harmonization of Wearable Data: A Generalizable Framework for Digital Health Models
Abstract: Wearable-based lifelog data offer a promising approach for digital mental health monitoring, but cohort heterogeneity, including device-specific measurement differences and variability in ecological momentary assessment (EMA) protocols, often limits model generalizability. To address this issue, we propose a large language model (LLM)-driven feature-weighting framework for cross-device harmonization in mood prediction. Leveraging few-shot learning, the framework infers cohort-specific rules from a small number of representative samples and converts them into executable weighting functions without requiring large-scale retraining. Four cohorts with distinct characteristics were used to generate cohort-specific weights, and an independent external cohort was used for validation. Model performance was evaluated by comparing classifiers before and after applying the generated weights, and traditional machine learning-based weighting methods were included as baselines to assess the validity of the LLM-based approach. Performance was measured using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and F1-score across five random seeds. LLM-based weighting improved external validation F1-score more consistently than machine learning-based weighting, particularly when GPT-OSS was used. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and correlation analyses indicated that the generated weights were actively used by the predictive models and were associated with relevant physiological and behavioral features. These findings suggest that LLM-driven rule-based feature weighting may improve the external generalizability of wearable-based digital health models across heterogeneous cohorts.

Title: A Compact, Autonomous, Submersible Holographic Microscope for Passive in-Situ Microbial Sensing
Abstract: The deep ocean remains one of Earth's most extreme and least understood environments, serving as a compelling analog to the icy ocean worlds beyond our planet. A major challenge in studying marine microbial communities is the difficulty of capturing and maintaining pressurized samples for laboratory analysis-a technique that becomes infeasible when operating in distant oceans across the solar system. To address this, we present a fully autonomous, submersible digital holographic microscope (DHM) designed for in-situ microbial imaging at depths down to 1000 meters. This compact, mechanically passive instrument contains no moving parts, enabling a robust, low-power architecture capable of operating reliably in harsh, remote environments. The internal electronics system is built around a Raspberry Pi 4 single-board computer that manages data acquisition, control, and sensor logging. Power is supplied by a 7000 mAh lithium-polymer battery and regulated by a Mini-box OpenUPS. Custom internal electronics further filter the power to reduce high-frequency noise before delivery to sensitive components such as the laser diode and Raspberry Pi, ensuring stable performance for noise-sensitive optical systems. The submersible supports both single and multi-wavelength DHM configurations. A collimated light beam is formed using a fiberpigtailed laser diode, which can be replaced with a multi-wavelength setup using a multi-wavelength or multi-diode fiber-coupled combiner. The base system operates at 405 nm, whereas multiwavelength configurations include 450 nm, 520 nm, and 638 nm to enable spectral absorption-based characterization. Interchangeable monochrome camera modules are supported, including a polarization-sensitive camera that enhances contrast and enables detection of birefringent structures, providing key metrics for analyzing microorganisms with complex internal morphology. All components are integrated into a compact package; thus, the instrument supports fully autonomous operation, with onboard software managing timing, environmental logging, and image capture. Initial deployments have demonstrated the successful performance of the custom housing and passive sample chamber at depths to 350 meters. Ongoing pressure and thermal testing are validating the structural and electronic integrity of the system at its 1000-meter target depth. Additionally, bio-safe 3D-printed resin components are being evaluated to optimize flow within the sample chamber, which functions without active pumping by leveraging natural liquid flow to direct microbial samples through the field-of-view of the imaging region. The complete software stack will be open-source, leveraging Python for control and logging, and C++ for time-critical tasks such as camera triggering and data acquisition. This architecture supports future integration of machine learning capabilities for eventtriggered imaging, adaptive sampling, and real-time microbial detection, thereby equipping the system to operate autonomously in environments where human intervention is not possible. Looking ahead, we plan to incorporate an internal thermal management system that sinks heat from high-power compute modules to the external housing and the surrounding ocean. This will enable the use of more computationally intensive platforms such as the Raspberry Pi with Hailo AI acceleration or NVIDIA Jetson modules, unlocking high-performance edge inference and onboard classification abilities. This complete system represents a foundational step toward autonomous, high-resolution biological analysis in environments where sample return is impractical and microbial life is most likely to be present.

Title: SurgXBench: Explainable Vision-Language Model Benchmark for Surgery
Abstract: Innovations in digital intelligence are transforming robotic surgery through more informed decision-making. Real-time awareness of surgical instrument presence and actions (e.g., cutting tissue) is essential, yet despite decades of research, most machine learning models rely on small datasets and still struggle to generalize. Recently, Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have achieved transformative advances in multimodal reasoning, suggesting strong potential for intelligent robotic surgery. However, surgical VLMs remain underexplored, and existing models show limited performance, underscoring the need for systematic benchmarks to assess their capabilities, limitations, and future development. To this end, we benchmark the zero-shot performance of several advanced VLMs on two public robotic-assisted laparoscopic datasets for instrument and action classification. Beyond standard evaluation, we integrate explainable AI to visualize VLM attention and uncover causal explanations behind predictions, providing a previously underexplored perspective for assessing model reliability. We also propose explainability-based metrics to complement standard evaluations. Our analysis reveals that surgical VLMs, despite domain-specific training, often rely on weak contextual cues rather than clinically meaningful visual evidence, highlighting the need for stronger visual and reasoning supervision in surgical applications. The code is provided in our public repository at: https://github.com/jiajun344/SurgXBench-Explainable-Vision-Language-Model-Benchmark-for-Surgery.

Title: Scalable Causal Tracing and Reproducible Episodes for Multi-Agent Systems
Abstract: Multi-Agent systems with Large Language Models enable complicated AI operations with distributed reasoning and coordination. The complex interactions between Multi-Agent systems challenge established observability paradigms. Agent-level coordination patterns, memory operations, and causal relationships required for debugging and optimising Multi-Agent systems are not supported by existing frameworks. MA-Trace is a complete observability framework that instruments causal linkages between agents, tools, and environments and ensures repeatable execution through deterministic replay. In MA-Trace, coordination graphs capture task delegation and negotiation structures, memory operation traces, and log episodic and semantic accesses with eviction reasons; environment contracts check state transitions with seed-controlled determinism. We establish innovative service level objectives as coordination efficiency, redundant action rate, and oscillation rate to evaluate multi-agent system health beyond existing metrics. Standard span models and exporters in OpenTelemetry provide compatibility with production observability infrastructure. ALFWorld and WebShop benchmarks show 55% mean-time-to-insight reduction with sub-1% performance overhead. Compared to baseline systems, this approach reduces coordination overhead by 26 %, duplicated actions by 50 %, and oscillation rates by 48 %. Internal model reasoning and external coordination traces match 70 % in causal path alignment validation. MA-Trace enables transparent debugging and systematic optimisation of complicated agent processes in multi-agent systems with production-ready observability.

Title: Hybrid Experimental–Machine Learning Framework for Environmental Optimization of Bio-Modified Bitumen
Abstract: The increasing need to use sustainable pavement materials has prompted the pursuit of alternatives to Petroleum bitumen made of bio-based materials. This work explores the environmental and mechanical behavior of bio-oil-modified bitumen within the framework of a hybrid experimental and machine-learning approach. Bio-binder was waste cooking oil used to partially replace conventional bitumen (ranging from 0 to 20 percent). The experimental analysis aimed to assess the binder's high-temperature deformation resistance using the rutting parameter (G*/sinδ). Three machine learning models were created with the use of key input variables such as bio-oil content, mixing temperature, aging condition, viscosity, and density to improve the predictive power and decrease the amount of effort expended on the experiment, including Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Random Forest (RF), and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost). Statistical measures such as R<sup>2</sup>, RMSE, MAE, and MAPE were used to assess model performance. XGBoost proved to be the most accurate, with higher accuracy than ANN and Random Forest. The environmental benefits have been estimated by quantifying the binder-related CO2 reduction when using bio-oil instead of oil. A Pareto optimization model was used to determine the best trade-off between environmental sustainability and mechanical performance. The findings suggest that a replacement level of bio-oil of 10–15% offers the most promising compromise, as it retains acceptable rutting resistance whilst achieving a considerable carbon reduction. In general, the suggested hybrid experimental-machine learning method can be considered an effective instrument for optimizing sustainable asphalt binder formulations and offers the possibility of the continuous incorporation of environmentally friendly materials into pavement engineering. The novelty of this study lies in integrating experimental characterization, machine learning prediction, and Pareto-based environmental optimization within a single framework for bio-oil-modified bitumen. Unlike previous studies that focused separately on mechanical performance and predictive modeling, the present work simultaneously evaluates rutting resistance, CO₂ reduction potential, and predictive accuracy using ANN, Random Forest, and XGBoost models to develop a sustainable and optimized asphalt binder formulation.

Title: Sea Surface Wind Speed From ICESat-2 Along-Track Wave Spectra
Abstract: Accurate estimation of sea surface wind speed is critical for oceanography, meteorology, and climate science. This study explores the potential of the advanced topographic laser altimeter system (ATLAS) onboard ICESat-2 to retrieve sea surface wind speed using along-track wave spectra (AWS). A deep neural network (DNN) model is employed to map the spectral features of the AWS, specifically the high-frequency equilibrium range, to 10-m wind speeds. The model was trained using ERA5 reanalysis data and validated against independent ERA5 datasets and in situ National Data Buoy Center (NDBC) buoy observations. The initial AWS-based model achieved an overall root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 1.34 m/s and a correlation coefficient against ERA5 data, demonstrating that ICESat-2 AWS contain robust wind speed signatures. Analysis of spectral sensitivity against wind speed and direction reveals that while the AWS is influenced by the relative angle between the satellite heading and wind direction, this directionality is not the dominant error source in moderate wind regimes. To further enhance accuracy, we integrated optical features and spatiotemporal information with AWS. This fusion model reduced the overall RMSE to 1.16 m/s against ERA5 and achieved an RMSE of 1.22 m/s against buoy measurements, indicating performance comparable to other spaceborne sea surface wind remote sensing techniques, although still exhibiting limitations under certain wind regimes. These findings suggest that ICESat-2 has the potential to serve as a complementary data source for existing global wind observation systems and provide an indirect validation of the reliability of the ICESat-2 AWS themselves.

Title: Navigating the Path to Carbon Neutrality Through Dynamic Digital Governance: Evidence From a Policy-Upgrade Perspective
Abstract: The intensifying global climate crisis necessitates a rapid transition toward systemic decarbonization, positioning urban carbon neutrality as a cornerstone of international sustainable development agendas. Within this framework, digital governance serves not merely as a technical instrument but as a critical transformative force for urban green transitions. However, most existing research conceptualizes digital interventions as static events, overlooking the dynamic marginal dividends generated by iterative policy refinements. This study addresses this gap by investigating the evolutionary path from the Information Benefiting the People (IBP) pilot to the Internet + Government Services (IGS) initiative, framing this transition as a strategic digital policy upgrade. To ensure robust causal inference, we employ a double machine learning (DML) framework and panel data from 266 Chinese cities. The empirical findings provide compelling evidence that digital governance significantly propels cities toward carbon neutrality. Crucially, this environmental impact is substantially amplified following the policy upgrade, confirming that the continuous optimization of digital platforms creates a synergy effect essential for long-term decarbonization. Mechanism analysis reveals that this dynamic empowerment is driven by the structural optimization of governmental attention, enhanced administrative efficiency, and the mobilization of public environmental participation. Furthermore, the efficacy of policy upgrading exhibits significant heterogeneity, with more pronounced benefits observed in larger cities and high-innovation hubs. These findings underscore that the path to carbon neutrality is not merely a matter of technical adoption but of continuous institutional evolution. This research offers a scalable blueprint for global policymakers to leverage dynamic digital governance as a catalyst for sustainable urban transitions.

Title: A Signal Processing-Guided Machine Learning Approach to Automated Detection of Time Signatures in Music
Abstract: Time Signature Detection plays a pivotal role in music information retrieval (MIR) and rhythm analysis. However, extracting meters directly from raw audio continues to remain a challenge. Traditional signal processing methods fall short of discriminative power, while deep learning models sacrifice interpretability for performance. This paper proposes a twostage framework to bridge this gap. First, we introduce a novel, interpretable signal processing pipeline. Using stem separation, spectral autocorrelation, and peak-consistency analysis, we infer the meter numerator, outperforming established baselines like ASM and BSM. Building on these insights, a machine learning framework was developed using informed feature engineering. By incorporating spectral, rhythmic, and harmonic representations, a Support Vector Machine (SVM) was trained on the Meter2800 dataset. This approach achieved 96% accuracy on binary (3, 4) classification and 94% on quaternary (3, 4, 5, 7) classification, notably outperforming both traditional signal processing methods and state-of-the-art ResNet18 model.

Title: Intelligent Vision-Based Framework for Billboard Detection and Information Extraction Using Deep Learning Techniques
Abstract: Billboards are still one of the major instruments in outdoor advertising, so their automatic detection and analysis, along with other means of marketing analytics, urban monitoring, and smart city applications, have become a must. But problems with identifying billboards arise from factors such as changes in lighting, background complexity, and camera angle differences, making it a tough computer vision problem. This paper presents a fully AI-driven solution capable of detecting, classifying, and extracting information from billboards in real-world settings. The system uses an annotated dataset of Street View images and a CNN-based object detection model, improved via transfer learning, to locate billboards with high accuracy. A classification component then further recognises the type of billboard, thereby facilitating better organisation and analysis. An OCR pipeline prepares the detected billboard areas for text extraction, enabling deeper insights into advertising occupancy and compliance. The model's performance is measured by precision, recall, F1 score, mAP, and OCR accuracy, and the results show that the method performs well in detection and that the extracted text is correct and reliable, even under challenging visual conditions. This integrated pipeline, unlike traditional methods that treat detection, classification, and text extraction as separate tasks, provides a more complete understanding of advertising content. The proposed model paves the way for easy, efficient implementation in large-scale commercial systems, automated monitoring, and datadriven decision-making in the outdoor advertising industry.

Title: AI-Assisted Medical Documentation in a Multilingual Swiss Health Care System: Proof-of-Concept Study
Abstract: Background: Medical documentation imposes a significant administrative burden on physicians and reduces time for direct patient care. Artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted tools such as automatic speech recognition and large language models (LLMs) promise to reduce this burden, but their performance in multilingual environments has not been explored. Switzerland is highly multilingual, and non-native German-speaking physicians may find documentation particularly challenging. Objective: This study aimed to compare the efficiency and documentation quality of four clinical documentation work-flows—including both AI-assisted and traditional methods—in a Swiss tertiary hospital setting characterized by linguistic diversity. Methods: In this proof-of-concept study at a Swiss tertiary hospital (Department of Plastic and Hand Surgery, Cantonal Hospital Aarau), two physicians—a native Swiss German speaker and a non-native German speaker—documented encounters with simulated patients having common hand disorders. Four documentation workflows were tested: (1) traditional dictation with transcription by a secretary; (2) real-time dictation using speech recognition software for voice to text transcription; (3) postencounter dictation transcribed by an AI (Whisper) and processed by a GPT-based agent; and (4) AI-assisted ambient dictation of entire appointments using audio recording and automatic transcription. Documentation efficiency was measured by recorded physician time, and note quality was assessed using a modified Physician Documentation Quality Instrument (PDQI-9) scored by three different LLMs. To protect patient privacy, only synthetic (simulated) patient data were used. Results: AI-assisted workflows—particularly workflow 4 (AI-assisted ambient dictation)—produced the shortest physician documentation times per report. In post-hoc comparisons, workflow 4 was significantly faster than solely the speech recognition software workflow (workflow 2) for both physicians (adjusted P<.001). For the non-native speaker, workflow 4 was not significantly faster than traditional dictation (workflow 1) after adjustment (P=.08). LLM evaluators assigned high absolute scores (median PDQI-9 >47/50); however, inter-rater reliability was poor (Krippendorff’s alpha=−.433, 95% CI: −0.444 to −0.416), indicating systematic disagreement that precludes definitive conclusions about documentation quality from these scores alone. Conclusions: AI-assisted documentation demonstrated significant time savings for the native speaker, though the reduction for the non-native speaker did not reach statistical significance in this pilot (P=.08). Such tools show potential to alleviate the linguistic challenges faced by non-native speakers, reduce administrative burdens, and enable physicians to spend more time with patients. However, the inconsistency of AI-based quality scoring suggests that LLMs cannot yet reliably replace human evaluation. Future studies should evaluate these workflows in real-world clinical implementation, address data privacy and security issues, and include human evaluators to validate the benefits observed in this study.

Title: A Design Thinking Approach to Developing Songtun for Student Assignment Management in Digital Learning Environments
Abstract: Task management has become a critical challenge for university students in the digital era, particularly in relation to missed deadlines and delayed assignment submissions, which can negatively impact learning performance and time management skills. Although various digital tools are available to support task organization, many existing solutions are not fully developed through genuinely learner-centered approaches, especially within the context of Thai higher education. This study aims to design and develop a mobile application named 'Songtun' to assist students in recording, tracking, and managing academic assignments by adopting the Design Thinking methodology as a human-centered innovation framework. The research involved 125 undergraduate students who participated in a real classroom implementation of the Songtun application. The research instruments included the developed application and a five-point Likert-scale satisfaction questionnaire. The development and evaluation process followed the five stages of Design Thinking: empathizing with users' needs, defining key problems, generating solution ideas, prototyping the application, and testing its usability in authentic learning environments. Participants used the application continuously over a two-week period, after which both quantitative and qualitative data were collected to assess system effectiveness and user experience. The findings indicate that the Songtun application effectively supports students in organizing academic tasks, reducing the likelihood of forgetting assignments, and encouraging more timely submission behaviors. Overall user satisfaction was reported at a high level (M=4.36, S D=0.52), with usability receiving the highest ratings among evaluated dimensions. These results suggest that integrating Design Thinking principles into the development of educational digital tools can significantly enhance learner experience and promote self-regulated learning practices. The study highlights the potential of the Songtun application as an innovative academic support solution tailored to the needs of students in Thai higher education institutions.

Title: Clinically Meaningful Phonocardiogram Denoising with Feature Aware Fine-Tuning for CHD Detection
Abstract: Phonocardiograms (PCGs) in conjunction with AI are increasingly used for detecting heart and lung pathologies. However, they are often corrupted by artifacts such as patient motion, background conversations, and equipment alarms, which can obscure cardiac murmurs critical for detecting congenital heart disease (CHD). In this work, we examine how denoising affects subsequent automatic CHD classification, and propose some considerations aimed to preserve a group of features commonly used by clinical classifiers. Our study couples a UNet-based spectrogram denoiser, pretrained on phonocardiogram recordings, with a clinically validated XGBoost screening model operating on interpretable, structured features derived from spectrograms. We show that applying a pretrained denoiser without proper adaptation substantially alters the distributions of clinically relevant features and degrades detection performance, despite achieving strong waveform reconstruction quality. Various fine-tuning strategies are examined to guide denoising toward preserving relevant features, starting with variations of the reconstruction loss, including Huber, L1, log-domain, and frequency-weighted objectives, preserving up to ≈92% of the diagnostic performance at 0 dB SNR compared to the observed on unaltered signals. Finally, we introduce a method for jointly training a convolutional denoiser and detector without phase annotations, with matching diagnostic performance in exchange for reduced interpretability. These results demonstrate that favorable reconstruction metrics alone (e.g., SI-SDR up to 14.77 dB at 0 dB SNR) are insufficient indicators of clinical fidelity, and that denoising strategies for PCG analysis should be explicitly aligned with downstream diagnostic objectives to ensure robust CHD screening.

Title: Enhanced Rainfall Prediction Using Conv1D and Temporal Fusion Transformers for Precision Forecasting
Abstract: The operational rainfall prediction function acts as the critical instrument for water resource management systems alongside functions that serve agricultural planning operations and disaster mitigation preparations. Preventing rainfall requires a review of ongoing data behaviors alongside complete evaluations using entire time-span historical data sets. The research establishes a deep learning structure built from the combination of Conv1D elementary blocks and Temporal fusion Transformer modules that feed into an MLP network for forecasting daily rainfall volumes. The Conv1D model identifies time-series changes in rainfall patterns by performing data analysis on existing sequences. Through its precise temporal tracking mechanisms, the Transformer network identifies patterns throughout every entry of the input data. The forecasting output of rainfall benefits from MLP layer data integration of results obtained from both Conv1D and Transformer models to predict the next period. The use of cooperating systems results in enhanced precision because they use specific methods to identify difficult nonlinear patterns and time-dependent forecasting properties. Presented assessments using past rainfall records confirm the model's effective performance by delivering accurate estimations in different areas.

Title: A Method for Synthetic Generation of Production Datasets for Machine Learning in Quality Prediction of Parts in Instrument-Making Manufacturing
Abstract: This paper proposes a method for synthetic generation of production data intended for training machine-learning models that predict the defect group of part batches in instrument-making manufacturing. The method targets the lack of fully labeled shop-floor data that is typical for low- and medium-volume production. Dataset generation is performed at the batch level and incorporates modeling of shift patterns, resource constraints, cumulative equipment wear, and human-factor effects. The core of the approach is an integral risk score that captures a nonlinear cause-effect relationship between batch defectiveness and technological and operational parameters, complemented by stochastic rare events that shape the tail of the quality distribution. The distribution of the nonconforming rate is parameterized via an external configuration file, enabling controlled class imbalance. Experimental validation on a synthetic dataset of up to 20,000 batches with time-based data splitting demonstrates that the trained model remains robust under severe class imbalance and that classification performance improves as the dataset size increases. The proposed method is positioned as a tool for preliminary development of machine-learning pipelines and for refining data collection requirements prior to deployment in a real production environment.

Title: Real-time multicenter semantic segmentation for laparoscopic gastrectomy: development, external validation and operating room deployment of an AI navigation system
Abstract: Background Laparoscopic gastrectomy is technically demanding and errors often arise from limited situational awareness. Artificial intelligence (AI)-based computer vision may enhance intraoperative recognition of instruments and anatomy, but evidence for generalizable, real-time deployment remains limited. Methods We conducted a multicenter study using laparoscopic gastrectomy videos from 4 tertiary hospitals. Data were split by institution into training, internal test, and external validation sets. A You Only Look Once version 10 (YOLOv10)-based model was developed to recognize 18 categories (11 instruments and 7 organs) and integrated into a lightweight user interface for bedside use. Mean average precision at Intersection over Union (IoU) 0.50 (mAP@50) and AP@[0.50–0.95] for boxes and masks, recall, and F1 score were calculated. The feasibility of live operating-room deployment was assessed. Surgeon cognitive workload was assessed using the National Aeronautics and Space Administration Task Load Index (NASA-TLX), and system usability was evaluated with the System Usability Scale (SUS). Results The training set comprised 4308 frames (41,066 labels); the internal testing set, 1803 frames (17,211 labels); and the external validation set, 721 frames (6685 labels). Training performance reached box precision 0.896, recall 0.891, mAP@50 0.937, and AP@[0.50–0.95] 0.846; mask AP@[0.50–0.95] was 0.809. On the internal testing set, box AP@[0.50–0.95] was 0.670 and mask AP@[0.50–0.95] 0.642. External validation achieved box precision 0.798, recall 0.773, F1 score 0.785, mAP@50 0.832, and AP@[0.50–0.95] 0.684; mask mAP@50 was 0.836 and AP@[0.50–0.95] 0.658. High-performing classes included stapler, ultrasonic scalpel, and forceps, whereas omentum and pancreas were relatively lower. The system operated in real time during laparoscopic gastrectomy on a laptop-grade GPU, providing on-demand overlays without workflow disruption. The NASA-TLX score was 26.72±6.51, indicating low cognitive burden, and the SUS score was 78.33±5.20, demonstrating good usability. Conclusions We present development, external validation, and live deployment of a real-time AI navigation system for laparoscopic gastrectomy across multiple centers. The model demonstrated robust detection and segmentation of instruments and organs and was feasible for bedside use. Prospective trials are warranted to evaluate effects on intraoperative safety, efficiency, and training.

Title: Prediction Model for Academic Burnout Using Machine Learning in University Students
Abstract: Academic burnout in university students constitutes a public mental health problem, with important repercussions on the academic performance and psychological well-being of students. Traditional assessment methods are predominantly reactive and lack predictive capacity for early intervention. This study proposes a machine learning-based predictive model using Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) to identify students at risk for academic burnout. The model was initially trained with survey data from 71 Peruvian university students, considering 18 academic, emotional and contextual variables. To improve robustness and generalizability, synthetic data were generated using the CTGAN model from the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) library, expanding the sample to 300 instances. The Oldenburg Burnout Inventory for Students (OLBI-S) instrument was used as the target variable. The model achieved an average R<sup>2</sup> of 0.70 (95% CI: 0.59–0.82) and an RMSE of 5.04 (95% CI: 4.71–5.36) under five-fold cross-validation. When evaluated on a hold-out set, performance increased to R<sup>2</sup> = 0.84 and RMSE = 4.43, indicating strong generalization. The SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) framework was used to ensure the interpretability of the model. Finally, the model was deployed as a REST API service using FastAPI, enabling real-time risk assessments. This approach enables early detection and promotes proactive mental health strategies within the university setting.

Title: Edge-Oriented Bearing Fault Diagnosis via Triple-Lightweight Network with Adaptive Pruning
Abstract: Real-time diagnosis of motor bearing faults is essential for fault detection and timely maintenance, minimizing operational risks. However, most existing approaches often depend on cloud platforms or high-performance local servers, which introduce latency and potential security vulnerabilities due to raw data transmission. To overcome these limitations, this paper presents an adaptive pruning triple-lightweight network (APTL-net), which achieves model lightweighting for edge deployment across three stages: model construction, feature extraction, and structural pruning. First, a lightweight fault diagnosis framework optimized for edge environments is proposed, enabling parallel training and recursive inference to eliminate the traditional trade-off between training efficiency and inference performance. Second, a frequency-domain decomposition-based, weight-sharing multiscale convolution module is designed to efficiently extract multiscale features from periodic signals while harmonizing scale variations. Moreover, a fully automated adaptive pruning strategy is proposed to dynamically group and remove redundant structures during training without manual intervention. Finally, APTL-net is deployed on the edge device and validated on the physical platform equipped with real hardware. Experimental results indicate that APTL-net achieves a diagnostic accuracy of 99.54% while reducing parameters by 47.82%, FLOPs by 49.98%, and edge inference latency by 20.59%, thereby delivering superior performance over existing lightweight fault diagnosis networks.

Title: Deep Feedback Cancellation in Hearing Aids
Abstract: Acoustic feedback is a persistent challenge in audio systems with both microphones and loudspeakers, such as hearing aids. Traditional adaptive feedback cancellation methods, while commonly used, still face limitations, which have recently been tackled with deep learning techniques. In this work, we extend our previously proposed Deep Feedback Cancellation (DFC) model to operate effectively on both speech and music signals. We further explore the benefits of pre-training and fine-tuning strategies, analyze critical system parameters influencing the convergence speed/steady-state performance trade-off, and conduct a comprehensive evaluation using both objective metrics and subjective listening tests. Additionally, we compare DFC not only against traditional methods but also DeepMFC, a recent DNN-based feedback cancellation system, demonstrating the advantages of our approach in diverse audio scenarios in terms of performance and computational complexity.

Title: NPLNet: A Noise-Prior Lightweight Network for On-Device Acoustic Fault Diagnosis of Railway Point Machines from Noisy Measurements
Abstract: Despite the remarkable success of deep learning in fault diagnosis for Railway Point Machines (RPMs), existing models often overlook the non-ideal conditions inherent in manual field maintenance, such as environmental noise and signal instabilities stemming from handheld acquisition. This leaves a critical gap: achieving high-performance diagnosis while maintaining the lightweight design required for end-to-end deployment on handheld diagnostic instruments remains a formidable challenge. We address this gap by proposing the Noise-Prior Lightweight Network (NPLNet), an end-to-end lightweight fault diagnosis network. To improve robustness to amplitude fluctuations, we introduce the Random Amplitude Perturbation (RAP) strategy, an empirical augmentation designed to mimic gain variations commonly observed in imperfect handheld acquisition. The architecture features a backbone that integrates a Noise-Prior Spectral Filtering (NPSF) module for robust noise suppression and stacked Attentive Hierarchical Redundancy-reduction Cell (AHRC) units for multi-scale feature extraction. This is followed by a Multi-granularity Semantic Aggregation (MSA) head that performs robust classification by fusing semantic information from the hierarchical feature maps. Experimental results on the noisy ZDJ9 RPM acoustic dataset demonstrate that NPLNet achieves a peak diagnostic accuracy of 99.59% with a high inference throughput of 228.9 samples/s on a single-thread ARM Cortex-A53 CPU. This performance demonstrates a favorable trade-off along the accuracy-throughput Pareto frontier, outperforming several lightweight architectures in accuracy while maintaining competitive CPU throughput. The proposed network provides a lightweight and noise-prior-guided solution for handheld RPM acoustic diagnosis in noisy environments.

Title: Emotion Analysis in Speech Based on Audio-Visual Fusion
Abstract: This paper introduces a deep learning-based emotion analysis method utilizing audio and video data, achieving enhanced accuracy in emotion recognition through comprehensive exploration of both modalities. The attention mechanism emphasizes the significance of key channels, capturing emotion-specific information more precisely. In the context of video analysis, this paper utilizes the R(2+1)D network, which effectively captures temporal relationships, enabling superior extraction of emotional features from video data. To holistically leverage audio and video information, this paper introduces a cross-modal attention mechanism to merge the two types of features. This fusion method aids in integrating information from different modalities, thereby enhancing the accuracy of emotion analysis. By focusing on the correlation between audio and video, this paper successfully elevates the performance of emotion recognition. Experimental results demonstrate significant advancements on a publicly available dataset (RAVDESS), achieving higher accuracy compared to previous methods. The success of this method lies in the comprehensive utilization of audio and video features and the introduction of a cross-modal fusion mechanism. This paper firmly believes that this approach holds significant research and practical value in the field of emotion analysis, providing a new perspective for a more comprehensive and accurate understanding and analysis of emotional information.

Abstract: Robot-Assisted Minimally Invasive Surgery (RAMIS) enhances surgeon dexterity, with newer platforms leveraging haptic feedback to further improve performance. Title: An Explainable Framework for Automated Speech Fluency Evaluation using Spectral Features with Statistical Classifiers
Abstract: Fluency is a critical component of oral communication and academic evaluation; however, traditional viva assessments are still subjective and inconsistent. Title: Collaborative optimisation of emotion regulation and audio synthesis based on PerformanceNet and multi-emotional music generation model
Abstract: In response to the three major challenges in AI music generation – limited chord representation, monotonous emotions, and low audio fidelity – this research proposes a novel end-to-end framework termed PEMF that integrates PerformanceNet with a multi-emotion music generation model. Title: Universal Sound and Language Understanding: A Deep Learning and NLP Framework for Multilingual Music Analysis
Abstract: In today's globalized digital world, music is being produced, shared, and consumed across diverse languages and cultures-especially on platforms like YouTube. Yet, most music analysis systems still focus on monolingual content, primarily in English, and struggle to scale across linguistic boundaries. At the same time, advances in deep learning have given us powerful tools: convolutional neural networks (CNN) for audio analysis, and transformer-based NLP models for understanding text. However, these are often used in isolation and rarely integrated into a unified framework for multilingual music understanding. This research work addresses that gap. We present a hybrid AI pipeline that combines AudioSet-pretrained CNNs for audio event detection with domain-adapted NLP tools for handling multilingual lyrics and metadata. By focusing on Hindi and English YouTube music videos, we demonstrate how this integration enables robust audio-text analysis, including transcription, translation, summarization, and keyword extraction-paving the way for better global music recommendation, discovery, and archival. We utilize the AudioSet-pretrained Cnn14 model for automatic audio event detection and integrate NLP techniques for summarization and keyword extraction from associated textual data.

Title: Anticipatory Analytics: Transforming Enterprise Decision-Making with AI
Abstract: In today's business environment, the critical challenge in enterprise activity is the non-transitional ability to predict market disturbances before they happen. Although significant milestones exist in the interaction intelligence world through the use of conversational AI systems, some conceptual differences still exist in the development of comprehensive analyses that involve the effective use of varying data flows along with contextual intelligence. In this study, the conceptual DRIFT- A conversational AI chat bot which has been already developed and functional is used. The framework is significantly more advanced in terms of requiring no reactive restrictions among intuitive multi-source data consolidation and dynamic context development. Using a rigorous methodological strategy involving the systematic use of longitudinal secondary data analysis techniques through the use of critical performance patterns among the business level along with qualitative evidence from the use of review-level organizational operational dashboards and the use of field-level investigation instruments among retail business, finance business, software business-as-a-service, or health business from 2020 to 2024. Analysis of the results shows dramatic improvement in performance, including the enhancement of lead conversion rates by as much as 124%, the increase in customer satisfaction rates from 75% to 91%, the decrease in response time by as much as 52%, and the improvement in predictive accuracy rates from 56% to 85%. Cross-industry implementations prove the effectiveness of these results, including the achievement of 17% stockouts and related revenue growth of 8.5% in the retail industry, the attainment of 31% and 22% in the reduction of unplanned downtime and emergency repairs of the manufacturing industry, and the reduction of fraud loss by 27% in the finance industry while reducing response times to merely 3 minutes from the initially 17 minutes. These findings set the groundwork for the application of anticipatory business intelligence in improving the ability of organizations to switch to predictive strategic decision-making rather than reactive analytics.

Title: A Multi-scale Residual Network with Hierarchical Feature Fusion for Robust Audio Deepfake Detection
Abstract: The growing number of audio deepfakes calls for strong detection tools to protect digital security and voice authentication. Presenting a sophisticated deepfake detection system that uses Constant Q Cepstral Coefficients (CQCC) and a multi-scale neural network with hierarchical attention, we get state-of-the-art performance on the ASVspoof 2019 benchmark. Our model achieves a record 4.91% Equal Error Rate (EER) by exposing minor synthetic artefacts via phase-aware feature extraction and adaptive attention techniques, hence improving baseline systems by 48.7%. Among the main innovations are: (1) Multi-scale phase analysis capturing vocoder distortions, (2) Dynamic frequency band weighting via cross-attention, and (3) Dilated residual blocks retaining temporal accuracy. While visual analysis shows the capacity of our model to detect discontinuous harmonics and anomalous energy spikes in synthetic speech, ablation studies show phase characteristics account for 33% of detection accuracy. Maintaining computational efficiency, the system far outperforms current methods (6.5% lower EER than prior best). With significant impact size (Cohen’s d = 1.24), statistical validation verifies p < 0.01 significance. These developments set fresh benchmarks for actual deployment in voice authentication, forensic analysis, and media verification. Generalisation to unknown spoofing tactics and real-time detection situations will be the subject of future development. With direct relevance in financial security, legal forensics, and disinformation avoidance, this study offers vital methods for fighting manipulation of audio produced by artificial intelligence. Our open-source solution allows quick integration into current speech verification systems.

Title: Multi-Modal Waste Recognition and Segregation Platform for Smart Cities
Abstract: The growing waste crisis in the world calls for intelligent, scaled, and automated solutions. Title: Enhanced Diagnostic Validation of the EfficientXGBoost Model for Accurate COVID-19 Pneumonia Detection
Abstract: In this paper, we put forward EfficientXGBoost, a hybrid model that combines EfficientNet-B0 to extract meaningful deep features with XGBoost to perform high-performance classification to enhance the automated detection of COVID-19 pneumonia on the basis of chest X-rays. In order to achieve robustness, the model was strictly tested through K-fold cross-validation to fully test its generalization ability over more data partitions. The presented system was compared to a vast variety of more traditional machine-learning algorithms including Support Vector Machine, Random Forest, and used separately XGBoost and deep learning models such as CNN, CNN + XGBoost, and DenseNet121 + XGBoost. By comparing the performance, as shown in the results of the experiment, in comparison to the traditional models, which obtained the accuracy of between 90 percent and 96 percent, and deep learning baselines, which reached up to 97 percent, the created EfficientXGBoost model, proved to be much more effective. The proposed method scored 99.10 in accuracy and always recorded higher precision, recall and F1-scores which were better than all other models used in the performance graph. These enhancements underscore the synergistic benefit of having EfficientNet-B0 optimized feature representation used with XGBoost in terms of high discriminative power of XGBoost. In general, the EfficientXGBoost model has an outstanding level of diagnostic reliability and stability highlighting its possible as a powerful clinical decision-support instrument to detect COVID-19 pneumonia within a short amount of time and with a high degree of accuracy.

Title: Beatless: A Deep Learning Approach for Percussive Removal in Music
Abstract: Melody, harmony and rhythm form the music audio's composition with rhythm being defined as the sequence of beats and other percussive elements. Despite being a fundamental component of all styles of music, the presence of a beat can adversely impact many functions, such as karaoke generation, remixing, melody separation and transcribing music. Current methods for separating the harmonic and percussive aspects of audio (e.g., harmonic-percussive source separation, NMF), are not ideal options for reducing beats. The performance, quality, and applicability of these methods, when applied to different musical styles, is often poor. With the rise of deep learning, music source separation has experienced major progress. Models such as U-Net, Wave-UNet, and Demucs have shown great ability to extract and remove audio sources with high quality. This paper reviews recent progress in deep learning applied to beat removal, mainly focusing on innovations in model architectures, lightweight real-time models and rhythm-aware designs. It also presents exploratory data analysis (EDA), which shows some key audio features such as zero-crossing rate, spectral centroid, and tempo that differentiate characteristics of beats compared to melodic elements. Also, the paper identifies some research gaps, including the lack of beat-annotated datasets, insufficient evaluation metrics specific to beat suppression and limited real-time implementations. The paper concludes with future research directions for more robust, advanced and user-friendly beat removal systems.

Title: ICA-Enhanced Feature Learning for Imagined Speech Classification Using Low-Density EEG
Abstract: Imagined speech decoding from electroencephalography (EEG) has emerged as a promising direction for non-invasive brain-computer interface (BCI) systems that can support communication without overt articulation. However, progress remains limited by the scarcity of publicly available datasets, the low signal-To-noise ratio of imagined-speech EEG, and the practical limitations of high-density recording setups. In this work, we revisit the Free and Easy Imagined Speech (FEIS) dataset, a lightweight 14-channel EEG corpus, to investigate whether a carefully designed classical machine-learning pipeline can improve decoding performance in a low-density setting. The proposed framework combines window-wise statistical and spectral feature extraction with first-and second-order temporal derivatives to capture temporal feature evolution, followed by Pearson-correlation-based feature ranking, an ICA-based feature-space transformation to reduce redundancy among selected features, SMOTE for class balancing, and classifier optimization using grid-searched SVM and XGBoost models. Under the subject-dependent protocol, the proposed ICA-SVM and ICA-XGBoost models achieve accuracies of $77.65 \pm 3.80 \%}$ and $73.43 \pm 4.72 \%$, respectively, improving upon the original FEIS baseline of 69.00%. Under the more challenging subject-independent protocol, ICA-SVM attains $73.33\%$ accuracy and ICA-XGBoost achieves $61.88\%$. These findings show that interpretable and computationally efficient classical pipelines remain competitive for low-channel imagined-speech decoding. At the same time, class-wise evaluation indicates that minority-class decoding remains difficult, highlighting the importance of reporting balanced metrics alongside accuracy.

Title: Hybrid Feature Selection and Classification Framework for Diabetes Prediction Using CFS, SSA, and Random Forest
Abstract: One of the common chronic metabolic disorders that require accurate and timely diagnosis is diabetes mellitus which helps reduce the risk of severe health complications. The paper presents a new hybrid machine learning model that will act in synergy with Correlation-based Feature Selection (CFS), the Salp Swarm Algorithm (SSA), and a Random Forest (RF) classifier to improve the prediction of diabetes. CFS method was applied to screen out unfounded and redundant data in the set and thus simplified the input variables. After that, the swarming concept of salps led to the SSA, which was used to further optimize the feature subset by including the most effective predictors in order to achieve better model performance. A Random Forest classifier was then trained on the optimized feature set and it uses the concept of ensemble learning to provide strong and precise predictions. In comparison with standalone classifiers and classical feature selection methods, the suggested CFS-SSA-RF framework was seen to be more effective across such important metrics as accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and Area Under the Curve (AUC), which is evaluated on a large-scale dataset on diabetes. The findings emphasise the predictive accuracy improvement, overfitting reduction, and the reliability of the framework as a useful, effective instrument in aiding clinical decision-making to diagnose diabetes.

Title: Comparative Study of ResNet Architectures for Photoplethysmography Sleep Apnea Detection
Abstract: Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA) is an unrecognized, highly prevalent respiratory disease that has important cardiovascular implications. The gold standard of diagnostics, polysomnography (PSG), is resource-consuming, complicated, and unavailable for mass screening. This paper presents a systematic construction of a powerful, automated sleep apnea recognition framework utilizing the more readily obtainable photoplethysmography (PPG) signal. A large dataset of overnight recordings from 246 subjects was used to systematically compare various deep learning models, such as a control 1D Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), a hybrid CNN-BiLSTM, and a deep Residual Network (ResNet). To guarantee the clinical generalizability of the results and to prevent data leakage, a stringent 5-fold subject-independent cross-validation procedure was used. Another important discovery recorded in the investigation is the instability of Focal Loss in the application to this task, which consistently caused model collapse. The final model obtained, a ResNet block trained on Binary Cross-Entropy and weighted on the classes, showed better performance. The ensemble model achieved an Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC) of 0.7997, a Precision-Recall AUC of 0.7463, and recall of 0.8852 at an F1-optimal threshold.These findings prove the model to be a highly effective and robust screening instrument, sensitive enough to realistically detect individuals at risk of sleep apnea, thus paving the way for more efficient and scalable diagnostic channels.

Title: EfficientNet-DR: A Deep Learning Approach for Diabetic Retinopathy Detection and Classification
Abstract: Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) is one of the main causes of preventable vision loss, especially among working-age populations. In this paper, an automated detection and multiclass classification system for DR is proposed, which is optimized for deployment on low-end devices with very confined hardware and limited software capabilities. For the purpose of this paper, we relied on the first ever published dataset representing the Indian population, IDRiD, that comprises pixel-level annotations of DR lesions and normal retinal structures. All images are also classified on the basis of DR severities ranging from 0 (no DR) to 4 (proliferative DR), which are essential while giving precise diagnoses and the need for intervention. Preprocessing techniques including data cleaning, resizing, normalization, transformations, and data augmentation form an integral part of our methodology to significantly improve model performance. The trained and validated model of EfficientNet-B0 achieved a testing accuracy of 84.2% for all the DR stages. The clinical utility of these results highlights the necessity to apply the idea of deep learning instruments to ophthalmology to more adequately screen system DR and patient outcomes.

Title: Integrated IoT and Deep Learning Architecture for Real-Time Crop Stress Detection and Irrigation Optimization
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become a crucial instrument of solving the resource optimization problems, climate resilience, and food security in poor countries due to precision agriculture. To implement real-time monitoring and decision support, this study proposes a combined architecture comprising of deep learning algorithms, multispectral drone cameras and appliance of the IoT, soil moisture sensors and nutrient sensors of the soil. A time-series predictor based on LSTM generated 9 2. 1 % accuracy in irrigation forecasting, and a crop-stress detection model based on CNN generated 94.8% classification accuracy. The system was introduced and evaluated over two crop cycles over a 1 5 0-hectare area of smallholder farms in rural India with significant improvements in agricultural productivity. The accuracy rate of 89.4% in identifying early diseases and pests led to a 28.6% decrease in water use, 17.5 % decrease in the use of fertilizers and 14.2 % decrease in the use of pesticides compared to the traditional methods. Yield performance was greatly improved with an average increase in crop production of 21.3 % and reduction in post-harvest losses of 19.6 %. Socioeconomic effects of the system were also proved with the reduction in labor dependency (32 %), a reduction in operating costs (18.7 %), and a net farmer income increase (24.5 %). The AI-based decision-support tool was also scalable by adapting to changing weather trends, with a 96.2 % generalization accuracy in different types of crops and soils. These results show that AI-enabled precision agriculture is a sustainable, flexible and cost-effective way to transform agricultural practices in poorly developed regions that ensure long-term stability and enhance livelihoods.

Title: Automated ECG Arrhythmia Classification Using Logistic Regression and Random Forest
Abstract: Electrocardiogram (ECG) plays an important role in the early detection and diagnosis of cardiac arrhythmias, which is one of the leading causes of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality globally. The process of manual interpretation of ECG signals is time-consuming and subjective, particularly in long term or large-volume recordings. The paper will rely on a machine learning-based automated ECG beat classification system to overcome these problems by utilizing classical algorithms of machine learning over the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Dataset. The researchers compare a linear model (Logistic Regression) and an ensemble-based model (Random Forest) for classifying multiclass ECG beats in an experimental reproducible environment. The segments of a heartbeat are each modeled as a 187 -sample number vector with five categories of heartbeats. Training and testing of 87,554 and 21,892 samples were done, respectively. To enhance scale-sensitive models, feature standardization is used to enhance numerical stability. Accuracy, precision, recall, and F1score (weighted) are taken to learn performance in consideration of class imbalance. According to experimental findings, the performance of Random Forest is much more effective than that of Logistic Regression in all metrics because it reaches 97.47 % accuracy and 97.30 % weighted F1- score, whereas the accuracy of Logistic Regression is 9 1. 4 8 %. The analysis based on the classes shows that the random forest recall is higher in the minority classes of arrhythmias and shows strong performance for nonlinear behavior and skewed class distribution. Such results confirm that ensemble-based classical machine learning models are effective and computationally efficient for ECG classification tasks. The code is available on the GitHub repository: https://github.com/mldlwork2026/ECG-LR-vs-RF

Title: Embedding Model Benchmarks for Text Classification
Abstract: The abundance of global news data creates a significant applied research challenge: enabling data-driven decision makers to rapidly identify topics of interest while filtering out undesirable content at production scale. In our case, the operational requirement is to classify approximately 600,000 multilingual news articles every day, motivating the need for a highly efficient and accurate automated pipeline. This paper compares the classification performance of three multilingual models-Gemma3, LaBSE, and mmBERT-as candidate components for such a pipeline. Each model, trained using a weighted random sampler to maintain a 1: 1 class balance during training, independently evaluates whether articles pertain to advertising, cyber security, or national security. Gemma3 and LaBSE rely on fixed multilingual embedding spaces, while mmBERT employs transformer layers that adapt embeddings during training; these architectural differences have implications for fairness and are discussed accordingly. We additionally acknowledge the methodological bias introduced by using Gemma-3 to generate training labels and then evaluating Gemma embeddings on those same labels. Beyond classification performance, we assess computation time and multilingual robustness, both critical considerations for large-scale operational deployment. Results indicate that Gemma3 and LaBSE compute substantially faster-typically under one minute per task-while mmBERT may require up to an hour. Across languages, all models demonstrate consistently strong but not perfectly language-agnostic performance, with F1 scores for English articles exceeding those for non-English articles by approximately 2%-10% depending on category. These findings inform the design of a scalable, real-time news classification pipeline capable of supporting high-volume analytic workflows.

Title: Neural network-based electrocardiogram signal abnormality detection
Abstract: An electrocardiogram (ECG) is a non-invasive diagnostic test that monitors the heart's electrical activity. It is a valuable instrument for detecting a variety of cardiac conditions. However, interpreting ECG data can be difficult, and diagnostic errors can have dire consequences. In recent years, machine learning techniques have been applied to ECG analysis to improve diagnosis and reduce error risk. In this endeavour, we propose an autoencoder neural network-based anomaly detection method for ECG analysis. Multiple layers of densely interconnected neurons comprise the encoder and decoder of the autoencoder. The encoder discovers a low-dimensional representation of the input data, whereas the decoder attempts to reconstruct the original data from the discovered representation. The autoencoder is taught a pattern of normal cardiac activity using normal ECG data. During testing, an ECG is deemed abnormal if the reconstruction error of the autoencoder exceeds a specified threshold. We evaluate the performance of the proposed method on a dataset of labelled ECG anomaly recordings. Our results indicate that the autoencoder method can detect anomalies in ECG data with an accuracy of 94%. In addition, we demonstrate that the method is robust to noise and generalizable to unobserved data. The proposed method demonstrates promising results for detecting anomalies in ECG data, which can aid in the diagnosis of cardiac conditions and reduce the risk of errors. Future research could involve further optimisation of the autoencoder architecture and investigation of the use of other machine learning techniques for ECG analysis.

Title: Hybrid machine learning models for predicting scour hole characteristics downstream of piano key weirs: a comparative analysis
Abstract: Accurate prediction of scour hole characteristics downstream of piano key weirs (PKWs) is vital for structural design and safety. This study employs machine learning (ML) techniques to predict scour parameters using inputs such as weir outlet key bottom slope, densimetric Froude number, and relative drop height. Extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) was also used for sensitivity analysis, identifying the densimetric Froude number as the most influential parameter–except for predicting the location of maximum scour depth. Four ML models–XGBoost, multilayer perceptron (MLP), support vector regression (SVR), and a stacking ensemble–were developed. Hyperparameters were optimized using grid search with cross-validation. Five hybrid models were created using stacking to enhance predictive performance. Evaluation using uncertainty analysis and regression diagnostics, including Taylor diagrams, showed that hybrid models consistently outperformed individual models. The best hybrid models achieved R<sup>2</sup> values of 0.864–0.966, NRMSE of 5.029–8.605, and average percentage errors ranging from 5.73% to 9.66%.

Title: Narrative2Nanyin: Generative Applied Intelligence for Heritage Nanyin Music
Abstract: Text-to-music generation has advanced but remains constrained by Western harmonic structures, limiting its applicability to non-Western traditions like the heterophonic Nanyin music. This paper introduces Narrative2Nanyin, a novel symbolic music generation system that creates multi-track MIDI compositions for Pipa, Sanxian, Dongxiao, and Erxian directly from narrative text. The system uses a culturally grounded tokenization scheme, NanyinTok, to capture pitch, rhythm, and instrument-specific techniques without relying on chords. Built on a BERT–GPT2 encoder–decoder architecture, the model is fine-tuned via Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) for efficient adaptation. An interactive interface enables expert-in-the-loop evaluation. Automatic evaluations demonstrate strong performance, with a Scale Adherence score of 0.803 and Dynamic Range score of 0.793, indicating the model’s ability to generate pentatonic and narratively expressive music. This approach advances culturally inclusive music generation by abstracting heterophony as a reusable representation.

Title: Algorithmic Support for Creative Learning: Assessing a Music Composition Intelligent Tutoring System from a Computer Science Perspective
Abstract: Advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI) have made its integration into the educational domain easy, with the improvement of Intelligent Tutoring Systems (ITS): adaptive computer systems capable of supporting (during the learning process) students in general, but particularly those with Specific Learning Disorders (SLD) such as dyslexia. The use of ITS has shown satisfactory results in many disciplines, but in the field of music it remains largely unexplored. In this paper, the concept of personalized adaptive learning is addressed in order to design and implement an AI-Tutor to support the individual study of the (dyslexic and non-dyslexic) student in the field of music composition. Taking advantage of Markov’s chains, a system was created that could note down (for each individual student) recurring errors in the harmonization of a musical bass line, and then suggest some reinforcement exercises to help overcome the difficulties: exercises generated by the system independently on the basis of the student’s mistakes, and not previously prepared by the teacher. The results showed that the AI-Tutor can be a useful tool to engage and motivate the student in the study of musical composition, thanks also to the personalized feedback proposed during the performance of the reinforcement exercises.

Title: Evaluation of Similarity Measures and Machine Learning Models for Collaborative Filtering in Recommender Systems
Abstract: Recommender systems are an important component of online platforms because they help people find relevant items in large amounts of data. Recommender systems are used in many areas, such as e-commerce, movie and music streaming services. They learn about a user's preferences based on their past interactions and make personalized suggestions. The effectiveness of recommender systems depends on several factors, including similarity measures, collaborative filtering strategies, and learning models. This paper presents a comparative evaluation of different similarity functions that are applied to compute relationships between users or items, followed by user-based and item-based collaborative filtering to generate rating predictions. Here we are comparing different machine learning models such as linear regression, k-nearest neighbors, and random forest are used for comparative analysis. Experiments are conducted on benchmark MovieLens100K and MovieLens1M datasets. The performance of all approaches is evaluated using rating prediction metrics, including Mean Absolute Error and Root Mean Squared Error, along with recommendation quality metrics such as Precision, Recall, and F1-score. Title: A Computational Approach for Music-Driven Group Dance Formation Generation
Abstract: Designing group dance choreography requires careful coordination of positional formations that align with musical rhythm while maintaining visual balance, spacing, and collision avoidance among dancers. This research has explored music-driven dance generation. Most existing approaches focus on individual dancer motion and do not effectively address the challenges of group level positional coordination. This limitation reduces their practicality to real-world choreography scenarios involving multiple dancers. This paper presents a music-driven system for automatic group dance formation generation using a modular learning-based approach. The proposed system breaks down the problem into three main stages: music structure analysis, positional formation generation, and transition optimization. Musical features such as tempo, rhythmic emphasis, and energy variation are extracted to identify suitable moments for formation changes. These features are then used to condition deep generative models that produce positional formations for a specified number of dancers. Two generative approaches, a Conditional Variational Autoencoder (CVAE), and a diffusion-based model, are investigated and compared to analyze their effectiveness in generating stable and visually balanced formations. To ensure smooth and physically feasible transitions between formations, dancer movement is modeled as a multi agent navigation problem and optimized using reinforcement learning based on Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO). Experimental evaluation demonstrates that diffusion-based formation generation produces more structured and stable positional layouts, while reinforcement learning based transition planning significantly reduces collision occurrences compared to non-learning baselines. The results highlight the effectiveness of combining music analysis, deep generative modeling, and reinforcement learning for group dance choreography. The proposed framework provides a flexible foundation for future research in automated choreography and creative performance applications.
