Title: Accurate diagnosis of mechanical faults in a single-phase AC electromotor through acoustic monitoring and machine learning techniques
Abstract: This study presents a non-invasive method for detecting mechanical faults in a single-phase AC electromotor using processed acoustic signals. Sound data were collected via a USB-connected microphone installed in the motor's electrical casing under diverse operating conditions. Ten statistical features were extracted from the acoustic signals and used as input to three classification algorithms: Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA), Quadratic Discriminant Analysis (QDA), and Support Vector Machine (SVM). Model performance was evaluated using confusion matrix metrics, including specificity, accuracy, precision, and sensitivity. Among the classifiers, SVM outperformed others, achieving average values of 99.5, 99.2, 97.1, and 96.7, respectively. The findings confirm that acoustic signal analysis is a reliable and cost-effective tool for real-time fault diagnosis in electromotors. Defects may be accurately found in the electromotor by using acoustic analysis to monitor its status. The proposed framework is adaptable to other rotating machinery through retraining, offering a valuable solution for predictive maintenance in industrial applications.

Title: Explainable Multi-Stage Alzheimer's Diagnosis Using Vision Transformers and GAN-Augmented MRI Data
Abstract: The type of disease, Alzheimer, has no cure, so necessary diagnosis at the earliest possible period is crucial to assist in timely intervention and developing of treatment. The current diagnostic frameworks have the limitation of having data imbalance, poor interpretability as well as weak generalization. To overcome them, the framework of explainable diagnoses that combines Vision Transformers (ViTs) to implement Wasserstein GANs with Gradient Penalty (WGAN-GP) to present a balanced synthetic MRI sample is proposed. The data are 4 cognitive levels, with the levels of no impairment, very mild impairment, mild impairment, and moderate impairment. There are 2560 high-resolution axial MRI scans per class. Through the world-scale local correlation in the spatial dimension and using the classification using the class-aware attention models, the ViT models can identify strong stage classification performance with increased sensitivity at earlier periods of impairments. Transformer Attention Maps and Attention Rollout enhance interpretability and empathize key brain regions with regard to context significance that can inform a clinical decision. By using experiments with hybrid set of real and synthetic scans, the researchers obtained a balanced accuracy of more than 99% and Matthews Correlation Coefficient of 97.5% indicating better detection of minority-classes and generalization of the model used. The method is an integration of generative data synthesis and interpretable transformers, which is a clinically advantageous and safe basis of beneficial AD diagnostic instruments

Title: Risk Stratification Framework for Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension Patient Management using LightGBM Model
Abstract: Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension (PAH) is a progressive cardiovascular condition linked to significant morbidity and death, rendering early risk assessment essential for tailored therapy and enhanced results. Conventional risk scoring methods depend on restricted clinical factors and often provide mediocre prediction accuracy with diminished interpretability. This paper presents a machine learning framework using the Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) method to categorize PAH patients into low, moderate, and high-risk classifications, therefore addressing existing constraints. The model incorporates clinical, haemodynamic, and biomarker data and was developed using a dataset of diagnosed PAH patients after preprocessing and feature selection. The optimized LightGBM model attained an accuracy of 97.33%, precision of 96.11%, recall of 96.00%, F1score of 96.01%, and an AUC-ROC of 0.98. SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analysis found mean right atrial pressure, NT-proBNP levels, and 6 -minute walk distance as main predictors improving interpretability. The proposed framework exhibits enhanced predictive performance and therapeutic significance, providing a dependable, data-driven instrument to facilitate early risk assessment and individualized therapy of PAH patients.

Title: Question-Aware Gaussian Experts for Audio-Visual Question Answering
Abstract: Audio-Visual Question Answering (AVQA) requires not only question-based multimodal reasoning but also precise temporal grounding to capture subtle dynamics for accurate prediction. However, existing methods mainly use question information implicitly, limiting focus on question-specific details. Furthermore, most studies rely on uniform frame sampling, which can miss key question-relevant frames. Although recent Top-K frame selection methods aim to address this, their discrete nature still overlooks fine-grained temporal details. This paper proposes QA-TIGER, a novel framework that explicitly incorporates question information and models continuous temporal dynamics. Our key idea is to use Gaussian-based modeling to adaptively focus on both consecutive and non-consecutive frames based on the question, while explicitly injecting question information and applying progressive refinement. We leverage a Mixture of Experts (MoE) to flexibly implement multiple Gaussian models, activating temporal experts specifically tailored to the question. Extensive experiments on multiple AVQA benchmarks show that QA-TIGER consistently achieves state-of-the-art performance. Code is available at https://aim-skku.github.io/QA-TIGER/

Title: An AI Framework for Microanastomosis Motion Assessment
Abstract: Proficiency in microanastomosis is a fundamental competency across multiple microsurgical disciplines, especially in neurosurgical training for procedures such as cerebrovascular bypass, where restoring brain perfusion and function is vital. These procedures demand exceptional precision and refined technical skills, making effective, standardized assessment methods essential for guiding surgical education and ensuring practitioner competence. Traditionally, the evaluation of microsurgical techniques has relied heavily on the subjective judgment of expert raters. While expert assessments offer valuable insights, they are inherently constrained by limitations such as inter-rater variability, lack of standardized evaluation criteria, susceptibility to cognitive bias, and the time-intensive nature of manual review. These shortcomings underscore the urgent need for an objective, reliable, and automated system capable of assessing microsurgical performance with consistency and scalability. To bridge this gap, we propose a novel AI framework for the automated assessment of microanastomosis instrument handling skills. The system integrates four core components: (1) an instrument detection module based on the You Only Look Once (YOLO) architecture; (2) an instrument tracking module developed from Deep Simple Online and Realtime Tracking (DeepSORT); (3) an instrument tip localization module employing shape descriptors; and (4) a supervised classification module trained on expert-labeled data to evaluate instrument handling proficiency. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the framework, achieving an instrument detection precision of 97 %, with a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 96 %, measured by Intersection over Union (IoU) thresholds ranging from 50 % to 95 % (mAP50-95). Additionally, the supervised skill classification module attains an overall accuracy of 87 % in reproducing expert assessments across three categories: Poor, Moderate, and Good. These findings underscore the potential of advanced computer vision techniques to provide objective, efficient, and high-fidelity assessments of surgical skill, thereby supporting more standardized training and evaluation in neurosurgical education. Clinical relevance - The proposed AI-aided surgical skill assessment framework facilitates an enhanced microanastomosis training experience for neurosurgeons.

Title: Speech-Driven Detection of Spam Calls with Whisper and RoBERTa Models
Abstract: This paper presents a real-time spam call detection system that combines speech-to-text transcription using OpenAI's Whisper model with content-based and machine learning-based spam analysis using a fine-tuned XLM-RoBERTa classifier. The system processes audio call recordings in segmented chunks, transcribes speech to text, and detects suspicious keywords or scam-like patterns using both rule-based and probabilistic methods. A Gradio-based user interface enables live transcription, progress monitoring, and playback interruption upon spam detection. The proposed method provides reliable detection of scam or robocalls with actionable insights in real-time and showcases the integration of modern NLP and audio processing techniques in voice security applications.

Title: Tadeusz Kantor—Artist of the Digital Age
Abstract: This article explores the enduring relevance of Tadeusz Kantor’s theatrical innovations within the context of contemporary digital performance. By analyzing Kantor’s radical redefinition of stage objects—particularly his concepts of bio-objects and emballage (wrapping)—the study demonstrates how his vision of autonomous, agential materiality prefigures modern experiments with digital avatars, generative AI, and immersive technologies. The authors trace the evolution of Kantor’s costume-as-actor paradigm into virtual avatars and AI-generated music, arguing that these digital quasi-objects extend his legacy by challenging anthropocentric hierarchies and redefining performer–audience dynamics. Through case studies such as the hybrid opera Orfeo & Lwanda (2024) and AI-based compositional systems, the paper examines how Kantor’s emphasis on object autonomy resonates with posthumanist frameworks, in which algorithms function as bodiless co-creators. The analysis also addresses aesthetic and ethical tensions arising from AI’s role in the performative arts, including questions of authenticity, emotional violence, and the “audio uncanny valley.” By situating Kantor’s theories within debates on digital twins, metaverse scenography, and neural-network-based perception, the article positions his work as a foundational lens for understanding theatre’s evolving relationship with technology.

Title: Multi-Speaker Speech Detection and Separation in Overlapping Scenarios: A Deep Learning Approach
Abstract: One of the biggest challenges involved with separating the speeches of multiple speakers in a noisy or overlapping speech environment is with regard to audio signal processing when there are more than two speakers speaking simultaneously. Even the best two-speaker separation circuits face challenges with regard to overall performance characteristics of the system. It was necessary to design a deep learning model with the help of a dual path Conformer that supports both simultaneous separate processing of speeches and overall recognition of those speeches. In the designed system, separate mixed speeches can be successfully generated from the dual path Conformer module that involves a deep learning approach with the support of multiple state-of-the-art modules such as Conv-Tas-Net, SepFormer, ECAPA-TDNN, and TF-Grid-Net. For assessing the performance of the designed system, multiple performance measures such as Scale-Invariant Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SI-SNR), Word Error Rate (WER), and Perceptual Evaluation of Speech Quality (PESQ) can be used. The system achieves SI-SNR improvements of 15-20 dB on clean mixtures and 10-15 dB under noisy conditions, with speaker identification accuracy exceeding 95% on standard benchmarks. State-of-the-art systems achieve SDR improvements of 12-18 dB on WSJ0-2mix datasets. Real-time factors below 0.1 for Conv-TasNet and 0.3-0.8 for transformer-based models demonstrate computational efficiency across different deployment scenarios. Apart from these modern performance measures, the designed system also supports real-time domain generalization performance characteristics that can adapt easily with multiple speakers with appropriate accuracy. It provides real-life applications in emergency situations, healthcare communication networks, and event organization, where appropriate understanding of overlapping speakers is crucial to facilitate proper communication and decision-making

Title: Intelligent Earthquake Forecasting Using a Dual-Layer DQN-ViT Model for Complex Spatio-Temporal Pattern Recognition
Abstract: Earthquakes have been one of the most devastating natural disasters, which result in massive human havoc, destruction of infrastructure and economic damages. The use of traditional seismological methods tends to be ineffective in the complex spatio-temporal dynamics of a seismic activity and this restricts the level of accuracy of earthquake predictions. To tackle these issues, this project will suggest a sophisticated earthquake prediction system based on deep reinforcement learning (DQN) with a Vision Transformer (ViT) that will utilize massive geological and seismic and feature images to predict earthquakes. The model will detect the latent time pattern within the seismic events and spatial relationships of the earthquake effects and classify the effects of earthquakes in terms of low, medium, high damage. An intensive data pre-processing pipeline and an extensive exploratory data analysis is used to make sure of a high-quality input data and this is essential to solid model performance. The experimental evidence proves that the given approach has an accuracy of 99.78 in providing the result when compared to the traditional statistical and machine learning techniques. This model helps reduce risks of disasters occurring by improving early-warning features, which allows the mitigation of disasters that can lead to disasters through early and prioritized response to emergency actions. Its incorporation in earthquake preparedness measures can drastically decrease human and economic casualties and can serve as a valid instrument of enabling authorities and communities to Bolster resilience to seismic threats.

Title: Facial Expression-Guided Music Generation and Recommendation: A Multi-Modal Approach to Emotional Music Synthesis
Abstract: Music is an important element of communication and expression of emotions. This paper describes a new multimodal AI, which is a hybrid of human psychology and high-end music generation to create emotionally adjustable music on the spot. This system records the live emotional status of the user by analyzing his face expression and translates the expression to personalized musical performance. The architecture is constituted of four fundamental parts, which are real-time emotion detection, contextual enhancement, music generation, and music recommendation. Recognition of emotions is carried out through face-api.js which recognizes seven basic emotions at 100 ms frame-processing rate to make sure of low latency and high responsiveness. An enhancement layer of the context is added to add user feedback and optional text input in order to improve emotional interpretation. To compose, the system uses Facebook MusicMe-Small, which transforms the emotional prompts into expressive musical parameters. The recommendation engine also compares emotional vectors and audio characteristics that give mood-congruent music in a curated database with the help of cosine similarity. According to experimental analysis, the median response time is 13.1ms, and emotional relevance is 15 percent higher than the conditions with evaluation of emotion-only systems. User interaction is also improved with the interactive interface which displays the emotions in real-time and allows the user to play it back. The article adds to the progress of affective AI and human-computer interactions in music, and has a solid implication of therapeutic, entertainment, and UX uses. The improvement in the future will be based on adding more biometric inputs, more detailed emotional models, and clinical research to evaluate the long time benefit of well being.

Title: Future-Proof: An Application of AI to Multi-Agent Cyber Defence System for Predictive Threat Analysis
Abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become a life-changing contributor to contemporary computing systems, making machines capable of producing human-like outputs in various domains, including text, image, music and code. Although these capabilities open up new vistas of automation and creativity, they also bring a spectrum of ethical issues, durability and interoperability in machines; data privacy breaches; algorithmic biases; concerns about content authenticity and the possibility for misuse. In this paper, we explore the ethical aspect of Generative AI and provide a responsible governance-based approach to achieve a balance between openness and accountability. Building on a review of recent literature and on empirical evidence from real-world AI deployments, we investigate how ethical lapses may become visible in generative models and point to the limitations in existing regulation and design practices. We present an end-to-end framework that systematically embeds transparency, fairness, and accountability in the AI lifecycle by applying bias mitigation methods, explainable AI modules, and risk-aware optimization techniques. The key part of our approach is to tradeoff between content fluency and ethical considerations on real datasets. Experimental results show that our method can maintain the performance and reduce the population of ethical violations. The findings suggest that incorporating ethical reasoning into Generative AI models does not come at the cost of stifled innovation. The paper ends by presenting institutional-level recommendations to utilize Generative AI with a sense of responsibility across the university, industry and governance.

Title: Multimodal Fusion for Hate Speech Detection in Videos: An Ablation Study on Modality Effectiveness
Abstract: Detection systems that use multimodal data are necessary due to the quick spread of hate speech on video platforms. An ablation study of a multimodal framework that combines text (BERT), visual frames (ResNet-50), and audio (MFCCs with Bi-LSTM) features is presented in this paper. The results show that the text-plus-audio model performs the best (87.33% accuracy, 88.41% F1-Score), which defies the notion that more modalities lead to better performance. Importantly, adding visual features results in a "fusion collapse,"which continuously deteriorates the output. This highlights the significance of linguistic and paralinguistic cues and the fact that strategic modality fusion, as opposed to merely aggregating all available data, is necessary for effective multimodal detection.

Title: Context aware Variational Autoencoder model for personalized music Recommendation
Abstract: Recent years has witnessed tremendous growth of the multimedia data from multimedia streaming platforms such as spotify and amazon. Hence it is becoming mandatory to provide advanced recommendation facilities to support user on providing the data suggestion on basis of their preference which reduces the searching time on the massive collection of data. However, modeling the user and music to exploit complex relationship considered as primary challenges of the recommendation system. In addition, recommendation modeling leads to cold start, data sparsity and long tail recommendation issues. Many recommendations model using machine learning and deep learning model has been presented but those architecture lags in security, accuracy and efficiency as streaming data is exploring in large extent. In order to handle those challenges, a new context aware variational Autoencoder model for personalized music recommendations has been proposed as well-designed deep learning based generative model. It is considered as Autoencoder model where its encoding distributions of the context data is regularized during training process to obtain the latent spaces for efficient recommendation. In particular, context data incorporates the user behaviors such as music listening records, music playing sequence and sessions. Initially low dimensional feature representation(embedding) of music pieces has to be carried out using encoder process from the high dimensional information network. It is considered as latent space which is composed of the different embedding to highlight different music aspect on interacting with various neighbour. Next, Variational Autoencoder captures intrinsic and extrinsic features of the item and user along dynamic relevance and interaction of different embeddings. Finally variational interference layer provides the music recommendation on basis of context information. Experimental result of the current Variational Autoencoder model is conducted using various real dataset and performance evaluation is carried out to verify accuracy and effectiveness of current approach against baseline approaches towards music recommendation.

Title: AI-Generated Emotional Background Music for Learning-Related Well-being: Task-Dependent Effects on Cognitive Performance, Workload, and Physiological State
Abstract: INTRODUCTION: Background music is frequently incorporated into learning environments not only to enhance cognitive engagement but also to regulate learners’ affective state and perceived mental effort, both of which are closely associated with learning-related well-being. However, empirical findings regarding its impact on memory performance remain inconclusive and appear to be contingent upon task characteristics as well as the emotional properties of the auditory stimulus. Recent advances in Artificial Intelligence Generated Content (AIGC) enable the parametric synthesis of music with systematically controllable emotional attributes (e.g., valence, arousal, motivational tone), thereby providing a novel methodological pathway for examining how adaptive auditory environments may support learners’ cognitive functioning, stress regulation, and psychological well-being beyond the constraints of pre-composed music. OBJECTIVES: This study investigates how emotionally differentiated AI-generated background music influences memory performance, subjective workload, and user preference within learning contexts, with particular attention to task-dependent effects across numerical and image-based memory paradigms. METHODS: Seventeen participants completed both numerical recall and visual memory tasks under four auditory conditions: positive/motivational, soothing, focus-oriented (Low-arousal) AI-generated music, and a silence control. Behavioural accuracy was recorded alongside indicators of electroencephalography (EEG) and heart rate variability (HRV). Subjective workload and affect were assessed using the NASA Task Load Index (NASA-TLX) and the Positive and Negative Affect Schedule (PANAS). RESULTS: Results revealed dissociable, task-dependent patterns across behavioural and psychophysiological measures. Silence yielded the highest accuracy in numerical memory tasks, whereas positive-valence music was associated with enhanced performance in image memory conditions. Distinct categories of AI-generated music also elicited differential neural and autonomic responses, suggesting variations in affective regulation and cognitive load during task execution, with focus-oriented music emerging as the most preferred auditory condition for sustained learning. Although overall behavioural accuracy remained relatively stable across conditions, emotionally parameterised AI-generated music may function as autonomy-supportive cognitive scaffolds CONCLUSION: These findings provide preliminary evidence that AIGC-driven auditory environments may function as autonomy-supportive cognitive scaffolds that dynamically regulate stress and attentional demands during task engagement. By adaptively aligning emotional soundscapes with task characteristics and user state, AI-generated background music holds promise as a well-being-aware intervention capable of promoting cognitive sustainability and reducing perceived mental strain in digitally mediated learning systems.

Title: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence for Designing Technological Nature-Inspired Performance Spaces
Abstract: This research looks at how AI and biophilic design may work together to develop performance venues that are beneficial for the environment and make people feel happy. As modern architecture progresses towards designs that are better for people and the environment, theatres and music halls are great places to mix AI-driven optimizations with designs that are inspired by nature. The study includes surveys and computer studies to find out what consumers enjoy about biophilic elements, how well AI algorithms work for design optimization, and how satisfied users are with critical environmental factors. The findings show that people appreciate things that originate from plants and natural light. Reinforcement Learning is the best technique for AI to aid in meeting design deadlines, improving sound quality, and saving energy. The research shows how mental health, green building, and AI innovation may work together. Architects, designers, and cultural groups need to know this information.

Title: Partially Fake Audio Detection Based on Mamba and Tensor Feature Fusion
Abstract: In recent years, models related to Artificial Intelligence Generated Content (AIGC) have advanced rapidly, opening up new possibilities for generating realistic speech. However, if misused, this technology can pose significant risks to information security. Consequently, the task of deepfake audio detection has emerged. Within this domain, the Manipulation Region Location (MRL) task specifically aims to identify the manipulated segments of speech, offering greater precision and facilitating downstream tasks such as intent analysis. In this paper, we first investigate the performance of various feature types in the MRL task to determine which features exhibit the best generalization ability. Then we propose a tensor-based feature fusion strategy to effectively capture the interrelationships among different features and produce a more representative fused feature. Furthermore, leveraging the strong temporal modeling capabilities of Mamba, we incorporate it into our framework. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to introduce Mamba into the MRL task. The model is trained on the ADD2023 dataset. Experimental results on the test set demonstrate that our approach achieves a 37.5% improvement in performance over the baseline system and outperforms other compared models.

Title: Multi-Scale Feature Extraction and Fusion for Presbyopic Lens Wavefront Detection
Abstract: To achieve high-precision and efficient evaluation of imaging quality in presbyopic lenses, this study proposes a deep learning-based wavefront aberration detection method for presbyopic lenses. This approach eliminates the dependency on centroid localization algorithms and precision microlens arrays inherent in traditional Shack-Hartmann sensors by establishing an end-to-end mapping from Hartmann sub-aperture spot patterns to Zernike coefficients. A virtual inspection system was constructed using an optical simulation platform to generate a synthetic dataset comprising lens spot patterns and their corresponding ground-truth 36-term Zernike coefficients. And constructed a multi-scale convolutional fusion network (MCFN) based on deep learning, whose core innovation lies in the network's two-stage feature processing architecture: multi-scale feature extraction network based on residual asymmetric convolution module(RAC) and multi-scale attention fusion module(MDPFA), which synergistically integrates shallow structural features and deep semantic features.Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves strong agreement with ground-truth lens wavefront reconstructions and exhibits superior wavefront aberration detection performance compared to existing methods. This methodology provides a novel framework for guiding lens design optimization and establishes an effective paradigm for aberration characterization in presbyopic lens manufacturing.

Title: Interpretable XAI-Driven Crop Price Prediction System Integrating Climatic and Market Dynamics for Trustworthy and Informed Agricultural Decision-Making
Abstract: Stability of agriculture, food security and economic planning depend on precise price prediction of crops. By incorporating both climatic and market dynamics and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI), one can make agricultural systems more transparent and build trust in their predictions. Nevertheless, most current models of crop price forecasting are plagued by low interpretability, weak nonlinear dependence treatment, and they cannot provide information on how climatic and economic variables affect the results of the predictions. To overcome these shortcomings, the proposed Explainable Hybrid Deep Learning using SHAP-based Interpretability (EHDL-SHAP) framework uses Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) to find temporal climatic effects, and Gradient Boosted Regression Trees (GBRT) to identify non-temporal market dynamics. SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) is also used to give explainable information by measuring the impact that each feature makes to the eventual prediction. The suggested system allows making agricultural choices based on the data and being transparent at the same time, correlating the predictions of the models with the reality of climatic and economic conditions. The experimental analysis of multi-regional crop data data shows that E HDL-SHAP has a stronger prediction accuracy, interpretability, and stakeholder confidence than traditional black-box models do. The framework is a smart, articulable and dependable instrument that farmers, policymakers, and agribusiness can use as a reference to make a substantial decision on crop management and pricing. The suggested approach significantly enhances the prediction performance of 94.8 percent, regional generalization performance by 0.9 percent or so, and the prediction performance of the temporal dependency captures the highest correlation.

Title: An Explainable MFCC-Based Deep Learning Framework for Song Emotion Recognition
Abstract: Automatically identifying the emotional elements within a piece of music and understanding music sentiment through audio captures an essential step within the realm of affective computing and music intelligence. This paper introduces a hybrid architecture that combines CNN, BiLSTM, and Attention, utilising CNN to analyse MFCC features extracted from audio signals, BiLSTM to model the audio sequence, and Attention to pinpoint emotionally salient regions. In addition to the mentioned features, the proposed architecture incorporates cost-sensitive learning to enhance performance and mitigate data imbalance. The MFCC-based deep learning framework is applied to song music in the RAVDESS dataset. The proposed method achieved an overall accuracy of 91.6% and a macro F1-score of 92.3%. Explainable AI, utilising Gradient-Based Feature Importance, focuses on the low-spectral to mid-spectral regions where the audio is emotionally and temporally impressive. These confirm that the proposed architecture is streamlined to label singing through music analysis emotionally. This can be extended to various applications, such as affective music in music therapy and Human-computer interaction.

Title: Research on Multi-Dimensional Time Series Prediction Model Based on PPCH-LSTM and Gradient Boosting Decision Tree
Abstract: This study establishes a predictive framework for sports performance analytics through the integration of multi-dimensional competition metrics. We propose a dual-model architecture addressing two core technical challenges: (1) quantitative outcome prediction via a PPCH-LSTM (Player-Program-Country-History Long Short-Term Memory) model and (2) breakthrough probability estimation using a gradient boosting decision tree (GBDT). For the prediction task, four computational metrics are constructed: athlete capability (weighted historical achievements and participation frequency), program competitiveness (discipline-specific performance indices), national capacity (hosting experience and team scale), and historical trends (cumulative performance records). The PPCH-LSTM model, configured with 200 hidden layers, achieves an RMSE of 0.663 on the test set when trained on historical competition data, demonstrating robust temporal pattern capture. Concurrently, the GBDT model optimizes breakthrough probability estimation through feature engineering of athlete participation density, event competitiveness metrics, and economic indicators, attaining an AUC of 0.76. Experimental results reveal declining performance trends for 8 of the top 10 nations in 2024 forecasts. Correlation analyses further identify nation-specific pivotal disciplines (e.g., ρ=0.9 for racquet sports in one nation, ρ=0.89 for aquatic sports in another). This work provides a technical framework for sports analytics through hybrid deep learning and ensemble methods, with generalizability to multi-disciplinary competitions.

Title: Method for Enhancing Underwater Images based on Optimized Multi-Scale Structures
Abstract: Underwater images are afflicted by dynamic blur, low illumination, poor contrast, and noise interference, hampering the accuracy of underwater robot proximity detection and its application in marine development. This study introduces a solution utilizing the MIMO-UNet network. The network integrates the Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling module between the encoder and the decoder to augment feature extraction and contextual information retrieval. Furthermore, the addition of a channel attention module in the decoder enhances detailed feature extraction. A novel technique combines multi-scale content loss, frequency loss, and mean squared error loss to optimize network weight updates, enhance high-frequency loss information, and ensure network convergence. The effectiveness of the method is assessed using the UIEB dataset. Ablation experiments confirm the efficacy and reasoning behind each module design while performance comparisons demonstrate the algorithm's superiority over other underwater enhancement methods.

Title: AI and Journalism: The Future of News Podcasts
Abstract: AI is changing the entire process of producing, distributing, and consuming news that is largely driven by the growing field of news podcasts. Technological advancements in AI such as natural language processing, synthesized speech, automated audio transcription, and content curation not only reveal the major changes that are coming in content generation but also signal how news organizations will interact with pod-casting in the future. These systems offer participatory journalism the tools to cut down on costs, raise the level of productivity, and deliver customized outputs while at the same time informing the audience in real-time and personalizing listening experiences. However, the use of AI in journalism is also behind the rise of a host of ethical as well as professional questions regarding authenticity of AI-generated voices, misinformation, biases that are inherent in AI algorithms, and the possibility of the human journalist losing his/her control over content creation. Such case studies and industry insights evaluate the integration of AI in news podcasts in terms of trends, risks, and potentialities. Moreover, the paper considers these trends as a factor that impacts rather than merely being the determinant of audience trust, media credibility, and the future of narrative forms in news storytelling.

Title: Transformer-Based Rhythm Quantization of Performance MIDI Using Beat Annotations
Abstract: Rhythm transcription is a key subtask of notation-level Automatic Music Transcription (AMT). While deep learning models have been extensively used for detecting the metrical grid in audio and MIDI performances, beat-based rhythm quantization remains largely unexplored. In this work, we introduce a novel deep learning approach for quantizing MIDI performances using a priori beat information. Our method leverages the transformer architecture to effectively process synchronized score and performance data for training a quantization model. Key components of our approach include dataset preparation, a beat-based pre-quantization method to align performance and score times within a unified framework, and a MIDI tokenizer tailored for this task. We adapt a transformer model based on the T5 architecture to meet the specific requirements of rhythm quantization. The model is evaluated using a set of score-level metrics designed for objective assessment of quantization performance. Through systematic evaluation, we optimize both data representation and model architecture. Additionally, we apply performance and score augmentations, such as transposition, note deletion, and performance-side time jitter, to enhance the model's robustness. Finally, a qualitative analysis compares our model's quantization performance against state-of-the-art probabilistic and deep-learning models on various example pieces. Our model achieves an onset F1-score of 97.3% and a note value accuracy of 83.3% on the ASAP dataset. It generalizes well across time signatures, including those not seen during training, and produces readable score output. Fine-tuning on instrument-specific datasets further improves performance by capturing characteristic rhythmic and melodic patterns. This work contributes a robust and flexible framework for beat-based MIDI quantization using transformer models.

Title: Marine Ship Target Segmentation Method Based on Improved DeepLabV3+
Abstract: Ship target segmentation plays a crucial role in enhancing the automation level of marine monitoring systems. However, the existing target segmentation methods often suffers from the issues such as mis-segmentation, susceptibility to noise interference, and low processing efficiency, making them difficult to adapt flexibly and efficiently to real-world scenarios. To address these challenges in maritime ship target segmentation tasks, a segmentation algorithm based on an improved DeepLabV3+ network, termed MET-DeepLabV3+, is proposed. During the image preprocessing stage, the bilateral filtering, multi-scale Retinex algorithm, and linear transformation are employed to mitigate the effects of noise, weather and other adverse factors. In terms of model design, the lightweight MobileNetV2 is used as the backbone network to reduce model complexity, and the ECA-Net attention mechanism is introduced to enhance the model's ability to capture the multi-scale features. Additionally, a transfer learning approach is adopted, and the feature weights pre-trained on the SeaShips dataset are applied to model training to further optimize the segmentation performance. Experimental results demonstrate that the improved algorithm achieves an average interaction-over-union (IoU) of 91.62 and an average pixel accuracy (PA) of 92.87, which are improved by 2.13 and 1.11, respectively, compared with those of the baseline DeepLabV3+ model. Moreover, it outperforms the segmentation models such as HRNet, PSPNet, and UNet, which effectively meets the practical demands of ship target segmentation tasks and offers significant application value.

Title: IMAiGen: A Cross-Modal Image-to-Music Generation with a Non-Deep Learning Core
Abstract: As generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) rises, music generation has nonetheless been unexplored, particularly image-to-music, and relies on deep learning methods. Existing neural-based models depend on large datasets, raising concerns about copyright infringement and increased costs for performance improvements. In contrast, we propose an innovative cross-modal Image-toMusic Artificial intelligence Generation (IMA<inf>i</inf> Gen) framework powered by a novel, non-deep learning music core, minimizing copyright infringement risks by utilizing a creative approach. The framework first generates latent rhythmic features from an input image using Large Language Models (LLMs) and follows with a purely algorithmdriven music core to automatically derive musical features, constructing symbolic music from rhythmic information. In this pilot study, we developed a web tool, GenAIM, based on this image-to-music framework that generates melodies adhering to music theory and rhythmic conventions. Experimental results show that our approach achieves an average music key confidence score of 85.3%, demonstrating its ability to produce diverse, human-like compositions. Therefore, this tool serves as a reliable copilot for composers as well as entertainment, advancing AI in music generation by bridging visual and auditory art forms across modalities. Title: Naive Bayes Classifier for Prostate Cancer Risk Prediction Using Patient Records
Abstract: In order to decrease mortality and improve treatment outcomes, early risk assessment is crucial for prostate cancer, one of the most common tumours affecting men worldwide. This research presents a Naive Bayes classification algorithm to forecast prostate cancer risk utilizing the publicly accessible Prostate Cancer Risk & Lifestyle Synthetic Dataset from Kaggle. The collection comprises 1,000 synthetic patient records that encompass attributes including age, PSA level, familial history, race, Gleason score, digital rectal exam (DRE) outcomes, and lifestyle factors. After the preprocessing and encoding of categorical data, a Gaussian Naive Bayes classifier was trained and assessed utilizing a stratified 80/20 train-test division. The model achieved a testing accuracy of 91.2%, a precision of 89.5%, a recall of 92.1%, and an F1-score of 90.8%. The area under the ROC curve (AUC) was measured at 0.94, signifying exceptional discriminative performance. The results indicate that Naive Bayes, despite its simplicity, may accurately predict prostate cancer risk based on both lifestyle and clinical characteristics. The method shows potential as a streamlined decision-support instrument for initial risk assessment in healthcare settings.

Title: Innovative Ultra-Wideband (UWB) Hands-Free Speaker: Advanced Interaction Driven by Machine Learning via Face and Gesture Recognition
Abstract: The rapid evolution of smart audio technology has necessitated innovative interaction mechanisms that enhance user experience, accessibility, and efficiency. This research presents an Ultra-Wideband (UWB) Hands-Free Speaker integrated with Machine Learning (ML)-driven Face and Gesture Recognition to enable seamless, intuitive control without the need for voice commands or physical contact. Traditional smart speakers primarily rely on voice-based interactions, which may be ineffective in noisy environments or inaccessible to individuals with speech impairments. Our proposed system leverages UWB-based localization, computer vision, and deep learning models to achieve precise face tracking, dynamic gesture control, and adaptive audio spatialization. The system architecture comprises three core components: (1) UWB Localization Module, which detects user presence and spatial positioning in real-time; (2) Computer Vision-Based Face and Gesture Recognition System, utilizing deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transformer-based models to recognize user identity and interpret gestures; and (3) AI-Driven Audio Processing, which dynamically adjusts sound directionality and volume based on user location and preferences. The proposed system employs a hybrid learning approach, combining pre-trained models (such as YOLO for gesture detection and FaceNet for identity recognition) with real-time adaptive learning for enhanced accuracy and personalization. Key innovations of this study include (i) precise gesture-driven speaker control using spatial UWB tracking and ML-based recognition, (ii) multi-user interaction with adaptive response, ensuring personalized settings for different individuals, and (iii) robust performance in challenging conditions, including low-light environments and high-noise surroundings. Performance evaluation across multiple test environments demonstrates superior recognition accuracy, low-latency response, and user adaptability compared to traditional voice-controlled and touch-based interfaces. This research contributes to the field of human-computer interaction (HCI), smart home automation, and accessible technology, offering a more inclusive, efficient, and intelligent user experience. Future work will explore integration with edge computing for real-time inference optimization and expansion into multimodal interaction combining facial expressions, body posture, and contextual AI-driven automation.

Title: 'Generative AI-Powered Portfolio Optimization Through Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Contextual Financial Knowledge Graphs'
Abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for portfolio optimization that leverages generative artificial intelligence (AI) through Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and contextual financial knowledge graphs. Traditional portfolio optimization methods often struggle with incorporating real-time market dynamics and complex interdependencies between financial instruments. Our proposed system combines large language models with structured financial knowledge representations to enhance decision-making processes in investment management. The framework demonstrates superior performance compared to conventional optimization techniques, achieving a 15.3% improvement in risk-adjusted returns and reducing portfolio volatility by 12.7%. Through comprehensive evaluation on real market data spanning 2020-2023, our approach showcases the potential of AI-driven methodologies in modern financial portfolio management.

Title: Adaptive Multi-Scale Attention Mechanism for Robust Action Recognition in Complex Scenes
Abstract: Behavior recognition has become a fundamental task in computer vision with broad applications in intelligent surveillance, human-computer interaction, and smart security systems. However, complex real-world scenarios present significant challenges, including occlusion, illumination variation, viewpoint changes, and background clutter, which severely degrade recognition performance. Existing methods primarily rely on fixed-scale feature extraction and single-dimensional attention mechanisms, limiting their robustness in complex environments. To address these issues, this paper proposes an Adaptive Multi-Scale Attention Mechanism (AMSAM) for robust behavior recognition. The proposed method employs a multi-branch convolutional architecture to capture spatiotemporal features at small, medium, and large scales simultaneously. An adaptive attention module integrating spatial, temporal, and channel dimensions is designed to dynamically evaluate feature importance across different scales. Furthermore, a feature alignment and adaptive weighted fusion strategy is developed to enable deep integration of multi-scale information. Extensive experiments on the benchmark datasets UCF101 and HMDB51 demonstrate that AMSAM achieves recognition accuracies of 95.1% and 77.9%. Under challenging scenarios such as occlusion and illumination variation, the proposed method exhibits significantly improved robustness. The results validate the effectiveness and practical applicability of AMSAM for behavior recognition in complex scenarios.

Title: Combating Misinformation with Deep Learning: Fake News Detection Using Recurrent Neural Networks
Abstract: Due to time passage the issue of false news propagation has acquired a complex character as it penetrates not only the form of developing politics but has also influenced the functioning of the entire society. also believe in the media. The traditional approaches to identifying fake and authentic news did not always go in parallel with the increasing speed at which the strategy of distributing disinformation was enhanced. As composed in the current study, it is revealed how Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) which is the most powerful and most expensive variety of deep learning networks can be used to identify false news and make it more precise and effective. We used over 44,000 news articles of both real and fake news in equal numbers to train our system and to evaluate our system. To use the data in a neural network, this data was pre-processed in order to remove extraneous information, normalize the text, and convert the words into numerical features or tokens. A model based on the bi-directional layers of LSTM has been developed to aptly describe the context of the given text and also ensure that the given sequence can read text in a flexible way. It also associates the early stopping mechanism with modeling dropout layers in order to produce the needed outcome in performance. It is our hope that our experiments will persuade. We obtained the accuracy of 99.04 percent on the test set using RNN-based model, but we overdid this mark in terms of precision and recall and rated 98.7 percent. Another indicator of RNN being an appropriate model to identify false information is the significant high accuracy rates related to these deep learning methods. A confusion matrix will also be tabulated to continue explaining the trend of predictive capacities. In such a way, the RNN technology can be regarded as an apt instrument of revealing fake information that is a solution to the specific issue concerning news in the contemporary world.

Title: Neuromorphic Architectures for Real-Time Speech Processing in Noisy Environments
Abstract: The processing of speech in acoustic cluttered environments (such as the cocktail party problem) continues to be an extremely difficult problem to the artificial auditory system. In this case, the human listeners excel at isolating and parsing speech through the use of biologically efficient neural networks, as opposed to conventional digital signal processing systems which are characterized by latency, energy dissipation and poor performance in multitalking or noisy conditions. In order to overcome these inadequacies, neuromorphic computing has emerged as one of the new radiant approaches by simulating the biological auditory pathway with respect to its structure and functionality. The framework that integrates a biologically-inspired cochlear front-end, attentional spiking neural units, and attention-directed temporal fidelity that has recently been proposed in this paper is called the Attention-Gated Spiking-FullSubNet (AGS-FSN). To achieve localization and separation of sounds, Cochlear unit performs this frequency decomposition in a neuromorphic filter bank whose phase and timing representations are crucial to sound localization and separation. Events Implemented and Gated spiking neuron, event-driven paradigm reduces computational cost and is very energy-efficient. FullSubNet-Like attention mechanism permits the selective amplification of the pertinent parts of the speech of the background speech interference to the side. Extensive experiments on noisy real world datasets reveal that AGS-FSN demonstrates state-of-the-art hearing enhancement and recognition capability, easily surpassing the conventional deep learning models by a large margin in terms of accuracies, and power consumption. The design is aimed at the neuromorphic hardware devices such as field-programmable gate arrays and event-based silicon processors, which offers a reasonable path to low-power and real-time edge AI via audition. AGS-FSN is a new milestone of robust/scalable and biologically-inspired speech processing in diverse acoustic conditions.

Title: Big Data and Machine Learning Intervention Strategies for Diabetes Prevention in High-Risk Populations
Abstract: Machine learning (ML) methods are appealing to prediction and classification problems and are particularly common in medical diagnoses. The aim of the techniques contributes to enhancing the accuracy and efficiency of the classification of illnesses. In order to manage,these are some of the obstacles that face many medical diagnostic and prognostic systems have been created in the form of expert systems, clinical prediction systems, decision support systems and personal health record systems. These instruments can help doctors and medical workers achieve more correct decisions to diagnose. Disease diagnosis is the process of making the symptoms of disease to be more specific and as a result results in better treatment response. It has however been observed that most of these systems are resource and power-hungry and they require intensive computing power. Furthermore, problems like absences of data and false values in medical data have been experienced commonly. Researchers have tried to address these problems by discarding records that have been affected or use the conventional imputation mechanism of mean, median or nearest-neighbor methods. However, such methods usually have ineffective outcomes. The second major problem which influences classification performance is the occurrence of some outliers in the data set. Although outliers have important effects, much work has not been conducted in medical data analyzes. Outlier detection has not been studied extensively in some of the few studies that have dealt with it. In this research, missing values and outliers are considered, which ought to improve quality of data and accuracy of the data classification. The suggested method is based on the machine learning approach to the missing data imputation problem, as well as the issue of outliers. Through these two prevalent data concerns, the study can guide the generation of stronger and efficient ML models in medical diagnosis that would result in enhanced decision-making and patient care.

Title: Implementing Real-Time VR Simulations for Complex Surgical Training
Abstract: This was a real time Virtual Reality (VR) simulation platform designed and experimented on to facilitate surgical training. The standard way of surgical training is usually constrained by a lack of practical experience, higher cost, and safety issues associated with patients. To overcome such concerns, the proposed VR system incorporates holistic 3D imaging of medical imaging with active tissue motion and various layers of biomechanics and, as a result, offers a realistic and interactive learning platform. The haptic feedback devices integrated into the simulation system contribute to the creation of the touch feeling of tissues and the instruments to be used during the treatment process, which makes the process appear more realistic. The monitoring algorithm is constantly testing the performance of the trainee by the accuracy, force applied, and time needed which is then adjusted to the difficulty level and negative reinforcement is provided to allow the trainee to succeed. GPUs are required to deliver fast rendering and low-latency sensor fusion which in turn results into a system that does not remain behind schedule, having a frame rate that exceeds 90 frames per second that can be used to give a smooth movement in the VR world. Experiments with surgical apprentices demonstrated that the results of this method were significantly more precise, fewer mistakes were made, and skills were learnt more quickly than with the traditional approach to teaching. Furthermore, users report feeling more confident and involved during practice. This research contributes to medical education by providing a system for practising intricate surgery in a systematic, affordable, and safe manner, thereby reducing the chances of mistakes during surgery and improving patient outcomes. Future updates are expected to be more anatomical libraries, improved AI feedback and the addition of teamwork collaborations for learning to work in teams during surgery.

Title: Zero-Shot to Zero-Lies: Detecting Bengali Deepfake Audio Through Transfer Learning
Abstract: The rapid growth of speech synthesis and voice conversion systems has made deepfake audio a major security concern. Bengali deepfake detection remains largely unexplored. In this work, we study automatic detection of Bengali audio deepfakes using the BanglaFake dataset. We evaluate zero-shot inference with several pretrained models. These include Wav2Vec2-XLSR-53, Whisper, PANNsCNN14, WavLM and Audio Spectrogram Transformer. Zero-shot results show limited detection ability. The best model, Wav2Vec2-XLSR-53, achieves 53.80% accuracy, 56.60% AUC and 46.20% EER. We then fine-tune multiple architectures for Bengali deepfake detection. These include Wav2Vec2-Base, LCNN, LCNN-Attention, ResNet18, ViT-B16 and CNN-BiLSTM. Fine-tuned models show strong performance gains. ResNet18 achieves the highest accuracy of 79.17%, F1 score of 79.12%, AUC of 84.37% and EER of 24.35%. Experimental results confirm that fine-tuning significantly improves performance over zero-shot inference. This study provides the first systematic benchmark of Bengali deepfake audio detection. It highlights the effectiveness of fine-tuned deep learning models for this low-resource language.

Title: SALG-QCNN-SER: A Noise-Robust Quantum Convolutional Neural Network with Enhanced Cross-Domain Generalization for Speech Emotion Recognition
Abstract: Emotion recognition in speech is essential for human-computer interaction. This study introduces a refined hybrid Quantum Convolutional Neural Network (QCNN) framework designed to substantially enhance Speech Emotion Recognition (SER). It addresses major challenges such as speaker variability, noise robustness, and cross-domain applicability that often limit classical deep learning models. By Utilizing quantum principles like superposition and entanglement within a 6-qubit, 8-layer parameterized circuit, the model derives highdimensional, noise-resistant features from speech signals. The method includes sophisticated preprocessing steps, such as bandpass filtering and energy-based Voice Activity Detection (VAD), followed by Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) extraction. Evaluated on a diverse dataset of 4,515 samples across eight emotions (Angry, Calm, Disgust, Fear, Happy, Neutral, Sad, Surprised), the QCNN achieved an accuracy of 86%, setting a new benchmark. It surpasses classical approaches such as a CNN with attention (77%), a traditional QCNN (77.87%), and a hybrid quantum-classical network (76%). The model demonstrated balanced performance, with precision scores ranging from 0.79 to 1.0 (including a perfect 1.0 for Fear) and recall scores from 0.82 to 0.94. These results underscore the promise of quantum-enhanced neural networks in capturing complex, nonlinear speech emotion patterns and establishing a new standard for robust, generalizable SER systems.

Title: XEndoSIS: Explainable Endoscopic Surgical Tool Segmentation via Dual Attention Mechanism
Abstract: Accurate segmentation of surgical instruments is a critical task for enabling intelligent assistance during minimally invasive procedures. This study introduces XEndoSIS, a novel deep learning based segmentation model developed for segmenting endoscopic tools on the Kvasir-Instrument dataset. Our approach integrates swin transformer, Efficient Channel Attention (ECA), and Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) blocks into a unified architecture to enhance both local and global feature extraction capabilities. Through extensive experiments, we benchmark our proposed model against popular baseline architectures including U-Net, ResNet, and SegNet. Results demonstrate that XEndoSIS, incorporating swin, ECA, and SE, achieves superior performance with an accuracy of 0.9913, Dice coefficient of 0.9492, IoU of 0.9036, and a loss of 0.0512, significantly outperforming existing methods. The integration of explainable AI technique such as Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME) enhances interpretability by revealing the decision-making process of the model. These results highlight the potential of our hybrid attention-enhanced framework in advancing precise and robust semantic segmentation of surgical instruments.

Title: Robust Audio Representation Learning with Differential Privacy via Self-Supervised Contrastive Pre-Training
Abstract: The growing use of machine learning to analyze sensitive biomedical audio signals, like coughs and breathing patterns, requires strong privacy-preserving methods. However, training models with Differential Privacy (DP) often reduces performance significantly, which limits real-world use. To tackle this privacy-utility issue, we propose a two-stage framework that separates representation learning from classification. First, we pre-train a VGG-based feature encoder on audio spectrograms using a self-supervised contrastive objective along with Differentially Private Stochastic Gradient Descent (DP-SGD). The resulting frozen, private encoder is then used to train a linear classifier for the main task. Experiments on the ESC-50 benchmark show that our method achieves a classification accuracy of 74.2% with a privacy budget of ϵ=5.0. This significantly outperforms a standard end-to-end supervised DP baseline by 12.7 percentage points. This work shows that self-supervised pre-training is a highly effective approach for creating accurate and private models for sensitive audio-based health applications.

Title: EENet: Bridging Speech Enhancement and Deep Learning for Robust Emotion Recognition
Abstract: Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) plays a crucial role in human-computer interaction, yet its performance is often hindered by noisy or low-quality recordings. This work investigates the impact of speech enhancement on six-class SER using two state-of-the-art enhancement models, CFTNet and DCCTN. A novel hybrid neural architecture, EnhanceEmotionNet (EENet), is proposed and evaluated alongside existing models-EmoNet, EmoTech, and EmoFormer-under different training setups, including Enhanced (training on standard IEMOCAP, validation on Noisy, CFTNet-enhanced, and DCCTNenhanced) and Mixed (training on combined standard and enhanced IEMOCAP, validation on Noisy, CFTNet-enhanced, and DCCTN-enhanced) conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that incorporating enhanced speech into training significantly improves model generalization. In the Enhanced setting, EENet achieves accuracies of 84.80% (Noisy), 85.00% (CFTNet), 84.50% (DCCTN), and 87.00% (Clean). In the Mixed setting, performance further improves with 86.22% (Noisy), 87.05% (CFTNet), 87.26% (DCCTN), and 87.00% (Clean). These results indicate that EENet is robust to various speech enhancement conditions and outperforms baseline architectures in capturing emotional cues. Overall, the findings highlight the effectiveness of integrating speech enhancement with hybrid neural architectures for robust SER in realistic acoustic environments.

Title: Hybrid CNN Feature Fusion Model with Class-Weighted Balancing and Explainable AI for Thoracic Diseases Classification
Abstract: Pneumonia and COVID-19 are both thoracic diseases that mainly affect the lungs and make breathing difficult. Radiological imaging techniques, particularly chest Xrays (CXR), play a crucial role in identifying these conditions. Although some signs on the X-ray may look similar, pneumonia usually appears as a solid white area in one part of the lung, while COVID-19 often shows up as light, cloudy areas spread across both lungs. To detect and classify these respiratory diseases the proposed method uses a hybrid CNN that combines features from pre-trained VGG16 and MobileNet networks with global average pooling to capture multi-scale representations from chest X-rays. The model is trained using 4-fold cross-validation with classweighted loss and data augmentation. As fusion combines the captured features from both networks, representing multi-scale, multi-level feature representations that improve performance, the model leverages K-Fold cross-validation, class-weighted training, and data augmentation to demonstrate generalization and robustness, while using pre-trained networks with global average pooling and visualizing intermediate features to provide both efficient learning and preliminary explainability. We evaluated the validity of the proposed approach on two datasets with varying class distributions, achieving 97% accuracy for binary classification and 98.25% for multi-class classification.

Title: Predicting Stock Prices in LQ45 Index in Indonesia Stock Exchange Using News Sentiment Analysis and Random Forest Algorithm
Abstract: Stock prices are influenced by a complex interaction of elements encompassing the company's intrinsic value and the broader economic and market circumstances. Other than that, news sentiment also correlates with stock price movements. Thus, Predicting the stock market become a compelling task. Several techniques are employed to achieve this objective, one of which is machine learning. Machine learning has become an effective instrument for predicting stock prices thanks to its ability to analyze and learn from complex datasets. This research integrates sentiment analysis and machine learning to predict stock prices, focusing on the LQ45 Index from Indonesian Stock Exchange and financial news from Indonesian news portals such as CNN Indonesia, CNBC Indonesia, and Detik.com. The study employs the Random Forest algorithm, incorporating sentiment scores from news articles as a feature. The results demonstrate that the Random Forest model achieves superior performance, yielding an average Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 68.77 and a Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 88.05 across eight major LQ45 stocks. Price-based features, particularly 'Low' and 'High', were most influential in predictions. Sentiment scores and volume had minimal impact when combined with price data. However, sentiment scores significantly influenced predictions when isolated from price-related features.

Title: Bridging Tradition and Technology: Automated Classification of Bengali Folk Music Using Machine Learning
Abstract: Music genre classification plays a key role in music discovery, recommendation, and digital preservation. Despite the richness and diversity of Bengali folk music, computational studies in this domain remain limited. This paper presents a machine learning approach to classify five prominent subgenres of folk song-Bhatiyali, Baul, Lalon, Dhamali, and Bhawaiya- using lyrics as the primary feature. The dataset was created by collecting songs from a publicly available book and from local individuals knowledgeable about traditional folk music. Preprocessing included text normalization and noise removal, followed by TF-IDF feature extraction. SMOTE was applied to address class imbalance in the training data. Six machine learning algorithms-Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest, Decision Tree, Na'ive Bayes, and XGBoost-were evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Among these, the SVM model achieved the highest accuracy of 85.32%, demonstrating balanced and reliable performance across most subgenres. These results indicate that lyrics-based features can effectively support structured analysis and classification of Bengali folk music. The proposed approach not only aids in music recommendation systems but also contributes to the digital preservation and systematic study of traditional folk heritage.

Title: SETBoost: An Interpretable Machine Learning Approach for Predicting Software Employee Turnover Tendency
Abstract: The software industry produces skilled professionals who drive technological advancement, yet high turnover rates among experienced engineers result in knowledge loss, reduced productivity, and increased recruitment costs. This research investigates employee turnover prediction through a data-driven machine learning approach to address this workforce retention challenge. We introduce the SET (Software Employee Turnover) dataset by making it publicly accessible, comprising 2,174 software employee records systematically collected from multiple Bangladeshi technology companies via structured survey instruments, encompassing organizational perception scores, tenure duration, project complexity indicators, and workplace satisfaction measures. Rigorous comparative analysis of various supervised learning algorithms was conducted to establish optimal classification performance for binary turnover prediction. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method SETBoost achieves superior predictive accuracy of 78.34%, substantially outperforming baseline approaches. Model interpretability was enhanced through implementation of Local Interpretable Modelagnostic Explanations (LIME) and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) frameworks, identifying company perception as the primary determinant of employee departure decisions. The analysis reveals that moderately satisfied employees are more likely to leave than highly dissatisfied employees, which is unexpected. These findings support data-driven HR strategies focused on improving company culture, compensation, and workload management to reduce turnover in technology companies.

Title: SAE-MRF: A Scale-Adaptive Encoder with Multi-Receptive Field Blocks for Nuclei Segmentation in Histopathology Images
Abstract: Accurate nuclei segmentation in histopathology is a core task for computational pathology applications. We propose a compact, convolutional architecture that focuses on adaptive multi-scale local processing: the Scale-Adaptive Encoder with Multi-Receptive Field blocks (SAE-MRF). The network replaces standard encoder blocks with an MRF block that computes parallel receptive fields and uses a Scale-Attention Gate (SAG) to weight them per pixel. We show through a 5-fold cross-validation on the MoNuSeg dataset that inserting MRF blocks consistently improves segmentation performance compared to U-Net-like baselines. Our main configuration (SAE-MRF) achieves a mean external Dice of 0.6939 ± 0.0463, demonstrating that adaptive multi-receptive processing is an effective and lightweight alternative to heavier global token or transformer mechanisms for this task.

Abstract: Music classification is vital for artists and composers to ensure accurate distribution, contribution tracking, and enhanced accessibility for music enthusiasts. Title: Non-Intrusive Speech Intelligibility Measures Using Multi-Metric Approach
Abstract: Most existing objective speech intelligibility measures require access to a clean reference signal, which limits their use in practical acoustic environments where clean speech is usually unavailable. This motivates the need for nonintrusive intelligibility assessment methods that operate directly on noisy signals. In this work, we focus on two complementary non-intrusive intelligibility metrics-Short-Time Objective Intelligibility (STOI) and the Spectrogram Orthogonal Polynomial Measure (SOPM) and highlight their conceptual similarity in capturing speech degradation under noisy conditions. Building upon this relationship, we propose a deep learning framework that jointly predicts STOI and SOPM using an encoder, convolutional feature extractors, Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Units (BiGRU), and a self-attention mechanism to model spectral-temporal dependencies. Experimental evaluations demonstrate strong predictive performance when each metric is estimated individually (SRCC: 0.9672 for STOI and 0.9650 for SOPM), while joint prediction yields even higher correlation (SRCC: 0.9747) and lower error (MSE: 0.0019). These findings reveal that combining both intelligibility metrics improves prediction accuracy compared to learning them independently. Overall, the proposed non-intrusive approach bridges the gap between traditional reference-based evaluation and real-world acoustic conditions while demonstrating the benefit of integrated intelligibility estimation.

Title: Explainable AI using Hybrid Deep Learning Model for Identification of cancer cells in bone marrow
Abstract: The presence of cancer cells in bone marrow can be diagnosed and treated through early and accurate detection of the disease. Despite the profound breakthrough of deep learning in automated cell identification, the majority of the existing algorithms are treated as black boxes with less transparency, which does not allow their implementation in clinical practice as interpretability is a crucial factor as accuracy. This research suggests a hybrid deep learning method that can be explained utilizing a better dual-threshold segmentation and a Dual-Channel Convolutional Block Attention Network (DCCBANet) and Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT)-based feature fusion. The segmentation module guarantees accurate separation of nucleus and cytoplasm and hybrid CNN-DWT module provides both spatial and frequency domain properties to provide robust features containing. To make the methods more interpretable, Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) and Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) are used to offer visual and feature-wise explanations. Tests on publicly accessible bone marrow data sets and clinical samples show state of art performance with macro-F1 scores of over 96% when classifying binary and more than 87% when classifying multi-class. The explainable visualizations were reviewed by pathologists who ensured that the highlighted areas were diagnostically significant cellular areas, which validates the medical relevance of the model. Using the proposed framework, accuracy, transparency, and clinical interpretability are combined, which is why it will be an effective instrument of AI-assisted hematological diagnosis.

Title: A Hybrid Multimedia Steganography Framework with Genetic Algorithm Optimization and Machine Learning-Based Packet Manipulation Detection
Abstract: The increasing demand for secure multimedia communication has driven the evolution of steganographic techniques beyond single-media approaches. This paper presents a novel hybrid steganography framework that integrates data hiding across multiple media types-images, audio, and video-while employing genetic algorithm optimization for embedding position selection and machine learning-based packet manipulation detection. The proposed system utilizes media-specific embedding strategies: LSB modification for images, phase coding for audio, and motion vector adjustment for video, unified under an adaptive framework with XOR encryption. Genetic algorithm optimization enhances imperceptibility by intelligently selecting embedding positions based on perceptual significance and robustness criteria. The integrated machine learning component provides real-Time packet manipulation detection with 98.7% accuracy, ensuring communication channel integrity. Experimental evaluation on benchmark datasets demonstrates superior performance with PSNR values exceeding 45 dB for images, SNR above 35 dB for audio, and motion distortion below 2% for video. The system achieves an extraction accuracy of 99.5% under various attack scenarios while maintaining computational efficiency suitable for real-Time applications. Comparative analysis reveals \mathbf{2 5-4 0 \% improvement in robustness over traditional single-media steganographic methods.

Title: Towards Object Counting by Efficient Scale Recognition Network
Abstract: In the realm of Intelligent Transportation Systems, tiny machine learning facilitates the deployment and training of AI models directly on devices, enabling efficient execution of crucial tasks such as predicting traffic patterns and ensuring pedestrian safety. Nonetheless, most existing object counting approaches rely on parameter-heavy architectures, resulting in significant computational demands that hinder their suitability for on-device applications. To tackle this issue, we present a lightweight network, named Efficient Scale Recognition Network (ESRNet), which enhances counting precision. Our design integrates a Lightweight Multi-scale Enhancement (LME) module utilizing deformable convolutions, which allows effective extraction of multi-scale features within tight computational budgets. To further improve adaptability to non-i.i.d. data, we propose a Statistical Moment Alignment loss (SMAloss), which promotes generalization across various traffic conditions. Experimental results across multiple benchmarks for vehicle counting verify that the proposed method delivers superior performance in both efficiency and accuracy.

Title: A voiceprint recognition method based on dual-channel fusion
Abstract: With the continuous advancement of intelligent devices and communication technologies, the challenges of speaker recognition across dialects, devices, and distances have become increasingly prominent. Accurately identifying speakers in diverse contexts has emerged as a critical problem to be addressed in both academia and industry. This paper presents a deep learning-based dual-channel method for speaker recognition to address this problem. Firstly, we employ a densely connected time-delay neural network (DTDNN) architecture and integrate a context-aware masking (CAM) module to focus on the target speaker while suppressing irrelevant noise, thereby constructing the CAM-DTDNN speech recognition model. Secondly, we design the ERes2Net speech recognition model through the integration of features at both the local (LFF) and global (GFF) levels to aggregate multi-scale features from different dimensions, along with an attention-based feature fusion (AFF) mechanism to dynamically assign attention weights to features at varying scales. To further enhance model performance, we combine these two models through a weighted matrix and optimize their fusion. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed weighted fusion approach achieves superior performance in speaker recognition tasks, validating the potential of dual-channel models in this domain. Additionally, the method exhibits strong transferability across different linguistic environments.

Title: 3C-Net: Cervical Cancer Cell Classification from Liquid-Based Cytology Pap Smear Images using Deep Learning Techniques
