Title: Employing Capsule Networks for Robust Speech Recognition in Noisy Environments
Abstract: Speech recognition in noisy environments suffers from degraded accuracy due to overlapping sounds, unpredictable distortions, and reduced signal-to-noise ratios (SNR). Traditional deep learning models such as CNNs and RNNs often fail to capture hierarchical relationships in acoustic signals, limiting robustness. This study proposes a Capsule Network (CapsNet)-based framework that leverages dynamic routing to model part-whole relationships and preserve spatial hierarchies in speech features. Primary capsules extract lowlevel acoustic representations, while higher-level capsules aggregate contextually relevant phoneme information. Experimental evaluations were conducted on noisy variants of the TIMIT and LibriSpeech datasets, with additional robustness analysis across varying SNR levels. The CapsNet framework achieved a word recognition accuracy of 92.1% at 5 dB SNR, outperforming CNNs by 12% and showing a 25% improvement in noise robustness compared to standard architectures. Furthermore, statistical significance tests (paired t-test, p< 0.05) confirmed the reliability of improvements. The proposed CapsNet-based system demonstrates strong resilience in noisy auditory conditions, scalable performance across diverse datasets, and suitability for real-world applications such as transcription services and voice-controlled devices. Future work will extend the framework to multilingual speech recognition and multimodal integration.

Title: Advances in Chemical Mechanical Polishing Endpoint Detection Technology for Integrated Circuits Manufacturing
Abstract: Chemical mechanical polishing (CMP) is a pivotal process in advanced semiconductor manufacturing that enables wafer surface planarization. CMP endpoint detection (EPD) technology achieves precise control over the wafer surface topography and material removal rates by dynamically adjusting the polishing pressure in different zones through real-time measurements of the thin film thickness. However, current EPD techniques face challenges in accurately capturing material removal rate variations in localized regions of wafers with complex patterns and nonuniform density distributions, leading to discrepancies between the detection signals and actual polishing states. Moreover, polishing processes involving multi-material systems suffer from limited signal resolution and selectivity, making it difficult to precisely detect interface changes. Thus, the investigation and optimization of CMP EPD technologies are crucial for addressing the challenges posed by multi-material and novel structures and improving the precision and stability of the process. This paper systematically reviews the current research on CMP EPD technologies, focusing on the principles, characteristics, and advancements in offline (e.g., the time method) and online (e.g., friction-based, optical, and eddy-current techniques) detection methods. In the early or stable stages of the CMP processes, endpoint control relies predominantly on experience and time-based polishing and lacks precise online detection. With technological advancements, four-probe offline detection instruments have been employed for post-polishing evaluations. However, these methods require extensive data accumulation and an understanding of the process parameters to determine the optimal polishing time for each material and process. Advanced CMP processes involve diverse materials, such as shallow trench isolation, interlayer dielectrics (SiO<inf>2</inf>), metal interconnects (Cu), and barrier layers (Ti / TiN), each with distinct polishing rates and removal mechanisms. Offline detection methods struggle to adapt to these variations in real-time. In addition, time-based offline detection fails to account for wafer-to-wafer differences, rendering it insufficient to meet the demands of advanced CMP processes for real-time monitoring and rapid response. Consequently, online detection methods are often required to ensure process stability and product quality. Online EPD technologies enable real-time monitoring and analysis of polishing conditions during the CMP process, ensuring the achievement of the desired endpoints. These technologies are pivotal for automating the polishing process and enhancing the integrated circuit yield. Friction-based online EPD techniques offer strong real-time performance and ease of integration, making them particularly suitable for capturing dynamic mechanical interactions during polishing. However, these methods are significantly influenced by process conditions, such as pad wear and slurry flow, with signal noise and external disturbances undermining the detection accuracy and reliability. Future advancements in friction-based EPD should include the introduction of adaptive calibration mechanisms to mitigate external disturbances and the development of high-sensitivity friction sensors to explore the nanoscale film removal characteristics and meet the requirements of advanced process nodes. Optical EPD techniques typically achieve sub-nanometer resolutions for film thickness measurements. However, optical methods are highly sensitive to environmental conditions, with polishing slurry, debris, and surface contamination potentially interfering with signals and reducing detection precision. Future improvements in optical EPD systems should focus on enhancing the optical system design to resist interference from slurry, contaminants, and environmental fluctuations. Eddy-current EPD provides nanometer-level thickness measurements at a relatively low cost and can be easily integrated with CMP equipment. However, its insensitivity to insulating materials, such as dielectric layers, limits its ability to independently detect dielectric and nonmetallic films. Furthermore, the development of eddy-current sensors capable of achieving high-precision (nano-/ sub-nanometer scale) measurements under large lift-off variations remains critical for future research. In the future, multi-physics field fusion methods will play a pivotal role in enhancing the detection performance to address the challenges posed by multilayer film stacks and heterogeneous material systems in 3D devices for advanced process nodes. By integrating optical, eddy-current, and friction-based techniques with multi-sensor collaborative acquisition and data fusion algorithms, the selectivity and accuracy of EPD can be significantly improved. Furthermore, AI-driven intelligent signal processing equipped with robust feature learning, pattern recognition, and intelligent decision-making capabilities enables the analysis and prediction of complex three-dimensional structural signals while adaptively adjusting the parameters, thereby enhancing the adaptability of EPD technologies. Additionally, flexible and customizable sensor designs combined with micro-area detection techniques contribute to increased spatiotemporal resolution, facilitating the precise monitoring and dynamic regulation of localized polishing conditions.

Title: TuFoC: regional classification of Turkish folk music recordings using deep learning on Mel spectrograms
Abstract: The regional classification of Turkish folk music remains a relatively unexplored domain in music information retrieval, particularly when leveraging raw audio signals for deep learning. This study addresses this gap by investigating how modern deep learning architectures can effectively classify regional folk recordings from limited original data using carefully designed spectrogram inputs. To address this challenge, we present Turkish Folk Music Classification (TuFoC), a deep learning-based approach that classifies Turkish folk music recordings according to their region of origin using Mel spectrogram representations. We investigate two complementary architectures: a MobileNetV2-based convolutional neural network (CNN) for extracting spatial representations, and a long short-term memory (LSTM) network for modeling temporal dynamics. To engage critically with the state of the art, we replicate a classical machine learning pipeline that combines histogram of oriented gradients (HOG) features with a Light Gradient-Boosting Machine (LightGBM) classifier and Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE)-based oversampling. This baseline achieves competitive results, particularly on GAD, with 92.53% accuracy and macro F1-score. However, our CNN architecture not only marginally outperforms the baseline on the gently augmented dataset (GAD) (92.68% accuracy) but also demonstrates superior consistency across all dataset variants. While the LSTM model underperforms on original dataset (OD) and strongly augmented dataset (AD), it improves markedly on GAD, validating the importance of balanced data preparation. Experimental results, obtained through stratified 10-fold cross-validation repeated over 30 independent runs, demonstrate that the proposed CNN architecture delivers the highest and most stable classification performance. Beyond performance gains, our approach offers key advantages in generalization, scalability, and automation, as it bypasses the need for domain-specific feature design. The findings confirm that deep neural models trained on Mel spectrograms constitute a flexible and robust alternative to classical pipelines, holding promise for future applications in computational ethnomusicology and music information retrieval.

Title: Xanadu: Generative Media Pipelines for Immersive Participatory Theater
Abstract: We present Xanadu, a full-scale participatory theater production that integrated generative AI into a live musical. Over two weeks, 500 audience members contributed sketches, movements, and sounds that were transformed in real-time —via pipelines combining vision-language models, diffusion models, and moderation— into images, 3D objects, poetry, and choreography rendered within an extended reality environment. Audience inputs were framed as ritual “offerings” to the Muses, with performers guiding participation and AI serving as interpretive intermediary. A hybrid hosting architecture combined controllable, research-driven models with fast foundation models, enabling 30–60 second generations while preserving stylistic and narrative coherence. We discuss design strategies and trade-offs that supported large-scale, group-level human–AI collaboration. This work contributes practical insights into deploying generative AI in live performance and highlights opportunities for designing AI systems that facilitate collective rather than individual creativity.

Title: Audio Tagging – Deep Learning Approach
Abstract: Having multiple applications in areas such as music curation, voice identification, and identifying environmental sounds, audio tagging proves to be a pivotal task within the realm of audio analysis and categorization. Due to their ability to capture complex characteristics from raw audio data, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have found extensive utility in the context of audio tagging tasks. The selection of the feature extraction technique is an important component of CNN-based audio tagging. In this study, we investigate how three well-liked features such as MFCC, GFCC, and Spectrograms affect the precision of a CNN-based audio tagging model. Using a sizable dataset of labelled audio clips, we train a base CNN model with three convolutional layers and two fully connected layers, and we compare the model’s performance using each feature extraction technique. According to the outcomes of our experiments, Spectrograms perform better than MFCCs and GFCCs in terms of accuracy and F1 score. Finally, the performance of the model is evaluated on several performance matrices and this approach enables us to effectively classify audio files into various categories.

Title: Visual-Informed Speech Enhancement Using Attention-Based Beamforming
Abstract: Recent studies have demonstrated that incorporating auxiliary information, such as speaker voiceprint or visual cues, can substantially improve Speech Enhancement (SE) performance. However, single-channel methods often yield suboptimal results in low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions, when there is high reverberation, or in complex scenarios involving dynamic speakers, overlapping speech, or non-stationary noise. To address these issues, we propose a novel Visual-Informed Neural Beamforming Network (VI-NBFNet), which integrates microphone array signal processing and deep neural networks (DNNs) using multimodal input features. The proposed network leverages a pretrained visual speech recognition model to extract lip movements as input features, which serve for voice activity detection (VAD) and target speaker identification. The system is intended to handle both static and moving speakers by introducing a supervised end-to-end beamforming framework equipped with an attention mechanism. The experimental results demonstrated that the proposed audiovisual system has achieved better SE performance and robustness for both stationary and dynamic speaker scenarios, compared to several baseline methods.

Title: Distributed Cross-Timescale Spatiotemporal Graph Neural Networks for Sea Surface Temperature Prediction
Abstract: Ocean data have strong spatiotemporal correlations and are also characterized by multisource, decentralized distribution, presenting significant challenges for distributed collaboration. To address these issues, in this article, we propose a distributed graph learning network (DGLN), a distributed graph convolutional network (GCN)-based prediction architecture that employs a decentralized training paradigm comprising local and distributed systems. The local system is designed to capture scale-specific features of marine data across different processors, while the distributed system learns and coordinates global cross-timescale features. The graph learning module in the distributed system integrates graph features from other processors without transmitting raw data, thereby ensuring local data security. To accelerate training and enhance model performance, a joint learning module is composed by cross-timescale computation with a new global weighted consensus algorithm, which is able to adaptively adjust the weights of different scales. Experimental results show that DGLN is able to improve the local prediction accuracy and capture cross-timescale features effectively while improving the training efficiency.

Title: Vegetation Indices Prediction Using Machine-Learning and Deep-Learning Approaches From RGB Calibrated Images
Abstract: The evaluation of the information provided by the vegetation indices (VIs) represents a substantial resource for the application of precision agriculture techniques. In addition to the numerous environmental challenges facing the control of agricultural activities, such as rising soil temperatures, limited access to water resources, and the containment of plant diseases, it is crucial to reduce management costs, especially for small and medium-sized farms. However, calculating VIs requires the use of advanced instrumentation equipped with hyperspectral or multispectral optical sensors and experienced operators trained to handle instruments for accurate acquisition of spectral data, which is essential to obtain parameters that can provide an estimate reflecting the real state of health or the physico-chemical characteristics of the crop in question. The aim of this study is to investigate whether the determination of VIs from RGB images, which can be acquired with cheaper devices, provides reliable results that can be used later in the development of prescription maps for irrigation or treatment distribution. In this study, 5 different VIs were considered to compare the performance of two different regression approaches: the first method uses a shallow neural network (SNN), estimating pixel value from calibrated RGB values; the second method uses a convolutional neural network (CNN U-Net) to generate images from calibrated RGB images. For both models, multiple tests have been carried out showing the effectiveness of regressive methods and supporting the results obtained and their possible practical use.

Title: A new method for assessing chronic insomnia: Machine learning-based fusion of TCM observation digital features
Abstract: Background: In the clinical assessment of chronic insomnia, modern medicine encounters challenges in the widespread adoption of objective assessment methods, such as polysomnography, due to their high costs and complex operational requirements. Therefore, it was crucial to implement objective and varied methods to accurately assess chronic insomnia. Methods: Clinical information was collected from 594 patients diagnosed with chronic insomnia. Their facial and tongue features, as observed through traditional Chinese medicine, were recorded using the tongue face diagnosis analysis-1 instrument and analyzed with the tongue/face diagnosis analysis system. Stepwise-regression analysis, principal component analysis, and zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) regression were employed for variable screening. Ultimately, the classification model for assessing the severity of chronic insomnia was constructed using six supervised machine learning methods: decision trees, neural networks, random forests, support vector machines, logistic regression, and naive Bayes. The model was evaluated using sensitivity, specificity, F1 score, precision, and accuracy. Visualization was conducted with the Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) explainer and decision curve analysis (DCA), and it was finally calibrated using Platt scaling. Results: A comprehensive evaluation revealed that model 4 exhibited superior performance. This model integrated baseline data, sleep symptoms, and facial features, achieving its highest receiver operating characteristic curve value of 0.822. Furthermore, DCA demonstrated that model 4 exhibited significant clinical utility. The SHAP illustrated that among the variables exerting the greatest influence on insomnia, the effects of Ch-Y and CH-G were notably prominent, compared to the conventional PSQI and SAS, followed by Ch-R. Finally, the results of Platt scaling calibration indicated that model 4 exhibited significant improvement post-calibration, with the predicted probabilities closely aligning with the actual probabilities of occurrence. Conclusions: This study emphasized convenient and non-invasive diagnostic methods for investigating specific facial and tongue features associated with chronic insomnia. A classification model for chronic insomnia has been developed through the integration of multiple features, enabling a more accurate assessment of insomnia severity and facilitating advancements in therapeutic interventions.

Title: Split Fine-Tuning of BERT-Based Music Models in the Edge-Cloud Continuum: An Empirical Analysis
Abstract: Transformer models have been instrumental in the proliferation of AI in modern life, with larger models demonstrating incredible performance in many domains and applications. While these models can be split across edge and cloud nodes, the communication overhead can be substantial, creating a bottleneck and impacting the viability of real-world deployment. Using a real edge device setup, we measure the communication time across the split, as well as the overhead introduced by compressing the communicated tensors. Title: Causal Gene Identification and Biomarker Prioritization in Periodontitis via Integrative Multiomics and Mendelian Randomization
Abstract: Introduction: Periodontitis is a common inflammatory disease that compromises oral and systemic health. This study aimed to elucidate its molecular mechanisms and identify potential biomarkers for early diagnosis and precision treatment. Methods: We integrated genome-wide association study (GWAS) and transcriptomic data from periodontitis patients and healthy controls. Summary data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR) and the heterogeneity in dependent instruments (HEIDI) test were used to identify genetically associated genes. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified using LIMMA, and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) revealed disease-related gene modules. Candidate biomarkers were prioritized through intersection analysis and evaluated using five machine learning algorithms. Causal relationships were further validated by two-sample Mendelian randomization (TSMR). Functional enrichment was assessed via gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) and gene set variation analysis (GSVA), and immune infiltration was analyzed using CIBERSORT. Results: SMR identified 360 gene-trait associations, with 320 passing the HEIDI test, corresponding to 294 unique genes. DEGs were enriched in immune and neuronal development pathways. WGCNA uncovered nine gene modules associated with periodontitis. Intersection and machine learning analyses identified five key biomarkers—GPX2, IGKV2D-30, CD34, GSTA4, and NYNRIN—with strong predictive performance, validated by MR analysis (p < 0.05). Immune infiltration analysis revealed increased regulatory T cells, activated mast cells, and neutrophils, and decreased memory B cells and resting mast cells in periodontitis, with biomarker expression levels showing significant immune correlations. Conclusion: This integrative multiomics analysis uncovers causal genes and robust biomarkers involved in periodontitis pathogenesis, providing new insights for early detection and individualized treatment strategies. Further experimental validation is needed to confirm their functional roles in disease progression and therapeutic potential.

Title: MSSI-Net: Multiscale Semantic-Guided Synergistic Interaction Network for Remote Sensing Image Change Detection
Abstract: Remote sensing change detection (RSCD) has become an essential tool in observing and analyzing geographical information. However, existing deep learning approaches dependent solely on visual modalities may encounter challenges in discerning subtle variations amidst noise interference. To overcome these issues, we propose a multiscale semantic-guided synergistic interaction network (MSSI-Net), which utilizes the advanced multimodal semantic representations for enhancing the capacity to perceive hierarchical changes. Specifically, we first devise a multiscale interaction module (MIM) that leverages a multiscale attention mechanism to guide the interaction between the coarse and fine stages of different visual features. The fine-grained visual features subsequently complement the semantic features through scale weight reassignment to enhance the discriminative capability of vision-language features. Furthermore, driven by the semantic-guided synergistic interaction mechanism, our developed cross-modal feature fusion module (CFFM) exploits both homogeneous and heterogeneous features among modalities. This ensures that the generated vision-language features are semantically representative. Finally, we formulate a manifold differential perception head (MDPH) to optimize the detection of changes by efficiently fusing diverse differential feature representations, achieving comprehensive performance enhancement. Extensive experiments conducted on four benchmark datasets (LEVIR-CD, CDD, SYSU-CD, and WHU-CD) indicate that the designed MSSI-Net achieves state-of-the-art performance compared with existing methods.

Title: HingeNet: A Harmonic-Aware Fine-Tuning Approach for Beat Tracking
Abstract: Fine-tuning pre-trained foundation models has made significant progress in music information retrieval. However, applying these models to beat tracking tasks remains unexplored as the limited annotated data renders conventional fine-tuning methods ineffective. To address this challenge, we propose HingeNet, a novel and general parameter-efficient fine-tuning method specifically designed for beat tracking tasks. HingeNet is a lightweight and separable network, visually resembling a hinge, designed to tightly interface with pre-trained foundation models by using their intermediate feature representations as input. This unique architecture grants HingeNet broad generalizability, enabling effective integration with various pre-trained foundation models. Furthermore, considering the significance of harmonics in beat tracking, we introduce harmonic-aware mechanism during the fine-tuning process to better capture and emphasize the harmonic structures in musical signals. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that HingeNet achieves state-of-the-art performance in beat and downbeat tracking.

Title: Where's That Voice Coming? Continual Learning for Sound Source Localization
Abstract: Sound source localization (SSL) is essential for many speech-processing applications. Deep learning models have achieved high performance, but often fail when the training and inference environments differ. Adapting SSL models to dynamic acoustic conditions faces a major challenge: catastrophic forgetting. In this work, we propose an exemplar-free continual learning strategy for SSL (CL-SSL) to address such a forgetting phenomenon. CL-SSL applies task-specific sub-networks to adapt across diverse acoustic environments while retaining previously learned knowledge. It also uses a scaling mechanism to limit parameter growth, ensuring consistent performance across incremental tasks. We evaluated CL-SSL on simulated data with varying microphone distances and real-world data with different noise levels. The results demonstrate CL-SSL's ability to maintain high accuracy with minimal parameter increase, offering an efficient solution for SSL applications.

Title: Exploring gestural affordances in audio latent space navigation
Abstract: The latent space of generative AI models affords unique creative possibilities and broad design space for AI-enhanced digital music instruments. While interface designs for latent space navigation typically rely on sound-producing gestures that involve bodily motions and movements, the underlying subjective perception of these gestures remains underexplored. To understand how musicians perceive sound-producing gestures and tailor performance techniques in audio latent space, we present a user study workshop with an AI-enhanced digital music instrument with a tablet interface. Eighteen musicians were recruited to test out open-ended gestures and tasked to create musical scores. We report how they use sound-producing gestures in the latent space and develop performance techniques. We contribute findings from an embodied music cognition perspective of how subjective perception of gestures shapes musicians' technique development in audio latent space navigation. We discuss the implications of new gestural affordances discovered by participants in our workshop, aiming to elucidate new opportunities for digital musical instruments with audio latent space navigation.

Title: Optimizing Biochemical Oxygen Demand Classification in Wastewater using Linear Discriminant Analysis
Abstract: Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) is an essential metric for evaluating water quality in wastewater management. Precise classification of BOD levels is crucial for efficient treatment methods. The primary challenge is that traditional BOD monitoring in wastewater is labor-intensive and time-consuming, preventing rapid classification and response. This work aims to enhance the classification of BOD by Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA), a statistical method that maximizes the differentiation across various BOD concentration classes. It used an extensive dataset of diverse wastewater samples defined by several physicochemical properties. The LDA model underwent training and validation with a k-fold cross-validation method to guarantee robustness and mitigate overfitting. Key performance parameters, such as accuracy, precision, and recall, were analyzed to evaluate the model's efficacy in categorizing BOD levels. The results demonstrate that the LDA method significantly improves classification accuracy relative to traditional techniques, with good feature selection being essential for model efficacy. It illustrates the efficacy of LDA in environmental monitoring, providing a dependable instrument for wastewater treatment plants to enhance their operations and ensure adherence to environmental standards. This research demonstrated that using LDA for BOD classification in wastewater archived an accuracy of 92%, validating its efficacy. Further research will investigate using machine learning methodologies to improve classification proficiency.

Title: Miniaturization of Circularly Polarized Magneto-Electric Dipole Antennas with Machine Learning-Assisted Optimization
Abstract: This work proposes a novel machine learningassisted design methodology for miniaturized magneto-electric dipole antennas. The proposed framework constructs a surrogate model of the antenna structure using machine learning techniques, which is then integrated with a particle swarm optimization algorithm to identify optimal electromagnetic response parameters. During surrogate model establishment, an adaptive data augmentation strategy featuring localized dense sampling near potential optimal solutions significantly reduces the required training dataset size. The multi-objective optimization framework incorporates key performance specifications including return loss, gain, axial ratio, and radiator patch area, achieving antenna size reduction while preserving radiation characteristics. To validate the proposed method, a parametric model of a 2.1 GHz circularly polarized magneto-electric dipole antenna was designed and optimized. Experimental results demonstrate a 30% reduction in training data requirements compared with conventional approaches, along with a 35% size reduction of the optimized radiator patch area relative to the initial configuration.

Title: Exploring Part-Informed Visual-Language Learning for Person Re-Identification
Abstract: Recently, visual-language learning (VLL) has shown great potential in enhancing visual-based person re-identification (ReID). Existing VLL-based ReID methods typically focus on image-text feature alignment at the whole-body level, while neglecting supervision on fine-grained part features, thus lacking constraints for local feature semantic consistency. To this end, we propose Part-Informed Visual-language Learning (π-VL) to enhance fine-grained visual features with part-informed language supervisions for ReID tasks. Specifically, π-VL introduces a human parsing-guided prompt tuning strategy and a hierarchical visual-language alignment paradigm to ensure within-part feature semantic consistency. The former combines both identity labels and human parsing maps to constitute pixel-level text prompts, and the latter fuses multi-scale visual features with a light-weight auxiliary head to perform fine-grained image-text alignment. As a plug-and-play and inference-free solution, our π-VL achieves performance comparable to or better than state-of-the-art methods on four commonly used ReID benchmarks. Notably, it reports 91.0% Rank-1 and 76.9% mAP on the challenging MSMT17 database, without bells and whistles.

Title: Towards Practical Real-Time Low-Latency Music Source Separation
Abstract: In recent years, significant progress has been made in the field of deep learning for music demixing. However, there has been limited attention on real-time, low-latency music demixing, which holds potential for various applications, such as hearing aids, audio stream remixing, and live performances. Additionally, a notable tendency has emerged towards the development of larger models, limiting their applicability in certain scenarios. In this paper, we introduce a lightweight real-time low-latency model called Real-Time Single-Path TFC-TDF UNET (RT-STT), which is based on the Dual-Path TFC-TDF UNET (DTTNet). In RT-STT, we propose a feature fusion technique based on channel expansion. We also demonstrate the superiority of single-path modeling over dual-path modeling in real-time models. Moreover, we investigate the method of quantization to further reduce inference time. RT-STT exhibits superior performance with significantly fewer parameters and shorter inference times compared to state-of-the-art models.

Title: Deploying Emotion-Aware Speech GANs on Edge Devices: A Real-Time Optimization Framework
Abstract: This study proposes a lightweight, real-time deployment framework for emotion-aware speech synthesis using Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) tailored for edge devices. By integrating model optimization strategies such as structured pruning, post-training quantization, and ONNX-based cross-platform conversion, the framework enables efficient on-device inference across diverse hardware including CPUs, GPUs, and the NVIDIA Jetson Nano. Performance evaluations highlight significant improvements, with inference latency reduced by up to 3.5 and memory usage by 2.8 on edge platforms, while retaining over 92% of perceptual quality based on Mean Opinion Score (MOS) metrics. On high-performance systems, the framework supports sub-50 ms latency, ensuring real-time responsiveness. These results affirm the feasibility of deploying expressive, emotionally adaptive speech systems in constrained environments. The proposed approach enhances user privacy through local processing and supports emerging applications in affective computing, conversational agents, and emotion-aware IoT systems. This work establishes a scalable benchmark for deploying generative audio models where both responsiveness and emotional nuance are vital.

Title: AI-Driven Noise Classification and Adaptive Filtering: Comparative Performance of LMS, NLMS and RLS Algorithms in Digital Hearing Aids
Abstract: Traditional hearing aids employ static or manually adjustable filters, which are unable to adapt to varying and unpredictable acoustic environments. These limitations result in subpar noise reduction and speech quality under a variety of conditions. This study bridges this gap by combining AI-driven noise classification with adaptive filtering techniques, such as Recursive Least Squares (RLS), Normalized LMS (NLMS), and LMS (LMS). This enables context-aware processing in real time. The UrbanSound8K dataset was used to train machine learning models, such as CNN, SVM, Random Forest, and MLP, to detect environmental noise patterns like traffic, industrial hum, and crowd chatter. The system dynamically chooses the best adaptive filter based on the classification output: RLS for quickly changing patterns, NLMS for moderately fluctuating noise, and LMS for stationary noise.MATLAB Simulink simulations and user trials demonstrate improvements over static filtering approaches, including higher signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), faster convergence, and enhanced speech intelligibility. These findings suggest that the foundation for next-generation hearing aids with intelligent real-time noise management may be formed by fusing adaptive DSP with AI inference.

Title: Categorizing Simple Versus OSAHS Snoring Sound Using Quantifiable Acoustic Features and Machine Learning Classifiers
Abstract: This work tackles audio signal analysis problems related to snoring sounds of simple and obstructive sleep apnea/hypopnea syndrome (OSAHS) snorers by optimizing acoustic feature extraction and training various machine learning models. Relevant acoustic features, including Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients, zero crossing rate, root mean square, and spectral features, were extracted from snoring sound recordings. Two main tasks are performed: firstly, the classification of snoring sounds from simple snorers versus OSAHS patients, and secondly, the discrimination between apnea/hypopnea events and normal snoring events of OSAHS patients. The results show an outstanding performance in differentiating between the snoring sounds of simple snorers and OSAHS patients with an accuracy of 0.9982. The challenge lies in the binary classification between apnea/hypopnea versus normal snoring events in patients with OSAHS, which was evaluated using the subject-independent leave-one-subject-out cross-validation (LOSOCV) technique, yielding an accuracy of 0.7838 and an F1-score of 0.7734 with the random forest model. Energy-related acoustic features were found to be crucial in distinguishing snoring patterns. Additionally, the apnea/hypopnea index (AHI) was subsequently estimated from the snoring pattern classification using the LOSOCV technique. The extra trees classifier demonstrated a 0.8689 Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) between predicted and actual PSG-measured AHI values. The highest performance in classifying subjects into three groups of OSAHS severity (mild, moderate, and severe) was achieved by the decision tree model with an accuracy of approximately 0.8621, based on the AHI value estimation of each subject. The voting classifier, constructed from five classifiers, provides a reliable prediction by reducing bias through the use of multiple models to mitigate the errors inherent in binary classification, achieving an accuracy of 0.8276. The study proposes estimating AHI values by analyzing individual events of snoring sounds to categorize patients into severity levels, paving the way for applying acoustic feature analysis for a non-constrained, simple, and accurate screening of sleep-related breathing disorders.

Title: AI Driven Evolutionary Optimization Framework for Patch Antenna Miniaturization
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for antenna miniaturization through the integration of parametric slotted patch design, convolutional neural networks (CNNs), and genetic algorithm (GA) optimization. Addressing the critical need for compact, high-performance antennas in modern wireless systems such as IoT and portable electronics, our methodology employs vector graphics to generate geometrically complex slotted patches with substantial footprint reduction. A CNN-based surrogate model is developed to predict the electromagnetic response of candidate geometries. The GA then iteratively optimizes slot configurations to achieve target resonance frequencies while minimizing physical dimensions. Implemented for 3.2 GHz and 4 GHz prototypes, the approach demonstrates significant size reductions of 75% (from 35 × 25 mm to 16 × 12 mm) and 65 % (from 26 × 21 mm to 16 × 12 mm), respectively, while maintaining excellent impedance matching. Comparative analysis with conventional rectangular patches confirms superior miniaturization capabilities.

Title: Heterogeneous Classifier Fusion for Preeclampsia Risk Assessment
Abstract: Preeclampsia is a hypertensive disorder that typically arises at the end of the 2nd trimester or the beginning of the 3rd trimester of pregnancy and is a major cause of maternal-fetal morbidity and mortality. In this study, four different machine learning algorithms (CatBoost, Random Forest, LightGBM, and Multilayer Perceptron) and a hybrid model created by combining these models with the soft voting ensemble method are comparatively evaluated for early prediction of preeclampsia risk. In the experimental studies performed on two distinct datasets, the Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE) method was implemented for feature selection, and the class imbalance problem was addressed with the SMOTE algorithm. The Soft Voting Ensemble Model (SVEM) demonstrated superior performance, with 92.50% accuracy and 97.63% Area Under the Curve-Receiver Operating Characteristic (AUC-ROC) values in the factors for Preeclampsia dataset and 92.16% accuracy and 93.35% AUCROC values in the Maternal Health Risk dataset. The Ensemble approach reduced the rates of false positive and false negative results by ensuring balanced classification success between positive and negative classes. The findings indicate that the proposed approach can serve as a reliable instrument within the framework of clinical decision support systems.

Title: Digital Technologies and the Effectiveness of Green and Blue Finance: Cross-Country Evidence Using Proxy Indicators
Abstract: This study investigates the differential impact of digital technology adoption on the performance of green and blue bonds across 30 economies over a 10-year panel. Using GHG Intensity, World Governance Indicator (WGI), and Ocean Health Index (OHI) as proxies for environmental and institutional performance, the paper develops a composite Tech Index derived from AI, IoT, Blockchain, and Big Data readiness scores. Empirical analysis employs fixed and random effects panel regressions with Hausman tests for model selection. Results show that IoT significantly reduces GHG Intensity (β =-0.1242, p < 0.01), while Big Data exhibits a counterintuitive positive association (β = 0.1159, p < 0.01). Governance outcomes (WGI) are positively influenced by digital readiness (NRI) but negatively by AI and Big Data adoption in transitional economies. The Tech Index is positively associated with marine ecosystem health, improving OHI scores significantly (β = 9.48, p = 0.011). These findings validate the use of proxy-based evaluation frameworks and demonstrate how digital maturity shapes environmental-financial performance asymmetrically across green and blue finance instruments. The study contributes to sustainable finance literature by integrating digital technology metrics into green and blue bond effectiveness models and offers policy pathways for digital-institutional alignment in ESG governance.

Title: Al-based Parkinson's Disease Diagnosis with Word Level Speech Data using Advanced Signal Processing Techniques
Abstract: Parkinson's Disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder that profoundly compromises patients' quality of life. Early and accurate diagnosis remains a clinical challenge, with voice signal analysis emerging as a promising non-invasive biomarker. Unlike the classical vowel sounds used in existing studies, we present a new PD sound dataset that includes a Turkish word "gofret"vocalized by the PD and control groups. The collected dataset was converted into images using Mel - Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs), spectrograms, chromograms and tempograms in order to develop vision-based deep learning models from audio recordings. To mitigate data scarcity and enhance model generalizability, a suite of data augmentation strategies including frequency masking, time stretching, shifting and masking were systematically applied. In this study, alternative deep learnnig architectures were developed and their performances were compared. Quantitative evaluations, employing rigorous cross-validation protocols, demonstrated superior classification performance of spectrogram-based models with 85.6% accuracy in PD diagnosis, underscoring their robustness in capturing pathological vocal characteristics. The findings advocate for the integration of advanced augmentation techniques and multifaceted acoustic representations to bolster automated PD detection efficacy from voice data.

Title: A Study of Word-informed Ensemble Speech Enhancement System
Abstract: Inspired by the success of ensemble speech enhancement methods that integrate diverse sound modalities, this study introduces the Word-Informed Ensemble Speech Enhancement (WI-ESE) system for noise reduction in speech signals. WI-ESE is a two-stage framework, designed based on the assumption that words within an utterance exhibit different phonetic variations. In the first stage, input speech is processed separately using utterance-based and word-based models, and in the second stage, the outputs are further enhanced. Experimental evaluations on the TMHINT dataset demonstrate that WI-ESE effectively leverages both models to achieve superior speech quality improvement.

Title: Advanced Diabetes Prediction System Leveraging Multi-Source Data and Ensemble Learning
Abstract: Early diagnosis of diabetes plays a critical role in reducing complications and improving patient outcomes. This study develops and evaluates a machine learning-based diabetes prediction system using two datasets of different scales: the well-established Pima Indians Diabetes Database (PIDD) and a larger Diabetes Prediction Dataset containing 100,000 patient records. The proposed methodology combines comprehensive data preprocessing, including missing value imputation, outlier removal, normalization, and feature selection, ensuring high-quality inputs for model training. A range of machine learning and deep learning algorithms were applied, including ensemble models and neural networks, with performance assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Gradient Boosting produced the best accuracy results through examination of the PIDD dataset which achieved 77% accuracy and the bigger dataset that reached 97% accuracy. The analysis demonstrates that applying balanced small datasets with diverse large datasets improves both model generalizations and makes them stronger. The system performs three-category classification through medical attribute analysis for non-diabetic and pre-diabetic and diabetic groups. The approach that uses two datasets enables better performance because it trains the model to recognize distinct clinical patterns alongside natural real-world diversity. The system's ability to work with evolving patient data is provided by this methodology which makes it an invaluable instrument for early diabetes screening combined with personalized risk assessment. Further research will add unstructured data sources to the system while also working to make its results more understandable for clinical practitioners.

Title: A Hybrid Deep Learning Model for Evaluation System of Traditional Chinese Music Performance
Abstract: Ancient Chinese music, with its rich cultural meanings and expressive subtleties, is quite challenging to objectively evaluate because it is interpretative, sensitive to tones, and heterogeneous in terms of style. Current systems of evaluation depend on the expert's subjective feedback or predetermined rubric scores, which are typically associated with inconsistencies, low scalability, and non-tailored treatment. To address these challenges, this research introduces an innovative intelligent assessment system that combined hybrid model to evaluate musical performances accurately and with stylistic sensitivity. The system receives audio inputs through sophisticated signal processing methods, extracting the most important musical features like pitch accuracy, rhythm stability, timbre tone, and dynamic intensity. These characteristics are subsequently examined by the deep learning model that has been trained on expert-annotated traditional Chinese music performances, mimicking human-like assessment patterns. Experimental confirmation on the dataset compiled for varied musical content yields excellent results with an accuracy of 96.6%, precision of 96.6%, recall of 96.4%, and an F1-score of 96.5%. This smart system not only increases consistency and interpretability but also provides useful real-time feedback for students and teachers, making it a potential tool for furthering the contemporary pedagogy of Chinese traditional music education.

Title: AI Agent-Based Framework for Personalized Music Recommendation
Abstract: Personalized music recommendation plays a critical role in modern digital media platforms, yet existing systems often lack adaptability, contextual sensitivity, and user transparency. This paper presents an AI agent-based framework designed to deliver real-time, personalized music recommendations by leveraging hybrid modeling and adaptive learning. The proposed architecture integrates collaborative filtering, content-based analysis, and contextual features using a multi-model ensemble comprising XGBoost, neural networks, and audio feature extractors. At its core, an intelligent AI agent employs reinforcement learning to continuously refine recommendations based on user feedback and listening patterns. The system further incorporates FAISS-powered memory for long-term user profiling and SHAP-based explainability to enhance trust and interpretability. Title: Investigation into the Factors Affecting the Integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Human Resources Management (HRM) within Jordanian Banks
Abstract: This study examines the factors that influence integrating artificial intelligence (AI) into human resources management (HRM) in Jordanian banks, a sector that has not yet extensively adopted AI. This study uses a mixed-method technique that includes both qualitative and quantitative approaches, the research consists of a sample of 130 HR directors and other stakeholders from seven commercial banks in Jordan. The main data-gathering instruments were surveys and interviews programmed to meet the research objectives and to confirm the research hypotheses. The major findings indicate some substantial barriers and challenges that prevent AI's integration into the HRM in Jordanian banks. Such barriers include a lack of knowledge, poor skillful personnel, employee resistance to change, and privacy and security concerns about data. Despite many challenges such as high costs of AI implementation, and difficulties in AI implementation, and regulatory and compliance issues the study demonstrates that AI can positively affect HRM by enhancing talent acquisition, automating routine tasks, and other HR functions. According to the experimental validation of our proposition, AI can be used in HRM to improve productivity and reduce time wastage on administrative tasks with enough provision of financial and material resources. It concludes by giving practical advice on how the given barriers and challenges may be overcome and how AI could be optimally employed to boost HRM services in Jordan's banking sector. If these barriers and challenges are addressed and the potential benefits of its implementation are showcased, then banks can enhance their HRM practices which will eventually lead to improved organizational performance as well as competitiveness.

Title: Data-Driven Spatial Dynamics Decoding for Remote Health Monitoring
Abstract: Remote health monitoring instrument, leveraging noncontact sensing device for achieving high convenience, is of great potential to establish long-term continuous big data toward precision medicine. The challenge arises in the quick decaying of the signal when propagating from the human body to the sensor remotely placed. Targeting this challenge, we propose a novel data-driven spatial dynamics decoding framework for mining the remotely captured array signals with health dynamics encoded. More specifically, the innovative framework leverages the two-stage deep learning architecture, which first boosts the array signal fidelity through the deep autoencoder-based distortion suppression and afterward extracts the spatial patterns and yields the inference results through the convolutional learning of the boosted array signals. Furthermore, the framework leverages the data-driven approach to avoid the need of the reference signal that is usually required in the communication system and also to boost the minority class given the imbalanced dataset. To evaluate the system, we have performed experiments on sleep apnea detection, with our customized on-bedframe sensing device and with the proposed deep learning framework. Through comprehensive comparison with the state of the art, we have demonstrated the superior performance of the proposed novel instrument that can achieve a detection accuracy of 94.4%, even with the decayed signal remotely captured. Title: Semi-Supervised Sound Event Detection Based on Multi-Scale Attention
Abstract: Sound event detection (SED) involves identifying the onset and offset times as well as the categories of acoustic events within an audio signal. In practical real-world situations, sound events frequently exhibit temporal overlap and substantial duration variability, making SED a crucial research area in audio signal processing. Although deep learning has significantly advanced SED performance, several challenges remain unresolved. The intrinsic diversity of sound events leads to significant disparities in their time-frequency features, making numerous current models ineffective for reliable event detection. To tackle these limitations, this research puts forward a semi-supervised learning framework for SED incorporating multi-scale attention mechanisms. The proposed model enhances discriminative capability across heterogeneous sound events through a dedicated multi-scale attention module. Furthermore, frequency-adaptive dynamic convolution is employed to improve the model's physical congruence with time-frequency patterns within acoustic events. Experimental validation on the DCASE 2021 Task 4 (DESED) dataset demonstrates the superior performance of our approach compared to existing methods.

Title: Integrating Advanced Machine Learning Techniques for Enhanced Customer Lifetime Value Prediction
Abstract: Customer Lifetime Value (CLV) forecasting is implemented by organizations as a core business strategy for customer interaction enhancement, marketing investment optimization, and sustained revenue generation. Accurate CLV predictions enable customer engagement adaptation, improved business decisions, and resource distribution optimization. Traditional CLV systems utilizing national data series with simple command-based models frequently failed in evolving consumer behavior analysis. Predictive performance, system responsiveness, and strategic business value are now significantly boosted by recent Machine Learning (ML) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) advancements. Sophisticated AI-based CLV prediction technology has been implemented in this study, uniting customer segments with multi-dimensional data, predictive analytics, and immediate response mechanisms. Transaction records, behavioral indicators, and demographic factors are incorporated into the model, with precise CLV calculation achieved through ensemble techniques, time-series forecasting, regression, and deep learning models. The study's key focus is formed by behavioral pattern analysis, with purchase frequency, engagement scores, retention probability, and churn risk being assessed. The value-based clustering and micro-segmentation results in focused marketing efforts by narrowing down what kind of customers can be applied. The value is estimated in terms of the financial value based on the projections of revenues, the cost of acquisition and the forecasted profitability. The real-time feedback loops adapt the CLV forecast scale to the changes of behavior. The predictive interaction modeling is quantified by customer touch point analysis, the cross-channel activities as well as the messaging strategies. Ethical AI development precludes biases when it comes to preserving privacy. The policies of the world, the uses of industry to different industries, the quality of data, the complex calculation in use, and explainable AI (XAI) are explored. AI-based CLV prediction instrument generates long-term business development and competitive advantages in the market transformation.

Title: Investigation of the Performance of Different EEG Channel Sets for Imagined Word Classification
Abstract: This study evaluates the impact of classification architecture and EEG channel configuration on imagined word recognition using data from the 2020 International BCI Competition. EEG signals corresponding to five imagined phrases were preprocessed and transformed into topographic brain maps, which were classified using a hybrid deep learning model combining 3D-CNN and LSTM layers. Two classification approaches were compared: a direct multi-class model and a nested framework that separates single and compound words. While both approaches showed comparable accuracy, the direct model demonstrated superior efficiency. In parallel, four EEG channel sets were analyzed to assess their influence on classification performance. The best-performing set, selected using subject-specific utility metrics, included electrodes spanning frontal, temporal, central, parietal, and occipital regions. This configuration achieved an average accuracy of 36.8% in multi-class classification and ranged between 31.1% to 39.1 % in the nested classification. These findings emphasize the value of optimized model structure and targeted channel selection in enhancing imagined speech decoding from EEG signals.

Title: Design and Application of Music Cloud Teaching Platform based on Artificial Intelligence Algorithm
Abstract: The rapid evolution of intelligent education platforms has greatly transformed traditional teaching methodologies, especially in music education. However, existing digital platforms do not offer adaptive, efficient, and context-sensitive learning experiences. To address these limitations, this research develops an adaptive cloud-based music education system powered by a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) algorithm. By modeling the sequential and temporal dependencies of musical elements, the proposed system supports real-time analysis of learner interaction patterns and enhances intelligent content delivery. The dataset used in this study comprises a diverse collection of user interaction data, audio features, and performance evaluations gathered from an online music learning environment. The BiLSTM model was employed to predict user skill levels and generate personalized learning paths. Experimental results demonstrated an accuracy of 98.2%, outperforming other learning models and confirming its effectiveness in addressing individual learner needs. Additionally, Precision (97.8%), Recall (98.1%), Specificity (97.9%), and F1-Score (97.9%) highlight the efficiency of the proposed method. The model is deployed within a cloud-based infrastructure, enabling seamless access to educational content, real-time monitoring of learner performance, and scalable delivery across institutions. Title: Comparison of MFCC and Spectrogram Analysis in Improving the Accuracy of CNN Models for Song Clip Prediction
Abstract: The performance of automatic music recognition models largely depends on the chosen feature extraction method. This study compares two widely used techniquesMFCC and Spectrograms-to determine which works better with CNNs for classifying short song clips. In conclusion, Spectrograms are more effective at capturing the intricate patterns in audio because they are more accurately classify songs.

Title: Enhanced Skin Cancer Classification with VGG-16 Using Dermoscopic Image Analysis
Abstract: One of the most often occurring cancers globally, skin cancer depends on early identification for efficient treatment. Often time-consuming and prone to human variability are traditional diagnostic techniques. This work improves skin cancer classification using dermoscopic image analysis using the VGG-16 deep learning (DL) model. 25,000 dermoscopic images from publicly accessible sources were utilized in a dataset; images were pre-processed using resizing, normalizing, and augmentation to enhance model generalizing. Transfer learning helped to refine the pre-trained VGG-16 model for binary classification benign against malignant. The experiment's results showed the proposed model's exceptional performance, which showed 100% accuracy. The technique also reduced false positives and negatives, providing ideal early detection. These results highlight the possibilities of DL in dermatology as they provide a quick and accurate AI-assisted diagnostic instrument. Real-time clinical validation and multimodal data integration will be the main emphasis of the next projects to improve model performance.

Title: A Novel Prediction of Tourism Economic Development Trends based on Machine Learning
Abstract: Tourism economic forecasting is a critical exercise hindered by cyclical variations, unforeseen factors, and multiple-variable interdependence. This study presents a prediction model based on neural networks that identifies intricate correlations among variables such as tourist arrival, seasonal patterns, consumption, and investment in infrastructure. Title: A Machine Learning based Intelligent Evaluation Technique for Information Literacy of Foreign Language Teachers
Abstract: Assessing information literacy of foreign language teachers is critical in improving teaching effectiveness and academic achievement. Current assessment frameworks, however, depend on qualitative surveys and conventional statistical models that are not flexible and not accurate. Conventional models, including rule-based and linear regression models, cannot identify nonlinear relationships among complex literacy indicators. This paper proposes a Radial Basis Function (RBF)-based deep learning model to overcome such constraints. The proposed model is efficient in handling intricate, multidimensional data with high generalization and increased convergence. Comparative study against conventional backpropagation neural networks and support vector machines shows the excellence of the proposed RBF model in performance with 96.2% accuracy and 95.8% F1-score, being superior to others by 6-10%. The system takes information behaviour measures, digital resource use, and cognitive ability indices as input parameters. This methodology not only improves the accuracy of assessments but also facilitates targeted intervention training for educators.

Title: Transformer-EKF for UWB Positioning: A Benchmark Against CNN and BiLSTM Models
Abstract: Ultra-Wideband (UWB) indoor positioning systems suffer significant accuracy degradation in Non-Line-of-Sight (NLoS) conditions, where multipath distortions in the Channel Impulse Response (CIR) lead to biased range estimates. While deep learning (DL) models have shown potential in predicting such errors from CIR data, most prior studies focus on isolated architectures and static pipelines, without evaluating their broader integration into full positioning systems. This work presents a comparative study of three DL models - Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory networks (BiLSTM), and Transformer - for CIR-based range error prediction, integrated into both Weighted Least Squares (WLS) and Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) frameworks. In WLS, predicted errors are used as adaptive weights to suppress unreliable measurements; in EKF, they dynamically scale the measurement noise covariance for more accurate filtering. We evaluate all models across four realistic indoor environments using a public UWB dataset. Our results show that Transformer-EKF achieves the best performance, reducing mean positioning error to 0.59m in Environment 2 (severe NLoS/multipath) while maintaining real-time inference at 0.059 milliseconds per position. These findings establish a comprehensive benchmark for learning-based UWB positioning and demonstrate the value of fusing data-driven range correction with model-based tracking.

Title: Segmentation Network with Strip⁃Like Feature Enhancement for Lithium Battery Electrode CT Images
Abstract: Objective The internal structure of lithium batteries, particularly the precise geometry and arrangement of their electrodes, is critical to their performance, safety, and lifespan, which directly affects the viability of new energy vehicles. Computed tomography (CT) provides high-resolution 3D imagery for inspecting these internal structures, enabling the assessment of key quality parameters such as electrode overhang and alignment. However, accurately segmenting individual electrodes in CT images presents significant challenges due to their strip-like geometry, dense packing, the presence of image artifacts, and low contrast inherent in CT scans of lithium battery materials. Existing instance segmentation models, including both established architectures and recent general-purpose or large-scale pre-trained models, often exhibit inefficient feature representation for these specific targets, leading to suboptimal segmentation accuracy, poor edge delineation, and connectivity issues. To address these limitations, we develop a novel deep learning network, Batt-Mask2Former, specifically optimized for the high-precision instance segmentation of these electrodes within CT images, thereby providing a reliable basis for subsequent quantitative quality assessment. Methods We propose Batt-Mask2Former, a novel instance segmentation network designed for the high-precision segmentation of electrodes in lithium battery CT images. Batt-Mask2Former enhances the Mask2Former framework by incorporating two key innovative modules: the cascaded multi-scale strip convolutional encoder (CMSCE) and the alternating path aggregation feature pyramid network (APAFPN), both specifically engineered to address the unique challenges of electrode feature extraction. The CMSCE module employs a cascaded architecture of multi-scale strip convolutional encoders. Each CMSCE, through its core multi-scale channel-weighted stripe convolutional attention mechanism, utilizes parallel branches with varying-kernel-size strip convolutions and channel-wise attention to effectively capture the elongated geometry and multi-scale contextual information of electrodes. The cascaded structure facilitates progressive feature refinement and cross-group information interaction. Following the CMSCE, the APAFPN integrates the processed multi-scale features using a three-stage alternating path strategy. Key components within the APAFPN include a dynamic upsampling module (DySample) for feature upscaling and standard downsampling convolutions. A specialized feature fusion module is also included, which combines standard convolutions with strip convolutions to further enhance the representation of slender electrode structures during the multi-level feature integration process. Results and Discussions The proposed Batt-Mask2Former is validated on a dataset derived from open-source lithium-ion battery CT scans, featuring pouch and 2170 cylindrical cell images (Fig. 8), as well as on a self-scanned blade lithium-ion battery CT dataset (Fig. 12). Performance of the proposed Batt-Mask2Former is benchmarked against several representative state-of-the-art instance segmentation methods, including SparseInst, SCNet, Cascade R-CNN, QueryInst, Mask2Former, Co-DETR, and DI-MaskDINO. On the pouch and 2170 cylindrical cell dataset (Table 2), Batt-Mask2Former demonstrates superior performance, achieving an mAP (mean average precision) of 46.8%, mAP50 [mAP at intersection-over-union (IoU) of 0.5] of 87.7%, mAP75 (mAP at IoU of 0.75) of 44.4%, and mAR (mean average recall) of 57.4%. These results represent improvements of 3.5%, 1.4%, 5.8%, and 2.5% in mAP, mAP<inf>50</inf>, mAP<inf>75</inf>, and mAR, respectively, over the Mask2Former baseline. While the inference speed is 14.1 frame/s, the quantitative gains highlight the effectiveness of Batt-Mask2Former for electrode segmentation. Visual comparisons on pouch (Fig. 9) and 2170 cell (Fig. 10) images further corroborate these findings. Ablation studies systematically validate the contributions of the proposed modules. The combined use of the CMSCE and the APAFPN proves optimal, achieving the peak mAP of 46.8% (Table 3). To assess generalization capabilities, Batt-Mask2Former is evaluated on the self-scanned lithium-ion battery CT dataset. On this distinct dataset, our method also achieves state-of-the-art results, with an mAP of 61.3%, an mAP<inf>50</inf> of 99.4%, an mAP<inf>75</inf> of 70.5%, and an mAR of 68.5% (Table 7). This performance confirms Batt-Mask2Former’s strong adaptability to different battery types and imaging conditions. Visual results on the blade lithium battery dataset (Fig. 12) further support this conclusion. Conclusions We address the significant challenge of accurately segmenting slender, high-aspect-ratio electrodes in lithium battery CT images, a critical task for non-destructive quality assessment and safety assurance. Existing instance segmentation models often struggle with inefficient feature representation for such specific geometries and are adversely affected by CT image artifacts. To overcome these limitations, we propose Batt-Mask2Former, a novel deep learning network. Batt-Mask2Former enhances the Mask2Former framework with two core innovations: a CMSCE designed to specifically capture elongated structural features and multi-scale contextual information, and an APAFPN engineered for effective fusion of multi-level features while preserving detail. Comprehensive evaluations on public pouch and 2170 cylindrical cell CT datasets, as well as a self-scanned blade lithium battery dataset, demonstrate that Batt-Mask2Former significantly outperforms several mainstream and state-of-the-art instance segmentation models in key metrics, including mAP, mAP<inf>50</inf>, mAP<inf>75</inf>, and mAR. The proposed method shows clear advantages in accurately delineating electrode edges and maintaining segmentation integrity across diverse battery types. While Batt-Mask2Former achieves superior segmentation accuracy, its introduced network complexity leads to a moderate inference speed. Future research will therefore focus on optimizing the model’s computational efficiency to better balance accuracy and real-time performance for industrial deployment.

Title: Interpretable Deep Learning for Music Genre Classification Using Spectrogram Analysis
Abstract: Recognizing and categorizing musical genres is a well-known and long-standing problem in music information retrieval, generally regarded as a black box problem among deep learning pipelines. This paper presents a new interpretable architecture for genre classification by using CNNs, and combining with the novel scripts related to explainability, to extract meaning from spectrograms in order to differentiate genres of music. We used the GTZAN dataset, and implemented three architectures-VGG19, ResNet18 and a custom CNN- and fine-tuned each model using the Mel spectrograms as input. Importantly, we inserted explainability via Grad-CAM, which provided explanatory visualizations, showing transparency into what each model is doing internally to arrive at their final decisions. The most successful performing model was VGG19, which yielded a peak validation accuracy of around 82%, followed by a Custom CNN model at 77.50%, while the ResNet18 had a moderate performance of 75.50%. ResNet18 model exhibited unique interpretability as seen in Grad-CAM. The Grad-CAM visualizations revealed interesting learning behavior: the VGG19 and Custom CNN models were often activated on the negative space in high-frequency regions, which was particularly for blues tracks, which suggests some sort of structural attention beyond the rhythmic contours. The ResNet18 model relied more on some consistent texture patterns. This study provides a general understanding of which frequency regions are most implicated in genre categorization which serves as an important link between the success of deep learning and human understanding of music.

Title: Detecting Process Equipment Failures Using Acoustic Data and Machine Learning
Abstract: Nuclear power plant (NPP) process equipment such as fans, motors, valves, and pumps generate frequent or continuous noise, and deviations from the normal operational sounds made by this equipment can indicate potential issues. These deviations can be identified via automated acoustic anomaly detection, which involves using acoustic sensors (i.e., microphones) alongside detection algorithms to continuously monitor for changes in acoustic signatures. This task is made challenging by the substantial background noise that exists, such as operators opening and closing doors, manipulating valves, and conversing-in addition to typical plant noises. In collaboration with a nuclear power utility partner, this effort assessed the efficacy of acoustic anomaly detection when using a specific acoustic sensor that compresses data into a fixed set of features that are transferable over a standard Internet of Things communication protocol, thereby improving usability but potentially degrading detection performance. Two methods of performing automated acoustic anomaly detection were evaluated: one-class support vector machine (OC-SVM) and isolation forest (iForest). To enable the use of high-quality acoustic data encompassing both normal and anomalous conditions, the study utilized the publicly available Malfunctioning Industrial Machine Investigation and Inspection dataset, which includes real measured acoustic sensor data for a range of equipment types, model numbers, and signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs), along with a benchmark set of detection results. Using this dataset, the methods were tested and then compared against the benchmark results. The results indicated that although the specific acoustic sensor did not enable as rich a feature set extraction, the proposed methods with the limited feature set performed just as well. This provides solid justification for both the methods and the use of the proposed acoustic sensor.

Title: Experimenting Active and Sequential Learning in a Medieval Music Manuscript
Abstract: Optical Music Recognition (OMR) is a cornerstone of music digitization initiatives in cultural heritage, yet it remains limited by the scarcity of annotated data and the complexity of historical manuscripts. In this paper, we present a preliminary study of Active Learning (AL) and Sequential Learning (SL) tailored for object detection and layout recognition in an old medieval music manuscript. Leveraging YOLOv8, our system selects samples with the highest uncertainty (lowest prediction confidence) for iterative labeling and retraining. Our approach starts with a single annotated image and successfully boosts performance while minimizing manual labeling. Experimental results indicate that comparable accuracy to fully supervised training can be achieved with significantly fewer labeled examples. We test the methodology as a preliminary investigation on a novel dataset offered to the community by the Anonymous project, which studies laude, a poetical-musical genre spread across Italy during the 12th-16th Century. We show that in the manuscript at-hand, uncertainty-based AL is not effective and advocates for more usable methods in data-scarcity scenarios.

Title: Tiny Noise-Robust Voice Activity Detector for Voice Assistants
Abstract: Voice Activity Detection (VAD) in the presence of background noise remains a challenging problem in speech processing. Accurate VAD is essential in automatic speech recognition, voice-to-text, conversational agents, etc, where noise can severely degrade the performance. A modern application includes the voice assistant, specially mounted on Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT) devices such as cell phones, smart glasses, earbuds, etc, in which the voice signal includes background noise. Therefore, VAD modules must remain light-weight due to their practical on-device limitation. The existing models often struggle with low signal-tonoise ratios across diverse acoustic environments. A simple VAD often detects human voice in a clean environment, but struggles to detect the human voice in noisy conditions. We propose a noise-robust VAD that comprises a light-weight VAD, with data pre-processing and post-processing modules to handle the background noise. This approach significantly enhances the VAD accuracy in noisy environments and requires neither a larger model, nor fine-tuning. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves a notable improvement compared to baselines, particularly in environments with high background noise interference. This modified VAD additionally improves clean speech detection.

Title: Predicting alcohol use disorder risk in firefighters using a multimodal deep learning model: a cross-sectional study
Abstract: Introduction: Firefighters constitute a high-risk occupational cohort for alcohol use disorder (AUD) due to chronic trauma exposure, yet traditional screening methodologies relying on self-report instruments remain compromised by systematic underreporting attributable to occupational stigma and career preservation concerns. This cross-sectional investigation developed and validated a multimodal deep learning framework integrating T1-weighted structural magnetic resonance imaging with standardized neuropsychological assessments to enable objective AUD risk stratification without necessitating computationally intensive functional neuroimaging protocols. Methods: Analysis of 689 active-duty firefighters (mean age 43.3±8.8 years; 93% male) from a nationwide occupational cohort incorporated high-resolution three-dimensional T1-weighted structural MRI acquisition alongside comprehensive neuropsychological evaluation utilizing the Grooved Pegboard Test for visual-motor coordination assessment and Trail Making Test for executive function quantification. The novel computational architecture synergistically combined ResNet-50 convolutional neural networks for hierarchical morphological feature extraction, Vision Transformer modules for global neuroanatomical pattern recognition, and multilayer perceptron integration of clinical variables, with model interpretability assessed through Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping and SHapley Additive exPlanations methodologies. Performance evaluation employed stratified three-fold cross-validation with DeLong's test for statistical comparison of receiver operating characteristic curves. Results: The multimodal framework achieved 79.88% classification accuracy with area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 79.65%, representing statistically significant performance enhancement relative to clinical-only (62.53%; p<0.001) and neuroimaging-only (61.53%; p<0.001) models, demonstrating a 17.35 percentage-point improvement attributable to synergistic cross-modal integration rather than simple feature concatenation. Interpretability analyses revealed stochastic activation patterns in unimodal neuroimaging models lacking neuroanatomically coherent feature localization, while clinical feature importance hierarchically prioritized biological sex and motor coordination metrics as primary predictive indicators. The framework maintained robust calibration across probability thresholds, supporting operational feasibility for clinical deployment. Discussion: This investigation establishes that structural neuroimaging combined with targeted neuropsychological assessment achieves classification performance comparable to complex multimodal protocols while substantially reducing acquisition time and computational requirements, offering a pragmatic pathway for implementing objective AUD screening in high-risk occupational populations with broader implications for psychiatric risk stratification in trauma-exposed professions.
