Title: An Observation Instrument for Technical and Tactical Actions in the Soccer Offense Phase: Design, Validation, and Reliability
Abstract: Coaches and other sports professionals are given adaptable tools by using observational methods in the context of sports. These tools are frequently used in team sports for technical and tactical analysis of the match. The goal was to build, validate, and evaluate the dependability of a mixed observational instrument of field formats and category systems to study technical and tactical activities in the offensive phase of soccer, taking into account the significance of data quality in these instruments. The device records data on the attacking team’s and goalkeeper’s actions with the ball, play moments (start, development, and end), and surrounding circumstances. Four steps were taken in the instrument design, validation, and reliability calculation: (a) literature review; (b) initial draft design; (c) qualitative and quantitative expert assessment of the instrument; and (d) observer training test (reliability calculation). Ten experts (soccer coaches with at least ten years of coaching experience or sports scientists with a PhD) determined the content validity. The Delphi process was applied. A quantitative (scale 0 10) and qualitative examination was performed by experts. The following topics were covered in the questionnaire for experts: (a) understanding of the criteria, categorical cores, degree of openness, and their definitions; (b) applicability of the categorical cores and degree of openness; and (c) decision-making on the inclusion of further categorical cores or degree of openness in the observation instrument. The categorical core "numerical situation with opponent goalkeeper" has the lowest Aiken’s V index of 0.91. The levels of agreement between and among observers were good. The category core "defensive pressing lines" had the lowest Kappa index (0.96 for inter-reliability and 0.98 for intra-reliability), as did the category core "ball height (start of ball possession)," "distance of the defensive player," "ball height (end of ball possession")," "numerical situation," and "defensive pressing lines." The generalizability analysis’ results demonstrated the instrument’s excellent level of accuracy, validity, and reliability. The findings demonstrate that the tool can be used to gather unbiased, trustworthy information regarding soccer’s offensive phase.

Title: Spiking Neural Network Design for on-board detection of methane emissions through Neuromorphic Computing
Abstract: Small satellite constellations have shown tremendous success for Earth observation missions and can mimic the performance of large satellite platforms while being cheaper and faster to deploy. Detecting fugitive methane emissions from ageing oil and gas infrastructures is an important use-case, as it helps facility operators to locate and mitigate these leaks, ultimately addressing the global climate crisis. For such applications, it is crucial for the data to be transmitted to the end-user in a timely manner for appropriate actions to take place. Edge Artificial Intelligence (AI) can address this issue by pre-processing the data on-board the spacecraft, dramatically reducing the amount of data to be sent to the ground and thus improving response times and bandwidth. As small satellites are greatly constrained by a low size, weight and power (SWaP), their ability to process AI algorithms with fewer computational resources is essential. AI applications often depend on real time data processing and analysis, yet most modern computers are inefficient in these tasks. Neuromorphic Computing's (NC) parallel and distributed architecture helps perform complex calculations faster while using less power, enabling more efficient in-orbit data processing and onboard adaptive learning. This paper evaluates the potential of a novel 6U CubeSat neuromorphic on-board computer, applied to a case study for point-source methane emissions monitoring. It involves the design, implementation, and evaluation of a Spiking Neural Network (SNN) tailored for small satellite platforms. The necessary processing steps for detection of point-source methane emissions using hyperspectral imagery are presented, and the potential of edge computing is discussed. A full processing pipeline enabling real-time monitoring is proposed, which involved an SNN for segmentation of methane plumes. The architectural specifications necessary for neuromorphic computing in the resource-constrained satellite environment are outlined. NC principles are incorporated into the SNN architecture design, leveraging event-driven computation to improve energy efficiency and computational throughput. The processor's performance is compared with traditional computing approaches. Finally, a plan to train the model using an annotated dataset from the AVIRIS-NG hyperspectral instrument is presented, although training and validation are left for future work. By embracing neuromorphic computing, an innovative approach inspired by the brain, satellites can achieve unparalleled efficiency and accuracy. The SNN model presented contributes to the scarce body of research on edge AI for greenhouse gas monitoring, providing a step forward towards real-time Earth observation.

Title: Cloud Detection with Deep Neural Networks from Multi-Temporal Sentinel-2 imagery
Abstract: Cloud cover significantly hampers the processing of time series data collected by space-based optical remote sensing instruments. By affecting the visibility of the background, clouds and their shadows greatly reduce the usability of images for land applications. Therefore, cloud identification is a crucial pre-processing step in all remote sensing based climate studies. Yet, it remains a challenging and unsolved task due to the variety of scenarios, including different degrees of occlusion, types of clouds, and a wide range of ground spectral signatures. Although numerous methods have addressed this issue, they often tackle the problem by classifying individual pixels based on their spectral signature or local context, which does not incorporate long-term patterns. These approaches often lead to misclassification of ambiguous reflectances, such as snow perceived as clouds, and terrain shadows or inland waters as cloud shadows. Together with the results of Cloud Masking Intercomparison exercise, we argue that complementary temporal sequences of images can alleviate these conflicts. Since a cloud is inherently transient, comparing images of the same area at different times may help to identify it. This study aims to model this intuition in a deep neural network. To achieve this, we propose a U-Net inspired network that fuses temporal features to support the interpretation of satellite image, thereby improving cloud mask decoding. In order to harness the full potential of the temporal dimension, we leverage state-of-the-art methods such as attention mechanisms. The training of this algorithm was enabled by the multi-temporal dataset CloudSEN12 offering 2 000 regions with 5 Sentinel-2 tiles each manually annotated. We initiated the process by building a mono-temporal model to serve as a baseline for comparison and highlight the contribution of time series data. In preliminary tests, our model already surpasses the performance achieved in CMIX on the CloudSEN12 dataset. Nevertheless, we conclude that a classical fusion of temporal features by convolution is unable to make the most of temporal examples. We then investigated other multi-temporal configurations in which this module could thrive, especially attention mechanisms. It is trained to enhance deep semantic features and reduce redundant information in temporal skip connections. To go further in the study and understand better the models behavior, we conducted experiments on the spectral bands, the characteristics and number of temporal examples. It mainly allowed us to highlight the strengths and the weaknesses of these attention mechanisms in this particular use case.

Title: Improved Mahalanobis-Taguchi System Versus Convolutional Neural Networks for Acoustic Signal Recognition: A Case Study on Car Window Motor Sound Monitoring
Abstract: This study conducts a comparative analysis of the Mahalanobis-Taguchi System (MTS) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for acoustic signal recognition, explicitly applied to monitoring car window motor operational sounds. Using a LabVIEW-based system, acoustic signals from operating motors were captured via a high-sensitivity microphone connected to a data acquisition device, yielding a dataset comprising 30 functional (GO) motors and 10 defective (NO-GO) motors. The primary objective was to assess the fault detection capabilities of both methodologies. For the CNN model, a hybrid Conv2D+LSTM architecture was employed to enhance performance in identifying subtle anomalies. Experimental results demonstrated that the CNN model achieved a classification accuracy of 98.3 % in identifying functional motors, outperforming the MTS, which attained an accuracy of 93.3%. These findings highlight the superior ability of CNNs to capture nuanced variations in acoustic signals, underscoring their potential in predictive maintenance and quality assurance applications within the automotive industry. The successful deployment of this acoustic signal recognition system illustrates the advantages of integrating machine learning and artificial intelligence into industrial processes. Future work should aim to expand the dataset by incorporating a wider variety of motor sound profiles and explore advanced AI techniques to enhance fault detection precision in manufacturing environments further.

Title: Research progress in the automatic identification and tracking of surgical instruments for endovascular intervention under X-ray fluoroscopy

Title: Instrument Independent Chord Recognition Using Lossless-to-Lossy Transcoding in Homophonic Audio Signals
Abstract: Chord recognition is a computationally demanding and time-consuming procedure that demands music-theoretical expertise. This science includes a variety of potential applications that can be used in the multidisciplinary field of Music Information Retrieval. Every chord recognition system starts with the use of an audio signal as an input to generate output chord sequences. Due to the complexity of the signal structure, musical instruments when played simultaneously can easily introduce ambiguities that will affect predictions. In this work, we propose an approach that will address the instrument dependency of chord recognizers using lossless-to-lossy transcoding. This approach aims to achieve correct chord predictions regardless of the instrument used in the homophonic audio signals and to prove that chord signals can be profiled using their frequency signature without any additional overhead in the computing requirements. The proposed method employs an algorithm based on ensemble-based learning. This approach uses a chord recognizer that was trained using plain chord recordings from different instruments and was evaluated on actual music recordings with vocals and mixed instrument signals. The proposed approach was able to achieve significant performance improvements in the test dataset outperforming its deep-learning counterparts. This proves that chord signals can be profiled without introducing additional computing resources in the process.

Title: A Data-Driven Signal Subspace Approach for Indoor Bluetooth Ranging
Abstract: Bluetooth ranging relies on two-way multicarrier phase difference (MCPD) channel frequency response measurements to mitigate time and phase offsets. However, the challenge of doubled multipath components under the two-way MCPD approach, especially with a low number of snapshots, further degrades the performance of the commonly utilized multiple signal classification (MUSIC) algorithm. In this article, we investigate a reduced complexity signal-subspace-based approach for wireless ranging using bluetooth low energy (BLE) in high multipath environments. We propose a novel signal subspace decomposition (SSD) algorithm where we utilize the span of individual signal subspace eigenvectors for range estimation. We formulate the integration of the Fourier transform and randomized low rank approximation into the SSD algorithm to reduce the computational complexity for better utilization in embedded devices. We then make use of the output features from the estimated pseudospectrum of the individual eigenvectors, obtained from the enhanced SSD algorithm, as an input to the long-short-term-memory (LSTM) recurrent neural network to obtain a data-driven SSD-LSTM wireless range estimator for the BLE. We evaluate our proposed approach using our real-world BLE data for single- and multiple-antenna scenarios. Our results show an improved performance of our proposed approach by more than 37%, while still enjoying the lowest computational complexity than existing MUSIC and support vector regression approaches for BLE ranging.

Title: Creative Artificial Intelligence for Music Theatre: AI mediation and artificial–human co-creativity in contemporary science-fiction opera
Abstract: Humanity has long expressed itself through the arts, yet the recent surge of artificial intelligence (AI) has sparked debate about its impact on human expression and connection. Situated at the nexus of concerns, hype and aspiration surrounding AI’s cultural implications, this article explores the evolving dynamics of artificial–human co-creativity in contemporary ‘science-fiction opera’, a sub-genre that adapts sci-fi narratives or integrates speculative technologies into live operatic performance. Although generative AI is increasingly reshaping artistic production across media, opera remains a unique domain where embodied expression and social interconnection take precedence. Drawing on Richard Grusin’s concept of ‘radical mediation’, this study examines how AI recalibrates processes of perception, affect and cognition within performance ecosystems of human and non-human agents. It addresses one central question: how does the complex mediation process in sci-fi opera contribute to humanizing technology, attuning artistic and design innovations to human experiences and cultural values? Focusing on two recent Swedish productions, The Tale of the Great Computing Machine and The Oracle, this article shows how technical and artistic media coalesce to create immersive, emotionally resonant experiences. These case studies illustrate varying degrees and various modalities of AI integration: interactive instrument design and robotic choreography in the former, generative text shaping real-time vocal performance in the latter. In both, AI functions as an active agent that mediates the real-time feedback loop of human performative expression. Positioned in wider debates on opera’s convergence with new media art, this article offers two key contributions to computational creativity, applied AI and performance studies. First, it illuminates how AI is transforming the contemporary performing arts landscape, highlighting its potential opportunities for future musical–theatrical practice. Second, it exemplifies how humanistic research, particularly music performance studies, can generate new knowledge about the creative dimensions of AI. This together ensures that embedding technology in the arts enables us to reimagine creativity and the ethics of creative work in today’s increasingly AI-led digital cultures.

Title: Improving Vocal Communication on Construction Sites Using a Fourier-CNN Hybrid Denoising Approach
Abstract: Construction noise is a major constraint affecting workers’ performance and communication. Voice messages at construction sites are always polluted by noise and difficult to interpret. Denoising algorithms and corresponding built-in hardware can potentially ease the problems, while the existing denoising algorithms, especially deep learning ones, rely mainly on data sources and following training performance. The current denoising models primarily focus on artificial noise scenarios. There is a lack of noise data sets and attempts to train models that specifically address the impact of noise on communication among construction workers. Additionally, it is worth noting that existing deep learning noise reduction techniques are mainly processing data in audio forms, while the effectiveness of deep learning methods in image-related tasks should not be overlooked. This study proposes a hybrid approach consisting of a Fourier-related transformation and convolution network to filter noisy voice audio as an image denoiser. The results demonstrate that the proposed approach effectively produces clearer audio with improvements in Root Mean Square Error, Signal-to-Noise Ratio, and Spectral Subtraction Ratio, which can enhance the comprehension of voice messages at sites.

Title: Life-cycle and operability of particle accelerators
Abstract: Particle accelerators are used to generate particle beams for different kinds of use. Operability must be easy and simple for an industrial version with a high Technological Readiness Level (TRL), or complex and critical for large single accelerators designed for new research objectives. Our present text mainly focuses on this second type of specific machines and facilities. Beyond associated physics and technologies considerations, they are systems and facilities to be designed, constructed, and used for the expected purposes. The particle accelerators devoted to research have generally a long life (> 20 years) and history shows that their lifecycles are unique, and generally neither smooth nor easy. Many good practices in project management and operation of particles accelerators can be found in the existing fields of building construction, or complex industrial systems (aeronautic, military) or other large scientific instruments (e.g. satellite). But they have their particularities: the specificities of the expected output (the particle beam, a complex multi-parametric physical object), the technologies (ion sources, RF, vacuum, etc.), the specific risks (direct or remnant radiations, electricity, etc.), the high expectation for performances or innovation, the usual associated international community. In the first section, we will describe the different classic stages of the lifecycle of a particle accelerator, in the second section we will focus on the operations stage with details on the reliability. In the third section, we will evoke some of the current trends: artificial intelligence, sustainability, and major cost of energy.

Title: DIGITAL TEACHING COMPETENCIES IN SABANA DE OCCIDENTE: THE INFLUENCE OF THE UNESCO FRAMEWORK ON DIGITAL EDUCATIONAL PRACTICE

Nevertheless, gaps remain, especially those linked to access and technological infrastructure in rural contexts. In conclusion, it is necessary to strengthen continuous and contextualised training, ensuring digital equity and pedagogical sustainability.

Our experiments begin by refining the Mamba network to handle both preceding and succeeding time series data for speech enhancement, specifically focusing on noise reduction. Title: Exploiting Legal Event Detection Based on the BERT and Graph Convolutional Network
Abstract: In a vast amount of legal documents and written judgement, there existing numerous dynamic processes of crime events, which serve as the basis for judges to understand the case and make the fair legal judgments. Therefore, it is very important for courts or the other judicial organs to extract events from a large number of legal texts using automated methods. With the development of deep learning, many scholars have proposed numerous legal event detection models based on deep learning technologies. However, these methods typically first only utilize the semantic information of context which mainly uses BERT to output their representations, and then detect the legal event trigger in the form of sequence labeling, whereas their efforts ignore the overfitting issues inherent in BERT itself, which leads to performance bottlenecks in the designing event detection models. To address the above issues, this paper designs a legal event detection method based on Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN) which can achieve the re-examining of attention weights. Specifically, this method can first construct a fully connected adjacency matrix acquired from the multi-head attention weights of each transformer layer in BERT, and then aggregate the contextual token nodes based on the edge weights inside the adjacency matrix, and finally achieve the re-examination of the BERT attention weights. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed model, some evaluated experiments are conducted on the large-scale Chinese legal event detection dataset LEVEN. The final experimental results demonstrate that compared to traditional BERT-based methods, the proposed GCN-based method achieves better performance in the legal event detection task.

Title: Enhancing the Audio MNIST Classification Process Through the Extraction of Temporal Features Through the Application of 1D-CNN and Attention Mechanisms
Abstract: The primary goal of this work is to improve Audio MNIST spoken digit categorization. Attention approaches extract and highlight temporal information in audio streams using 1D convolutional neural networks (1D-CNNs). This work processes raw audio waveforms directly, unlike many current algorithms that use 2D representations like Mel Spectrograms or other frequency-domain characteristics for audio classification, especially speech detection. We can better record voice dynamics with higher temporal resolution input features. This method improves voice sequential pattern learning and temporal continuity by employing 1D-CNNs to analyze raw time-domain input. Attention mechanisms allow the model to focus on specific audio signal locations. This attention-based architecture lets the network dynamically select the most informative waveform sections, enhancing the model's capacity to discriminate spoken numbers and voice characteristics. The suggested method can be tested using the Audio MNIST dataset, which contains thirty thousand recordings of spoken numbers from zero to nine from sixty speakers. The proposed 1D-CNN with attention mechanisms is extensively tested against baseline models like typical CNNs trained on spectrograms and CNNs based on raw waveforms without attention. Under noisy or demanding settings when minor temporal factors are crucial for differentiation, classification accuracy improves significantly. The model's performance is tested by employing self-attention and temporal attention layers. These tactics improve model interpretability and generalization to speakers with different accents and languages by emphasizing key input signal elements. This hybrid approach uses 1D-CNNs with attention mechanisms to efficiently extract the temporal features from the audio input. Example tasks include spoken digit recognition, speaker identification, and speech pattern analysis. All signs support this. Title: Comparative Study of KNN Over CNN for Music Genre Classification to Improve Accuracy
Abstract: In the study of music genre recognition, a comparison was made between K-Nearest Neighbors and Convolutional Neural Networks to determine which method provides better classification accuracy. The analysis was conducted using ten iterations for each algorithm, with the dataset split into 70% for training and 30% for testing. The results revealed that K-Nearest Neighbors achieved a remarkable accuracy of 95.3%, significantly outperforming CNN, which had an accuracy of 90.49%. The statistical significance of these results was confirmed with a p-value of 0.01, indicating that the observed difference in performance is statistically significant (p<0.05). This study clearly demonstrates that K-Nearest Neighbors is more effective for music genre classification compared to CNN. The KNN algorithm not only provided higher accuracy but also proved to be a more reliable method for identifying different types of music genres. This suggests that for tasks involving genre recognition, K-Nearest Neighbors may offer a more precise and dependable solution than CNN.

Title: ‘Waiting for the Barbarians’: constructing the visible invisibility of Australia’s ‘boat people’
Abstract: The image of the barbarian at the border has long captured the imagination of ‘civilized’ communities. Drawing on C P Cavafy’s 1904 poem, Waiting for the Barbarians, and J M Coetzee’s 1980 novel of the same name, this article explores the Australian polity’s responses to the arrival of ‘boat people’, who embody the ‘barbarian Other’ in the Australian psyche. Examining the response to unauthorised boat arrivals on Australian Federal Election day in 2022, it situates those events as part of Australia’s performance of Waiting for the Barbarians. It then examines how ‘visible invisibility’ of ‘boat people’ is constructed visually, juridically and geographically. It considers how the cultivation of fear, hostility, and forgetting enable the visible invisibility so constructed. Finally, it turns to the possibilities of resistance to the construction and devastating human effects of visible invisibility. To do this, it looks to those who are ‘visibly invisible’ for inspiration, exploring how documentary, literature, art, music, and artificial intelligence can be harnessed as powerful forms of non-violent resistance. As Cavafy and Coetzee do, the article serves as a reminder that the barbarian is within us as it ponders the possibility of ‘boat people’ offering ‘us’ a different kind of solution.

Title: Evaluation of Machine Learning Methods for Pancreatic Cancer Detection Using CT Scans
Abstract: The application of machine learning algorithms in medical image processing has emerged as a possible means of achieving this goal. Early identification of pancreatic cancer is essential for enhancing patient outcomes. In this study, we studied how to identify pancreatic cancer utilising CT scan images using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN), Support Vector Machines (SVM), and Random Forest (RF). To thoroughly test these algorithms, a dataset of 2000 CT scan images was meticulously divided into training and testing subsets. With an accuracy rate of 94.34%, the CNN model performed remarkably well, establishing a new standard for accuracy in the diagnosis of pancreatic cancer. In addition to exhibiting outstanding accuracy rates above 88%, KNN, SVM, and RF also shown their potential as therapeutic instruments. Furthermore, we thoroughly evaluated the prediction skills of the models using performance metrics like precision, recall, F1 score, and accuracy. This study promises prompt intervention and better patient outcomes, which is a significant advance in the early diagnosis of pancreatic cancer. These findings inspire further investigation and innovation in the area of medical image processing in addition to highlighting the transformational potential of machine learning in medical diagnostics.

Title: An Efficient Arthritis Diagnostic Model using CoAtNet by Integrating Convolutional and Attention Mechanisms for Enhanced Precision
Abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a common joint disease that lowers quality of life and causes damage worldwide. It is more common in elderly people, with knee OA being the most common type. While traditional machine learning and deep learning methods have validated potential in OA identification, they normally struggle to balance spatial feature abstraction and interpretability. Interestingly, the effective combination of convolutional and attention mechanisms to enhance diagnosis accuracy, specifically in OA severity categorization, remains unexplored. Our goal is to minimize this performance discrepancy by developing an efficient diagnostic model for knee OA utilizing CoAtNet. This hybrid architecture combines the advantages of attention mechanisms with convolutional layers for optimal performance. The Kaggle knee osteoarthritis dataset was used to train and assess the model thoroughly. To ensure robustness, key preprocessing methods such as image normalization and data augmentation were used. Experimental results show that the suggested CoAtNet-based model obtains 9 6 % accuracy, 88% F1 scores, and 87% precision, culminating in an astounding Top 1 accuracy of 9 6 %. In addition to providing a more precise means of diagnosing OA, this model offers a scalable instrument that may be easily included in clinical processes. Using this method could improve knee OA early identification and treatment planning, which would improve patient results and boost overall healthcare proficiency.

Title: Effective Visualization of Individual Piano Performance Style Preferences Using Tempo and Dynamics Features with AIME
Abstract: In appreciating piano performances, listeners often develop preferences for specific performance styles even for the same musical piece. This study proposes and validates a method for visualizing individual preferences in professional piano performances. By analyzing performance features, such as tempo and its first and second derivatives, and dynamics and its first and second derivatives, this method generates visual representations of preferred stylistic traits. Furthermore, by leveraging the Approximate Inverse Model Explanation (AIME) method from Explainable AI (XAI), the method extracts comprehensive preference features for each listener across multiple pieces. The key strength of this method is its ability to articulate a listener's preferred performance style in concrete terms. This empowers individuals to incorporate these elements into their play, thereby facilitating self-improvement. This also facilitates connections between individuals with shared stylistic preferences, fostering a deeper appreciation for musical nuances. This study presents a practical tool with the potential to translate abstract musical preferences into concrete, understandable, and actionable insights, thereby enhancing the experience of both performers and listeners.

Title: Experimental Study on Speech Synthesis Using Advanced Neural Network Models

The experimental setup considers the following TTS models: Tacotron2 and Fastspeech2 acoustic models, both of which are used with MelGAN and Multiband MelGAN vocoders. The parameters' models are trained and tuned on the English LJSpeech dataset. Performance metrics used are WER objective and MOS subjective metrics. The mean opinion score (MOS) as subjective metrics is based on naturalness and intelligibility measures. Title: Multi-Modal Fusion With Machine Learning Integrated Approach for the Investigation of Honey Adulteration
Abstract: In this study, the efficacy of multi-modal data fusion in detecting honey adulteration using spectral data from FT-NIR, FT-MIR, and CRM sensors was explored. Feature-level fusion was implemented to develop two distinct scenarios for assessing the performance of three one-class classifiers: OC-SVM, LOF, and Isolation Forests. Notably, the OC-SVM classifier demonstrated superior performance in scenarios where data from multiple spectral instruments were integrated, achieving high recall rates and effectively reducing false positives. The high performance indicates the potential of the use of non-invasive spectral techniques in honey adulteration.

Title: Exploring Cloud Computing for Real-Time Analysis and Storage of Data Generated by Medical Devices
Abstract: Real-time analysis and storage of data measured by native medical instruments, including insulin pump, pacemaker, and wearable monitor, is crucial for the advancement of modern healthcare and that has made cloud computing vital. These devices produce real-time data that has to be analyzed to make timely interventions in the projects. This work discusses the execution of these devices by using cloud- based systems such as AWS and Google Cloud for dealing with the data produced by such devices. Since cloud is inherently scalable and computational, real-time monitoring and analytical capabilities is possible, potentially beneficial in diabetes and arrhythmias. The implementation of Random Forest model together with LSTM models improved the accuracy in diseases diagnosis and patient tracking. Various strategies to tackle the scarcity issue of the real-time data include data augmentation techniques which acted as a powerful strategy used to enhance the performance of the models. The results indicated excellent fitness in outcome anticipation while the evaluation time in the cloud platforms was remarkably low. For patient monitoring, another web-based dashboard was also designed to show information about patient health to allow healthcare professionals monitor their patients from a distance. Title: Dynamic Financial Time Series Modeling with Rapid Adaptation via Meta Learning
Abstract: The Meta learning framework for financial time series forecasting is proposed here, which can adapt to new financial market datasets efficiently with minimal retraining. This methodology includes two phases: the first one is cross-financial time series training on a meta-model and the second adapts this meta-model using recent data to novel market conditions. Title: Surgical Tools Detection and Localization using YOLO Models for Minimization of Retained Surgical Items
Abstract: Accurate identification and localization of surgical instruments during procedures are essential for minimizing the risk of retained surgical items. Such retained items result in serious and preventable health complications for patients. This paper investigates the application of YOLO (You Only Look Once) deep learning models for the real-time detection and localization of surgical instruments, aiming to minimize the occurrence of retained surgical items (RSIs) during surgical procedures. The methodology involves a comparative analysis of YOLO versions, including YOLOv5, YOLOv8, and YOLOv10, to evaluate their performance in detecting and classifying surgical tools. The models were trained on a specialized dataset that included diverse surgical scenarios, ensuring a comprehensive assessment of their capabilities. Key performance metrics such as precision, recall, and F1 score were utilized to quantify the effectiveness of each model, with results indicating high performance across the board, particularly in distinguishing between various surgical instruments. The findings demonstrate that YOLO models, particularly the latest versions, possess significant potential for Integration into surgical environments, enhancing the tracking and monitoring of surgical tools. The study concludes that implementing these models could improve patient safety by reducing the risk of RSIs, thereby contributing to the advancement of automated systems in healthcare.

Title: Intelligent Systems for Chronic Disease Management: Integrating IOT and AI for Enhanced Delivery of Healthcare
Abstract: The latest advancements like Artificial Intelligence (AI), the Internet of Things (IoT), and cloud computing have transformed healthcare from conventional to intelligent in order to enhance medical care. Additionally, the Isolation Forest (iForest) approach is utilized to eliminate outliers in this approach. CSO improves CLSTM method diagnostics significantly. CSO-LSTM model performance was validated using information related to healthcare. In experiments, the CSO-LSTM model achieved the highest accuracies of 97.02% and 97.7% in identifying diabetes and heart disease. Title: Audio Sentiment Detection using a Hybrid Analysis Model
Abstract: Analyzing customer sentiment calls is crucial for organizations to monitor customer satisfaction, identify pain points, and improve service quality. Each of the models is assessed according to metrics for accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. High accuracies of 86.58% for TF-IDF+Naive Bayes, 84.90% for Naive Bayes, 84.42% for CNN+SVM, and 67% for CNN+LSTM are shown in the results, demonstrating the usefulness of the suggested methodology for sentiment prediction tasks.By providing insightful information for applications in domains including opinion mining, social media monitoring, and customer feedback analysis, this research advances sentiment analysis techniques on audio inputs. Future developments in the fields of sentiment analysis and audio processing are outlined, along with additional improvements and expansions of the suggested methodology.

Title: An Attention Based CNN-LSTM Hybrid Approach for Music Genre Classification
Abstract: This research designs and implementation of a music genre classification system that leverages an innovative hybrid approach combining Convolutional Neural Networks, Long Short-Term Memory networks, and an attention mechanism. Title: Comparative Analysis of Gaussian Naïve Bayes with Bernoulli Naïve Bayes for Guitar Chord Classification
Abstract: Naïve Bayes Algorithm is extensively used in machine learning for classification problems. Guitar chord classification is a trivial problem in music recognition where Naïve bayes algorithm is exploited. To further investigate the performance of Naïve bayes, its types can be experimented. Guitar chord classification problem has been explored and experimented in more than one dimension for music recognition and recommendation models. The preprocessing of guitar chords audio into numerical data is computationally extensive. In order to test the performance of variants of Naïve Bayes Algorithm we have considered the harmonics generated during the preprocessing and data transformation stage and analyzed the effect of higher order harmonics. In this paper we have evaluated and compared two versions of Naïve bayes algorithm for guitar chord classification problem for two sets of harmonics count. Gaussian Naïve bayes is compared with Bernoulli's Naïve bayes for datasets of guitar chords with harmonics count from 4th harmonic to 9th harmonic. This paper has interesting findings that at lower harmonic counts Gaussian Naïve bayes performs better and if the feature count of harmonics is higher, in that case Bernoulli's Naïve bayes exhibits better performance. Title: Exploring Receptance Weighted Key Value Model for Single-Channel Speech Enhancement
Abstract: Speech enhancement has significantly benefited from advancements in deep learning, particularly in terms of intelligibility and perceptual quality. Traditional time-frequency (TF) domain methods rely on convolutional neural networks (CNNs) or recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to predict TF masks or speech spectra. In this study, we introduce a novel network architecture, the Receptance Weighted Key Value (RWKV) model integrated with the Deep Complex Convolution Recurrent Network (DC-CRN), aimed at effectively training complex targets. This model combines the strengths of RNNs and Transformers, redefining the attention mechanism for speech enhancement tasks to avoid the exponential growth in computational complexity typically associated with traditional Transformer models. Through a series of experiments on the VoiceBank+Demand dataset, the RWKV-DCCRN model has demonstrated superior performance, efficiency, and scalability in handling long-range dependencies compared to traditional DCCRN models. Title: Effective features to define harmonic distance models
Abstract: Tonal Pitch Space (TPS) has been proposed as a harmonic distance model, which provides a way to compute numerical distances between two chords with keys. Although the theory itself seems sound, it still contains arbitrary presuppositions in its definition, and its adequacy has not well been investigated. In this study, we propose a framework in which we construct, train, and evaluate a variety of distance functions that share the same domain and range as TPS. We define three basic harmonic features (mode, tonic, and degree), and utilise these to define various distance functions by combining them, and then we evaluate all simple combinations exhaustively. We then train and evaluate each function through the task of key estimation. This entire process is to provide a perspective from which to examine how well various features and their combinations can represent harmony through our distance models. Experiments confirmed that some aspects of the TPS are indeed well designed, but also showed that its performance can be surpassed with a considerably smaller number of parameters.

Title: Stacked-KBR: An Ensemble Method for Analyzing YouTube Bangla Song Reviews Using a Novel Dataset

The prime goal of this investigation is to employ various machine learning algorithms to precisely recognize the sentiments expressed in Bangla song reviews and apply explainable AI to provide explanations. Title: Comprehensive Lung Disease Detection Using Deep Learning Models and Hybrid Chest X-ray Data with Explainable AI
Abstract: Advanced diagnostic instruments are crucial for the accurate detection and treatment of lung diseases, which affect millions of individuals globally. This study examines the effectiveness of deep learning and transfer learning models using a hybrid dataset, created by merging four individual datasets from Bangladesh and global sources. The hybrid dataset significantly enhances model accuracy and generalizability, particularly in detecting COVID-19, pneumonia, lung opacity and normal lung conditions from chest X-ray images. A range of models, including CNN, VGG16, VGG19, InceptionV3, Xception, ResNet50V2, InceptionResNetV2, MobileNetV2 and DenseNet121 are applied to both individual and hybrid dataset. The results show superior performance on the hybrid dataset, with VGG16, Xception, ResNet50V2 and DenseNet121 each achieving an accuracy, precision, recall and f1-score of 99%. This consistent performance across the hybrid dataset highlights the robustness of these models in handling diverse data while maintaining high accuracy. To understand the models implicit behavior, explainable AI techniques are employed to illuminate their black-box nature. Specifically, LIME is used to enhance the interpretability of model predictions, especially in cases of misclassification, contributing to the development of reliable and interpretable AI-driven solutions for medical imaging.

Title: An Error Correction Model for Piano Teaching Based on Improved Endpoint Detection with CNN-HMM
Abstract: Piano teaching is based on teaching performance skills, which is an important practical discipline for interactive and personalized teaching. In order to realize the automation and digital teaching of piano, and to improve the level of piano performance and aesthetic effect, the research firstly uses the endpoint detection technology to realize the temporal value detection of the audio data, and then integrates the convolutional neural network and the Hidden Markov Model for the extraction and recognition of the note events, and finally completes the transcription of the piano audio and the correction of the errors. The experimental results show that the research-designed method outperforms the baseline model in terms of F1 value and receiver operating characteristic curve, with the highest convergence of F1 value at 88.47% and the maximum curve area at 0.906, which makes the model classify better. The method has the smallest average error on different datasets, the average absolute value error is lower than 0.25, the root mean square error is lower than 0.20, and the classification accuracy of note events is superior. In practical use, the research-designed method has a greater advantage in recognition accuracy and error correction accuracy compared with the manual method, which significantly improves the overall accuracy of piano error correction and is conducive to the development of piano teaching. The research-designed piano teaching aid error correction method is conducive to improving the efficiency and quality of piano teaching, and provides an effective reference for the application of artificial intelligence in the field of music education.

Title: Exploring Dimensionality Reduction Techniques in Word Classification using Surface EMG Signals
Abstract: Surface Electromyography (sEMG) is a revolutionary technology in the field of unvoiced speech recognition that captures and analyzes electric signals produced by facial muscles during speech. Despite the significance of providing an interface for recognizing and synthesizing spoken words, research in this area does not investigate and compare the impact of dimensionality reduction techniques to reduce complexity. This study aims to develop a frame-based word classification system incorporating dimensionality reduction techniques using surface EMG speech signals. To attain this objective, several ML models including Decision tree, KNN, Random Forest, XGB, and Bidirectional LSTM are developed as classifiers integrating the dimensionality reduction algorithms Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) and Principal Component Analysis (PCA). The study found that the Random Forest classifier along with LDA performed remarkably in the experiment yielding an accuracy of 96.28%. Again, the XGB classifier showed an impressive classification accuracy of 93.45% with PCA. However, both KNN and DT performed poorly across both dimensionality reduction techniques, and the neural network (BLSTM) showed around 85% accuracy with both LDA and PCA. This research provides important insights into the application and effectiveness of dimensionality reduction techniques in improving the performance of different machine learning models for sEMG-based unvoiced speech recognition.

Title: AI Meets Agriculture: Advanced Rice Yield Forecasting Based on Historical Data using Machine Learning Approaches
Abstract: Despite the global importance of agriculture, inefficient practices persist, particularly in poorer regions. A big obstacle to increasing agricultural outputs is the inefficiency of conventional methods and the absence of accurate instruments for predicting crop yields. While various machine learning techniques have been used by several researchers to forecast yields, the difficulty lies in developing models that adequately account for regional nuances. To overcome this problem, this study proposed a novel machine learning-based approach for crop yield prediction focused on the Sylhet region, Bangladesh with a large unique dataset named "EcoRiceDynamics (1971-2021)."Four models - Linear Regression, Random Forest, Gradient Boosted, and K-Nearest Neighbors are evaluated to improve forecast precision. Performance was measured using the R<sup>2</sup> value and error reduction metrics. Our results show that the Gradient Boosted model achieved the highest R<sup>2</sup> value of 95% and MAE 6.71%, indicating its superior fit to the dataset. However, the Random Forest model excelled in minimizing prediction errors by 6.37% with R<sup>2</sup> value of 94.1%. Random Forest reduces prediction errors effectively, while Gradient Boosted explains variance better. Incorporating these models into agricultural systems could enhance decision-making and crop yields in regions like Sylhet. This study highlights the potential of machine learning in advancing agricultural sustainability on yield estimation.

Title: A Review of Audio Classification Techniques
Abstract: Audio classification is a rapidly advancing field, driven by the increasing demand for intelligent audio processing systems in various applications such as speech recognition, environmental sound classification and music genre detection. This survey paper provides a comprehensive overview of audio classification techniques, focusing on machine learning methods, Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and hybrid models. Traditional techniques including k-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN), Support Vector Machines (SVM) are reviewed for their foundational contributions. RNNs with their temporal sequence modeling capabilities are explored for applications where time dependencies are critical. CNNs widely used for their effectiveness in learning spatial hierarchies are highlighted for their transformative role in audio classification. Additionally, hybrid models that combine the strengths of multiple architectures such as CNN-RNN and CNN-SVM, are discussed for their ability to capture both spatial and temporal features. The survey critically examines the strengths and limitations of each approach, compares their performance on various datasets and outlines current challenges and future directions in the field.

Title: Leveraging CNNs for Efficient Classification of Apple Leaf Diseases
Abstract: This study investigates the use of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to classify apple plant diseases based on photographs of their leaves. The study makes use of a dataset of tagged photos of apple leaves, which includes both healthy and diseased leaves from conditions including cedar apple rot and apple scab. Data collection, preprocessing, CNN model architecture creation, and training are all part of the methodology. Several CNN architectures are taken into consideration, including VGG, ResNet, and Inception. The model is trained on a split dataset and its performance is monitored on a validation set to prevent overfitting. Evaluation measures include F1-score, recall, accuracy, and precision. Findings show that CNNs are good at correctly identifying apple leaf diseases. The study emphasizes how this strategy may be used in apple farming for early disease identification and well-informed decision-making. Suggestions for future research include integrating numerous imaging modalities, real-time field classification, and multi-class categorization for various illness types. This study advances the creation of cutting-edge instruments for managing diseases in apple cultivation, which could enhance crop yields and health.

Title: Various Signal Transformation for Optimizing CNN Model Performance of Earthquake Detection
Abstract: Given the frequency of earthquakes in Indonesia, it is crucial to accurately identify them in order to prevent unnecessary alarms over their mitigation. In the context of earthquake detection and classification, the development of artificial intelligence is ongoing to achieve a dependable system. The objective of this work is to compare the signal transformations as a preprocessing step in order to achieve optimal performance outcomes for the deep learning model in detecting seismic signals. The signal transformations used in this study are Fourier, wavelet, Hilbert, and probability of power spectral density (PPSD) methods to obtain a visual representation of the signal spectrum. The unprocessed data obtained from the Indonesia Tsunami Early Warning System (InaTEWS) server underwent a classification process including three distinct categories: earthquake, background noise, and instrument noise. Seismic signal identification is performed by utilizing the signal spectrum obtained from preprocessing the raw data on the optimized convolutional neural network (CNN) model. The assessment revealed that PPSD represents the optimal signal transformation approach, achieving a peak accuracy of 97.2% under RMSprop optimization, whereas Adam optimization exhibits slightly superior precision and F1 scores of 97.3 % and 97.2 %, respectively. It is believed that these favorable results will improve the dependability of the earthquake detection system based on artificial intelligence, therefore minimizing the occurrence of detection errors that may result in public widespread panic and chaos.

Title: Research on Voice Humming to Guzheng Audio Transcription and Pitch-Lowering Processing Based on Genetic Algorithm and YIN Algorithm
Abstract: In recent years, AI-based music generation and transformation technologies have received widespread attention. This study presents an automated system for transcribing vocal humming audio into Guzheng audio, integrating the YIN algorithm and genetic algorithm, and optimizing pitch and timbre matching through pitch-lowering processing. First, the YIN algorithm is used to extract the fundamental frequency of the humming audio, and then the genetic algorithm optimizes the frequency sequence to better align with the Guzheng's pitch range. To further improve the audio generation quality, the system introduces pitch-lowering processing, adjusting the generated audio frequencies to fit within the Guzheng's pitch range. Experimental results show that pitch-lowering processing significantly enhances the accuracy of the pitch and timbre matching. Moreover, the genetic algorithm outperforms the YIN algorithm in optimizing pitch and timbre, with the generated audio exhibiting a more realistic Guzheng timbre. Ultimately, the system achieves significant improvements in pitch, timbre, and auditory effects. The proposed transcription scheme demonstrates good applicability in musical applications involving pitch range conversion and provides new research insights for automated instrument transcription.

Title: Classifying musical reading expertise by eye-movement analysis using machine learning
Abstract: Music reading is the key to literacy for musicians in the Western music tradition. This high-level activity requires an efficient extraction of the visual information from the score to the current needs of the execution. Differences in eye movements between expert and non-expert musicians during music reading have been shown. The present study goes further, using a machine learning approach to classify musicians according to their level of expertise in analyzing their eye movements and performance during sight-reading. We used a support vector machine (SVM) technique to (a) investigate whether the underlying expertise in musical reading could be reliably inferred from eye movements, performance, and subjective measures collected across five levels of expertise and (b) determine the best predictors for classifying expertise from 24 visual measures (e.g., the number of progressive fixations, the number of regressive fixations, pupil size, first-pass fixations, and second-pass fixations), 10 performance measures (e.g., eye–hand span, velocity, latency, play duration, tempo, and false notes), and 4 subjective measures (perceived complexity and cognitive skills). Eye movements from 68 pianists at five different levels of music expertise (according to their level in the conservatory of music—from first cycle to professional) were co-registered with their piano performance via a Musical Instrument Digital Interface, while they sight-read classical and contemporary music scores. Results revealed relevant classifications based on the SVM analysis. The model optimally classified the lower levels of expertise (1 and 2) compared to the higher levels (3, 4, and 5) and the medium level (3) compared to higher levels (4 and 5). Furthermore, across a total of 38 measures, the model identified the four best predictors of the level of expertise: the sum of fixations by note, the number of blinks, the number of fixations, and the average fixation duration. Thus, efficiently classifying musical reading expertise from musicians' eye movements and performance using SVM is possible. The results have important theoretical and practical implications for music cognition and pedagogy, enhancing the specialized eye and performance behaviors required for an expert music reading.

Title: Professionals’ Perspectives of Smart Stationary Bikes in Rehabilitation: Qualitative Study
Abstract: Background: Stationary bikes are used in numerous rehabilitation settings, with most offering limited functionalities and types of training. Smart technologies, such as artificial intelligence and robotics, bring new possibilities to achieve rehabilitation goals. However, it is important that these technologies meet the needs of users in order to improve their adoption in current practice. Objective: This study aimed to collect professionals’ perspectives on the use of smart stationary bikes in rehabilitation. Methods: Twelve health professionals (age: mean 43.4, SD 10.1 years) completed an online questionnaire and participated in a semistructured interview regarding their needs and expectations before and after a 30-minute session with a smart bike prototype. Results: A content analysis was performed with inductive coding. Seven main themes emerged: (1) bike functionalities (cycling assistance, asymmetric resistance, and forward and backward cycling), (2) interface between bike and users (simple, user-friendly, personalized, with written reminders during training), (3) feedback to users (user and performance data), (4) training programs (preprogrammed and personalized, and algorithmic programs), (5) user engagement (telerehabilitation, group sessions, music, and automatic suggestion of training), (6) the bike as a physical device (dimensions, comfort, setup, screen, etc), and (7) business model (various pricing strategies, training for professionals, and after-sales service). Conclusions: This study provides an interpretive understanding of professionals’ perspectives regarding smart stationary bikes and is the first to identify the expectations of health professionals regarding the development of future bikes in rehabilitation.

Title: Development of an Automatic Musical Keys Notes Detection Technique Using Mir Toolbox
Abstract: Musical key recognition has traditionally been a difficult endeavor for humans, especially for people who lack adequate musical training. The musical key detection problem was transformed into a form of comparison of the audio waveforms and other musical features of the audio sample in this research, as a significant approach to solve the problem of music transcription. The MIR toolbox database which has recordings and Musical Instrument Digital Interface (MIDI) files of isolated piano and guitar sounds, was used to collect the training and testing data.The model's accuracy level was assessed using a confusion matrix as a performance indicator, and it turned out that the model has a 68% precision and 69% sensitivity, which shows a relatively high accuracy. Title: The Comparison of Different Deep Learning Models for Chinese Musical Instrument Recognition
Abstract: Instrument recognition plays a crucial role in various domains such as music, education, artificial intelligence, and cultural preservation. While deep learning technologies have achieved significant success in the recognition of Western musical instruments, their application to Chinese musical instruments remains relatively unexplored. To bridge this gap, this study investigates the use of deep learning techniques for the recognition of traditional Chinese instruments. Four deep learning models - RNN, ResNetSE, TDNN, and ECAPA-TDNN - were chosen as experimental models for the task. A diverse dataset consisting of 37 traditional Chinese instruments, including the Erhu, Pipa, Guzheng, and Dizi, was created. The dataset incorporates different tones, timbres, and playing speeds, ensuring a comprehensive representation of Chinese musical instruments. For feature extraction, Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCC) and spectrograms were employed to capture significant audio features from the instrument sounds. The Chinese instrument recognition system processes the audio through three stages: preprocessing, feature extraction, and deep learning-based classification. The study further compares the performance of MFCC and spectrograms in terms of recognition accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that MFCC provides superior feature extraction results. Among the models using MFCC features, ECAPA-TDNN achieved the highest accuracy at 97.18%, followed by TDNN at 96.02%, ResNetSE at 95.01%, and RNN at 92.59%. These findings suggest that the TDNN-based neural networks are particularly effective for recognizing Chinese instruments.

Abstract: With the continuous improvement of the power grid lean management requirements, the existing smart turnover cabinet has limitations in the degree of automation, failure rate, etc., and has been unable to meet the needs of the full life cycle management of electric energy measuring instruments. For this reason, this paper designs and realizes a smart electric energy measuring apparatus full life cycle management system based on AI image recognition. First, the system adopts a model architecture combining ResNet and EfficientNet, using the deep network robustness of ResNet and the efficient deployment capability of EfficientNet to ensure the accuracy and real-time performance of the system in complex tasks; second, combining with the attention mechanism to optimize the extraction capability of key features, the system designs a customized classification layer to meet the demand of electric energy measuring instruments for multi-category recognition; finally, this paper designs and implements an intelligent electric energy measuring instruments life cycle management system based on AI image recognition. Finally, the system enhances the adaptability to low-light, reflective and other complex scenes through the image preprocessing module. The system realizes the functions of automatic storage and retrieval, real-time monitoring and early warning of measuring instruments, effectively improves the lean level of the whole life cycle management of measuring assets, and provides important support for promoting the modernization of the management of intelligent electric energy measuring instruments.

Title: SHAP-1DCNN Based Detection of Analogue Operational Amplifiers
Abstract: In the face of highly integrated and complex integrated circuits, traditional IC testing often relies on complex test designs and specialised test instruments, making it difficult to balance testing costs and efficiency. Deep learning algorithms can automatically learn and extract complex features from data, which can be adapted to various types of IC testing and help to realise the intelligence of the testing process. In this thesis, a SHAP-1DCNN based analogue operational amplifier testing technique (title) is proposed based on the actual test data of analogue integrated operational amplifiers (OPAs) using the SHAP-1DCNN deep learning algorithm.Firstly, the traditional CNN deep learning algorithm model is improved using SHAP analysis, and secondly, the general analogue integrated operational amplifier chip test circuit is drawn, and the precision components are patched and soldered to test the circuit board. Testing the key performance parameters of a large number of chips to obtain data sets. Train the optimised and improved SHAP-1DCNN deep learning model based on the collected data, and finally integrate this deep learning model in FPGA and accelerate its computation. The validation results show that the proposed test technique achieves a single OPA test time of 0.6s with an accuracy of 97.3%.

Title: Explicit Content Classification in Indonesian Song Lyrics Using the LSTM-CNN Method
Abstract: Music services are currently very popular and accessible to anyone, particularly through internet platforms. However, this widespread accessibility necessitates careful consideration, as music and songs can introduce explicit content to underage children and teenagers, especially through song lyrics. Manual labeling of songs for explicit content is prone to errors and time-consuming, but this process can be improved with Natural Language Processing (NLP) technologies, such as text classification using deep learning. The LSTM-CNN model was chosen for its ability to leverage the strengths of both Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN). LSTM captures long-range dependencies in sequential data, while CNN is effective at extracting localized features from text. This combination makes LSTM-CNN ideal for the complexity of Indonesian song lyrics, which often involve context-dependent content. In this research, the LSTM-CNN model demonstrated optimal performance in classifying explicit content in Indonesian song lyrics. The best results were achieved with a balanced dataset of 5,470 rows, an 80: 20 data splitting ratio, 5 epochs, a batch size of 128, and a dropout rate of 0.5. The model's performance metrics were as follows: accuracy of 74.52%, precision of 75.22%, recall of 74.37%, and an F1-score of 74.68%.

Title: Road Crack Detection using Deep Learning
Abstract: The road is a path that helps to connect various locations. It is essential to our day-to-day existence. The state of the weather conditions, overloading, poor maintenance, and a few other factors all contribute to road distress. The prevalent stressors are cracks, rutting, and potholes. Accidents on the roads have increased recently as a result of poor upkeep. Safety and road upkeep are important issues for transportation infrastructure. Road cracking is the fundamental and underlying source of other damages like potholes, etc., so manually identifying this distress requires labor-intensive, human inspection. Among the many difficulties, seeing fractures in the road ahead of time is crucial to avoiding collisions and expensive repairs. In this study, we provide an automated deep learning framework technique for spotting road cracks. The suggested method is trained using road photo datasets from many sources, which include a range of road surface types, lighting situations, and fracture severity. After that, data augmentation approaches are utilized to enhance model generalization. We use a variety of deep learning frameworks and fine-tune the hyper parameters to further enhance the model's performance and Reliability and consistency in grading outcomes are provided by the proposed deep learning approach, which is also computationally less expensive. The recommended deep learning method shows amazing accuracy in identifying and categorizing potholes, making it a useful instrument for road maintenance agencies.

Title: The impact of artificial intelligence on musicians
Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is forecasted to have more of an impact on some occupations and industries than others. We examine the impact that AI will have on musicians and singers. This analysis provides an interesting example as musicians typically engage in physical activities when playing, performing, and use creativity when writing songs. We contribute to the existing literature by linking AI to both an occupational analysis and delving into the emotional aspects AI might not be able to provide for musicians. We explore the pros and cons of using AI for the creation of AI generated music. Further, this paper explores music creation to focus on production and performance. Additional consideration is provided regarding the legal and ethical considerations of AI for musicians.

Title: Comparing Rayleigh Waves for Seismograph Health Diagnostics Based on Machine Learning
Abstract: The need for high-quality seismic data requires the development of seismograph health diagnostic methods to detect instrument problems early. The rapid expansion of seismic networks, increasing data volume, and the growing complexity of analysis methods for detecting component degradation are challenged by limited resources. To overcome this problem, a more efficient method is needed to assess the health of seismographs at each station. We propose a simple seismograph health diagnostic method that uses machine learning to classify seismographs based on their condition. This method analyzes parameters derived from the similarity of teleseismic Rayleigh waves recorded by a target station and several nearby reference stations. Key metrics, including cross-correlation coefficient, amplitude ratio, and cross-spectral density coherence (CSD), are essential to label the condition of each station based on its actual status when the teleseismic event occurs, thus creating a comprehensive dataset. We rigorously evaluated this dataset using three leading classification models: Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost). Among these, XGBoost demonstrated superior performance, achieving the highest accuracy (0.97), precision (0.99), recall (0.97), and F1 score (0.98). These results establish XGBoost as a reliable method for assessing seismograph health, classifying their status as excellent, good, fair, or poor. This approach is expected to enhance the seismograph health diagnostic and improve seismic network reliability.

Title: Comparison of Emotion Recognition from Baby Cries Using CNN and SVM with Noise Reduction Techniques
Abstract: Emotion recognition from baby cries has become an important field of research, with potential applications in healthcare and caregiving. This paper presents a comparison of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Support Vector Machines (SVM) for classifying emotions from baby cries, focusing on categories such as hunger, pain, tiredness, discomfort, and burping. Noise interference is a significant challenge in cry recognition, and noise reduction techniques are applied to enhance model accuracy. A 5-fold cross-validation approach is used to evaluate the performance of both models under noisy conditions. According to preliminary findings, the SVM outperformed the CNN, which had an accuracy of 81.7%, with an accuracy of 84% across all emotion categories. Both models demonstrated significant improvements with noise reduction, with the SVM model achieving the highest accuracy increase, rising from 81.2% to 84%. This paper highlights the effectiveness of deep learning models for real-time emotion detection and underscores the importance of noise reduction in achieving reliable results.

Title: Mood Classification of Indian Melodies Automatically Through Random Forest Method
Abstract: Most frequently, we decide to play a song or piece of music that best suits our current state of mind. Despite this significant link, the majority of the music software programmes available today do not yet offer the capability of mood-aware play-list building. By associating songs with the appropriate emotion category they communicate, music listeners might avoid spending more time manually compiling a list of tracks that suit a given mood or occasion. The challenge is to automatically and intelligently recognise this element because it is time-consuming to manually add lyrics to music with the appropriate emotion. Machine learning & data mining techniques have made significant contributions to analysing and determining how music and emotion relate to one another, which has given rise to a lot of interest in the research of mood detection in the field of music in recent years. By attempting to develop a system for automatically identifying the mood underlying the audio track<sup>s</sup> by mining their spectral, temporal audio properties, we carry the same inspiration forward and make a contribution. Hindi songs that are popular in India are the main focus. In order to educate, prepare, and evaluate the model that captures the emotions of these audio songs, several data classification techniques were evaluated and created an open source platform for it. By using the grouping (ensemble) of random-forest-approach tested on a set of 2700 audio samples and determined the mood underlying Indian popular music with an adequate precision of 70% to 75%.

Title: Optimizing Music Genre Classification: A Hybrid Approach with ACO and Ensemble Learning
Abstract: The classification of music genres accurately is an ongoing challenge due to the diverse and complex nature of music. Current methods can struggle to identify genres correctly. This study introduces a combination of ensemble learning and Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) to better select features that are key to identifying music genres. Using a diversified collection of songs from Spotify, the research applies detailed data preparation before utilizing a Stacking Classifier framework, which brings together several base learners and an Extra Trees algorithm to improve prediction accuracy. This method achieved a 96.75% accuracy in classifying music genres, surpassing previous methods and advancing the field. The study also compares this new model with other innovative models, highlighting the effectiveness of using a mix of methods. These improvements have important implications for building better music recommendation systems that are both accurate and user-friendly, paving the way for future developments in automatic music analysis.

Title: Instrumentality Classification Evaluation System for Natural Sounds
Abstract: Exploring the captivating realm of natural sounds in music creation typically presents unique challenges. Although the simplicity of producing melodies with glasses filled with varying amounts of water is enchanting, replicating such versatility with other natural sounds poses difficulties. The limitations lie in the inherent properties of most natural sounds, which lack the pitch modulation freedom akin to glass instruments, resulting in homogeneity or complexity that may not be conducive to direct musical application. This study addresses these challenges by proposing an evaluation method that leverages neural networks and deep learning techniques. Our method uses a dataset of natural sounds to train a deep neural network model, extracting feature vectors that encapsulate their sonic characteristics. Subsequently, these extracted features are applied to instrumental sound datasets, enabling the modeling of natural sound dimensions within the instrumental realm. Through a classification model, the obtained features facilitate the comparison of natural and instrumental ensembles, offering insights into the suitability of natural sounds as musical instruments. By applying this methodology, our study illustrates how natural sounds such as cowbells can be evaluated in comparison with conventional instruments such as the marimba. This approach enhances our understanding of natural sound potential in music composition and performance, offering new avenues for creative exploration and innovation in sound design.

Title: Instrumental Timbre Transfer Based on Disentangled Representation of Timbre and Pitch
Abstract: Timbre transfer is a complex audio synthesis task that changes the distinctive perceptual attribute of one instrument to resemble another while preserving the underlying musical content. In order to investigate the possibility of effective representation for pitch and timbre, this paper explores recent advances in timbre transfer using deep learning models, and presents a framework for multiple-to-multiple instrumental timbre transfer using a beta-variational autoencoder β-VAE). Through the dual-encoder system, it effectively disentangles the timbre and pitch, enabling the transfer of timbral characteristics across different musical notes and instruments while preserving the original pitch information. The performance of our approach, evaluated through metrics including Frechet Audio Distance (FAD), pitch accuracy, and Structural Similarity Index (SSIM), suggests its effectiveness for timbre conversions. This research offers potential applications in music production, audio synthesis, and sound design, paving the way for more adaptable and efficient timbre transfer solutions.

Title: Detection of Voice Disorder Using Spectral and Statistical Audio Features and SVM-RBF
Abstract: The detection of voice disorders using voice signal processing and machine learning has emerged as a promising early diagnosis and treatment approach. This paper presents a machine learning-based automatic voice disorder detection framework extracting and selecting optimum features from voice audio signals. The practical challenge of class-imbalanced scenario of disorder and healthy voices data is addressed using the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE). Several features, i.e., Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC), Chroma Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT), zero crossing rate, root mean square, skewness, and kurtosis; have been studied in spectral and statistical domains. Finally, the optimum features are selected using the Recursive Feature Elimination with Cross-Validation (RFECV) technique to reduce the classifier model’s complexity. A support vector machine (SVM) classifier with a Radial basis function kernel is developed, prioritizing simplicity and efficiency. The SVM model is trained and tested using the well-accepted VOICED database of PhysioNet Data Bank where the audio is captured using a smartphone. The performance of the overall framework shows an accuracy of 95% and 100% precision and specificity, demonstrating its resilience for precise evaluations and smartphone-based diagnosis applications.

Title: Similarity Metrics for Late Reverberation
Abstract: Automatic tuning of reverberation algorithms relies on the optimization of a loss function. While general audio similarity metrics are useful, they are not optimized for the specific statistical properties of reverberation in rooms. This paper presents two novel metrics for assessing the similarity of late reverberation in room impulse responses. These metrics are differentiable and can be utilized within a machine-learning framework. We compare the performance of these metrics to two popular audio metrics using a large dataset of room impulse responses encompassing various room configurations and microphone positions. The results indicate that the proposed functions based on averaged power and frequency-band energy decay outperform the baselines with the former exhibiting the most suitable profile towards the minimum. The proposed work holds promise as an improvement to the design and evaluation of reverberation similarity metrics.

Title: The Impact of AI on Accounting Technology Adoption the Mediate Role of Business Performance
Abstract: How the effect of Artificial Intelligence (AI) on accounting technology adoption and explore whether business performance mediates this relationship. The study follows a descriptive research design conducted in Amman, Jordan that seeks to investigate the effects of AI-based accounting technologies on businesses. Sample practitioners120 business administrators were selected through a purposive sampling technique. A questionnaire was the primary data collection instrument, and face content [30] validation was conducted to assure its accuracy, relevance, and comprehensiveness. The reliability of the scale was confirmed with Cronbach Alpha, which has a value of 0.84, which indicates high enough consistency; Analysis of collected data was performed using the regression and has been assessed by level 0.05(alpha). This study discovers the positive effects on business performance by implementing AI-equipped accounting technology in terms of increasing efficiency, reliability and resources. By incorporating AI in accounting duties, it is feasible to remove workloads speedily and also minimize costs which leads further in getting reliable financial information on time. The study concludes that AI-enabled accounting technology has a positive influence on business performance, playing an essential role in promoting operational outcomes. The research advises organizations to embrace AI-driven accounting tools that can lead the way towards better financial transparency and operational proficiency. Companies must train and retrain professional accountants who develop or review financial information to maximize their utilization of AI technologies for rapidly delivering the financial data needed.
